title: Coupling composition design with defect engineering: An oxygen-doped Ti-Zr-Nb strain glass alloy with enhanced high-temperature shape memory effect
abstract: High-temperature shape memory alloys (HTSMAs) are critical for temperature-sensitive applications, yet the trade-off between high transformation temperatures and large recoverable strains remains a long-standing challenge. This study addresses this limitation by deploying a composition control and defect engineering strategy to regulate the martensitic transformation in HTSMAs via a strain glass while preserving elevated transformation temperatures. By introducing 1 at.% oxygen as point defects, a Ti47Zr47Nb5O1 strain glass alloy with a freezing temperature of about 462 K was fabricated. The microstructure consists of a strain‑glass‑dominated β matrix with minor residual α″ martensite. The low Nb content destabilizes the β phase, enabling the alloy to retain a high transformation temperature of about 745 K. Enabled by the strain glass state and the remarkable theoretical transformation strain derived from the addition of high-content Zr with large atomic radius, this alloy exhibits nearly full recoverability for pre‑strains up to about 5%, and achieves a shape memory recovery strain of ∼5.7% at a pre‑strain of 10%, outperforming most reported HTSMAs. The underlying deformation mechanism is attributed to the stress-induced reversible β → α″ martensitic transformation together with martensitic variant reorientation, which cooperatively accommodate local strains within nanoscale domains. © 2026 Chinese Society of Metals

title: Strategic deployment of seasonal thermal energy storage for decarbonizing remote northern communities in Canada: A multidimensional evaluation framework
abstract: Remote northern communities face major energy-transition challenges due to extreme climates, prolonged heating seasons, geographic isolation, dependence on imported fossil fuels, and limited energy infrastructure. Seasonal Thermal Energy Storage (STES) can address the mismatch between renewable heat availability and winter heating demand, but technology selection must account for environmental, geological, logistical, economic, and socio-technical constraints alongside conventional engineering performance. This review evaluates seven STES technologies using a northern-specific multidimensional framework integrating thermodynamic performance, technical maturity, economic performance, constructability and logistics, permafrost compatibility, and community implementation capacity. The framework operationalizes this assessment through non-compensable feasibility screening and TOPSIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis using a literature-informed technology-performance matrix, an equal-weight reference, two contrasting northern deployment archetypes, and weight- and score-sensitivity analyses. Results show that suitability depends on the interaction between technology characteristics and deployment context rather than engineering performance alone. Tank Thermal Energy Storage (TTES) exhibits the most robustly favourable profile across the evaluated scenarios and sensitivity analyses, whereas Pit Thermal Energy Storage (PTES), Borehole Thermal Energy Storage (BTES), and Rock Thermal Energy Storage (RTES) are more context dependent. Phase Change Material (PCM) and Thermochemical Energy Storage (TCES) offer high theoretical storage potential but remain limited by large-scale operational validation, while Aquifer Thermal Energy Storage (ATES) is conditional on suitable hydrogeological conditions. The proposed framework shifts STES selection from performance-based ranking toward context-driven decision support, providing developers, utilities, engineering practitioners, and community decision-makers with a transparent and reproducible methodology for identifying robust candidates, context-sensitive alternatives, and critical deployment constraints before detailed site-specific assessment in northern Canada and other circumpolar regions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Enhancing accounting students’ writing performance through problem-based learning: Evidence from a vocational higher education context
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) has gained momentum in English for specific purpose (ESP) education, yet little is known about how PBL functions in vocational higher education settings for accounting for students' writing. This study investigated the effectiveness, benefits, and challenges associated with accounting students' writing performance. This study employs a mixed-methods design involving 60 students from one of the state polytechnics in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. The experimental group (N=30) experienced PBL, and the control group (N=30) received conventional learning. Data were collected through writing tests to investigate students' improvement in their writing performance, and interviews to explore students' perceptions of benefits and challenges. The results of the writing test were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics via SPSS, and the interview results were analyzed using thematic analysis. The quantitative results reveal that there is a significant difference in the writing performance of accounting students who were taught by using PBL and those who were taught by using conventional learning, with PBL being better than conventional learning. It can be concluded that PBL is effective at enhancing accounting students' writing performance. The qualitative results of the interviews revealed that the accounting students mentioned the benefits of PBL, including improvement in students' writing skills, development of students' problem-solving skills, development of students' critical thinking, team collaboration, and real accounting problem connections. However, they listed the challenges of PBL, which include difficulty relating to the varied ideas and a lack of experience with the problems. Future research is recommended to extend the study duration to better capture the lasting impacts of PBL, offering a more comprehensive understanding of this approach. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Ultramicropore-Confined Solvation and Interphase Regulation Unlock High-Performance Hard Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Hard carbon (HC) anodes are promising for sodium-ion batteries, yet achieving high initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), large plateau contribution, and fast charge-transfer kinetics remains challenging due to insufficient control of micro–nanostructure and interphase chemistry. Here, we present a precursor-level molecular engineering strategy that simultaneously regulates sodium desolvation and interphase chemistry in HC. An iodine-mediated oxidative cross-linking process converts starch into spherical HC with uniformly distributed ultramicropores and carbonyl-rich surfaces. These nanoconfined pores are proposed to act as molecular sieves, preferentially excluding bulky solvent molecules while allowing PF6−-coordinated Na+ access, thereby favoring anion-enriched electrolyte structures under confinement. Surface carbonyls exhibit strong PF6− affinity, which may promote fluorine-rich inorganic interphases on pore surfaces. The synergistic effects of anion-selective adsorption and confined desolvation are suggested to favor thin and robust NaF-rich interphases at external surfaces and within nanoconfined pore regions, contributing to reversible interfacial reactions and rapid Na+ storage kinetics. Consequently, the HC delivers an ICE of 88.4%, a reversible capacity of 352.9 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, excellent rate capability (288.9 mAh g−1 at 5C), and 95.6% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This work offers a molecular-level design paradigm integrating efficiency, capacity, and kinetics in HC anodes. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Polyhydroxy Molecular Regulator Enabled Interfacial Microenvironment Programming for Alkaline Zinc–Iron Flow Batteries
abstract: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (ZIFBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost, intrinsic safety, and scalable architecture, yet their practical deployment remains hindered by hydrogen evolution and uncontrolled Zn deposition in three-dimensional porous electrodes. Here, we report that isomalt acts as a polyhydroxy molecular regulator that reconfigures the interfacial microenvironment of porous carbon felt, thereby endowing the porous electrode with a more deposition-directing function for reversible Zn plating/stripping. In the bulk electrolyte, isomalt reconstructs the local hydrogen-bond network, lowers water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. At the carbon/electrolyte interface, its preferential lateral adsorption establishes a hydroxyl-rich interphase that homogenizes zincate transport and directs Zn growth toward a preferred (002) orientation, thus promoting compact and reversible deposition. This interfacial microenvironment programming markedly reduces the charge-transfer resistance and activation barrier of the Zn anode, enabling stable cycling for over 500 cycles at 20 mA cm−2. In full-cell tests, the optimized ZIFB delivers a high energy efficiency of 87.5%, substantially outperforming the pristine electrolyte. Beyond identifying a low-cost green additive, this work establishes polyhydroxy molecules as interfacial programming units for three-dimensional porous electrodes, offering a new design concept for directional metal deposition in aqueous flow-battery systems. title: Capacity Degradation Mechanisms, Recovery Strategies, and Challenges of Flow Batteries
abstract: Redox flow batteries, by virtue of their advantages in power/capacity decoupling, high safety, and long cycle life, have become a strategic support for long-duration energy storage systems; however, capacity degradation remains a bottleneck for their commercialization. This review systematically identifies the multi-dimensional mechanisms of capacity degradation: including volume imbalance caused by transmembrane migration, inactivation and decomposition of active species, electrode degradation, and valence imbalance induced by side reactions. Targeting these challenges, the review deeply explores recovery strategies from physical repair to intelligent scheduling: covering the research and development of high-selectivity membranes, precise regulation of valence states, functionalized repair of electrodes, and model-driven predictive pathways integrating digital twins. Finally, current challenges such as characterization limitations and incomplete recovery rates are summarized, and future development directions for capacity recovery are envisioned. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for extending the system cycle life of flow batteries and improving capacity recovery efficiency. title: Hotspot to Homogeneous: Amorphous Interfacial Current Redistribution Enables Stable Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
abstract: Interfacial instability in oxide ceramic electrolyte (OCE)-based solid-state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) is conventionally attributed to chemical incompatibility or mechanical failure, yet the underlying atomic-scale mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we reveal that grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline OCEs function as bipolar interfacial hotspots, accelerating three degradation pathways: lowering barriers for Li dendrite nucleation and enabling electron-leakage-driven reduction at anode side, while generating localized overpotentials for cathode phase transformation. To deactivate these GB-driven hotspots, we develop a laser-induced amorphization strategy that constructs a GB-free amorphous interlayer capable of homogenizing Li+ flux and blocking electron migration. Applied to a representative sodium superionic conductor-type electrolyte, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3, this approach delivers substantially increased critical current density in Li symmetric cells (1.4 to 2.4 mA cm−2) with stable cycling over 2000 h, and achieves an exceptional capacity retention of 101.9 mAh g−1 after 800 cycles in LiCoO2 full cells operated at 4.5 V. The generality of this strategy is further validated on garnet-type and perovskite-type OCEs. This work introduces amorphous interfacial current redistribution as a universal paradigm for engineering stable interfaces, providing a critical atomic-scale interface engineering route to unlock high-voltage, dendrite-free SSLMBs. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Multicomponent Nitride/High-Entropy Alloy Heterostructures as Highly Active and Stable Electrocatalysts for Ampere-Level Water Oxidation
abstract: Developing highly active and stable oxygen evolution reaction catalysts is paramount for cost-effective large-scale green hydrogen production via water electrolysis. Here we report nonprecious metal-based multicomponent nitride/high-entropy alloy heterostructures as cost-effective electrocatalysts to efficiently mediate alkaline water oxidation by in-situ configurating cooperative Brønsted basic oxyanion-solid interfaces during phase transformation of multicomponent nitride into amorphous N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH along with partial dissolution of high-value metals of Mo and Cr to form molecular MoO42− and CrO42− species. The protonation of Brønsted basic oxyanions facilitates the critical *OOH intermediate formation on N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH with near-optimal adsorption energy, substantially accelerating the oxygen evolution reaction kinetics. Consequently, the heterostructure electrode exhibits superior oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysis in 1 M KOH solution, delivering ultrahigh current density of ~ 2.5 A cm−2 at low overpotential of 300 mV. Its alkaline water electrolyzer operates stably at ampere-level current density for > 1700 h. Our findings reveal an unconventional molecule-assisted multi-site mechanism of multicomponent catalysts to accelerate multiple-intermediate reaction. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

abstract: Through a comparative analysis, this study investigates the development, simulation, and application of mathematical models for integrated analysis of copper rod production in order to improve product quality, reduce costs, and minimize risks. The purpose of this article is achieved by creating mathematical descriptions of real processes, which are then used to conduct computer experiments. In contrast to the traditional molecular dynamic methods, this study used information technology to obtain the characteristics of the flow field in technological equipment. The novelty lies in: integration of thermomechanical modeling with an optimization algorithm; introduction of a criterion minimizing mechanical property variation; consideration of reduction and redistribution effects on roll wear; possibility of adaptive real-time control. An information analysis of the profiles of copper melt flow velocities in a wide range of temperatures in the Copper Rod Production Plant Kazkat is presented. Information Technology fulfils the need to address the problem of determining the optimal values of temperature, rolling speed, and other parameters to achieve the best quality and productivity of copper rod production processes. Based on these findings, this study proposes the optimization directions for the temperature field profile in the rolling rolls, which leads to a decrease in roll wear and an increase in the uniformity of the wire rod structure, focusing on improving microstructural properties. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Interface Contact Optimization via Phosphomolybdic Acid Enables 24.9% Efficiency in MoOX-Based Silicon Solar Cells
abstract: The development of cost-effective carrier-selective passivating contacts is critical for enhancing the commercial feasibility of silicon compound solar cells. Molybdenum oxide (MoOX) has garnered considerable interest as a promising hole transport layer (HTLs). A key advantage of MoOX is high work function, in addition to the low-cost processability. However, in silicon photovoltaics, MoOX-based p-type contacts face fundamental limitations at hydrogenated amorphous silicon (i-a-Si:H)/MoOX interface, where oxygen vacancy defects lower work function, as well as, weak van der Waals-dominated interactions impair charge carry transport. To address these challenges, we introduced an ultrathin phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) interlayer at the i-a-Si:H/MoOX interface. PMA passivated oxygen vacancy defects, resulting in a notable improvement in open-circuit voltage from 713 to 730 mV, and 0.11 eV work function elevation via dipole formation; meanwhile, PMA strengthened the interfacial bonding energy, reducing saturation current density and contact resistance by 63% and 24%, respectively, contributing to a fill factor enhancement from 83.7% to 84.9%. In the end, we demonstrated a record efficiency of 24.9% for MoOX-based silicon solar cells, which provides valuable insights for developing high-performance MoOX HTL devices for dopant-free p-type contact technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Anionic Bottom-Up Flux Orchestrated via Hard Carbon Surface Chemistry for Stable Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries suffer from unstable solid-electrolyte interphase formation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and poor cycle stability. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface. By engineering a synergistic pair of pyridinic-N and carbonyl groups on the carbon surface, we create a functional-differentiation microenvironment where pyridinic-N selectively anchors PF6− anions, while the cooperative carbonyl repels solvent molecules. This dual functionality establishes a sustained concentration gradient that drives a continuous reverse flux of anions toward the interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition pathway from solvent-dominated to anion-preferential. The tailored surface lowers the PF6− decomposition barrier by over 70%, yielding a thin, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase dominated by NaF and Na2O. The optimized anode achieves 91.9% Coulombic efficiency with high reversible capacity of 368.2 mAh g−1, and 96.5% capacity retention after 5,000 cycles. A pouch cell assembled with NFPP cathode achieves an energy density of 239.1 Wh kg−1 and stable operation over 500 cycles, demonstrating strong practical potential. This work establishes active surface-guided anionic transport as a powerful strategy for interphase engineering in advanced sodium-ion batteries. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Elucidating the Respective Roles of Photochemical and Photothermal Effects in Photocatalytic Methanol Decomposition
abstract: Photocatalytic reactions can be driven by both photochemical and photothermal processes. However, their individual contributions and synergistic effect remain to be clarified. Herein, we investigated the respective roles of these effects using a Cu–TiO2/Ti model catalyst that integrated photochemical and photothermal functionalities within a single photocatalytic system. Employing photocatalytic methanol decomposition as a model reaction, the Cu–TiO2/Ti catalyst achieved a high H2 yield rate of 0.511 mmol h−1 with selectivity of 96.6% toward HCHO among oxidation products, attributed to the cooperative action of photochemical and photothermal processes. In situ resonant Auger electron spectroscopy (RAS), together with in situ Cu K-edge X-ray absorption fine structure and excited-state density functional theory calculations, revealed the accumulation of photogenerated electrons at Cu sites from TiO2, suggests the possible formation of an electron transfer pathway from TiO2 to Cu, which promotes stepwise methanol dehydrogenation to HCHO and H2. Simultaneously, the photothermal contribution from Ti enhanced catalytic activity by accelerating reaction kinetics and promoting the desorption of HCHO, thereby suppressing its overoxidation to CO. abstract: This study focuses on the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker using local raw materials found in the Aral Sea region of the Republic of Uzbekistan and on its properties. The obtained results highlight the technological, economic, and environmental advantages. The raw material mixtures consisted of limestone, barren sand, kaolin, and iron-containing industrial waste, resulting in a clinker with an optimized oxide composition (LSF = 0.82, SR = 2.15, AP = 0.94). X-ray phase analysis reveals a high content of alite (C3S ≈ 38.6%) and belite (C2S ≈ 41.0%) phases, which ensures high mechanical strength. Low tricalcium aluminate content (tricalcium aluminate < 5%) and sufficient ferrite content (C4AF ≈ 16.2%) increased sulfate resistance and phase dominance. Sulfate resistance tests conducted in accordance with ASTM C1012/C1012M showed that sulfate-resistant Portland cement had the lowest swelling index among samples immersed in a 5% Na2SO4 solution, demonstrating its superior stability compared to conventional Portland cement and mixed cement types. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of producing high-quality sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker using local raw materials and demonstrate its potential for use in the sulfate-rich conditions of the Aral Sea region. From an economic perspective, the use of local raw materials reduces production costs, the need for imports, and increases the competitiveness of the cement industry in our region. From an environmental perspective, the long service life of sulfate-resistant Portland cement and the ability to utilize industrial waste align with the principles of a "green economy" and promote waste reduction and sustainable growth. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Screen-Printed Li Arrays with Reinforced Interphase as Ultrathin Anodes for High-Energy–Density Liquid- and Solid-State Batteries
abstract: High-energy–density lithium metal batteries, either liquid or solid state, require ultrathin Li anodes, but their implementation is hindered by poor Li processability in fabrication and inhomogeneous Li plating behaviours upon cycling. This work addresses these challenges through a mask-patterned discrete array using a molten salt-derived Li nanocomposite. The screen-printing strategy circumvents the poor wettability of molten Li on copper that causes high Li|Cu contact angle and non-uniform Li spreading, thus fabricating ultrathin Li foils with equivalent thicknesses below 30 μm. Concurrently, the molten salt-derived inorganic nanoparticles in Li favour homogeneous Li deposition and induce inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase to jointly suppress active Li consumption. The resulting Li array (10–28 μm) anodes demonstrate remarkable performance in both liquid- and solid-state systems, achieving high energy densities up to 504 Wh kg−1/1071 Wh L−1 and stable cycling over 260 cycles with high-loading cathodes. This integrated approach resolves both fabrication and cycling challenges of ultrathin Li anodes and offers an alternative solution for high-performance liquid-/solid-state batteries. title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. In the 90° case, VG orientation achieved the highest electrical efficiency at (Re = 11000), achieving an electrical efficiency of 16.9% and maximum achievable electrical power output of approximately 88 W, after accounting for DC fan power consumption, with the 90° VG configuration still showing the highest system electrical power. The 30° scenario, by contrast, resulted in the best thermal efficiency—nearly 80% and the greatest thermal power—over 420 W demonstrating practical merit in providing guidance for selecting PV cooling configurations based on specific electrical-output or thermal-recovery priorities. ©2027 The author(s). title: Research on online multi-step short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on selective representation-driven concept drift adaptation
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the secure operation and optimal scheduling of power systems. However, PV power data are highly non-stationary due to weather fluctuations, seasonal transitions, and changing operating conditions, which often cause concept drift in real-world scenarios. Most existing methods are developed in offline settings and lack the ability to adapt continuously to evolving data streams. To address this issue, this study proposes an online learning framework for multi-step short-term PV power forecasting. Specifically, a shared-parameter dual-branch Informer concept encoder is designed to capture concept discrepancies between historical and incoming data, while a mixture-of-experts adaptive parameter generator is introduced to produce targeted update parameters for different drift patterns. In addition, a selective segmentation mechanism is incorporated into the TimeBridge backbone to improve the modeling of critical temporal blocks. Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for drift-aware online PV forecasting and offers practical support for enhancing the reliability, stability, and dispatch efficiency of power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Comparative evaluation of SRF-PLL and instantaneous-power LVRT control for a three-wire grid-connected PV system under ground faults
abstract: The performance of low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control depends on the voltage information used for synchronisation and current-reference generation, as well as the physical current paths of the converter. In this paper, four synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) and instantaneous power theory (IPT) implementations are compared on a common 1.504 MW photovoltaic simulation model under single line-to-ground and double line-to-ground faults. The three-wire converter is connected through a delta–grounded-wye transformer. Consequently, its zero-sequence line current is constrained to zero, although ground-fault current is present on the grounded transformer side. The current-control action is therefore confined to the two independent converter axes. The comparison uses conventional and positive-sequence-conditioned SRF and IPT implementations with a shared reactive-current-priority LVRT law, DC-voltage regulation and current-reference limits. For the double line-to-ground case, positive-sequence IPT provides 730.6 kvar at the low-voltage measurement point, compared with 376.1 kvar for instantaneous-voltage IPT, while its nonfundamental current residual decreases from 22.06% to 0.037%. However, the latter controller has a smaller 100 Hz active-power component, demonstrating a trade-off between power oscillation and current quality. Actual transient current reaches 1.234 pu despite a 1.2 pu reference ceiling. Sequence-extraction diagnostics against established DSOGI and DSC methods, together with transformer-side measurements, explain these outcomes. Hardware-in-loop captures document laboratory-platform observations; all quantitative controller comparisons are based on simulations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A robust energy management model for unbalanced microgrids under electricity price uncertainty considering central inverters and demand response for voltage unbalance mitigation
abstract: The increasing penetration of unbalanced loads, such as single-phase electric vehicles, in microgrids (MGs) can lead to significant Power Quality (PQ) issues, requiring demand response and ancillary services for mitigation. In this regard, an energy management model for renewable energy resources (RES) and energy storage (ES)-based buses is proposed, in which central inverters are used to support PQ and coordinate energy trading. An unbalanced IEEE 13-bus test system is used to evaluate the proposed framework, with particular emphasis on voltage unbalance mitigation and energy management. The results show that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage unbalance Indicator (VUI) from approximately 4% to below the 2%, with only a 0.35% increase in operating cost. In addition, a robust optimization approach is employed to address electricity price uncertainty, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework under uncertain operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing wind energy forecasting under constrained data conditions: a CRISP-DM-based deep neural network approach
abstract: Accurate forecasting of wind energy production plays a crucial role in the efficient operation of energy markets. However, many advanced models depend on extensive datasets and detailed meteorological information that are rarely available in industrial environments. This work investigates short-term wind power forecasting under constrained industrial conditions, including limited data availability, incomplete high-resolution meteorological information, and noisy operational measurements. A Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM)-based workflow is adopted to support data preprocessing, model training, and validation throughout the forecasting process. An openly available dataset containing hourly records from multiple European wind farms is used, focusing on a single wind farm subset to evaluate forecasting performance under realistic single-site deployment conditions. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model combined with lag-based and nonlinear feature engineering techniques is implemented to capture operational relationships without relying on complete external meteorological fields. Experimental results show that feedforward architectures can provide competitive forecasting performance under constrained data scenarios. The findings highlight the importance of balancing model complexity, data availability, robust validation, and deployability in real-world wind energy forecasting applications. © 2026

title: Prioritizing resilience criteria and indicators in urban disadvantaged areas using the Best-Worst Method (BWM)
abstract: Urban disadvantaged areas are highly vulnerable to natural hazards due to physical, social, economic, and institutional deficiencies. These areas-such as historic residential area, decayed residential areas, informal settlements, and social housing-experience distinct challenges that necessitate tailored resilience strategies. Considering Iran's high hazard proneness, strengthening resilience in such areas is an urgent priority. Existing resilience literature often adopts a generalized, city-wide perspective, lacking the granularity for effective local-level resource allocation in diverse disadvantaged areas. This study aims to identify and prioritize resilience criteria and indicators across the four types of disadvantaged areas. A comprehensive literature review extracted potential resilience criteria, refined and validated using the Delphi method with 16 experts engaged via snowball sampling. The Best-Worst Method (BWM), an MCDM approach, weighted and ranked criteria for each area type. Results show economic capacity is most critical in informal settlements. Physical-environmental aspects (building quality, infrastructure) dominate historical and decayed areas. Institutional dimensions (governance, accountability, policy support) are most influential in social housing resilience. Cross-area comparison reveals shared and context-specific determinants, underscoring the need for integrated, area-sensitive resilience planning. Findings offer a framework for urban planners to prioritize targeted interventions, balancing physical upgrades with social empowerment, economic capacity building, and institutional strengthening for sustainable and inclusive resilience. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Deterministic branch-and-bound global MPPT using surrogate-derived power bounds for partially shaded PV arrays
abstract: Partial shading fragments the power–voltage characteristic of series-connected photovoltaic (PV) arrays into multiple local peaks, rendering conventional trackers ineffective and exposing the reliance of metaheuristic global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) methods on random initialization and empirical tuning coefficients. This paper proposes TSB-GMPPT, a deterministic tanh-surrogate branch-and-bound GMPPT algorithm that eliminates both dependencies. A control-oriented hyperbolic-tangent surrogate of the PV I–V characteristic admits a non-iterative Lambert W asymptotic approximation for the maximum power point voltage. During discovery, a single saturation-region measurement per candidate is sufficient to construct a calibrated optimistic bound, safely pruning the search space before final peak localization. An offline polynomial calibration recovers the remaining parameters from short-circuit current. During discovery, an optimistic branch-and-bound rule maintains an upper power bound for each unconfirmed layer and permanently discards candidates that cannot exceed the incumbent confirmed power, contracting the admissible search space without exhaustive probing. A five-state finite-state machine governs initialization, shading-topology detection, discovery, winner refitting, convergence, and adaptive reinitialization. Experimental validation using a Chroma 62150H solar array simulator and a dSPACE DS1104 platform on five-module benchmark cases and additional eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases demonstrates average tracking efficiencies of 99.94% under partial shading and 99.98% under uniform irradiance, with corresponding average convergence times of 0.25 s and 0.21 s, respectively, for the five-module test set. Further validation under eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases and dynamic irradiance transitions confirms rapid re-tracking, accurate GMPP identification, and robust operation under realistic operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Fabrication of bioactive hydrogels stabilized by gluten amyloid fibrils and ε-polylysine: Effects of fibril morphology and blending ratios
abstract: The introduction of ε-Polylysine (PL) provides additional functional activities for hydrogels. However, it simultaneously impairs their mechanical properties to a certain extent. To address this trade-off, we hypothesized that gluten protein amyloid fibrils (GAFs) with distinct topological morphologies—long rigid fibrils (LRF), long flexible fibrils (LFF), and fibril networks (FN) differentially modulate PL hydrogels through site-specific molecular bridging and spatial cross-linking. Driven by strong electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding, GAFs and PL underwent ratio dependent systemic reorganization and assembly. The physicochemical properties of GAFs/PL hydrogels were primarily governed by the combined regulation of GAFs morphology and blending ratios. Specifically, at the same GAFs/PL ratio, FN exhibited superior spatial connectivity, contributing to enhanced water immobilization within the hydrogel network. Meanwhile, LRF and FN were more effective in constructing continuous force transmission pathways, thereby improving hardness and dynamic viscoelasticity. These findings demonstrate that the functional performance of GAFs/PL hydrogels can be tailored by selecting appropriate fibril morphologies and blending ratios according to specific application requirements. However, the network formed by LFF was more susceptible to deformation, resulting in a relatively limited mechanical reinforcement effect on the hydrogel skeleton. Ultimately, this study aims to clarify the assembly pathway driven by the cooperative contribution of GAFs and PL. This study provides a theoretical foundation and design strategies for developing food-grade composite materials with tunable mechanical properties and bioactive functionalities. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Energy trading and demand response strategies for energy flexible manufacturing systems under temporary electricity shortages: A noise-robust multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
abstract: This paper investigates the energy management of energy flexible manufacturing systems (EFMS) under temporary electricity shortages (TES). TES disrupt the real-time balance of energy supply and demand. Meanwhile, multi-source measurement noise can degrade dynamic state estimation and affect scheduling decisions. To address these challenges, a hybrid approach integrating a generalized loss cubature Kalman filter (GLCKF) and a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is proposed. First, a dynamic pricing model based on the real-time demand-supply ratio, retail price, and feed-in tariff is designed to keep local trading prices within the grid price bounds. Second, GLCKF is used to suppress the effects of non-Gaussian measurement noise and random outliers. The resulting state estimates are used by MADDPG to jointly optimize real-time energy trading and demand response (DR) strategies. The framework is evaluated using a simulated four-EFMS cluster over a one-day scheduling horizon. The case incorporates industrial load profiles, photovoltaic generation, energy storage parameters, and time-of-use electricity prices. Comparative results show a 53.76% reduction in state-estimation root mean square error relative to CKF-MADDPG under the selected mixed-Gaussian noise setting. The results indicate that the framework improves economic performance and supports supply-demand balance in the tested TES scenarios. © 2026

title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention networks for multi-regional load forecasting in modern power systems with missing data
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy and multi-regional power system operation creates new challenges for short-term load forecasting (STLF), particularly under missing data, dynamic spatial dependencies, and uncertainty. Existing approaches often separate data imputation from forecasting, rely on static spatial structures, and provide deterministic predictions, limiting their applicability in risk-aware power system operation. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Graph Attention Network (UA-DGAT) for multi-regional load forecasting under incomplete and uncertain data conditions. The proposed framework integrates probabilistic masked self-attention imputation, uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale temporal modeling based on discrete wavelet transform within an end-to-end architecture. Unlike conventional pipelines, UA-DGAT explicitly propagates imputation uncertainty, spatial dependency uncertainty, and predictive uncertainty throughout the forecasting process. Extensive experiments on NYISO and ISO-NE datasets demonstrate that UA-DGAT achieves superior performance in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting metrics, reducing MAE and RMSE while attaining approximately 87% prediction interval coverage. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each component and confirm the significant role of uncertainty-aware conditioning. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains robust forecasting performance under missing data rates up to 50%, with particularly improved resilience under block missing patterns. The results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware modeling of data reconstruction and spatial dependency learning enables more accurate, reliable, and risk-aware load forecasting for modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Under fixed online time budgets, the MOA framework improves the mean HV by 31.13%–80.04% relative to five comparison methods and achieves the lowest mean inverted generational distance (IGD) on 14 of the 15 instances. The related data are available at https://github.com/fenglinggui/MOA-EP-RDSP. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Dual-Objective Design of Broadband Rectenna and Anchor Node Optimization for Energy Harvesting and High-Accuracy UWB Localization
abstract: Wireless sensor networks and portable devices face two major challenges: sustainable energy supply and high-precision indoor localization. While far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) offers energy solutions, it suffers from low power density and environmental sensitivity. To mitigate these drawbacks, the proposed system incorporates polarization diversity and a wideband impedance matching strategy. Simultaneously, GPS fails in indoor environments, driving the need for ultra-wideband (UWB) localization to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. This paper presents a dual-objective framework to tackle both issues. First, it designs a broadband antenna array (1–20 GHz) with multi-polarization reception, combined with an optimized matching network and Schottky-based rectifier to enhance RF-to-DC conversion under low power. Second, it introduces an anchor placement optimization algorithm for UWB that uses probabilistic target behavior models to minimize positioning errors. Simulation results confirm that the energy harvester remains effective across various incident angles and frequencies, while the localization error is consistently reduced to around one centimeter. The integrated approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation WSNs, overcoming power management bottlenecks while elevating localization accuracy to approximately one centimeter. © 2027 The author(s). title: Tuning oxygen-proton coupling of oxygen electrodes to match electrolyte transport in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
abstract: Understanding how oxygen-electrode functionality interacts with electrolyte transport is essential for advancing reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs), yet their coupling remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal an electrolyte-dependent performance reversal arising from the interplay between oxygen-proton coupled reaction pathways and electrolyte transport. Surface functionalization of BaCe0.5Pr0.3Y0.2O3−δ (BCPY) oxygen electrodes with Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3−δ (PBC) and Ni-substituted Pr0.5Ba0.5Co0.5Ni0.5O3−δ (PBCN) perovskite coatings selectively tunes surface defect chemistry and reaction pathways. PBC promotes lattice-oxygen activation and oxygen-vacancy-mediated processes, whereas Ni substitution in PBCN suppresses vacancy formation while enhancing proton hydration through strengthened Co–O covalency and optimized adsorption of oxygen intermediates. Consequently, PBC-BCPY delivers superior performance on BaZr0.8Yb0.2O3−δ (BZYb) electrolytes with limited proton conductivity, whereas PBCN-BCPY outperforms on highly proton-conductive BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) electrolytes. Benefiting from the optimized coupling between electrode surface functionality and electrolyte transport, the PBCN-coated BCPY electrode achieves a peak power density of 1.88 W cm⁻2 and a current density of 2.57 A cm⁻2 at 700 °C and 1.3 V on BZCYYb, while maintaining stable operation for 300 h at 600 °C. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for tailoring electrode surface functionality to match electrolyte transport, offering new design principles for high-performance R-PCECs. © 2026

title: Multi-objective optimization and decision-making for renewable energy production and enhancement of wind turbine selection in Morocco
abstract: Selecting an appropriate wind turbine for a specific location requires the simultaneous evaluation of energy output, cost, and site-specific deployment constraints. This research introduces a comprehensive framework that integrates simulation, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), and hybrid deep learning to enhance the selection of turbines for various sites. One year of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis version 5 (ERA5) reanalysis data and geographical information from satellite and elevation datasets was used to model the energy output of 40 commercial turbines in 15 Moroccan cities. A weighted scoring procedure was developed to evaluate turbines based on their capacity factor, annual energy production (AEP), capital and operating expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), topographical constraints, and proximity to infrastructure. Two hybrid models, convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural network-Transformer (CNN–Transformer), were trained on structured inputs that included meteorological, topography, and spatial data to enhance decision assistance. The CNN–Transformer model outperformed the CNN–LSTM model in predictions and closely aligned with the expert rankings derived from simulations. Constraint-aware filtering and cost-performance trade-offs were employed to enhance the final turbine suggestions. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning for large-scale energy planning at specific locations. This framework supports future upgrades to renewable energy systems, including AI-based digital twins, real-time monitoring, and use across more locations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A study on the site selection of pumped storage power plants based on GIS and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Models: A case study of China
abstract: Pumped storage power plants (PSPPs) are essential for enhancing power system flexibility and supporting renewable energy integration. However, PSPP site selection involves complex spatial constraints and multi-dimensional trade-offs among technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. This study proposes a two-stage GIS–MCDM framework for PSPP site selection. First, GIS-based spatial screening with veto criteria is applied to identify feasible candidate sites. Subsequently, an integrated AHP–entropy weighting approach and TOPSIS method are employed for comprehensive evaluation, with VIKOR, TODIM, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation used to verify robustness. A case study in Guangxi, China identifies the optimal site among seven alternatives, and the results demonstrate the stability of the proposed framework under different weighting scenarios. Furthermore, theoretical energy storage assessment and comparison with an approved PSPP project provide additional evidence for the engineering feasibility of the selected site. The proposed approach offers an effective decision-support tool for PSPP planning and clean energy development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

title: When static Volt–VAr control helps and when it does not: Operational and planning lessons from a weak radial distribution feeder
abstract: Long radial distribution feeders are increasingly exposed to sustained undervoltage as electrification-driven load growth outpaces reinforcement. Static inverter Volt–VAr curves are attractive because they can be deployed through existing controller settings, but standard curves may be too conservative for electrically weak feeders. This paper evaluates the operational and planning value of feeder-specific static Volt–VAr settings under data conditions commonly available to distribution system operators: sparse voltage measurements, hourly feeder-level inputs, and offline parameter updates. The study applies the slope-selection procedure developed in [1] to a predefined BESS Volt–VAr curve and evaluates the resulting setting through quasi-static time-series power flow for a real 22 kV radial feeder in Northern Norway. During the constructed 168 h high-load/no-generation stress period, the model-based, condition-matched comparison produced 153 h within the adopted target band with the full feeder-specific setting, compared with 8 h under the IEEE 1547-type setting and 1 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. An independent 2025 operating period was used for quantitative comparison with field measurements. The model reproduced the average voltage and voltage-band occupancy, while the disagreement in hourly variation limits its use to comparative screening rather than point-by-point prediction. The transferred feeder-specific setting produced 0 h outside the target band, compared with 16 h under the IEEE-type curve and 55 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. Higher-resolution measurements from the BESS and hydropower plant were used separately to examine interaction between the two local controllers. Under the 59% industrial-growth stress scenario, 4 MVAr was the smallest tested reactive-power rating that kept all 168 hourly voltages at or above the lower limit of the adopted target band after feeder-specific slope selection. The results provide a practical DSO screening procedure: test static tuning first, then identify whether the remaining limitation is curve setting, VAr headroom, or interaction between independently controlled assets. © 2026 The Authors

title: PC-TD3-based multi-objective adaptive dispatch method for microgrids guided by a meta-policy
abstract: To address the dynamic multi-objective trade-off between economic performance and system safety in microgrid operation, this study proposes a meta-policy-guided PC-TD3-based adaptive multi-objective scheduling method for microgrids. The method uses a high-level meta-policy network to generate scheduling preferences online, while a lower-level preference-conditioned TD3 policy is trained over the full preference space so that a single model can approximate continuous economy-safety trade-offs. A two-layer safety projection mechanism is further introduced to embed local battery constraints and global voltage constraints into action execution. Long-horizon simulations based on real-world data show that PC-TD3 achieves the lowest average daily operating cost among the compared methods, at 111,405 CNY, and the lowest average number of voltage violations, at 22.1 counts/day. Across 100 test days, the cumulative economic benefit of PC-TD3 relative to the average baseline reaches approximately 0.56 million CNY. Ablation experiments further show that full-preference-space training, dynamic preference generation, and safety projection jointly improve dispatch adaptability: the complete framework maintains stable voltage responses under both normal-load and high-load scenarios, whereas removing safety projection leads to voltage violations and single-preference training weakens SOC regulation under high-load conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can adaptively coordinate economic performance and operational safety under dynamic operating conditions, providing a practical reference for reinforcement-learning-based multi-objective microgrid dispatch. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. More broadly, physically modified cereal ingredients can be designed as functional phase-state regulators in frozen staple foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing DER hosting capacity of unbalanced low-voltage distribution networks with network exchangers: An Australian case study
abstract: The rapid growth and subsequent utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly in low-voltage networks, is pushing distribution networks to the brink of their hosting capacity. Distribution network operators, especially in DER-rich countries such as Australia, are exploring novel technologies and effective strategies to enhance DER integration while maintaining network integrity, as an alternative to costly network upgrades. One such technology developed and introduced is the network exchanger (NEx), which aims to enhance hosting capacity by regulating voltage, mitigating current imbalance, and power factor correction at the distribution transformer. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of NEx, compared with on-load tap changers and distribution static synchronous compensators, through an extensive simulation study that models projected growth in photovoltaic and electric vehicle penetration as per the Integrated System Plan released by the Australian Energy Market Operator, using a large-scale, real-world distribution network comprising over 8000 buses, and located in Queensland, Australia. Simulation results indicate breaches in network integrity under business-as-usual conditions in both step-change and progressive-change scenarios. The performance of each technology is benchmarked across six low-voltage networks that exhibit higher levels of network violations and photovoltaic curtailment, with NEx resolving all voltage breaches and reducing transformer loading and photovoltaic curtailment by noticeable amounts, which can aid in delaying costly network augmentation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Based on Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) for uncertainty quantification, a three-layer robust optimization model is formulated to maximize the uncertainty radius under a predefined power loss target. By incorporating the worst condition defined as minimized power generation coupled with maximized load, the original three-layer model is converted into a two-layer model for efficient solution. Furthermore, the Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm (RVEA) is employed to solve the model, obtaining a Pareto solution set that reflects the trade‑off between robustness and economy. Simulations based on the IEEE 33‑bus system demonstrate that ESS forms differentiated charging and discharging strategies for different operating scenarios, and the system exhibits higher sensitivity to wind power fluctuations. These results verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in identifying uncertainty impact pathways and optimizing ESS strategies. © 2026
