title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A study on the site selection of pumped storage power plants based on GIS and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Models: A case study of China
abstract: Pumped storage power plants (PSPPs) are essential for enhancing power system flexibility and supporting renewable energy integration. However, PSPP site selection involves complex spatial constraints and multi-dimensional trade-offs among technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. This study proposes a two-stage GIS–MCDM framework for PSPP site selection. First, GIS-based spatial screening with veto criteria is applied to identify feasible candidate sites. Subsequently, an integrated AHP–entropy weighting approach and TOPSIS method are employed for comprehensive evaluation, with VIKOR, TODIM, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation used to verify robustness. A case study in Guangxi, China identifies the optimal site among seven alternatives, and the results demonstrate the stability of the proposed framework under different weighting scenarios. Furthermore, theoretical energy storage assessment and comparison with an approved PSPP project provide additional evidence for the engineering feasibility of the selected site. The proposed approach offers an effective decision-support tool for PSPP planning and clean energy development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

title: When static Volt–VAr control helps and when it does not: Operational and planning lessons from a weak radial distribution feeder
abstract: Long radial distribution feeders are increasingly exposed to sustained undervoltage as electrification-driven load growth outpaces reinforcement. Static inverter Volt–VAr curves are attractive because they can be deployed through existing controller settings, but standard curves may be too conservative for electrically weak feeders. This paper evaluates the operational and planning value of feeder-specific static Volt–VAr settings under data conditions commonly available to distribution system operators: sparse voltage measurements, hourly feeder-level inputs, and offline parameter updates. The study applies the slope-selection procedure developed in [1] to a predefined BESS Volt–VAr curve and evaluates the resulting setting through quasi-static time-series power flow for a real 22 kV radial feeder in Northern Norway. During the constructed 168 h high-load/no-generation stress period, the model-based, condition-matched comparison produced 153 h within the adopted target band with the full feeder-specific setting, compared with 8 h under the IEEE 1547-type setting and 1 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. An independent 2025 operating period was used for quantitative comparison with field measurements. The model reproduced the average voltage and voltage-band occupancy, while the disagreement in hourly variation limits its use to comparative screening rather than point-by-point prediction. The transferred feeder-specific setting produced 0 h outside the target band, compared with 16 h under the IEEE-type curve and 55 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. Higher-resolution measurements from the BESS and hydropower plant were used separately to examine interaction between the two local controllers. Under the 59% industrial-growth stress scenario, 4 MVAr was the smallest tested reactive-power rating that kept all 168 hourly voltages at or above the lower limit of the adopted target band after feeder-specific slope selection. The results provide a practical DSO screening procedure: test static tuning first, then identify whether the remaining limitation is curve setting, VAr headroom, or interaction between independently controlled assets. © 2026 The Authors

title: PC-TD3-based multi-objective adaptive dispatch method for microgrids guided by a meta-policy
abstract: To address the dynamic multi-objective trade-off between economic performance and system safety in microgrid operation, this study proposes a meta-policy-guided PC-TD3-based adaptive multi-objective scheduling method for microgrids. The method uses a high-level meta-policy network to generate scheduling preferences online, while a lower-level preference-conditioned TD3 policy is trained over the full preference space so that a single model can approximate continuous economy-safety trade-offs. A two-layer safety projection mechanism is further introduced to embed local battery constraints and global voltage constraints into action execution. Long-horizon simulations based on real-world data show that PC-TD3 achieves the lowest average daily operating cost among the compared methods, at 111,405 CNY, and the lowest average number of voltage violations, at 22.1 counts/day. Across 100 test days, the cumulative economic benefit of PC-TD3 relative to the average baseline reaches approximately 0.56 million CNY. Ablation experiments further show that full-preference-space training, dynamic preference generation, and safety projection jointly improve dispatch adaptability: the complete framework maintains stable voltage responses under both normal-load and high-load scenarios, whereas removing safety projection leads to voltage violations and single-preference training weakens SOC regulation under high-load conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can adaptively coordinate economic performance and operational safety under dynamic operating conditions, providing a practical reference for reinforcement-learning-based multi-objective microgrid dispatch. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. More broadly, physically modified cereal ingredients can be designed as functional phase-state regulators in frozen staple foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing DER hosting capacity of unbalanced low-voltage distribution networks with network exchangers: An Australian case study
abstract: The rapid growth and subsequent utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly in low-voltage networks, is pushing distribution networks to the brink of their hosting capacity. Distribution network operators, especially in DER-rich countries such as Australia, are exploring novel technologies and effective strategies to enhance DER integration while maintaining network integrity, as an alternative to costly network upgrades. One such technology developed and introduced is the network exchanger (NEx), which aims to enhance hosting capacity by regulating voltage, mitigating current imbalance, and power factor correction at the distribution transformer. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of NEx, compared with on-load tap changers and distribution static synchronous compensators, through an extensive simulation study that models projected growth in photovoltaic and electric vehicle penetration as per the Integrated System Plan released by the Australian Energy Market Operator, using a large-scale, real-world distribution network comprising over 8000 buses, and located in Queensland, Australia. Simulation results indicate breaches in network integrity under business-as-usual conditions in both step-change and progressive-change scenarios. The performance of each technology is benchmarked across six low-voltage networks that exhibit higher levels of network violations and photovoltaic curtailment, with NEx resolving all voltage breaches and reducing transformer loading and photovoltaic curtailment by noticeable amounts, which can aid in delaying costly network augmentation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Based on Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) for uncertainty quantification, a three-layer robust optimization model is formulated to maximize the uncertainty radius under a predefined power loss target. By incorporating the worst condition defined as minimized power generation coupled with maximized load, the original three-layer model is converted into a two-layer model for efficient solution. Furthermore, the Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm (RVEA) is employed to solve the model, obtaining a Pareto solution set that reflects the trade‑off between robustness and economy. Simulations based on the IEEE 33‑bus system demonstrate that ESS forms differentiated charging and discharging strategies for different operating scenarios, and the system exhibits higher sensitivity to wind power fluctuations. These results verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in identifying uncertainty impact pathways and optimizing ESS strategies. © 2026

title: Hand clearances in ergonomic design: A scoping review of types, methods, and measurements
abstract: Hand clearances, the space available for hand access and operation, are essential for manual workspace design. However, clearance types lack systematic characterization, unified methods, and standardized criteria for defining adequate space during manual tasks. This scoping review analyzed 26 records published between 1960 and 2026. Ninety-four unique clearances were identified and organized into four categories: Openings, Operational Clearances, Object-Specific Clearances, and PPE Allowances. Four methodological approaches and eight methodological gaps were identified, including reliance on static measurements, inadequate treatment of PPE, small or outdated samples, and limited reporting standards. Widely cited clearance values originate from small, demographically narrow 1960s studies and have propagated with limited re-validation. The review introduces the functional clearance margin as a conceptual proposition describing the additional space beyond hand dimensions required for functional operation rather than fit alone. These findings provide a foundation for developing more representative, dynamic, and standardized approaches to hand clearance design. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modeling the propagation of risk in large-scale power outages: Integrating ETA, directed-weighted CN, and risk chain mining
abstract: To understand the systemic propagation and interdependencies of various risk factors in large-scale power outages, a novel risk evolution framework is proposed, incorporating Event Tree Analysis (ETA), directed-weighted Complex Network (CN), and risk chain mining. A network comprising 37 nodes and 130 edges is constructed using data from 29 large-scale power outages spanning from 1965 to 2025. Topological analysis identifies critical propagation nodes, including power plant failures and grid instability. Robustness tests reveal the network's resilience to random disruptions but also expose its vulnerability to targeted attacks. Furthermore, high-risk causal chains are directly extracted and classified from the network, and path mining further uncovers 24 high-risk six-node chains, which are categorized into four distinct propagation patterns. This integrated framework offers a data-driven methodology for characterizing large-scale power outage risks, yielding structurally suggestive priorities to inform prevention and mitigation strategies for power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Non-covalent interactions between pectin and volatiles modulate flavor formation in goji berry (Lycium barbarum L.) during pulsed vacuum drying
abstract: Pectin plays a crucial role in modulating the flavor attributes of goji berry. This study investigated dynamic variations of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), non-volatile organic compounds (NVOCs), and pectin fractions, as well as their interactions in goji berry during pulsed vacuum drying (PVD), focusing on the chelator-soluble pectin (CSP) fraction. The results showed that 121 differential VOCs (DVOCs) were identified throughout the PVD process. The transition from stage III to V, during which rapid moisture migration occurred, was determined as the critical period for flavor formation. NVOCs involving soluble sugars, organic acids and amino acids affected VOC profiles. CSP exhibited substantial nanostructural rearrangement and interconnected network reconstruction, showing strong negative correlations with key aroma-active compounds such as acetic acid and octanal. It was further revealed that CSP interacted with acetic acid predominantly through hydrogen bonding, while octanal binding likely involved both hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding. These non-covalent interactions inhibited pectin aggregation, reduced particle size, and promoted the formation of stable porous fibrous microstructure that may facilitate flavor retention. Therefore, these findings indicate that pectin regulates flavor formation during PVD not only through structural transformation but also via non-covalent interactions with VOCs. This study provides theoretical basis for clarifying flavor-formation mechanisms of goji berry during PVD processing. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: High-thermal-conductivity GFRP for dry-type air-core reactors: thermal-electrical performance and trade-off analysis
abstract: Dry-type air-core reactors suffer from localized overheating due to the limited thermal conductivity of conventional glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) insulation. Enhancing the thermal conductivity of GFRP provides a potential approach for improving reactor heat dissipation; however, excessive incorporation of thermally conductive fillers may compromise electrical insulation reliability. This study establishes an integrated material-to-equipment evaluation framework to investigate the thermal-electrical trade-off of high-thermal-conductivity GFRP (HTC-GFRP) for dry-type air-core reactors. HTC-GFRP samples with different alumina contents were prepared, and their thermal conductivity, dielectric properties, AC flashover voltage, and breakdown strength were experimentally characterized. The results demonstrate that increasing alumina loading effectively enhances thermal conductivity by promoting the formation of thermally conductive pathways, whereas excessive filler incorporation leads to deterioration of insulation performance. Considering both thermal enhancement and electrical insulation reliability, a favorable thermal conductivity range of approximately 0.75–0.95 W/(m·K) was identified. Furthermore, multiphysics simulations of a 10 kV dry-type air-core reactor reveal that increasing the GFRP thermal conductivity from 0.35 to 1.3 W/(m·K) reduces the maximum operating temperature by approximately 3 °C. These results demonstrate the thermal-electrical trade-off of HTC-GFRP and provide quantitative guidance for balancing heat dissipation capability and insulation reliability in dry-type air-core reactors. © 2026

title: Activating slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 on CeO2 with concentrated sunlight to enable ethylene and propylene synthesis
abstract: Harnessing solar light to convert CO2 and H2O into multi-carbon (C2+) fuels constitutes a critical strategy toward achieving carbon neutrality. This necessitates the development of photocatalytic systems and catalysts capable of breaking the linear activity-selectivity trade-off, which ultimately rests on a fundamental understanding of the key factors controlling C1–Cn (n ≥ 2) coupling selectivity. Herein, with CeO2 and Pr6O11 selected as model catalysts, we clarify that the decisive factor governing C2+ production is interfacial CO2 adsorption strength/coverage, rather than interfacial photogenerated charge carrier density or H2O dissociation/adsorption. Therefore, a solar‑concentrating photocatalytic system was designed to activate slightly stronger adsorbed CO2 with high local coverage, ultimately achieving substantial generation of C2+ products by a *CO–free formaldehyde self–condensation pathway, whereas almost no multi‑carbon products were observed under conventional photocatalytic reaction systems. Intriguingly, within this system, CeO2, despite its inferior photoelectric response and H2O activation capability compared to Pr6O11 and the Pr6O11/CeO2 composite, delivered the highest C2+ yield and molar selectivity. Over 56 h, it produced 109.69 μmol of C2H4 (19.79%) and 31.0 μmol of C3H6 (5.59%). These findings establish that, in concentrated solar light catalytic systems, the formation of C1–Cn bonds is closely related to interfacial CO2 adsorption behavior, and that slightly stronger CO2 adsorption strength is clearly beneficial for the generation of C2+ products. This insight advocates a new design paradigm under concentrated solar catalytic systems, focused on modulating CO2 adsorption strength/coverage rather than that of the *CO intermediate, moving beyond the traditional practice of avoiding either strong or weak binding. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Ghost-ResDSCNet:lightweight residual depthwise separable convolution with spatial pyramid pooling for power quality disturbance classification
abstract: The increasing complexity of power quality disturbances (PQDs) calls for lightweight yet accurate classification methods suitable for edge deployment. This paper proposes Ghost-ResDSCNet, a multi-scale deep network that first converts voltage signals into time–frequency spectrograms via short-time Fourier transform. A residual depthwise separable convolution backbone performs efficient feature extraction, Ghost modules reduce computational cost by cheap feature generation, and a spatial pyramid pooling module captures multi-scale contextual information. On a 21-class synthetic PQD dataset, Ghost-ResDSCNet achieves an average accuracy of 99.34% on clean signals, along with 99.26%, 99.11%, and 95.80% under 40 dB, 30 dB, and 20 dB SNR respectively, with only 0.12M parameters, outperforming MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet. On a real-world five-class dataset, it attains 100.00% accuracy on clean and 40dB signals, and 99.96% and 94.02% under 30dB and 20dB SNR. Grad-CAM++ visualization confirms that the model focuses on physically interpretable time–frequency regions. title: Spatial analysis of the 15-minute city concept in three historically distinct urban areas across metropolitan greater Cairo
abstract: This paper explores how the 15-min city concept plays out in Greater Cairo by examining three neighbourhoods: Agouza, Madinaty, and Badya. To do so, it draws on a systematic approach that includes selecting case studies, identifying key service categories, extracting POI and street-network data, mapping service areas in ArcGIS, and presenting the results through service area analysis and thematic mapping. To complement this, accessibility was assessed through four measures: cumulative opportunities, land-use entropy, functional redundancy, and space syntax (integration) metrics. The findings show that access in Cairo depends not just on distance but also on the diversity of available services, the degree of proximity between services, and the way streets connect different areas. Cycling makes a clear difference in widening reach and reducing accessibility inequalities and fragmentation. The findings suggest that, in addition to clinics and schools, social anchors such as souqs, ahwa, and cultural places emerge as vital parts of daily urban life. The paper argues that in Cairo, the 15-min city concept, whether built from scratch or adapted to existing urban fabrics, should not be treated as a universal recipe but as a flexible framework. The concept is part of a longer lineage of planning ideals, adopted in the planning of several areas of Cairo, from the Garden City movement to New Urbanism. It should build on the city’s own urban vocabularies, shaped through layered urban planning and lived experiences, which continue to define how urban spaces and services are used and valued within the 15-min radius or beyond. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Adaptive ADMM-based optimal power flow for distribution systems via dynamic penalty strategy
abstract: To mitigate voltage fluctuations caused by intermittent distributed generation (DG), this paper proposes a reactive power optimization strategy based on an Improved Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (I-ADMM). The model coordinates switchable capacitor banks (SCBs), on-load tap changers (OLTCs), and the reactive power capabilities of DGs to balance voltage quality and active power losses. Simulation results on the IEEE 33-bus system show that the proposed I-ADMM reduces total voltage deviation by 18.71% and 25.94%, and decreases branch losses by 9.51% and 10.67% compared with T-ADMM and C-OPF, respectively. In addition, a multi-period validation under time-varying DG and load conditions shows that the proposed method maintains effective performance across representative operating periods while preserving voltage security. Additional validation on a modified IEEE 69-bus system further confirms the scalability of the proposed method. These results demonstrate improved computational efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive penalty strategy for distributed OPF under representative time-varying operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5. ©2027 The author(s). title: Enhancement of power system steady-state stability through allocation of quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization algorithm-based multiple D-STATCOM Units
abstract: Modern distribution networks suffer from power losses and voltage instability under various loading conditions. Mitigating these operational issues requires optimal allocation of custom power devices, such as Distribution Static Compensators (D-STATCOMs). To address this challenge, this study develops a quantum-inspired grey wolf optimization (QGWO) algorithm for allocating D-STATCOMs to ensure steady-state stability, improve bus voltage profiles, and reduce power losses. Distinct from existing variants, QGWO models search agents as probabilistic quantum state vectors, utilizing a fitness-driven amplitude scaling and dynamic phase angle adaptation. Using the backward-forward sweep (BFS) load-flow method, the performance is evaluated across base-load, load-increment, and single-phase fault scenarios on practical 44- and IEEE 69-bus test systems. The voltage stability margin (VSM) is utilized to determine maximum loading factors. For the 44-bus system, buses 22, 29, and 41 with capacities of 637.69 kVAR, 503.75 kVAR, and 351.01 kVAR are found as the optimal locations and sizes. With these units, power losses are reduced by 50.894% under the base-load scenario. For the IEEE 69-bus system, buses 11, 17 and 61 with capacities of 358.69kVAR, 254.02kVAR and 1206.75kVAR reduce power losses by 42.76% under the base-load scenario. Using VSM, the maximum loading factor is found as 1.53 and 2.65 for 44- and 69-bus systems. Statistically, the proposed QGWO achieves the lowest mean power loss, with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests confirming its advantage over PSO, APSO, GWO, and CGWO. Weight sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the optimal solution remains invariant to changes in objective-function weights. Economically, cost-benefit sensitivity analyses confirm the financial viability of the project. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS frequency regulation and SoC management
abstract: This paper proposes a severity-based adaptive control strategy for BESS-based primary frequency regulation (PFR) and state-of-charge (SoC) management. Conventional adaptive droop controllers commonly use decoupled gain structures, fixed nonlinear curves, or multi-parameter logistic functions, which complicate tuning and may increase unnecessary battery cycling. The proposed controller introduces a unified Δf–SoC map in which a single concavity parameter β shapes the frequency-severity response. A multiplicative SoC weighting function enforces dynamic participation limits, while a hybrid β-adaptation mechanism distinguishes sustained volatility from high-RoCoF events. A frequency-gated restoration loop is added to recover SoC without interfering with critical frequency support. The controller is evaluated through SFR-model simulations and IEEE 9-bus multi-machine studies, supported by sensitivity analysis, stability verification, and battery degradation assessment. Results show that the proposed method provides a balanced trade-off between frequency regulation and battery utilization. In the continuous stochastic case, it reduces BESS energy throughput and total degradation damage compared with the benchmark controllers. In the severe IEEE 9-bus step disturbance, it achieves the lowest RMS frequency deviation and maximum deviation among the tested methods. These results confirm that the proposed strategy improves large-disturbance frequency support while preserving battery lifetime and maintaining stable operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Congestion management in electric distribution systems through flexibility services: a bibliometric and analytical review
abstract: Electricity systems are rapidly evolving toward decentralized architectures with high shares of variable renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources (DERs), increasing congestion in medium- and low-voltage networks. This paper presents a structured mixed-source review combining bibliometric mapping and targeted analytical synthesis on flexibility services for congestion management in electric distribution systems. Analysis of the quality-controlled Q3 corpus (n = 1827) identifies China as the leading national contributor and substantial collective European participation, with 79.6% of records published from 2018 onward. Author-keyword mapping reveals five streams: distribution-network optimization, market-based congestion management, uncertainty-aware active-network operation, flexibility-service coordination, and demand-response smart-grid control. Novelty lies in keeping the validated bibliometric corpus separate from an independently assembled, question-driven evidence base until interpretation. The analytical synthesis shows that distributed locational marginal pricing (DLMP), particularly in iterative formulations, can internalize network constraints and provide locational signals for DER coordination, although its effectiveness depends on adequate network modeling, uncertainty treatment, and flexible-demand participation. The review also identifies converging trends toward multilayer coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs), local flexibility procurement, and digital platforms for ancillary-service provision. Across jurisdictions, explicit remuneration, interoperable data, and coordinated governance recur, but uneven implementation precludes causal comparisons or effectiveness rankings. The paper concludes by identifying research gaps related to cost–benefit validation, regulatory standardization, data interoperability, and large-scale implementation in distribution systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Energy management systems for hybrid AC/DC microgrids: a problem-oriented review of system challenges and control architectures
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources introduces several system-level challenges for hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs), including power coordination, voltage regulation, uncertainty management, load–demand balancing, and energy storage coordination. Energy management systems (EMS) play a key role in addressing these challenges and ensuring reliable and efficient MG operation. Existing review studies mainly focus on methods and optimization techniques, while system challenges are not always clearly identified or examined from a structured perspective. This paper reviews studies that support system design and the mitigation of operational challenges and presents a comprehensive classification of MGs and EMS. Review and research studies are compiled in separate tables and categorized according to system challenges and the applied EMS approaches. System challenges are identified and related to the control layers responsible for addressing them across primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The proposed classification explicitly covers rule-based, method-based, and objective-based EMS strategies and presents a multi-dimensional framework that links system challenges, control structures, and energy management approaches. The resulting framework provides a consolidated and problem-oriented perspective and supports future research toward the development and evaluation of effective energy management solutions for hybrid AC/DC MGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Emotional preferences in LoRA-driven AI-generated urban vitality spaces: A study using discrete choice models
abstract: China's transition toward urban stock renewal has heightened the focus on the emotional quality of urban vitality spaces. While AI generative design offers new approaches, whether AI-generated images as visual representations for specific spaces can meet people's emotional needs remains insufficiently examined. This study examines whether AI-generated visual representations of such spaces evoke image-based emotional preferences comparable to those for real photographs, and identifies which spatial attributes drive these preferences. Using THE BOX in Beijing as a case, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models generated visual representations of seven chosen scenes. Emotional preferences were measured through validated scales completed by 115 participants. A discrete choice model was used to compare participants' preferences between photographs of the real space and AI-generated images and identified influential attributes. Results showed that participants with design-related backgrounds preferred real photographs. Positive affect toward AI-generated images was the strongest predictor of preference. Real-scene color, natural elements, and uniqueness reduced the odds of choosing AI-generated versions, whereas AI-generated form and structure, natural elements, and changeability increased them. The study contributes a replicable workflow linking generative AI with emotional preference measurement, offering a structured approach for evidence-based design review. The findings are preliminary due to the single case, modest sample, and reliance on static images. Future work should extend to diverse urban contexts and multimodal evaluation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. By leveraging large language models to quantify complex external influences and semantic relationships, this framework provides a new perspective for improving the accuracy and interpretability of tourism flow forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A tri-objective goal programming approach to generator maintenance scheduling
abstract: The generator maintenance scheduling problem is a key decision-making task in power system planning, requiring schedules that ensure reliability while controlling operational costs. Motivated by reliability challenges and financial constraints in systems such as South Africa's, this paper proposes a tri-objective optimisation framework that simultaneously minimises generator failure probability, production cost, and reserve margin. The model is formulated using goal programming to balance these competing objectives and is solved using simulated annealing and constraint programming. It is evaluated on the IEEE reliability test system and a large-scale Eskom-inspired system with 157 generating units. The results characterise trade-offs among reliability, cost, and reserve margin objectives, approximate a Pareto frontier, and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a decision-support tool for practical generator maintenance planning. © 2026 The Authors

title: Analysis of retail resilience in Seoul's neighborhood commercial districts Amidst the COVID-19 shock
abstract: This study examines the economic resilience of neighborhood commercial districts in Seoul in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Moving beyond static before–after comparisons, we employ a Panel Interrupted Time Series (Panel ITS) design to separately identify (i) the immediate level shift at the onset of the shock, conceptualized as resistance, and (ii) the subsequent change in the growth trajectory as conditions transitioned toward the endemic phase, conceptualized as recoverability. The results show that structural diversity, operationalized via Shannon's entropy, functions as a key buffering mechanism: it attenuates initial revenue losses and is associated with a steeper post-shock recovery trend. Importantly, we also document pronounced spatial heterogeneity across Seoul's five major sub-markets. Central business districts exhibit heightened exposure and larger initial downturns, while recovery trajectories vary across sub-markets. Taken together, these findings imply that urban management should complement place-based physical upgrading with ecosystem-oriented strategies—specifically, “portfolio diversification” approaches that strengthen sectoral complexity and reduce systemic vulnerability within local commercial ecosystems. © 2026 The Authors.

title: When AI ads violate expectations: the interplay of AI character, product type, and advertising appeal of AI ads on consumer attitudes
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping video advertising production. Using expectancy violations theory as an interpretive lens, this study develops a framework in which ad appeal (rational vs. emotional), product type (high-tech vs. low-tech), and AI character embodiment (no character vs. animal-like vs. human-like) jointly relate to ad attitude and to two appraisals: perceived novelty and perceived uncanniness. This study tests the framework in five between-subjects experiments with consumers recruited from an online panel. Results show that rational appeals outperform emotional appeals in AI-generated ads, especially for low-tech products. Novelty is positively and uncanniness negatively associated with ad attitude, and the indirect effects through both appraisals are consistent with the proposed process. Human-like AI characters amplify uncanniness in emotional low-tech executions. In one rational low-tech execution, an animal-like character lowered uncanniness relative to a no-character baseline, but ad attitude did not differ significantly. The findings extend expectancy-violation theorizing in AI advertising and offer configuration-level design guidance for brands deploying disclosed AI-generated advertising. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Layered Defect-Filling co-Assembled Carbazole-Based SAMs Deliver 20% Organic Solar Cells and 17% Mini-Modules
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-transport layers (HTLs) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet conventional single-component SAMs often form quasi-monolayers with incomplete coverage and interfacial defects that become increasingly detrimental upon device scaling. Here, we develop a co-assembled multilayered SAM (coSAMu) strategy that combines two SAM molecules, 2PACz and 2Cl-4PACz, with distinct dipoles and steric configurations through blend casting and sequential casting. Photoelectron spectroscopy, X-ray analysis, and molecular simulations support a layered structure in which a chemisorbed, 2PACz-rich bottom layer primarily sets the indium tin oxide (ITO) work function, while a 2Cl-4PACz-rich upper layer fills interfacial voids, improves molecular packing, and passivates defects. Consistent with this picture, coSAMu promotes a more favorable vertical composition near the ITO surface and suppresses trap-assisted recombination, enabling more efficient charge extraction and collection. Consequently, a representative D18:L8-BO OSC incorporating the sequential-cast coSAMu HTL achieves a power conversion efficiency of 20.1% (0.042 cm2), outperforming pristine 2PACz. Importantly, when scaled to a 17.14 cm2 mini-module (six serially connected subcells), coSAMu delivers 17.0% efficiency versus 12.2% for the 2PACz control. This work demonstrates controlled multilayer co-assembly as an effective strategy for scalable OSC interface engineering that is broadly applicable to multiple donor–acceptor systems. title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: High-Conductivity and Moisture-Tolerant Sulfide Electrolyte Enabled by Bifunctional Coating for Practical All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
abstract: The pursuit of safer and higher-energy-density batteries has driven the advancement of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Among various material systems, sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SEs) stand out as highly promising candidates owing to their exceptional ionic conductivity. Nevertheless, their extreme sensitivity to moisture results in the release of toxic H2S and rapid structural degradation, which severely impedes their scalable manufacturing under ambient conditions. A bifunctional (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) coating strategy is herein presented to shield Li5.5PS4.5Cl0.8Br0.7 (LPSCBr) from moisture-induced degradation. The MPTMS layer forms a hydrophobic barrier of approximately 10 nm, which reduces H2S emission by 93.0% after 35 min of exposure to 30% relative humidity, while maintaining 83.1% of the initial ionic conductivity (10.8 mS cm−1). This approach tackles the core challenge associated with sulfide solid-state electrolytes: the realization of compatibility with controlled ambient air without sacrificing critical electrochemical properties. The modified electrolyte maintains a high ionic conductivity (> 5.7 mS cm−1) even after 10 h of air exposure. When applied in all-solid-state cells paired with LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.06O2 cathodes, it exhibits remarkable electrochemical performance, delivering a capacity retention of 84.6% after 1000 cycles. By enabling moisture-tolerant processing, MPTMS-modified LPSCBr SEs lay a solid foundation for the scalable, high-performance, and cost-effective production of ASSLBs. title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
abstract: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, legality, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints. © 2027 The author(s). title: Empirical Stage-Damage Functions for SME Content Losses in Australian Flood Vulnerability Assessment
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) dominate Australian business activity, yet empirically calibrated functions for nonresidential flood-related contents losses remain limited. Postevent surveys of 185 SMEs across 12 business types and 14 towns affected by the February-April 2022 Northern Rivers floods were used to derive stage-damage functions for stock, equipment, and fit-out. Contents-specific damage indices combined peak internal flood depth (0-6 m, relative to finished-floor level) with self-reported losses and preevent replacement values. Pooled curves were fitted using LOESS and a beta-family generalized additive model (Beta-GAM); a hierarchical Beta-GAM (HBGAM) generated business-type functions under partial pooling, while random forest and XGBoost provided depth-only predictive benchmarks. Across the pooled models, performance on the corresponding within-event 25% holdout sets was moderate (R2=0.57-0.69; RMSE=0.23-0.27), and neither machine-learning benchmark consistently improved performance. The Beta-GAM was retained because it provided smooth, bounded, interpretable relationships, model-based and bootstrap uncertainty intervals, and extractable threshold depths. The fitted mean damage index reached 0.50 at 1.03 m for stock, 1.09 m for equipment, and 1.27 m for fit-out, with uncertainty generally increasing above 3 m as data density declined. HBGAM-derived D50 values ranged from 0.66 to 1.18 m for stock, 0.81 to 1.18 m for equipment, and 1.09 to 1.48 m for fit-out, indicating model-derived sector variation. These event-calibrated functions support screening-level relative SME contents-loss assessment and evaluation of loss-reduction options in comparable settings; application elsewhere requires external validation or local recalibration. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. title: Not alone: How group photos enhance audience responses to virtual influencers
abstract: Although marketers increasingly use virtual influencers to engage consumers, concerns about authenticity continue to limit their effectiveness. This research examines whether group photos can make virtual influencers appear more socially connected and authentic, thereby improving audience responses. We propose that, compared with no-person images or solo photos, group photos provide visual social cues that place virtual influencers in recognizable interpersonal contexts and make them appear more socially connected in shared experiences. Across one large-scale field study and two experiments, we test this proposition. Study 1 draws on a large-scale Instagram dataset of 17,878 posts from 109 virtual influencers collected between 2023 and 2026, with the main analyses based on 8558 non-video posts and finds that group photos receive higher post engagement than no-person images and solo photos. Study 2 provides controlled experimental evidence consistent with this effect and suggests that perceived social connectedness and perceived authenticity sequentially account for the relationship between group photos and favorable post evaluations. Study 3 identifies virtual influencer type as an important boundary condition: group photos are more effective for human-like virtual influencers, whereas this advantage weakens for cartoon-like virtual influencers. These findings contribute to research on virtual influencer humanization and authenticity by showing that visual social connectedness can make virtual influencers appear more socially embedded, more authentic, and more favorably evaluated. The results also offer actionable insights for marketers and content creators seeking to design virtual influencer content that elicits more favorable audience responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Breaking the Specific Capacity Limit: 409% Boost in Manganese-Based Redox Flow Batteries at High Current Densities with a MnO2Semi-Solid Slurry Electrolyte
abstract: The common-ion effect of SO42− limits the solubility of MnSO4 to ≤ 1 M in conventional H2SO4 electrolytes, resulting in low specific capacity of manganese (Mn)-based redox flow batteries (RFBs). Although MnO2 semi-solid RFBs are expected to improve the specific capacity, the sluggish electrochemical reaction kinetics leads to low operating current densities (≤ 1 mA cm−2). Herein, we employ a reverse-design strategy by introducing additional high-concentration MnO2 into the conventional Mn-based electrolyte. Leveraging the MnO2/Mn2+ electrochemical reaction successfully circumvents the common-ion effect, raising the concentration of soluble Mn species in the electrolyte to 3.76 M and achieving a specific capacity of 156.2 Ah LCatholyte-1 —a 409% increment over reported MnSO4-based electrolytes. Subsequently, the reverse disproportionation of electrolytic MnO2 generated during the second charging cycle shifts the redox mechanism from the MnO2(s)/Mn2+ couple to the solution-phase Mn3+(aq)/Mn2+ pair. This transformation not only elevates the discharge voltage but also enables stable operation at 30 mA cm−2, representing a current density 30-fold higher than reported Mn-based semi-solid RFBs. This work demonstrates a rational design strategy for semi-solid slurry electrolytes to enhance the specific capacity of RFBs, thereby advancing their applicability in grid-scale renewable energy storage.
