title: Wastewater heat recovery systems for sustainable building energy efficiency and decarbonization: A comprehensive review with practical insights
abstract: Growing energy demand and carbon emissions pose a major challenge to the building environment, particularly in addressing heating and cooling needs sustainably. In this context, wastewater is recognized as an unconventional and largely untapped thermal energy resource due to its consistent supply and generally stable temperature. Wastewater heat recovery has the potential to significantly improve building energy efficiency and boost decarbonization efforts. This review provides a comprehensive and system-level assessment of wastewater heat recovery technologies for building- and district-scale applications, with particular emphasis on heat extraction locations, heat exchanger configurations, and wastewater source heat pump systems. Rather than treating individual components in isolation, the study integrates heat exchanger and heat pump technologies within a unified framework to support practical design and implementation decisions. State-of-the-art literature covering wastewater characteristics, recovery locations, heat exchanger technologies, and combined wastewater heat exchanger-heat pump systems is critically analyzed through comparative evaluation of performance indicators, benefits, and limitations. Key recovery locations, including building outlets, sewer networks, and wastewater treatment plants are examined in terms of thermal potential, operational constraints, and system compatibility. The review highlights that appropriately selected heat exchangers and wastewater source heat pump configurations can significantly improve energy recovery efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Finally, practical recommendations are provided to guide the selection, installation, and integration of wastewater heat recovery systems, identifying fouling control, system optimization, and data-driven design as critical factors for advancing wastewater as a viable unconventional thermal energy resource in modern building energy systems. © 2026 The Authors. title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 208 students enrolled in entrepreneurship-related courses at a Spanish public university, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that DTCT is a strong positive predictor of IEO; Type I intellectual styles are positively related to both DTCT and IEO, whereas Type II styles display negative relations with entrepreneurial orientation. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. The study argues that entrepreneurship courses should explicitly treat DTCT and IEO as learning outcomes and intentionally adapt tasks, scaffolding, and assessment to diverse intellectual style profiles in order to support more inclusive and opportunity-oriented entrepreneurial learning. © 2026 The Authors

title: Brand stereotypes, information processing, and consumer acceptance of Chinese automobiles: The moderating roles of perceived brand globalness and brand credibility in an emerging market
abstract: Stereotypes about Chinese products persist in many developing economies, even as Chinese manufacturers have substantially upgraded their technological capabilities and product quality. However, the cognitive pathways linking systematic and heuristic information processing to consumers’ stereotype-based perceptions of brand warmth and competence remain underexplored in the evaluation of high-involvement foreign products. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, stereotype content model, and signaling theory, this study develops and tests a process-based framework explaining how information processing routes shape stereotype-based brand perceptions, which in turn influence product evaluations and purchase intentions toward Chinese automobiles in Vietnam. A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. A qualitative phase with 20 in-depth interviews was conducted to explore consumers' cognitive processes and refine the theoretical framework. Subsequently, survey data from 638 Vietnamese consumers were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings demonstrate that systematic information processing strengthens perceived brand competence and warmth, whereas heuristic processing weakens both dimensions, thereby reinforcing brand stereotypes. Perceived brand competence and warmth enhance product receptivity, judgment, and quality, which collectively drive purchase intention. Perceived brand globalness weakens the negative effects of heuristic information processing and amplifies the positive effects of systematic information processing on stereotype-related perceptions. Brand credibility strengthens the conversion of product-level evaluations into purchase intention. Theoretically, this study integrates HSM, SCM, and ST to clarify the sequential relationships linking information processing, stereotype-based brand perception, product evaluation, and purchase intention. Practically, the findings offer actionable guidance for Chinese automobile brands seeking to attenuate legacy stereotypes and build consumer acceptance in culturally resistant emerging markets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. This model offers a decision-support framework for assessing long-term fisheries management strategies. © 2027 The author(s). title: How certification credibility and benefit framing shape heterogeneous consumer responses to sustainable products in e-commerce
abstract: On e-commerce platforms, sustainable products succeed or fail on a compressed product page where certification logos, benefit descriptions, and platform trust cues compete for attention. Retailers treat these cues as interchangeable signals, yet they address two different questions: can the product be trusted, and is it right for me? Signalling theory answers the first through costly, verifiable certification; goal-framing theory answers the second through benefit claims activating competing motivations. Whether they operate as one mechanism or two remains unresolved in retailing research. Using a discrete choice experiment with 477 Chinese consumers analysed through aggregate conditional logit, latent class analysis, and trust-stratified models, we show they are separable strategic levers. The certification credibility hierarchy (dual and international premiums above the domestic schemes) holds broadly across all three motivational segments, whereas benefit-framing valuation differs sharply between them, and this segment-level dissociation is the evidence for their separability. Platform trust does not significantly moderate certification premiums. Latent class analysis reveals a dual-motivated majority (53.5 per cent) that stated self-classification systematically understates, making choice-derived rather than self-reported segmentation essential for targeting. Extending goal-framing theory, the study's central contribution shows certification quality as a novel external cue: superior certification shifts dual-motivated consumers' default health preference toward environmental framing, narrowing it to near-parity, with a ¥16.68 break-even threshold at which the two framings reach indifference. These findings show heterogeneous consumer response is structured by the interaction between signal architecture and motivational composition, with implications for certification investment, benefit communication, and segmentation in sustainable retailing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. This paper presents “Leading in the Age of AI”, a card-based serious game in which student teams assume asymmetric C-suite roles, make AI deployment decisions under constraints, and document their reasoning in Model Cards adapted from AI documentation practice. Conceptually, the paper frames AI governance education as accountable decision-making under uncertainty: students negotiate competing priorities, allocate scarce safeguards, respond to disruption, and prepare written accounts for scrutiny. The paper contributes a reusable game design, a pedagogical adaptation of Model Cards as justification artefacts, and design patterns for management-education contexts involving accountable decisions under uncertainty. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Students evaluated the activity positively and reported immediate confidence gains across knowledge, ethics, and governance composites (dz=0.44 to 1.00), while quiz gains were modest and not statistically significant. Model Card analysis suggests the activity generated inspectable governance reasoning, while leaving causal learning, retention, and transfer for future research. © 2026 The Author

title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Child-level analyses indicated a statistically significant improvement in overall DT competence favoring the intervention group (Cohen’s d=0.38). However, gains were uneven across specific DT dimensions. Children showed more apparent gains in Empathize, Define, and Prototype, whereas no significant gains were observed in Ideate and Test. Furthermore, the youngest children appeared to show larger gains, whereas gender did not significantly moderate the intervention effects. Qualitative interviews provided insight into the cognitive processes underlying these developmental variations. Together, these preliminary findings may inform DT education research and practice in early childhood settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Results confirm that biospheric values significantly shape awareness of environmental consequences, moral responsibility, and personal norms, which in turn directly influence behavioral intention. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. This research extends theoretical understanding by linking ethical and volitional determinants of sustainable consumption and offers managerial insights for airlines and policymakers to design effective carbon offset communication, education, and engagement strategies. title: How social media content shapes enrollment intention: Distinguishing firm-generated and user-generated effects through TPB and self-identity
abstract: The increasing reliance on social media has transformed how prospective students gather and evaluate information when selecting universities. This study examines how firm-generated content (FGC) and user-generated content (UGC) influence students' behavioral intention to enroll in private universities through psychological mechanisms grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and self-identity. Specifically, the study investigates both direct and indirect effects of FGC and UGC on behavioral intention, mediated by attitude toward behavior, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and self-identity. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed, with data collected from 295 final-year high school students in Banten, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that FGC has a significant direct and indirect effect on behavioral intention, whereas UGC does not have a significant direct effect but appears to operate primarily through indirect pathways. Among the mediators, subjective norms emerge as the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, followed by attitude toward behavior and self-identity. In contrast, perceived behavioral control does not significantly influence behavioral intention. The findings suggest that FGC and UGC function through distinct mechanisms. While institutional content can directly shape behavioral intention, user-generated content primarily influences intention through social and psychological processes. These results highlight that the effectiveness of social media communication depends not only on information exposure but also on how information is cognitively evaluated, socially validated, and integrated into individuals' self-concept. This study contributes to the literature by distinguishing between different types of social media content and extending the TPB framework with self-identity in the context of higher education decision-making. The findings provide insights for understanding how digital communication influences complex behavioral decisions in contemporary educational environments. © 2027 Malque Publishing, .

title: Dynamic regulation of β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrillation by hydroxytyrosol: Structural and functional insights
abstract: β-lactoglobulin amyloid fibrils (LGF) are promising emulsion stabilizers, while their limited antioxidant activity restricts wide applications. In this study, hydroxytyrosol (HT) was introduced at different stages of β-lactoglobulin (LG) fibrillation to investigate its effects on fibril structure and emulsifying function. HT introduced at the initial stage inhibited nucleation and β-sheet accumulation, while HT at the end of the lag phase interfered with fibril elongation, producing shortened fibrils. HT added at the end of the growth phase remodeled complexes structure, preserving the typical fibrillar architecture. Moreover, the LGF-HT complex prepared with 100 μM HT at the end of the growth phase (LGF8-HT100) showed the best emulsifying performance (EAI: 14.28 m2/g; ESI: 71.36%), and enhanced the resistance of LGF-stabilized emulsions to lipid oxidation, decreasing TBARS value from 68.03 μM to 28.74 μM. LGF8-HT100 stabilized emulsions also exhibited the highest interfacial protein adsorption percentage, and reduced intestinal FFA release from 75.67% to 62.04%, indicating enhanced resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. Accordingly, surface hydrophobicity analysis showed that HT intervention at this stage retained a higher H0, indicating that the hydrophobic driving force stabilizing the fibrillar structure was largely preserved. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that HT formed stable hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions within a buried LG pocket, and engaged a distinct surface groove on the LGF core. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms by which HT regulates protein fibrillation and lay a theoretical foundation for the design of LGF-based emulsion stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant capacity and stability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: From brand hate to behavioral response: A recourse-contingent exit-voice-loyalty-neglect framework for digital consumer markets
abstract: Three decades of brand hate research have mapped what triggers consumer hate and catalogued how hateful consumers respond, avoiding, switching, complaining, retaliating, subverting, without connecting these two halves through one behavioral logic. This paper closes that gap by importing the Exit-Voice-Loyalty-Neglect (EVLN) framework into the brand hate domain and extending it with a boundary condition the literature has ignored: structural recourse availability. Brand hate's dimensional profile, whether anger, contempt, aversion, or fear dominates, depends on whether its trigger is relational (betrayal, transgression, ideological incompatibility) or structural (algorithmic, platform-based, institutional unfairness), and this profile sets a default EVLN response tendency. Whether that tendency is realized depends on structural recourse, the inverse of switching costs, platform dependence, and powerlessness. When recourse is blocked, Exit tendencies redirect toward Voice where a channel exists, and toward Neglect, termed informed helplessness, where none does. We develop eight propositions specifying this redirection process, including a measurement-validity proposition showing informed helplessness is indistinguishable from loyalty in standard satisfaction measures, and a release proposition explaining how dormant hate resurfaces when conditions change. The framework helps managers and policymakers identify trapped haters and sets an agenda for measuring them. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Determinants of visit intention to Lake Toba geopark: The roles of publicity, destination awareness, destination image, and word of mouth
abstract: Tourism research has increasingly emphasized the importance of communication and perception factors in shaping tourists’ behavioral intentions, particularly in sustainable tourism destinations such as geoparks. However, limited studies have comprehensively examined the interplay between destination publicity, word of mouth (WOM), destination awareness, destination image, and visit intention within the context of UNESCO Global Geoparks. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the relationships among these variables in the context of Lake Toba Geopark, Indonesia, by applying the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework. A quantitative approach was employed using a structured online survey distributed to 425 respondents who had previously visited Lake Toba Geopark. The collected data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS. The findings reveal that destination publicity does not significantly influence destination awareness or destination image. Similarly, destination awareness does not directly affect tourists’ visit intention. In contrast, WOM significantly influences destination awareness, while destination awareness significantly enhances destination image. Furthermore, destination image emerges as the strongest determinant of visit intention. These findings indicate that tourists’ behavioral intentions are shaped more strongly by interpersonal communication and psychological perceptions than by conventional publicity exposure. This study contributes theoretically by extending the application of the SOR framework in geopark tourism through the integration of publicity, WOM, awareness, and image variables into a single model. Practically, the findings suggest that tourism stakeholders and destination managers should prioritize strategies that encourage positive WOM, strengthen destination awareness, and enhance destination image through authentic tourist experiences and digital engagement. Ultimately, destination image plays a central role in encouraging tourists’ intention to visit Lake Toba Geopark. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: How do sustainability capabilities create retail performance over time? dynamic evidence from U.S. and Chinese retailers
abstract: This study examines how sustainability-oriented technological innovation, sustainable supply chain management, and corporate social responsibility relate to environmental and manager-reported organisational performance in retail firms over time. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, institutional theory, and stakeholder theory, the study analyses a 12-wave monthly panel of 2410 retailers in the United States and China, comprising 26,998 firm-month observations. A multi-group hierarchical Bayesian continuous-time dynamic structural equation model estimates within-firm relationships, effects over one-, three-, and six-month intervals, time-varying mediation, and country differences. Technological innovation predicts environmental performance in both countries, but it strengthens sustainable supply chain management only in China. Sustainable supply chain management predicts organisational performance in both countries. Corporate social responsibility predicts environmental performance in both countries, while its direct short-run organisational effect is positive in the United States and negative in China. Environmental performance converts into organisational performance, and all three proposed indirect effects emerge, only in China during the focal six-month window. Exploratory analysis identifies integration-driven accelerators, evidence-driven pragmatists, and weakly-coupled drifters. The findings characterise retail sustainability as a dynamic conversion system with country-specific pathways to environmental and organisational outcomes; implications for individual customer responses require separate empirical testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Green by association? Restaurant presence on food-waste reduction platforms as a hybrid sustainability signal for brand equity
abstract: Food-waste reduction platforms allow restaurants to redistribute surplus food, but their branding implications remain unclear. Drawing on signaling theory, we conceptualize restaurant presence on these platforms as a hybrid sustainability signal that embeds sustainability and commercial meanings within the same marketplace cue. Across three experiments, we examine whether this hybrid signal enhances restaurant brand equity through green brand image and whether consumer residence and restaurant type condition its effects. Study 1 shows that platform presence enhances brand equity, partially through green brand image. Study 2 replicates the main effect and provides directional evidence that the premium of platform presence may be stronger among urban than rural consumers. Study 3 shows that this effect depends jointly on consumer residence and restaurant type, and that mediation through green brand image is evident primarily for full-service restaurants. These findings identify platform presence as a hybrid, context-dependent sustainability signal with branding implications. © 2026 The Authors

title: Design and simulation of a renewable energy-based microgrid for Accra Technical University
abstract: Rising electricity costs, coupled with the unreliability of the supply, are big challenges facing higher learning institutions in developing nations, where the use of fossil fuels in centralized power generation systems limits the efficiency of the systems in providing sustainable power services. In the case of Ghana, the challenges are more pronounced in urban-based institutions where the availability of electricity is essential in the conduct of learning, research, and administrative activities. This study outlines the design and techno-economic optimization of the microgrid system, powered by renewable energy, for Accra Technical University (ATU) in Ghana, with the aim of providing reliable energy services while minimizing the cost of energy production and its impact on the environment. Using HOMER PRO, the study developed the microgrid model, where the optimized microgrid is composed of a solar–battery microgrid, comprising 3400 solar panels, Schneider Core inverters, and lithium iron phosphate battery systems, where the simulation results indicate the ability of the microgrid system to generate energy that meets 100% of the energy demand, with the expected energy generated per annum being 3.35 GWh, while the autonomy of the battery is expected to be 68.5 h. Economically, the optimized design realizes a Net Present Cost of GHS 17.1 million and a Levelized Cost of Electricity of GHS 0.350/kWh, which reflects a significant reduction in electricity cost compared to traditional grid-connected supply. The optimized configuration supplies the full campus electricity demand primarily from solar-based generation supported by battery storage, thereby reducing dependence on conventional grid electricity and improving the environmental performance of the institution. Apart from the cost savings, the suggested microgrid design enhances the reliability of electricity supply, reduces the risk of power outages, and realizes a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, which aligns with the renewable energy goals of Ghana. The results prove that renewable energy-based microgrids for university campuses are technically viable and economically justifiable. This paper also presents a model that can be followed for developing reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective microgrids for universities in developing countries. © 2026 The Authors. title: ThreatNet: A multi-class dataset and LLM-based framework with class-imbalanced fine-tuning for life threat detection
abstract: Detecting life-threatening intent in online text is an increasing challenge as social media increasingly influence public conversation. Current models often face challenges related to insufficient data, class imbalance, and domain variability between platforms. This study proposes ThreatNet, a manually annotated multi-class dataset that contains a variety of linguistic indicators and different intensities of threats sourced from multiple online sources. Using this benchmark, we perform a comprehensive empirical evaluation of seven instruction-tuned LLMs (Flan-T5, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-4B-IT, Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-Instruct-7B, Zephyr-7B-Alpha, Phi-3-Mini-3.8B) and four transformer baselines (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, DeBERTa). We analyze the impact of class imbalance mitigation strategies, few-shot prompting (0, 4, 8, 16 shots), and model scale. Experimental results, reported with standard deviations over five runs, show that Flan-T5 achieves 85.67% ± 0.81% macro-average F1 on ThreatNet, while LLaMA-3.1-8B attains 97.12% ± 0.38% accuracy on the YouTube-Threat-Corpus. These results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its usefulness for life-threatening intent detection. The code is available at https://github.com/AIPMLab/ThreatNet. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective
abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Analysis of 406 participants exposed to an AI-generated tourism video reveals that true-to-ideal and true-to-fact authenticity show significant direct effects on destination attractiveness, whereas true-to-self authenticity operates entirely indirectly, consistent with a meaning-making route. For parallel mediation, true-to-ideal and true-to-self authenticity exert significant indirect effects via both mediators, whereas true-to-fact authenticity does so only through place imagination. The sequential pathway from place imagination to mental simulation receives consistent support across all dimensions. Theoretically, this study advances the ERC framework from a static typology to a processual account by delineating the distinct cognitive routes of each referent and highlighting both the conceptual promise and measurement challenges of operationalizing true-to-self authenticity as perceived communicative sincerity in algorithmically generated portrayals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Micro-foundations of destination supply: A configural analysis of herders’ livelihood strategies in grassland tourism
abstract: Based on the revised Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis was used to investigate the combinatorial effects of social, human, cultural, policy, physical, natural, and financial capital on herders' livelihood strategies in Chen Barag in the Hulunbuir Grassland, to identify the key drivers of herders’ adoption of a tourism livelihood. The results identify six differentiated livelihood configuration types. Traditional pastoral livelihoods are associated with resource-constrained configurations and high thresholds for tourism participation under ecological, market, and institutional conditions. Conversely, mixed livelihoods are associated with configurations involving productive resource release, locational advantages, cultural commodification, and intergenerational labour division, while governance tensions between institutional arrangements and diversified livelihood needs may create additional constraints. These findings highlight the joint importance of asset-related thresholds and institutional conditions in shaping differentiated tourism participation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Biomimetic Gradient Porous Core–Shell Fibers with Enhanced Gas Sensing for CO-Temperature Dual-Mode Early Fire Warning
abstract: Early fire detection systems that are highly sensitive are essential for reducing the impact of fire disasters. However, their development still faces significant challenges due to the lack of capability for simultaneous monitoring of both temperature and gas. Herein, we propose a facile coaxial wet-spinning strategy to fabricate a dual-parameter fiber sensor capable of simultaneously detecting carbon monoxide (CO) and temperature for early combustion warning. The resulting core–sheath structured fiber consists of a CO sensing sheath made of SnO2/In2O3 heterojunction/aramid nanofiber (ANF)/silver nanowire composite with biomimetic gradient pores, an ANF isolation layer, and a temperature sensing core composed of MXene. The gradient porous sheath constructed by gradient-induced phase separation technology exhibits gradually decreasing pore sizes from outer (> 10 μm) to inner (< 3 μm) regions. This structure demonstrates a significant enhancement in the fiber sensor’s sensitivity to CO, achieving a 15% higher response compared to non-gradient porous structures (ΔR/R0 = 0.95%/ppm; detection limit of 10 ppm), with the response time reduced to 19.28 s, surpassing the response speed of most fire-warning fibers. Additionally, this fiber sensor can rapidly monitor abnormal temperature increases, enabling flame alarm functionality within 3 s. It also achieves precise real-time temperature detection within the range of 50–300 °C, exhibiting high sensitivity (20.6 μV K−1) and a strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.99). This work highlights the significant potential of gradient pore in enhancing CO sensing and offers a novel perspective for the design of ultrafast early fire-warning fiber sensors. title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Data were collected from 389 graduate students in Chinese universities using a two-wave survey design, and the hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using hierarchical regression analyses supplemented by the PROCESS macro. The results indicate that illegitimate tasks exert opposing indirect effects on research creativity through distinct reflective cognitive pathways. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Supervisor-student relationship quality further shaped how illegitimate tasks were interpreted and which reflective pathway was activated. These findings clarify the cognitive mechanisms and relational conditions through which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity and contribute to understanding how task legitimacy shapes creative thinking in graduate research contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Exploring the role of green human resource management in enhancing employee well-being and job satisfaction in the it sector
abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has received a growing academic interest with organizations starting to incorporate the sustainability of the environment into their strategic human resource management. The present paper offers a synthesis and systematic review of the existing body of literature to identify the impacts of GHRM practices on employee well being, job satisfaction as well as environmental performance, especially in the IT industry. A systematic literature review was conducted. The sources of records were Google Scholar (n = 317) and Scopus (n = 312), which returned 629 preliminary studies. After applying inclusion criteria based on peer-review, relevance and timeframe criteria, 156 articles were selected for detailed analysis. Literature was grouped based on the Ability-Motivation-Opportunity (AMO) framework to assess the performance of GHRM practices in the main HR functions. The results show that green training and development (80% implementation impact; 90% environmental impact) and reward management (85% implementation impact; 90% environmental impact) have the greatest correlation with the employee engagement and sustainability outcomes. The other contribution made towards the development of a psychological green climate and the encouragement of organizational citizenship behaviour towards the environment (OCBE) is recruitment, job design, and performance appraisal. Nevertheless, there are gaps of measurement structures and multi-level empirical validation of sectors. The research finds out that holistic integration of GHRM between HR functions boosts employee motivation, job satisfaction, and performance on organizational sustainability. Organizations can attain long-term competitive advantage by integrating environmental values into the HR systems, especially those operating in the knowledge-intensive sectors like the IT sector, in addition to promoting the sustainability of the larger society. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. At the concept level, government failure, incentives, and user-pays lay on the higher-difficulty side, while demand and costs, price discrimination, and public, private, and club goods fell on the lower-difficulty side. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. These patterns remained broadly stable in supplementary analyses assessing sensitivity to question selection. title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. This paper addresses this fragmentation through the first systematic cross-domain seating assignment literature review, analyzing publications via bibliometric analysis and examining assignment methods (including optimization techniques) across transportation (airplanes and trains), dining establishments, entertainment venues, and classrooms. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. The review concludes that limited real-world implementation stems partly from researchers' inability to access successful approaches from adjacent fields, highlighting opportunities to advance seating assignment methods through integrated frameworks. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

abstract: Grammarly is one of the most widely used software applications for the automatic detection of grammatical errors in texts translated from Persian into English. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Grammarly and to propose suggestions for improving its performance. To achieve this objective, a corpus consisting of English translations of booklets introducing works of resistance literature was analyzed. After grammatical errors had been identified by the researchers (human evaluators), the electronic versions of the booklets were submitted to Grammarly for error detection. The identified errors were then categorized, and the results obtained by the researchers were compared with those generated by the software. Following the qualitative and quantitative analyses of the errors and the presentation of the findings, recommendations were made to enhance Grammarly’s effectiveness. According to the findings, of the 98 instances identified by Grammarly as errors, 16 were not actual errors. In four cases (4.9%), Grammarly failed to correctly identify the type of error. The software demonstrated its weakest performance in the detection of spelling errors and the misuse of masculine and feminine pronouns. Overall, Grammarly exhibited a high level of effectiveness, correctly identifying 82.8% of the errors. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Smart and green solutions in the catering and hospitality: A review of the existing literature
abstract: The integration of digital technologies and sustainability practices is reshaping the catering and hospitality industry, yet research on smart and green solutions remains fragmented. This study maps the intellectual and thematic development of this field through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications using VOSviewer, Biblioshiny, and Microsoft Excel. The findings reveal substantial growth in research interest and increasing interdisciplinary contributions across countries, institutions, and authors. Keyword analysis identifies artificial intelligence, sustainability, digital transformation, and social media as dominant themes, while circular economy, Internet of Things (IoT), and customer behavior represent emerging areas. The analysis also highlights a relatively underexplored intersection of AI, IoT, and circular economy, suggesting important opportunities for future research. By consolidating the intellectual structure and emerging themes, this study provides a research agenda for advancing smart and sustainable solutions that enhance operational efficiency, customer experience, environmental performance, and competitiveness in the hospitality sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrating Business Impact Analysis, Scenario-Based FMEA, and Business Continuity Planning in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing: A Product-Level Case Study
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the product-level integration of Business Impact Analysis (BIA), scenario-based Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and Business Continuity Planning (BCP) for a selected finished medicinal product. Methods: A single-site case study was conducted for cefixime 400 mg film-coated tablets in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical organization. Data were collected over approximately six months through four structured questionnaires, documentary and operational-record review, facilitated interviews, and cross-functional consensus sessions. BIA established Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD), Recovery Time Objective (RTO), and Work Recovery Time (WRT). Twenty-five de-identified scenarios, were assessed using predefined 1–4 scales for severity, frequency, and detectability; RPN was calculated as S × F × D. Results: IT and Technology had the shortest recovery requirement (MTD 48 h, RTO 24 h, WRT 24 h). Twelve scenarios were low risk and 13 were medium risk; none was high or critical. Material-transport interruption and adverse commercial and market conditions had the highest RPN of 16. Thirteen scenarios required additional controls. Sensitivity analysis showed that selected medium risks could move to high risk after a one-level score increase. Conclusion: The integrated approach supported transparent recovery prioritization and translation into product-specific continuity actions. Findings are context-specific and require prospective testing and replication. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Negotiating your way to the top: Conflict management by women leaders in family businesses
abstract: Family businesses are a fertile ground for women to take up different leader roles. The way up as well as functioning at the nexus of the business family and family business offer unique negotiation challenges. Women leaders play a central role in preserving family harmony while safeguarding business performance, acting as mediators in cases of intra-family conflict and developing their career as leaders. Traditionally oriented succession dynamics, inequality, and lack of legitimacy as business leaders and family leaders require specific and high-level negotiation competencies. This review explores the structural and cultural challenges that women face in their family businesses as family members as well as the negotiating and conflict management competencies needed in both family and business. © 2026

title: Designing Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells with Self-Assembled Monolayer Hole Transport Layers
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as highly versatile interfacial materials in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), offering tunable molecular structures, favorable energy-level alignment, high optical transparency, and minimized non-radiative recombination losses. With the rapid advancement of inverted (p-i-n) PSC architectures, SAM-based hole-selective contacts have demonstrated distinct advantages in achieving superior power conversion efficiency, cost-effective fabrication, and strong compatibility with scalable manufacturing processes. This review first summarizes the evolution of SAM applications, with a particular focus on SAM-based materials in p-i-n PSCs. Subsequently, the fundamental aspects of SAMs are systematically discussed. Further, common preparation methods of SAMs are reviewed, along with the key challenges encountered in achieving uniform SAM coating. Based on this, recent progress in SAM-based PSCs is comprehensively summarized, including their applications in high-efficiency single-junction devices, perovskite tandem solar cells, and large-area photovoltaic modules. The crucial roles of SAMs in energy-level modulation, interfacial modification, defect passivation, and charge transport are highlighted. Finally, the remaining challenges and future prospects of SAMs in inverted PSCs are discussed, with particular emphasis on interfacial stability and long-term operational reliability. This review aims at providing systematic insights and guidance for the further development of SAM-based inverted PSCs. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
abstract: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries. title: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COIN: CLICKBAIT’S INFLUENCE ON CONSUMER PURCHASE INTENTION IN SOCIAL MEDIA
abstract: As social media increasingly operates within algorithm-driven attention economies, clickbait has become a pervasive engagement tactic. However, prior research has not fully explained the psychological mechanisms linking clickbait to downstream consumer behavior. Existing studies have also largely treated clickbait as an isolated persuasive cue, overlooking its dynamic interactions with other elements in social media ecosystems. Drawing on psychological reactance theory (PRT) and uses-and-gratifications theory (UGT), this study develops an integrated framework to examine when clickbait harms versus facilitates consumer responses. Across four experiments, we test a sequential mediation model in which perceived intrusiveness and advertising avoidance transmit the effects of clickbait on purchase intention. We further introduce message appeal congruence as a key boundary condition. The results indicate that clickbait does not uniformly produce negative outcomes. When headline-induced motivations align with the gratifications delivered by the content, perceived intrusiveness and reactance are attenuated. When they are misaligned, advertising avoidance increases and purchase intention declines. This research advances the clickbait literature by shifting attention from static credibility judgments to dynamic goal-directed processing and by identifying gratification fulfillment as an upstream regulator of psychological reactance in social media contexts. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. .

title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. The findings demonstrate that structured, pedagogically guided AI integration transforms AI from a passive information source into an active learning scaffold. The SAIL approach, supported by RACE, offers a practical and transferable pathway for educators seeking to prepare students to navigate AI-augmented professional environments with critical, reflective, and responsible judgment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Inflow modeling strategies designed to enhance the ecological sustainability of hydroelectric reservoir operation planning
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid global expansion of water infrastructure alters major rivers, causes severe biodiversity declines, and destabilizes aquatic ecosystems. Amid intensifying eco-hydrological pressures, accurate prediction of reservoir inflow remains imperative to safeguard downstream aquatic ecosystems, yet data-sparse tropical environments chronically impair the generalizability of deep learning architectures due to pronounced overfitting. The study objectives were to evaluate three statistical inflow modeling frameworks, representative of design-era hydrological understanding, against the observed 1998–2023 flow regime to identify the most reliable forecasting approach for supporting environmental-flow-informed reservoir operation planning under monsoonal variability. METHODS: Using a multi-decadal hydro-meteorological dataset from 1998 to 2023 ( n = 312 monthly time steps) at Karian Reservoir in Banten Province, Indonesia, three primary modeling approaches were tested: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, Markov Chain, and Multiple Linear Regression. To rigorously assess model diagnostics and predictive performance across historical drought and wet regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient, Kling-Gupta efficiency, and operational trajectory metrics were integrated. FINDINGS: Deterministic multiple linear regression achieved the highest overall predictive accuracy with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.74, a Kling-Gupta efficiency of 0.64, and a superior operational trajectory guideline correlation of 0.85. The observed enhancement in model efficacy stems from the methodical integration of lagged streamflow predictors that effectively characterize catchment-scale moisture persistence. Conversely, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model exhibited the weakest diagnostic capability (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.62; Kling-Gupta efficiency = 0.60) due to systematic overestimation of dry-season baseflows, risking artificial inflation of safe water availability. Meanwhile, the stochastic Markov yielded a commensurate aggregate Kling-Gupta efficiency score of 0.66 and exhibited a superior proficiency in replicating long-term probability distributions. CONCLUSION: While Multiple Linear Regression shows the strongest performance for monthly operational scheduling, the Markov Chain model offers a complementary probabilistic framework for screening extended seasonal drought risk. Independent out-of-sample validation against a held-out 2019-2023 period revealed substantial performance degradation for both models (Multiple Linear Regression Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.61 to 0.02; Markov Chain Nash-sutcliffe efficiency declining from 0.28 to -1.01), directly evidencing non-stationary rainfall-inflow relationships. Ultimately, these results establish that the evaluated models serve as an initial decision-support tool for raw water allocation planning, though their sustained operational reliability necessitates systematic recalibration. title: Waiting for Uganda’s first commercial ‘Pearl Sweet’ oil: Discourses on social and environmental impacts and safeguards
abstract: Uganda discovered approximately 3.5 billion barrels of commercially recoverable oil reserves in 2006 and is poised to become a major oil producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. In assessing progress towards full–scale oil production, expected by the end of 2026, Uganda’s President referred to the country’s commercial crude oil as “pearl sweet”, highlighting its medium-to-heavy, highly waxy characteristics, relatively low sulphur content, and ease of refining. Despite the anticipated economic benefits, considerable debate persists regarding the potential social and environmental impacts of oil development and the adequacy of safeguards ahead of full–scale production. Drawing on experiences from established oil–producing countries, this paper examines how environmental and social impacts are framed, how safeguards are prioritised, and what this implies for Uganda’s emerging oil sector. Anchored in environmental justice and political ecology, the study adopts a sequential integrative design combining a systematic literature review with empirical insights from twelve purposively selected stakeholders in Uganda’s oil-producing districts and national regulatory institutions. The literature review used Boolean search strings that connected terms within conceptual blocks using OR and combined blocks using AND, following a PRISMA-guided process across Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar and institutional data bases. Of 1800 records identified, 95 key sources were retained for analysis. The findings indicate that, although Uganda has initiated several safeguards measures including oil–spill preparedness training, buffer zone enforcement, afforestation, and resettlement programs – implementation remain fragmented, under–resourced, and heavily centralised. Comparative analysis further indicates limited integration of international climate frameworks, including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, into national oil governance. We argue that Uganda’s challenge is not simply the absence of safeguards, but the persistence of centralised, uneven, and under–resourced governance arrangements that constrain the translation of international safeguard commitments into effective national practice. This study contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while also intersecting with SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Unpacking the pathways from green intellectual capital to green recovery performance: The power of employee voice and intrinsic motivation
abstract: Our paper proposes and tests a moderated mediation model that examines how green intellectual capital relates to green recovery performance, highlighting green promotive and prohibitive voice behaviors as mediators and intrinsic motivation to share knowledge as a moderator. Results based on time-lagged data gathered from FLEs in environmentally certified Spanish hotels revealed that the association between green intellectual capital and green recovery performance operated through green voice behaviors. Both green promotive and green prohibitive voice behaviors mediated the green intellectual capital-green recovery performance link. However, intrinsic motivation to share knowledge strengthened only the promotive pathway. This finding underscores an asymmetry in how motivational states condition the translation of intangible resources into recovery behaviors. Our research positions voice behavior as a proximal mechanism through which green intellectual capital translates into sustainable outcomes and shows that the amplifying role of intrinsic motivation depends on the form of voice at stake. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Charging station planning strategy considering imbalanced distribution of response propensity
abstract: With the advancement of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, Electric Vehicle (EV) participation in grid scheduling has become a growing trend. This paper addresses the heterogeneous response propensity of EVs under different operating states by proposing a charging station planning strategy that accounts for the imbalanced distribution of planning-relevant EV response characteristics. Firstly, an improved synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) based on driving routes is introduced to tackle the data imbalance among EVs with different states of charge (SOC). By generating synthetic samples, this method enhances the accuracy of charging station planning under imbalanced data conditions. Next, an improved Mean Shift algorithm is proposed for charging station siting, which considers differences in the planning-level response propensity of EVs under different SOC states, thereby reducing the distance required for EVs to respond to grid scheduling. Finally, a capacity configuration strategy is designed to optimize charging station capacity by comprehensively considering the charging and discharging demands of EVs in the area and their response characteristics. Validation using real data from Chicago demonstrates that the proposed strategy effectively reduces EV response distance in scheduling, achieving an 8.3% reduction in response distance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Psychological safety as a driver of student learning outcomes in team-based learning environments: The mediating role of teamwork quality
abstract: With the rise of constructivist approaches, team-based learning (TBL) has gained popularity as an instructional design in the field of management education. The extant research indicates that the positive effects of TBL on student learning outcomes, which many studies report, might depend on individual as well as social-contextual drivers. In this paper, we introduce psychological safety and the quality of teamwork processes as two important social-contextual drivers of student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Based on research on team processes and TBL, we argue that psychological safety fosters student learning outcomes because of its positive effect on intrinsic motivation and group interaction. We further hypothesize that the relationship between psychological safety and student learning outcomes is mediated by the quality of teamwork processes within the student teams. A field study based on a computerized business simulation involving 169 undergraduate management students, nested within 44 teams, at a German university supports our hypotheses. We contribute to research on constructivist learning and TBL by introducing psychological safety as an important driver and the quality of teamwork processes as a mediating mechanism for student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Our study also has practical implications for the design, support, and facilitation of psychologically safe team-based learning environments. © 2026

title: The power of gastronomic cultural capital: How local food culture shapes residents' recommendation intention
abstract: While destinations increasingly leverage cultural capital for competitiveness, research predominantly focuses on top-down promotions of monument-centered heritage, neglecting the distinct social logic of gastronomic culture. Grounded in cultural capital theory, this study aims to examine how Hong Kong's tea restaurants food culture translates into residents' recommendation intentions toward culturally diverse individuals. It untangles the core inquiries: how everyday food culture fosters attachment; how this attachment subsequently shapes cultural identity and confidence; and how nostalgia and knowledge moderate these psychological pathways. Additionally, it identifies which specific tea restaurant's food culture dimensions serve as the primary drivers. Utilizing an empirical sample of 615 Hong Kong residents, this research adopts a PLS–SEM–ANN approach. The PLS–SEM analysis confirms that cultural identity and confidence act as pivotal mediators, while the complementary ANN analysis reveals that gastronomic identity, exceeding mere sensory flavour, is the predominant driving dimension. Empirically, nostalgia amplifies the culture–attachment link, and knowledge strengthens the attachment–confidence relationship. These findings advocate for a paradigm shift in destination marketing: beyond institutional campaigns, mobilizing residents as active cultural transmitters is crucial for gastronomic tourism, establishing a scalable mechanism for everyday cultural capital transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Rational Design of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Oxygen Electrocatalysis: Recent Advances and Mechanistic Insights
abstract: Due to the excessive consumption of fossil fuels and the increasingly severe global environment, the world urgently needs to develop new clean and renewable energy sources. However, these energy sources have intermittency and instability, so it is necessary to vigorously develop efficient and large-scale energy conversion and storage technologies such as fuel cells, water electrolyzers, and metal–air batteries based on the core reactions of oxygen evolution reaction and oxygen reduction reaction. Because of their excellent molecular designability and structural tunability, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) show great potential for applications in this field. In this review, we first classify COF-based electrocatalysts based on the nature of active sites. Subsequently, strategies including structural design and functional synthesis for improving performance of COF-based electrocatalysts in the field of oxygen catalysis are systematically reviewed. Importantly, mechanism discussion of the performance improvement is highlighted. Finally, we put forward prospects for the future research directions, challenges, and development opportunities in this field. This review aims to provide guidance for the development of high-performance COF-based electrocatalysts through critical analysis of existing research, revealing the correlation between material design and mechanism for performance improvement. title: When service environments signal ideology: Customer responses to ideological cues
abstract: Service environments increasingly contain visible cues that communicate political engagement, religious identities, LGBTQ + affiliation, environmental advocacy, and other collective values. Although servicescape research has traditionally emphasized atmospheric, aesthetic, and functional cues, less is known about how customers interpret ideological cues embedded within routine service encounters. Drawing on servicescape research and social identity theory, this research examines how ideological servicescape cues are associated with customer discomfort, avoidance intentions, and stated store-choice decisions. Three preregistered, scenario-based experiments in a coffee shop context examine ideological cues displayed through employees and the physical service environment. Study 1 shows that political cues generate greater discomfort than environmental and lifestyle cues, although they do not differ significantly from religious or LGBTQ + cues. Study 2 shows that matching political cues displayed across employee and environmental touchpoints generate greater discomfort than political cues displayed through a single source, while perceived authenticity does not account for this association. Study 3 shows that political cues are associated with lower stated store choice than environmental cues, particularly when matching political cues appear across employee and environmental touchpoints. Across studies, customer discomfort statistically accounts for part of the association between ideological cue conditions and avoidance intentions or stated store-choice decisions. The findings extend servicescape scholarship by showing that politically charged symbolism may shape customer responses through both cue content and cue-source configuration. Because the studies rely on scenario-based experiments and stated responses, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of observed marketplace behavior or realized financial outcomes. © 2026 The Authors

title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. This study contributes to the literature on rural tourism marketing and highlights the strategic value of moral appeals, particularly for rural destinations with limited resources. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
