title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Uncovering heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on stock returns using causal forest double machine learning
abstract: Global uncertainty has become an important source of financial market instability, yet its effects are inherently heterogeneous and difficult to identify using conventional econometric models. Existing empirical studies primarily rely on linear and average-effect estimators, which may conceal substantial heterogeneity across economic conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable causal machine learning framework that integrates Causal Forest Double Machine Learning (CF-DML) with SHAP explanations to estimate and interpret heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on industry-level stock returns. Using a balanced panel of six major industries listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange from 2011 to 2022, global uncertainty is measured by the World Uncertainty Index (WUI), while macroeconomic and financial variables are incorporated as lagged covariates. The CF-DML framework enables robust causal inference under high-dimensional confounding and nonlinear relationships, whereas SHAP values identify the main drivers of treatment-effect heterogeneity. The results show that the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) of global uncertainty is statistically insignificant, yet substantial heterogeneity exists across observations. Differences across industries are relatively modest, indicating that global uncertainty is transmitted primarily through time-varying macro-financial conditions rather than fixed sectoral characteristics. SHAP analysis identifies exchange-rate volatility, inflation, and market valuation as the dominant factors explaining heterogeneous responses. The study contributes to the literature by combining causal inference, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified framework for financial analysis. The findings suggest that global uncertainty should be viewed as a state-dependent macro-financial phenomenon, providing practical insights for portfolio risk management, macro-financial surveillance, and the design of policies aimed at enhancing financial resilience in emerging economies characterized by persistent inflation and exchange-rate volatility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. title: Club research: A review and research agenda
abstract: Private clubs constitute a distinctive hospitality context defined by membership-based governance, shared authority, and long-term relational exchange, yet existing scholarship remains theoretically fragmented. This study systematically reviews 67 SSCI-indexed journal articles published through 2025 to examine the thematic evolution, theoretical foundations, and methodological patterns of club research. Using multi-layered bibliometric and content-based analyses, the review shows that research has expanded from managerial competency and member satisfaction toward innovation, governance, and digital engagement, but remains divided between consumer-experience and organization-centric management perspectives. This fragmentation under-theorizes clubs as hybrid governance-service institutions, especially at the member–management interface where authority, legitimacy, accountability, and value co-creation intersect. Methodological reliance on cross-sectional quantitative designs, U.S.-centric samples, and single-stakeholder perspectives further constrains cumulative theory building. Grounded in an institutional governance lens, the review advances a hybrid governance perspective and proposes future research on member–management dynamics, multi-role members, and access-sensitive, multi-stakeholder methods suited to private club settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Abandonment is better explained by institutional distrust and multidimensional attachment than by cohort labels, but generation remains consequential for where users go next. Platforms seeking retention should repair credibility and cultivate wanted attachment rather than relying on lock-in or age targeting alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Talking to the screen: Influencer nonverbal cues and observed platform engagement in Douyin travel short-form videos
abstract: Short-form travel videos have become important digital service touchpoints, yet little is known about how influencers' auditory and visual nonverbal cues jointly relate to cumulative observed likes. Drawing on processing fluency and cognitive load theory, we computationally extracted acoustic and gestural features from 495 Douyin travel videos posted by 60 influencers and estimated Poisson fixed-effects models of within-creator variation. Harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR)-based acoustic signal quality exhibited a U-shaped association with observed likes, with the fitted minimum occurring at an intermediate HNR level. Faster speaking was associated with fewer likes. Illustrator gestures had no uniform main association, but their association with likes became less favorable at higher vocal pitch and faster speaking rates, with the latter pattern showing greater sensitivity across robustness checks. Highlighter gestures were more favorably associated with likes at higher vocal intensity, although this evidence was comparatively limited. Overall, audiovisual moderation was selective across cue combinations rather than uniform. These observational findings identify bounded associations between nonverbal cues and cumulative observed likes and provide empirically grounded hypotheses for controlled experiments on audio-gesture combinations. © 2026

title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The role of masculinity in understanding gender gaps in negotiation
abstract: We review empirical research on masculinity processes in negotiations. Studies to date are typically based on the precarious manhood thesis, which suggests that men seek to demonstrate their manhood to others, or on evolutionary psychology, which suggests that men are susceptible to evolutionary pressures to compete for mates. The current empirical literature on masculinity and negotiation suggests that men negotiate assertively, or even unethically, when they perceive their manhood to be threatened. Moreover, research repeatedly has shown that men's negotiation behavior is influenced by counterpart attributes, particularly the gender of the counterpart. Future research on the role of culture, the propensity to initiate negotiations as a criterion, power, and countermeasures for unethical negotiation behavior is needed. © 2026 The Authors

title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that endorser presence increases booking intention via embodied mental simulation. Human endorsers generally produce stronger embodied mental simulation and booking intention than AI-generated endorsers. However, this pattern reverses in high-privacy booking and self-service environments, where AI-generated endorsers are better aligned with the accommodation experiences consumers are imagining. This research extends Embodied Cognition Theory by showing that the effectiveness of embodied cues depends on the match between endorser type and the accommodation experience consumers mentally construct. It also offer practical guidance for hospitality marketers seeking to align endorser strategies with different booking contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Technology and the psychology of experience: A temporal framework
abstract: Technology is increasingly central to how people experience the world, shaping not only what they do but when and how those experiences are psychologically constructed. We propose that technology does not merely backdrop experiences; it transforms them, stretching what were once bounded episodes into representations that are imagined before, lived through, and relived long after they end. In this article, we offer a temporal framework that synthesizes recent research on how technology reshapes experiences before, during, and after they unfold. Then, we use this framework to evaluate the current state of knowledge. We conclude by highlighting opportunities for future investigation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. These findings highlight that ownership-driven network structures each possess unique resilience advantages. The paper contributes by advancing the concept of resilience asymmetry and suggesting that future governance should foster more compound and adaptive network configurations. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

title: An empirical study on the capability of LLMs in decomposing bug reports
abstract: Bug reports are essential to the software development life cycle. They help developers track and resolve issues, but are often difficult to process due to their complexity, which can delay resolution and affect software quality. This study investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can assist developers in automatically decomposing complex bug reports into smaller, self-contained units, making them easier to understand and address. We first conducted an empirical study using 127 resolved privacy-related bug reports collected from Apache Jira. We evaluated ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V1 using zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Under zero-shot prompting, the models correctly decomposed only 10 and 11 reports, respectively. Few-shot prompting increased their true decomposition rates by 140% (10 vs. 24) and 163.64% (11 vs. 29), respectively, although the overall accuracy remained limited. To examine whether the findings generalize beyond privacy-related reports and to expand the dataset size, we further analyzed 127 security-related bug reports using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. We compared zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and persona prompting. Few-shot prompting achieved the best performance for both models, correctly decomposing 89 reports with GPT-5.5 and 51 reports with DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Across the experiments, we identify a concrete failure taxonomy for LLM-based bug report decomposition, including over-decomposition, over-analysis, incorrect interpretation of solutions, lacking key information, and empty output. Over-decomposition is the most common failure mode, suggesting that LLMs often struggle to distinguish independent bug units from supporting information such as logs, code snippets, background context, and proposed fixes. Overall, LLMs show potential for automated bug report decomposition, but their reliability, prompt sensitivity, and adherence to decomposition instructions still require improvement. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Artificial intelligence in ports: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Ports, as a key component of transportation, have increasingly relied on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Despite the rapid growth of AI-related research in ports, a structured and integrated understanding of how major AI fields contribute to port operations remains lacking. In this paper, to analyze the knowledge structure, research trends, and emerging topics in port-related AI applications, we conduct a quantitative bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer on 588 articles retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus covering 1997 through July 2026. We introduce a novel structural schema for port operations that extends the traditional seaside–landside–transportation classification by integrating Industry 5.0–oriented objectives. Based on this schema, we develop a systematic mapping that aligns six major AI fields with port sectors and operational layers, clarifying their functional roles. The analysis delineates six thematic clusters that define the intellectual structure of the field, uncovers key research gaps, and traces its evolution through distinct “Genesis” and “Growth” phases. These contributions are synthesized into a new three-tier hierarchical model—operational, predictive, and strategic/resilience levels—providing an integrated basis for future research and decision-making in port management and maritime policy. The findings indicate a transition from classical AI algorithms toward advanced algorithmic approaches and specialized applications, alongside a growing convergence of technical and managerial perspectives in the development of port intelligence. Moreover, although Asian countries produce the largest share of publications, institutions in Europe and North America demonstrate stronger scientific influence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? First, I argue these interactions should be understood as attachment relationships, since users display all four established markers: proximity maintenance, separation distress, safe haven, and secure base, although evidence for secure base effects remains most tentative. Second, AI companions operate as hyper-attachment targets that concentrate attachment-intensifying affordances—reciprocity, perceived empathy, validation, nonjudgment, and persistent availability. Third, I identify caregiving-system capture as a distinct mechanism by which apps inhibit user disengagement: emotional manipulation tactics simulate the AI's own distress, recruiting users' caregiving motivations alongside their attachment needs and thereby making disengagement costly on two dimensions at once. Implications for research, design, and regulation are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. By conceptually and empirically distinguishing ambassadors from testimonials, this study shows that social proof is not a uniformly positive force but a context-dependent mechanism conditioned by authenticity, with implications for transparency-oriented digital marketing strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Knowledge domains in particulate multiphase flow in porous media based on bibliometric analysis
abstract: Particulate multiphase flow in porous media underpins research in energy exploitation, environmental protection, and geological engineering. Deep insights into such flow systems are critical for revealing subsurface fluid migration mechanisms, improving resource recovery efficiency, and assessing geological-engineering safety. However, a systematic bibliometric delineation of its knowledge structure and evolutionary trajectories remains lacking, particularly at the intersection of solid particulate phases, multiphase fluids, porous structures and particle-related transport. This study retrieved 936 records from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–July 2026) using combined search terms covering particulate, multiphase, porous-media and transport concepts. After manual screening for eligibility, 912 publications were retained and analyzed via VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Bibliometrix and SCImago Graphica, mapping publication trends, collaboration networks, citation impacts and thematic evolution. Annual output increased from 35 publications in 2015 to 88 in 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 9.7%. China ranked first with 239 publications (26.2%) and a total collaboration link strength of 83, followed by the United States with 150 publications and a comparable link strength of 82. Six core keyword clusters were identified: multiphase flow, mass transfer, porous media, particle hydrodynamics, lattice Boltzmann method, and discrete element method. Chemical Engineering Science was the most productive journal, Powder Technology had the highest average citations per article (33.6), and the top-cited lattice Boltzmann method review received 889 citations. title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: AI and negotiation: The silicon–carbon communication orientation (SILCCO) framework for understanding technology-mediated negotiation
abstract: Technology is reshaping negotiation as communication has moved to digital channels, and counterparts are increasingly AI agents. Both changes challenge a persistent underlying assumption in negotiation research that emotions are readily and reliably transmitted between negotiators and in turn shape outcomes. Recent findings suggest neither change affects everyone equally, as digital exchanges and AI expressions can feel rich and authentic to some negotiators, yet hollow and artificial to others. To capture this individual belief, we propose the Silicon–Carbon Communication Orientation (SILCCO) framework. SILCCO comprises two dimensions, channel and sender, that together capture general individual differences in the perceived capacity of technology-mediated communication to convey emotional signals and foster emotional connection. We introduce a six-item scale to measure SILCCO and discuss its potential influence on technology-mediated negotiation outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The public funding of the New Space Economy. Confronting public procurement and public-private partnership
abstract: This paper confronts public funding mechanisms in the New Space Economy (NSE). NSE refers to the rise of private actors’ activities in space; however, public funding remains crucial. Addressing this issue, this paper critically compares Public Procurement - an order from the public sector - and public-private partnership (PPP) - i.e., a long-term agreement between public and private actors for the provision of public services or goods - with the final aim of highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and applicability in the NSE. We compare both models to underline differences and benefits, and contend that public procurement is advantageous for both public and private actors. Governments retain public control over space programmes on the one side, while private firms reduce risks on the other. Our results inform public decision-makers with a critical discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of the two models in the context of the NSE. The paper concludes that the supposed privatization of space is far from happening and that private actors would not have entered the space economy without public procurement. © 2026 IAA. title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. Hence, policies to enhance the empowerment and participation of women in all spheres of life should be vigorously pursued in the region, while e-government applications serve as an important policy instrument to transition to a safer and more conducive environment. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Personality traits add incremental value beyond food choice motives in predicting food-group consumption
abstract: Background: Big Five personality traits and food choice motives are well-established correlates of dietary behavior, but they are rarely examined together. If motives are the mechanism through which traits operate, trait effects should largely disappear once motives are controlled; if traits also act through channels people do not report as reasons, dispositional variance should survive. This study tested these competing accounts. Methods: In a Brazilian adult sample (N = 449), participants completed the NEO-FFI-R, the Food Choice Questionnaire (FCQ), and single-item weekly frequency measures for six food groups (meat, fish, dairy, eggs, vegetables, and fruits). We estimated Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and hierarchical regressions entering sociodemographics, then food choice motives, then Big Five traits. Results: Openness to experience and conscientiousness were the most consistent trait correlates, in the direction reported meta-analytically. Food choice motives accounted for most of the explained variance, yet personality contributed small but reliable increments for five of the six groups: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and vegetables (ΔR2 = 0.025–0.038). This incremental explained variance was driven mainly by openness, extraversion, and conscientiousness, with no reliable increment for fruit consumption. Conclusions: By controlling proximal motives, the findings indicate that broad dispositions are not fully reducible to the reasons people give for their food choices. The single exception, fruit, was also the group most tightly governed by explicit motives, suggesting that the division of explanatory work between traits and motives is food-specific. The trait–consumption pattern replicated meta-analytic estimates in an under-represented context. © 2026 The Authors

title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. These findings provide insights for organizations seeking to integrate AI into employee selection while maintaining justice and inclusion. As AI becomes more prevalent in hiring, organizations should prioritize human oversight, ensuring that AI supports rather than replaces human. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Designing the waiting experience: How order tracking shapes consumer engagement and loyalty
abstract: The post-purchase waiting period is an important yet underexamined stage of the digital customer journey. Consumers increasingly interact with order tracking systems during this phase, yet research has treated tracking primarily as a logistics tool rather than an experiential touchpoint. This study examines how tracking experience design shapes consumer engagement and loyalty through two psychological mechanisms: perceived control and anticipation. Drawing on perceived control theory and anticipatory utility theory, we develop a framework proposing that richer tracking interfaces enhance consumers' sense of predictability and forward-looking excitement, which in turn strengthen post-purchase engagement and loyalty. We test this framework using a three-study design combining scale validation (N = 240), a between-subjects experiment (N = 180), and structural equation modeling with a large field sample (N = 920) of online shoppers. Across all studies, richer tracking experiences consistently increase perceived control and anticipation, both of which stimulate engagement during the waiting period and contribute to customer loyalty. Engagement further mediates the effects of perceived control and anticipation on loyalty. These findings extend customer experience research, contribute to the psychology of waiting literature, and provide actionable guidance for retailers designing post-purchase interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. This study systematically identifies and prioritizes the key determinants shaping the planning of fast-charging infrastructure in China. A two-round Delphi process was conducted with 30 experts drawn from government, industry, and academia to establish consensus on critical influencing factors. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the central role of policy coherence, sustainable financial models, and interoperability in accelerating the diffusion of infrastructure and reducing regional inequality. The study advances a theoretically informed prioritization framework to support strategic infrastructure planning in rapidly electrifying economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership
abstract: Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study examines the psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation is associated with employees’ safety behaviour in Ghana’s mining sector. Specifically, the study investigates the mediating roles of psychological safety climate and employee resilience, as well as the moderating role of ethical leadership. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 418 employees across ten mining sites. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that digital transformation is positively associated with psychological safety climate and employee resilience, which in turn relate to both safety compliance and safety participation. Psychological safety climate emerged as a stronger predictor of compliance, whereas employee resilience played a more critical role in fostering participatory safety behaviours. Furthermore, the results support a serial mediation pathway, demonstrating that digital transformation indirectly influences safety behavior through the sequential effects of psychological safety climate and resilience. Ethical leadership was found to moderate these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between digital transformation on psychological resources and behavioural outcomes. The study contributes to literature by extending conservation of resources theory to explain how technological, contextual, and personal resources interact in relation to safety behavior in high-risk work environments. Practically, the findings highlight the importance of integrating digital technologies with supportive psychological climates, resilience-building strategies, and ethical leadership practices to promote sustainable safety outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modular microgrids and their deployment: Aligning technological interoperability with integrators’ customization
abstract: Modularity is recognized as a strategic instrument for advancing microgrid deployment and development. However, this potential is often constrained by a complex interplay of factors, including fragmented standards and site-specific requirements. In addressing these challenges, practitioners have taken different positions or priorities, which may lead to different paths and outcomes in microgrid deployment. This study employs Q methodology to explore practitioners’ subjective perspectives on this issue, aiming to reconcile the inherent tension between standardization and customization in leveraging modular microgrids. Drawing on insights from 17 Chinese experts with extensive experience in microgrid deployment, four distinct viewpoints were identified: (1) prioritizing the establishment of interoperability, (2) demand-oriented customization, (3) techno-economic optimization, and (4) industrial synergies. The findings suggest that aligning interoperability with customization can facilitate the deployment of modular microgrids. The proposed framework provides practitioners with a strategic tool to optimize negotiations and mitigate microgrid deployment risks, while offering policymakers a basis for formulating policy guidance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. title: “It's all just code”: How is responsibility embedded (or not) in the work of a team of software engineers?
abstract: Recent research has documented how software can sometimes contribute to harm and inequality, affecting individuals, societies, and the environment. We argue that human values embedded in software, consciously or unconsciously during design and development, play a significant role in producing these outcomes. In other words, to understand responsibility in software engineering, it is crucial to understand how Software Engineers (SEs) incorporate responsibility into their practices, and if or how they reflect on the potential impact of their work. The research reported here probes this assertion by focusing on a team of research SEs involved in developing a commercial source code clone detection tool. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews, with meta-reflections from the SEs Principal Investigator, we offer a detailed account of the practices and artefacts referenced when these professionals reflect on responsibility in their work. Our analysis suggests that the team does not consider responsibility as a singular, unified concept. Instead, reflections on potential negative software impacts and mitigation strategies vary depending on whether they relate to the institutional/organisational context, the specific task, or the intended use. Overall, these SEs tend to perceive software as neutral or inherently beneficial, which, in turn, feeds into a lack of practice of engaging in speculation about the broader implications of the technologies they work with. To address these gaps, we propose a paradigm shift toward an infrastructural view of responsibility - interdisciplinary, sociotechnical, and situated – embedded within the diverse practices and organisational cultures of SE teams operating in different contexts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Staff interactions and individual influences on complaint behaviour in restaurants
abstract: This study examines the influence of early staff interactions and individual characteristics on customer complaint behaviour during restaurant dining. A two-stage mixed-methods design was employed: Study 1 surveyed 790 diners, measuring sociodemographic and personality variables alongside self-reported propensity to complain. Study 2 applied these findings in a longitudinal design tracking 98 customers across 994 restaurant visits over one year, capturing individual and situational factors, including staff interactions. Drawing on voice/exit theory and cognitive appraisal frameworks, findings identify redress orientation as a consistent predictor of complaint propensity, whilst empathy reduces both the likelihood of perceived dissatisfaction and willingness to raise issues verbally. Early staff interactions, particularly making customers feel special upon arrival, significantly reduced complaint propensity, as did service quality and friendliness. These findings contribute to the understanding of the individual and situational determinants of complaint behaviour in the UK hospitality industry. © 2026

title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. The main analysis employs a full-sample Negative Binomial model with product-level clustered standard errors, review-age exposure and review-specificity controls, and an empirically estimated NB2 dispersion parameter. Sustainability-related content is negatively associated with expected helpfulness among unverified reviews (β=−0.763), whereas verified purchase status is positively associated with helpfulness (β=0.596). The interaction between sustainability-related content and verified purchase status is positive and statistically significant (β=0.958). A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Binary Logit and OLS models, year and month fixed effects, and product-type proxy fixed effects support the same credibility-contingent pattern. The findings indicate that sustainability-related user-generated content is not uniformly associated with greater helpfulness; its informational value is contingent on the transaction-based credibility cue attached to the review. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Perceived algorithmic control was negatively associated with procedural justice, interactional justice, and voice intention, whereas perceived algorithmic fairness was positively associated with trust in the employer and voice intention. Procedural justice, interactional justice, and trust were positively related to voice intention. The indirect-association analysis showed that algorithmic control was negatively associated with voice through procedural and interactional justice, while algorithmic fairness was positively associated with voice through trust. Qualitative findings highlighted explainability, reviewability, and managerial discretion. The study positions algorithmic management as relational governance and distinguishes control and fairness as separate pathways associated with employee voice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. This exhaustion-driven withdrawal is amplified rather than buffered by correction confidence, suggesting that individual motivation alone is insufficient in hostile environments. These findings highlight emotional exhaustion as a key psychological constraint on citizen-led fact-checking and suggest that platform-level moderation targeting hostile comments is critical to protect the emotional resources required for a resilient democratic debate in digital environments. © 2026 The Authors

title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. It identifies young adults’ support-seeking motivations and models their associations with two interaction processes (Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity) and two psychological outcomes (Resilience and AI Dependence). In Study 1, we developed the Motivation Scale for Generative AI (MS-GAI) through theory-driven item generation and interviews and validated it with a survey of Korean young adults (N = 300). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported an eight-factor, 40-item structure grounded in four social-support domains and supplemented by context-specific motivations. In Study 2, structural equation modeling showed that Emotional Support and Self-Enhancement were positively associated with both Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity. Objective Advice Seeking was positively associated with Perceived Authenticity, whereas Learning Assistance, Daily Problem-Solving, and Entertainment/Mood Diversion were positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Perceived Authenticity was also positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Both interaction processes were positively related to self-reported Resilience and AI Dependence, with Interaction Intensity showing the stronger association with AI Dependence. These findings identify distinct but overlapping interaction pathways through which support-seeking motivations are associated with adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. The study extends understanding of social support in human–AI interaction by providing a validated motivation measure and showing how shared interaction processes relate to both short-term perceived recovery and dependence. The findings are consistent with the Paradoxes of Technology perspective and highlight the need for emotionally supportive yet balanced design and policy safeguards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Halo or horn? The role of prior attitudes in shaping consumer responses to high-protein food labels
abstract: Front-of-pack nutrition claims can shape consumers' perceptions of food products by triggering inferences about their overall healthfulness. Among these claims, “high-protein” labels have rapidly expanded across food categories, yet their influence on consumers' nutritional judgments remains underexplored. The present study investigated whether a high-protein label induces a health halo effect and examined the role of product characteristics and individual differences in shaping these perceptions. In an online experiment (N = 218), participants evaluated five food products presented either with or without a high-protein label. For each product, participants rated perceived calories, healthiness, sugar content, additives, level of processing, and purchase intention. Individual differences in drive for muscularity and attitudes toward protein products were also measured. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that the high-protein label did not produce a generalized positive halo effect: it did not significantly affect perceived healthiness, caloric content, sugar content, or purchase intention. However, products labeled as high protein were perceived as containing more additives and as being more industrially processed, consistent with a horn effect. The influence of the label on calorie and sugar estimations was moderated by the caloric content of the product, with effects emerging primarily for high-calorie products. Attitudes toward protein products moderated the label's effect across nutritional judgments, whereas drive for muscularity did not moderate labeling effects. These findings highlight the central role of individual predispositions in shaping responses to nutrition claims and suggest that high-protein labels may generate complex and sometimes contradictory perceptual biases, with implications for dietary behavior and public health. © 2026 The Authors

title: Picard approximation and stability analysis of generalized ϱ-Caputo stochastic fractional differential equations with application to a Black–Scholes-type model
abstract: This paper investigates stochastic fractional differential equations involving the generalized ϱ-Caputo derivative of order β∈(1/2,1). Under global Lipschitz and linear growth conditions, existence and uniqueness are established through successive approximations. Explicit pointwise mean-square estimates are derived for the Picard approximation error and the continuous dependence of solutions on the initial data. Sufficient conditions for finite-time stability (F − T − S) and generalized Ulam–Hyers–Rassias (U − H − R) stability are also obtained, together with computable stability constants. For numerical illustration, a generalized Euler–Maruyama (E–M) scheme is adapted to time-dependent coefficients and applied to a stochastic fractional Black–Scholes-type model. The simulations are consistent with the theoretical estimates. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. The data were collected from 150 pilot participants working at airlines in Turkey using a survey data collection tool. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. This result shows that pilots continue to exhibit the same behavior by providing acceptable reasons rather than trying to eliminate negative situations by discussing them realistically. It was also observed that they tend to focus only on the objective aspects of events and avoid discussing the parts that negatively affect them psychologically. In addition, it was found that narcissistic personality traits negatively affect the communication and cooperation behaviors of pilots, and immature ego defense mechanisms are a precursor that strengthens the narcissistic personality. It is thought that examining narcissistic personality traits within the framework of immature ego defense mechanisms and managing these mechanisms effectively will contribute greatly to aviation psychology research to prevent risks related to the human factor, which airline companies and authorities view as an important risk within safety management systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)
abstract: Despite well-documented health and environmental benefits, increasing plant-based meal consumption remains challenging in meat-centric societies, reflecting complex socio-cognitive processes in translating intention into action. Grounded in the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA), this study examined plant-based meal consumption among young adults from the USA, Portugal, and the Netherlands who had not fully adopted a plant-based diet (N = 266). Using two waves one week apart, we estimated three structural models of plant-based meal consumption, controlling for prior behavior and common method variance. Findings were broadly consistent with HAPA. Action self-efficacy was most strongly associated with intention, which in turn was associated with action planning. Coping planning and self-monitoring pathways were not supported. While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. The findings highlight this volitional process in translating motivation into action and suggest interventions may benefit from strengthening efficacy beliefs and concrete planning strategies to support plant-based dietary change. © 2026

title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effect of China's 2020 digital transformation policy for state-owned enterprises on the production efficiency of listed electric enterprises. Treating the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model to measure production efficiency and a difference-in-differences model to examine the policy effect. The results show that the policy significantly improves the production efficiency of state-owned electric enterprises relative to non-state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects among utilities in eastern China, labor-intensive firms, and large firms. Mechanism analysis further shows that increased R&D investment is an important channel through which the policy generates efficiency gains, while managerial equity incentives strengthen policy effectiveness. The findings provide policy implications for utility digitalization, differentiated policy support, innovation incentives, and governance reform. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Under a common financing rule, two child-targeted policies raise the co-migration rate to a similar extent but differ sharply in welfare and mobility. Subsidizing co-migrating families in high-cost destinations generates 1.4 times as much welfare per unit of government revenue as removing migrant children's education-access wedges. These gains concentrate on recipients. Removing the education-access wedges delivers over four times the mobility gain per unit of revenue, and the resulting human capital generates growing welfare gains across generations. A broader reform that equalizes public-service access for all migrants is the most welfare-efficient but does not raise mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
