title: Layered Defect-Filling co-Assembled Carbazole-Based SAMs Deliver 20% Organic Solar Cells and 17% Mini-Modules
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-transport layers (HTLs) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet conventional single-component SAMs often form quasi-monolayers with incomplete coverage and interfacial defects that become increasingly detrimental upon device scaling. Here, we develop a co-assembled multilayered SAM (coSAMu) strategy that combines two SAM molecules, 2PACz and 2Cl-4PACz, with distinct dipoles and steric configurations through blend casting and sequential casting. Photoelectron spectroscopy, X-ray analysis, and molecular simulations support a layered structure in which a chemisorbed, 2PACz-rich bottom layer primarily sets the indium tin oxide (ITO) work function, while a 2Cl-4PACz-rich upper layer fills interfacial voids, improves molecular packing, and passivates defects. Consistent with this picture, coSAMu promotes a more favorable vertical composition near the ITO surface and suppresses trap-assisted recombination, enabling more efficient charge extraction and collection. Consequently, a representative D18:L8-BO OSC incorporating the sequential-cast coSAMu HTL achieves a power conversion efficiency of 20.1% (0.042 cm2), outperforming pristine 2PACz. Importantly, when scaled to a 17.14 cm2 mini-module (six serially connected subcells), coSAMu delivers 17.0% efficiency versus 12.2% for the 2PACz control. This work demonstrates controlled multilayer co-assembly as an effective strategy for scalable OSC interface engineering that is broadly applicable to multiple donor–acceptor systems. title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Extending ethanol energy fractions in ethanol-diesel dual-fuel combustion through EGR, intake conditions, and injection strategies
abstract: Misfire and excessive maximum pressure rise rates (MPRR) typically limit the ethanol energy fraction (EEF) in ethanol–diesel dual-fuel combustion. To extend the allowable EEF while maintaining combustion stability and acceptable MPRR, experiments were conducted on a medium-duty engine (1.1 L/cylinder) operating in intake-fumigation dual-fuel mode with ethanol and diesel. Tests at 6, 10, and 15 bar gross indicated mean effective pressure (IMEPg) evaluated the effects of EGR, intake conditions, diesel injection timing, rail pressure, and injection strategy on combustion, emissions, and efficiency. At 10 and 15 bar IMEPg, operation was primarily constrained by excessive MPRR. Under baseline conditions, maximum EEF was limited to 51 % at 10 bar IMEPg and 39 % at 15 bar IMEPg. Increasing EGR from 14 % to 48 % at 10 bar IMEPg reduced peak heat release rates, lowering MPRR below 5 bar/deg and extending achievable EEF to 82 %. Intake temperature influenced combustion phasing and burn rates; reducing intake temperature from 350 K to 330 K decreased MPRR and widened the allowable EEF range. At 6 bar IMEPg, operation was limited by misfire rather than MPRR. Stable combustion could not be sustained above 87 % EEF because high ethanol fractions suppressed diesel cool-flame reactivity. Increasing intake pressure improved combustion quality by advancing combustion phasing and increasing in-cylinder temperatures. Diesel injection timing and rail pressure were varied to assess diesel reactivity under high-EGR, high-EEF conditions. Lower rail pressures favored advanced injection timings because richer spray plumes promoted stronger early-stage reactivity, whereas higher rail pressures benefited from later injection timings to avoid excessive spray overmixing before ignition. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ensuring eco-resilience in Physical Internet-enabled production routing problem under ripple effect: a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach
abstract: Abstract: Resilience and eco-friendliness have emerged as two pivotal objectives for modern supply chains facing increasing disruptions and sustainability demands. The Physical Internet (PI), characterized by interconnectivity, resource sharing, and adaptability, represents a transformative approach to enhancing supply chain flexibility while mitigating environmental impacts. This study develops a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer optimization model to design a PI-enabled resilient production-routing system under the ripple effect. Furthermore, the model evaluates the influence of four distinct carbon policies, capturing the trade-offs between resilience and eco-friendliness. To address hybrid uncertainties arising from parameters, objectives, and constraints, this study proposes a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach. The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed model and solution approach are validated through a case study. The results demonstrate that the PI significantly enhances both resilience and environmental sustainability by optimizing vehicle utilization, a benefit that cannot be realized in traditional noncollaborative or collaborative supply chains. Moreover, the analysis reveals that as policymakers adopt more conservative approaches, both total costs and carbon emissions increase simultaneously. Furthermore, higher carbon prices and lower carbon emission caps do not always lead to lower carbon emissions. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Physiological and behavioral modeling of stress and cognitive load in web-based question answering
abstract: Time pressure and question difficulty can trigger stress and cognitive overload in web-based surveys, compromising data quality and user experience. Most stress detection methods are based on low-resolution self-reports, which are poorly suited for capturing fast, moment-to-moment changes during short online tasks. Addressing this gap, we conducted a 2 × 2 within-subjects study (N = 29), manipulating question difficulty and time pressure in a web-based multiple-choice questionnaire. Participants completed general knowledge and cognitive questions while we collected multimodal data: mouse dynamics, eye tracking, electrocardiogram, and electrodermal activity. Using condition-based and self-reported labels, we used statistical and machine learning models to model stress and question difficulty. Our results show distinct physiological and behavioral patterns within very short timeframes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of rapidly detecting cognitive-affective states in digital environments, paving the way for more adaptive, ethical, and user-aware survey interfaces. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: High-Conductivity and Moisture-Tolerant Sulfide Electrolyte Enabled by Bifunctional Coating for Practical All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
abstract: The pursuit of safer and higher-energy-density batteries has driven the advancement of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Among various material systems, sulfide solid-state electrolytes (SEs) stand out as highly promising candidates owing to their exceptional ionic conductivity. Nevertheless, their extreme sensitivity to moisture results in the release of toxic H2S and rapid structural degradation, which severely impedes their scalable manufacturing under ambient conditions. A bifunctional (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) coating strategy is herein presented to shield Li5.5PS4.5Cl0.8Br0.7 (LPSCBr) from moisture-induced degradation. The MPTMS layer forms a hydrophobic barrier of approximately 10 nm, which reduces H2S emission by 93.0% after 35 min of exposure to 30% relative humidity, while maintaining 83.1% of the initial ionic conductivity (10.8 mS cm−1). This approach tackles the core challenge associated with sulfide solid-state electrolytes: the realization of compatibility with controlled ambient air without sacrificing critical electrochemical properties. The modified electrolyte maintains a high ionic conductivity (> 5.7 mS cm−1) even after 10 h of air exposure. When applied in all-solid-state cells paired with LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.06O2 cathodes, it exhibits remarkable electrochemical performance, delivering a capacity retention of 84.6% after 1000 cycles. By enabling moisture-tolerant processing, MPTMS-modified LPSCBr SEs lay a solid foundation for the scalable, high-performance, and cost-effective production of ASSLBs. title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
abstract: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, legality, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints. © 2027 The author(s). title: Empirical Stage-Damage Functions for SME Content Losses in Australian Flood Vulnerability Assessment
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) dominate Australian business activity, yet empirically calibrated functions for nonresidential flood-related contents losses remain limited. Postevent surveys of 185 SMEs across 12 business types and 14 towns affected by the February-April 2022 Northern Rivers floods were used to derive stage-damage functions for stock, equipment, and fit-out. Contents-specific damage indices combined peak internal flood depth (0-6 m, relative to finished-floor level) with self-reported losses and preevent replacement values. Pooled curves were fitted using LOESS and a beta-family generalized additive model (Beta-GAM); a hierarchical Beta-GAM (HBGAM) generated business-type functions under partial pooling, while random forest and XGBoost provided depth-only predictive benchmarks. Across the pooled models, performance on the corresponding within-event 25% holdout sets was moderate (R2=0.57-0.69; RMSE=0.23-0.27), and neither machine-learning benchmark consistently improved performance. The Beta-GAM was retained because it provided smooth, bounded, interpretable relationships, model-based and bootstrap uncertainty intervals, and extractable threshold depths. The fitted mean damage index reached 0.50 at 1.03 m for stock, 1.09 m for equipment, and 1.27 m for fit-out, with uncertainty generally increasing above 3 m as data density declined. HBGAM-derived D50 values ranged from 0.66 to 1.18 m for stock, 0.81 to 1.18 m for equipment, and 1.09 to 1.48 m for fit-out, indicating model-derived sector variation. These event-calibrated functions support screening-level relative SME contents-loss assessment and evaluation of loss-reduction options in comparable settings; application elsewhere requires external validation or local recalibration. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. title: Breaking the Specific Capacity Limit: 409% Boost in Manganese-Based Redox Flow Batteries at High Current Densities with a MnO2Semi-Solid Slurry Electrolyte
abstract: The common-ion effect of SO42− limits the solubility of MnSO4 to ≤ 1 M in conventional H2SO4 electrolytes, resulting in low specific capacity of manganese (Mn)-based redox flow batteries (RFBs). Although MnO2 semi-solid RFBs are expected to improve the specific capacity, the sluggish electrochemical reaction kinetics leads to low operating current densities (≤ 1 mA cm−2). Herein, we employ a reverse-design strategy by introducing additional high-concentration MnO2 into the conventional Mn-based electrolyte. Leveraging the MnO2/Mn2+ electrochemical reaction successfully circumvents the common-ion effect, raising the concentration of soluble Mn species in the electrolyte to 3.76 M and achieving a specific capacity of 156.2 Ah LCatholyte-1 —a 409% increment over reported MnSO4-based electrolytes. Subsequently, the reverse disproportionation of electrolytic MnO2 generated during the second charging cycle shifts the redox mechanism from the MnO2(s)/Mn2+ couple to the solution-phase Mn3+(aq)/Mn2+ pair. This transformation not only elevates the discharge voltage but also enables stable operation at 30 mA cm−2, representing a current density 30-fold higher than reported Mn-based semi-solid RFBs. This work demonstrates a rational design strategy for semi-solid slurry electrolytes to enhance the specific capacity of RFBs, thereby advancing their applicability in grid-scale renewable energy storage. title: Cultural value configurations and guests’ evaluations of AI-enabled service technologies
abstract: As Artificial Intelligence reshapes hospitality service delivery, understanding how culturally diverse guests evaluate AI-enabled encounters is critical. This study examines how cultural value configurations shape evaluations of service robots in hotels. Cultural value configurations are coherent combinations of orientations that jointly influence how individuals interpret and assess service encounters. Using more than 3000 robot-related hotel reviews from guests across 77 countries, we integrate Hofstede's dimensions with Schwartz's value theory to explain cross-cultural differences in sentiment. Masculinity and uncertainty avoidance predict more negative sentiment, individualism shows a positive association that is sensitive to model specification, and power distance shows no direct effect. One configuration is robust: masculinity combined with uncertainty avoidance amplifies dissatisfaction, and this interaction holds under multilevel and combined estimation and survives correction for multiple testing. Two further configurations remain suggestive: power distance combined with uncertainty avoidance attenuates risk aversion, and individualism combined with masculinity increases tolerance for imperfection. Both are marginal and do not persist under multilevel or joint estimation, so we report them as patterns for replication rather than as established effects. Hofstede's indices provide the measurement, while Schwartz's value theory serves as an interpretive lens rather than as a measured individual-level construct. Findings position culture as a configurational system and provide guidance for AI service design and communication. © 2026 The Authors

title: A graph model for conflict resolution incorporating movement willingness intensity under linguistic uncertainty
abstract: In the graph model for conflict resolution (GMCR), decision-makers (DMs) are required to express their preferences over feasible conflict states. Under uncertainty, however, such preferences are often difficult to quantify precisely and are more naturally represented by linguistic preference relations. To address this issue, this study develops a linguistic GMCR framework. Four linguistic stability concepts, namely linguistic Nash stability, linguistic sequential stability, linguistic symmetric metarationality, and linguistic general metarationality, are defined in logical form for general multi-DM conflicts. Corresponding matrix-based representations are then derived to facilitate stability computation. To capture heterogeneity in DMs’ willingness to transition between states, the framework is further extended by introducing a two-degree linguistic preference structure with two flexible formulations of the linguistic satisficing threshold. This extension distinguishes strong and mild transition willingness and yields three classes of linguistic stability, namely general linguistic stability, strong linguistic stability, and weak linguistic stability. The proposed framework is applied to the Elmira groundwater contamination conflict to demonstrate its practical applicability. Sensitivity and comparative analyses show that the two-degree linguistic framework identifies differentiated stability patterns that cannot be captured by single-threshold approaches, thereby providing a more refined basis for conflict diagnosis and resolution under linguistic uncertainty and heterogeneous transition willingness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: MAGE: A structural-prior-guided graph-language multimodal framework for business process anomaly detection
abstract: Business process event logs record activities, resources, timestamps, and other process attributes, and therefore provide the basis for trace-level anomaly detection. Existing methods often lack a unified reference for normal behavior and do not explicitly coordinate structural deviations with semantic information. We propose MAGE, a structural-prior-guided graph-enhanced language embedding framework for business process anomaly detection. MAGE first constructs structural priors solely from normal traces in the training set, including normal directly-follows relations, trace-length statistics, and adjacent-event resource-switching statistics. It then compares each trace with these priors to generate structural deviation signals and constructs both an activity-resource-time-slice heterogeneous graph and a structure-aware textual representation. A heterogeneous graph Transformer extracts structural representations, while a LoRA-adapted Qwen3 model extracts semantic representations. Gated cross-attention fuses the two modalities for trace-level anomaly classification. The structural prior and graph self-supervised pretraining use only normal training traces, whereas the final multimodal classifier is jointly optimized on labeled training samples. Experiments on synthetic logs and public real event logs with controlled anomaly injection show that MAGE achieves the highest mean F1-scores of 0.872 and 0.860, respectively, among the compared methods under the evaluated settings. Ablation results further indicate that the structural prior, heterogeneous graph encoding, structure-aware prompting, and cross-modal fusion each contribute positively to F1-score under the evaluated settings. Together, these findings provide evidence for combining normal-process structural constraints with language-based semantic information in trace-level business process anomaly detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From generative AI usage to entrepreneurial intention: The sequential roles of task and social self-efficacy
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is rapidly evolving and creating new possibilities for supporting students' entrepreneurial development. However, limited research has examined how GAI usage is associated with entrepreneurial intention (EI) through specific psychological pathways. Drawing on self-efficacy theory, this study examines the relationship between GAI usage and EI, focusing on the mediating roles of task and social self-efficacy. Using survey data from 521 Chinese university students, this study empirically tests the proposed model. The results show that GAI usage is positively associated with students' task and social self-efficacy. However, task self-efficacy (TSE) is not directly associated with EI. In contrast, social self-efficacy (SSE) accounts for a significant indirect association between GAI usage and EI. Moreover, a significant sequential indirect association is observed, linking GAI usage with EI through TSE and SSE. By disentangling the distinct roles of TSE and SSE, this study shows that the association between GAI usage and EI is consistent with pathways that differ in their functions and proximity to entrepreneurial action. The findings also provide practical insights for entrepreneurship education and AI-supported learning environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: What Strategies Can Payers Use to Negotiate Medicine Prices Globally? Insights and Lessons for Low-Income Countries from a Scoping Review
abstract: Objectives No comprehensive global review has synthesized mechanisms, strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges of pharmaceutical pricing policies. This scoping review aimed to examine global pharmaceutical pricing policies and generate policy-relevant insights, particularly for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods Electronic searches were conducted in Medline, CINAHL, EconLit, and Embase using predefined inclusion criteria. Gray literature was identified through government publications and World Health Organization reports, and reference lists of relevant studies were screened. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines. Results Searches conducted up to May 2024 and updated in February 2026 identified 88 eligible studies. Reference pricing was the most commonly reported strategy, used in 85% of identified countries, offering simplicity and transparency through price benchmarking. Value-based pricing was widely adopted in high-income countries, aligning prices with health outcomes but requiring strong health technology assessment infrastructure. Managed entry agreements were reported in 56% of countries and were used to improve access to new medicines while mitigating financial risk. Indication-specific pricing was implemented in 9 countries but faced operational challenges. Compulsory licensing in several LMICs improved access to essential medicines at lower cost, although concerns regarding impacts on pharmaceutical innovation were noted. Most countries combined multiple pricing approaches to balance affordability, access, and innovation. Conclusions Although value-based pricing and managed entry agreements are common in high-income settings, simpler approaches such as reference pricing and compulsory licensing may be more feasible in LMICs. Context-specific strategies are needed to balance access, affordability, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From waste to Watts: Causal evidence on AI-enabled waste-to-energy and financial performance in tourism and hospitality using an empirics-first investigation
abstract: This study examines whether artificial intelligence enabled waste to energy adoption improves financial performance in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms and identifies the mechanisms and conditions shaping these effects. Using an empirics first mixed methods design, we combine interviews with 41 managers and a firm year panel of United Kingdom listed tourism, travel, and hospitality firms from 2015 to 2025. Difference in differences models with firm and year fixed effects show that adoption is associated with significantly higher financial performance, particularly at greater levels of adoption intensity. The findings indicate that energy cost savings and operational efficiency partially explain these gains. Performance benefits are also stronger in firms with higher baseline waste intensity and during periods of elevated energy prices. The study demonstrates that AI enabled waste to energy functions as an operational capability that can generate measurable economic value when integrated into organisational routines and governance systems. © 2026 The Author.

title: Chefs, kitchens, and stars: A literature review of fine dining in hospitality and management studies
abstract: Fine dining represents a niche within the restaurant industry, yet it has garnered significant attention from both scholars and practitioners. Fine dining, due to its distinctive characteristics - such as extreme creativity and innovation, adherence to strict institutional logics, a rigorous system of social evaluation from customers and critics, and the juxtaposition of artistic logics and commercial logics - is a compelling setting for hospitality and management scholars. However, fine dining literature is quite fragmented. Drawing on a thematic analysis of 101 articles, this literature review provides scholars with five thematic clusters that emerged: (1) Work environment and career path; (2) Creativity and innovation; (3) Social evaluation and institutional logics; (4) Customer experience and engagement; (5) Entrepreneurship and business model innovation. Moreover, by presenting tensions among the clusters and illustrating gaps and opportunities in the methodological approach, this literature review develops a prospective research agenda for hospitality and management scholars. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Understanding the mixed consequences of diversity practices: A typology of migrant employees
abstract: Organizational diversity practices are widely implemented to support the workplace integration of international migrants (IMs), yet their outcomes remain inconsistent. Little is known about why IMs respond differently to the same initiatives offered by their organizations or why these practices sometimes fail or backfire. Drawing on signaling and attribution theory, we argue that IMs interpret diversity practices through the lens of two key disadvantages: unfamiliarity with the destination country and exposure to discrimination within this context. We develop a dual disadvantage typology of IMs and theorize how resource and nondiscrimination practices differentially affect organizational commitment depending on migrants’ disadvantage configurations. This typology refines existing diversity frameworks by introducing a configurational view of migrant diversity and explaining why identical practices may produce divergent outcomes. Using survey data from 394 IMs working in Germany, we find that while nondiscrimination practices are consistently positively associated with commitment, the effects of resource practices vary: some IMs view them as empowering, while others interpret them as stigmatizing or misaligned with their needs. In particular, training initiatives can backfire for IMs who are already familiar with the labor market and face discrimination. Our findings demonstrate the importance of tailoring initiatives to different migrant groups. We contribute a theory-driven framework that explains how diversity signals are differentially interpreted across migrant disadvantage configurations and when diversity practices produce intended versus unintended effects. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Spatial trajectories and land-use potential of China's utility-scale photovoltaic expansion toward 2035
abstract: China aims to reach 3600 GW of combined wind and solar capacity by 2035, requiring substantial expansion of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) deployment. Quantifying the geospatial footprint of this expansion is essential for sustainable land-use planning and ecological protection. This study develops a nationwide assessment framework that integrates multi-source remote sensing observations, Random Forest (RF) suitability modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for model interpretation, and scenario-based spatial allocation. Historical PV data from 2000 to 2025 show that China's utility-scale PV farms expanded to 13,800 km2, with growth concentrated in northwestern mega-bases and emerging decentralized installations in central-eastern regions, indicating a dual-track spatial trajectory. Scenario projections suggest that Scenario B (NDC Update-Aligned Pathway) requires an additional 21,420 km2, whereas Scenario C (Wind-Slowdown Compensation) increases land demand moderately to 24,405 km2. Scenario A (Business as Usual) could require up to 63,990 km2 and would disproportionately affect croplands and forests. However, China retains more than 206,000 km2 of high-potential land, indicating that ecological conflicts are driven mainly by spatial mismatch rather than absolute land scarcity. These findings underscore the need for integrated spatial governance, optimized ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission, and distributed PV deployment. By linking observed spatial trajectories, interpretable suitability modeling, and capacity-to-land translation, this study provides a transferable framework for assessing the land-use potential of utility-scale PV expansion toward 2035. © 2026

title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Decarbonization within racial capitalism continues to reproduce extractivist inequalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evaluating visitor satisfaction in protected areas: a case study of Samaria National Park
abstract: This study examines visitor satisfaction in the Samaria National Park, Crete, Greece, focusing on the pre and post-COVID-19 pandemic periods. Utilizing data from 2018 to 2022 and employing the Multi-Criteria Satisfaction Analysis (MUSA) method, we evaluated various aspects influencing visitor experiences, such as available time, landscape quality, safety, and local businesses. The findings indicate a consistently high overall satisfaction, with notable variations in the importance and satisfaction levels of specific criteria across different years since the pandemic brought a shift in visitor priorities. This paper also discusses the implications of these findings for park management, highlighting the need for tailored strategies to maintain high visitor satisfaction and promote sustainable tourism. The study underscores the critical role of protected areas in offering safe and enriching experiences. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: International scaling of social innovations through digitalization: A 3D framework
abstract: Social enterprises that embed social innovations (SIs) play a critical role in advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), representing an estimated US$12 trillion market opportunity. Yet, how SIs internationalize in the presence of institutional voids remains underexplored in international business research. Using a history-to-theory and history-in-theory approach, this study examines how dynamic capabilities and digitalization enable the international scaling of SIs. We find that international diffusion depends on capabilities such as boundary spanning, international sensing, legitimacy building, business diplomacy, and market shaping. Digitalization accelerates scaling, contingent on factors including timing, resources, intellectual property ownership, purpose, and technology scope. Our findings also suggest that traditional internationalization metrics—such as exports, FDI, subsidiaries, and foreign sales—do not adequately capture SI internationalization. Instead, internationalization is reflected in the cross-border diffusion of innovations and social impact, alongside the ability to attract international funding, partnerships, talent, and legitimacy while balancing social impact with financial sustainability. title: Exploring the key drivers of biogas adoption: a business model for livestock farmers in developing countries
abstract: The increasing number of livestock farms, coupled with inadequate waste management infrastructure, has become a growing concern, contributing to environmental pollution and productivity loss. Biogas technology presents a viable solution to address these challenges by transforming waste into a sustainable energy source. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the key factors influencing the adoption intention of biogas technology as a business Model among livestock farmers. Employing a purposive sampling approach, this study gathered data from 336 livestock farmers. To ensure a comprehensive analysis, a combined methodological framework integrating both symmetric and asymmetric techniques was utilized, providing a profound understanding of the determinants impacting the intention to adopt biogas technology. This study observes a notable consistency between the findings derived from PLS-SEM and ANN. The analysis indicates that awareness of consequences (AOC) significantly influences ascription of responsibility (AOR). Additionally, findings indicate that personal norms are significantly shaped by herd mentality, initial cost, AOC, AOR, and self-esteem. Furthermore, herd mentality, personal norms, and self-esteem are significantly associated with biogas adoption. However, no significant association was found between perceived ease of use and personal norms. Meanwhile, findings from the fsQCA revealed eight distinct pathways leading to a strong intention to adopt biogas, highlighting herd mentality and AOC as critical prerequisites. Insights gained from this study will be instrumental for stakeholders involved in shaping policies, making investments, and providing technological assistance for the effective installation and operation of biogas technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The role of deontological morality in shaping demand within the sharing economy
abstract: This study examines how deontological and consequentialist appeals in Airbnb host self-descriptions relate to trust-related attention and marketplace performance. Study 1 combines a five-city listing panel with third-party New York property-month records; Study 2 analyzes a behavioral highlighting task. In the five-city models, deontology was negatively associated with Expected Demand and Expected Income, but its interactions with deontological sentiment were positive, indicating a framing-dependent pattern. In a six-month New York DID-style pre/post comparison under conditional parallel trends, entropy-balanced ATT weighting indicated 18.6% higher monthly revenue for positive deontological but not positive consequentialist baseline framing relative to neither-positive framing (nominal p = .038). The corresponding ATO estimate was 14.0% for the covariate-overlap population (nominal p = .042), not an independent replication. In Study 2, participants identified trust-eliciting content more often in deontological than consequentialist descriptions; the retained data support differential attention, not a causal effect on trust or booking behavior. The New York estimand concerns a bundled baseline language state, not the effect of editing language; its interpretation is conditional, and neither revenue estimate survived multiplicity adjustment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Factors associated with perceived frugal-innovation capability in traditional craft villages: A respondent-level PLS-SEM study in Hanoi, Vietnam
abstract: Frugal innovation is increasingly treated as a capability for developing affordable, resource-efficient, and context-appropriate solutions, yet its antecedents remain fragmented across the literature and are insufficiently examined in community-embedded craft production. This study evaluates two connected sets of respondent-level associations in traditional craft villages in Hanoi, Vietnam. The resource-recombination route links perceived empowering leadership, knowledge management, organic innovative culture, and network embeddedness with bricolage and, in turn, perceived frugal-innovation capability. The institution-market route links network embeddedness with perceived government support, perceived customer requirements, customer participation, and frugal-innovation capability. A cross-sectional survey produced 432 returned questionnaires; 416 retained cases were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). All constructs are interpreted as respondents’ perceptions of practices and conditions in their focal production or business units rather than as objective organization-level measures. Bricolage had the largest direct association with perceived frugal-innovation capability (β = 0.441), and empowering leadership had the largest association with bricolage (β = 0.492). Network embeddedness was associated with several specific indirect routes, while perceived government support was associated with frugal-innovation capability both directly and through customer-facing constructs. The model explained 52.5% of the adjusted variance in perceived frugal-innovation capability. The findings support a resource-conversion interpretation centered on bricolage, but the cross-sectional, single-source design does not establish temporal mediation or causal effects. The craft-village setting informs interpretation; heritage preservation, cultural authenticity, and objective resource scarcity were not directly measured and therefore remain boundary conditions for future research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Navigating travel paradoxes: Gen Z coping responses and implications for destination management
abstract: Paradoxes involve contradictory yet interdependent poles that persist rather than disappearing when one side is chosen. Tourism routinely exposes travelers to such tensions, but traveler-level paradoxes and the responses used to navigate them remain underexamined. Using the early tourism-recovery period of 2022 as the empirical context, this study examines paradoxical tensions perceived by young adult Gen Z student travelers and how they respond to them. A two-stage qualitative design was employed. Study A recruited 98 Norwegian Gen Z student travelers, of whom 95 provided useable responses; Study B recruited 48 Gen Z student travelers from the United Kingdom and the United States, of whom 46 provided useable responses. Online open-ended essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, with constant comparison used as an iterative coding technique. Four persistent traveler-perceived tensions emerged: personal travel fulfillment versus environmental responsibility, community economic benefit versus community livability, business recovery versus service-capacity strain, and travel maximization versus travel restraint. Responses clustered into four types: integrative or balancing, prioritization, avoidance or resignation, and externalization or delegation. These responses did not permanently resolve the paradoxes; instead, they temporarily stabilized the tension, privileged one pole, reproduced it, or displaced responsibility. The study therefore positions the 2022 recovery period as an external intensifying condition that made enduring tensions especially visible and connects traveler paradox management to destination governance and shared responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Enhancing wind energy forecasting under constrained data conditions: a CRISP-DM-based deep neural network approach
abstract: Accurate forecasting of wind energy production plays a crucial role in the efficient operation of energy markets. However, many advanced models depend on extensive datasets and detailed meteorological information that are rarely available in industrial environments. This work investigates short-term wind power forecasting under constrained industrial conditions, including limited data availability, incomplete high-resolution meteorological information, and noisy operational measurements. A Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM)-based workflow is adopted to support data preprocessing, model training, and validation throughout the forecasting process. An openly available dataset containing hourly records from multiple European wind farms is used, focusing on a single wind farm subset to evaluate forecasting performance under realistic single-site deployment conditions. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model combined with lag-based and nonlinear feature engineering techniques is implemented to capture operational relationships without relying on complete external meteorological fields. Experimental results show that feedforward architectures can provide competitive forecasting performance under constrained data scenarios. The findings highlight the importance of balancing model complexity, data availability, robust validation, and deployability in real-world wind energy forecasting applications. © 2026

title: GenAI support to the rescue: Mitigating employees’ psychological stress following tourism service recovery
abstract: Growing evidence suggests that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has a notable impact on employees' attitudes and behaviors, yet its potential to mitigate psychological stress remains underexplored. Combining conservation of resources (COR) theory with the “computers are social actors” (CASA) paradigm, this study investigates whether and how GenAI support (emotional versus informational) reduces tourism employees' post-recovery psychological stress. The results show that: (1) GenAI support effectively alleviates such stress following tourism service recovery; (2) emotional (vs. informational) support exerts a stronger stress-alleviating effect, which is serially mediated by social presence and emotional energy; (3) framing GenAI as an assistant (vs. a friend) further amplifies the relative effectiveness of emotional over informational support. This study enriches the understanding of GenAI's benefits and extends the workplace support literature. It also offers actionable insights into leveraging digital support tools to manage employee stress in tourism workplaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Ultralow Noise Orthogonal Fluxgates Enabling Weak Magnetic Field and Biomolecular Detection
abstract: Noninvasive detection of ultra-weak biomagnetic signals is crucial for modern biosensing, but conventional magnetic sensors are fundamentally limited by intrinsic noise. Orthogonal fluxgates (OFGs) enable high signal-to-noise-ratio detection of weak magnetic fields, yet their performance is still constrained by intrinsic 1/f noise and Barkhausen-related magnetic fluctuations. This study reports a low-noise orthogonal fluxgate in which a newly designed magnetic core and circuit mitigate existing noise limitations. The CoP/Ag composite core, featuring an amorphous-nanocrystalline dual phase, is associated with reduced low-frequency magnetic loss and improved noise performance. When integrated with a closed-loop feedback, the sensor achieves a noise floor of 8 pT/√Hz at 1 Hz. The sensor enables reliable detection of ultralow-concentration magnetic-bead signals. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was used as a model biomarker in an immunomagnetic bead assay, yielding a linear response from 50 fg mL−1 to 100 ng mL−1 and a detection limit of 50 fg mL−1, which compares favorably with representative reported AFP magnetic biosensors. OFGs demonstrate strong prospects in biosensing, geomagnetic measurements, and weak field detection. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Direct Technology Diffusion in Higher Education: Evidence from Doctoral Students
abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Using a quantitative survey of research scholars, the study finds that direct diffusion significantly improves outcomes. Similarity levels decreased substantially under direct diffusion, indicating more accurate application of plagiarism rules. Additionally, direct diffusion reduced the time required and lowered costs considerably. The findings suggest that direct access empowers users, minimizes intermediary-related inefficiencies, and enhances both effectiveness and efficiency. The study highlights cost-effectiveness as a key enabler and recommends that policymakers and institutions promote direct technology diffusion to improve adoption and strengthen academic integrity in higher education. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Assessment innovation in management education: Authentic assessment evaluation to develop workplace-ready graduates
abstract: Authentic assessment is increasingly seen as essential in management education for aligning assessment tasks with the complex, collaborative, and uncertain, multi-stakeholder demands of modern workplaces. This paper argues that, despite its popularity, the impact of authentic assessment on graduate preparedness remains poorly understood. To address this, the paper builds and evaluates an integrative model relating authentic assessment design, feedback and reflection, perceptions of assessment value, professional self-efficacy, and perceived workplace outcomes among management students. Drawing on literature about authentic assessment, experiential learning, situated cognition, assessment for learning, and employability, the paper frames authentic assessment as a holistic pedagogical system. A cross-sectional survey of 412 undergraduate and postgraduate students in business and management at four universities provides the empirical basis. The instrument was honed through expert review and a pilot test, and analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity checks, correlations, and hierarchical regression and mediation tests. The findings show that authentic assessment design strongly correlates with workplace readiness, especially when dialogic feedback, reflection, and professional self-efficacy are present. External audience group projects, live case analysis, simulations, and portfolio-based evaluation proved effective with clear criteria and guided post-task reflection. The paper contributes a process model and actionable design principles for educators to enhance employability through meaningful assessment, advancing the discourse on management education. © 2026

title: Time for challenge, money for relaxation: The resource-activity fit in tourism
abstract: Although money and time are essential resources that influence consumer decision-making, research has mostly ignored how resource concept activation affects tourists' decisions in the context of tourism. Drawing on mental simulation theory, this study investigates how activating time versus money resource concepts influences tourists' preferences for different types of tourism activities. Across three experiments, the results show that when the concept of time is activated, tourists report stronger preferences for challenging activities, whereas when the concept of money is activated, they report stronger preferences for relaxing activities. Outcome-focused simulation mediates the relationship between time activation and challenging activity preference, whereas process-focused simulation mediates the relationship between money activation and relaxing activity preference. These indirect pathways are further conditioned by maximization: the time-related pathway becomes stronger as maximization increases, whereas the money-related pathway becomes weaker. The results offer practical implications for tourism destinations that can tailor marketing strategies based on tourists’ decision-making tendencies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
abstract: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. However, conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face inherent limitations at low temperatures by intrinsic hurdle of poor ionic mobility in liquid electrolytes. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), which replace liquid electrolytes with non-flammable and non-freezing solid electrolytes, are considered promising alternatives because these solid electrolytes provide high ionic conductivity at low temperatures, superior temperature stability, and exceptional safety. ASSBs still face practical limitations at extremely low temperatures due to degradation caused by interfacial side reactions and mechanical instabilities that increase resistance and polarization. Addressing these challenges is critical to realize the advantages of ASSBs and enable their practical deployment in low-temperature applications. This review provides an overview of historical developments, critical challenges, and recent progress in advancing the low-temperature performance of ASSBs. The key components of ASSBs, including solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, are systematically investigated to develop strategies for improving ASSBs at low temperatures. By highlighting future perspectives, we emphasize both the potential and necessity of ASSBs to overcome the intrinsic limitations of LIBs and ensure reliable energy storage in harsh environments. title: Trustworthy artificial intelligence in advanced manufacturing
abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). title: From Screening to Site Control: Phytic-Acid Mediated P-Tuning of M–N Coordination to Balance Iodine Adsorption and Stability in Zn–I2 Batteries
abstract: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries (AZIBs) show promise for grid-scale energy storage, but they are hampered by polyiodide shuttling, sluggish iodine redox kinetics, and irreversible active-site poisoning caused by uncontrolled adsorption. We provide a comprehensive screening of M1 (M1 = P, S, B) heteroatom dopants, and P is identified as the best candidate for achieving coordination-tuned, moderate adsorption that balances adsorption and catalytic activity while mitigating site poisoning. Using phytic acid as both the P source and an etchant, we create a universal in situ approach to core–shell single-atom catalysts (M2-P-CSNC, M2 = Fe, Co, Ni). The unique core–shell structure achieves stable confinement of polyiodides, rapid ion transport, and protection of active sites, while in situ P doping precisely regulates the local electronic environment and d-band center of the Fe–Nx active centers. In situ characterization confirms that Fe–P-CSNC has a strong reversible anchoring ability for polyiodides, which can significantly accelerate redox kinetics. The optimized Fe–P-CSNC/I2 exhibits almost no capacity decay after 20,000 cycles at a current density of 2 A g−1. This work’s facile heteroatom doping strategy for electronic modulation offers a reference for high-performance catalyst design in conversion-type energy storage systems. (Figure presented.) title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in East Java Non-Profit Organizations
abstract: Non-profit organizations in East Java need dependable electricity for service continuity, daily operations, and cost control, yet face capital, regulatory, behavioral, and tropical-climate barriers to rooftop solar photovoltaic adoption. This study combines a focused literature review, bibliometric mapping of 25 verified domain studies selected from 79 unique Scopus records, a random-effects synthesis of five Global Solar Atlas locations, and a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo model for a common 12 kWp system. The 25 studies met predefined adoption, finance/policy, governance/behavior, and tropical-performance criteria and passed metadata verification. Modeled annual output ranges from 17.231 to 18.227 MWh; pooled yield is 4.03 kWh/kWp/day (95% CI: 3.92–4.14). Median NPV is IDR 40.7–54.9 million, with a conditional positive-NPV probability of 86.4–92.5%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate, tariff escalation, capital cost, avoided electricity value, and self-consumption as the dominant drivers of NPV. The five-city results are screening evidence, not a representation of all tropical climates or roofs. A 30% grant or blended-finance contribution raises positive-NPV probability above 99.8% and reduces median payback to 5.8–6.2 years. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. .

title: Developing and validating a scenario-based evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services
abstract: As population aging and digital transformation advance, IPTV has become an important media platform for older adults. However, mismatches between interface design and older users’ capabilities continue to limit effective use. This study develops and validates a contextualized evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services. Policy review, interviews with older users, and regional case analysis were conducted to identify eight typical IPTV usage scenarios and construct an initial indicator pool. A two-round Delphi consultation refined the framework, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) determined indicator weights. The final framework comprises five primary dimensions and 22 secondary indicators. Evaluation of three provincial IPTV projects showed that security management, functional operation, and service quality are the highest priorities for improving user experience, whereas content format and product characteristics support initial adoption. Interviews further revealed that limited stakeholder coordination and delays between user feedback and system updates constrain age-friendly implementation. The proposed framework quantifies the alignment between older users’ capabilities and large-screen interaction while tracing usability problems to specific usage contexts. It also informs optimization through hierarchical support, progressive capability support, and social support mechanisms. The scenario-based indicators can be adapted to local technical infrastructures, service processes, and user behaviors, supporting localized application across diverse large-screen media ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: How have flight operations between China and Europe changed since the Russia–Ukraine war?
abstract: This study examines how direct flight services between China and Europe changed during the COVID-19 pandemic and after the Russia–Ukraine war began in February 2022. We use monthly airport pair–airline data from January 2014 to September 2024. Our baseline model is a panel regression with route fixed effects. As a robustness check, we also estimate a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) specification with route and period fixed effects. After February 2022, passenger traffic fell and yields rose on the sampled routes, and these changes differed between European and Chinese carriers. In the baseline route fixed-effects model, European carriers had approximately 32.7% lower revenue passenger miles and 14.4% lower yields than Chinese carriers during the war period, relative to pre-war differences. The TWFE specification gives interaction estimates of similar sign and magnitude. These differences arose at the same time as the closure of Russian airspace to European carriers and are consistent with the longer routings that other studies document, together with other concurrent factors. During the COVID-19 period, passenger traffic fell sharply. Yields rose in the pooled sample but not in either travel direction separately, which is consistent with unequal travel demand in the two directions. Taken together, these findings highlight persistent vulnerabilities in the China–Europe aviation market and point to potential airline strategies, including greater operational flexibility, service enhancements, code-sharing arrangements, and bilateral coordination, that may strengthen market resilience. title: Inclusive education as organizational inclusion: Creating inclusive business schools through co-curricular learning
abstract: Knowing how to create inclusive business schools is crucial for the development of leaders navigating the workforce. This research examines co-curricular First-Year Experience (FYE) programming as an approach to supporting student integration, learning, and experiences. Using a quasi-experimental design, two studies examined academic performance and perceived transition success, belonging, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and time management behaviours across in-person and online learning contexts. In Study 1, in-person students demonstrated higher academic performance and perceived transition success than online students. At the end of the semester, online and in-person students were comparable in outcome expectations, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management. General belonging was lower among online students across the two measurement occasions however, this difference was already present at baseline and did not change significantly over time. General belonging, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management were positively associated with perceived transition success, whereas outcome expectations were not a significant unique correlate. Study 2 identified exploratory within-format patterns across co-curricular in-person, bespoke in-person, and bespoke online course formats, with university belonging emerging as a significant correlate of perceived transition success across all three. Together, these findings position co-curricular and bespoke FYE approaches as promising frameworks for supporting inclusive business education while highlighting the central role of belonging in students’ transition experiences. © 2026 The Authors

title: Navigating the successful digital transformation of correctional services: Challenges, good governance, and a hybrid framework
abstract: Digital transformation initiatives are essential for advancing correctional services toward digital maturity in Macao. However, the absence of a well-defined overarching strategy presents a significant impediment to the effective implementation of reforms. Due to the fact that the intelligent construction of the penal system has not yet been integrated with the extant eGovernment, the governance of the correctional system and its capabilities necessitate rigorous enhancement. Good governance encompasses legitimacy, accountability, transparency, capacity, fairness, responsiveness, participation, and consensus, which are widely considered core principles of public administration and are well-suited to linking the vision of digital transformation and smart correction initiatives. Based on the practice of eGovernment in Macao, which aspects can facilitate the digital transformation of correctional services to enhance the modernization of governance systems and capabilities, and achieve good governance? This study employs qualitative research methods, including a comprehensive literature review, secondary data collection, and analysis of legal documents, regulations, and sentencing policies within the Macao penal system. A SWOT-Plus analysis is conducted to assess potential internal and external trends and identify extant challenges. A hybrid framework is proposed that incorporates the incentives for eGovernment and the fundamental principles of good governance, including key governance beliefs and values such as organization, process, regulation, and culture. The findings also outline a series of expected impacts on correctional services that navigate the transformation ideology and foster successful implementation, thereby coordinating the vision of smart government. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Reputation and value signals as moderators of advertising spend efficiency in E commerce search advertising
abstract: China hosts the world's largest e‑commerce search advertising market, yet merchants persistently misallocate advertising budgets by treating ad spend as a monotonic driver of sales efficiency. Drawing on the Resource‑Based View (RBV) and Information Overload Theory, this study investigates how advertising spend intensity (ASI) affects two core efficiency metrics—the Ad‑to‑Sales Ratio (ASR) and Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), as well as the moderating roles of two structural market factors. Keyword Specificity (KS) reflects the semantic breadth of keywords ranging from generic terms to long‑tail queries, whereas Category Competition Intensity (CCI) captures the density of competing products within each keyword market. Based on keyword‑level panel advertising data from a home appliances and household goods retailer operating on China's leading business‑to‑consumer platform, alongside supplementary observational data on competing products, this study identifies an inverted‑U‑shaped relationship between ASI and both ASR and ROAS: advertising efficiency improves with greater spending initially but declines after crossing a category‑specific threshold. KS shifts the efficiency peak toward higher spend levels, meaning long‑tail keywords can maintain efficiency under greater advertising investment. By contrast, CCI compresses this optimal spending range and triggers earlier efficiency deterioration in highly competitive categories. These findings extend the RBV and Information Overload Theory to sponsored‑search research and provide keyword‑type and competition‑dependent spending benchmarks for practitioners in Chinese e‑commerce. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
