title: Learn AI with AI: Designing conversational agents to support older adults in learning about AI
abstract: Older adults are motivated to develop AI literacy and consider it important. Prior research suggests that conversational agents can support older adults’ AI literacy learning by simplifying AI concepts and providing interactive learning experiences. However, little is known about how such agents should be designed to address the learning challenges older adults face. To address this, we interviewed nine older adults to explore their challenges and identify design opportunities. Findings revealed affective barriers related to confidence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of peer-like characteristics in agents, such as reciprocal knowledge sharing. Guided by these insights, we designed a peer-like agent and compared it with a website and an assistant agent in a between-subjects study with 45 older adults learning about deepfakes. Results showed that the peer agent fostered higher engagement and supported confidence more than the others. We conclude with design recommendations for conversational agents to support older adults’ AI learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. A mixed-methods case study design integrated qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine stakeholder perspectives. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Production decisions of a leasing-selling closed-loop supply chain under different authorization strategies
abstract: Leasing or selling, when to choose which? This paper investigates the production decisions of a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) considering authorized remanufacturing (royalty/fixed-fee authorization) under different business mode combinations. Furthermore, win–win authorization strategies for the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the third-party remanufacturer (TPR) are analyzed. The conclusion shows that: (1) Regardless of the business mode chosen by the OEM, the sensitivity of unit product authorization fee to consumer perceived value of remanufactured products (RPs) is always higher when the TPR chooses the selling mode than when it chooses the leasing mode. (2) For selling new products (NPs) and RPs mode and selling NPs and leasing RPs mode, the fixed-fee authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for selling is high and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range, and the royalty authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when this cost is low and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range. The win–win authorization strategies for the leasing NPs and selling RPs mode and leasing NPs and RPs mode are affected by the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for leasing and the fixed authorization fee. (3) Under the royalty authorization strategy, the TPR is more profitable when the OEM chooses the leasing mode, but the OEM is more profitable when the TPR chooses the selling mode. Under the fixed-fee authorization strategy, when one of the two players chooses the leasing mode, the other is always more profitable. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Spectrally Partitioned All-Optical Memristors for Highly Linear Neuromorphic Vision Systems
abstract: All-optical control of synaptic weights offers a promising route toward low-power and massively parallel neuromorphic hardware. However, existing optoelectronic memristors often require electrical assistance or exhibit nonlinear and asymmetric conductance updates, limiting their energy efficiency and scalability. Herein, we report a spectrally partitioned all-optical memristor based on a PbS/PEDOT:PSS/VOx heterostructure, in which near-infrared and visible light are coupled to opposite defect-state filling and depletion pathways. Near-infrared illumination selectively excites PbS quantum dots and drives gradual electron transfer into oxygen-vacancy-related defect states in VOx through the PEDOT:PSS-regulated interface, producing continuous conductance potentiation. By contrast, visible illumination activates VOx and promotes interfacial hole-assisted recombination, leading to reversible depletion of defect-state electrons and conductance depression. This wavelength-selective carrier-transfer process enables highly linear and symmetric all-optical weight updates, achieving a linearity of 0.9994 and an effective 8-bit conductance resolution. The electrical energy consumption per optically induced synaptic event is calculated to be as low as 0.63 fJ under an ultralow probing bias. By integrating the devices into a 32 × 32 all-optically programmed array, we further demonstrate hardware-based BloodMNIST microscopic blood-cell image classification with an accuracy of 96.5% and strong noise robustness. These results provide a viable strategy for developing high-linearity, low-power, and spectrally programmable neuromorphic hardware. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: A Manganese-Chlorella Hydrogel for an Integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” Strategy in Pancreatic Cancer Therapy
abstract: Pancreatic cancer faces the challenges of tumor progression and postoperative pancreatic fistula during the perioperative period, which severely affect patient prognosis. In this study, an injectable self-healing multifunctional hydrogel (CMCGel) was developed based on dynamic cross‑linking between manganese ions (Mn2+) and carboxymethyl chitosan loaded with chlorella extract (CE). This platform implements an integrated “Remove–Remodel–Repair” (3R) strategy for comprehensive perioperative management. CMCGel exhibits distinctive pH/laser dual-responsive behavior: In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the accelerated release of CE and Mn2+ enhances photodynamic therapy and chemodynamic therapy (CDT). This combination, activated by laser and gated by endogenous pH, achieves remarkable tumor suppression rates of 85.81% in vitro and 96.01% in vivo. title: Mechanisms for digital business model innovation in international new ventures from developing economies
abstract: Digital international new ventures (DINVs) increasingly leverage ecosystem partnerships to drive digital business model innovation (DBMI) and navigate global markets. However, research to examine how such partnerships contribute to DBMI is limited, particularly in resource-constrained firms from developing economies. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view, organizational learning theory and an ecosystem-based digital learning perspective, we investigate the role of ecosystem partnerships in enabling DBMI through the development of digital learning capabilities. Based on survey data from 147 DINVs in a developing economy, findings suggest that ecosystem partnerships enhance digital learning, which in turn facilitates DBMI. Moreover, foreign market turbulence tends to positively moderate the relationship between ecosystem partnerships and digital learning capability. In addition to demonstrating how DINVs build innovation capacity under volatile conditions, findings help to extend perspectives on capabilities, learning, and ecosystems. Leveraging ecosystem partnerships, digital learning, and digital business model innovation appears to enhance the performance of DINVs. Ecosystem partnerships appear to be especially valuable to DINVs when market turbulence is high. The study offers theoretical and practical insights into the mechanism through which DINVs from developing economies can achieve digital innovation, and provides policy implications for supporting their international growth. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From sustainability awareness to practical agency: Translating institutional activity into meaningful student learning
abstract: The Principles for Responsible Management Education initiative calls upon business schools to embed sustainability and responsible management within their curricula. Although higher education institutions have made progress, student perspectives remain underrepresented in Education for Sustainable Development research. Drawing on an integrated theoretical framework comprising Transformative Learning Theory, the sustainability competency framework, social learning and students-as-partners pedagogy, this exploratory study reports a mixed-methods survey of 130 Business and Management students across two UK higher education institutions. The findings indicate generally favourable sustainability attitudes among the participating students, consistent with previous responsible management education research. Exploratory comparisons found broadly similar patterns across two contrasting UK cohorts: full-time undergraduate students and employed degree apprentices. The more distinctive finding concerns an institutional-to-educational translation gap. Students acknowledged aspects of current provision but indicated that institutional sustainability activity did not always become visible, participatory or educationally meaningful within their programmes. Across both cohorts, students called for stronger collaboration, practice-oriented education and solutions-focused learning through which sustainability knowledge could be connected with authentic organisational and societal challenges. These findings underpin a student-informed conceptual framework, Towards Transdisciplinary and Transformative Sustainability Education, which identifies conditions through which institutional sustainability activity may become visible, participatory and educationally meaningful to students. The study does not directly assess institutional transformation, transformative learning or behavioural change, nor does it test whether favourable attitudes persist when sustainability entails difficult financial, professional or lifestyle trade-offs. The Framework should therefore be understood as a conceptual proposition for supporting meaningful engagement rather than as evidence that transformative or behavioural outcomes have occurred. © 2026 The Authors

title: The value of lost load in electricity intensive industry – combining and comparing stated and production value approaches
abstract: The value of lost load (VoLL) is a monetary metric quantifying the cost of unsupplied energy (€/kWh) during outages, providing valuable insights for policymakers, utility providers, and industrial stakeholders. Leveraging a mixed-method approach that integrates and compares survey data with publicly available microeconomic data insights, results show how value-added based measures significantly underestimate the financial impact of power outages. Shorter outages are found to be disproportionately costly, primarily due to high fixed costs associated with initial disruptions. Businesses report that the effects of a 1-h outage could linger for months, with some unable to fully recover even 12 months after the event. These extended disruptions underscore the enduring consequences of power outages, particularly for electricity-intensive industries. In a regression type of approach, the cost of power interruptions is not significantly influenced by the type of industry. Instead, the economic impact of an outage is more closely tied to the volume of electricity consumed, duration and production hours. Highlighting sectoral aspects and methodological sensitivities, the paper offers relevant insights for setting reliability standards, designing compensation schemes, and for guiding infrastructure investment. © 2026 The Authors. title: How does responsible governance affect firms’ Innovation resilience? A matching perspective on responsible leadership and responsible AI
abstract: Innovation resilience has become a critical capability for firms to withstand risks and achieve sustainable growth. However, how responsible governance shapes firms’ innovation resilience remains underexplored. Drawing on signaling theory and conservation of resources theory, this study examines the effects of responsible leadership, responsible AI, and their congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. Using survey data from 480 firms in China’s manufacturing and strategic emerging industries, we conduct empirical analyses with nonlinear regression and response surface analysis. The results show that: (1) responsible leadership has an inverted U-shaped relationship with firms’ innovation resilience; (2) responsible AI has a negative effect on firms’ innovation resilience; (3) congruence between responsible leadership and responsible AI is conducive to firms’ innovation resilience; (4) firms exhibit higher innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration than under the low responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; (5) compared with the low responsible leadership-high responsible AI configuration, firms achieve higher levels of innovation resilience under the high responsible leadership-low responsible AI configuration; and (6) organizational unlearning and organizational innovation climate positively moderate the effect of responsible leadership-responsible AI congruence on firms’ innovation resilience. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Optimizing equity and efficiency in the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem
abstract: This study addresses the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem, formulated as the strategic prepositioning of a heterogeneous aerial firefighting fleet across capacity-constrained airbases. A novel bi-objective model is proposed that simultaneously optimizes efficiency (aggregate risk-weighted accessibility) and equity (minimized regional service disparities). The model employs an enhanced spatial accessibility method with a distance-decay function to evaluate coverage effectiveness and distribution fairness. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is implemented to generate Pareto-approximate solutions, revealing quantifiable trade-offs. Applied to a national-scale case study in Greece using 25 years of wildfire data, results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides significantly wider coverage than current practices, thereby extending protection to underserved regions while reducing redundant overlap. Sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across various real-world conditions, such as different budget levels and aircraft availability. This transferable tool enables policymakers to make data-driven decisions by quantifying the balance between response effectiveness and social fairness in wildfire-prone regions. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Sour grapes or strategic choice? Socially disadvantaged tourism entrepreneurs' pursuit of ‘break out’
abstract: While structural conditions impacting immigrant entrepreneurs' ‘break out’ are well-documented in tourism research, the underlying psychological processes remain underexplored. Informed by self-determination theory and adaptive preferences, this ethnographic study conducted between December 2024 and May 2025 explores how socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs negotiate structural constraints and individual agency while pursuing ‘break out’. Drawing on 345 h of ethnographic observation, digital data from two focal Nepali tourism entrepreneurs in Hong Kong SAR, and longitudinal object-oriented interviews with nineteen stakeholders, it reveals a psychological mechanism where frustration of basic psychological needs triggers adaptive preferences, hindering ‘break out’ efforts. It also shows how tourism's experiential nature enables entrepreneurs to counter stigma and negotiate autonomy. Practically, the findings highlight the need for psychologically informed support that goes beyond traditional skill-based training. While focused on Hong Kong's Nepali diaspora, the study offers broader insights into entrepreneurial ‘break out’ among socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A game-theoretic approach for the retailer-third party multiple market-site capture competition in an end-of-life product collection system
abstract: This paper introduces a bi-level game-theoretic model for competition between two players collecting End-Of-Life (EOL) products within a circular economy framework. The model focuses on strategic market targeting in a geographically segmented market dominated by an established retailer. A new entrant (third party) acts as the leader, selecting a subset of nodes to capture. The incumbent retailer responds as the follower, recapturing lost nodes under its own budget. Due to NP-hardness, a Benders cut-based solution approach is developed. The model is extended to a partial interdiction formulation with continuous capture decisions, allowing gradual market entry. A genetic algorithm has also been developed for large-scale instances. A case study on EOL mobile phone collection in Tehran illustrates the practical application. Entry points and defensive and offensive strategies are derived under various budget scenarios. Results show that entry is not always advantageous. As the retailer’s budget increases, the third party faces higher financial barriers to entry, requiring a disproportionately larger budget to remain competitive. In the partial interdiction setting, the model captures nodes fully when the budget permits, reserving fractional capture only when resources are insufficient. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Tackling cold-start emissions: an integrated strategy of active thermal management and oxygenated fuel formulation
abstract: This study investigates the integration of bio-oxygenated fuel formulation with an electrically heated catalytic system to mitigate low-temperature cold-start emissions in compression-ignition engines. Four 20 % v/v oxygenated blends, comprising linear alcohols (butanol, pentanol) and cyclic compounds (cyclopentanol, cyclopentanone), were evaluated in a single-cylinder research engine coupled to a diesel oxidation catalyst. Linear alcohol blending reduced the CO light-off threshold (T50,CO) by 26 °C (butanol) and 16 °C (pentanol) relative to neat diesel by suppressing heavy hydrocarbon precursors and limiting active-site blocking on platinum group metals, whereas engine-out measurements showed that cyclic fuels yielded an initial particulate number reduction exceeding 85 % (reaching up to 90 % for cyclopentanone) compared to neat diesel. Active thermal management at DOC inlet temperatures of 355 °C to 415 °C achieved approximately 99 % CO conversion and 72 % total hydrocarbon reduction and increased the downstream NO2/NOx ratio up to 0.34. Catalytic post-treatment further reduced total particle number concentration by 41.1 % to 57.2 % with a simultaneous increase in count median diameter. These results, constrained by the single-cylinder steady-state operating conditions and specific engine loads evaluated, indicate that coupling tailored fuel formulations with active electrical heating offers an integrated methodological framework with the potential to resolve cold-start emissions limitations in low-exhaust-temperature applications. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Hydrophobic Eutectogels Reinforced by Zn2+-Coordinated Lignin Nanoparticles for Underwater Wearable Electronics
abstract: Wearable flexible sensors for underwater communication and biomotion monitoring are gaining attention. However, developing gel-based strain sensors with high toughness, anti-swelling performance, robust underwater adhesion, and long-term stability remains challenging. Herein, we present a hydrophobic eutectogel (DPF-Zn@LNP-HEG) fabricated via the assembly of a polymerizable hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (PHDES), 2-phenoxyethyl acrylate (PEA), and Zn2+-coordinated lignin nanoparticles (Zn@LNP). The resulting structure, composed of hydrophobic polymer networks and metal-phenolic complexes, forms hydrophobic microdomains that disrupt the hydration layer and prevent water penetration. Meanwhile, Zn@LNP serve as dynamic sacrificial cross-linkers, enhancing the material’s mechanical strength, energy dissipation, and anti-swelling properties. The resulting eutectogel exhibits remarkable tensile strength (1.14 MPa), superior toughness (3.15 MJ m−3), excellent anti-swelling properties (< 1% after 30 days), and robust underwater adhesion (1.07 MPa on glass). Based on these properties, we demonstrate an underwater strain sensor with high sensitivity (gauge factor = 8.12) and long-term stability, enabling underwater Morse code transmission, biomotion monitoring, and Bluetooth-based tracking of swimming movements. This work not only provides a versatile design paradigm for multifunctional underwater sensing platforms but also advances the high-value utilization of bio-based materials in next-generation flexible electronics. title: Online direct-to-consumer channel introducing and ordering strategies of fresh supply chain considering disruption risks and yield constraints
abstract: The rise of online direct-to-consumer (DTC) channels expands fresh producers’ distribution networks while intensifying competition with traditional retail channels. Meteorological disasters threaten the DTC channel's reliability, dynamically reshaping the coopetition between fresh producers and retailers. This study develops a theoretical framework to examine strategic interactions within a fresh supply chain, comparing a traditional monopoly model with an integrated distribution system that incorporates both DTC and traditional retail channels. Disruption risks and yield constraints faced by producers are considered. The findings suggest producers should introduce DTC channels during yield contraction but exercise caution in surplus periods. Despite disruption risks, DTC channels pressure retailers to accept higher wholesale prices and increase orders, enhancing the sales revenue of fresh produce with limited yield. However, rising disruption probabilities incentivize retailers to reduce order quantities strategically, leading to a higher risk of stagnation for fresh produce. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Artificial intelligence disclosure and the value relevance of earnings
abstract: This study investigates the effect of AI disclosure on the value relevance of earnings using Chinese listed companies from 2013 to 2022. We find that AI disclosure significantly enhances earnings’ value relevance. Mechanism tests show that AI disclosure increases firms’ earnings quality and boosts investor attention, thus elevating the value relevance of earnings. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that this effect is more pronounced in firms in advanced manufacturing industries, firms in highly competitive industries and non-SOEs. Overall, this study highlights the important role of AI disclosure in the price discovery of both fundamental and unexpected earnings, and contributes to a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms through which AI affects the value relevance of earnings. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Advances in TMDs-Based Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers: From Structural Engineering to Multicomponent Synergy
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered considerable attention as advanced electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) materials due to their unique layered structures, tunable electronic properties, and intrinsic defect-induced polarization mechanisms. This comprehensive review systematically summarizes recent advances in TMDs-based absorbers, with particular focus on two fundamental development strategies. The first involves multiscale structural design of pure phase TMDs spanning from atomic to submillimeter dimensions, achieved through precise defect regulation, phase engineering, and sophisticated morphological manipulation to optimize electromagnetic parameters and attenuation capabilities. The second strategy focuses on constructing multicomponent composite systems, incorporating dielectric matrices, magnetic elements, and multicomponent hybrids to achieve synergistic enhancement through interfacial polarization, conductive loss, and magnetic dissipation mechanisms. The review critically analyzes pioneering research achievements across various subfields while identifying specific challenges and opportunities within each domain. Future perspectives highlight emerging frontiers including atomic level interface engineering, inverse design of multicomponent and multiscale architectures, sustainable large-scale synthesis techniques, and development of multifunctional smart-response systems. This work aims to establish fundamental principles and provide forward-looking guidance for designing next-generation high-performance TMDs-based EMA materials with tailored functionalities. title: Don't promise me, prove it: Leveraging blockchain affordances to reduce uncertainty and build consumer purchase confidence in sustainable fashion
abstract: While the role of blockchain technology in shaping sustainable consumer behaviors is increasingly examined, empirical understanding of its capability to reduce uncertainty and enhance consumers' purchase confidence remains limited, particularly within the sustainable fashion context. In addressing this gap, the current study examines how blockchain affordances, including transparency, traceability, and immutability, contribute to sustainable product uncertainty reduction (SPUR) and strengthen consumers’ purchase confidence. It further examines the mediating roles of perceived information diagnosticity (PID), perceived sustainable product quality (PSPQ), and the moderating role of information literacy (IL). A hybrid PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach was applied to analyze the data from 437 Vietnamese Gen Z sustainable fashion consumers. PLS-SEM results reveal that blockchain affordances indirectly affect purchase confidence, primarily through PID and PSPQ rather than SPUR, with IL exhibiting mixed moderated mediation effects. Complementarily, fsQCA identifies ten solution configurations leading to high purchase confidence and seven associated with its absence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer municipal plastics for enhanced environmental sustainability
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical recycling of municipal plastic waste can reduce landfill burden, energy demand, and environmental impacts while recovering reusable polymers. The study objectives were to assess the performance of polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene using polymer-specific pre-processing methods, shredding, thermal consolidation, and compression moulding. The assessment focused on waste minimization, material recovery, energy requirements, estimated carbon dioxide emission reductions, sustainability, and mechanical and thermal performance. METHODS: A total of 37 kilograms of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene was separately processed using polymer-specific treatment and compression moulding. Environmental performance was evaluated within a cradle-to-gate framework using secondary emission factors, and the Sustainability Index was derived from predefined parameters. Recycled materials were evaluated for mechanical and thermal properties. Exploratory one-way analysis of variance assessed polymer differences, with probability values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. FINDINGS: Waste reduction and material recovery rates exceeded 95 percent for all polymers, with low-density polyethylene achieving the highest recovery of 99 percent. Low-density polyethylene also showed the lowest energy consumption of 0.95 kilowatt-hours per kilogram and the observed sustainability index of 82.6 ± 2.1, although polymer-specific differences in the Sustainability Index were not statistically significant. Polyethylene terephthalate showed the highest tensile strength (55.2 megapascals), compressive strength (83.4 megapascals), density (1.36 grams per cubic centimetre), and carbon dioxide emission reduction (2.10 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilogram). High-density polyethylene showed intermediate performance. Analysis of variance indicated polymer-specific differences, with F-statistic values of 1.72–412.3 and probability values of <0.001–0.27. After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, most physical and mechanical properties, energy consumption, and carbon dioxide emission reduction showed significant differences, whereas landfill diversion and the Sustainability Index did not differ significantly. CONCLUSION: Polymer-specific mechanical recycling of pre-sorted post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene achieved high material recovery while maintaining mechanical and thermal properties. The polymers showed differences in material recovery, energy consumption, carbon dioxide emission reduction, and evaluated material properties. Further evaluation using heterogeneous municipal plastic waste and larger-scale processing is required. © 2027 The author(s). title: Mixed methods research: Critical review and guidelines for stronger design, integration, and contribution
abstract: Mixed methods research has a prominent place in tourism and hospitality scholarship, yet adoption has advanced faster than methodological selectivity, which leaves many studies combining qualitative and quantitative strands without explaining why both strands were necessary, how the strands were related, or what integrated inference their combination alone made possible. Drawing on a critical review of 222 mixed methods studies published in leading tourism and hospitality journals, this article identifies dominant patterns, strengths and weaknesses, and underused possibilities. In response, the article offers a stage-based guide that links problem formulation, purpose selection, design fit, sampling bridges, strand roles, integration, divergence handling, reporting architecture, and contribution development. In doing so, the article advances a more demanding standard for mixed methods scholarship and argues that the next phase of tourism and hospitality research should shift from routine method combination toward integrated inferences that are conceptually sharper, methodologically clearer, and practically more useful. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Fostering creativity through interdisciplinary teaching: A meta-analysis of effectiveness
abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching is widely promoted to cultivate students’ creativity, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis synthesized 55 quantitative studies (70 effect sizes, 7490 students) from 2013 to 2024, applying random-effects models using Hedges’ g. Creativity outcomes were decomposed into three theoretically grounded dimensions: creative thinking process, creative practice ability, and creative personality and psychology. Results indicated a large overall positive effect ( g + = 1.090, 95% CI [0.913, 1.266]), with very high heterogeneity ( I 2 = 96.017%). Dimensional analysis revealed significant variations: the strongest effects on creative practice ability ( g + = 2.164), followed by creative thinking process ( g + = 1.253), while effects on creative personality and psychology were smaller ( g + = 0.478). Moderator analyses revealed that educational stage, dominant subject, pedagogical approach, intervention duration, and group activities significantly influenced outcomes, while class size and instructional setting did not. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Balancing economic and environmental goals in green supply chains through a multi-objective optimization on financing and coordination contract
abstract: This study aims to develop a green supply chain management (GSCM) framework that integrates buyer-backed purchase order financing (BPOF), advance payment discounts (APD), and coordination agreements to enhance sustainability and financial stability. This research work applies Stackelberg game theory and multi-objective optimization to investigate how BPOF and APD can be used to promote both economic stability and environmental performance. The combination of these financing options with revenue-sharing and cost-sharing agreements provides a comprehensive view that is frequently lacking in green supply chain models. The main innovation is that financial mechanisms and multi-objective goals are considered simultaneously within a coordinated framework. The effect of coordinating contracts and funding mechanisms on the overall performance of the supply chain is evaluated using numerical analysis. The results indicate that BPOF improves financial flexibility for manufacturers, promoting higher green investment levels. Among financing strategies, advance payment discount (APD) appears as the most effective, delivering around 10–20% larger profits than other mechanisms, while buyer-backed purchase order financing (BPOF) is a viable option under liquidity restrictions. The findings have significant management and industrial consequences. Manufacturers should prioritize low-cost financing solutions, such as APD, to support green developments, especially in areas with high environmental awareness. The model is especially applicable in industries like electric automobiles, battery recycling, and sustainable manufacturing, where companies must strike a balance between economic performance and environmental responsibility. This paper presents a practical decision-making framework for increasing profitability and sustainability in modern supply chains. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Continuous Fabrication of Bioinspired All-Biomass Aerogel Fibers for Thermal Insulation
abstract: Aerogel fibers have been considered as a promising solution for thermal protection textiles due to their high porosity and low thermal conductivity. However, the scalable production of sustainable and mechanical strong aerogel fibers remains a critical challenge. Here, inspired by the porous core–shell structure of polar bear hair, we report a continuous strategy to fabricate all-biomass aerogel fibers featuring an encapsulated core–shell architecture using silk fibroin as the core and cellulose as the shell. This tunable structure, with radially aligned sheet-like pores and adjustable shell thickness, is achieved through hydrogen bond-driven cellulose contraction and alcohol-induced curing of sheet-like silk fibroin. Such a porous architecture effectively suppresses convective heat transfer and promotes a multi-reflective effect for infrared radiation. The resulting fibers exhibit good mechanical robustness with a tensile load of a single aerogel fiber is up to 200 g without reinforcement. Meanwhile, the aerogel fiber maintains high porosity (79.78%), low thermal conductivity (52.4 ± 4.2 mW m−1 K−1), and low density (0.193 ± 0.01 g cm−3). Furthermore, an aerogel glove fabricated from these fibers demonstrates good thermal insulation. These results provide new insights for the design of biomimetic aerogel fibers with core–shell architecture, offering a scalable and eco-friendly pathway toward advanced wearable thermal management. title: Wearable Electronics for Precision Diagnosis Through Advanced Manufacturing and Integration
abstract: Wearable electronics are rapidly transforming healthcare by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and molecular signals directly at the point of need. This shift supports a transition from episodic, generalized care toward precision diagnosis, where individualized, longitudinal data guide early detection, risk stratification, and treatment decisions. Central to this transformation is the convergence of advanced manufacturing and heterogeneous integration strategies, which enable the development of compact, multimodal, and highly conformable diagnostic platforms. In this review, we examine how advances in materials engineering, micro/nanofabrication, and system integration have transformed wearable devices from single-parameter sensors into fully integrated, multimodal diagnostic systems. We outline key architectures and transduction mechanisms and highlight manufacturing approaches such as printing, 3D fabrication, photolithography, and laser writing. We emphasize heterogeneous integration strategies that combine sensing, electronics, power, and communication into skin-conformal platforms for long-term use. These advances enable precision diagnostics through continuous monitoring, multimodal data fusion, and individualized baselines. We also outline key challenges to clinical translation and discuss future directions toward robust, scalable, and clinically actionable systems, providing a strategic outlook for next-generation wearable electronics in precision diagnosis. title: The impact of entrepreneurship education on sustainable entrepreneurial intentions: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: In this paper, we examine how a semester-long sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship course shapes sustainable entrepreneurial intention (SEI) through individual sustainability orientation (ISO). Grounded in an adaptation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, ISO is conceptualized as a multidimensional construct encompassing sustainability-oriented (SO) values, SO motivation, awareness of sustainability issues, and SO self-efficacy, dimensions expected to mediate educational effects on SEI with different temporal sensitivities. We implemented a quasi-experimental design across two graduate introductory entrepreneurship courses at two Canadian universities: one redesigned around sustainability mechanisms (treatment, N = 112) and one covering standard content (comparison, N = 47). Pre- and post-test surveys were conducted. Results show no direct effect of the treatment on SEI and no change in SO values, which were high at baseline. However, the treatment significantly increased students’ sustainability awareness, self-efficacy, and, unexpectedly, motivation. Among these, changes in awareness and self-efficacy were positively associated with changes in SEI. These findings indicate that semester-long interventions can reliably influence proximal cognitions (awareness and self-efficacy), while deeper dispositions such as values, and to a lesser extent motivation, likely require longer-term or more immersive exposure. Theoretically, this study conceptualizes ISO as a temporally layered construct that helps explain why prior findings on education–SEI links are mixed. Methodologically, it demonstrates the value of coupling quasi-experimental designs with pedagogical reporting. Practically, it highlights workable mechanisms, such as sustainability-anchored projects, sustainable business modeling, and impact-oriented pitches, that strengthen awareness and SO self-efficacy. These insights encourage moving beyond outcome-level evaluations toward understanding how entrepreneurship education can foster SEI. © 2026 The Authors

title: Dual-Ion Co-Storage via Solvation Structure Tuning Toward Ultrafast and Durable Zinc-Organic Batteries
abstract: Aqueous Zn-organic batteries are promising due to the sustainability and tunability of organic cathodes. However, the critical challenge in their practical application lies in dissolution, degradation, and sluggish kinetics, ultimately degrading the cycling stability and rate capability. Herein, we demonstrate a simple effective electrolyte engineering strategy by introducing potassium chloride (KCl) as a co-solute into the ZnCl2 electrolyte to achieve high-performance Zn batteries utilizing 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) as the cathode. Experimental studies and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that KCl addition not only enhances electrolyte conductivity but also modulates Zn2+ solvation environment to form [Zn(H2O)2Cl4]2−, significantly improving ion diffusion kinetics. Consequently, the Zn//PTCDA in the ZnCl2-KCl electrolyte exhibits a remarkable capacity of 124.7 mAh g−1 with an average voltage of 0.65 V, exceptional rate performance (56% capacity retention at 30 A g−1), and prolonged cycling performance (90.9% retention after 10,000 cycles). Experimental and density functional theory mechanistic studies unveil a new reversible Zn2+/K+ co-storage mechanism in the PTCDA cathode, where K+ acts as a charge shield and structural pillar, synergistically decreasing the ion migration energy barrier, enhancing reaction kinetics, and stabilizing the cathode structure. This work elucidates dual-ion storage chemistry and highlights rational electrolyte design for durable, high-power metal–organic batteries. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Exploring the linkage between entrepreneurial education and entrepreneurial intentions among university students in Morocco
abstract: The Moroccan labor market continues to struggle with the incorporation of its university graduates and the interest in entrepreneurship as an employment option is growing. Higher education institutions are an essential part of developing students' entrepreneurial competencies and intentions. This research investigates the effects of entrepreneurship education on students' entrepreneurial intention as based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The research also investigates how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, creativity, proactive behavior, and family background influence entrepreneurial intention. A self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data from 226 students at the Faculty of Economics and Management at Beni Mellal, Morocco, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that entrepreneurship education is positively related to entrepreneurial intention both directly as well as indirectly through attitudes toward entrepreneurship and perceived behavioral control; also, creativity and family background were found to positively influence entrepreneurial intention. In contrast, subjective norms and proactive behavior do not show a significant effect in this context. These findings highlight the importance of entrepreneurial education in strengthening students' entrepreneurial orientation while suggesting that social influences and individual proactivity may operate differently within the Moroccan context. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence from a developing country context and offers implications for policymakers and educators seeking to enhance entrepreneurship education programs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Will this time be different? Just transition pathways in eastern and Southern Africa’s critical minerals sector
abstract: The global energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems. However, the future translation of mineral reserves into equitable socio-economic development in the region depends on policy frameworks and governance systems that promote inclusive participation, recognition, and benefit-sharing. This paper examines pathways for inclusive economic transformation, analyzing the conditions required to ensure mining-affected communities benefit equitably from the critical minerals boom. We employ a justice-centered framework of distributional, procedural, recognition and restorative justice to analyze five countries (Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and Burundi) through stakeholder interviews with 43 actors and document and policy analysis, including Malawi and Burundi, whose emerging sectors are largely absent from the peer-reviewed record. Across the five cases the four dimensions are not encountered as separate problems. Findings suggest that employment opportunities do not always reach local populations, revenue mechanisms face transparency challenges, consultation processes have limited influence over outcomes, customary tenure is inconsistently recognized, and environmental legacies often persist without adequate remediation. Ensuring that the substantial economic opportunities created by critical mineral demand are realized inclusively will require simultaneous interventions across all four justice dimensions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Not that simple: How can generative artificial intelligence be used to develop college students’ entrepreneurial ability?
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become increasingly relevant to entrepreneurship education, yet its association with college students' entrepreneurial ability remains contested. To address this gap, we conceptualize GenAI as encompassing both routine and innovative uses, providing a more comprehensive understanding of its role in entrepreneurial ability. Based on questionnaire data, our empirical findings show that both routine and innovative use of GenAI are positively associated with entrepreneurial ability. Moreover, we find that potential and realized absorptive capacity mediate this relationship, while interaction analyses indicate that these associations are stronger at higher levels of design thinking. These findings contribute to the entrepreneurship education literature by revealing the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which GenAI use enhances college students’ entrepreneurial ability. The study also provides insights into how college students can use GenAI more effectively in complex business contexts to strengthen their entrepreneurial ability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors. title: Political elites and access to economic opportunities in China's rural market transition
abstract: Understanding whether political elites maintain advantages in accessing economic opportunities during market transitions is crucial for assessing the distributional consequences of market-oriented reforms. This study examines whether political status provides rural households with advantages in accessing production resources and income opportunities during China's recent wave of marketization, and how these advantages vary with the degree of market development. Using three waves of the China Family Database spanning 2015–2019 and employing an instrumental variable approach, we find that political elites maintain persistent advantages in accessing economic opportunities. Relative to non-elites, cadre households exhibit 20.1 percentage points higher rates of receiving agricultural subsidies, 38.8 percentage points higher rates of owning agricultural machinery, and 9.7 percentage points greater likelihood of operating nonfarm businesses. As marketization advances, the sources of elite advantage shift from agriculture to commercial activities. While advantages in agricultural production weaken, reflecting reduced state-controlled resource allocation channels, advantages in business operations strengthen consistent with elites converting political capital into entrepreneurial opportunities. Our findings suggest that rural marketization in China reallocates rather than reduces opportunity gaps. This pattern indicates that even as market reforms diminish traditional avenues for political privilege, they simultaneously open new market-based opportunities that preserve elite advantage. These findings have broader implications for understanding how political power influences access to opportunities during market transitions in developing economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Covalent Organic Framework Membranes through Sequential Imine Exchange for Precise Molecular Separation
abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with high crystallinity hold great promise in precise molecular separation, but often suffer from the intercrystalline defects and thus poor membrane-formation ability. This study reports a sequential imine exchange strategy to fabricate highly crystalline, defect-free COF membranes for precise molecular separation. Two functional amines (aromatic and aliphatic amines) are employed in highly reversible imine exchange reaction to separately conduct crystallization and defect remedy processes according to their different energy gaps. Aromatic amine, which serves as COF framework building unit, undergoes the first-step imine exchange for high crystallinity because of its lower energy gap. Afterward, the hyperbranched aliphatic amine with abundant amino groups undergoes the second-step imine exchange, affording the tight connections between adjacent crystals and the excellent membrane-formation ability. Accordingly, the COF membrane exhibits high permeance (344 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for water, 462 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 for methanol) and rejection (> 99.9% for Congo red and Alcian blue). Meanwhile, the membrane is endowed with an ultrahigh separation factor (> 528) for mixed dye aqueous solutions and large-scale processability (> 290 cm2). This work offers a new strategy to fabricate highly crystalline and defect-free COF membranes, revealing their large potential in diverse practical applications. title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Results showed that identity performance is associated with distinct configurations of audiences' behavioral engagement. The “docent” generated more audience engagement than other identities, including audiences' learning, endorsing, and intending to participate dimensions. Guided by the knowledge gap theory, a subsequent experiment showed that the “docent” identity increased engagement by sparking curiosity. These findings guide content creators in adopting effective identity performance strategies, destinations in partnering with well-aligned content creators, and platforms in using algorithmic curation to achieve desired marketing outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). However, how students self-regulate their learning while working with genAI during authentic tasks remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by examining (RQ1) how students' self-regulatory strategies manifest during genAI-assisted learning and (RQ2) how these strategies change through genAI interaction. A thematic analysis was conducted of 34 metacognitive reflections generated across two scaffolded, four-stage experiential learning activities in a Lean Startup unit. Findings inform a three-stage AI-mediated recursive loop model, comprising monitoring, strategic adoption, and limitation identification, that extends cyclical models of self-regulated learning by showing how regulation may be initiated within the task by genAI-generated suggestions. Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. GenAI-supported cognitive deepening was task-contingent, emerging most strongly during applied refinement tasks. The model offers management educators a pedagogical process model for designing scaffolded genAI-assisted activities that elicit monitoring, selective adoption, and critical reflection. © 2026 The Authors

title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 590 stakeholders involved in tourism village governance across four regencies and one city in Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention
abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Drawing on mindfulness theory, this study examines the role of mindfulness cultivated during Buddhist monastery retreats in influencing emotional solidarity, experience self-connection, place identity, and behavioural intention. Data were collected from 430 visitors and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM results underscore the critical role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ social interactions, emotional attachment to the destination, and self-connection, all of which significantly impact their intention to engage in spiritual retreats. Emotional solidarity and self-connection are found to significantly influence place identity and future behavioural intention. The MGA findings indicate that generational and experiential segmentation reveals that Generation Z is more responsive to mindfulness and experience self-connection, while older cohorts are more influenced by emotional solidarity. Repeat visitors report stronger mindfulness effects across all outcomes, whereas first-time visitors rely more on emotional bonding. These insights underscore the value of tailoring mindful retreat experiences to foster deeper engagement and sustained support for religious tourism destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Decoupling Ion–Dipole Interactions via Competitive Coordination for Durable Dendrite-Free Zinc Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract: The aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are famous for high-safety and high-energy-density, but limited by severe challenges around the Helmholtz plane layer such as the strong ion–dipole interactions between Zn2+ and H2O, resulting in slow desolvation processes and limited transport kinetics as well as corresponding higher barriers. To reconstruct the ion–dipole surroundings, the interface chemistry of employing a high permanent dipole moment of L-Carnosine (L-CN) has been proposed, weakening the interactions between Zn2+ and H2O to realize a crowded Zn2+-conductive structure, accelerating the desolvation kinetics. As revealed, the strong affinity between L-CN and Zn2+ enables the L-CN molecules to repulse H2O, reconfiguring the inner Helmholtz plane layer, thereby inhibiting the active water molecular to form hydrogen evolution reactions. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells with Helmholtz plane modulation achieve a long lifespan up to 7000 h, a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.72%, and a high stabilization at high depth of discharge (85.4%). The assembled Zn//V2O5−x full cell with optimal electrolyte delivers the capacity of 289 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g−1 under an N/P ratio of 3.98. Impressively, the large-scale pouch cell with optimal electrolyte stabilizes for 200 cycles, offering the bright future of reconstructing Helmholtz plane for achieving high-performance AZMBs. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Employee cybersecurity awareness impact on cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada
abstract: This study investigates the impact of employee cybersecurity awareness on the cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada, as the prevalence of cyber threats, such as ransomware, phishing, and data breaches, continues to rise. The study adopts Servant Leadership (SL) theory as the analytical framework, with particular emphasis on SL’s attributes of employee empowerment, training, and organizational culture as factors in building resilience against cyber threats. A systematic literature review (SLR) methodology was employed, drawing on peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 from databases including Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science. The review process followed PRISMA guidelines, with rigorous application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the AMSTAR and CASP tools, resulting in 30 articles for the SLR. The findings reveal that organizations with strong servant leadership attributes, employee empowerment and training, combined with a cybersecurity-conscious culture, enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and training. The study further found that clear and consistently enforced policies are critical for guiding employee behaviour and fostering long-term adherence. The study recommends adopting targeted role-based and scenario-driven training approaches on cybersecurity for employees to improve their knowledge retention and threat response to cyberattacks for strengthening organizational cybersecurity posture in Canada. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Seeing through the mind: Explainable multimodal AI for depression detection—A review
abstract: Depression detection using multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving, transitioning from traditional machine learning techniques to deep learning architectures built on pre-trained transformer encoders. These systems integrate textual, acoustic, visual, and physiological signal streams through early, intermediate, late, and hybrid fusion strategies to improve predictive performance. However, a significant gap persists in model interpretability: post-hoc attribution frameworks (such as SHAP and LIME) dominate recent work, accounting for over 70% of studies published in 2024–2025, while clinician-centered validation is reported in only about 18% of the full reviewed corpus. Consequently, existing explanations are rarely validated for explainability quality dimensions; for example, SHAP attributions are known to degrade under inter-modality collinearity, and reported systems frequently lack alignment with established diagnostic criteria (e.g., DSM-based or PHQ-9 symptom structures). To close the gap between predictive accuracy and clinical utility, this review jointly synthesizes multimodal datasets, feature extraction strategies, machine learning and deep learning taxonomies, fusion strategies, and explainability techniques across 72 included studies. Finally, we outline critical future directions, emphasizing standardized XAI benchmarks, clinician-in-the-loop validation studies, and knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic reasoning. © 2026

title: Techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production utilizing offshore wind energy using the AHP method and the Weibull distribution approximation. A case of Sakhalin Island
abstract: The study is devoted to assessing the suitability of the Sakhalin Island offshore zone for the development of a wind energy complex, with a focus on the potential production of green hydrogen. In the course of the research, the hierarchy analysis method was applied along with fuzzy logic. Criteria influencing the placement of wind farms were selected, experts in the field were interviewed to compile pairwise comparison matrices, after which the weights of these criteria were obtained. Using fuzzy logic functions, the absolute values of the parameters were unified. The territories where the construction of wind farms is undesirable were also taken into account. As a result, the final data set was obtained using the weighted linear combination method. As a result, it was possible to identify 4 zones with the best indicators of suitability for the construction of wind farms. The territories in the Gulf of Patience near the port of Poronaysk look the most promising. Based on the data collected, 8 promising locations within 4 zones have been identified. For each location, the potential amount of electricity and green hydrogen that can be produced has been calculated using the Weibull distribution model, with 6 different methods to parameter estimation. Six different turbine models have been used in the analysis. Additionally, LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy) and LCOH (Levelized Cost of Hydrogen) calculations were conducted. As a result, the minimum LCOE calculated was 0.087 $/kWh and the lowest LCOH recorded was 7.4 $/kg. The Vestas V236-15.0 MW wind turbine demonstrated optimal performance for the study area. If actively invested in this area, this area could become an important hub for hydrogen trading in the Asia-Pacific region. © 2026 The Authors. title: Tuning oxygen-proton coupling of oxygen electrodes to match electrolyte transport in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
abstract: Understanding how oxygen-electrode functionality interacts with electrolyte transport is essential for advancing reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs), yet their coupling remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal an electrolyte-dependent performance reversal arising from the interplay between oxygen-proton coupled reaction pathways and electrolyte transport. Surface functionalization of BaCe0.5Pr0.3Y0.2O3−δ (BCPY) oxygen electrodes with Pr0.5Ba0.5CoO3−δ (PBC) and Ni-substituted Pr0.5Ba0.5Co0.5Ni0.5O3−δ (PBCN) perovskite coatings selectively tunes surface defect chemistry and reaction pathways. PBC promotes lattice-oxygen activation and oxygen-vacancy-mediated processes, whereas Ni substitution in PBCN suppresses vacancy formation while enhancing proton hydration through strengthened Co–O covalency and optimized adsorption of oxygen intermediates. Consequently, PBC-BCPY delivers superior performance on BaZr0.8Yb0.2O3−δ (BZYb) electrolytes with limited proton conductivity, whereas PBCN-BCPY outperforms on highly proton-conductive BaZr0.1Ce0.7Y0.1Yb0.1O3−δ (BZCYYb) electrolytes. Benefiting from the optimized coupling between electrode surface functionality and electrolyte transport, the PBCN-coated BCPY electrode achieves a peak power density of 1.88 W cm⁻2 and a current density of 2.57 A cm⁻2 at 700 °C and 1.3 V on BZCYYb, while maintaining stable operation for 300 h at 600 °C. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for tailoring electrode surface functionality to match electrolyte transport, offering new design principles for high-performance R-PCECs. © 2026

title: Rheologically Engineered 3D-Printed Highly Loaded Magneto-Dielectric Absorbers for Device-Level Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Highly loaded magneto-dielectric composite systems are promising for achieving strong electromagnetic loss and structural design flexibility, yet their processability and geometric controllability remain extremely challenging. Herein, a rheologically engineered direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing strategy is developed. Graphene (Gr) is introduced to reconstruct the particle-loading network, which synergistically improves the ink’s yield behavior, shear-thinning property, structural recovery, and a magnetic–dielectric synergistic loss system is constructed with carbonyl iron powder (CIP). The critical CIP content (~ 84.06 wt%) is determined by the yield model, and a tunable Gr/CIP (GC) composite ink is obtained. The correlation among rheological response, geometric fidelity, and temporal stability is established, enabling high-fidelity 3D-printed gradient honeycomb structures. The rationally designed 3D-printed GC honeycomb (GCH) absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 18 GHz–4 THz, with an RLmin of − 84.30 dB at a thickness of 2.6 mm. When integrated into device-level terahertz reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), the GCH absorber contributes to a ~ 3.3 dBi main lobe gain enhancement, 1.9–3.3 dB sidelobe suppression, and a ~ 58% reduction in reflection beamwidth, showing excellent electromagnetic compatibility performance for communication, imaging, and radar. This work offers a practical strategy for the structural fabrication and device integration of high-load magneto-dielectric synergistic absorbers. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

title: An integrated analytical framework for natural gas pricing: combining multi-source drivers, forecast enhancement, and model interpretability
abstract: With the global pursuit of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), accurate forecasting and mechanistic interpretation of natural gas pricing have become increasingly important. As a transition fuel in the shift toward a low-carbon energy system, natural gas plays a vital role in balancing energy accessibility and environmental sustainability. However, rising economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks present significant challenges to effective price forecasting and policy formulation. In response, we develop a data-driven analytical framework for natural gas pricing that integrates feature engineering and forecast enhancement to achieve accurate point-interval forecasts and investment timing. Leveraging advanced explainability techniques, the framework systematically uncovers the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in global gas market drivers. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional models in predictive accuracy and reveals important lag effects and interaction mechanisms among influencing factors. These findings validate the framework's ability to support pricing decisions and risk hedging for energy enterprises, and to provide scientific evidence for regional energy policymaking through quantification of heterogeneity. Ultimately, it offers key support for improving resource allocation efficiency and advancing the achievement of SDG targets. © 2026

title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Grounded in the processual entrepreneurial concept, this study explores how handicraft artisans understand the challenges they face and how they enact resilience in response. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. The study identifies a novel “recurrent–eroding” dichotomy as a framework for understanding challenge temporality and three resilience enablers, namely personal resources, social support networks, and operational responses. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Practically, it provides critical insights for policymakers, advocating for institutional shifts from crisis-response measures to strengthening accountable support mechanisms, market linkages, and protections for cultural work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
