title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. title: Physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation for single-phase-to-ground fault type identification in distribution networks
abstract: Single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults are the most frequent fault type in medium-voltage small-current grounding distribution networks. Due to arc suppression coil compensation and nonlinear grounding behaviors, fault currents are weak and highly nonstationary, making accurate fault type identification challenging under complex operating conditions. This paper proposes a physics-inspired multimodal collaborative representation framework based on the Hilbert–Huang Transform (HHT) for SPG fault type identification. A typical 10 kV distribution network model is established in PSCAD/EMTDC to generate multi-scenario fault samples. HHT is applied to construct complementary dual-modal features, including time–frequency energy maps and instantaneous temporal evolution sequences. A parallel Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture is developed to model spectral–spatial patterns and temporal dependencies, while channel and temporal attention mechanisms are introduced for adaptive feature enhancement. Results show that the proposed method achieves an overall accuracy of 99.2% across five fault types. Under additive white Gaussian noise with signal-to-noise ratios down to 5 dB, the accuracy remains above 93.6%. These simulation-based results indicate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance within the modeled PSCAD/EMTDC scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge of the Arhuaco People on Water Management in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
abstract: This article analyzes the role of Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) of the Arhuaco people in water management in the upper Ariguaní river basin, in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Colombia), in a context of accelerated socio-environmental transformation. From an ethnohydrological approach, the study adopts a mixed-methods design that integrates community surveys, participatory techniques, spatial analysis of land use change (2000–2023), and dynamic socio-hydrological modeling. A TEK Index was constructed to evaluate three dimensions of water management: cultural management, indigenous norms, and government norms. The results show that traditional water knowledge is mainly based on ritual practices and indigenous norms guided by indigenous spiritual authorities, while coordination with state institutional frameworks is limited. Spatial analysis shows a loss of forest cover and expansion of agricultural uses around the sacred sites that sustain TEK. Modeling indicates that, although indigenous norms slow the deterioration of the system, only co-governance scenarios can cushion pressures and avoid trajectories of collapse. Taken together, the findings show that the effectiveness of TEK depends on its articulation with multiscale governance arrangements. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Bridging the implementation gap in MCABC inventory management: from a taxonomy to practical archetypes
abstract: Despite increasing demands for resilient and sustainable supply chains, inventory management often relies on outdated single-criterion analyses. While multi-criteria ABC (MCABC) analyses provide a theoretically mature assessment of resilience-sustainability-benefit trade-offs in inventory, their adoption remains limited due to fragmented methodologies, lack of standardization, and unclear design guidance. This study addresses this gap by developing a taxonomy of eight dimensions and 25 characteristics to structure the MCABC analysis design space. Using a dataset of 108 configurations, cluster analysis identifies six recurring archetypes that serve as implementation-ready templates for inventory analysis. Archetype 2: artificial intelligence (AI)+-driven cluster minimalist enables rapid, cost-focused inventory structuring with minimal data and no expert input. In contrast, Archetype 1: AI+-driven complex ranker uses expert-weighted multi-criteria analysis to support holistic and sustainability oriented inventory strategies. The taxonomy and archetypes provide a unified framework for researchers to theorize inventory design trade-offs and for practitioners to apply scalable blueprints for mature inventory analyses. © 2025 The Author(s). title: Decoding entrepreneurial intention: A systematic review, theoretical framework synthesis, and research trajectories
abstract: Entrepreneurial intention (EI) is a critical psychological construct for understanding the precursors of entrepreneurial behavior. Despite a surge in empirical research over the past decade, the literature on EI remains fragmented across theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and contextual applications. This study systematically reviews 53 peer-reviewed articles on entrepreneurial intention published between 2018 and 2025 to synthesize theoretical frameworks, methodological patterns, key findings, and future research directions. Guided by the PRISMA approach, the review reveals the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as the predominant model, frequently integrated with constructs from Social Cognitive Theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and moral or contextual frameworks. Quantitative cross-sectional designs dominate the methodological landscape, often involving university student samples and the use of structural equation modelling techniques for hypothesis testing. Findings consistently confirm the central role of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and self-efficacy in predicting EI, while more recent studies highlight the growing significance of emotional intelligence, cultural influences, institutional support, and entrepreneurship education. However, the review identifies key limitations, including the overreliance on student-based samples, a lack of longitudinal and experimental designs, and limited generalizability to actual entrepreneurial behavior in real-world settings. Additionally, contextual diversity across emerging and developed economies remains underexplored. In response, the study proposes five future research trajectories: theoretical expansion beyond dominant models, increased adoption of behavioral and longitudinal approaches, broader contextual and demographic inclusion, pedagogical innovation in entrepreneurship education, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. By mapping evolving trends and gaps in EI research, this review provides a foundation for more dynamic, inclusive, and practically relevant scholarship in entrepreneurship studies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

title: Municipal utilities and SDG adoption: Evidence from Austria and Germany
abstract: This paper explores how municipal utilities (MUs) in Austria and Germany adopt and integrate the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into their strategies, strategic projects and management controls (MCs). MUs have a long tradition of delivering public infrastructure services, such as energy, water, and public transport, in the two focus countries. As important municipal enterprises, MUs must position themselves on a continuum between their public mission and their business orientation, and therefore act in a financially sustainable manner. Taking SDG adoption seriously is in line with the public mission orientation. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the study investigates whether MUs engage with the SDGs symbolically or substantively. The research is based on nineteen semi-structured interviews conducted with representatives from sixteen MUs, allowing for an in-depth qualitative analysis of strategic alignment, project implementation, and related MCs. The findings reveal considerable variation in SDG integration, showing that most MUs are still in an early, emerging stage of adoption, which is still at a symbolic level. By providing empirical insights from two countries with long-standing traditions of municipal service provision by local government-owned public utilities, the study contributes to the limited literature on SDG adoption in municipal enterprises and enhances understanding of the legitimacy dynamics shaping SDG practices in local state-owned entities. © 2026 The Authors. title: Enhancing repeat patronage in beauty clinics: An integrated model of trust and consumer perceptions
abstract: This study aims to explain how trust drives repeat patronage in the beauty clinic industry by examining the roles of service quality, price fairness, and influencer credibility. A quantitative explanatory approach was applied using survey data from 360 beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS to test direct and indirect relationships among variables. The results show that perceived service quality, perceived price fairness, and influencer credibility each have positive and significant direct effects on both repurchase intention and brand trust, and that brand trust itself significantly and positively drives repurchase intention. Brand trust also partially mediates the effects of all three antecedents on repurchase intention, indicating that consumers' evaluations of service, price, and influencers shape repeat patronage both directly and through the trust these evaluations help to build. These findings suggest that improving service quality, price fairness perception, and influencer credibility can enhance consumer trust in a brand, which ultimately increases repurchase intention in beauty clinic services. This study is limited to beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. Beauty clinic managers should focus on trust-building strategies through consistent service quality, transparent pricing, and collaboration with credible social media influencers to foster long-term consumer relationships. This study provides an integrated model that empirically demonstrates the mediating role of brand trust in the beauty clinic industry. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Environmental sustainability in the Lancang–Mekong River Basin: Research progress, emerging themes, and future directions under climate change and hydropower development
abstract: Climate change and hydropower development are reshaping environmental sustainability in the Lancang–Mekong River Basin (LMRB) through their interacting effects on hydrological processes, ecosystems, water resources, and socioeconomic systems. This study provides an integrated review of environmental sustainability research in the LMRB by combining scientometric analysis with systematic thematic synthesis. A total of 356 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2005 to 2024 were analyzed to characterize the evolution of research output, collaboration patterns, influential studies, and major thematic hotspots. The reviewed literature is concentrated around three broad themes: climate change and hydrological change, environmental degradation and ecosystem responses, and hydropower development and water-resource interactions. The synthesis further highlights important concerns related to river connectivity, sediment and fisheries, biodiversity, water quality, and the social consequences of environmental change. An indicator-based comparative risk characterization shows that connectivity loss and sediment–fishery interactions represent particularly important environmental pressures, while social dimensions such as equity, vulnerability, public health, and adaptive capacity remain comparatively underrepresented in basin-scale assessments. Future research should strengthen multi-source data integration, cumulative-impact assessment, environmental–socioeconomic analysis, and transboundary cooperation to support more adaptive and integrated sustainability management across the basin. title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. These findings should be interpreted in light of the qualitative nature of the synthesis. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Targeted Modulation of Zn Deposition Behavior toward High-Performance Stable Zn Anodes
abstract: Dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions at the Zn metal anode remain critical obstacles to the commercialization of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Zn anode design regulates Zn deposition behavior from its thermodynamic and kinetic roots and is therefore recognized as a pivotal strategy to address the above bottlenecks. However, Zn deposition evolves through a complex multistage nucleation-growth process, and the structure–property relationship between the anode designs and practical Zn deposition behavior remains to be elucidated. This review focuses on Zn deposition substrate and functional interphase engineering, systematically elucidates the microscopic mechanisms and key regulatory targets of Zn deposition at each stage, and establishes a multidimensional regulation framework covering atomic tuning, interfacial modification, and spatial confinement. Based on this framework, we summarize three core design strategies, namely zincophilic regulation, lattice-matched effects, and three-dimensional structural engineering, and provide in-depth elucidation of the working mechanism and structure-property relationship of each strategy. By correlating these fundamental principles with the latest research advances in the field, we highlight the paradigm shift from empirical trial and error to rational material design. Finally, we outline the prevailing challenges and future research directions for Zn anode design, aiming to provide actionable insights for the development of advanced dendrite-free Zn anodes toward high-performance AZIBs. title: Optimal carbon quota allocation for power system decarbonization: a two-stage peer-to-peer market framework
abstract: Amid the global pursuit of deep decarbonization, effectively harnessing demand-side resources has emerged as a crucial strategy, particularly as end-user consumption is a primary driver of carbon emissions. However, existing demand-side carbon policies often impose a significant financial burden on consumers and struggle to utilize carbon quota resources to achieve effective emission reductions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel two-stage framework for carbon quota allocation to advance the decarbonization of power systems. The first stage introduces an allocation strategy that accounts for the heterogeneous low-carbon potential among different consumers, thereby regulating the supply-demand dynamics of the secondary carbon market. The second stage establishes a peer-to-peer carbon market based on a double-auction mechanism to support efficient and transparent rule-based trading. Within this market, an optimal bidding model is formulated to capture the strategic interactions among participants. To solve this complex optimization problem, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is developed, which incorporates a centralized reward mechanism to improve computational tractability. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework. © 2026

title: AI guest personalization as driver of hotel performance and hotel guest behavior: A dual-model analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven personalization is reshaping hotel operations, yet evidence on its financial effects and guest acceptance mechanisms remains limited. This study adopts a dual-perspective design combining hotel-level performance modeling with guest-level behavioral analysis. Study 1 examines revenue dynamics using Interrupted Time Series (ITS), SARIMA forecasting, and TOPSIS, comparing AI-driven and non-AI-driven hotels based on publicly documented implementations of AI personalization. Findings indicate heterogeneous short-term responses but more consistent differences in long-term revenue stability and predictability. Study 2 develops a Diffusion of Innovation–based structural model extended with trust in AI as a mediator, using survey data from 1396 hotel guests. Relative advantage and compatibility increase trust and adoption intention, whereas complexity reduces them; trust partially mediates these effects. Multi-group analysis reveals model differences between business and leisure guests. Overall, the study provides complementary evidence on revenue dynamics and adoption mechanisms of AI personalization in hospitality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT
abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Previous studies in general management have indicated that the decision-making processes are highly related to stakeholders’ attributes (power, legitimacy and urgency). However, such studies have not yet been conducted in the field of campus management. Therefore, this paper aims to identify the importance of key stakeholders in campus development and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) that are essential for decisionmakers in determining and explaining how their efforts are progressing towards achieving various stakeholders’ goals. To explore the underlying importance of campus stakeholders, a theory on stakeholder salience and a questionnaire survey among Polish public HEIs were employed. In turn, to identify various KPIs, the content analysis of institutions’ strategies was conducted. Empirical research suggests that in Polish public HEIs, authorities and academic staff continue to be regarded as the most important stakeholders (at different stages of the building’s life cycle, respectively). This contrasts with the growing market-oriented approach seen in higher education globally. Moreover, the KPIs presented in HEIs’ strategies are predominantly result-focused and rarely user-centric (which have begun to be perceived as the most significant with respect to building performance). © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Research Competence of a Modern Teacher as a Factor in Improving the Quality of Education and Supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: This study examines teacher research competence as a factor in improving educational quality and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Using theoretical analysis, survey data, and economic-mathematical modeling, the study clarifies the structure, conditions, and impact of research competence in modern teaching. Data from 10 secondary school teachers were collected through a questionnaire assessing professional competencies, temperament, motivation, stress resistance, and burnout. Communicative and methodological competencies were strongest, while research, managerial, digital, and inclusive competencies need further development. Research competence was positively related to intrinsic motivation and methodological competence. title: Government subsidy policy and farmer’s live-streaming strategy in the fresh agricultural products supply chain
abstract: Live-streaming serves as an effective means to promote the sales of fresh agricultural products. Farmers cooperate with streamers for live-streaming through the direct or resale live-streaming strategy. The third-party logistics service provider offers cold-chain services to maintain the freshness of agricultural products. Meanwhile, the government provides subsidies to farmers, streamers, or consumers. Motivated by this background, this study investigates a farmer’s choice of live-streaming strategy and its impact on other supply chain members. We find that, first, when streamer traffic is high, the farmer should adopt the resale live-streaming strategy. When streamer traffic is low, the farmer should adopt the direct live-streaming strategy if the government subsidizes farmers or consumers; if the government subsidizes streamers, the farmer’s decision on live-streaming strategy is also affected by unit subsidy. Second, the high-traffic streamer always prefers the resale live-streaming strategy, whereas the low-traffic streamer’s preference for the live-streaming strategy depends on the government subsidy policy. Finally, if streamer traffic is low (high) and subsidy is low, the government can promote the sales of fresh agricultural products, increase the farmer’s profit, and improve social welfare by subsidizing farmers (streamers); otherwise, subsidizing consumers may improve social welfare, but it is not conducive to the sales of fresh agricultural products or farmer’s profit. Furthermore, we conduct an extension study with an endogenous subsidy to verify the robustness of the main results. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Why travelers prefer humans over artificial intelligence (AI): Developing and testing an AI aversion model in tourism
abstract: As tourism businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance traveler decision-making, a persistent reluctance to rely on AI-generated recommendations has emerged as a critical barrier. This research addresses this gap by developing and validating an AI aversion model that identifies the factors driving traveler resistance to AI-generated recommendations. Using a mixed-methods approach, this research uncovered five core drivers rooted in the perceived absence of human nature attributes: lived experience, emotional engagement, contextual understanding, domain specific knowledge, and proactive engagement in communication. Twenty-three items were developed and validated in a multicultural context. Additionally, we revealed that individual differences (i.e., rational vs. emotional personalities) play a moderating role, which can offer a way to mitigate the negative impacts of AI. The findings offer theoretical contributions by enriching the understanding of AI aversion and repositioning technology resistance through a human lens and extending practical implications for firms aiming to integrate AI effectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Scenario-based robust optimization for the design of a resilient and sustainable power supply chain network using energy storage system
abstract: The increasing demand for electricity, along with the growing reliance on intermittent renewable energy sources, presents significant challenges for building resilient and cost-efficient power supply chains. This study introduces a hybrid multi-objective mathematical modeling framework that integrates renewable and non-renewable power generation units, multi-level substations, and strategically located energy storage systems. A scenario-based robust optimization model is developed to jointly minimize total system costs and maximize the performance of selected energy storage system technologies. The latter is quantified through a hybrid hierarchical group decision-making method combining the best‒worst method and the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution and is incorporated into the model as a secondary objective via the improved weighted augmented ε-constraint technique. To strengthen system resilience, the model includes strategies such as diversification of generation technologies, capacity expansion of substations and lines, deployment of redundant transmission paths, and optimal siting of energy storage systems. A real-world case study from an Iranian province is conducted to evaluate the model’s effectiveness under disruption scenarios. The results demonstrate the framework’s ability to provide robust infrastructure planning under uncertainty. Furthermore, Pareto-based analysis reveals the trade-offs between investment cost and system performance, supporting informed decision-making in resilience-oriented energy planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Breaking the cycle of malice: Influence mechanism and intervention of social exclusion on malevolent creativity in adolescents
abstract: Creativity is the core driving force for humans to break through existing boundaries and promote continuous social progress, and its positive impacts have been widely recognized. However, creativity also has a dark side, namely, malevolent creativity, which poses significant potential harm to society. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to conduct research on malevolent creativity to prevent its negative impacts. Based on the 4P model of creativity, this study explored the impact mechanism between social exclusion and malevolent creativity (Study 1) and the effectiveness of a group counseling intervention for self-concept clarity (Study 2). Study 1 conducted a field questionnaire survey (N = 1567). The results showed that social exclusion not only directly increased malevolent creativity, but also indirectly predicted it through the independent mediating effects of reduced self-concept clarity and heightened negative emotions, as well as through the serial mediating effect whereby reduced self-concept clarity led to increased negative emotions, which in turn predicted malevolent creativity. Trait mindfulness moderated the impact of social exclusion on self-concept clarity, with higher levels of trait mindfulness alleviating the negative effects of social exclusion on self-concept clarity. Study 2 utilized a group counseling intervention (N = 30) and demonstrated that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in self-concept clarity and a significant decrease in malevolent creativity after the intervention. The study's conclusions provide educators with references and insights for correctly understanding the impact of social exclusion and for offering interventions to enhance self-concept clarity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Enhanced Antibiotics Sieving by Exfoliated TiS2 Membranes via Surface Functionalization and Passivation
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanolaminate membranes hold great promise for molecular sieving due to their two-dimensional capillary structures, which facilitate size-restricted diffusion. However, many transition metal sulfides exhibit intrinsic instability and are highly susceptible to oxidation, which severely limits their durability under reverse osmosis operating conditions. In this work, we introduce a stable 1T phase titanium disulfide (TiS2) constructing nanolaminate membranes from Group IVB, enabling the formation of tunable capillary channels and achieving a permeance up to 46.8 L m−2 h−1 bar−1. Experiments confirm that water-initiated hydrolysis, rather than direct oxidation by molecular O2, dominates the degradation of TiS2, while alkyl-chain hydrophobic barriers effectively suppress this water-triggered degradation. The enhanced surface hydrophobic properties simultaneously improve antioxidation stability and ensure sustained performance over 30 filtration cycles and 15 days of continuous operation. Functionalized membranes further reached 96.9% rejection for diverse antibiotics, such as sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and rifampicin. This work opens new avenues for exploring emerging TMD materials in the efficient and reliable removal of trace antibiotics from water, contributing to safer water resources and promoting sustainable ecological practices. title: Bioinspired Molecular Magnetic Field-Responsive Catalyst for On-Demand Switching of 2e− and 4e− Oxygen Reduction
abstract: Achieving precise and on-demand steering of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) pathway between the efficient 4e− route to H2O and the valuable 2e− route to H2O2 remains a pivotal challenge in electrocatalysis. Herein, we address this challenge by designing a bioinspired molecular magnetic field-responsive catalyst (MMFR-C) via magnetic single-atom-anchored Salen-based covalent organic frameworks (MSA-Salen COFs) onto magnetic nanoparticles (single/multi-domain Fe3O4). Mimicking cytochrome c oxidase, the MMFR-C employs MSA-Salen COFs as an ordered proton-transfer channel and well-defined N2-M-O2 moieties as enzymatic O2 activation sites, with Fe3O4 providing a built-in magnetic field for remote regulation of the active-site electronic structure. The bioinspired MMFR-C exhibits switchable ORR pathways. Relative to the pristine Co-Salen COF (26% H2O2 selectivity, n = 3.48), the MMFR-C integrated with a single-domain Fe3O4 exhibits a remarkably enhanced H2O2 selectivity of 63.9% (n = 2.72), while that with a multi-domain Fe3O4 diverts the ORR pathway toward the 4e− route (n = 3.67). (i) We elucidate that the uniform magnetic field from the single-domain Fe3O4 in MMFR-C favors orbital hybridization between its active N2-M-O2 moieties and the *OOH intermediate, with moderate *OOH adsorption suppressing O–O scission and thus steering ORR selectivity toward H2O2. (ii) In contrast, the enhanced specific magnetism from its multi-domain Fe3O4 core optimizes the d-band center of MMFR-C’s active sites, stabilizes triplet O2 adsorption, and reduces spin-forbidden transition barriers, thereby facilitating O–O cleavage and diverting its ORR pathway to the 4e− route. title: Management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises: The roles of technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality in an ai-driven business environment
abstract: The tourism industry is experiencing unprecedented transformation driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and the rapid evolution of smart tourism ecosystems. At the same time, tourism enterprises face growing pressure to enhance service quality while controlling operational costs and improving managerial responsiveness. In this context, management accounting effectiveness has become a critical capability for supporting strategic decision-making and maintaining sustainable competitiveness. Although previous studies have examined digital transformation and accounting systems separately, limited attention has been paid to how technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality jointly influence management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises operating in emerging economies. Addressing this research gap, the present study investigates the effects of these three determinants on management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism enterprises. Grounded in the resource-based view, contingency theory, dynamic capabilities theory, and sociotechnical systems theory, the study adopts a mixed-method research design consisting of expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. Data were collected from 315 tourism enterprises, with chief accountants, general accountants, and management accounting personnel serving as key respondents. The data were analyzed using SPSS through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The empirical findings demonstrate that technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality all exert positive and statistically significant effects on management accounting effectiveness. Among these determinants, information technology infrastructure emerges as the strongest predictor, followed by technology readiness and data quality. These findings indicate that tourism enterprises equipped with integrated digital infrastructure, advanced technological capabilities, and high-quality accounting data are better positioned to generate timely, accurate, and strategically relevant management accounting information in AI-enabled business environments. This study extends the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy and contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation and management accounting. The findings also offer practical implications for tourism managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital accounting capabilities, improve managerial decision-making, and enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism enterprises in the era of AI-driven business transformation. title: An advanced integrated cross-sectoral model for formulating government strategies on energy consumption management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions toward achieving net-zero emissions in the future
abstract: This study aims to develop a model that identifies alternative scenarios for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by examining the interrelationships among the circular economy, socio-cultural, and environmental sectors, with the ultimate goal of supporting Thailand's net-zero emissions target. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study provides a foundation for developing integrated national management strategies that promote long-term sustainability. A novel model, referred to as the Path–Probit–Logit–ARx Model (Path Analysis–Probit–Logit Model based on Autoregressive with Exogenous Variables), was developed to address the study objectives. The findings reveal that, during the period 1992–2025, the circular economy sector experienced continuous growth, which directly contributed to the steady expansion of the socio-cultural sector. The growth of both sectors also exerted a positive influence on the environmental sector. Furthermore, the environmental sector was found to have a direct positive effect on the socio-cultural sector, indicating a bidirectional relationship between these two sectors. This finding suggests that environmentally responsible societies can promote long-term ecosystem development and that environmental and social development should progress concurrently. Based on the analysis, the study identified the adoption of electric vehicles as the most sensitive and effective scenario for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Under this scenario, the growth rate of final energy consumption is reduced to 33%, while greenhouse gas emission growth decreases to 53.73%, remaining below the critical threshold of 590.05 Mt CO2 equivalent and thereby meeting the government's target. To enhance the policy relevance and credibility of the findings, a focus group consisting of 15 experts was conducted to validate the results. The experts confirmed the appropriateness and accuracy of the proposed scenario and agreed that it is suitable for promoting sustainable development in Thailand. However, they emphasized the need for immediate action and strong governmental support to ensure effective implementation. Therefore, the findings of this study can support evidence-based decision-making and strategic planning, contributing to the development of Thailand's long-term national strategies through 2065. © 2026 The Authors. title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Integrating culturally embedded human factors with organisational safety mechanisms provides a more comprehensive approach to engineering safety management and supports the development of human-centred safety interventions for complex industrial operations. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. .

title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality
abstract: Existing coke quality prediction methods mainly rely on a two-stage prediction strategy, where blended coal properties are first estimated from individual coal properties and then used for coke quality prediction. This process inevitably introduces information loss and accumulated prediction errors, which limit the prediction accuracy and reliability of these models in practical coal blending applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes, for the first time, a graph-based direct association strategy linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality. Each coal blending scheme is transformed into a graph structure, where individual coal samples are regarded as graph nodes and their corresponding coal properties together with blending ratios are used as node features. Different graph neural network models are further investigated to directly learn the relationship between individual coal properties and coke quality indicators, namely Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). A total of 306 coal blending schemes are used for model development and evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed one-stage graph-based framework outperforms traditional two-stage prediction methods. Among different graph neural network models, the graph attention network achieves the best overall prediction performance, obtaining mean absolute errors of 2.06 and 2.60 for CRI and CSR prediction, respectively. The t-SNE visualization further demonstrates that the proposed one-stage framework can learn more discriminative feature representations than the traditional two-stage framework. In addition, the proposed framework demonstrates good robustness under blending conditions with different numbers of coal types and can provide interpretable analysis through feature importance and node importance visualization. Furthermore, fuzzy interpretability is introduced at the feature level to characterize the gradual contribution levels of different coal properties. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Diversification or concentration? Supply chain configuration responses to decoupling risk
abstract: This study investigates corporate supply chain configuration strategies in the context of perceived decoupling risk. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2023, we employ textual analysis to construct a firm-level index of perceived decoupling risk. Building on this index, we empirically examine its effect on corporate supply chain configuration strategies. The findings reveal that a higher level of perceived decoupling risk prompts firms to pursue greater supply chain diversification, leading to a significant decrease in supply chain concentration; notably, the diversification response is concentrated among firms facing high-intensity risk perception, while low-intensity risk perception is associated with minimal supply chain adjustment. Further analysis reveals that this negative association is attenuated by both executive risk preference and the level of corporate investment irreversibility. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the reduction in supply chain concentration is more pronounced for firms with high overseas revenue exposure, those in strategic emerging industries, and small-scale enterprises. Additionally, this impact is amplified during periods of heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly following the U.S.-China trade frictions in 2018, and is more pronounced in the upstream ends of supply chains. Finally, we find that the proactive supply chain diversification triggered by decoupling risk significantly enhances firms' operational resilience after a three-year adjustment period, demonstrating a long-term benefit for corporate stability. By quantifying firms’ subjective perception of decoupling risk and confirming its significant impact on supply chain configuration, this study provides novel micro-level evidence on firms’ supply chain behaviors in response to external environmental uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: An Analysis of Interactive and Interactional Metadiscourse Markers in Applied Linguistics Webinars: The Case of Top-Tier Native vs. Non-Native Speaking Scholars
abstract: Within the ecosystem of genres, audiences, and modalities, knowledge dissemination relies on metadiscourse markers that guide and engage academic audiences. Despite digital technologies reshaping communication after the pandemic, their use in academic webinars, especially regarding speakers’ linguistic backgrounds, remains an underresearched area of inquiry. Accordingly, this study aimed to comprehensively analyze interactive and interactional metadiscourse markers utilized by both top-tier native and non-native scholars in Applied Linguistics webinars. To this end, a corpus of 24 webinars (24 hours and 35 minutes) conducted by top-tier Applied Linguists over five years was purposively selected and analyzed using Hyland’s (2005) metadiscourse model, focusing on the frequency and distribution of interactive and interactional markers. The results showed that native scholars employed metadiscourse markers (both interactive and interactional) somewhat more frequently than non-natives, though both groups used them extensively to organize and engage audiences. While natives favored interactional markers over interactive ones, non-natives demonstrated the opposite trend, relying more on interactive than interactional markers. These findings highlight the need for EAP/ESP pedagogy to extend beyond accuracy, fostering non-native scholars’ interactional competence through training in hedges, boosters, attitude markers, and self-mentions, empowering them to communicate confidently, engage audiences, and sustain presence in global academia. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Economic design of residential solar resources under uncertainty: An adaptive robust optimization approach for EV households
abstract: The integration of residential PV systems with electric vehicles (EVs) offers significant opportunities to enhance self-consumption, reduce reliance on the grid, and lower household energy costs. Effective PV system sizing, however, is challenged by uncertainties in PV generation, household electricity demand, and EV charging behavior. While traditional approaches often ignore uncertainties or assume predefined values for uncertainties, this paper develops an adaptive robust optimization framework for sizing residential PV systems in EV-integrated households, explicitly accounting for operational uncertainties and calibrating the uncertainty parameters using a Genetic Algorithm. The proposed model explicitly incorporates multi-source uncertainty using a budgeted adaptive robust optimization approach. Investment decisions, such as PV capacity, are modeled as here-and-now variables, while operational variability is captured as wait-and-see decisions responding to uncertainty realizations. To mitigate the inherent conservatism of robust optimization and identify optimal uncertainty settings, a Genetic Algorithm–based calibration is integrated. The GA iteratively searches for the best combination of uncertainty parameters through simulation-based evaluation, balancing robustness and economic efficiency. The results show that calibrated uncertainty parameters provide a cost-effective and resilient system design, avoiding oversized PV capacities while improving household energy performance by reducing the cost of energy up to 18%. © 2026

title: Offshore infrastructure decommissioning, just transitions, and the struggle for the right to the sea: Small-scale fishers’ perspectives from coastal Ghana
abstract: Offshore petroleum infrastructure decommissioning is usually framed as a technical and environmental process requiring technical expertise. Yet, offshore infrastructure decommissioning could have deleterious consequences on adjacent coastal communities and livelihoods. Drawing on qualitative data from 65 respondents from Ghanaian coastal communities of Saltpond and Kormantse, this paper investigates small-scale fishers’ experiences of offshore oil and gas infrastructure decommissioning. The paper frames decommissioning as a critical phase of energy transition and interrogates its outcomes through the dual lenses of just transitions and the “right to the sea.” The findings reveal that decommissioning produces socio-ecological and economic disruptions. These include the creation of offshore safety zones leading to spatial exclusion of fishing activities, the erosion of socio-ecological knowledge systems, material precarity through asset loss, and ecological uncertainty linked to perceptions of pollution. While these processes are officially justified on grounds of safety and environmental protection, they are experienced locally as forms of livelihood dispossession and governance exclusion. The study argues that decommissioning represents an unjust transition, in which the challenges associated with post-extractive restructuring are disproportionately shifted onto vulnerable coastal communities. At the same time, it is a struggle over the right to the sea, as regulatory and security mechanisms reconfigure access to marine space in ways that privilege state and industrial actors over fisherfolk. The paper concludes that achieving socially just and sustainable decommissioning outcomes requires moving beyond technical compliance toward inclusive governance frameworks that recognise local knowledge, ensure equitable access to marine resources, and address the livelihood impacts of transition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Influencer beware: The buffering role of sponsor–influencer fit in the commercialization-authenticity trade-off
abstract: As social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly commercialize their online presence through sponsored content, understanding how sponsorship intensity shapes consumer responses has become important. Drawing on attribution and congruence theories and the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how sponsorship levels influence audience engagement and purchase intentions through perceived personal authenticity (PPA) and whether these effects depend on sponsor–SMI fit. Three experimental studies were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results show that higher sponsorship levels reduce consumers’ intention to follow influencers and share their content. Sponsor–SMI fit attenuates the negative effect of sponsorship intensity on PPA. Thereby mitigating its adverse effects on consumer engagement and purchase intentions. We further demonstrate that sponsorship level affects consumer responses indirectly through PPA and that this indirect effect is contingent on sponsor–SMI fit. These findings advance the influencer marketing literature by applying the ERC framework to distinguish the different authenticity types and their impact on consumer behavior. The study also extends attribution and congruence theories by explaining how and when commercialization influences consumer responses and offers practical guidance for balancing monetization and authenticity in influencer marketing. © 2026 The Authors

title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

title: Transforming value of sustainability in urban development: Reconfiguring logistics service in the construction industry
abstract: Urban development depends on construction activity to improve sustainability, yet the logistics required to move materials, equipment, waste, and workers remains insufficiently integrated into urban planning. This paper examines how construction logistics can be integrated into municipal urban planning by analysing how actor groups perceive its impacts and coordinate value creation across fragmented urban systems. The study applies a qualitative interactive research design based on a Swedish construction logistics project. Data were collected between August 2022 and March 2024 through eight semi-structured group interviews, joint workshops, actor-specific validation workshops, and a final synthesis workshop with developers, main contractors, suppliers, and trade organizations. The analysis combines iterative thematic coding with value configuration theory. The findings show that suppliers emphasize efficiency and climate savings, main contractors focus on project efficiency and safety, developers stress sustainability, accessibility and accountability, while trade organizations highlight knowledge-building and sector coordination. These differences create misalignment because societal benefits are often separated from project-level costs. Four conditions are identified as central: clearer procurement requirements, stronger logistics knowledge, scalable logistics service designs, and systematic follow-up of time, cost, and emission effects. The paper concludes that municipalities should use procurement, planning requirements and follow-up mechanisms to enforce construction logistics values in urban planning. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A blockchain-enabled distributed service configuration approach for distributed smart manufacturing systems
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, distributed manufacturing (DM) paradigms, exemplified by cloud manufacturing (CMfg), have garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. These paradigms aim to achieve the precise matching of geographically dispersed manufacturing resources with personalized demands. However, existing research on service configuration predominantly relies on centralized information architectures, which pose critical challenges such as single point of failure (SPoF), data privacy leakage risks, and limited scalability. To address these issues, this paper investigates how blockchain technology can be leveraged to enable trustworthy collaboration and distributed decision-making in DM systems. Specifically, we propose a Blockchain-enabled Cyber-Physical Network (BCPN) architecture and design a complete and executable business process tailored to service configuration requirements. Furthermore, a systematic solution is developed that integrates several key components, including a reputation evaluation contract, a service pre-screening contract, a proof of reputation (PoR) consensus mechanism, a distributed service configuration contract, and a backward time propagation smart contract based on breadth-first search (BFS). Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed BCPN solution in trust establishment, privacy preservation, and system scalability, providing a novel theoretical framework and methodological pathway for the distributed governance of DM systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Hot war tourism: The touristification of unresolved conflict
abstract: This article conceptualises hot war tourism as the touristification of unresolved conflict: configurations in which conflict continues materially to shape civilian vulnerability, security and visitor access while conflict-affected places and experiences acquire experiential, representational or market value. A critical integrative review clarifies its boundaries with dark, battlefield, military, risk, recovery and solidarity-oriented tourism and identifies five dimensions: temporal immediacy, spatial proximity, commodification, moral and motivational ambiguity, and governance and responsibility. Ukraine and Syria illustrate contrasting active-war witnessing and recovery–normalisation configurations. A relational framework locates war-related tourism according to the degree of unresolved conflict and the intensity of touristification, while a multi-actor governance framework specifies responsibilities for access, risk disclosure, representation, consent, platform accountability, humanitarian non-interference and escalation. The concept links tourism value production to unresolved harm and provides a basis for analysing when conflict-related visitation requires facilitation, restraint or restriction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java: The roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, innovation capability, and ESG
abstract: This study examines the determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java by analyzing the roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) implementation, innovation capability, and organizational performance. Social enterprises in emerging economies increasingly face challenges in maintaining long-term sustainability due to resource limitations, institutional uncertainty, and dynamic social demands. Although previous studies have explored intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, ESG practices, and innovation capability separately, limited empirical research has integrated these variables into a comprehensive sustainability model within the context of social enterprises in emerging economies, particularly Indonesia. Therefore, this study seeks to address this gap by developing and testing an integrated model of social enterprise sustainability. This research adopts a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were collected from 200 owners and managers of social enterprises operating across six provinces on Java Island. The findings reveal that entrepreneurial orientation has a strong and significant effect on innovation capability (β = 0.699, p < 0.001), while ESG implementation significantly influences social enterprise performance (β = 0.402, p < 0.001). Intellectual capital and entrepreneurial orientation significantly contribute to innovation capability, whereas ESG implementation directly improves organizational performance and sustainability. Furthermore, innovation capability acts as a crucial mediating variable that strengthens the relationship between strategic organizational resources and sustainability outcomes. Social enterprise performance also demonstrates a significant mediating role in achieving long-term sustainability. These findings highlight the importance of innovation-driven strategies, knowledge-based resources, and ESG-oriented governance in strengthening the resilience and sustainability of social enterprises. This study contributes to the development of sustainability and social entrepreneurship literature while providing practical implications for managers and policymakers in building a more sustainable social enterprise ecosystem in emerging economies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process
abstract: Digital technologies influence consumers across need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase activity. This study examines how six features of digitally mediated promotion—informativeness, personalisation, interactivity, entertainment, credibility, and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)—shape attitudes and subsequent behavioural responses among Albanian consumers. It also evaluates attitude as a mediator, media literacy as a moderator, and differences across decision-journey stages. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 487 valid responses from adults residing in Albania who had recently used online channels in purchase-related activity. The conceptual model integrates the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the Theory of Planned Behaviour, and the customer-journey perspective. Measurement and structural relationships were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples; supplementary analyses tested mediation, moderation, age-group differences, and stage-specific effects. Results: Credibility was the strongest predictor of attitude (β = 0.291), followed by positive eWOM (β = 0.245) and informativeness (β = 0.230). Attitude positively predicted purchase intention (β = 0.597), online engagement (β = 0.467), and recommendation intention (β = 0.517), while purchase intention predicted self-reported purchasing (β = 0.553). Attitude mediated the effects of all six promotional features on purchase intention. Media literacy strengthened the informativeness–attitude relationship (β = 0.109), whereas age-group differences were not significant. Influence was greatest during information search and alternative evaluation. Conclusion: Effective online communication depends more on usefulness, credibility, and authentic social evidence than on entertainment alone. The findings extend evidence from a Southeast European setting and show that favourable attitudes translate into purchases only when perceived value, affordability, payment, and delivery conditions permit conversion. Managers should therefore combine transparent information and trustworthy reviews with financially clear offers and sustained post-purchase support. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: From eco-signals to green trust: How tourists evaluate sustainability credibility through online reviews
abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. This study examines how tourists interpret environmental practices by analyzing 138,683 online reviews from major Southeast and East Asian coastal and island destinations. Drawing on signaling theory and attribution theory, the study proposes that observable sustainability cues are associated with eco-authenticity inference, which is linked to green trust and, in turn, more positive review sentiment. Using natural language processing, topic modeling, regression analysis, mediation analysis, and robustness checks for sparse text-derived variables, the findings show a positive association between eco-signal richness and eco-authenticity inference, as well as a significant indirect association from eco-authenticity inference to sentiment through green trust. Eco-authenticity inference is not directly associated with more positive sentiment once green trust is included. Because the focal sustainability, authenticity, and trust expressions are infrequent and have median values of zero, the findings identify a consistent but sparse textual pattern rather than a large or pervasive psychological effect. Because the Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner (VADER) is English-oriented, VADER-based sentiment models were also checked using the English-language subset; the qualitative pattern remained consistent. Topic modeling provides supplementary contextual evidence that sustainability discourse in reviews is episodic and grounded in concrete visitor experiences. Practically, the findings suggest that destinations and tourism providers should make sustainability practices visible, verifiable, and experience-based rather than relying on abstract promotional claims. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Can a transversal adaptation of teaching materials foster students’ entrepreneurial intentions? A quasi-experimental exploration in a statistics course setting
abstract: We propose that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content within other curricula may be an effective approach to foster students' entrepreneurial intentions. We embedded entrepreneurship content in an otherwise unrelated statistics course targeting the theory of planned behavior constructs of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms in relation to entrepreneurship. 350 Swiss students (193 intervention group, 157 control group) participated in a nine-week quasi-experiment to explore the effects of this intervention. Structural equation modeling suggests that being in the intervention group affected students' attitude toward entrepreneurship, which in turn was associated with higher entrepreneurial intentions by the end of the intervention. The intervention did not affect perceived behavioral control nor subjective norms and changes in these variables were neither associated with change in entrepreneurial intentions. Unexpectedly, the intervention did not improve students' attitude ratings but appeared to prevent their decline over time. A qualitative follow-up exploration with seven participants suggested that the data collection itself may have prompted students to reassess their attitude toward entrepreneurship. We conclude that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content into university curricula could play a key role in enhancing students’ entrepreneurial mindset and may, over time, support conditions conducive to innovation and creativity. © 2026 The Authors

title: Human capital development through community digital centers for inequality reduction in Thailand
abstract: Driving human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality requires multiple interrelated factors and components to ensure successful implementation. This study aims to examine the mechanisms of human capital development through community digital centers and to analyze the causal factors influencing human capital across various dimensions, with the goal of synthesizing practical recommendations for integrated community digital centers that support economic and social development. A mixed-methods approach was employed, consisting of quantitative research using questionnaires administered to 398 participants selected through accidental sampling with proportional allocation, along with qualitative research conducted through in-depth interviews with seven community digital center administrators selected using purposive sampling. The quantitative data were analyzed using Pearson's correlation coefficient and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that digital infrastructure, organizational management, personnel competency, and community participation were positively correlated with human capital development. The results of the multiple regression analysis indicated that digital infrastructure (B = 0.137), organizational management (B = 0.244), personnel competency (B = 0.225), and community participation (B = 0.303) significantly influenced human capital development through community digital centers to reduce inequality (p < 0.05). The qualitative findings further suggested the need for urgent policy reforms to improve management processes and transform community digital centers into learning hubs that emphasize the development of basic digital skills, foster motivation for technology use in daily life, and promote sustainable income generation within communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Exploring digital culture: A bibliometric review using keyword co-occurrence and performance analysis
abstract: Digital culture has become a central organizational phenomenon shaping how firms navigate digital transformation, emerging technologies, and sustainability pressures, yet prior research remains fragmented across disciplines and contexts. This study provides the first large-scale bibliometric mapping of digital culture research from an organizational perspective. Using the Scopus database, we analyzed 212 publications published between 2008 and 2025. Bibliometric techniques and VOSviewer were applied to examine (i) annual publication trends, (ii) thematic structures through keyword co-occurrence networks, (iii) influential knowledge producers across authors, affiliations, and countries, and (iv) document type distribution to infer field maturity. The results show a clear acceleration after 2020, culminating in more than 60 publications per year by 2025, indicating that digital culture has shifted from a niche conceptual topic to a consolidated research stream. Keyword co-occurrence reveals eight interconnected thematic clusters, with “digital culture” and “digital transformation” acting as the primary conceptual anchors and linking strongly to (1) digitalization and Industry 4.0 in SMEs, (2) performance and dynamic capabilities, (3) sustainability/ESG-oriented transformation, (4) digital strategy and structural alignment, (5) AI and IoT as emerging technological drivers, (6) the digital economy, (7) marketing and consumer interaction, and (8) leadership-driven innovation. Country production patterns highlight a recent geographic diversification, with rapid growth from emerging economies alongside established contributors. Document type analysis further indicates a field dominated by journal articles (68.0%), supported by book chapters (18.5%) and conference papers (11.0%), while reviews remain scarce, suggesting strong empirical expansion but limited synthesis. Overall, the study clarifies the intellectual structure, growth trajectory, and research frontiers of digital culture, offering a structured knowledge map to guide future theory building and research agendas. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Social and Spiritual Aspects Affecting Psychosocial Well-Being Among Early- and Late-Stage Oral Cancer Patients Presenting with Restricted Oral Functioning
abstract: Objective: There is increasing awareness of the diverse negative effects of cancer stage on the psychosocial well-being of patients with oral cancer. This study examined the role of social support and spiritual aspects in predicting psychosocial well-being among the early-and late-stage Malaysian oral cancer patients with restricted oral functioning, to inform a holistic model of cancer care. Material and Methods: Secondary data analysis was performed based on a health-related quality of life dataset among 96 oral cancer patients, collected from the Functional-Assessment of Cancer-Therapy–Head and Neck, Version 4.0 instrument between 2008 and 2015. Descriptive analyses, including correlation, were performed, followed by a hierarchical multiple regression using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) Version 25.0. Results: The multivariate analyses indicated moderate-strong relationships between the mean scores for oral functioning, social support, spiritual aspect, and psychosocial well-being among a cohort of both early (n=31) and late-stage (n=65) patients attending three visits: pre-treatment, 1 month, and 3 months post-treatment. However, only oral functioning and social support were found to be significant predictors of patients’ psychosocial well-being; with social support being the most significant predictor for both groups. In addition, social support was a mediator of oral functioning at pre-treatment among the late-stage group. Conclusion: These findings provide insights into how social support and spiritual aspects can contribute to improved psychosocial well-being among patients with compromised oral functioning. The results could potentially outline new provisions for a better holistic care model for oral cancer patients in Malaysia. © 2027 JHSMR.

title: Mining transitions in the Mid West of Western Australia: A regional transition knowledge system
abstract: Mining transitions are typically understood as the shift from active mining to post-mining futures requiring technical planning and stakeholder consultation. This framing overlooks how mining regions experience continuous transitions throughout project lifecycles and marginalises the knowledge communities accumulate through navigating these changes. Drawing on social constructionism and knowledge systems, this paper argues communities in the Mid West of Western Australia experience mining transitions within a broader regional context. Through community-engaged methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-two participants, including First Nations community members, across diverse sectors and sub-regions. Analysis revealed three interconnected knowledge forms: contextual knowledge situating mining within regional systems; observed knowledge from direct experiences of the mining industry; and practical knowledge of mining transitions and strategies to manage them. These forms constitute a regional transition knowledge system that already exists within communities in mining regions, distinct from industry expertise. The paper's contribution is identifying this knowledge system. Community knowledge operates across generations and addresses questions industry knowledge is not designed to ask about social disruption, intergenerational consequence, and the lived reality of being on the receiving end of decisions made elsewhere. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Towards a digital skills framework for the energy sector: Evidence from the Australian LNG industry
abstract: Digital innovations have become increasingly widespread in almost every industry, and Australia’s energy sector has not been immune to this. It therefore follows that the coordination of energy exports like liquified natural gas (LNG) across government, industry, and community stakeholders will be largely dependent on the ability of these constituents to share digital information between and among each other in useful timeframes. However, the success of these integrated data systems will hinge on the ability of the energy sector’s workforce to use these technologies effectively, but it is increasingly coming into focus that the industry’s workers have very uneven levels of proficiency with digital technologies. By synthesizing earlier digital skills frameworks from other industries and adding qualitative evidence distilled from 42 interviews with a broad range of employees throughout a midsize Australian LNG company, this paper puts forward a digital skills framework for the energy sector which identifies five skill areas that will be required in 2030: (1) data analytics, (2) digital communication and collaboration, (3) digital security, (4) digital ethical and social responsibility, and (5) digital innovation. The required level of proficiency that will be required in 2030 for each of these skill areas is then assessed for different discipline groups throughout the industry. We conclude by explaining how the presented framework can be used as an assessment tool for identifying skill gaps throughout the energy sector, and exploring the policy-related implications of the findings. © 2026 The Authors.
