title: Surfactant-Derived Nitrogen-Bridged MoS2/C Heterostructures for Robust Lithium-Ion Storage
abstract: Structural stability, ionic transport, and electronic conductivity are the major challenges of layered transition-metal dichalcogenide/carbon nanocomposites (LTMD/C) for lithium-ion storage. Herein, to address these challenges, a quaternary ammonium surfactant-mediated strategy is proposed to simultaneously construct porous MoS2 architectures and in situ generate nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) layers chemically coupled to MoS2 via interfacial Mo–N bridges. The resultant N-bridged MoS2/C heterostructures (denoted as MoS2–N–C) exhibit excellent structural robustness, expanded interlayer spacing, and improved charge-transfer kinetics. As an anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), the optimized MoS2–N–C700 electrode delivers remarkable cycling stability (~ 100% capacity retention after 800 cycles at 0.5 A g−1) and excellent rate capability. Moreover, lithium-ion supercapacitors (LISCs) based on the as-prepared MoS2–N–C composite achieve an ultrahigh power density of 3500 W kg−1, and excellent cycling stability over 10,000 cycles. The cycling performance in both LIBs and LISCs surpasses that of most previously reported MoS2/C nanocomposites and conventional carbon-based anodes. This surfactant-derived interfacial bridging structure design offers a general platform for developing robust LTMD/C heterostructured electrodes for energy storage systems. © Crown 2026.

title: E-retailer channel selection in live-streaming commerce: balancing traffic attraction and information disclosure
abstract: Live-streaming commerce allows e-retailers to attract new consumers, but it also provides valuation-relevant information that can make consumers more selective. This paper studies an e-retailer’s channel-entry and pricing decisions when a live broadcast channel simultaneously generates additional traffic and discloses noisy information about consumers’ true valuations for a new product. In our model, consumers in the original channel are initially uncertain about their match values and purchase based on their prior expected valuation. If the retailer opens the live broadcast channel, newly attracted consumers and informed consumers from the original channel can watch the live stream and update their valuations, whereas uninformed consumers remain in the original channel. We show that live-channel entry is governed by a tradeoff between traffic attraction and information disclosure. Although the live broadcast channel expands market reach, more accurate information induces low-valuation consumers to exit and weakens the retailer’s pricing power. Consequently, the retailer’s profit decreases with information accuracy, and entry is profitable only when the traffic-attraction effect is sufficiently strong. We further show that the retailer’s optimal price is non-monotonic in information accuracy because demand preservation, value exploitation, and convergence incentives dominate in different regions. Welfare analysis shows that live-channel entry always increases consumer surplus but may reduce social welfare when information disclosure is strong. Finally, channel-based differentiated pricing can improve both retailer profit and consumer surplus by separating prices across informed and uninformed consumers. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Financial leverage in business sector profitability: A review
abstract: This study examines the relationship between financial leverage and corporate profitability in a context of heightened economic uncertainty following the COVID-19 pandemic, a period during which organizations have been compelled to redefine their financing strategies in order to preserve sustainability and financial performance. The primary objective was to systematically analyze recent empirical evidence on the impact of financial leverage on corporate profitability. To this end, a systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using the Scopus database. The search strategy incorporated terms related to financial leverage, financing, profitability, and firms, while the 2020–2025 period and the explicit inclusion of key topic-related concepts were established as the main eligibility criteria. From an initial total of 7,587 identified records, a rigorous screening process was carried out based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the final selection of 36 articles for qualitative analysis. The study employed synthesis matrices, bibliometric analysis, and keyword co-occurrence networks, which made it possible to identify trends, predominant methodological approaches, and the main findings. The results indicate that companies rely on a combination of internal and external financing sources, including bank credit, bond issuance, informal financing, and fintech tools. In general, financial leverage has a positive effect on indicators such as ROA, ROE, and ROI, provided that adequate financial planning, cost control, and efficient debt management are in place. However, in SMEs or firms with high levels of indebtedness and limited managerial capacity, the impact may be negative or statistically insignificant. It is concluded that financial leverage constitutes a strategic tool for enhancing profitability, provided that it is managed prudently and within a comprehensive financial risk management framework. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Augmented reality as a digital scaffold for slow travel: The roles of cultural competence and tourist engagement at a heritage site
abstract: Heritage sites are designed to foster in-depth cultural experiences for tourists at destinations and are well suited for promoting slow travel. However, cultural differences and tourist’ limited awareness often hinder its practice. While augmented reality (AR) is typically used to provide immediate destination information, its potential to build cultural competence and influence slow travel intentions has not been examined. Grounded in zone of proximal development theory, this study reveals that the perceived enjoyment of AR is positively associated with cultural competence, but only for highly engaged users. For less engaged users, personal innovativeness moderates the relationship between perceived advantage and cultural competence. Across both groups, cultural competence strengthens both empathy and slow travel intentions. These findings offer guidance for implementing slow travel initiatives at cultural heritage sites. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: High-Spatiotemporal and Multimodal Soft Tactile Interface with Layered Architecture for Simultaneous Structural and Thermal Perception
abstract: Advanced robotic systems require tactile perception to interact reliably with objects in environments where visual information is limited by occlusion, illumination variations, and focusing issues. However, conventional tactile sensors are limited to single-stimulus recognition and face fundamental challenges in scalability and functionality, as miniaturizing sensor pixels reduces baseline signal levels and degrades the SNR. This study presents a high-spatiotemporal and multimodal soft tactile interface for simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles, fabricated through a layered architecture enabled by additive manufacturing. The proposed interface incorporates a 3D-stacked capacitive pressure sensor that combines buried interdigitated capacitors and a parallel-plate capacitor, and a reduced graphene oxide based temperature sensor within the same pixel area. The 3D-stacked electrode architecture enhances baseline capacitance within a miniaturized pixel footprint, and a via-free, interlayered interconnection scheme resolves wiring complexity in the temperature sensor array. Each sensing layer operates through independent transduction mechanisms, enabling the simultaneous perception of structural and thermal profiles with minimal cross-interference. The fabricated multimodal array can spatially resolve both contact geometry and localized thermal distributions with high-spatiotemporal resolution. Furthermore, by applying a tactile scanning strategy in robotic perception, the platform successfully identifies geometric features and surface thermal profiles of target objects even under vision-limited conditions. This study provides a scalable and robust foundation for multimodal tactile perception in advanced robotic manipulation and human–robot interaction. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: The Integration of Islamic Religious Values in the Ritual Mantras of Pinisi Boat-Making as Instructional Material for Literature Learning in Islamic Schools
abstract: This study aims to integrate Islamic religiosity values embedded in the ritual mantras of Pinisi boat-making into literary learning materials for madrasah education. Employing a mixed-methods approach with an exploratory sequential design, the research began with qualitative data collected through interviews with five pammaca (ritual specialists) and document analysis. This phase was followed by a quantitative survey involving five teachers and ten students in Bulukumba, Indonesia. The findings reveal that Islamic values are reflected in several ritual stages, including annakbang kalabiseang, annattak kalabiesang, apasilli, and ammocci, encompassing dimensions of faith, knowledge, worship, spiritual experience, and practical application. Both teachers and students expressed strong support for integrating these values into literary learning materials, as it enriches instructional content, strengthens character education, and contributes to the preservation of local culture. Furthermore, the study highlights the practical relevance of this integration for curriculum development and culturally responsive teaching strategies. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. This study investigates whether, and to what extent, VR-based experiential learning is associated with students' communication competence and managerial self-efficacy, drawing on Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Using a cross-sectional survey design complemented by platform-generated usage logs, we analyzed survey and behavioral data from 412 postgraduate and undergraduate management students across three program types at a research-intensive business school. Ordinary least squares regression served as the primary analysis, supplemented by instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), generalized method of moments (GMM), and propensity score matching to address potential endogeneity and selection bias. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that experiential learning depth and reflective practice partially mediate the associations between VR intensity parameters and both outcomes. Heterogeneity analyses revealed stronger associations among executive-education participants and where instructor facilitation quality was high. Findings were robust to alternative specifications and sample-trimming procedures. The study contributes a multi-method framework for integrating immersive technology into business-school curricula and offers actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional administrators, and educational-technology policymakers. © 2026

title: Is green product trade a pathway to better air quality in China?
abstract: This study evaluates whether green product trade can serve as an effective pathway to improving air quality in China. Using panel data for 28 provinces from 2010 to 2021, we are the first to jointly examine the impacts of green trade on six major air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NOx, and CO2) while simultaneously identifying both its temporal dynamics and spatial spillover effects within a unified empirical framework. We construct an integrated green-product trade database combining the APEC, OECD, and World Bank classifications and employ System GMM and the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to address spatial-temporal dependence. The results show that a 1% increase in green trade reduces PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations by approximately 1.1%. Moreover, green imports in neighboring provinces generate strong spatial spillovers, lowering local PM2.5, PM10, CO, and SO2 emissions by about 5%. We also find that green imports exert significantly stronger pollution-reduction effects than green exports, suggesting an import-driven technology-upgrade mechanism typical of developing economies. These findings provide robust evidence that green trade contributes to China's environmental improvements and offer important policy insights for emerging economies seeking to leverage green globalization for sustainable, lower-emission development. title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Using high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson models and a panel of 154,561 events in Houston, Texas, we estimate reduced-form associations across event attributes and offense types. The event-crime association is statistically detectable but economically modest. Formal comparisons reveal selective offense heterogeneity, with the Crimes Against Society coefficient exceeding the Violent Crime coefficient. Public opportunistic crime also shows stronger associations than private opportunistic and non-opportunistic crime, but not Other Crime. Event size exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the largest events showing stronger associations than those in all lower-attendance categories. Event type, day-type context, duration, and recurrence are not statistically distinguishable. Adjustment for contemporaneous foot traffic attenuates the event coefficient. The findings suggest proportionate, targeted situational prevention rather than generalized security escalation in urban destination safety planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chain performance, ripple effects, and viability
abstract: We simulate impacts of a global energy crisis on supply chains (SCs). First, we articulate the specific features that frame a global energy crisis as a unique type of SC large-scale systemic shocks characterized by a long-term disruption existence, disruption propagations (i.e., the ripple effect), a combination of immediate and delayed effects, cross-industry ripple effects, and mutual interrelations of SC and economic impacts. Second, we demonstrate how simulation-based methodology can be used to examine and predict the impacts of global energy crises on SC performance using the example of the Strait of Hormuz blockage and anyLogistix software. The major observation from the simulation experiments is that global energy crisis impacts resemble the COVID-19 pandemic patterns and ripple effects in 2020–2022 with reduced logistics capacities, delivery delays, and production shutdowns, supplemented by inflation effects observed in tariff turbulences in 2025. Other important factors influencing the shock impacts and propagation mechanisms are the duration of the energy crisis and SC viability. We observe that viable SCs with greater variety in production, supply, logistics, and energy structures are better able to absorb shocks. The outcomes of this research can be used by decision-makers to predict the operational and long-term impacts of global energy crises on SCs and to develop viability strategies. Our models are readily available to be used in practice for SC stress testing. They offer recommendations on proactively building adaptability and reconfiguring in response to disruptions to survive in a world without a reliable energy supply, incorporating large-scale systemic shocks into operational models. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Energy security risks and democratic vulnerability in the European Union
abstract: Over the past decade, growing vulnerabilities in the global energy system have affected both economic stability and the quality of democratic governance. The COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine war have intensified energy security risks, imposing new pressures on democratic processes and public accountability. Structural imbalances in energy markets, particularly within the European Union (EU), have necessitated the redefinition of energy policies and the reduction of external dependency. This study empirically investigates the impact of energy security risk on democratic governance using data from 25 EU countries for the period 2008–2023. The Voice and Accountability indicator from the World Bank’s World Governance Indicators serves as the measure of democratic governance, while dynamic interrelationships are analyzed through a Panel Vector Autoregression model estimated via the generalized method of moments (Panel GMM-VAR). The findings indicate that energy security risk has predictive precedence over democratic accountability. Granger causality analysis shows a unidirectional relationship running from energy security risk to Voice and Accountability, with no significant reverse effect. The cross-sectional association between the two is negative, although the dynamic responses are modest in magnitude and conditional on the identification ordering. At the policy level, energy supply diversification and resilience-building measures should be prioritised in efforts to protect democratic stability. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Assessing the viability of urban rooftop photovoltaic systems under new regulatory frameworks in Brazil via an evolutionary real options approach
abstract: The transition towards decentralized and sustainable urban energy systems requires robust decision-making frameworks that account for policy changes, market uncertainties, and investment flexibility. This study applies an Evolutionary Real Options Approach (EROA) to evaluate the economic viability of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems in Brazil under the New Mark of Distributed Generation (NMDG), a regulatory change that alters incentives for net metering. By incorporating stochastic volatility models, such as the Heston model and Geometric Brownian motion (GBM) with jumps, this work quantifies the impact of regulatory changes on investment timing and system sizing decisions. Results indicate a significant reduction in financial returns and a delay in investment decisions under the new regulation. The introduction of the new regulation has led to reductions in returns of approximately 18% and 23% for the Heston and GBM with jumps models, respectively. In terms of decision sequences, the Heston model presents increased opportunities for phased investment due to its greater flexibility. On the other hand, the GBM with jumps model encourages immediate investment in a complete solar system. The new regulation results in a delay of 6 to 12 months at entry points, regardless of the chosen model. These findings contribute to the understanding of urban energy transitions, policy impacts on decentralized generation, and investment dynamics in sustainable urban infrastructure. © 2026 The Authors

title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. The analysis identified four major constraints to conventional volcanic geothermal development: high exploration risk and capital expenditure (CAPEX), land-use conflicts with protected forests, electricity tariff policies linked to coal-based generation costs, and persistent social resistance (NIMBY/Not in My Backyard syndrome). The findings indicated that diversifying geothermal development toward non-volcanic back-arc sedimentary basins, particularly through co-production with mature Oil and Gas (O&G) fields, provided a practical pathway to reduce exploration risk, lower infrastructure costs, minimize permitting conflicts and social resistance, and improve project economics. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. title: Career plateau and multifaceted turnover pathways in the airline industry: Evidence from full-service and low-cost carrier cabin crew
abstract: This study examines how career plateau influences stress, burnout, and multifaceted turnover intentions among airline cabin crew members by comparing full-service carriers (FSCs) and low-cost carriers (LCCs). Career plateau was categorized into hierarchical and job content career plateaus, and their psychological and behavioral impacts were assessed. Data were collected through a survey of 382 Korean cabin crew members with at least three years of experience and in-depth interviews with 14 participants. Quantitative results showed that a job content career plateau significantly heightened stress, leading to burnout. LCC crew members reported stronger turnover intentions, whereas burnout among FSC crew members did not necessarily translate into turnover intentions, suggesting that its effects may be constrained by organizational and labor market conditions. Qualitative findings revealed coping strategies such as goal adjustment and highlighted carrier-specific interpretations of turnover. Social support moderated the burnout–turnover link, buffering negative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Polar-Twisted Electron-Transport Layer Simultaneously Breaks Efficiency-Flexibility-Cost Limits in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Perylene diimide (PDI)-based electron-transport layers (ETLs) are fundamental in governing charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and the operational longevity of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet their molecular design still lacks transferable principles. Here we present a PDI-ETL molecular design framework that couples bay-position engineering with polar, bulky side-chain modulation to improve additive-free alcohol solubility, suppress over-crystallization, and mitigate oxidative degradation. With this framework, H75-DMA suppresses reactive-oxygen-driven chemical evolution and interfacial trap accumulation, thereby stabilizing interfacial energetics and electron transport. Binary OSCs based on H75-DMA achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) above 20% and exhibit improved mechanical toughness and bending durability in flexible devices. Its smooth, high-surface-energy interface also induces continuous growth of ultrathin metal cathodes, leading to increased light-utilization efficiency in flexible semitransparent OSCs. In addition, H75-DMA enables cathode substitution from Ag to Cu while retaining about 97% of the PCE of the Ag-based devices, thereby improving cost-effectiveness at the device level. title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Beyond green claims: a social-ecological assessment of cruise tourism sustainability
abstract: Cruise tourism sustainability discourse prioritises vessel level innovation, marginalising destination level social ecological impacts. To address this, we develop a structured literature based conceptual model of cruise mobility as a coupled global and local social ecological system. Supported by AI assisted extraction and synthesis of multidisciplinary literature, this paper constructs a governance-oriented framework. The analysis identifies two interacting dynamics: a reinforcing expansion loop where revenues stimulate infrastructure and deepen dependency, and a degrading acceptance loop where cumulative stress erodes tolerance. Presented as heuristic formalisation devices, these loops help explain why vessel efficiency alone cannot prevent destination level degradation. We translate these findings into a five-pillar governance framework featuring capacity thresholds, social monitoring, economic diversification, power rebalancing, and multi-level coordination. This shifts attention from ship focused compliance towards destination embedded sustainability governance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Charge-Carrier Behavior and Molecular Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
abstract: Molecular interface engineering has become increasingly important for improving the efficiency and stability of perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Although highly emissive perovskite materials have advanced rapidly, their translation into high-performance devices remains limited by interfacial losses, unbalanced charge injection, and instability under electrical operation. In this review, we first discuss charge-carrier behavior in perovskite materials and devices, with emphasis on radiative and non-radiative recombination, carrier accumulation under injection, and the device-level consequences of interfacial constraints. We then examine the development of interfacial molecular strategies in PeLEDs, including self-assembled monolayers and related interfacial molecules, and summarize how such molecular layers influence charge injection, interfacial recombination, local electronic structure, and film formation at both charge-injection interfaces. On this basis, we further consider the implications of these interfacial effects for molecular regulation in light-emitting devices, with particular attention to electronic regulation under bias, chemically persistent passivation, and structural compatibility with emissive-layer formation. By connecting carrier physics, interfacial function, and molecular regulation, this review aims to provide a clearer framework for understanding and developing molecular interfacial strategies for high-performance PeLEDs. title: Redox-Active Ligand-Stabilized Lithium Iron Phosphate Nanoparticles for High-Performance Lithium-Ion Battery Cathode with High Capacities and Long-Term Stability
abstract: Developing cathodes that simultaneously deliver high capacity, superior rate capability, and long-term cycling stability remains a major challenge in lithium-ion batteries. Here, we report a high-performance textile cathode constructed via interfacial interaction-mediated assembly of high-energy porphyrin (PP) ligand-stabilized LiFePO4 nanoparticles (LFP NPs). For this, 19 nm LFP NPs with olivine-type intercalation mechanism were covalently integrated with amine-functionalized PP to enable multi-electron redox activity, followed by encapsulation with multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) multilayers. Subsequent thermal annealing transformed the MWCNT layers into a covalently cross-linked conductive network. As a result, the textile cathode delivers an unprecedented specific capacity of ~260 mAh g−1 at ~0.1 C, excellent rate capability, and retains over 93% of its initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 1 C with nearly 100% Coulombic efficiency. This work highlights interfacial interaction-mediated ligand assembly as a powerful strategy for next-generation high-capacity and durable cathodes. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Ethical reasoning and responsible use of ChatGPT in higher education: Integrating technology acceptance and moral cognition
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has raised important questions about how students evaluate the ethical implications of AI-assisted academic practices and whether those evaluations are linked to intentions to use these tools responsibly. While previous research has largely focused on technology adoption and acceptance, it has paid less attention to the relationship between ethical reasoning and intentions to use these tools responsibly. This study develops and tests an integrated framework that combines the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and moral cognition theory to examine how technology perceptions and academic and cognitive factors relate to students’ ethical reasoning and intentions to use ChatGPT responsibly. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design among business and management students in Oman and analysed the data using structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, academic pressure, and moral disengagement are positively associated with ethical reasoning, whereas perceived usefulness is not significantly associated with ethical reasoning. Ethical reasoning is positively associated with behavioural intention to use ChatGPT responsibly. In contrast, ChatGPT usage does not significantly moderate the relationship between academic pressure and ethical reasoning. These findings suggest that students’ responsible-use intentions are associated with their ethical evaluations of ChatGPT-assisted academic practices, while conventional technology acceptance perceptions and usage frequency alone offer a more limited explanation of ethical reasoning. The study contributes to emerging research on responsible generative AI use by extending TAM beyond conventional adoption outcomes and integrating it with a moral cognition perspective. It highlights the relationship between ethical reasoning and responsible-use intentions while distinguishing ethical evaluation from technology acceptance and usage frequency. The findings also provide context-specific evidence from Omani higher education, while recognising the limitations of the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and a context-specific sample. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Supporting initial teacher education student creativity and critical thinking using active constraints in assessment: A scoping review
abstract: Assessment design plays a critical role in shaping student learning in higher education, particularly in disciplines where creativity is both a learning outcome and a pedagogical approach. In Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this role is intensified, as assessment tasks often function as the primary site of learning for time-poor students and simultaneously model pedagogical practice for future teachers. While constraints are frequently embedded within assessment tasks, their role in supporting creativity remains under-theorised and inconsistently articulated in the literature. This scoping review examines how constraints are used within assessment tasks that aim to foster creativity and/or critical thinking in social sciences, humanities, education and creative arts courses in higher education in order to consider implications for enhancing creativity through assessment tasks in ITE. Using a scoping review framework, 28 empirical studies published since 2000 were identified and analysed thematically. Six key themes emerged: the role of prior experience, constraints as catalysts for creativity, task design and flexibility, rubrics and scaffolding as support structures, the domain-specificity of creativity, and the presence of “invisible architectures” in task design. Findings indicate that constraints function as powerful pedagogical mechanisms when they are intentionally designed, aligned with disciplinary practices, and calibrated to student readiness. However, many studies prioritise creative outcomes without sufficiently detailing the task conditions that shape them. title: Artificial intelligence and generative AI in entrepreneurship education: A systematic review of competency development, entrepreneurial intention, and the sustainability disconnect
abstract: Entrepreneurship education increasingly deploys artificial intelligence (AI), yet claims that it builds entrepreneurial competence and advances sustainability rest on an unexamined evidence base. This review asks what that evidence supports, and what it does not. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and Web of Science searches yielded 21 empirical studies with approximately 7800 unique participants across 14 countries. Studies were stratified as generative, broader or analytical AI, quality was appraised item by item with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and every conclusion was tested by sensitivity analysis. CIMO logic specified the question; TCM-ADO organised the synthesis. AI was positively associated with entrepreneurial intention in every study that measured it, but its magnitude cannot be established: the largest estimates come from the lowest-quality studies, and few report uncertainty estimates. Competency development, the assumed mechanism, rests almost entirely on non-generative AI studies and is untested for generative systems. Self-efficacy operates as a boundary condition, raising an equity concern no study measures. Nominal relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals is widespread, yet none measured a sustainability outcome or named an environmental goal. It supplies a stratified, quality-weighted evidence base and shows that closing the sustainability gap requires theory and instruments, not more intention surveys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026

title: Investigating the interplay between public art, urban design, and national identity: Case of the UAE
abstract: Public art and culturally responsive urban environment play a crucial role in shaping national identity, particularly in culturally diverse and rapidly evolving societies like the UAE. This study examines how different forms of public art, their integration into urban spaces, and digital platforms influence perceptions of national identity. Grounded in Social Identity Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and Public Space Theory, it employs structural equation modeling (SEM) and thematic analysis using data from 543 respondents across UAE emirates. The SEM model explains 40.3% of the variance in Perceived National Identity (PNI), emphasizing the significant role of public art and digital platforms in cultural engagement. Mediation analysis highlights the importance of interactive experiences in strengthening cultural connections, while thematic analysis identifies cultural integration, community involvement, and sustainability as key themes. Findings suggest that combining traditional Emirati artistic elements with modern digital technologies enhances inclusivity and engagement. However, the limited direct impact of urban design on national identity highlights the need for culturally relevant elements to maximize its effectiveness. By integrating quantitative and qualitative insights, this study offers clear implications for policy and practice by recommending participatory planning, integration of heritage-based design elements and use of digital platforms to enhance cultural visibility and engagement. It provides a practical framework for urban planners, cultural policymakers, and designers to develop inclusive public spaces that reinforce national identity in the UAE. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective
abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Existing research has revealed the proximate motives of such behavior centered on identity construction, but the ultimate motives remain underexplored. Using a qualitative research design, this study explores motivations in Chinese costume travel photography by applying three interpretive lenses derived from evolutionary psychology, namely performative affiliation, temporary status, and scripted exploration. The findings indicate that participants' motivations are satisfied in Chinese costume travel photography as follows: temporary immersion and affiliation are gained from symbolic imitation and contextual co-performance; contextualized status enhancement is acquired by enacting ideal identities and collecting digital validation; and novelty seeking is met through experiences grounded in symbolic imagination and pre-arranged scripts. This study provides insights into the ultimate drivers of tourists’ surface motivations and the possible satisfaction mechanisms of deep evolutionary motives in Chinese costume travel photography. It also offers practical insights for tourism experience design and marketing by focusing on the satisfaction of deep motives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Bolstered Interfacial Field Chemistry for Deep Fast-Charging Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
abstract: Deep fast-charging capability has become the core pursuit for practical applications of aqueous zinc metal batteries, yet it is critically impeded by unfavorable interfacial field evolution at the electrode/electrolyte interface under high-current–density conditions. The coexistence of sluggish Zn2+ desolvation, competitive H2O reduction corrosion, uneven electric field, and concentration field collectively leads to poor rate performance. To tackle these issues, a bolstered interfacial field chemistry strategy was developed via sulfosuccinic acid to precisely regulate the physicochemical and electrochemical properties within the inner Helmholtz plane. The tuned interfacial field comprises a homogeneous distribution of interfacial ions and electric fields, promoting fast desolvation and interfacial electron transfer. Consequently, the modified Zn||Cu asymmetric cells deliver an outstanding average Coulombic efficiency of 99.48% over 1600 cycles at 2 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, the modified Zn||Zn symmetric cells demonstrate exceptional stability under challenging conditions of 5 mA cm−2, 2 mAh cm−2 (over 1600 h), and 10 mA cm−2, 10 mAh cm−2 (over 675 h, depth of discharge = 17.08%). Impressively, a substantial cumulative capacity of 3500 mAh cm−2 is attained at 10 mAh cm−2 and a 56.93% Zn utilization rate. Besides, the enhanced Zn (10 µm) ||I2 (10.87 mg cm−2) full cell sustains over 1490 cycles at 1 A g−1 with 77.13% capacity retention and a harsh N/P ratio of 2.31. Remarkably, the Zn (10 µm) ||I2 pouch cell achieves over 680 cycles with an ultralow N/P ratio of 2.04. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Advanced optimization problems and solution methods for renewable energy integration - A bibliometric review
abstract: The worldwide shift to sustainable energy supply has led to extensive incorporation of renewable energy sources into modern power systems incorporating specifically with wind-turbine and solar-photovoltaic systems. The stochastic and intermittent nature of such renewable energy sources, however, poses significant challenges in their operation and planning, especially regarding optimization and system coordination. This paper provides a detailed overview of various advanced optimization problems and solution methods for the integration of renewable energy in today's power systems. The study divides important optimization problems into three categories: active and reactive power management, uncertainty modelling and real-time stochastic operation of power systems. Coordination of active and reactive power resources is a critical issue that needs to be addressed to ensure voltage stability and reliability of the grid with high penetrations of renewables. The review also explores the concept of stochastic energy and reactive power markets, which entails optimizing ancillary services like voltage support and reactive power dispatch together, considering interactions between transmission system operators and distribution system operators. Moreover, the traditional optimization techniques such as linear programming, nonlinear programming and mixed-integer programming are compared with the new ones such as the intelligent and hybrid techniques. The current review is a structured reference which combines technical analysis with bibliometric analysis and indicates future research directions to develop resilient, intelligent and market-oriented power system optimization frameworks. © 2026 The Authors. title: From fragmentation to integration: Rethinking the measurement of responsible management education
abstract: Responsible Management Education (RME) has become a central agenda within business schools, as institutions seek to prepare graduates capable of addressing complex sustainability and societal challenges. Despite its growing prominence, approaches to evaluating RME remain fragmented, with studies measuring diverse educational, institutional and societal outcomes using inconsistent conceptualisations and indicators. This study systematically reviews the contemporary literature to examine how RME is currently measured and develop a more coherent conceptual framework for evaluation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review of 62 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 using the Scopus database—an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop thematic synthesis identified and consolidated 328 measurement-related concepts. The synthesis identified five complementary measurement domains: implementation, learning, behaviour, performance and impact, alongside five stakeholder groups: students, educators, institutions, industry and society. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Integrated Responsible Management Education Measurement Framework (IRMEF) as a multidimensional conceptual evaluation architecture that organises these domains and stakeholder perspectives. Rather than representing an empirically validated measurement model, the IRMEF provides a common conceptual vocabulary for organising existing approaches and guiding future evaluation and empirical validation. It provides a foundation for greater theoretical coherence and methodological consistency while supporting business schools, accreditation bodies, and policymakers seeking more balanced, multidimensional, and contextually appropriate approaches to RME evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Negotiating the contested: A framework for studying social issue negotiations
abstract: Negotiation research has yielded useful insights on how to manage economic and business interactions by highlighting the importance of information sharing, trade-offs, and integrative solutions in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. However, these approaches inadequately explain why negotiations over social issues such as immigration reform and climate change can remain deadlocked despite sustained efforts to reach agreement. Drawing upon recent research, we introduce an organizing framework that identifies three common features of such negotiations: moralization, identity threat, and public contestation. Moralization frames issues as matters of right and wrong, reducing willingness to compromise; identity concerns transform policy disagreements into threats to group membership and self-concept; and public scrutiny increases reputational risks and constrains flexibility. Together, these dynamics hinder engagement, value creation, and the quality of agreements. We review emerging interventions—including moral reframing, perspective sharing, high-quality listening, informal dialogue, and third-party mediation—that may mitigate these barriers. We conclude by highlighting the need for research examining how moral, identity, and public pressures interact across levels of analysis to shape social issue negotiation processes and outcomes. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Advancing family bonding: A conditional framework from immersion to communitas
abstract: A gap still exists between mobile social media-embedded modern family tourism and family relationship improvement. From a communitas perspective, this study proposes a conditional immersion-communitas relationship improvement framework to address this gap. Evidence from multi-wave surveys, an eye-tracking experiment, focus group interviews, and multiple field experiments shows that: (1) social media notification management is a key precondition for relationship improvement; compared with notification-off, visual, or auditory models, haptic notifications better sustain relationship improvement through the full chain mediation of immersion and communitas; (2) happiness experience type (eudaimonia vs. hedonia) moderates the immersion maintenance mechanism, with hedonia family members relying more on notification management; (3) family structure (intragenerational vs. intergenerational) also moderates the process: the positive effect of communitas on family relationship improvement is stronger in intergenerational families than in intragenerational ones. This study advances understanding of modern family tourism and offers practical implications for both individual management and external intervention. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

abstract: In mining ‘remoteness’ was once a measure of isolation from other activities and communities. title: E-recruitment adoption and candidate's intention to apply: The mediating role of person-organization fit and the moderating role of digital literacy
abstract: E-recruitment is increasingly recognized as a strategic digital tool that enables organizations to attract and communicate with potential candidates more efficiently. As organizations continue to shift from traditional recruitment methods to internet-based platforms, understanding how job seekers respond to these systems has become increasingly important, particularly among Generation Z applicants who are highly exposed to digital technologies. However, despite the widespread adoption of e-recruitment, many candidates still fail to complete online job applications. Prior research has mainly emphasized the organizational benefits of e-recruitment, while limited attention has been given to the psychological and individual mechanisms through which e-recruitment adoption shapes candidates’ intention to apply (ITA). This study aims to examine the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) of e-recruitment on ITA among Vietnamese final-year students and recent graduates. It also investigates the mediating role of person–organization fit (POF) and the moderating role of digital literacy (DL). Adopting a quantitative approach, the study used convenience sampling and collected survey data from 368 valid respondents in Vietnam through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that PU and PEOU positively influence both POF and ITA. POF significantly enhances ITA and mediates the relationships between e-recruitment adoption and application intention. In addition, DL significantly strengthens the effects of PU and PEOU on both POF and ITA. These findings highlight the importance of designing informative and user-friendly e-recruitment systems while recognizing DL as a critical condition influencing applicant responses in digital recruitment contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: From personality to prestige: A dual-method analysis of masstige consumption using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
abstract: “Masstige”, a new trend in marketing, represents a hybrid concept that stands for ‘prestige or luxury for the masses’. With the growing number of high-end middle class, there is a tendency among the people to have a premium product which is in between exclusive luxury and midrange products, accompanying with high quality and exclusivity at a reasonable price. However, research is limited about how internal psychological factors and external motivational factors affect consumer attitude and consumption of masstige brands. Hence, this study aims – to explore the status of masstige among the popular smartphone brands in Bangladesh using MMI (Masstige Mean Index), and to investigate the influence of internal (personality traits) and external (perceived product quality and perceived prestige value) factors on consumer attitude and consumption behavior of masstige brands. Besides, this study examines the moderating effect of materialism in the association between consumer attitude and masstige consumption. In total, 418 responses were gathered in study 1 to identify the masstige status of smartphone brands in Bangladesh and 341 responses were collected in study 2 from the same country utilizing a structured instrument and analyzed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA. The findings of study 1 represent that iPhone is appeared as masstige category; whereas, the outcomes of study 2 indicate that except neuroticism, all personality traits along with product quality and prestige value have positive impact on attitude towards masstige brands, which in turn affects the masstige consumption. Moreover, materialism strengthens the influence of consumers' attitude towards masstige consumption. The fsQCA results identified eight different configurations that successfully lead to masstige consumption. Additionally, the analysis highlighted five essential elements of perceived prestige value, conscientiousness, extraversion, openness, and attitude as necessary for achieving high levels of masstige consumption. In the milieu of masstige literature, this study strengthens the theory of masstige consumption by integrating the theory of personality traits. This study provides practical guidance for the marketers of masstige brands to uphold consumers' attitude and accelerate their masstige consumptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Traditional or simplified Chinese? Exploring the use of linguistic variants in tourism linguistic landscape
abstract: By employing a two-phase mixed-method research design (i.e. survey and interviews), this study investigates residents' and tourists' perceptions of the effectiveness of language variants of Chinese characters in public signage within Macao's tourism landscape. The findings reveal that while simplified Chinese may be favored for its practicality, traditional Chinese retains significant cultural and identity values among residents and enhances the travel experiences by signally authenticity. Additionally, the research highlights perceived cultural erosion among the local community and concerns over prioritizing tourists' needs at the expense of local identity. This study extends linguistic landscape scholarship by illustrating how script variants within a shared language carry distinct practical and symbolic meanings for different stakeholders. Finally, this research proposes an exploratory needs–affect–attachment framework and a theoretically informed model of tourism power relations to conceptualize these dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Uncovering creative metacognition patterns in TVET innovation education: insight from an epistemic network analysis of students’ self-reflective assessments
abstract: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) increasingly position creativity as a teachable competence in innovation and entrepreneurship education, yet little is known about how Creative Metacognition (CMC) elements are structurally interconnected and activated to facilitate creativity in TVET learners. To address this gap, this study provides an exploratory epistemic network analysis on structural mapping of CMC in TVET innovation and entrepreneurship course. Forty TVET learners completed a three-stage authentic Creative Problem-Solving task focused on venture design for a remote region. Their self-reflective assessments were segmented into 1,506 theory-driven semantic fragments and coded into Creative Strengths (CS), Creative Restrictions (CR), and Creative Contextual Knowledge (CK). Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was employed to model the co-activation patterns and relational intensity among CMC elements. Results show that students with high scores exhibited a stronger connection between CS and CK, suggesting that contextual knowledge was framed as creative affordances. title: Strategies of Designing High-Efficiency Electrolyte Additives for Aqueous Magnesium Batteries: A Review
abstract: With the development of next-generation energy storage systems focusing on green, safe, and sustainable devices, aqueous magnesium (Mg)–air batteries have emerged as promising candidates owing to the intrinsic merits of the Mg metal anode, including low cost, large volumetric capacity, a highly negative electrode potential, and excellent safety. However, the high self-discharge rate and formed discharge products substantially impair the practical discharge performance of Mg anodes with poor anode utilization efficiency and low cell voltage. While anode alloying and electrolyte additive strategies can help mitigate this issue, designing highly efficient electrolyte additives that are compatible with the established anode remains a challenge. This review summarizes recent progress toward understanding the role of electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries, provides insights into the discharge mechanism of Mg-based anode materials in different types of additive-containing electrolytes, and offers strategies for designing high-efficiency mixtures of electrolyte additives. Moreover, a highly promising direction of AI-supported and robotic workflows for the future fast design of advanced electrolyte additives for aqueous Mg batteries is discussed. title: Extruded cornmeal improves freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough by restricting water mobility
abstract: In frozen cereal-based foods, water is not only a structural plasticizer but also a destructive phase-change medium. Temperature fluctuations during frozen storage promote water migration and ice recrystallization, which weaken the gluten-starch matrix and lead to cracking, water loss, and textural deterioration. Existing strategies mainly rely on gluten reinforcement or hydrocolloid addition, whereas starch-rich non-gluten ingredients are often regarded as formulation diluents because they disrupt dough network formation. This study investigated whether extrusion can convert cornmeal into a functional water-state regulator that improves the freeze-thaw stability of wheat dough. Wheat flour (CK), wheat flour containing 15% native cornmeal (NC-15) and wheat flour containing 15% extruded cornmeal (ECM-15) were compared. ECM-15 significantly reduced freezable water content (from 71.85% in CK to 51.63%, a reduction of 28.14%) and melting enthalpy, and showed the lowest water loss throughout five freeze-thaw cycles. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) analysis revealed restricted water mobility in ECM-containing dough, indicating that extrusion-modified starch immobilized water fractions that would otherwise contribute to freezing and migration. Consistently, ECM-15 exhibited higher water-holding capacity, swelling power and farinograph water absorption, together with lower pasting viscosity and setback. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and Raman analyses indicated that these effects arose from extrusion-induced amorphization and short-range disordering of starch, rather than simple cornmeal addition. Notably, this improvement was achieved despite reduced dough mixing stability, indicating that extrusion-induced water-state regulation offers a label-friendly strategy for frozen dough improvement, distinct from conventional gluten reinforcement. More broadly, physically modified cereal ingredients can be designed as functional phase-state regulators in frozen staple foods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
abstract: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets. © 2026

title: A Buried Sulfonate Molecular Bridge for Synchronous Charge Transport and Defect Passivation in High-Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: The quality of the buried interface between the self-assembled molecules (SAM) and the perovskite layer directly governs the processes of charge carrier transport and non-radiative recombination, which ultimately dictates the efficiency and stability of the inverted perovskite solar cells. However, the simultaneous mitigation of poor SAM layer adhesion and perovskite substrate interface defects remains a significant challenge. Herein, low-cost and readily available 2‑formylbenzenesulfonic acid sodium salt (2‑FAS) is employed as a bifunctional interlayer to molecularly bridge the SAM and perovskite. The benzene ring of 2‑FAS interacts via π–π stacking with the SAM, strengthening adhesion and promoting hole transfer, while its sulfonate group (-SO3−) coordinates with Pb2+ to regulate crystallization and passivate surface defects. As a result, the 2-FAS-modified devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.21%, with a significant fill factor of 86.15%. Furthermore, Na+ from 2‑FAS occupies A‑site vacancies in the perovskite lattice, which effectively suppresses ion migration and phase transition, thereby enhancing structural integrity. Benefiting from these combined effects, unencapsulated devices retain over 90% of their initial PCE after 4500 h of storage in a nitrogen atmosphere, demonstrating exceptional long-term stability. title: Driving police engagement through talent management: Evidence from Abu Dhabi
abstract: This study examines the relationship between talent management practices and employee engagement, as well as the moderating role of business analytics and the subsequent impact on employee performance within the Abu Dhabi Police. Specifically, the research explores how talent attraction, retention, learning and development, and career management influence employee engagement, which in turn affects job performance. Drawing on social exchange theory, dynamic capability theory, and Aon Hewitt's employee engagement model, a quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to senior officers across various departments. A total of 383 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.3.9. The findings reveal that all four dimensions of talent management (talent attraction, talent retention, learning and development, and career management) have significant positive effects on employee engagement. Furthermore, employee engagement strongly and significantly influences employee performance, underscoring its pivotal role in organizational effectiveness. The results of the moderation analysis indicate that business analytics significantly strengthens the relationships between talent attraction, learning and development, and career management and employee engagement, with learning and development and talent attraction showing the strongest moderating effects, whereas the moderating effect on talent retention is statistically insignificant. The model explains 53.8 of the variance in employee engagement, indicating satisfactory predictive power. These findings contribute to the literature by integrating business analytics into the talent management—engagement—performance nexus, particularly within a public sector policing context. Practically, the results highlight the strategic importance of leveraging data-driven and analytics-enabled HRM practices to personalize talent management interventions, enhance perceived fairness, and improve engagement outcomes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that while business analytics enhances most talent management dimensions, its influence is not uniform across all practices, particularly in the case of talent retention. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers and HR leaders seeking to build agile, high-performing, and engaged workforces in dynamic environments. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Enhancing DER hosting capacity of unbalanced low-voltage distribution networks with network exchangers: An Australian case study
abstract: The rapid growth and subsequent utilization of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly in low-voltage networks, is pushing distribution networks to the brink of their hosting capacity. Distribution network operators, especially in DER-rich countries such as Australia, are exploring novel technologies and effective strategies to enhance DER integration while maintaining network integrity, as an alternative to costly network upgrades. One such technology developed and introduced is the network exchanger (NEx), which aims to enhance hosting capacity by regulating voltage, mitigating current imbalance, and power factor correction at the distribution transformer. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of NEx, compared with on-load tap changers and distribution static synchronous compensators, through an extensive simulation study that models projected growth in photovoltaic and electric vehicle penetration as per the Integrated System Plan released by the Australian Energy Market Operator, using a large-scale, real-world distribution network comprising over 8000 buses, and located in Queensland, Australia. Simulation results indicate breaches in network integrity under business-as-usual conditions in both step-change and progressive-change scenarios. The performance of each technology is benchmarked across six low-voltage networks that exhibit higher levels of network violations and photovoltaic curtailment, with NEx resolving all voltage breaches and reducing transformer loading and photovoltaic curtailment by noticeable amounts, which can aid in delaying costly network augmentation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From diagnosis to explanation: An integrated framework for examining spatially heterogeneous associations between temporary industrial-land use and neighborhood gentrification
abstract: As Chinese megacities transition to post-industrialism, the socio-spatial consequences of temporary industrial land reuse—a pivotal urban renewal strategy—remain under-theorized. This study integrates Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR), Geodetector, and Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) to examine associations between four functional types of temporary use and a Standardized Gentrification Index (SGI) capturing changes in educational and floating-population composition across 134 Beijing subdistricts. The results reveal differentiated and context-dependent patterns. Technology-oriented use density exhibits a stable and spatially widespread positive association with SGI. Cultural-use area is positively associated with SGI across most subdistricts, whereas cultural-use density is predominantly negative. Production-service area is significant only in a limited set of locations, while consumer-service measures show no statistically significant local MGWR coefficients. Cultural and technology clustering recur as the principal correlates of coefficient heterogeneity, whereas production clustering, transport-accessibility growth, and housing-price change matter in specific relationships. These findings suggest a state-mediated, technology-oriented pathway of demographic upgrading and a more conditional cultural pathway. Methodologically, the framework moves from mapping spatial non-stationarity to interpreting its contextual correlates, providing evidence for differentiated urban-renewal governance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Embedding ESG, sustainability and ethics in accounting assessment: Bridging global standards and educational practice
abstract: The growing prominence of environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, sustainability, and ethical accountability is reshaping expectations of accounting and management graduates. While these competencies are increasingly embedded within global professional standards and competency frameworks, their translation into educational assessment remains underexplored. This study examines how ESG, sustainability, and ethics are embedded in documented assessment across global standards, professional competency frameworks, and Australian university accounting education. Using qualitative comparative document analysis, the study analyses the International Federation of Accountants’ International Education Standards, the competency frameworks of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and assessment documentation from 104 undergraduate accounting units across 26 Australian universities. The findings reveal partial and uneven alignment. Although sustainability and ethics are explicitly articulated within global and professional frameworks, they are frequently embedded implicitly within technically oriented assessment tasks rather than explicitly assessed as judgement-focused competencies. To explain this pattern, the study introduces the concept of differential assessability, which explains why some professional competencies are more readily translated into assessment than others despite comparable prominence within professional standards. By reframing ESG integration as an assessment design challenge, the study extends assessment theory and offers practical implications for responsible management and accounting education. © 2026

title: Designing ethical negotiation simulations for measurable metacognitive development: Boundary conditions in SCELM
abstract: Ethical negotiation simulations generate strong engagement but often fail to produce measurable metacognitive development in students. This boundary condition design study argues that the problem is structural: many simulation formats are misaligned with the consolidation phase through which disruption becomes learning. We evaluated two implementations of Structured Cross-Cultural Ethical Leadership through Multilateral Negotiations (SCELM): a multicultural rotating format (N = 84 responses; matched n = 26) and a bilateral intercultural format (N = 39; Battle 1 n = 30) across four high-institutional-distance dyads in this study. Paired t-tests and thematic analyses of 124 reflections (κ = 0.81) were conducted in parallel. The rotating format produced no significant within-person changes across any metacognitive index (all d ≤ 0.17). In contrast, the bilateral format generated greater baseline assumption disruption, as indicated by a significant Welch's t-test (p = .028) and marginally higher role tension (p = .063). Qualitative findings showed that perspective revision occurred primarily during structured intra-team consolidation rather than during negotiations, indicating that immediate post-battle surveys underestimate learning. We propose four educator-facing design principles and a dual-timepoint Assurance of Learning protocol, recommending that perspective-shift outcomes be assessed after structured consolidation rather than immediately following negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From influence to empowerment: Unpacking capacity building and social learning in virtual communities
abstract: This study explores how independent travel empowers women travel influencers and how meanings of empowerment are negotiated through interactions with their followers by examining the empowerment process at both individual and social levels. Drawing on capacity building theory and social cognitive theory, it investigates how travel experiences and digital content creation contribute to personal agency, skill development, and socially mediated expressions of empowerment. Using an interpretive paradigm and a netnographic approach, the study analyses the social media practices of 17 female travel influencers. Findings show that independent travel fosters self-efficacy, confidence, and the acquisition of skills and knowledge among influencers, while followers express inspiration, aspiration, identification, and negotiation of constraints in response to shared narratives of empowerment. The study underscores the dynamic interplay among digital influence, community engagement, and gendered empowerment, offering insights into virtual capacity building within contemporary travel cultures. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Generative AI communications and firm value: Evidence from digital innovation in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms using deep learning
abstract: This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. The final sample includes 177 firms from 2018 to 2024, comprising 68 firms with verified WeChat official accounts and 109 firms retained with zero-valued communication measures. From 105,429 archived posts, we develop a bilingual annotation scheme and supervised deep-learning classifiers to identify GenAI communication and distinguish implementation-salient disclosures from generic mentions. Our preferred measures are share-normalized, capturing both GenAI communication intensity and implementation emphasis relative to total posting activity. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Digital innovation partially mediates this relationship, while industry dynamism and complexity strengthen it, but munificence does not. The study contributes a tourism-specific measure of GenAI capability signaling and clarifies the value relevance of implementation-oriented communication in service-intensive digital contexts. © 2026 The Author.

title: Mental Health and Neurodivergence Disclosure Risk Mitigation in Private Higher Education Institutions: An Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to Support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: This study examines mental health and neurodivergence disclosure risk mitigation in private higher education institutions through an Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 297 academic and non-academic staff from selected private higher education institutions in Selangor, Malaysia. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Structural power asymmetry, institutional trust deficit, stigma anticipation, and absence of safeguards reduce psychological safety in disclosure. Perceived enforceability of protection moderates these relationships and strengthens the explanatory power of the model. This study highlights perceived enforceability of protection as a key risk mitigation mechanism for developing inclusive, psychologically safe, and sustainable higher education governance. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Atomic High-Spin Cobalt Unlocks Reversible Multi-Electron Transfer Chemistry for Superb Aqueous Zn-Mn Batteries
abstract: To settle inherent irreversible phase transition and motivate re-dissolution of deposited “dead” MnO2 without acid and redox mediator addition, we introduced atomic-dispersed Co atoms with high-spin state into layered MnO2, denoted as Co–MnO2, via an in situ topological phase transformation strategy, thereby unlocking reversible multi-electron transfer chemistry for superb Zn–Mn batteries. Specifically, atomic-distributed Co atoms within Co–MnO2 effectively modulate [MnO6] octahedral symmetry and reduce Co–O bond covalency along with enhanced lattice oxygen activity. Based on this, high-spin Co (t2g4eg2) greatly mitigates the Jahn–Teller distortion as well as promotes electrolytic MnO2 deposited onto the cathode surface completely converted from adsorbed Mn2+ for inhibited “Mn dendrites”, achieving reversible MnO2/Mn3+ and electrolytic MnO2/Mn2+ reactions with highly thermodynamical favorability. Benefiting from the “two-step, three-electron” mechanism triggered by high-spin Co, Zn//Co–MnO2 battery delivers an outstanding capacity of 658 mAh g–1 and ultra-long lifespan over 15,000 cycles. title: Workplace management of musculoskeletal and mental health risks: translating evidence into practice
abstract: There is a large body of research evidence identifying the biomechanical and psychosocial hazards that can affect work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and stress-related mental health problems (MHPs). The APHIRM Toolkit was developed to facilitate more effective translation of this evidence into workplace risk management practices. Using APHIRM survey data from three occupations in the healthcare sector, this project compared hazard ‘riskiness’ profiles: (a) at occupational versus local workgroup levels, and (b) using hazard constructs versus individual hazard items. It was concluded that effective risk management is likely to require: risk assessment and prioritisation of control actions separately for each local workgroup; assessment of specific hazards rather than the generic constructs used by researchers. Results highlight the value of managing MSD and MHP risks together, because both were affected by both psychosocial and biomechanical hazards in combinations that varied widely between workgroups. © 2026 The Authors.
