title: Photothermal Superhydrophobic Textiles: An Emerging Paradigm from Passive Water Repellency to Active Thermal Management
abstract: Photothermal superhydrophobic textiles represent an emerging paradigm integrating active light-driven functionality with passive liquid repellency. While previous reviews treated superhydrophobicity and photothermal effects in isolation, this work pioneers a systematic analysis of their synergistic interplay—a critical, underexplored mechanism where superhydrophobicity preserves photothermal efficiency by minimizing water-induced heat loss, while photothermal activity prevents surface fouling that compromises non-wetting performance. Through detailed case studies of advanced material systems, this review highlights how this synergy supports significant advancements in adaptive wearable technology, energy-efficient infrastructure, and eco-friendly water treatment. This review presents an original “lab-to-life” roadmap that structurally links material design to durability assessment, environmental impact evaluation, and scalable manufacturing strategies—a holistic framework absent in existing literature. The review emphasizes urgent sustainability priorities including green material substitutions, non-toxic solvent processing methodologies, and circular design principles aligned with global environmental regulations. By connecting fundamental mechanisms to real-world deployment scenarios while outlining transformative future directions such as AI-accelerated material discovery, stimulus-responsive systems, and intelligent manufacturing protocols, this work provides a timely and actionable reference for advancing next-generation textiles toward technological sophistication and practical viability in sustainable development. title: Integrating Computational Thinking and Islamic Values in Geometry Learning: Effects on Pre-Service Primary Teachers’ Conceptual Understanding
abstract: This study examines the integration of computational thinking and Islamic values in geometry learning for Primary School Teacher Education (PSTE) students. Using a quantitative descriptive approach, the research involved 70 PSTE students at Universitas Islam Riau. Data were collected through tests, observations, and interviews, and analyzed using triangulation to ensure validity. This integration significantly improves students’ conceptual understanding, as reflected in the increase in post-test scores. The one-sample t-test yielded a significance value, confirming a meaningful difference between pre-and post-test results. In addition, students internalized Islamic values such as honesty, cooperation, and spiritual awareness during learning activities. This study responds to the need for educational models that balance cognitive skills and character development. The integration of technology and Islamic principles creates a holistic learning experience, contributing to the development of competent, ethical, and responsible future educators. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Urbanisation, gender vulnerability, and ecovocation among migrant women in prostitution
abstract: This study examines how rapid metropolitan transformation in Jakarta produces structural vulnerability and social inequality among female migrants involved in covert sexual labour within the SPA industry. It investigates the relevance of the right to the city and an eco-vocational educational approach within Population and Environmental Education as critical frameworks for understanding exclusion, agency, and citizenship. Using a qualitative multi-sited case study design, the research draws on in-depth interviews, limited participant observation, and document analysis involving women workers, SPA managers, community actors, civil society representatives, and policymakers. The data were analysed thematically through critical urban studies and feminist perspectives. The findings show that women's involvement in covert sexual labour cannot be understood simply as an individual moral failure or fully voluntary decision. Rather, it reflects constrained agency shaped by unequal labour markets, limited educational capital, family economic responsibilities, debt relations, migration pressures, and regulatory ambiguity surrounding the SPA sector. Participants experienced layered forms of exploitation, symbolic violence, stigma, and disconnected citizenship: they contributed to the city's informal service economy but remained socially marginalised, politically unrecognised, and institutionally underprotected. Urban governance practices tended to intensify this vulnerability by emphasising surveillance, raids, and moral regulation rather than social protection, labour justice, and inclusive public policy. The study argues that the right to the city offers a useful analytical lens for revealing spatial injustice and the denial of substantive citizenship among marginalised women. It further proposes eco-vocational education as a transformative framework for restoring dignity, strengthening capabilities, expanding livelihood alternatives, and promoting more inclusive, just, and humane urban futures. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Energy transition materials, climate knowledge, and the imagined supply chain: Escaping the productive paradox of necessary mining
abstract: Much scholarship, public discourse, and policymaking on ‘energy transition materials’ (ETMs) imagines a supply chain from material production to climate mitigation, despite the absence of any mechanism ensuring that mined materials will become an electrification technology, let alone replace fossil fuels or avoid warming impacts. Scholarship about energy transition material (ETM) discourse, including criticism, largely neglects this material-discursive contradiction and truncates final analyses to paradoxes productive toward extractive futures. Leveraging a review of 99 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013-2025, this article brings mining scholarship into conversation with climate knowledge politics. It charts the dematerialization of climate knowledge from warming impacts to values negotiated along three spectra (urgency, scale, and sacrifice) and rematerialization reflected in extractive rationales (developmental, Indigenous rights, nature, and futures). Most ETM discourse is enclosed in three narrative boundaries, which lean on the imagined supply chain and foreclose non-extractive possibilities: (1) The contingencies that link climate policy and mining, such as materials science, technological manufacturing and use, are taken for granted; (2) Scalar formulations separate and compare anthropogenic climate change and mining impacts; and (3) ETMs wield climate knowledge itself as a supply chain, dialectically illustrating a problem to its own solution. Pathways to overcome the boundaries can center the materiality of mining and climate change over the abstractions of supply chains and imagined climate benefits, critically reflect on the relationships between material production and technopolitical knowledge, and take seriously actually occurring alternative livelihoods. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Impact of Livelihood Capital on Farmers’ Adoption of Sustainable Crop Residue Management Practices: Empirical Evidence from Punjab Province, Pakistan
abstract: Sustainable crop residue management can increase agricultural productivity and reduce farming-related carbon emissions, yet adoption of sustainable crop residue management practices (SCRMPs) remains limited. This study investigates how farmers’ livelihood capital shapes SCRMP adoption in Punjab, Pakistan, using survey data from 500 farmers in three agro-ecological zones. A multivariate probit model, weighted with the entropy-TOPSIS method, estimates the effects of human, social, natural, physical, and financial capital on practices including on-farm use, livestock feed, residue retention, and biogas production. Human, social, financial, and physical capital positively influence on-farm residue use, while all five forms of capital significantly promote biogas production. Although livestock feed remains the most common use, many farmers are willing to adopt alternatives such as biofertilizer production and biogas. These findings indicate substantial potential to expand sustainable residue management in the region. Policymakers should prioritize farmer training, credit access, rural infrastructure, biogas technologies, extension services, and farmer cooperatives to encourage environmentally and economically sustainable practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Genesis and evolution of metaverses as socio-technological realities; [پیدایش و تکامل متاورس در جایگاه واقعیتی اجتماعی و فناورانه]
abstract: This article focuses on exploring the evolution of metaverses as socio-technological virtual spaces, which, with further development, will lead to the growth of existing or potentially new forms of social interaction. Approaches to defining the key characteristics and stages of metaverse development are considered. Various forms of social activity within metaverses are analyzed with reference to specific examples, such as political activity, economic activity, and the implementation of socio-cultural projects. The article is based on a systemic analysis that enables the consideration of the technological and social aspects of metaverse development in their interrelation and dynamics, as well as scenario analysis to predict future forms of social interaction in virtual spaces. The emergence of increasingly new forms of social interaction may lead to the manifestation of a confrontational political potential, expressed in virtual protests, rallies, calls for a change of power, etc. The derived conclusions highlight the importance of developing inclusive mechanisms and models for managing and regulating metaverses in terms of social, public, and political risks. © 2026, University of Tehran. .

title: Beyond Digitalization: A Conceptual and Institutional Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
abstract: Digital transformation in higher education has emerged as a strategic priority for universities worldwide over the past decade. Despite the rapid growth of scholarly interest in this field, the existing literature remains conceptually fragmented, disproportionately focused on technological aspects, and limited in providing integrated frameworks to guide digital transformation processes. This study aims to systematically synthesize the digital transformation literature in higher education, identify dominant trends, key dimensions, challenges, and research gaps, and develop an integrated conceptual framework to address these limitations. Using a systematic literature review approach in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, 145 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2026 were analyzed. Data were examined through systematic content analysis across multiple levels, including temporal and geographical trends, methodological characteristics, thematic classifications, and conceptual integration of findings. The results reveal a clear shift in the literature from technology-centered perspectives toward a multidimensional, institutional, and strategic understanding of digital transformation in higher education. Three interrelated dimensions, digital technologies and infrastructure, human resources and digital skills, and leadership, culture, and policy were identified as the core components of effective digital transformation. The findings further highlight persistent research gaps related to organizational readiness, institutional implications, change management, and the contextual localization of digital transformation frameworks, particularly in developing country contexts. In response to these gaps, this study proposes an integrated conceptual framework that conceptualizes digital transformation in higher education as a dynamic four-stage process encompassing readiness and assessment, pilot implementation, scaling and integration, and continuous optimization and innovation. The proposed framework offers both an analytical foundation for future research and a practical reference for university leaders and policymakers seeking to design and implement sustainable digital transformation initiatives. © 2027 The author(s). title: A dynamic graph query-based data pricing method via multi-armed bandits
abstract: Graph query-based data pricing is promising for pricing answer subgraphs in graph databases according to diverse buyer queries. However, existing methods provide limited support for adaptive price updates when the broker must balance transaction revenue with transaction success rate under incomplete buyer-valuation information. To bridge this gap, we propose GQPRM, which includes: (1) a vertex-edge pricing mechanism that prices a first-time queried answer graph through non-negative atomic prices; (2) a multi-armed bandit (MAB)-based strategy that discretizes repeated-query prices into candidate actions and uses historical acceptance/rejection records for exploration and exploitation; (3) an entropy-weighted feedback update that allocates the observed subgraph-level price variation to vertices and edges in a demand-sensitive manner, rather than assuming that binary feedback uniquely identifies a single overpriced element; and (4) a smart contract-based incentive allocation mechanism that records ownership and supports auditable reward allocation between the data broker and data owners. Experiments on three typical datasets demonstrate that GQPRM improves cumulative transaction value and transaction success rate over the static baseline under the evaluated settings. © 2026

title: Food souvenir SMEs performance: Digital marketing, branding, innovation, and Hexa Helix moderation
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in the food souvenir sector, play a vital role in supporting local economic development. However, increasing competition and rapid digital transformation require SMEs to strengthen their strategic capabilities in order to maintain their marketing performance. Previous research has largely examined digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation separately, with limited attention to the combined effects of these three factors and the moderating role of collaborative ecosystems such as the Hexa Helix model. This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation on marketing performance, while also examining the moderating role of Hexa Helix collaboration. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 335 SMEs owners, and the data were analyzed using Warp Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (WarpPLS-SEM). The results indicate that branding has the strongest positive effect on marketing performance ( β = 0.318, p < 0.001 ), followed by digital marketing capabilities ( β = 0.289, p < 0.001 ) and product innovation ( β = 0.117, p = 0.015 ). Regarding the moderating role, the findings indicate that the Hexa Helix does not significantly moderate the relationship between digital marketing capabilities and marketing performance, nor between branding and marketing performance. However, the Hexa Helix significantly strengthens the relationship between product innovation and marketing performance ( β = 0.217, p < 0.001 ). These findings suggest that while internal strategic capabilities are the primary drivers of SMEs performance, external collaborative support through the Hexa Helix is highly effective in amplifying the impact of product innovation rather than uniformly strengthening all strategic relationships. This study contributes to the literature by providing a deeper understanding of the conditional role of collaborative ecosystems in SMEs performance. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Evolving the DarTwin evolution language
abstract: DarTwin is a notation for describing and planning evolution of digital twin systems. Originally conceived as a graphical notation, DarTwin has evolved into a domain-specific language formally defined in SysML v2. This evolution exposed challenges related to graphical notation support, tooling interoperability, and co-evolution between notation, language definition, and modelling environments. We experienced that SysML v2 tooling was not adequate to provide our DarTwin graphical notation even with some post-processing. The SysML v2 definition of DarTwin did, however, motivate improvements of the DarTwin DSL. To provide fruitful DarTwin graphical notation and still maintain the formal definition in SysML v2 we demonstrate how domain-specific tooling (MetaEdit+) helps improving the graphic editing and rendering support and thus achieve a more effective and intuitive use of DarTwin. By generating SysML v2 from MetaEdit+ we preserve the connection between the adequate graphical notation and the precision and formality of DarTwin. The combined DarTwin tooling made the methodology to apply general evolution transition patterns (DarTrans) more formal and precise while still intuitive through graphic notation using colour and dashes. This in turn motivated enhancing the DarTwin language by adding concepts related to the evolution transitions to facilitate discovering and documenting the transitions. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Atomic and Molecular Structure Regulated In Situ Cross-Linked Polyurethane Gel Electrolyte for High-Performance Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: The incompatibility of conventional electrolytes with high-voltage cathodes and lithium metal anodes limits the performance of lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Here, an in situ cross-linked polyurethane gel electrolyte (G-P3 AR) is designed through atomic and molecular structure regulation. The polyester segments widen the highest occupied molecular orbital–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital gap, extending the electrochemical stability window to 4.97 V for compatibility with NCM811 cathodes. Polyether segments exhibit a lower Li+ binding energy, reducing the desolvation barrier and enhancing anode stability. At the atomic level, sp2-hybridized boron in the chain extender immobilizes anions (TFSI− and DFOB−) through Lewis acid–base interactions, raising the Li+ transference number to 0.78 and enabling exceptional rate capability (157.7 mAh g−1 at 2 C in the Li||NCM811 cell). Hydrogen bonding between the polymer and solvent restructures the solvation sheath, promoting inorganic-rich interphases. title: Creative thinking ability: A hybrid systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: This study explores the development of creative thinking ability over the past few decades using a interdisciplinary approach in a global context. Various studies have investigated creative thinking ability over the past several decades, but the search is still fragmented in each field. Therefore, there is a significant gap in our understanding of how these concepts of creative thinking overlap and interact across disciplines. So that, in-depth research on this subject remains necessary. This study is a systematic literature review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of creative thinking ability based on empirical studies that have been conducted. The methodology used in this study is a systematic literature review using term “creative thinking ability” in the article title, abstract, and keywords from the Scopus database, resulting in 4,487 publications from 1968 to 2025. The evaluation was conducted on January 5, 2026. The collected data were analyzed bibliometrically using the VOS (visualization of similarities) viewer. This study found that creative thinking intersects various disciplines, including psychology, education, and business, which holistically intersect with the cognitive dimension, the affective dimension, and the socio-cultural dimension. In psychology, an individual’s creative capacity can be optimized through cognitive stimulation aligned with their personality characteristics. In the business sector, a climate of innovation is encouraged through structured training programs adaptively designed based on employee perceptions and needs. Meanwhile, in the educational context, students’ creativity can be effectively cultivated through the implementation of transformative learning models supported by practical instructional strategies in the classroom. By integrating insights from these fields, it will be able to improve educational practices and foster a conducive environment for creativity that can lead to innovative teaching strategies. So that educational institutions can prepare students to design innovative solutions to address various pressing global challenges, in line with sustainable development goals (SDGs). © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Brains on copy-paste mode? A mixed-methods study on the relationship between generative artificial intelligence use and students’ critical thinking skills
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence tools, such as ChatGPT, into higher education has raised important questions about their relationship with students' critical thinking (CT) skills. This study explored these associations among 398 undergraduate students using a mixed-methods design. Quantitatively, participants completed validated measures of critical thinking and a survey assessing frequency of AI use in academic contexts. Correlation analyses indicated a significant negative association between AI use and Analyzing/Organizing skills. Moderation analyses revealed that academic achievement moderated this relationship for Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating, with higher achievers showing a stronger negative association. No significant effects emerged for gender and age on the remaining CT dimensions. Likewise, qualitative analyses of 200 open-ended responses identified three user profiles: (1) instrumental/uncritical, comprising younger low-achieving male students emphasizing AI speed and utility while reporting reduced verification effort; (2) stable/complementary, comprising older high-achieving students perceiving little change in their evaluative practices; and (3) ambivalent/skeptical-trusting, comprising women with medium achievement, divided between increased skepticism and greater reliance on AI outputs. Supplementary analyses linking Analyzing/Organizing and Evaluating scores to these profiles showed that lower development of both skills consistently aligned with the instrumental/uncritical profile. The interpretive consistency between both analytical strands suggests that the relationship between generative AI use and CT skills is nuanced and profile-dependent, limited in scope to specific dimensions and student groups rather than reflecting a broad negative impact, while highlighting the risks of uncritical reliance and the potential of AI as a complementary academic tool when used reflectively. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Rethinking institutional support for migrant businesses in Sweden: A strategic management– oriented scoping review
abstract: Migrant entrepreneurship has become an increasingly important contributor to Sweden’s economic and social landscape; however, the institutional environment supporting migrant-owned businesses remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. This study conducts a scoping review to map existing knowledge on the opportunities, barriers, and systemic gaps affecting migrant entrepreneurs in Sweden. The review draws on peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and grey literature published between 2020 and 2026, identified primarily through the Scopus database and complementary manual searches. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach. The findings reveal that migrant entrepreneurs contribute significantly to job creation, innovation, and regional development, particularly in sectors such as retail, hospitality, and services. However, they face persistent barriers including limited access to finance, bureaucratic complexity, language constraints, and weak integration into institutional support networks. The analysis further shows that although Sweden possesses a wide range of support mechanisms, these are often poorly coordinated, resulting in duplication, inefficiencies, and limited accessibility for migrant entrepreneurs. Guided by the resource-based view (RBV) and contingency theory, this study develops a strategic pathways model consisting of three interrelated pillars: resource mobilization, adaptive strategy, and collaborative alignment. The model provides a conceptual framework for enhancing institutional effectiveness and improving the inclusiveness of entrepreneurial support systems. The study highlights the need for a more integrated, flexible, and strategically coordinated support ecosystem. It also identifies critical gaps in empirical research and calls for future studies to test the proposed model in real-world institutional settings. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. This study analyses the highly fragmented literature on maritime clusters and sustainability using a novel combination of bibliometrics and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven thematic analysis. On this basis, a framework is developed that captures the interaction between clusters and the key components of sustainability. The findings suggest that sustainability should not be treated as an isolated strategic initiative or the outcome of regulatory pressure, but as a key dimension of cluster competitiveness. Additionally, it emerges that digital innovation acts as a cross-cutting enabler of sustainability in maritime clusters, linking the economic, social/governance, and environmental pillars of the proposed framework. Overall, this study provides actionable insights for maritime practitioners and policy makers alike. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A reciprocal perspective on internationalization and ESG in EMNEs: The role of digitalization
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) has become a critical measure of multinational enterprises’ global competitiveness, yet emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face distinct legitimacy challenges due to weak home-country ESG regulations, known as the liability of home origin. Although prior studies have examined the relationship between internationalization and ESG, they have largely treated the two directions separately, leaving unclear whether they operate as competing explanations or as mutually reinforcing processes. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study conceptualizes internationalization and ESG performance as exhibiting mutually reinforcing associations over time. Using longitudinal data from 2460 Chinese listed firms between 2009 and 2020, we examine the reciprocal relationship between internationalization and ESG performance, and the moderating role of digitalization. Findings indicate that internationalization is consistently associated with stronger ESG performance, suggesting EMNEs use ESG to mitigate liabilities of origin and build legitimacy abroad. The reverse association is weaker but most robust for foreign-country scope, indicating that ESG performance may support international expansion by signaling alignment with international sustainability expectations. The moderating associations of digitalization are uneven and are concentrated in visible foreign organizational and geographic presence, such as overseas subsidiaries and foreign-country scope, rather than overseas revenues. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Perceived placeness in creative tourism: Conceptualization, scale development and implications for transformative experiences
abstract: Creative place-making combines cultural heritage, spatial design, creative symbolism, and experiential affordances to cultivate distinctive destinations, yet what tourists holistically perceive in these places remains underexplored. Drawing on atmospheric aesthetics theory, this study conceptualizes perceived placeness in creative tourism as tourists' holistic perception of the environmental and atmospheric qualities that make creative tourism destinations experientially distinctive. To operationalize this construct, content analysis was used to identify its dimensions and initial items. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses refined these items into a 20-item, five-dimensional scale comprising environmental qualities, historical-cultural embeddedness, creative-symbolic ambiance, restorative affordance, and emotional affordance. The nomological relevance of the scale was further established by examining its implications for transformative experiences via authenticity. Theoretically, this study positions perceived placeness as an integrative perceptual field between place-making and tourists’ psychological responses, and contextually elaborates atmospheric aesthetics theory in creative tourism. Practically, the scale provides a timely tool for evaluating and planning creative place-making efforts and curating meaningful tourist experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Developing Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Gen Z accounting students: The roles of AI Competency, Systematic Thinking Ability, and Design Thinking Ability
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in accounting practices have significantly increased the complexity and uncertainty of professional work environments, making Dynamic Risk Management Skills a critical competency for contemporary accounting graduates. This study aims to examine the relationships between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills among Generation Z (Gen Z) accounting students, with Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability considered as mediating variables. A quantitative research design was employed, collecting data from 571 fourth-year accounting students across Thailand. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that AI Competency is significantly and positively associated with Systematic Thinking Ability, Design Thinking Ability, and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. Moreover, Systematic Thinking Ability and Design Thinking Ability significantly account for the indirect associations between AI Competency and Dynamic Risk Management Skills. These findings extend theoretical understanding of risk management skill development in accounting education and offer practical implications for curriculum design by emphasizing the integration of AI with higher-order thinking skill development to better prepare graduates for complex and rapidly changing professional environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Greenhouse gas emission under a dual-disposability approach: Assessing environmental technical efficiency in the airline industry
abstract: This study provides a robust analysis of environment-adjusted airline efficiency under a dual-disposability assumption for undesirable output. It employs also a two-stage methodology to investigate the complex and heterogeneous relationships between airline operational profiles and their environmental efficiency. Technical efficiency is estimated in the first step using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) based on the Directional Distance Function (DDF) under both assumptions of the technological characterization of gas emissions, contractible versus non-contractible. In the second step, to analyze the factors influencing the estimated efficiency scores, a Tobit second-stage regression is employed. Results show that efficiency scores under strong disposability are systematically and significantly higher than those obtained under weak disposability, with an average difference of 11.9 percentage points. The findings also indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between the LCC variable and technical efficiency, implying that airline groups with LCC subsidiaries achieve higher efficiency levels. Based on their specific trade-off between operational and environmental inputs, the analysis of technical efficiency elasticities classifies airlines into five groups. These range from “Strong Proactive Environmental Performers” to “Low Efficiency High-Cost” groups, whose efficiency improvements are structurally linked to either an optimization or a deterioration of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions performance. The technical efficiency elasticity with respect to revenue share and to fuel efficiency are parallel across all airlines, while the elasticity for GHG consistently exhibits the opposite sign. We provide one of the few systematic comparisons of efficiency scores under weak versus strong disposability. This comparison allows us to quantify the systematic contraction in measured efficiency that occurs when greenhouse gas emissions are modeled as a technologically costly output rather than a costless byproduct. © 2026 The Authors.

title: ResGAT: A residual graph attention network for technology transfer prediction in Chinese universities
abstract: University patent transfer in China remains sparse, and only a small fraction of university patents are licensed or assigned. Technology-transfer offices must still judge which patents are worth promoting and which enterprises are plausible recipients. Existing matching methods rely on content similarity, collaborative filtering, or shallow heterogeneous graphs. They rarely model patent–patent, patent–entity, and entity–entity relations together with patent attributes when positive transfer labels are extremely scarce. This study proposes a residual graph attention network (ResGAT) for technology-transfer object recognition. Built on three meta-paths, ResGAT uses relation-specific attention together with a shared feature transformation. It stacks residual graph-attention layers on the homogeneous branches to limit over-smoothing, and it uses a shallow cross-type branch to pass entity information to patents. A two-stage procedure then estimates transfer probability and ranks candidate transferees by dot-product similarity. On a civil-engineering patent graph from a Chinese university, and on seven strategic-emerging-industry subsets, ResGAT outperforms heuristic, linear, and multi-relational graph baselines under the same 10-fold protocol. The model also returns ranked enterprise lists for high-potential patents, so transfer offices receive a concrete shortlist rather than only a transfer score. © 2026

title: Optimizing renewable energy planning: a Monte Carlo–analytical hierarchy process framework for net-zero transitions
abstract: As the world pursues net-zero emissions, selecting renewable energy technologies presents a complex challenge balancing technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods support decisions by comparing alternatives against multiple criteria. However, traditional MCDM approaches, reliant on fixed inputs, often fail to capture real-world variability in energy planning, yielding less reliable outcomes. This study introduces a novel Monte Carlo–Analytical Hierarchy Process (MAHP) framework that integrates AHP's structured evaluation with Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to model uncertainty in criteria weights and alternative scores. The MAHP framework was applied to support Sheffield's 2030 net-zero target by evaluating five renewable energy technologies: solar PV, onshore wind, biomass, hydropower, and geothermal. Thousands of simulations were conducted to reflect different stakeholder priorities, covering technical, environmental, social, economic, and equal-weighting scenarios. The analysis demonstrated that technology rankings are highly sensitive to stakeholder priorities, underscoring the need for adaptable planning approaches, and showing that no single technology consistently dominates when priorities are balanced. Overall, the results support a hybrid mix centred on solar PV, onshore wind, and hydropower for Sheffield. This framework strengthens renewable energy planning by moving beyond single deterministic rankings and instead quantifying how robust each recommendation is under uncertainty and shifting priorities. By making ranking stability and trade-offs explicit, MAHP enhances the credibility of technology selection and provides decision-makers with clearer evidence to support defensible net-zero strategies in dynamic urban contexts. More broadly, probabilistic ranking supports portfolio planning by identifying consistently competitive technologies, reducing over-commitment when stakeholder priorities and evidence are uncertain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Covalent Organic Framework-Anchored Carbon Nanotubes Enabling Ultra-Thin Robust Polyimide Films for High-Specific-Power Flexible GaAs Solar Cells
abstract: Free-standing polymer films that are ultra-thin, lightweight, and robust hold significant promise for applications in flexible electronics. However, their performance has been constrained by the challenge of simultaneously enhancing mechanical strength and reducing density. Herein, an ultra-thin and robust polyimide (PI)-based covalent organic framework-modified multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT-COF) film is demonstrated for high-specific-power flexible GaAs solar cells. The film exhibits a high Young’s modulus of 1.53 GPa, a tensile strength exceeding 97.53 MPa, and a low density of 0.73 g cm−3, representing a 45.1% reduction in density. The incorporation of 3D interconnected layered and porous MWCNT-COF significantly enhances the film’s mechanical properties while reducing its density. The synergistic effects of robust MWCNTs and covalently bonded COF layers, combined with the thermally stable PI molecular structure, impart exceptional strength and lightness to the film. Computational studies further confirm that COF-grafted MWCNTs effectively modify the polyamide acid matrix, substantially improving the mechanical properties of the PI films. Moreover, flexible dual-junction and triple-junction GaAs solar cells were successfully fabricated using 6 µm-thick MWCNT-COF/PI composite films, delivering outstanding specific powers of 8998 and 7749 W kg−1, along with efficiencies of 26.6% and 31.5% (AM0), respectively. These results underscore the potential for high-performance applications in space and energy systems. This work offers valuable insights into the development of high-performance flexible GaAs solar cells based on ultra-thin and robust PI films for a wide range of applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: The Fragility of Collective Action in Community Forest Management: Social Feedbacks, Trust, and Cooperation Dynamics
abstract: In community forest management, cooperation is rarely a one-time decision. It depends on whether local actors continue contributing time, labor, and resources year after year. We examine this problem with a system dynamics model that follows changes in trust, reputation, reciprocity, perceived benefits, and free-riding. The model adapts an earlier structure to the case of ejido La Loma, Mexico. The case material guided several modeling decisions, especially the choice of variables and the interpretation of the scenarios. It did not, however, provide enough information for full empirical calibration. The simulations show that trust and reputation may sustain cooperation even as participation declines. Over time, however, the loss of active members can weaken monitoring and place collective action at risk. One result is particularly relevant: a favorable starting point does not guarantee long-term stability. title: Materials–Structure–Hardware–Algorithm Co-Driven Hierarchical Optimization for Flexible Sensors
abstract: Flexible electronics represent a paradigm shift in modern electronics, with flexible sensors serving as pivotal components in these systems. Despite significant advances driven by innovations in materials, structures, hardware, and algorithms, conventional design approaches that focus on optimizing individual hierarchies have inherent performance trade-offs, limiting further development. This review contends that future performance enhancements can no longer rely solely on breakthroughs in separate components. Still, it must adopt a new co-design paradigm spanning the “materials–structure–hardware–algorithm” hierarchy. In this review, we systematically organized the research landscape and representative advances across these four key hierarchies, analyzed the importance and recent breakthroughs in hierarchical synergy, and established a forward-looking theoretical framework to foster innovation and development in the field of flexible sensing. title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. While regional integration aims to reduce such barriers, prior research predominantly treats regional integration as a discrete accession event, leaving post-accession adaptation dynamics and their underlying mechanisms underexplored. Drawing on new institutional economics and social learning theory, we argue that joint regional membership duration increases CBA completion likelihood, with country-dyadic M&A stock serving as the mediating carrier via the sequential pathways of institutional alignment and social learning. We further examine how initial regulatory distance and cultural distance condition this mechanism. Using a sample of 8009 announced CBAs across the European Union (2010–2022), we find support for the mediation pathway and show that both regulatory and cultural distance weaken this indirect effect. This study advances the literature by moving beyond discrete event-based integration framing and refines the understanding of cross-national distance within integrated regional blocs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Territorializing the sea: fragmented operational control in offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia
abstract: The expansion of offshore tin mining transforms the sea into a space of extraction, yet territorial claims over this space do not necessarily translate into operational control. Studies of territorialization have largely focused on the formation of claims rather than on the processes through which such claims are converted into operational control. This article examines the territorialization of offshore tin mining on Bangka Island, Indonesia, through three interrelated analytical moments: territorial claims, securing access, and operational control. This qualitative study draws on fieldwork comprising interviews with 23 informants and observations, supplemented by a review of relevant literature and an analysis of regulatory documents, corporate reports, and news coverage. The findings show that exploration and regulatory arrangements produce epistemic and legal claims over marine space but do not, in themselves, enable mining operations. Companies and their local networks must still secure access by cultivating and representing support, engaging village institutions and local intermediaries, negotiating benefits, and making personal approaches to key actors. Their success varies across locations, shaped by local power relations, actor legitimacy, and fisher resistance. Consequently, operational control is contingent, partial, fragmented, and continuously negotiated: mining operations can proceed in some locations, whereas elsewhere territorial claims remain in force without being translated into operational control. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Multi-level analysis of firearm reoffending: the importance of community and incident context
abstract: Criminologists have long noted the exacerbated rates of firearm-related offending in the United States in comparison to other developed nations. There has been a renewed focus on gun crime in the wake of a recent dramatic reversal of the long-trending decrease in firearm-related violence. Although they provide valuable insights, explorations of the factors that contribute to firearm offending are often restricted to large metro areas like Chicago, New York City, and Philadelphia—which may have limited generalizability to more common small and medium sized cities in the United States. This study attempts to address this concern through examination of the factors that contribute to firearm re-offending among arrestees in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Specifically, multi-level analysis is used to explore the relative influence of neighborhood conditions, arrestee demographics, gang involvement, and offense characteristics on the odds of firearm reoffending among a sample of individuals arrested for gun crimes committed between 1/1/21 and 4/30/23 (n = 937). Our findings reveal null influence across contextual factors, while gang membership and juvenile status are each associated with increased odds in firearm reoffending. These results suggest the importance of early intervention on the part of criminal justice professionals as a matter of preventing future violence, while also presenting questions as they relate to the impact of structural conditions on repeat and chronic firearm offending. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Expand or carve up? Evaluating market dynamics of premium airline entry with extended synthetic control methods: Evidence from STARLUX airlines
abstract: This study examines the effects of STARLUX Airlines' entry as a newly established premium full-service carrier on Taiwan's international air transport market. Using the synthetic control method (SCM) and an extended SCM framework, the analysis evaluates changes in passenger demand following the airline's entry, encompassing both single and multiple treated units, including individual routes and interconnected markets. A conditional growth model was subsequently employed to distinguish market expansion from demand redistribution. Results indicate that although only 9 out of 24 treated markets showed statistically significant expansion, STARLUX's entry still revealed latent demand and contributed meaningfully to overall market growth despite the relatively small size of STARLUX as compared to its primary competitors, China Airlines and EVA Airways. This effect was particularly evident in business-oriented and transfer-focused segments, while some tourism-driven and politically sensitive markets saw limited or negative responses. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the demand-side influence of premium airline entry, extending SCM to multi-unit and network-based applications, and providing a replicable framework for evaluating airline market interventions in liberalized environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Chatbot service quality in omnichannel retailing: Effects of ChatbotSQ on decision confidence and customer behavior
abstract: AI chatbots are increasingly being embedded in omnichannel retail ecosystems; however, research on how chatbot service quality relates to customer behavior is limited. In this paper, we conceptualize chatbot service quality (ChatbotSQ) as a formative construct comprising six dimensions: functional, integration, interface, safety, emotional, and personalization quality. Drawing on means-end chain theory, we examine decision confidence as a mechanism underlying the association between chatbot service quality and customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in and explore the moderating role of chatbot comfort level. We use partial least squares structural equation modeling, importance-performance map analysis, and necessary condition analysis to analyze survey data from the United States (N = 345) and Saudi Arabia (N = 302). The results show that chatbot service quality is positively associated with customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in in both countries. These relationships are mediated by decision confidence, which also emerged as a necessary condition for achieving both behavioral outcomes. Chatbot comfort level significantly moderates the relationship between ChatbotSQ and decision confidence in Saudi Arabia but not in the United States, indicating that this boundary condition is context-sensitive across the two samples examined. We also validate a condensed six-item ChatbotSQ measure that provides a parsimonious alternative for research and practice. These findings advance retailing research by showing that AI chatbot service quality is associated with behavioral outcomes through customers’ decision confidence. © 2026 The Authors

title: Beyond positive attitude: What motivates stem undergraduates to engage in classroom discussions?
abstract: Fostering active participation in classroom discussions remains a persistent challenge in higher education, particularly in STEM fields where lecture-based instruction remains prevalent. While positive attitudes are often considered an important predictors of participation in classroom discussions, this study examines a broader set of psychological factors associated with STEM undergraduates’ intention to participate in classroom discussions. We propose and test an integrated model incorporating attitude, subjective norms, perceived need, and self-efficacy. Using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) on data from 550 undergraduates from engineering-focused universities, the study examines the motivational factors associated with participation intention and willingness to recommend classroom discussions. Perceived need and self-efficacy showed the strongest statistical associations with both outcomes. Subjective norms were positively associated with participation intention but not willingness to recommend, whereas attitude did not demonstrate a significant unique effect in the full model. Additional analyses suggest that this pattern reflects the stronger explanatory role of perceived need when considered alongside students’ general evaluations of classroom discussions. These findings highlight the importance of perceived learning value and confidence in predicting students’ participation in classroom discussions and provide context-specific implications for discussion-based teaching in engineering education. title: Non-covalent interactions between pectin and volatiles modulate flavor formation in goji berry (Lycium barbarum L.) during pulsed vacuum drying
abstract: Pectin plays a crucial role in modulating the flavor attributes of goji berry. This study investigated dynamic variations of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), non-volatile organic compounds (NVOCs), and pectin fractions, as well as their interactions in goji berry during pulsed vacuum drying (PVD), focusing on the chelator-soluble pectin (CSP) fraction. The results showed that 121 differential VOCs (DVOCs) were identified throughout the PVD process. The transition from stage III to V, during which rapid moisture migration occurred, was determined as the critical period for flavor formation. NVOCs involving soluble sugars, organic acids and amino acids affected VOC profiles. CSP exhibited substantial nanostructural rearrangement and interconnected network reconstruction, showing strong negative correlations with key aroma-active compounds such as acetic acid and octanal. It was further revealed that CSP interacted with acetic acid predominantly through hydrogen bonding, while octanal binding likely involved both hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding. These non-covalent interactions inhibited pectin aggregation, reduced particle size, and promoted the formation of stable porous fibrous microstructure that may facilitate flavor retention. Therefore, these findings indicate that pectin regulates flavor formation during PVD not only through structural transformation but also via non-covalent interactions with VOCs. This study provides theoretical basis for clarifying flavor-formation mechanisms of goji berry during PVD processing. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A Malatya Centrality-based algorithm for optimal solutions to maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover problems in lattice graphs
abstract: A lattice graph constitutes a fundamental graph type utilized across various domains and for addressing distinct challenges. The literature acknowledges a plethora of lattice graphs, each characterized by unique structures and attributes. Among the problems defined on lattice graphs are the Maximum Independent Set Problem (MISP) and the Minimum Vertex-Cover Problem (MVCP). MISP entails identifying the largest set of vertices in a graph that are not adjacent via edges. Conversely, MVCP involves determining the smallest set of vertices necessary to encompass all edges between nodes. Numerous methodologies have been suggested to resolve these issues within the context of lattice graphs. This research introduces an algorithm to address both MISP and MVCP on lattice graphs, leveraging the Malatya centrality algorithm. The algorithm calculates the centrality values of nodes within a lattice graph based on their degrees. Initially, it identifies the optimal solution set for MISP by employing the Malatya centrality values of the nodes. Subsequently, it ascertains the optimal solution set for MVCP based on the solution derived for MISP. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm was verified through its application to sample lattice graphs of varying sizes and configurations. It offers an efficient and robust solution in polynomial time across different lattice graph categories. Mathematical analysis and empirical studies on prevalent lattice graphs in the literature affirm that the algorithm yields optimal and effective resolutions for MISP and MVCP. Moreover, it generates solutions that are not contingent on constraints such as the number of iterations or initial conditions, and it produces effective outcomes in scenarios where integer linear programming methods fall short. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Harnessing the power of AI in qualitative research: Role assignment, engagement, and user perceptions of AI-generated follow-up questions in semi-structured interviews
abstract: Asking appropriate follow-up questions is an important aspect of semi-structured interviews, yet interviewers’ knowledge and skills may limit their depth and affect outcomes. While many studies have demonstrated the usefulness of large language models (LLMs) for qualitative analysis, their potential in data collection remains underexplored. We adopt an AI-driven/Reverse “Wizard-of-Oz” setup to investigate how real-time LLM support for generating follow-up questions shapes semi-structured interviews. Through a study with 17 participants, we examine the value of LLM-generated follow-up questions, the evolving division of roles, relationships, collaborative behaviors, and responsibilities between interviewers and AI. Our findings (1) provide empirical evidence of the strengths and limitations of AI-generated follow-up questions (AGQs); (2) introduce a Human-AI collaboration framework in this interview context; and (3) propose human-centered design guidelines for AI-assisted interviews. We position LLMs as complements, not replacements, human judgment, and highlight pathways for integrating AI into qualitative data collection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: 40 years of equity sensitivity: A theoretical and meta-analytic review of relations, roles, and remaining questions
abstract: Organizational scholars have studied equity sensitivity (ES) for nearly half a century. Yet, a lack of synthesis in the ES literature suggests important questions remain regarding our understanding of the concept, its nomological network, the theoretical role(s) it may play in shaping employee attitudes and behaviors, and its relations to adjacent theories of equity and organizational justice. In the current work, we address these questions via a theoretical and meta-analytic review of the ES literature encompassing 117 articles, 144 samples, and 36,177 participants. In synthesizing the literature, we (1) describe and alleviate existing tensions surrounding the construct's conceptualization, (2) provide empirical insights regarding the construct's associations and relative importance in the prediction of key workplace outcomes, and (3) present an integrative model of ES's potential theoretical moderating role in equity and justice relationships. Our work provides clarity regarding ES's nomological network and offers critical directions for future scholarship. Specifically, we draw special attention to opportunities for new work exploring ES's potential as a key linking mechanism among equity and organizational justice theories. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A review on model innovation and applications through network data envelopment analysis
abstract: Over last 25 years, network data envelopment analysis (NDEA) provides effective framework for assessing efficiency in systems characterized by multiple interconnected stages and hierarchical levels. This review presents PRISMA 2020 based systematic review of NDEA literature by analysing studies sourced from multiple academic databases. The retained literature was used for bibliometric analysis and 260 selected studies were comprehensively synthesized to examine evolution in NDEA from conventional DEA models to network based formulation that capture internal structures, intermediate links, shared inputs and environmental interactions. Important methodological advancements in NDEA include slack-based measures, dynamic models, stochastic and fuzzy extensions. This study also discusses approaches that integrated undesirable outputs, time-dependent variables and hybrid AI/ML-based models, which enable more accurate and data-driven efficiency assessments as compared to traditional DEA. Bibliometric and qualitative analyses indicate substantial methodological advancement and increasing application of NDEA across diverse domains. Banking, healthcare, energy, transportation and supply chain applications demonstrate need of NDEA. Despite of recent progress, challenges associated with variable selection, data quality, model standardization and result robustness continue to exist. Future research should focus on harmonizing input–output structures, enhancing sensitivity analysis, strengthen model validation and integration of NDEA results with cost-effective assessments and policy oriented evaluations. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: IrMn-Cluster-Based Artificial Metalloenzymes with Radiosensitized Systemic Antitumor Responses to Prevent Malignant Tumor Metastasis and Recurrence
abstract: Developing radiosensitizing agents to amplify tumor-eradicating effects on primary, regional recurrence, and distant metastases plays a transformative role in modern cancer care. Here, we report the de novo design of biocatalytic artificial metalloenzymes with an IrMn-cluster-based redox center (IMM) to achieve radiosensitized systemic antitumor responses for preventing malignant tumor metastasis and recurrence. Notably, our findings indicate that Mn-organic ligands substantially enrich the electron density of Ir clusters, thereby optimizing their interaction with oxygen species and markedly enhancing the production of both reactive oxygen species and molecular oxygen. When combined with radiotherapy, the IMM effectively amplifies DNA damage and induces pronounced apoptosis by alleviating intratumoral hypoxia. This shift reprograms the tumor microenvironment, enhancing radiosensitivity and facilitating the infiltration and activation of intratumoral CD8⁺ T cells and dendritic cells. Moreover, when integrated with anti-PD-1 therapy, this coordinated therapeutic regimen elicits potent systemic immune responses and durable antitumor memory, effectively suppressing tumor recurrence and metastasis while markedly improving therapeutic efficacy and long-term survival. We anticipate that this conceptual design could offer a promising and translationally relevant nanomedicine platform for radiotherapies. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Consumer awareness, participation, and accessibility in sustainable electronic waste management
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The rapid increase in electronic waste has created increasingly complex environmental and health challenges, especially in developing countries like Indonesia. The study objectives were to examine how household awareness and accessibility of electronic-waste management facilities are associated with consumer participation, controlling for socioeconomic factors, demographics, and the region's spatial characteristics. METHODS: This study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design to examine household consumers living near electronic waste management facilities in Indonesia. To analyze the data, Spearman's rank correlation was employed to evaluate variable relationships, ordinary least squares regression to estimate the associations of awareness and accessibility with participation levels, Kruskal-Wallis test to examine group differences, and Geographic Information System-based spatial analysis to describe the spatial patterns of facility distance, accessibility, and electronic waste management participation. FINDINGS: Consumer awareness of the consequences of electronic waste showed a significant positive correlation with the intention to manage electronic waste, with a correlation coefficient of 0.340, but showed no significant correlation with actual behavior, with a correlation coefficient of only 0.067. Accessibility showed a significant positive correlation with both intention and actual behavior, with correlation coefficients of 0.197 and 0.416, respectively. Accessibility had the largest reported regression coefficient for actual behavior ( β = 0.449 ), followed by awareness of consequences ( β = 0.182 ). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed significant differences in intention and actual behavior across accessibility levels, with chi-square values of 11.67 and 35.91, respectively. Spatial analysis using the nearest neighbor method produced a nearest neighbor ratio of 0.60 with a z score of -10.01. Spatial analysis revealed that highly aware and active residents are significantly clustered rather than randomly dispersed, with the vast majority residing within a functional catchment area defined by 10 to 30 kilometer distances or 10 to 30 minute travel times from e-waste facilities. CONCLUSION: The findings underscore the need for electronic waste management policies that prioritise facility accessibility and spatially based approaches to strengthen community participation within a circular economy framework. title: Two pathways at once: An investigation of how reactance and ethicality shape student learning with AI
abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates. © 2026

title: Digital influences on green economic participation: The role of eWOM in shaping circular consumption among young vietnamese consumers
abstract: Circular business models (CBMs) are increasingly recognized as a strategic mechanism for advancing sustainable consumption and supporting green economic growth, particularly in emerging economies where rising consumption intensifies pressures on natural resources and waste management systems. Concurrently, the rapid expansion of social media and digital commerce has elevated electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to a central role in shaping how young consumers interpret, evaluate, and normalize sustainability-oriented business practices. Despite this growing intersection, limited empirical evidence explains how specific attributes of eWOM translate into consumers’ intentions to participate in CBMs, especially in developing-market contexts such as Vietnam. Addressing this gap, the present study adopts a quantitative approach using survey data from 1,142 young Vietnamese consumers to examine how core dimensions of eWOM influence information acceptance and, subsequently, participation intentions in CBMs within the retail sector. A rigorous multi-stage analytical procedure was employed, including reliability testing, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to validate the measurement model, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to assess the structural relationships among latent constructs. The results indicate that all four eWOM attributes positively influence information acceptance, which in turn significantly drives participation intention. Among these factors, relevance emerges as the most influential attribute, suggesting that sustainability-related messages are most effective when aligned with consumers’ personal needs, values, and decision contexts. The findings also confirm the mediating role of information acceptance in translating eWOM quality into behavioral intention. By validating both the measurement and structural models, this study enhances the robustness of IAM-based explanations in the context of circular consumption and extends the literature on digital influence in emerging markets. Practically, the study highlights the importance of designing relevant, credible, and comprehensive sustainability communication strategies. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted with caution due to the cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling approach. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Ultramicropore-Confined Solvation and Interphase Regulation Unlock High-Performance Hard Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Hard carbon (HC) anodes are promising for sodium-ion batteries, yet achieving high initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), large plateau contribution, and fast charge-transfer kinetics remains challenging due to insufficient control of micro–nanostructure and interphase chemistry. Here, we present a precursor-level molecular engineering strategy that simultaneously regulates sodium desolvation and interphase chemistry in HC. An iodine-mediated oxidative cross-linking process converts starch into spherical HC with uniformly distributed ultramicropores and carbonyl-rich surfaces. These nanoconfined pores are proposed to act as molecular sieves, preferentially excluding bulky solvent molecules while allowing PF6−-coordinated Na+ access, thereby favoring anion-enriched electrolyte structures under confinement. Surface carbonyls exhibit strong PF6− affinity, which may promote fluorine-rich inorganic interphases on pore surfaces. The synergistic effects of anion-selective adsorption and confined desolvation are suggested to favor thin and robust NaF-rich interphases at external surfaces and within nanoconfined pore regions, contributing to reversible interfacial reactions and rapid Na+ storage kinetics. Consequently, the HC delivers an ICE of 88.4%, a reversible capacity of 352.9 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, excellent rate capability (288.9 mAh g−1 at 5C), and 95.6% capacity retention over 200 cycles. This work offers a molecular-level design paradigm integrating efficiency, capacity, and kinetics in HC anodes. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Impacts of tourism development on residents’ quality of life: A dual spillover perspective
abstract: Tourism development can influence residents’ quality of life through bottom-up spillover (i.e., mediation) across life domains and through spatial spillover across regions. However, existing research has not integrated these micro and macro perspectives. This study develops an innovative theoretical framework to account for both spillover effects simultaneously. Using a constructed panel dataset from England and Wales, which integrates national longitudinal survey data, tourism statistics, socioeconomic indicators and geographic information, we apply dynamic spatial lag X panel models to verify the above framework. Results indicate that tourism development affects overall life satisfaction only indirectly, through spatial spillover effects mediated by different life domains, depending on the tourism indicators employed, underscoring the complexity of its impacts and the need for multifaceted tourism policymaking. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Transformational entrepreneurship education in the AI era: Reframing entrepreneurial readiness through AI literacy and digital entrepreneurial capability
abstract: Artificial intelligence integration is reshaping entrepreneurship education and increasing the need for pedagogical approaches that prepare students to act under digital uncertainty. Drawing on Transformational Learning Theory, Growth Mindset Theory, and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines how Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy contribute to Entrepreneurial Readiness directly and through Digital Innovation Skills and Digital Growth Mindset, the complementary dimensions through which Digital Entrepreneurial Capability is conceptually expressed. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Survey data from 698 Indonesian university students were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, followed by semi-structured interviews with 24 students. The findings show that Transformational Entrepreneurship Education was positively related to AI Literacy, Digital Innovation Skills, Digital Growth Mindset, and Entrepreneurial Readiness. AI Literacy was also positively related to both capability dimensions and Entrepreneurial Readiness. Both dimensions significantly mediated the relationships of Transformational Entrepreneurship Education and AI Literacy with Entrepreneurial Readiness, while the corresponding direct effects remained significant. Qualitative findings showed that reflective AI engagement, iterative experimentation, feedback, and persistence supported capability development, whereas passive AI reliance and limited scaffolding constrained capability translation. The study advances entrepreneurship education and AI Literacy research by reframing Entrepreneurial Readiness as an action-oriented outcome. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The effect of agricultural taxes and local agricultural policies on enhancing food security and environmental sustainability
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Indonesia is currently working towards sustainability in line with Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Anticipated demographic growth to 10.8 billion by the year 2050 is expected to place unprecedented strain on global food security and production systems. The study objectives were to examine the biophysical factors, production inputs, economic conditions, socio-technological factors, agricultural business management, and agricultural tax policies regional agricultural policies and, ultimately, agricultural productivity. METHODS: This quantitative study employed structured questionnaires administered to a sample of 200 farmers in Surabaya. The instrument used a one-to-five Likert scale covering biophysical factors, economic factors, tax policy, tax morale, and agricultural productivity. Data was analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling version 3. The analytical procedure comprised three distinct phases: first, evaluating the outer model for convergent and discriminant validity; second, conducting reliability assessments; and third, testing the inner model via bootstrapping to determine the coefficient of determination, the effect size, and hypothesis significance. Hypothesis significance was determined using t-statistic values of at least 1.96 and p-values of no more than 0.05. FINDINGS: Four hypotheses were rejected: economic factor on regional agricultural policy (p-value 0.557), agricultural taxation policy on tax morale (p-value 0.072), tax awareness on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.058), and tax morale on agricultural productivity (p-value 0.208). The findings reveal that regional agricultural policies are substantially driven by three key dimensions: biophysical factors (beta coefficient of 0.251, probability value of 0.000), production inputs (beta coefficient of 0.253, probability value of 0.002), and agricultural business management (beta coefficient of 0.228, probability value of 0.007). Agricultural tax policy significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.229, probability value of 0.000), while tax administration efficiency also significantly affects tax awareness (beta coefficient of -0.345, probability value of 0.000) and tax morale (beta coefficient of -0.634, probability value of 0.000), since clarity on procedures, benefits, and regulations fosters public responsibility and awareness of taxpayer obligations and rights. CONCLUSION: Elevating agricultural output demands comprehensive frameworks characterized by active farmer participation, supportive regulatory policies, targeted outreach regarding tax frameworks, and enhanced coordination between industry stakeholders and governmental bodies. Regional agricultural policies and tax awareness significantly influence agricultural productivity. These findings offer practical insights for policymakers aiming to strengthen agricultural governance and tax compliance frameworks in support of sustainable rural development. title: Moral responsibilisation in destination management: The strategic framing of civic practices by DMOs
abstract: This paper examines moral responsibilisation as an emerging destination governance mechanism through which destination management organisations (DMOs) and local stakeholders mobilise visitors to support sustainability goals. Drawing on an intrinsic qualitative case study of the Danish DMO, Wonderful Copenhagen , we develop a practice theory-based model showing that responsibilisation extends beyond narrative persuasion to include the organisational and material reframing of civic conduct. Analysis of interviews, participant observation, documents, and netnography identifies four interrelated stages: interpellation, involvement, intervention, and institutionalisation. Together, these stages connect inspirational messaging with participatory experiences, reward schemes, and decentralised service design. The findings also reveal tensions around the relevance, inclusivity, and feasibility of emerging civic practices. Resistance to responsible subject positions stems from stakeholders’ differing interpretations, negotiations, and disengagement from DMO-prescribed roles. The study advances the understanding of responsibilisation as a practice-based mode of governance and offers insights that may inform destination managers in varied tourism contexts. © 2026 The Authors.
