title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Touchable cultural heritage: How alternative touch experience facilitates visitors’ cultural inheritance behavior
abstract: Touch is a fundamental human need, yet in cultural heritage tourism, it is strictly restricted to protect fragile artifacts. While essential for preservation, touch restrictions limit multi-sensory experience and impede deeper cultural participation. This research addresses this touch dilemma by introducing alternative touch experiences, wherein tourists touch surrogate objects (e.g., artifact replicas) that simulate the haptic attributes of authentic artifacts. Across four studies with qualitative, experimental, and field evidence, we found that alternative touch experiences enhance tourists’ psychological closeness to heritage, which in turn fosters cultural inheritance intentions and actual behaviors (e.g., cultural learning, cultural knowledge sharing, and donation to protect heritage). However, this touch effect diminishes when artifacts carry negative (vs. positive) superstitious associations. These findings offer a new theoretical perspective on enabling embodied experience within the traditionally sensory-restricted context, and highlight the role of sensory engagement in facilitating heritage appreciation and cultural inheritance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Sustainable urban planning in conflict-affected cities: Governance, displacement, and hierarchical sustainability in Marib, Yemen
abstract: Sustainable urban planning frameworks presuppose institutional stability and regulated development, yet their applicability to conflict-affected cities remains theoretically underexamined. This qualitative case study examines how sustainability is interpreted and prioritised in Marib city, Yemen, an urban centre experiencing rapid growth amid armed conflict and mass internal displacement. Drawing on a framing analysis of global sustainability frameworks, semi-structured interviews with 16 city stakeholders, and structured observations in seven neighbourhoods, the study identifies a structural mismatch between global sustainability paradigms and local planning practice. Whereas international models assume balanced domain integration, the evidence from Marib reveals a context-conditioned hierarchy in which governance capacity and essential service provision operate as preconditions structuring environmental management, economic activity, and technological uptake. Locally, environmental sustainability is reduced to basic service continuity; social sustainability is dominated by displacement-driven absorptive pressures; economic sustainability narrows to livelihood survival; and technological adoption is fragmented and institutionally constrained. The paper advances a context-conditioned, hierarchical model of urban sustainability that challenges the implicit universality of parallel-domain planning approaches and calls for planning paradigms that recognise institutional capacity as foundational in fragile urban contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: An audio-visual fusion emotion generation model based on neuroanatomical alignment
abstract: In the field of affective computing, traditional methods for generating emotions predominantly rely on deep learning techniques and large-scale emotion datasets. However, deep learning techniques are often complex and difficult to interpret, and standardizing large-scale emotional datasets are difficult and costly to establish. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework named Audio-Visual Fusion for Brain-like Emotion Learning(AVF-BEL). In contrast to conventional brain-inspired emotion learning methods, this approach improves the audio-visual emotion fusion and generation model through the integration of modular components, thereby enabling more lightweight and interpretable emotion learning and generation processes. The framework simulates the integration of the visual, auditory, and emotional pathways of the brain, optimizes the fusion of emotional features across visual and auditory modalities, and improves upon the traditional Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) model. The experimental results indicate a significant improvement in the similarity of the audio-visual fusion emotion learning generation model compared to single-modality visual and auditory emotion learning and generation model. Ultimately, this aligns with the fundamental phenomenon of heightened emotion generation facilitated by the integrated impact of visual and auditory stimuli. This contribution not only enhances the interpretability and efficiency of affective intelligence but also provides new insights and pathways for advancing affective computing technology. Our source code can be accessed here: https://github.com/OpenHUTB/emotion. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. title: The AI-augmented collaborative learning model: A conceptual framework for integrating generative AI in business and management education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) amplifies four tensions in business and management education: the threat to pedagogical coherence, the literacy-to-competency gap, pervasive ethical risks, and the assessment crisis. A first wave of practice-oriented frameworks – including the Human-Centric AI-First (HCAIF) framework and the Leeds Model – offers actionable roadmaps but lacks the theoretical architecture needed to explain the systemic classroom dynamics GenAI introduces. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by developing the AI-Augmented Collaborative Learning (ACL) Model, a second-wave framework organised around three research questions: (RQ1) which theoretical lenses explain the classroom dynamics that generative AI creates in business and management education; (RQ2) how can these be synthesised into an integrated pedagogical framework whose pillars address the four systemic challenges; and (RQ3) how can human-AI collaboration be operationalised as an assessable pedagogical meta-skill. Using Socio-Technical Systems Theory, Activity Theory, Actor-Network Theory, Constructivist and Experiential Learning Theories, and the AI-TPACK framework, the ACL Model specifies four interlocking pillars – Pedagogical Intentionality, Developmental Scaffolding, Ethical Guardrails, and Authentic Assessment. The paper's primary theoretical contribution is to relocate the unit of analysis from the individual student to the student-AI network and to define collaborative intelligence as the resulting meta-competency. A six-proposition validation agenda guides testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Familiar faces, honest answers? The impacts of enumerator familiarity and modality on survey responses
abstract: Survey data can be distorted through mistrust, discomfort, or demand effects on the part of respondents. We test whether familiar enumerators – those with whom a respondent has completed a prior survey – influence data quality in a panel survey with small business owners in Uganda. We randomly assign respondents to a familiar or a new enumerator and cross-cut a second randomization to an in-person or phone-based interview modality. Across a broad set of outcome types, we observe few impacts of either survey method on means, distributions, or attrition. However, respondents are significantly more likely to give norm-congruent answers to new surveyors compared to familiar ones. The effect of familiarity does not interact significantly with a prior experiment conducted with the same sample, suggesting that familiarity influences estimates of levels but not of treatment impacts. These findings suggest that surveys by familiar enumerators can improve the measurement of sensitive beliefs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Polyhydroxy Molecular Regulator Enabled Interfacial Microenvironment Programming for Alkaline Zinc–Iron Flow Batteries
abstract: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (ZIFBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost, intrinsic safety, and scalable architecture, yet their practical deployment remains hindered by hydrogen evolution and uncontrolled Zn deposition in three-dimensional porous electrodes. Here, we report that isomalt acts as a polyhydroxy molecular regulator that reconfigures the interfacial microenvironment of porous carbon felt, thereby endowing the porous electrode with a more deposition-directing function for reversible Zn plating/stripping. In the bulk electrolyte, isomalt reconstructs the local hydrogen-bond network, lowers water activity, and suppresses hydrogen evolution. At the carbon/electrolyte interface, its preferential lateral adsorption establishes a hydroxyl-rich interphase that homogenizes zincate transport and directs Zn growth toward a preferred (002) orientation, thus promoting compact and reversible deposition. This interfacial microenvironment programming markedly reduces the charge-transfer resistance and activation barrier of the Zn anode, enabling stable cycling for over 500 cycles at 20 mA cm−2. In full-cell tests, the optimized ZIFB delivers a high energy efficiency of 87.5%, substantially outperforming the pristine electrolyte. Beyond identifying a low-cost green additive, this work establishes polyhydroxy molecules as interfacial programming units for three-dimensional porous electrodes, offering a new design concept for directional metal deposition in aqueous flow-battery systems. title: The dialectic of the carrot and the stick in the expansion of the extractive frontier in Oaxaca, Mexico
abstract: The expansion of large-scale mining in Mexico since the 1990s has been accompanied by intensifying socio-environmental conflicts, particularly in rural and Indigenous territories. While existing literature has shown that extractive governance frequently combines coercive practices with strategies aimed at securing local legitimacy, this article argues that these mechanisms are mutually constitutive rather than simply simultaneous or complementary. It develops the concept of the dialectic of the carrot and the stick to explain how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and coercion recursively reshape the conditions under which one another operate over the life of an extractive project. The article examines the San José silver and gold mine in Oaxaca, Mexico, operated by Fortuna Silver Mines (FSM). Drawing on qualitative fieldwork conducted between 2023 and 2024, including interviews, field observations, corporate publications, media reports, and civil society sources, it traces extractive governance over more than a decade of conflict. It shows that community programmes and relationships with local institutions produced differentiated and conditional forms of legitimacy, while repression, intimidation, and violence increased the costs of dissent and weakened resistance networks. Coercion thus transformed the terrain on which legitimacy was subsequently cultivated, while persistent limits to legitimacy generated renewed pressures to contain opposition. The dialectic therefore describes a recursive process through which coercion and consent reshape one another, enabling extraction to persist despite sustained opposition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Navigating CSRD compliance: Challenges in sustainability reporting for the real estate sector
abstract: This study aims to investigate the challenges faced by the Norwegian real estate sector in complying with the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), addressing a critical gap in understanding how these regulations impact sustainability reporting practices. The research seeks new insights into the barriers to implementing CSRD-compliant reporting, contributing to a deeper understanding of the sector's readiness and areas requiring improvement. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, utilizing a scoping literature review to map existing knowledge and semi-structured interviews with industry stakeholders to supplement findings. Data were collected from peer-reviewed articles, master's theses, and interviews with key stakeholders, and analyzed using thematic coding and qualitative analysis. The results reveal that the main challenges include limited knowledge of sustainability matters, difficulties in conducting Double Materiality Assessments (DMA), high costs, poor data systems, and administrative burdens. These findings provide evidence that while some companies proactively prepare for CSRD compliance, many, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), struggle due to resource constraints and a reliance on manual processes. This highlights significant implications for improving digital solutions and stakeholder collaboration. This research offers a novel perspective on sustainability reporting in the Norwegian real estate sector, providing valuable insights into the sector's preparedness and key barriers. The study's findings contribute to advancing digital reporting practices and support for SMEs, highlighting areas for future research and potential policy development to ease the transition to CSRD compliance. title: Capacity Degradation Mechanisms, Recovery Strategies, and Challenges of Flow Batteries
abstract: Redox flow batteries, by virtue of their advantages in power/capacity decoupling, high safety, and long cycle life, have become a strategic support for long-duration energy storage systems; however, capacity degradation remains a bottleneck for their commercialization. This review systematically identifies the multi-dimensional mechanisms of capacity degradation: including volume imbalance caused by transmembrane migration, inactivation and decomposition of active species, electrode degradation, and valence imbalance induced by side reactions. Targeting these challenges, the review deeply explores recovery strategies from physical repair to intelligent scheduling: covering the research and development of high-selectivity membranes, precise regulation of valence states, functionalized repair of electrodes, and model-driven predictive pathways integrating digital twins. Finally, current challenges such as characterization limitations and incomplete recovery rates are summarized, and future development directions for capacity recovery are envisioned. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for extending the system cycle life of flow batteries and improving capacity recovery efficiency. title: Beyond compliance: Community development committees and the transformation of resource governance in Tanzania
abstract: Resource-rich countries worldwide often face persistent imbalances in the redistribution of resource wealth. Although mineral extraction generates substantial revenues, these funds are typically centrally managed and redistributed, leaving host communities, who bear the social and environmental burdens of extraction, impoverished and marginalized. In Tanzania, despite provisions allowing Local Government Authorities to levy a 0.3% service charge on mining revenues and receive Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions intended to support local development, means of engaging host communities remain a challenge. Community Development Agreements (CDAs) have been identified as potential instruments to safeguard the interests of host communities. However, despite their widespread promotion, a critical gap remains in understanding how communities can effectively engage in, negotiate, and implement CDAs, particularly in contexts marked by power asymmetries. Communities are often poor, with limited knowledge of mining and the broader extractive industry, and with no access to decision-making power. This study addresses the gap by examining Community Development Committees (CDCs) as an inclusive, participatory institutional mechanism through which communities can effectively articulate their development priorities. Using semi‑structured interviews with 36 key informants across the mining value chain, including central government officials, mining representatives, and local communities, the study finds the CDC model as an effective approach for strengthening community voice, enhancing transparency, improving negotiations, and monitoring project implementations. Although grounded in Tanzania’s mining sector, the study offers insights relevant to other resource dependent economies seeking to foster more equitable social contracts. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Hotspot to Homogeneous: Amorphous Interfacial Current Redistribution Enables Stable Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
abstract: Interfacial instability in oxide ceramic electrolyte (OCE)-based solid-state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) is conventionally attributed to chemical incompatibility or mechanical failure, yet the underlying atomic-scale mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we reveal that grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline OCEs function as bipolar interfacial hotspots, accelerating three degradation pathways: lowering barriers for Li dendrite nucleation and enabling electron-leakage-driven reduction at anode side, while generating localized overpotentials for cathode phase transformation. To deactivate these GB-driven hotspots, we develop a laser-induced amorphization strategy that constructs a GB-free amorphous interlayer capable of homogenizing Li+ flux and blocking electron migration. Applied to a representative sodium superionic conductor-type electrolyte, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3, this approach delivers substantially increased critical current density in Li symmetric cells (1.4 to 2.4 mA cm−2) with stable cycling over 2000 h, and achieves an exceptional capacity retention of 101.9 mAh g−1 after 800 cycles in LiCoO2 full cells operated at 4.5 V. The generality of this strategy is further validated on garnet-type and perovskite-type OCEs. This work introduces amorphous interfacial current redistribution as a universal paradigm for engineering stable interfaces, providing a critical atomic-scale interface engineering route to unlock high-voltage, dendrite-free SSLMBs. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Multicomponent Nitride/High-Entropy Alloy Heterostructures as Highly Active and Stable Electrocatalysts for Ampere-Level Water Oxidation
abstract: Developing highly active and stable oxygen evolution reaction catalysts is paramount for cost-effective large-scale green hydrogen production via water electrolysis. Here we report nonprecious metal-based multicomponent nitride/high-entropy alloy heterostructures as cost-effective electrocatalysts to efficiently mediate alkaline water oxidation by in-situ configurating cooperative Brønsted basic oxyanion-solid interfaces during phase transformation of multicomponent nitride into amorphous N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH along with partial dissolution of high-value metals of Mo and Cr to form molecular MoO42− and CrO42− species. The protonation of Brønsted basic oxyanions facilitates the critical *OOH intermediate formation on N-doped NiFeCoMoCrOOH with near-optimal adsorption energy, substantially accelerating the oxygen evolution reaction kinetics. Consequently, the heterostructure electrode exhibits superior oxygen evolution reaction electrocatalysis in 1 M KOH solution, delivering ultrahigh current density of ~ 2.5 A cm−2 at low overpotential of 300 mV. Its alkaline water electrolyzer operates stably at ampere-level current density for > 1700 h. Our findings reveal an unconventional molecule-assisted multi-site mechanism of multicomponent catalysts to accelerate multiple-intermediate reaction. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Assessing the environmental–economic viability of expressway photovoltaics in China: A spatio–temporal life cycle perspective
abstract: Expressway corridors are increasingly considered for distributed photovoltaic deployment, but their environmental–economic viability depends strongly on local solar resources, infrastructure availability, grid structure, and future decarbonization pathways. This study develops an integrated framework that combines spatio–temporal assessment with environmental life cycle costing to evaluate the deployment potential and comprehensive benefits of expressway photovoltaic systems across 351 prefecture–level cities in China. The assessment covers service areas, rest areas, and expressway slopes under business-as-usual and carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenarios. Results indicate that expressway slopes provide the greatest installation potential, with 49.71% of cities supporting more than 200 MW. At the national-average level, expressway photovoltaic systems yield a net internal benefit of 317.05 USD/kW and a net environmental benefit of 249.48 USD/kW under the business-as-usual scenario. Inverter and monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic module production are the main contributors to environmental costs. Under the carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenario, grid decarbonization reduces the avoided environmental burden of photovoltaic electricity and delays the transition to positive net environmental benefits from 2035 to 2037. These findings support a shift from capacity-oriented expansion to region-specific life cycle planning, prioritizing corridors where solar resources, expressway availability, grid displacement benefits, and recycling infrastructure are jointly favorable. © 2026

title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Drawing on Kolb's experiential learning theory, we carried out a quantitative survey with the use of a structured questionnaire. We collected data from 251 undergraduate students in a UK university and analyzed them using structural equation modeling. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Our findings highlight the potential value of integrating experiential learning tools, such as simulation games, into business education suggesting an association with improvements in students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Theoretical and practical implications for researchers, universities, and practitioners are discussed. © 2026 The Authors

title: Screening out ethics: How technology enables ethical fading in negotiations
abstract: Negotiations are rife with opportunities and temptations to engage in unethical negotiating behavior. Such behavior is not always strategic or even intentional; rather, it can emerge from situational characteristics of the negotiation environment. One psychological process through which situational characteristics influence unethical behavior is ethical fading, a process that limits one's ability to recognize the ethical aspects of the situation and behave in line with one's ethical values. As technologies such as email, video conferencing, and artificial intelligence (AI) become increasingly common in negotiations, an important question is whether these technologies facilitate ethical fading. In this review, we explore the impact that technology and AI have on ethical fading and unethical negotiating behavior. We propose that technology and AI use in negotiations promotes three cognitive processes that facilitate ethical fading: psychological distance, cognitive offloading, and displaced accountability. We review how technology may serve as an antecedent to each of these processes and explain why these processes may facilitate ethical fading in negotiation contexts. Because research on the relationship between technology and unethical negotiating behavior remains limited, we conclude by identifying promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Interface Contact Optimization via Phosphomolybdic Acid Enables 24.9% Efficiency in MoOX-Based Silicon Solar Cells
abstract: The development of cost-effective carrier-selective passivating contacts is critical for enhancing the commercial feasibility of silicon compound solar cells. Molybdenum oxide (MoOX) has garnered considerable interest as a promising hole transport layer (HTLs). A key advantage of MoOX is high work function, in addition to the low-cost processability. However, in silicon photovoltaics, MoOX-based p-type contacts face fundamental limitations at hydrogenated amorphous silicon (i-a-Si:H)/MoOX interface, where oxygen vacancy defects lower work function, as well as, weak van der Waals-dominated interactions impair charge carry transport. To address these challenges, we introduced an ultrathin phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) interlayer at the i-a-Si:H/MoOX interface. In the end, we demonstrated a record efficiency of 24.9% for MoOX-based silicon solar cells, which provides valuable insights for developing high-performance MoOX HTL devices for dopant-free p-type contact technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. This study investigates how security-related perceptions influence tourism support in Northeast India's Seven Sisters region, a politically fragile zone characterized by prolonged insurgency. Using a mixed-method hybrid design, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, sensitivity analysis, and content analysis were applied to 584 stakeholder surveys and 25 in-depth interviews. EFA identified four latent constructs: security forces concern, moral panic, social stability, and cognitive concern, which collectively explain 57% of tourism support variance. ANN modeling revealed a nonlinear inverted-U relationship between security visibility and stakeholder support, interpreted as a “ security-skepticism dilemma” grounded in Prospect Theory. Security forces concern (35%) and moral panic (24%) were the most influential predictors. These findings advance tourism resilience theory and provide actionable governance guidance for conflict-affected destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to design more inclusive and contextually relevant mentorship interventions for women entrepreneurs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Anionic Bottom-Up Flux Orchestrated via Hard Carbon Surface Chemistry for Stable Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries suffer from unstable solid-electrolyte interphase formation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and poor cycle stability. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface. By engineering a synergistic pair of pyridinic-N and carbonyl groups on the carbon surface, we create a functional-differentiation microenvironment where pyridinic-N selectively anchors PF6− anions, while the cooperative carbonyl repels solvent molecules. This dual functionality establishes a sustained concentration gradient that drives a continuous reverse flux of anions toward the interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition pathway from solvent-dominated to anion-preferential. The tailored surface lowers the PF6− decomposition barrier by over 70%, yielding a thin, inorganic-rich solid-electrolyte interphase dominated by NaF and Na2O. The optimized anode achieves 91.9% Coulombic efficiency with high reversible capacity of 368.2 mAh g−1, and 96.5% capacity retention after 5,000 cycles. A pouch cell assembled with NFPP cathode achieves an energy density of 239.1 Wh kg−1 and stable operation over 500 cycles, demonstrating strong practical potential. This work establishes active surface-guided anionic transport as a powerful strategy for interphase engineering in advanced sodium-ion batteries. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Elucidating the Respective Roles of Photochemical and Photothermal Effects in Photocatalytic Methanol Decomposition
abstract: Photocatalytic reactions can be driven by both photochemical and photothermal processes. However, their individual contributions and synergistic effect remain to be clarified. Herein, we investigated the respective roles of these effects using a Cu–TiO2/Ti model catalyst that integrated photochemical and photothermal functionalities within a single photocatalytic system. Employing photocatalytic methanol decomposition as a model reaction, the Cu–TiO2/Ti catalyst achieved a high H2 yield rate of 0.511 mmol h−1 with selectivity of 96.6% toward HCHO among oxidation products, attributed to the cooperative action of photochemical and photothermal processes. In situ resonant Auger electron spectroscopy (RAS), together with in situ Cu K-edge X-ray absorption fine structure and excited-state density functional theory calculations, revealed the accumulation of photogenerated electrons at Cu sites from TiO2, suggests the possible formation of an electron transfer pathway from TiO2 to Cu, which promotes stepwise methanol dehydrogenation to HCHO and H2. Simultaneously, the photothermal contribution from Ti enhanced catalytic activity by accelerating reaction kinetics and promoting the desorption of HCHO, thereby suppressing its overoxidation to CO. (Figure presented.) © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
abstract: Generative AI tools can now create photorealistic destination images at low cost, yet whether such images motivate travel as effectively as human-generated images remains unclear. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, this research examines differences between AI-generated and human-generated tourism images through three studies. Study 1 shows that AI-generated images receive higher ratings of perceived aesthetics but lower ratings of perceived authenticity, narrative transportation, and visit intention than human-generated images. Study 2 identifies 19 computable visual indicators across three dimensions and finds that AI-generated images exhibit stronger visual schema characteristics, whereas human-generated images show richer visual structure. Study 3 uses XGBoost and SHAP analysis to identify the visual features associated with different psychological responses. These findings connect computational visual analysis with tourism consumer research by identifying differences in audience responses to AI-generated and human-generated images and the visual features associated with those responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Component-aware topology-guided task release and collision-free bimanual scheduling for cooperative disassembly of retired EV battery packs
abstract: Retired EV battery-pack disassembly requires robots to handle fastening dependencies, occlusion, tool compatibility, and inter-arm collisions in a compact workspace. title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. After generating each idea, participants reported their feelings of ease and evaluated the creativity of each idea. Participants then reported their confidence in the ideas generated and selected their most creative idea. Results showed negative, curvilinear trajectories of feelings of ease and self-evaluations of the creativity of each idea. Feelings of ease in generating ideas were positively related to self-evaluations and the decisions to continue generating ideas and negatively related to choosing the first idea as the most creative. In addition, feelings of ease were indirectly and positively related to post-task confidence through their relationship with self-evaluations. These findings provided initial, empirical evidence that feelings of ease acted as cues to inform relevant judgments and decisions in the process of ideation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. Although established procedures guide the process, diversions remain complex and time-sensitive due to operational and logistical constraints, and there is no universal framework for selecting the most suitable alternate airport. This paper proposes a decision support system to assist diversion decision-making through a modified data envelopment analysis–slack-based measure (DEA-SBM) efficiency-based proxy model. The model evaluates the efficiency-based diversion risk proxy (EDRP) index for airports using relevant input and output variables associated with the diversion process. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. The resulting model outputs are consistent with the actual diversion decisions implemented in operational practice. This alignment provides empirical support that the model can function as a reliable decision support tool for diversion management, particularly in replicating observed operational judgment under real-world constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Energy management systems for hybrid AC/DC microgrids: a problem-oriented review of system challenges and control architectures
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources introduces several system-level challenges for hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs), including power coordination, voltage regulation, uncertainty management, load–demand balancing, and energy storage coordination. Energy management systems (EMS) play a key role in addressing these challenges and ensuring reliable and efficient MG operation. Existing review studies mainly focus on methods and optimization techniques, while system challenges are not always clearly identified or examined from a structured perspective. This paper reviews studies that support system design and the mitigation of operational challenges and presents a comprehensive classification of MGs and EMS. Review and research studies are compiled in separate tables and categorized according to system challenges and the applied EMS approaches. System challenges are identified and related to the control layers responsible for addressing them across primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The proposed classification explicitly covers rule-based, method-based, and objective-based EMS strategies and presents a multi-dimensional framework that links system challenges, control structures, and energy management approaches. The resulting framework provides a consolidated and problem-oriented perspective and supports future research toward the development and evaluation of effective energy management solutions for hybrid AC/DC MGs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data from 168 students using validated measures, and Latent Profile Analysis identified naturally occurring learning profiles. Four distinct learning configurations emerged: Low Learning Orientation (10.1%), Developing Learning Orientation (11.9%), Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation (31.0%), and Integrated Learning Configuration (47.0%). The Integrated Learning Configuration represented the largest group. Notably, the Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation profile reflected students with stronger task value and effort regulation relative to critical thinking. This finding suggests that valuing learning and regulating effort alone may be insufficient for developing higher-order financial reasoning. Profile membership differed by programme of study but not by sex or age. The study advances management education by conceptualising learning in Financial Management as an integrated configuration of motivational, behavioural, and cognitive dimensions rather than isolated learner characteristics, informing pedagogical connoisseurship in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. We show that it outperforms popular literature benchmarks in terms of forecast accuracy by up to 10%. We also propose two simplified variants of the method, granting a vast decrease in computation time with only minor loss of prediction accuracy. Finally, we compare the forecasts’ performance in a battery storage system trading case study and propose a new automated trading strategy. We find that using a forecast-driven strategy can consistently achieve a substantial share of theoretical maximum profits while trading, demonstrating business value in practical applications. © 2026

title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. Gender representation was investigated using the framework proposed by Dahmardeh and Kim (2020), and the scale developed by Solhaug and Kristensen (2020) was used as the criteria for investigating intercultural competence. The data were coded and counted using manifest content analysis. The results showed that Iranian English coursebooks mentioned males and females unequally in their texts across different decades, with one gender being represented more in each decade. Regarding gender representation in the images, males were represented more than females in almost all decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. In fact, the coursebooks addressed only one category out of the 11 categories. Finally, the study ends with implications for coursebook authors, materials designers, teachers, students, and teacher trainers. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. In fragile settings, such education should cultivate reflective attitudes and moral engagement alongside structural reforms that enable normative support for socially oriented careers. © 2026

abstract: This study focuses on the production of sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker using local raw materials found in the Aral Sea region of the Republic of Uzbekistan and on its properties. The obtained results highlight the technological, economic, and environmental advantages. The raw material mixtures consisted of limestone, barren sand, kaolin, and iron-containing industrial waste, resulting in a clinker with an optimized oxide composition (LSF = 0.82, SR = 2.15, AP = 0.94). X-ray phase analysis reveals a high content of alite (C3S ≈ 38.6%) and belite (C2S ≈ 41.0%) phases, which ensures high mechanical strength. Low tricalcium aluminate content (tricalcium aluminate < 5%) and sufficient ferrite content (C4AF ≈ 16.2%) increased sulfate resistance and phase dominance. Sulfate resistance tests conducted in accordance with ASTM C1012/C1012M showed that sulfate-resistant Portland cement had the lowest swelling index among samples immersed in a 5% Na2SO4 solution, demonstrating its superior stability compared to conventional Portland cement and mixed cement types. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of producing high-quality sulfate-resistant Portland cement clinker using local raw materials and demonstrate its potential for use in the sulfate-rich conditions of the Aral Sea region. From an economic perspective, the use of local raw materials reduces production costs, the need for imports, and increases the competitiveness of the cement industry in our region. From an environmental perspective, the long service life of sulfate-resistant Portland cement and the ability to utilize industrial waste align with the principles of a "green economy" and promote waste reduction and sustainable growth. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants
abstract: Research indicates that the fashion industry can be made more environmentally friendly by introducing a closed-loop economy – also known as a circular economy – and implementing sustainable business models in areas such as clothing resale, rental, repair, and remake. Secondhand clothing is the sector to which research attributes the greatest potential for success in introducing new sustainable business models. This study examines the secondhand subscription box and eleven potential determinants from the secondhand fashion consumption literature. It complements a constraint-based approach (Necessary Condition Analysis – NCA) with an effect-based approach (regression analysis) to identify the necessary-but-not-sufficient conditions and the key (regression) factors shaping purchase intention. Using a sample of 215 German participants, we found that most determinants are necessity-based bottlenecks. They must be present and reach a certain threshold. Some are also key factors that drive purchase intention. The relevance of the determinants varies across sub-groups. This has implications for both academia and practice in designing secondhand subscription boxes. However, the study reveals that the determinants are context-dependent and no general principle can be transferred to other circular economy or sustainable consumption contexts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Screen-Printed Li Arrays with Reinforced Interphase as Ultrathin Anodes for High-Energy–Density Liquid- and Solid-State Batteries
abstract: High-energy–density lithium metal batteries, either liquid or solid state, require ultrathin Li anodes, but their implementation is hindered by poor Li processability in fabrication and inhomogeneous Li plating behaviours upon cycling. This work addresses these challenges through a mask-patterned discrete array using a molten salt-derived Li nanocomposite. The screen-printing strategy circumvents the poor wettability of molten Li on copper that causes high Li|Cu contact angle and non-uniform Li spreading, thus fabricating ultrathin Li foils with equivalent thicknesses below 30 μm. Concurrently, the molten salt-derived inorganic nanoparticles in Li favour homogeneous Li deposition and induce inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase to jointly suppress active Li consumption. The resulting Li array (10–28 μm) anodes demonstrate remarkable performance in both liquid- and solid-state systems, achieving high energy densities up to 504 Wh kg−1/1071 Wh L−1 and stable cycling over 260 cycles with high-loading cathodes. This integrated approach resolves both fabrication and cycling challenges of ultrathin Li anodes and offers an alternative solution for high-performance liquid-/solid-state batteries. title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). title: Registered Report Stage I: Signaling green, securing greenbacks: Sustainability claims and venture funding in hospitality & tourism start-ups
abstract: Tourism's sustainable transition increasingly depends on startups capable of scaling credible innovations. Yet to lead this transformation, they must convince investors that sustainability claims reflect genuine commitment rather than symbolism. This study tests whether, and under what conditions, startups' sustainability communication on X (Twitter) attracts external funding. Integrating signaling and legitimacy theory, we argue that costly, externally validated messages (e.g., stakeholder collaborations or investment-backed actions) enhance pragmatic legitimacy and capital inflow. Analyzing 3869 startups across 94 countries, we link few-shot-classified social-media posts with Crunchbase funding data using a multilevel hurdle model. The study positions startups as the vanguard of tourism's sustainable future, introduces investor funding as an outcome of sustainability communication, and demonstrates a scalable machine-learning approach for field-wide analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The adopter's conundrum: Institutional drivers and performance outcomes of innovation in travel distribution
abstract: This paper investigates the link between institutionally driven innovation and firm performance within the travel distribution sector. Focusing on the adoption of the New Distribution Capability (NDC), we employ a Difference-in-Differences (DID) methodology on a proprietary dataset of travel agency sales spanning four years. The results provide causal evidence that adoption leads to improved sales performance. Moreover, we identify a clear premium for early adoption, with dynamic effects accelerating over time, indicating that firms faster to adopt obtain superior results. The study contributes to the literature by validating the economic benefits of technological innovation using objective market data rather than subjective measures, offering key insights for managers navigating industry-wide technological shifts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. By leveraging large language models to quantify complex external influences and semantic relationships, this framework provides a new perspective for improving the accuracy and interpretability of tourism flow forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. We conducted a scoping review of 68 studies (2010–2025) using a structured screening and synthesis process. Findings show that migration results from interacting economic, infrastructural, geographical, policy, and social pressures rather than a single employment factor, with reinforcing feedback effects such as land abandonment, declining agricultural viability, weakened local services, and heightened human-wildlife conflict that can intensify future migration. The study synthesizes an evidence-graded portfolio of interventions: livelihood diversification, agri-value-chain strengthening, digital access and skills, climate-resilient infrastructure, community-based and eco-tourism, and improved local service delivery and governance support, contributing an integrated conceptual framework linking drivers, feedback loops, and intervention levers for coordinated, place-based mountain-region planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Inside and out: Exploring how internal and external CSR perceptions influence hospitality employees’ service sabotage
abstract: Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been shown to exert positive effects on hospitality organizations and their stakeholders, the interactive effect of internal CSR (ICSR) and external CSR (ECSR) perceptions on employees’ subsequent service behaviors remains unclear. Drawing on social cognitive theory and cue consistency theory, this study aims to explore how the interaction between ICSR and ECSR perceptions influences employees’ service sabotage. Time-lagged data were collected from 366 hotel employees at two time points and analyzed using hierarchical regression. The results indicate that the ICSR × ECSR interaction has a significant effect on employee service sabotage. Specifically, ECSR perceptions suppress service sabotage only when ICSR perceptions are high. This relationship is mediated by perspective taking. Furthermore, corporate reputational identification strengthens the negative effect of perspective taking on service sabotage. This study offers valuable insights for CSR practices in the hospitality industry and points to promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Renewable electricity penetration and retail price dynamics: Global evidence on transitional costs of the energy transition
abstract: The global expansion of renewable energy represents a structural transformation with profound macroeconomic and financial implications. This study investigates the impact of renewable electricity penetration on retail electricity prices using a multi-country panel. The study employs a comprehensive multi-layered empirical framework to address endogeneity, dynamic adjustment, and cross-country structural heterogeneity. The results reveal that renewable penetration is associated with statistically significant short-to medium-term increases in residential electricity prices. However, this effect is nonlinear and conditional on fossil fuel dependence. Once fossil reliance falls below a critical threshold, the marginal price impact weakens substantially. Distributional evidence shows that renewable price effects are amplified in high-price electricity markets. These findings suggest that renewable expansion generates transitional system costs rather than permanent inefficiencies, highlighting the importance of structural conditions in shaping energy transition outcomes and broader economic stability. © 2026 The Authors. title: The impact of technological developments on the changing role of HR(M): A scoping review and research agenda
abstract: Due to technological developments, jobs disappear, new jobs arise, and existing jobs change. This leads to opportunities and challenges regarding human resource management (HRM) and the role of the HR function in the future of work. In this article, we explore how technological developments such as the use of smart technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotics influence HRM and the role of the HR function. Through a scoping review, we highlight the influence of technological developments across macro (societal), meso (organization/HRM) and micro (individual workers) level work themes. We specifically focus on the dynamic interplay between technological developments and HRM. At the meso level, the analysis zooms in on how technological developments influence HRM at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels within organizational contexts. Our findings inform a future research agenda comprising avenues aimed at deepening our understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with technological change in the context of HRM. More specifically, we propose future research to explore how the HR function can prepare the organization, itself, and other stakeholders, including line managers and workers, for the impact of technological developments to enhance HRM for the greater good. title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures
abstract: Online retail platforms are increasingly mediating customer–vendor interactions, yet research offers limited insight into how platform governance shapes service failure attribution, especially after recurring failures. Drawing on attribution theory, this paper examines how centralized versus diffused governance structures influence consumers’ attribution of causality to the platform after service failure and their responses to recurring failures. Study 1 analyzes customer reviews using computational text analysis and shows that customers recognize governance structures and attribute causality to the platform more often under centralized than diffused governance. Employing scenario-based experiments, Study 2 demonstrates that centralized (vs. diffused) governance leads to higher failure attribution to the platform. Finally, we show that attribution following single and recurring failures serially mediates the relationship between governance structure and repurchase intention after a recurring failure. Importantly, platform attribution exerts opposite effects across failure episodes: following a single failure and successful recovery, greater platform attribution increases repurchase intention by signaling platform accountability and resolution capability. However, following a recurring failure, greater platform attribution decreases repurchase intention because recurrence signals a stable, persistent cause and reduces attributional uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Hemisphere-aware Graph Convolution and 3D Structural Fusion for multi-modal fMRI brain-disorder classification
abstract: Multimodal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data is a valuable source of information for precisely classifying neurological disorders, which is why it is widely used in the diagnosis of these diseases. However, traditional methods struggle to capture the spatiotemporal dynamics of the brain and single-modality approaches overlook voxel-level structural information. This limits the accuracy of imaging diagnoses of neurological diseases. This study therefore selected resting-state fMRI samples from the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ABIDE) and Parkinson's Disease (PPMI) datasets, proposing the multi-modal half-brain perception framework MSHAGL. This comprises a shared-weight half-brain–whole-brain graph convolutional network (CHW-GCN) and a three-dimensional structure encoder (GBConvNet3D). These are combined with multi-head gated fusion and redundancy suppression loss for joint optimization. Specifically, dynamic maps of the left and right hemispheres and the whole brain are constructed, cross-scale functional connectivity features are extracted, and 3D fMRI volumes are utilized to capture spatial structural patterns. Gating mechanisms achieve dynamic alignment and weighted fusion of temporal-structural features. title: Developing a cyber-resilience framework for UAVs: insights from expert interviews on addressing cybersecurity challenges
abstract: Rapid technological advances have greatly enhanced the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their potential for beneficial uses. Such uses, however, have been limited by cybersecurity concerns. Despite considerable research attention, threat levels are increasing, and this is likely to further inhibit UAV use. A different approach is therefore required, one that marks a change from reactive mitigation to proactive prevention. This study proposes a holistic cyber-resilience framework for UAVs based on five resilience features, which are redundancy, flexibility, modularity, diversity, and tightness of feedback loops. Such a change, called for by several authors but yet to be achieved, can come through the components of a framework that are supported by expert perspectives. The study employs a mixed-methods design with in-person interviews of 32 expert professionals across eight sectors (aviation, military, security, insurance, aerospace, cybersecurity, logistics, and academia). A total of 261 vulnerabilities ranging across five threat categories are identified, with those related to communication facilitating a point of entry for cascading attacks. Drawing on expert evaluations of five resilience features, the novelty of this study is its proposed lifecycle-based framework that shifts UAV security from mitigation to embedded resilience. Practical trade-offs that include weight, power and relative costs as well as the position of the framework in relation to existing standards such as NIST CSF and MITRE frameworks are discussed. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Dynamic Diffusion of Legal Compliance and Ethical Conduct among Construction Project Owners: An Epidemiological Modeling Approach
abstract: Construction industries worldwide face persistent challenges of ethical misconduct, contractual violations, and regulatory noncompliance, imposing substantial legal liabilities and undermining sustainable development. Although legal frameworks exist to govern owner behavior, their dynamic enforcement effects and interactions with market-driven compliance mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study pioneers the application of epidemiological modeling to legal compliance and ethical behavior diffusion among construction project owners. An extended susceptible-exposed-infected-removed (SEIR) model was developed to analyze how statutory enforcement and voluntary market adoption jointly drive compliance diffusion, simulated via MATLAB. Three findings emerged: (1) the diffusion of ethical behavior exhibits S-shaped evolution with global asymptotic stability, providing a predictable basis for legal intervention design; (2) resistance parameters demonstrate positional asymmetry, revealing where legal safeguards are most needed; and (3) government-mandated enforcement and voluntary adoption generate superlinear synergistic effects, suggesting compliance frameworks achieve maximum efficacy when paired with market incentives. These findings offer quantitative decision support for policymakers and legal practitioners designing effective governance instruments. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: How to deal with AI technology anxiety and its negative consequences? The role of strengths-based leadership
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into hospitality operations, employees’ AI technology anxiety has emerged as a salient managerial concern. Drawing on social information processing theory, this study examines the effect of strengths-based leadership on AI technology anxiety and the subsequent influence of this anxiety on employees’ social loafing behavior. Across a time-lagged field study and an experiment, the findings reveal the following key results. First, strengths-based leadership effectively alleviated hospitality employees’ AI technology anxiety, thereby reducing their social loafing behavior. Second, job automation weakened the negative effect of strengths-based leadership on AI technology anxiety. In turn, the indirect effect of strengths-based leadership on social loafing behavior through AI technology anxiety was also attenuated under high levels of job automation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Explainable spatiotemporal modeling in crime analytics: Robbery prediction via graph neural networks
abstract: Urban crime prediction is a critical task for ensuring public safety, yet it faces challenges related to model accuracy and transparency. While crime is an inherently temporal phenomenon, its embedding within the city’s structure suggests that integrating spatiotemporal dependencies via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can improve model robustness, particularly in data-sparse environments. Traditional grid-based methods often fail to capture the complex network topology of cities, while the “black-box” nature of advanced models raises ethical concerns for predictive policing. This study proposes an explainable spatiotemporal framework to predict robbery risk by uniquely integrating three elements: (1) fine-grained, citizen-sensed data from a public safety application in Santiago, Chile; (2) a tailored graph neural network to learn how to represent the urban environment as a graph; and (3) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) component using Integrated Gradients to ensure transparency. We evaluate the model’s performance against traditional classifiers across various prediction horizons (1, 3, and 7 days) and spatial granularities. The results show that the tailored architecture dramatically improves predictive accuracy (average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve -AUC- ≈ 0.85) compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, the XAI analysis provides novel empirical evidence that citizen reports of “suspicious activity” are highly significant predictors of future burglaries, often more so than prior robbery incidents themselves. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
