title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)
abstract: Despite well-documented health and environmental benefits, increasing plant-based meal consumption remains challenging in meat-centric societies, reflecting complex socio-cognitive processes in translating intention into action. Grounded in the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA), this study examined plant-based meal consumption among young adults from the USA, Portugal, and the Netherlands who had not fully adopted a plant-based diet (N = 266). Using two waves one week apart, we estimated three structural models of plant-based meal consumption, controlling for prior behavior and common method variance. Findings were broadly consistent with HAPA. Action self-efficacy was most strongly associated with intention, which in turn was associated with action planning. Coping planning and self-monitoring pathways were not supported. While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. The findings highlight this volitional process in translating motivation into action and suggest interventions may benefit from strengthening efficacy beliefs and concrete planning strategies to support plant-based dietary change. © 2026

title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effect of China's 2020 digital transformation policy for state-owned enterprises on the production efficiency of listed electric enterprises. Treating the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model to measure production efficiency and a difference-in-differences model to examine the policy effect. The results show that the policy significantly improves the production efficiency of state-owned electric enterprises relative to non-state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects among utilities in eastern China, labor-intensive firms, and large firms. Mechanism analysis further shows that increased R&D investment is an important channel through which the policy generates efficiency gains, while managerial equity incentives strengthen policy effectiveness. The findings provide policy implications for utility digitalization, differentiated policy support, innovation incentives, and governance reform. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Under a common financing rule, two child-targeted policies raise the co-migration rate to a similar extent but differ sharply in welfare and mobility. Subsidizing co-migrating families in high-cost destinations generates 1.4 times as much welfare per unit of government revenue as removing migrant children's education-access wedges. These gains concentrate on recipients. Removing the education-access wedges delivers over four times the mobility gain per unit of revenue, and the resulting human capital generates growing welfare gains across generations. A broader reform that equalizes public-service access for all migrants is the most welfare-efficient but does not raise mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Transformative leadership models and styles to improve the quality and development of Muhammadiyah school education in Blora Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to investigate models and leadership styles that are effective in improving the quality of education in Muhammadiyah Schools in Blora, Indonesia. The research method used is a case study with a focus on qualitative data analysis, including interviews, observations, and analysis of related documents. This research identifies various leadership models that have been applied in Muhammadiyah Schools, including transformational, transactional, and participatory leadership. In addition, this study explores stakeholder preferences and perceptions of the most effective leadership styles in the context of Islamic education in the Muhammadiyah school environment in Blora. The results showed that transformational leadership models and styles play a key role in designing strategic vision and driving educational innovation in Muhammadiyah Schools. The implementation of transactional and participatory strategies has also proven important in day-to-day management and consensus-based decision-making. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for policymakers and education leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools, to optimize leadership strategies to improve the quality of Islamic education in Blora. The novelty of this study lies in the identification of a combination of transformational and participatory leadership as an optimal leadership model in the context of Islamic education. This research also adds a new perspective on stakeholder preferences in the implementation of leadership styles in Muhammadiyah schools. The implication of this study is the need for educational leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools to consider the application of a combination of flexible and innovative leadership models, in order to achieve continuous improvement in the quality of Islamic education. This can be a reference for policymakers to formulate more effective leadership strategies in facing future educational challenges. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: How can hotels strategically enhance competitive performance? Investigating the dynamic roles and impacts of service attributes on customer satisfaction and dissatisfaction
abstract: This study examines the asymmetric impact of service attributes on customer satisfaction (CS) and dissatisfaction (DS) in the luxury and upper upscale hotel segments, utilizing Impact Asymmetry Analysis and Impact Asymmetry Competitor Analysis. Grounded by the two-factor theory, this study integrates insights from online review ratings and textual sentiment to gauge customer evaluations. The findings reveal that attributes have discrete impacts on CS and DS when comparing high and low performance consistency brands. Hotels exhibiting low performance consistency are advised to prioritize managing attributes such as rooms, followed by value and cleanliness in rating-based evaluations. Additionally, location is identified as a key competitive disadvantage requiring urgent action in sentiment-based assessments. This study extends the understanding of the two-factor theory by examining the distinct impacts of attributes on CS and DS under varying performance consistency, providing actionable insights for hoteliers to strategically enhance attribute-level performance that strengthens customer experience and competitive standing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). To address this deficiency, this study, conducted in the Republic of Ireland, adopts a sequential research design in which expert workshops and focus groups were used to develop a nationally representative discrete choice survey (n = 970) to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for environmental improvements and to enhance the effectiveness, legitimacy, and practical uptake of SEA. Our findings reveal strong public support for planning scenarios that include greater public participation, substantial increases in local green space (10–30%), and acceptance of short procedural delays (1–2 years) in SEA processes to ensure comprehensive environmental assessment. Model estimates indicate that respondents expressed a WTP of approximately €48–€63 per year for a 30% increase in green space, with the lower estimate derived from the multinomial logit (MNL) model and the higher estimate from the random parameters logit (RPL) model. Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. The study presents a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem service valuation and measurable forms of public participation into SEA processes to support more effective and legitimate environmental decision-making. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Fixed or flexible: How product formats affect consumer redemption behavior for live-streamed food and beverage (F&B) products
abstract: With the rapid growth of live-streaming e-commerce in the food and beverage industry, low redemption rates despite high sales volumes have become a critical challenge for merchants. This research investigates how product formats and familiarity affect consumer redemption behavior and identifies the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions. Through five studies using one archival-data study, three scenario-based experiments, and one field experiment, we find that: product formats and familiarity interact significantly: set meals yield higher redemption under low familiarity, while vouchers perform better under high familiarity. This relationship is mediated through a dual-pathway mechanism: at low levels of familiarity, a loss-avoidance pathway prevails through perceived risk, whereas at high levels of familiarity, a gain-seeking pathway dominates through perceived preference fit. Purchase type further moderates this interaction, such that the effect emerges only under impulse purchase conditions. title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Trust patterns in food chain actors in the European region over a six-year period (2019-2024): an exploratory analysis
abstract: We analyse consumer trust in food chain actors, both commercial and authorities, in 12 European countries and Israel over a period of 6 years, including the years of the Covid-19 pandemic, based on data from the EIT Food TrustTracker® yearly data collection. While we find considerable differences in consumer trust between countries, an analysis over time shows that trust levels have been remarkably stable. However, in some countries there was a change in trust level during the Covid-19 years. In some countries, trust in commercial actors increased slightly during Covid-19, and stayed at this higher level after the pandemic. Also, trust in authorities increased slightly in some countries during Covid-19, but mostly regressed to pre-Covid levels afterwards. These changes are interpreted in terms of disruptions in the food supply chain during Covid-19 and their perception by consumers, and in terms of governmental reactions to the pandemic. © 2026 The Authors

title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Yet, the literature remains overwhelmingly anchored to a unidimensional metric: review helpfulness. Challenging this utilitarian bias, this study establishes a dual-value evaluative paradigm that encompasses both diagnostic helpfulness and enjoyment to decode peer evaluations of hedonic digital product reviews. Grounded in processing fluency theory, we investigate how cognitive stimuli (product informativeness) and affective stimuli (emotional richness) synergistically yet distinctly drive these dual dimensions. Leveraging a dataset of 12,823 reviews from Steam, we deploy a rigorous methodological triangulation: extracting deep semantic features via Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VADER sentiment analysis, estimating causal mechanisms via Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) regressions, and validating predictive robustness using Random Forest algorithms. The empirical findings reveal that review breadth and thematic distribution divergence concurrently enhance both outcomes. Review thematic density exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship across both dimensions. While the negative sentiment rate enhances utilitarian risk-mitigation but severely disrupts hedonic gratification. The study advances eWOM literature by establishing a dual-value evaluative paradigm, providing actionable guidelines for digital platforms to optimize content distribution for review helpfulness and enjoyment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness
abstract: Political activism is commonly conceptualized as a form of collective action that promotes individual empowerment, collective efficacy, and societal well-being. However, this research demonstrates that activism focused on the pursuit of a collective goal can also have paradoxical consequences by increasing subsequent indulgent preferences. Drawing on moral licensing theory, when high-effort, in-person activism is grounded in moral conviction, actors may interpret their effortful involvement as a morally meaningful contribution to a collective cause, enhancing a sense of perceived moral contribution, which heightens perceived deservingness and, in turn, indulgence. Across four experimental studies (n = 852) in emerging and developed economies, the results highlight that participants exposed to high-effort, in-person activism scenarios subsequently demonstrated higher levels of indulgence than those in low-effort online actions or the control condition. These effects are moderated by consumer type in emerging markets, with the effect of high-effort activism on indulgence being stronger among bottom-of-the-pyramid (BOP) consumers. Our findings caution advocacy organizations against assuming that effortful civic participation consistently reinforces prosocial behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. .

title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mapping the research landscape of generative artificial intelligence in education with implications for teacher education: A bibliometric analysis
abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models, has significantly transformed educational research and practice, resulting in a rapidly expanding yet fragmented body of literature. This study aims to systematically map the research landscape of GenAI in education and examine its implications for teacher education through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 16,250 documents published from 2021 to 2025 were analyzed through performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship network analysis, and citation analysis to capture the structural and intellectual development of the field. The findings reveal a sharp increase in publication output beginning in 2023, indicating a transition from an emergent to a high-growth phase of research development. Research productivity and scholarly influence are concentrated among a limited group of authors, institutions, and countries, particularly the United States and China, reflecting uneven global participation. Collaboration networks exhibit a multi-clustered structure, suggesting active yet fragmented research communities with limited cross-group integration. Citation patterns indicate that a small number of recent publications exert strong influence and serve as foundational references in the field. Thematic analysis further identifies three dominant and interconnected areas: core technological developments, educational applications, and domain-specific implementations, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of GenAI in education. The field is expanding rapidly but remains structurally fragmented and is still undergoing intellectual consolidation. These findings emphasize the need for more cohesive research efforts, stronger international collaboration, and greater integration across thematic domains. Implications for teacher education include the integration of AI-related competencies into pre-service programs, the adoption of pedagogically grounded and context-sensitive approaches, and the provision of continuous professional development to support teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Techno-economic study and sensitivity analysis- benefits of complex petrochemical waste refining
abstract: For the petrochemical industry to maintain resource sustainability, complex waste must be treated effectively. In the previous work, the Aspen Hysys V12.0 modeling tool was used to analyze the regeneration of water, aromatics (BTX), and glycols (MEG, DEG, and TEG) from petrochemical effluent and the operating parameters were validated with experimental study. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of an integrated petrochemical wastewater treatment system with resource recovery. The process enables recovery of water (7.8 MM kg/year), aromatics such as benzene and toluene (468,000 kg/year each), and glycols (over 16.5 MM kg/year). The total capital investment is estimated at $42.4 MM, with annual operating costs of $8.46 MM and revenue of $18 MM. The system achieves a net present value (NPV) of $31.8 MM, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 19.9%, and a payback period of 4.87 years. Sensitivity analysis identified product price and electricity cost as key economic drivers. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) showed a 95% probability of positive NPV, indicating robust performance under uncertainty. The carbon footprint is estimated at 11,970 tons CO2/year (0.12 kg CO2/kg treated), representing an 87% reduction compared to conventional systems. Carbon pricing further enhances economic viability. The novelty of this work lies in integrating techno-economic analysis, uncertainty quantification, carbon footprint evaluation, and circular economy principles into a unified framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed system is a sustainable and economically viable solution for petrochemical wastewater management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Turning climate concern into climate courage: Female parliamentarians, environmental taxation and SDG13
abstract: Environmental issues, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and air pollution, have received heightened international attention following the adoption of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which aim to promote global sustainable development. The presence of women in parliament has proven to be highly effective in advancing environmental tax policies that help reduce vulnerability to climate change. Using panel data from G20 and N11 economies between 2002 and 2022, this study provides evidence that women's presence in parliament is a critical determinant of achieving environmental sustainability. The models' results show that female parliamentarians with significant representation are more effective, and they reach the ‘Climate Action’ goal by reducing CO2 and GHG emissions, among other environmental targets. Notably, the country's ecological achievements can be intensified by implementing more efficient environmental taxation policies. We mitigate endogeneity by using Lewbel-IV and GMM estimation. Moreover, this study also highlights the significance of this relationship when the government invests more in renewable energy, emits less CO2, has a significant forest reserve, and offers better employment opportunities. © 2026 The Authors. title: From growth mindset to social-emotional skills in early and mid-adolescence: A educational-cultural examination of an integrated mind-body-behavior framework
abstract: Background: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is a core educational goal, yet little is known about how adolescents’ cognitive beliefs, body-related self-perceptions, and everyday health behavior jointly relate to social-emotional skills across diverse cultural contexts and school stages. Objective: Based on mindset theory and self-regulation perspectives, we examined an integrated Mind-Body-Behavior framework in which growth mindset, positive body image, and health behavior show a theoretically specified pattern of associated with adolescents’ social-emotional skills. Sample: Participants were 62,105 adolescents from 15 regions where data were drawn from the OECD 2023 Study on Social and Emotional Skills. Methods: A two-stage quantitative design combined structural equation modeling and machine learning. Results: Growth mindset was associated with social-emotional skills both directly and indirectly associations via body image and health behavior. The direct association was substantially stronger than the combined indirect associations, indicating partial rather than complete support for the full proposed pattern. Scalar invariance across the seven clusters was not supported, so cluster-level comparisons were treated as descriptive. Associations differed between cohorts: the association between growth mindset and body image was stronger in the younger cohort, whereas the association between health behavior and social-emotional skills was stronger in the older cohort. Conclusions: The study contributes an integrated view of how beliefs, body-related self-perception, and health behavior relate to social-emotional skills. The framework shows that cognitive, body-related, and behavioral domains each relate to adolescents’ social-emotional skills and that these relations change between school stages. © 2026 The Authors

title: A probabilistic model for situation awareness reliability assessment in uncertain environments
abstract: Human error remains a major contributor to accidents in safety-critical systems, partly because operators may fail to establish effective situation awareness (SA) within critical time windows. Existing approaches to situation awareness reliability (SAR) often use SAGAT scores directly as reliability measures, conflating observed single-trial performance with the probability of successful SA formation under repeated conditions. They also lack a unified probabilistic framework integrating individual cognitive ability, task uncertainty, and available time. To address these limitations, this study applies the stress-strength interference principle from reliability engineering and models SA formation as a stochastic competition between cognitive strength and cognitive demand. A closed-form SAR expression with interpretable parameters is derived, forming the SAR-SSI model. The model was evaluated in a controlled experiment involving 29 participants and 1740 trials. Trial-level AUCs were 0.8032 for the full-sample fit and 0.8011 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, indicating similar discrimination for held-out participants within the same experimental paradigm. Higher values of the task-related indicator C and longer available time were associated with higher SAR, whereas greater task uncertainty was associated with lower SAR and attenuated these relationships. The SAR-SSI model provides an interpretable probability-based tool for comparing how alternative information-presentation and task configurations may affect the likelihood of successful SA formation in controlled dynamic tasks. title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. These findings extend sustainable-consumption research by identifying population composition as a social-environmental condition relevant to men's green product evaluations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. This gap highlights the need to better understand the factors that influence individuals’ willingness to adopt digital channels for charitable giving. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence individuals’ intentions to contribute to cash waqf via digital platforms by employing the Technology Readiness framework. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. The findings provide practical implications for waqf institutions and policymakers to design strategies that reduce technological barriers while strengthening moral and religious motivations, thereby encouraging wider adoption of digital cash waqf platforms, particularly in developing countries with similar socio-economic environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm
abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from 544 luxury fashion consumers and were analysed using Hayes' PROCESS Model 15. Both brand experience and brand mystery were positively associated with brand attachment. Brand attachment was also positively associated with CBBE and significantly mediated the indirect associations between experiential and symbolic brand resources and CBBE. Furthermore, subjective norm moderately weakens the positive relationship between brand attachment and CBBE, indicating that while subjective norm weakens the relationship between emotional attachment and consumers' evaluations of luxury fashion brands, it does not replace it. This study advances luxury branding research by showing how an identity-based relational mechanism is associated with broader CBBE, with experiential encounters and symbolic meanings relating to brand equity through emotional attachment. By integrating Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour within a unified framework, the study shows that experiential and symbolic brand resources are associated with luxury brand equity through complementary relational pathways. © 2026

title: Descriptive or injunctive? The interactive effects of influencer type and social norms on alternative protein purchase intention
abstract: As alternative protein products attract increasing attention, understanding how social norm messages and influencer type jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention has become increasingly relevant. Drawing on schema congruity theory, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments with Chinese panel participants. The studies manipulated influencer type (human vs. virtual) and social norm framing (descriptive vs. injunctive), with regulatory-mode message priming introduced in Study 3. The results showed significant interactions between influencer type and norm framing. In Study 1, human influencers elicited higher purchase intention than virtual influencers under injunctive framing, whereas virtual influencers elicited higher purchase intention under descriptive framing. However, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention than injunctive framing within both influencer conditions. Study 2 provided evidence of moderated mediation through information processing fluency: the conditional indirect effect was significant for virtual influencers but not for human influencers. In Study 3, injunctive framing generated higher purchase intention than descriptive framing for human influencers under assessment-oriented priming, whereas this difference was not significant under locomotion-oriented priming. For virtual influencers, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention under both priming conditions. These findings extend research on influencer marketing and social norms by identifying how influencer type and norm framing interact, highlighting information processing fluency as a potential explanatory mechanism and regulatory-mode priming as a boundary condition. They also provide practical guidance for selecting influencers and designing social norm messages in alternative protein marketing. © 2026 The Authors

title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets
abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. However, push and pull theory in the field of pedestrian street is not addressed in the existing research. This study takes the perspective of pedestrian-street consumers, follows a systematic scale-development procedure, and uses samples from eight Chinese cities to develop and test a scale measuring perceived push and pull factors. The scale is composed of 11 dimensions for each of the push and pull domains. This study then examines the nomological validity by testing the associations between push and pull factors and revisit intention and recommendation intention. The results of the study support the nomological validity of the proposed relationships. This study does not propose push and pull as new constructs. Instead, it organizes and validates their context-specific manifestations within Chinese pedestrian streets and provides a culturally grounded measurement instrument for subsequent retail and consumer research. The evidence supports its initial applicability across the Chinese cities examined, while its cross-national applicability remains to be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. However, multimodal evidence from real-world retail settings remains limited regarding how product visual form relates to consumer evaluations in online reviews and satisfaction. Using data from 200 smart standing desks, 41951 valid reviews, and 200 product images, this study combined engineering-attribute encoding, CLIP image embeddings, and CLIP-text concept scores to construct a multilayer representation of product visual form. A large language model was used to extract affective and functional evaluations from the reviews, and the platform favorable rate served as a product-level proxy for satisfaction. Product-level path analysis showed that PC3 (Non-standard premium form) was positively associated with affective evaluation, and affective evaluation was positively associated with satisfaction. Together, these coefficients yielded a significant positive indirect association (indirect association = 0.075, 95% BCa CI [0.021, 0.156], FDR-Adj. p = 0.014). Functional evaluation, by contrast, was negatively associated with satisfaction (β = −0.254, p < 0.01). Further decomposition showed that this negative association was more closely related to functional-mention coverage than to overall polarity of functional evaluations. Noise control and Workspace size adequacy were the principal negative sources. These findings indicate that affective and functional evaluations relate to satisfaction in distinct ways. For online retailers and e-commerce platforms, combining analysis of product visual form with online-review monitoring can help identify design value, detect quality risks, and prioritize service recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Experimental and simulation studies on plasma gasification of medical waste for the co-production of ammonia and urea
abstract: This study explores the novel integration of plasma gasification and urea synthesis using medical waste as a feedstock, a research area largely unexplored compared to conventional plasma gasification applications. This investigation is designed to evaluate the technical and economic viability of producing hydrogen-rich syngas followed by the synthesis of ammonia and urea via advanced process simulation and experimental validation. Medical waste gasification occurs under a CO2 environment to increase syngas quality when using medical waste such as syringes, gloves, surgical masks, and drip sets. Although, the maximum value of lower heating value (LHV) (12.4 MJ/m3) was achieved by utilizing plasma at 1.25 kW, the highest energy efficiency of 53.8 % was obtained at 1.00 kW due to lower energy input. Residue content decreased from 19 wt% (0.75 kW), 14 wt% (1.0 kW), and 11 wt% (1.25 kW). A sensitivity analysis of the simulation indicates that increasing feed rates and plasma power improve syngas quality: CO reaches a maximum of 69 vol% and H2 rises to 31.1 vol%. Ammonia and urea units show N2 and CO2 conversion efficiencies of 87.6 % and 81.56 %, respectively, with maximum urea production of 2853 kg/h. Techno-economic analysis shows that a CAPEX of $32.9 million and OPEX of $4.49 million/year result in a competitive urea cost of $0.49/kg and annual revenue of $6.7 million. The cost analysis showed that a strong positive cash flow and net earnings in a period of 10 years confirm the long-term economic viability and sustainability of this waste utilization for fertilizer production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform
abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. However, little research has systematically investigated the role of algorithmic recommendations in this phenomenon. Our study addresses this gap by auditing the recommendation algorithm of TikTok, the leading short video platform, through four experiments. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Our audits yielded a novel dataset comprising 8535 auto-complete suggestions, 1606 search queries, and 2893 videos labelled by stance (promoting misinformation, neutral in nature, or debunking misinformation). Our analysis reveals that TikTok’s algorithm exhibits sensitivity to user behaviours, often in unexpected ways. We find the algorithm recommends substantially more misinformation to newly created accounts lacking search histories, potentially shaping the tone of the content these accounts engage with. We also find that watching and engaging with videos (e.g., liking and favouriting) dynamically influence misinformation prevalent on the platform, potentially reinforcing existing beliefs and contributing to echo-chambers. Further, we emphasise how engaging with misinformation on one topic serves as a gateway, prompting the algorithm to recommend misinformation spanning both related and unrelated topics. Our work stands as the first large-scale, systematic, and empirical assessment of misinformation in TikTok’s recommendations, contributing valuable insights on the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on TikTok and also underscoring the pressing need for responsible auditing practices across digital platforms. © 2026 The Authors. title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior
abstract: As voice agents become embedded in products as well as service interactions, firms increasingly seek personalization strategies that strengthen consumers' acceptance and engagement. This research examines whether voice agents that sound more similar to users' own voices elicit more favorable behavioral responses. Moreover, we investigate through which psychological mechanisms these effects occur. Across two experiments, we manipulate voice similarity using (1) pretested similar versus dissimilar AI voices and (2) individualized voice cloning that replicates users' voices. Results consistently show that higher voice similarity increases purchase intention, use intention, and willingness to disclose personal information. Mediation analyses indicate that voice similarity operates via two parallel mechanisms: self-congruency and trust. Our research advances research on voice agent-consumer relationships and demonstrates that increasing voice similarity is a robust personalization strategy that enhances consumers’ behavioral responses. © 2026 The Authors

title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Drawing on affordance theory and uses and gratifications reasoning, this research examines whether screenshotable ad design increases preservation-oriented engagement by making ads seem useful for later use. Across five studies, including controlled online experiments and a naturalistic simulated-feed experiment, screenshotable ads were associated with higher ad saving intention and Facebook ad liking relative to non-screenshotable ads. The results are consistent with perceived future utility as a mediating mechanism: screenshotable design increased perceived future utility, which in turn was associated with higher saving-related responses and Facebook ad liking intention. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. In addition, screenshotable design more strongly increased perceived future utility when information density was high rather than low, indicating that saveable structure is most effective when the ad contains enough substantive content to justify preservation. The findings contribute to consumer research on digital advertising response by identifying screenshotable ad design as a distinct visual structure that can shape consumers’ interpretation of an ad as a later-use resource, and they offer guidance for managers designing social media ads intended to be kept, revisited, and positively engaged with over time. © 2026

title: Threats to food security in rice farming: A scientific mapping of climate change impacts
abstract: Climate change is severely disrupting many aspects of human life worldwide, particularly rice farming, as it feeds many people worldwide. In the absence of stable rice production, food security will is threatened for the global population. This paper examines how climate change is related to rice farming and what it means for overall food security. I used bibliometric analysis to examine the literature on this topic from 1998 to 2024, a 26-year period. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using specific keywords, yielding 549 matching documents. Using VOSviewer helped visualize connections and identify trends in the research. Researchers have consistently focused on climate change, rice farming, and food security over time, but have not yet mapped the interrelationships between these variables. The findings suggest a reciprocal relationship. Agriculture produces greenhouse gases that exacerbate climate change, but climate change subsequently reverses itself and harms agricultural productivity. It is particularly difficult for rice to respond to changing temperatures, unusual rainfall patterns, and recurring extreme weather events. As a result, when crop yields decline, the availability of rice as a staple food decreases, directly impacting food security. These findings directly relate to Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger, making it urgent to find better ways to adapt agriculture to climate change and make it more sustainable. This necessary adaptation in rice farming aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 13, Climate Action. Therefore, this Action requires support from the government and the agricultural sector workforce to achieve food security and sustainable rice farming. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference
abstract: Although considerable attention has been paid to enhancing the visual appeal of food, less is known about how plateware design should align with the sensory characteristics of food. Drawing on shape-taste correspondence research and processing fluency theory, this research examines the congruence between plateware shape and food pungency. Across four online experiments with Chinese participants, we obtained 754 valid responses covering all seven major geographic regions of China. The results show that pungent foods elicit more favorable consumer responses when served on angular rather than round plateware, whereas mild foods are evaluated more favorably when served on round rather than angular plateware. Processing fluency mediates the effects of plateware shape and food pungency congruence on food evaluation and ordering intention. title: TKAM: A temporal-availability-aware encoder-decoder framework for multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices
abstract: Accurate multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices is important for hedging, inventory management, and agricultural market risk management. Existing soybean futures price forecasting studies often organize heterogeneous predictors as a unified input sequence and overlook differences in their temporal availability at the forecasting origin. In addition, how complex forecasting models use information across forecast horizons remains insufficiently explained. This study proposes TKAM, an interpretable framework for multi-step soybean futures price forecasting. TKAM separates past-observed market variables from future-known time features, uses a Mamba-based encoder to represent historical market dynamics, and employs a Temporal Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (TKAN) decoder with a multi-output forecasting strategy to generate forecasts for multiple future trading days. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used to examine horizon-specific feature contributions. The empirical analysis uses 4165 daily observations from the No. 1 yellow soybean futures contract listed on the Dalian Commodity Exchange in China, covering the period from May 9, 2008, to June 27, 2025. The results show that TKAM achieves competitive and stable point-forecasting accuracy compared with twelve benchmark models, particularly for biweekly and monthly forecasts. The ablation results indicate that the branch-based input organization contributes substantially to forecasting performance and that the Mamba encoder is effective within this structure. The SHAP analysis shows that related agricultural futures prices, domestic spot prices, and time features contribute differently across forecast horizons. These findings provide methodological insights for multi-step agricultural futures price forecasting and empirical evidence for understanding the horizon-specific forecasting behavior of complex models in agricultural markets. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Using China's Enterprise Environmental Credit Evaluation System (EECES) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of corporate environmental credit rating on capital-labor conflicts. The results indicate that EECES reduces capital-labor conflicts in polluting industries by approximately 17.63%, although its effect weakens over time. Channel tests show that EECES mitigates capital-labor conflicts by reducing workers' pollution exposure risk, improving corporate environmental information transparency, and enhancing social trust in corporations. Moreover, in cities with weaker social governance capacity, EECES exerts a stronger restraining effect on capital-labor conflicts, suggesting that it effectively compensates for deficiencies in social governance. Further analysis reveals that although EECES reduces industrial output, it significantly promotes economic transformation. Overall, these findings highlight EECES as an effective policy tool for safeguarding social stability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Integrated cognitive processing model of phishing detection: Mood state as moderating factor in the mindful cognition mediated detection process
abstract: Previous studies have shown that security awareness alone is not consistently associated with phishing detection accuracy, yet the processes through which awareness is associated with detection remain underexplored. Existing phishing research has also predominantly adopted a cognitive perspective, despite the interdependent nature of affect and cognition in decision-making. To address these gaps, this study adopts an affect-integrated cognitive processing perspective and examines a proposed cognitive process involving security awareness, domain mindfulness, cognitive processing, and mood state, with particular attention to the conditional role of positive mood in performance-focused phishing judgments. Our findings show that security awareness is not directly associated with phishing detection accuracy; rather, a significant indirect association is observed through domain mindfulness and cognitive processing. Although temperament is not directly associated with detection accuracy, it is positively associated with mood state. Positive mood is negatively associated with detection accuracy, and the estimated beneficial indirect associations involving domain mindfulness and cognitive processing are weaker at higher levels of positive mood. Together, the results are consistent with a phishing-detection process involving both cognitive and affective factors. This study extends cognition-focused phishing-detection models by integrating affective boundary conditions into the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Store coolness in luxury fashion: Antecedents, outcomes, and the moderating role of price consciousness
abstract: In the context of luxury fashion stores, this study investigates the mediating role of the dimensions of store coolness (extraordinary, subcultural, iconic, and high status) in linking service quality of employees, store display, and store creativity with customers' behavioral intention and positive word-of-mouth (WOM). Additionally, the study examines whether price consciousness moderates any of these relationships. To gain a deeper understanding of how coolness is perceived in luxury fashion stores, we collected customer insights through interviews with 16 frequent store visitors. We then tested our proposed model using a survey administered to shoppers immediately after they visited luxury stores (N = 213). Our results indicate that the extraordinary and subcultural dimensions of coolness positively mediate the effects of store display and creativity on behavioral intention and positive WOM. However, the iconic dimension did not play a mediating role, while the high status dimension negatively mediated these paths, including those involving service quality. Finally, we found that price consciousness weakens the path from store creativity to the studied outcomes via the extraordinary dimension. Building on these findings, we provide managerial insights for designing luxury fashion store experiences that foster store coolness and positive customer responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Tell me the truth: Consumer responses to feedback solicitation with robots versus humans
abstract: Advanced technologies enable service robots to handle a broader range of tasks than ever before. Among these, this research examines the potential of service robots to solicit and collect high-quality consumer feedback. This research, comprising four experimental studies, including a field study in a hotel, demonstrates that unsatisfied consumers are more likely to provide honest feedback to service robots than to human employees. Drawing on the theory of mind perception, the present research finds that such an effect is attributed to consumers’ concern for others' feelings (i.e., empathetic concern). Moreover, the proposed effects are diminished when the robot has a high (vs. low) level of emotional capability but are more pronounced among consumers with interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal. This research offers practical insights that enable advanced robotic technologies to be useful beyond simple physical tasks: consumer feedback management. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: CONSENT IS NOT JUST ABOUT ASKING: HOW YOU REQUEST CONSUMERS’ AGREEMENT TO COOKIES MATTERS
abstract: Website cookie notices influence consent decisions by configuring multiple design cues within the privacy calculus consumers apply when evaluating data disclosure. Results of an online experiment (N = 776) suggest that freedom of choice and cookie notice placement influence consumers’ perceived power. In addition, technical language influences perceived risk. Perceived power, perceived risk, and consumers’ emotions influence behavioral intentions toward cookie notices. The findings show that cookie notice cues operate configurally rather than independently, revealing a configurational privacy calculus in which the impact of any single design element depends on the broader configuration of cues in which it appears. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. .

title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. This study addresses a critical gap by exploring how ICT, particularly mobile Internet connectivity, influences climate change literacy in Africa. I provide the first systematic evidence on the impact of mobile Internet connectivity on climate change literacy by exploiting variations in peer-based Internet connectivity in an instrumental variable strategy. Using newly georeferenced individual-level data on climate change literacy from over 42,000 respondents across 31 African countries, I show that mobile Internet connectivity has a modest yet robust effect on climate literacy, raising it by approximately 0.57 points for a typical adopter. Heterogeneity analysis shows that mobile Internet access primarily enhances the knowledge-based dimensions of climate literacy, particularly climate awareness and understanding, while also improving risk perceptions to a lesser extent. This suggests that mobile Internet contributes to climate literacy mainly by expanding access to factual information and knowledge about climate change. Suggestive evidence reveals that Internet connectivity can help close climate-related information gaps, among socio-economically disadvantaged groups, such as women, farmers, and those without formal education. Although Internet connectivity increases the frequency of using Internet and social media for news, there is no strong evidence that these platforms serve as channels linking Internet connectivity to climate literacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Advancing bibliometric analysis: Evidence-based guidelines with insights from senior journal editors
abstract: Bibliometric analysis is a powerful means of evaluating research. This article employs a sequential mixed-methods approach to enrich the understanding of bibliometric analysis and presents a structured guide to maximize the technique's benefits. A thematically synthesized narrative commentary on bibliometric review papers, based on input from 53 senior editorial members of leading hospitality and tourism journals, constitutes the study's foundation. Cutting-edge literature comprising 195 bibliometric investigations is also considered. Our evidence-based guidance provides scholars with a roadmap for conducting state-of-the-art bibliometric analyses. These suggestions are intended to improve the method's quality and accessibility, affirming its utility. Ultimately, this paper seeks to enhance bibliometric studies’ clarity, rigor, and efficacy by presenting forward-looking, real-world insights. Its step-by-step guide will facilitate decision-making and advance the field's theoretical and managerial understanding. © 2026

title: Should generative AI be responsible to users? Developing and validating the user-generative AI psychological contract scale
abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Drawing on Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) theory and psychological contract theory, this study defines the user–generative AI psychological contract (AIPC) as users' beliefs about the responsibilities and obligations GenAI should fulfill toward them during ongoing interaction and develops a corresponding scale. Study 1 used purposively recruited interviews (N = 26) to identify the construct content domain. Study 2 used two nonprobability online-panel samples of active GenAI users (N = 507 and N = 506) to develop the items and examine the factor structure, reliability, and construct validity. Study 3 used the same 506-case sample employed for structural validation in Study 2 to provide an initial test of the nomological network among AIPC, AI anthropomorphism, and co-creation intention. Results indicate that AIPC consists of three dimensions—the functional support contract, relational collaboration contract, and ethical safety contract—and forms a 16-item scale. Users reported the strongest expectations regarding ethical safety. Anthropomorphism was indirectly associated with co-creation intention through functional support and relational collaboration, but not through ethical safety. The findings extend psychological contract theory to user–AI relationships and provide a measurement tool for studying responsibility expectations toward GenAI. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Factors affecting public transport adoption in Riyadh- case study
abstract: Riyadh's greenhouse gas emissions and urban climate risks are likely heightened by accelerated urbanization and profound dependence on private cars. Despite the government's investment in public transportation, societal resistance to giving up private cars and using public transit persists due to cultural and traditional factors. Within the Gulf context, this study is the first to investigate the unique socio-cultural and urban context of Riyadh to understand university students' mobility behavior, identify four factors that significantly are associated with their travel choices, and quantitatively rank the relative influence of these factors. Surveys (n = 710) were used to assess four key factors, analyzed via multiple regression, chi-square, and t-tests. Results indicate that, in descending order of influence, psychological factors (explaining 23% of the variance) have the most significant association with students' willingness to switch to public transport in Riyadh, followed by trip characteristics (13%), urban factors (12%), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (12%). The result suggests that, alongside infrastructure improvements, coordinated strategies are required to change social norms, enhance environmental awareness, and create culturally responsive incentives. The findings support the implementation of place-based policies for sustainable mobility. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Hungry for change: Inclusive dining for travelers with dietary restrictions
abstract: Dining is central to tourism experiences, yet for travelers with dietary restrictions, it can become a source of exclusion rather than enjoyment. Guided by stigma theory, this study examines how dietary restrictions function as a form of concealable stigma in tourism dining contexts. Using a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design, the study combines Critical Incident Technique interviews with 32 individuals and text mining of 3,165 traveler Yelp reviews. Findings reveal that stigma manifests through internal (self-burden, anticipatory anxiety) and external (public, structural, associative) forms producing psychological and behavioral consequences that constrain participation in dining experiences. Individuals employ a range of voluntary and involuntary coping responses to navigate such challenges. Building on these findings, the study proposes a mutual reinforcement model in which internal and external stigma recursively sustain one another across repeated dining encounters, highlighting the anticipatory and cumulative nature of dietary stigma in tourism and offering theoretical and practical insights. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Recommend or not? Investigating the effectiveness of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising
abstract: Online charitable platforms are important channels through which the public participates in micro-donations, and these platforms have increasingly leveraged algorithmic recommendation technologies to deliver personalized charitable advertisements to potential donors. Nonetheless, whether personalized algorithmic recommendations enhance or undermine consumers’ micro-donation intentions remains unclear. Drawing on moral identity theory, our research addresses this gap through five online scenario-based experiments. The results show that consumers exhibit lower micro-donation intentions when exposed to micro-donation advertisements with personalized algorithmic recommendations, and that this negative effect is driven primarily by perceived identity value threat. Furthermore, we find that the negative effect of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising is attenuated in the presence of legitimization cues or among consumers with low scores on the moral identity scale. Our findings not only extend the literature on the antecedents of micro-donations and the economic consequences of algorithmic personalization in the charitable advertising context, but also offer actionable guidance for charitable platforms seeking to optimize their algorithmic recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Appliance-level energy assessment and its implications for the environmental impact of household energy conservation: Evidence from urban China
abstract: Accurate appliance-level energy judgments may help households identify and prioritize meaningful electricity-saving opportunities, with potential implications for the environmental benefits of household conservation. Using survey and experimental data from 2592 residents in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, this paper assesses how accurately urban households estimate the electricity consumption of 11 common appliances, whether their judgments exhibit patterns consistent with availability-based reasoning, and whether a randomized heat-related information cue improves relative appliance-energy judgments. The results reveal substantial misalignment between perceived and benchmark electricity use: (1) respondents tend to overestimate the energy use of low-energy, frequently used appliances (e.g., televisions) while underestimating high-energy, infrequently interacted devices (e.g., water heaters); (2) appliance use frequency is positively associated with perceived energy consumption, a pattern consistent with greater cognitive accessibility of frequently used appliances; (3) random assignment to the heat-related cue increases perceived energy use for heat-producing appliances and improves respondents' measured relative correspondence with the benchmark; and (4) further analyses show that higher educational attainment is associated with closer benchmark alignment and that closer alignment is associated with lower reported household electricity expenditures. These findings document systematic deviations in appliance-level energy judgments and show that a targeted information cue can improve such judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.
