title: What drives hybrid cultivated meat acceptance? Evidence from a controlled real-product tasting
abstract: Despite growing interest in cultivated meat, most consumer-related evidence remains based on hypothetical assessments rather than real product exposure, limiting understanding of actual sensory-driven acceptance. To address this gap, the present study investigated consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated chicken product through a controlled affective sensory evaluation with young Singaporean consumers. Participants (n = 82) evaluated overall liking and sensory liking for appearance, smell, taste, texture, and aftertaste, completed Just-About-Right (JAR) diagnostics and were segmented according to Net Promoter Score (NPS) responses. JAR penalty analysis suggested that deviations from optimal sensory intensity systematically affected overall liking, with excessive intensity perceived in taste, smell, and aftertaste generating the largest penalties. Across sensory dimensions, oral attributes exerted a stronger influence on liking than appearance, with taste emerging as the primary driver of acceptance and texture showing a secondary contribution. Multiple regression analysis confirmed taste liking as the strongest predictor of overall liking, whereas the remaining sensory aspects showed weaker or non-significant effects. NPS segmentation further revealed clear differences in recommendation behaviour across detractors, passives, and promoters, closely mirroring hedonic liking patterns and supporting consistency between sensory evaluation and recommendation-oriented behavioural responses. Overall, this study provides an initial empirical benchmark of consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated meat product under controlled conditions, highlighting the central role of taste quality and sensory balance in shaping hedonic responses and consumer satisfaction. title: Persuasive triggers and psychological pathways: Unplanned purchase behavior in live-streaming blind box commerce
abstract: Unplanned purchasing is increasingly embedded in digital experiences in which consumers encounter commercial opportunities without a prior intention to shop. This study examines how such opportunities become valued and actionable in live-streaming blind-box commerce. Using survey data from 231 Chinese consumers with experience purchasing blind boxes through livestreams, we test a process model linking scarcity messages, time pressure, economic benefits, and fear of missing out (FOMO) with perceived value, emotional and cognitive self-efficacy, and unplanned purchase behavior (UPB). All four conditions were positively associated with perceived value, which was positively associated with both forms of self-efficacy; emotional and cognitive self-efficacy were, in turn, positively associated with UPB. Streamer persuasiveness strengthened the relationships between all four antecedent conditions and perceived value. The findings show that an unplanned purchase need not arise simply from impulsive responding. Consumers may encounter an unexpected opportunity, judge it to be worthwhile, and feel capable of acting even when the purchase was not previously planned. The study extends research on livestream commerce by explaining how persuasive conditions relate to value appraisal and perceived capability, providing a process-based account of UPB in an uncertain and interactive retail setting. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of combining persuasive communication with clear and transparent presentation of purchase conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When loyalty points become donations: The effects of redeemability, point expiration, and descriptive norm information
abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. To address this gap, the present research examines, across three studies, the effect of point redeemability on consumers’ donation intention through online checkout charity, as well as the moderating roles of point expiration and descriptive norm information. Study 1 shows that consumers exhibit higher donation intention when their reward points are non-redeemable than when they are redeemable. Study 2 demonstrates that the interaction between point redeemability and point expiration significantly influences donation intention, while Study 3 shows that the interaction between point redeemability and descriptive norm information also significantly affects donation intention. The findings provide actionable insights for retailers seeking to design more effective reward point donation programs and enhance social impact through online checkout charity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A framework integrating topological potential and semantic embeddings for identifying scientific research clusters in scholarly collaboration networks
abstract: Multi-team collaboration is essential for addressing major scientific challenges. Previous methods focus predominantly on individuals or single teams, making it difficult to capture the structure of multi-team collaborative innovation systems. To address this, this study conceptualizes a research cluster as a multi-team system formed through inter-team relationships and related research goals within complex collaborative research environments. We further introduce a four-phase Topological Potential–Semantic Embedding Research Cluster Identification (TPSE-RCI) framework to identify scientific research clusters. First, research teams are detected and a team collaboration network is constructed. Second, team feature vectors are generated via topological potential–enhanced Node2Vec and initial clusters are identified with HDBSCAN. Third, team publications are analyzed using BERTopic with BGE-M3 semantic embeddings to derive hierarchical research goals. Fourth, validity criteria are applied to filter scientific research clusters. Using medical informatics publications as a case study, we detected 4262 research teams from 81,557 publications by 269,598 authors. At the structural level, 702 initial scientific research clusters were identified. At the thematic level, 319 topics were extracted from the team publications and consolidated into 21 secondary and 7 primary research goals. By integrating structural and thematic results, we ultimately identified 239 scientific research clusters. Comparative and ablation analyses indicate that incorporating topological potential improves team representation and structural-clustering quality within this empirical setting. The identified research clusters can provide decision support for practical tasks such as organized research management, major project coordination and optimization, domain expert identification, and research resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Repairing trust in AI: Attribution, anthropomorphism, and the illusion of difference
abstract: Trust repair between humans and AI systems is an emerging area of inquiry that builds on a well-established literature in human–human (HH) interactions. This review examines how key HH findings, particularly the differential effectiveness of repair strategies following competence versus integrity violations, generalize to human–robot interaction (HRI). While some patterns hold, important divergences exist. The paper argues that better operationalizations of integrity violations and increased anthropomorphism can align HRI findings more closely with HH research. However, enduring challenges remain regarding the ethics of anthropomorphic design, the moral values AI should adopt, and how AI should extend trust to humans. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Online dating paradox: Why lonely hearts choose to ghost
abstract: This study examines the differential associations of state and trait loneliness with ghosting behavior in online dating, considering self-presentation strategies and dating fatigue as potential explanatory pathways. Survey data from 881 Chinese mobile dating app users were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that state loneliness was negatively associated with ghosting, whereas trait loneliness was positively associated with ghosting. Dating fatigue was positively associated with ghosting and statistically mediated the associations between both forms of loneliness and ghosting in opposite directions. Acquisitive self-presentation was positively associated with state loneliness and negatively associated with trait loneliness; unexpectedly, it was negatively associated with dating fatigue. Authentic self-presentation was not significantly associated with loneliness or dating fatigue. These findings suggest that temporary and chronic loneliness may correspond to different patterns of engagement and disengagement in online dating. The study contributes to mobile dating research by distinguishing state and trait loneliness and by identifying dating fatigue as an important correlate of ghosting behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. The paper reflects on epistemic justice in energy- and ocean governance, and asks whether and how United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) facilitates that such justice is sought in the regulatory process of deep sea mining by focusing on procedural rules for the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and the representation of different knowers in the decision-making process, including its Council's structure, authority, and composition. It concludes that a very small number of individuals has the power to bring about a very large change in deep sea mining regulations, currently without legal requirements to include experiential, traditional or other forms of knowledges beyond the scientific method in the decision-making process. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. First, a regional tourism-pressure screening index is constructed for Euro-Mediterranean NUTS-2 regions to identify broader high-pressure contexts. Second, an Overtourism Vulnerability Index (OVI) is implemented for the main tourism hotspots in Apulia, Italy, using eight normalized indicators capturing direct tourism pressure, air accessibility, accommodation platformisation, economic dependence and heritage attractiveness. Rather than treating the OVI as a ranking device, the framework decomposes vulnerability into three diagnostic dimensions: direct pressure, structural fragility and gateway/heritage amplification. These dimensions identify four regimes: critical overload and fragility, gateway/heritage pressure, coastal fragility and platformisation, and monitor-and-prevent contexts. Robustness checks and an external waste-based plausibility check support the diagnostic interpretation. The resulting toolbox links each regime to assessment, monitoring and candidate intervention priorities, helping planners move from regional pressure screening to municipal scoping and targeted environmental and carrying-capacity assessment. © 2026 The Authors

title: When GAI backfires: Understanding the process mechanism of consumers’ avoidance of generative AI conversational recommendation agents from a misaligned affordance perspective
abstract: Generative AI-enhanced conversational recommendation agents (GCRAs) are being widely deployed on e-commerce platforms; however, consumers increasingly avoid these advanced recommendation tools. Prior research has not systematically identified which specific features of GCRAs drive such avoidance, nor has it clearly articulated the underlying process mechanisms through which avoidance emerges. To address these gaps, this study draws on affordance actualization theory and misaligned affordance theory to systematically investigate consumers’ perceived GCRA misaligned affordances and to model the complete pathways from these misaligned affordances to consumer avoidance behaviors. We employed a sequential mixed-methods approach. First, a qualitative interview research (N = 19) combined with a simple experiment identified three key GCRA misaligned affordances: limited choices, iterative dialogue, and hallucinated information. Second, a quantitative research (N = 538) validated that these misaligned affordances trigger cost-based comparative appraisals (opportunity and transaction costs), which in turn lead to negative experiences (both outcome-related and process-related), ultimately driving consumer avoidance. Finally, by integrating the findings across studies, we developed a comprehensive framework explaining consumers’ avoidance of GCRAs. Theoretically, this research advances the misaligned affordance actualization theory by highlighting the novel comparative appraisal stage, moving the theory from qualitative conceptualization to process-level mechanisms. Collectively, these findings provide new theoretical insights and practical guidance for improving the design and deployment of GCRAs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Effects of AI-based chatbot coaching on goal attainment, self-efficacy, and stress: A longitudinal randomized experiment
abstract: Students in higher education face a range of academic challenges, which leads to high levels of stress among many students. While coaching has been shown to help students address these challenges, it is resource-intensive and therefore not broadly accessible. AI-based chatbots may help broaden access by providing interactive and personalized guidance at scale, yet empirical evidence on their effectiveness remains limited, particularly from longitudinal experimental studies. Addressing this gap, we conducted a longitudinal between-subjects experiment with four measurement points across an academic semester, randomly assigning 101 students to one of three conditions: AI-based chatbot coaching, literature-based self-study (active control), or a waitlist control condition. Students in the chatbot coaching and literature study conditions engaged in repeated interactions with the intervention, averaging approximately 100 min of cumulative interaction time accumulated across four sessions of 23–28 min each. We examined how students’ goal attainment, university-related self-efficacy, and stress developed over the course of the study. Results showed that students in the AI-based chatbot condition achieved significantly stronger increases in goal attainment over time compared to students in both control conditions. Self-efficacy also increased in the AI-based chatbot condition over time; however, between-condition differences were not consistent across time points, suggesting that the intervention had a more limited impact on self-efficacy relative to goal attainment. Furthermore, no significant effects were found for university-related stress. The findings suggest that AI-based chatbot coaching can effectively support students in achieving university-related goals and strengthening their self-efficacy, while its impact on stress reduction may be limited. © 2026 The Authors

title: Conflict expression: A decade of group conflict research
abstract: The conflict expression framework was developed to generate new practical and theoretical insights into how conflict communication affects group processes and negotiated outcomes. The framework proposes that conflict expressions vary along two dimensions: directness and oppositional intensity. The framework suggested that the effects of different types of conflict on group processes and outcomes likely depend on how the conflict is expressed, that conflict within groups is likely perceived differently by different members of the same social unit, and that conflict affects negotiation processes dynamically through reciprocated statements and responses. We review research building on the framework – including empirical tests of the main propositions, methodological advances, and as a theoretical foundation for conflict communication research more broadly – and identify directions for the future. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Performative narratives and destination image in cross-cultural tourism livestreaming
abstract: Tourism livestreaming allows global audiences to encounter destinations in real time, yet how livestreamers’ expressive behaviors shape audiences’ destination evaluations across cultures remains unclear. Drawing on a performative perspective, this research conceptualizes expressed destination image formation as a temporally situated process generated through live narrative enactment. Using multimodal cross-cultural livestream data, the study shows that emotional expression is positively associated with expressed affective destination image, explicit self-disclosure is positively associated with expressed cognitive image, and interactive engagement shows partial evidence of an inverted U-shaped relationship with expressed cognitive destination image. Cross-cultural proximity further operates unevenly: cultural distance reshapes the interaction–cognition pathway, whereas linguistic accessibility improves destination image expression but does not consistently amplify performative cues. Finally, post-livestream destination image expression attenuates over time, with affective impressions fading faster. Overall, this research clarifies how destination image expression is performatively activated, cross-culturally conditioned, and temporally attenuated in tourism livestreaming. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Drawing on schema theory, this study examines how latent cultural identification (LCI) emerges when sedimented cultural meanings become perceptible and interpretable during travel. Based on interviews with 41 Vietnamese tourists traveling in China, the findings indicate that material, social, and mediated cues make routinized meanings noticeable, while internalized cultural schemata help tourists interpret them in relation to their cultural self-understanding. Affective resonance amplifies this process by intensifying the salience and self-relevance of interpreted meanings. Behavioural responses vary across compliance, inquiry, reinterpretation, and co-creation, reflecting different degrees of self-reflection and social embeddedness. By highlighting the role of cultural schemata in LCI, this study extends tourism identity research and shows how LCI can help tourists locate their own culture within the wider world-cultural landscape, enrich personal meaning-making, and foster intercultural exchange. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modeling Japanese consumers' acceptance and rejection of tech-enhanced foods
abstract: To maintain the well-being of the global population, strengthening the food supply system is necessary. A promising solution is the development of new food manufacturing technologies related to the production, processing, and preservation of food. Foods produced with such technologies are referred to as tech-enhanced foods. While the promotion of tech-enhanced foods is important, they have yet to be widely used in Japan. An understanding of consumers' psychological reactions and related factors is considered useful when designing and promoting tech-enhanced foods. Thus, this research aimed to construct a model explaining the psychological factors pertaining to consumers' acceptance and rejection of four types of tech-enhanced foods: genetically modified (GM) foods, meat alternatives, cultured meats, and edible insects. The proposed psychological model was based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework and supplemented with elements from the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The analysis revealed that positive and negative affects emerge as the most significant factors associated with intake intention and rejection, respectively. Moreover, the potential damage and benefits of tech-enhanced foods, along with reliability of regulation, were found to be associated with emotional responses, rejection, and intake intention. These findings may provide useful insights for designing interventions aimed at promoting the acceptance of tech-enhanced foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Activating competing goals: The dual effect of environmental fee
abstract: While economic intervention is increasingly used to support environmental protection, its effectiveness in tourism contexts remains unclear. By introducing symbolic interactionism, this research examined how environmental fee cues influence tourists’ environmentally responsible behavior across different attraction types and quality levels. We conducted a field observation study (N = 500), two field surveys using questionnaires (total N = 765), and one online experiment (N = 293). Results showed that environmental fee cues increased environmentally responsible behavior in resource-based attractions by activating moral norm goals, but decreased environmentally responsible behavior in market-based attractions via thrift goal activation. Moreover, this study further refined the environmental fee strategy and examined its effectiveness and mechanism across all attraction quality levels. The findings provide novel theoretical insights and practical implications for designing adaptive environmental fee strategies. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Barriers and enablers to circular economy implementation in 3D concrete printing: A fuzzy decision-making approach
abstract: The circular economy (CE) is increasingly emphasised in 3D concrete printing (3DCP), yet evidence remains limited on the key barriers to its implementation and the enablers needed to support practical uptake. This study addresses that gap through a sequential mixed-methods design combining a literature-informed review to identify initial barriers, ten semi-structured expert interviews to refine them and elicit corresponding enablers in the 3DCP context, and a questionnaire survey of 58 academic and industry specialists from multiple regions to prioritise their relative importance using a fuzzy synthetic evaluation approach. The findings show that CE implementation in 3DCP is constrained less by isolated technical limitations than by wider system conditions shaping approval, investment, knowledge translation, and supply-chain coordination. Regulatory and standardisation issues emerged as the most critical barrier theme, followed by financial and market constraints, while the gap between low-TRL academic research and high-TRL industrial implementation was identified as the most prominent item-level barrier. The most influential enablers were CE-oriented standards, cost-effective process maturation, targeted R&D support, and stronger validation and implementation pathways. By revealing convergence between academia and industry on the main priorities, the study contributes a context-specific methodological approach for investigating CE implementation in 3DCP and establishes a prioritised evidence base on the barriers and enablers shaping circular 3DCP. It also provides practical guidance for researchers, industry stakeholders, and policy actors by identifying where intervention is likely to be most effective, particularly in standards development, technology validation, investment support, and supply-chain coordination, to scale circular 3DCP in support of net-zero and zero-waste ambitions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Emotional interaction and conversion value in live streaming E-commerce
abstract: Multi-agent emotional interaction constitutes a core characteristic of live streaming e-commerce. Nevertheless, prior research has yet to build a unified analytical framework incorporating streamers, viewers and live streaming assistants, and rarely explored how emotional dynamics shape live streaming performance. Based on minute-level panel data of 4671 min retrieved from 40 Taobao live streaming sessions, this study adopts sentiment analysis to quantify the emotional expressions of streamers and viewers. Applying the Panel Vector Autoregression (PVAR) model and impulse response analysis, this study constructs a tripartite emotional interaction system among streamers, viewers and assistants, and investigates its dynamic linkage with core operational performance, including product sales and new follower growth. The empirical results are consistent with a unidirectional streamer-to-viewer emotional association, whereby streamer emotions are closely associated with viewer interaction and purchase decisions. By contrast, intra-viewer emotional association is not statistically supported, whereas viewer emotions are positively associated with new follower growth. Higher frequency of live streaming assistant intervention shows a dual association pattern: it is positively associated with viewer interaction frequency, but negatively associated with product sales. This study extends the application scope of emotional contagion theory in the live streaming context, enriches the role configuration of the live streaming e-commerce ecosystem, and offers practical and targeted operational strategies for live streaming management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The temporal shift in consumer hue preferences in hotel booking
abstract: Despite the hospitality industry's ongoing pursuit of optimal color marketing strategies, it remains unclear whether consumers respond more favorably to cool or warm hues. This research investigates how consumers' hue preferences in digital marketing imagery shift as a function of time of day. Through a case coding analysis (n = 4510), an eye-tracking experiment (n = 105), three online experiments (n = 981), and a quasi-experimental field survey with real tourists (n = 316), this research reveals temporal shifts in hue preference in hotel booking contexts, such that consumers prefer hotel room photos with cool hues in the morning and warm hues in the evening. These preferences are mediated by the need for uniqueness and the need for belonging, respectively. Furthermore, the effect is moderated by visual temporal cues (window view) and individual circadian rhythms (chronotype). Our findings challenge static perspectives on color psychology and offer actionable guidance for time-adaptive visual marketing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an Identifiable and Authorized Privacy-Preserving Data Retrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. IAPDR uses DIDs to provide verifiable, globally unique identities while preserving anonymity and self-sovereign management. It uses non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs) for anonymous authorization. The data controller can verify the lawfulness of each retrieval request without learning any personally identifiable data, thereby upholding data minimization. For scalable retrieval, IAPDR employs Private Set Intersection with Payload (PSI-Payload) to execute large-batch matching while keeping both identifiers and associated records confidential. We prove anonymity and unforgeability, and give a Universal Composability (UC) security analysis in the semi-honest model. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. These enhancements make GDPR compliant privacy-preserving data retrieval practically feasible. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Automotive warranty intelligence through evidence-grounded graph retrieval and agentic reasoning
abstract: Automotive warranty records contain detailed evidence on field failures, repeated repairs, and repair actions, but heterogeneous fields and fragmented vehicle–part–fault relations make reliability-oriented synthesis difficult. We introduce a confidential industrial protocol for automotive warranty intelligence and evaluate an evidence-grounded framework over 16,948 anonymized after-sales records. The evaluated framework combines GraphRAG evidence packs from a 2500-record test-reference-enriched index, Dynamic ACE-Agent governance with an evidence workspace and frozen procedural memory, and retrieval-aware supervised fine-tuning. Eight system configurations were tested on a locked 150-item set covering single-record diagnosis, multi-record fault reasoning, and global reliability-evidence synthesis. The full system achieved the highest blind-judge integrated quality score (4.224/5 versus 3.272 for the Flat Hybrid-RAG baseline) and reduced the hard-error rate from 48.7% to 22.0%. In a stratified double-rated expert review of 45 items, it also achieved the highest weighted score (4.237), exceeding the strongest competing configuration by 0.199 points (95% confidence interval, 0.115–0.281; Holm-adjusted p=0.0131). Within this controlled protocol using a test-reference-enriched GraphRAG index, the integrated configuration produced the strongest observed traceable warranty responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Is state fragility a hindrance to trade openness in Africa?
abstract: This paper analyses the effects of state fragility on trade openness in Africa, using panel data for 50 African countries over the period 1995–2018. We use the recent de facto trade openness indicators developed by Squalli and Wilson (2011) because it reflects the actual degree of trade and the Fraser Institute’s de jure Trade Freedom index. Estimates obtained using the feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and the system generalized method of moments (system GMM) show that the inability of African states to provide basic public services and ensure high-quality institutions has a negative effect on these countries’ trade openness. However, the magnitude of the estimated effects varies considerably according to the different measures of trade openness used. Furthermore, the quantile regression approach shows that the effect of state fragility and its dimensions varies across the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th quintile. The results are also robust when distinguishing other measures of state fragility and trade openness. Based on these results, it would be worthwhile for African countries to strengthen state capacity and the quality of their institutions in order to ensure an effective and sustainable improvement in trade transactions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: From perceived attractiveness to visitation: Multi-scale measurement and influencing factors across 143 Chinese historic cities
abstract: Effective tourism management requires understanding how attraction attributes and supporting factors shape tourists’ perceived attractiveness, and how these in turn translate into visitation. We develop a tourist-centered framework using 610,136 reviews across 2128 heritage attractions in 143 cities, measuring multi-scale perceived attractiveness with a large language model pipeline and visitation with review volume, then identifying the factors that influence both metrics using XGBoost and SHAP. Results show that (1) perceived attractiveness and visitation share a multi-core spatial structure, while visitation displays a polarized long-tail distribution; (2) attraction attributes, especially official designation, visual quality, and ticket pricing, dominate both metrics but shape them differently; (3) positively perceived social, economic, scientific, historic and aesthetical values increase visitation, whereas political value is negatively associated; and (4) accessibility and spatial agglomeration also contribute positively. Practically, multi-scale benchmarking identifies underperforming attractions, while attraction-scale value profiles and the identified influencing factors guide targeted strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Achieving emotionally and factually grounded interactive comments through a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine
abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, online product comments have become a major reference point for consumers in making purchase decisions. However, current comment systems are challenged by uneven comment quality, limited accuracy in sentiment expression, and a lack of verification for factual information, which together reduce the usefulness and credibility of the comments. Grounded in dual process theory and adaptive control theory, this study proposes a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine framework that enables intelligent generation of interactive comments through an emotion-fact dual-anchoring mechanism. The framework dynamically adjusts its interaction strategy according to the dialogue state and user feedback, while preserving authentic emotional expression and ensuring the reliability of objective information. The findings show that interactive comments generated by large language models perform well in terms of content authenticity, emotional consistency, user satisfaction, and readability. This study offers an innovative solution to key limitations in e-commerce comment systems and is of significant importance for improving comment quality and user engagement on digital commerce platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Do platform and seller cues improve price prediction? A study on online food delivery platforms using machine learning
abstract: This study investigates value-based pricing on online food delivery platforms by examining the role of beyond-core service attributes—platform brand and Observed Restaurant Activity Duration—as observable platform- and restaurant-level cues. Drawing on signaling theory as a conceptual lens, we adopt a theory-guided predictive modeling approach to assess whether these cue-related variables improve the prediction of the final price paid per order under varying levels of order urgency. Using a dataset of 1536 cross-platform transactions in Vietnam and applying a broader model-benchmarking strategy, including Random Forest, linear regression, XGBoost, and other machine-learning models, we show that nonlinear machine-learning models provide stronger out-of-sample predictive accuracy than traditional linear estimation. XGBoost achieves the strongest overall predictive performance and is therefore used as the primary model for permutation feature-importance and hypothesis analyses, while Random Forest serves as a robustness benchmark. Both platform brand and restaurant activity duration emerge as meaningful predictive contributors beyond core service attributes. Importantly, platform brand shows a substantial increase in predictive importance under high-urgency conditions, whereas restaurant activity duration remains comparatively stable across urgency levels. These findings contribute to value-based pricing and digital platform research by highlighting how theoretically informed observable cues contribute to price prediction across transaction conditions, and provide actionable insights for restaurants seeking to support pricing decisions in multi-platform environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. While prior research has separately examined algorithmic homogeneity risks or efficiency gains, how consumers simultaneously process these opposing signals, and whether this processing differs from human-generated design, remains unclear. This study investigates how the attribution of design to AI (vs. human) influences consumer evaluations via dual pathways—perceived homogeneity and trend relevance—and examines brand positioning as a boundary condition. A 2 (design source: AI vs. human) × 2 (brand positioning: avant-garde vs. mainstream) between-subjects experiment with 412 consumers reveals that AI-attributed designs simultaneously heighten both perceptions. Multi-group analysis demonstrates that these perceptions operate through perceived manipulative intent, a mechanism significantly stronger for AI- than human-attributed designs. The two pathways exert opposing effects on brand sincerity and purchase intention. Brand positioning moderates these effects asymmetrically: the negative homogeneity pathway is amplified for avant-garde brands, while the positive trend-relevance pathway is strengthened for mainstream brands. These findings identify perceived manipulative intent as the core mechanism translating AI design attribution into consumer responses, and demonstrate that aligning AI adoption with brand positioning can either help or hurt brand sincerity. For fashion retailers, the implications are clear: communicate AI usage as value-creating rather than cost-cutting, and tailor AI strategies to brand positioning—avant-garde brands should emphasize human-AI collaboration, while mainstream brands should leverage AI's trend-sensing capabilities while guarding against stylistic sameness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions
abstract: Short-form retail videos frequently depict food consumption, yet little is known about whether the identity of the visible eater shapes how consumers evaluate the product. We conceptualize eating-agent identity as a contextual product cue and develop a cue-based inference account in which a pet eater makes nature-related meaning salient and, through visible consumption, connects that meaning to the focal food. Consequently, consumers infer greater product naturalness and greater healthiness, increasing purchase intention. This inference depends on how the consumption episode is structured: visible human assistance attenuates the pet advantage by altering the product-use relationship, whereas sponsorship disclosure changes the surrounding commercial context without necessarily disrupting that relationship. Five preregistered online experiments with 2462 retained participants from Chinese consumer panels support this account. Study 1 establishes the effect and examines alternative explanations. Study 2 demonstrates the sequential pathway through perceived naturalness and perceived healthiness. Study 3 manipulates naturalness information to provide causal evidence for the perceived naturalness component of the proposed pathway, Study 4 identifies eating autonomy as a boundary condition, and Study 5 shows that the focal pathway remains evident in the sponsorship disclosure context. The findings distinguish visible product users from promotional sources and reveal a scene-based route through which the contextual features of consumption episodes shape food attribute judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: WISE: An interpretable word intensity framework for emotion-aware conversational systems
abstract: Emotion-aware conversational systems are increasingly adopted in healthcare, yet most emotion detection approaches rely on sentiment polarity, which fails to capture emotional nuance and intensity in short, informal chat messages. To overcome these limitations, this study develops an interpretable emotion-aware framework called Word Intensity Scoring Engine (WISE) that explicitly models emotional intensity in short-form conversational text. Grounded in Plutchik's Wheel of Emotions, WISE integrates lexicon-based emotion labeling, synonym expansion, semantic similarity using word embeddings, and negation-aware feature extraction to calculate intensity-weighted emotion scores at the word level. The WISE framework is evaluated through experimental benchmarking and an expert review involving practicing healthcare professionals. Results show that WISE enhances the performance of ML and LLM-based classifiers. Further, expert evaluations indicate that WISE-derived responses are perceived as professional, contextually appropriate, and empathetic. This study contributes a transparent, theoretically grounded design artifact that advances affective computing research and informs the deployment of emotion-aware conversational agents in healthcare. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Knowledge graph–based data governance for small and medium-sized enterprises: A systematic literature review and socio-technical framework
abstract: Established data governance frameworks provide valuable guidance for large enterprises, yet their assumptions about stable funding, dedicated governance teams, and mature infrastructure often do not reflect the realities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Recent research has explored the use of semantic technologies and knowledge graphs to automate governance tasks, improve traceability, and support policy enforcement. Yet, whether these approaches effectively address SME-specific needs remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic literature review of knowledge-graph-based data governance approaches, focusing on their relevance to SMEs. Following the PRISMA method, we analyzed evidence from 43 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 through multiple lenses, including core data governance activities (Define, Implement, Monitor), components of the Data Governance Institute framework, and stages of the data lifecycle. Using thematic network analysis we synthesize recurring limitations and structural patterns across the literature. Our findings show that while semantic technologies demonstrate strong potential for automating policy enforcement, metadata integration, and interoperability, most approaches are designed for mature enterprises. They commonly assume formal governance hierarchies, specialized expertise, and sustained operational capacity, conditions that are often absent in SMEs. As a result, governance designs are skewed toward technical controls and early lifecycle stages, with limited attention to monitoring, organizational roles, decision rights, and end-to-end governance. Building on these findings, this study advances a socio-technical perspective on data governance in SME contexts by reframing governance as a lifecycle-embedded and practice-oriented capability rather than a purely technical implementation. It further conceptualizes knowledge graphs as boundary objects that mediate between governance intent, technical enforcement, and organizational practice. Our key contributions include a structured synthesis of knowledge-graph-based data governance research, identifies eight recurring gaps that hinder SME applicability, and derives nine design principles alongside a conceptual research framework to guide future research and the development of SME-suitable governance solutions. © 2026

title: Fuel vs. food? Climate shocks, biofuel expansion, and the future of global food security
abstract: The expansion of biofuel production has generated debate over its potential trade-off with food security, particularly regarding land diversion, rising food prices, and climate-related agricultural stress. This study utilizes panel data from 5 emerging (BRICS) and 7 advanced economies (G7) employing Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for robustness to examine the association between biofuel production and agricultural total-factor productivity, crop value, and global food security during the period 2012-2022. Grounded in bioeconomy transition theory, induced innovation theory, the Porter hypothesis, and sustainable intensification, the empirical evidence indicates that biofuel expansion does not create a homogeneous food–fuel trade-off; instead, its associations vary across development and performance regimes. Biofuel production is positively associated with crop value in both groups but shows contrasting productivity associations, particularly across quantiles. Temperature anomalies exhibit heterogeneous associations with agricultural outcomes, while food prices are more strongly associated with food security. In line with induced innovation theory, innovation capacity is positively associated with several agricultural outcomes, while the climate–innovation interaction indicates heterogeneous adaptive associations across country groups. The differing associations of environmental policy stringency are broadly consistent with the conditional predictions of the Porter hypothesis, rather than indicating uniform regulatory benefits. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between biofuel expansion and food-system performance is conditional on development stage, climate exposure, innovation capacity, environmental policy stringency, and food-price conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group
abstract: The energy transition triggers urgent questions about what values are important, who controls transitional processes, and who has the power to define the answers to the climate crisis. Energy companies claim their central role in the development of renewable energy as the ultimate solution. However, communities affected by large-scale renewable energy projects have extensively raised environmental and social justice concerns and denounced the industry's poor practices and abuses.In this article, we analyse 15 socio-environmental conflicts around renewable energy projects owned by the Enel Group, one of the world's largest energy utilities, through the values and valuation languages of the affected communities. We map them onto five dimensions: environmental, health-related, socio-economic, ontological, and political. We build on environmental justice and ecological economics literature on valuation languages and employ counter-accounting to gather bottom-up evidence of grievances.We argue that, while the company claims that RE is the ultimate solution and the ‘Creating Shared Value’ approach is beneficial to all parties, those impacted by Enel's projects question the corporate model of energy transition and defend a plurality of values embedded in relational worldviews that are systematically misrecognised. We eventually criticise the corporate self-attributed moral and value-centred mandate in the energy transition and call for inclusive research about desirable energy futures rooted in plural and relational value systems. title: What counts as urban smartness? A longitudinal thematic analysis of smart city indexes
abstract: Smart city indexes increasingly influence urban governance, policy benchmarking, and investment narratives, yet their conceptual evolution remains insufficiently examined. This article investigates how major smart city evaluation frameworks changed between 2017 and 2022 through a longitudinal thematic analysis of six prominent smart city indexes selected from an initial inventory of sixteen. The findings suggest a shift in the smart city index landscape from more technocentric assessment frameworks toward more integrated evaluation logics that give greater attention to governance capacity, economic conditions, and societal dimensions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From precarious work to occupational health outcomes in hotel housekeepers: a narrative review with meta-synthesis
abstract: Introduction: Hotel housekeepers sustain the core functioning of the hospitality industry yet perform demanding, repetitive, and undervalued work associated with substantial physical and psychosocial risks. Understanding how working conditions shape health, motivation, and lived experience is essential for informing prevention strategies and promoting decent work. Methods A sequential narrative review and qualitative meta -synthesis were conducted to integrate and reinterpret evidence across disciplines and study designs. Searches covered five academic databases and gray literature without year or language limits. Studies were screened using predefined criteria, appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and synthesized through narrative, tabular, and meta -analytical thematic analysis, with findings interpreted through the JD-R framework. Results Findings revealed employment precarity, work intensification, musculoskeletal pain, chemical and biological hazards, and elevated stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Time pressure fostered coping strategies such as skipping meals and delaying bathroom use. Gendered labor divisions, discrimination, and negative supervision contributed to invisibility and limited autonomy. Workers also expressed pride, intrinsic motivation, and collective action to make their contributions visible. Conclusions This review demonstrates that housekeeping is characterized by structural precarity and cumulative health burdens alongside resilience and emerging activism. Improving occupational health requires organizational and policy transformations: realistic workloads, safer equipment, secure contracts, participatory risk management, and leadership practices grounded in dignity and fairness; rather than reliance on individual coping. Structural change is essential to advance safer, more equitable, and sustainable workplaces in the hospitality sector. The JD-R framework highlights the need to reduce demand and strengthen resources. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Research on interruption risk propagation in aircraft supply chain network: A multi-layer network coupling model
abstract: The aircraft supply chain (ASC) is a core component of national high-end equipment manufacturing systems, which have complex network characteristics of strong coupling. Once an interruption occurs at any node, it will propagate to relevant enterprises along the supply-demand relationship. However, the propagation process of interruption risks is not merely a matter of physical transmission, it is typically accompanied by the spread of risk information and the adoption of preventive measures. Therefore, investigating the dynamic coupling characteristics among risk information diffusion, adoption of preventive measures, and interruption risk propagation is of great significance for exploring the interruption risk propagation mechanisms in ASC. Considering the above facts, this paper proposes a three-layer coupled network model. This model divides enterprises into multiple different states and innovatively proposes different network layer propagation mechanisms and interlayer coupling methods. Subsequently, the microscopic Markov chain approach is employed to establish state transition Eqs., and the mathematical characteristics of interruption risk outbreak are derived through theoretical deduction. The proposed model is applied to the risk propagation analysis of real ASC networks, and the proposed method and key findings were visually demonstrated. The research results provide decision-making references for risk management in the aviation industry chain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Trends in access to basic sanitation services across Brazilian municipalities under a new legal framework
abstract: Federal Law No. 14,026/2020 updated Brazil's sanitation legal framework, reinforcing universalization targets for water supply and sewage services. It mandates that by the end of 2033, sanitation contracts must ensure 99% of the population has access to potable water and 90% to sewage collection and treatment. Given Brazil's vast territory and regional disparities, achieving these targets across all municipalities poses a significant challenge. This article examines whether water and sewage coverage rates converged between 2010 and 2022, analyzing municipalities segregated by state and region. The study provides an up-to-date assessment of these indicators and identifies challenges in meeting the established targets. Empirical estimation of convergence draws on economic methodologies for growth and income convergence, incorporating beta-convergence and sigma-convergence hypotheses. This robust methodological approach enables a comprehensive analysis of the evolution of sanitation services in Brazil, offering insights to guide effective public policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Material use and its relationship with per capita income. A panel data analysis at the global level
abstract: Global use of materials has significantly increased over recent decades, causing a wide range of environmental and social concerns. In this study, we use the latest available data from the UN database on global material flows to investigate the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for two widely used material flow indicators, Domestic Material Consumption and Material Footprint, for a dataset of 147 countries. Using both semiparametric and parametric methods over a longer period than any previous study (1970–2019), we find no evidence in support of the EKC hypothesis. A concerning result is that material-income elasticities are higher after 1989, implying that the situation has not improved. We conclude that major changes have not yet occurred in the income-material use relationship and that strong policy measures remain necessary to reduce material consumption. title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors' Takeaways for Future Pandemics
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors' perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. This is positioned as one of the limited studies identifying both positive and negative impacts and suitable preventive measures in managing the identified causes. The findings can be applied for developing contexts of a similar nature, particularly in managing disputes during future pandemics. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships
abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework as an organizing logic, this study examines associations among club anthem attractiveness (CAA), positive emotion (PE), post-exposure brand cognition (BC), and fan–brand resonance (FBR) in sports leisure services. Data were collected from a screened nonprobability online sample of 468 respondents in China. Participants listened to one of three standardized 90-s club anthem excerpts before evaluating CAA, PE, BC, and FBR. CAA was positively associated with both PE and BC, and these responses were positively associated with FBR. The two prespecified coefficient products were positive, whereas the residual direct CAA–FBR association was not significant. A separate balanced validation study (N = 450) supported CAA's empirical distinction from simple anthem liking, PE, BC, FBR, and prior brand attitude. CAA explained additional variance in PE and BC beyond simple liking and pre-exposure controls, while its incremental association with FBR was small. The findings indicate that evaluations of recurring auditory brand cues covary with consumer–brand relationship outcomes alongside affective and cognitive responses. This study extends auditory branding and sensory service literature by conceptualizing recurring branded sound as a service-embedded cue and examining theoretically ordered affective and cognitive associations. Because CAA was measured and the focal constructs were self-reported within one session, the findings support an association-based interpretation and do not establish temporal mediation or causality. © 2026

title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. By conceptualising consumer trust as a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by interactions between users, technology, and institutions, we offer a research agenda with actionable directions for advancing blockchain trust theory and practice. © 2026 The Authors

title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Perceived organizational support buffers these effects. The study contributes to workplace incivility research in collectivist and high power-distance cultures and offers practical implications for hotel management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Incompetence or deception: Unraveling the asymmetric mechanisms of AI hallucinations on trust and distrust
abstract: Reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for knowledge work is increasing, yet confidently presented hallucinations can elicit strong negative user reactions. Existing literature frames hallucinations as technical failures that reduce trust, conflating the decline of trust with the emergence of distrust. However, trust and distrust are theoretically distinct constructs rather than opposite ends of a single continuum. Drawing on information manipulation theory (IMT), this study reconceptualizes AI hallucinations as violations of conversational norms. It proposes a model linking hallucination cues to perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially related to trust and distrust. It further examines whether perceived AI autonomy moderates the relationship between hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The model was tested using a sequential mixed-methods design that combined qualitative semi-structured interviews with a two-wave survey of 506 GenAI users. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings revealed that hallucination cues were differentially associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, with the former more strongly associated with trust and the latter with distrust. Perceived AI autonomy moderated the associations between some hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The PLS-SEM–NCA analysis provided complementary evidence on net effects and necessary conditions that neither method could offer alone. Overall, this study extends research on AI hallucinations by conceptualizing them as distinct forms of conversational norm violations and explaining how different hallucination cues are associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially linked to trust and distrust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Software-defined vehicle ecosystems in transformation
abstract: Context: The automotive industry is transitioning from hardware-centric development toward software-defined vehicles (SDVs), where software drives functionality, value creation, and competitive differentiation. This shift challenges proprietary software development, firm-centric innovation, and traditional supply chain models, giving rise to ecosystem-based collaboration. However, SDV transformation is primarily framed as a technical change, leaving its broader ecosystem implications insufficiently understood. Objective: This study explores the transformation of SDV ecosystems, their stakeholders, collaborative structures, roles and authority, and highlights associated challenges and opportunities. Methods: This systematic literature review collected 351 studies from six databases and selected 25 for detailed analysis. Results: Four interrelated shifts (from hardware-centric to software platforms, from supply chains to collaborative ecosystems, from proprietary to open and standard solutions, and from firm-level control to distributed governance) characterise the transformation, with six levels of collaboration involving twelve stakeholder groups. These collaborations are influenced by five dimensions of authority. The literature also highlights six core software development challenges and various organisational, industry and market, and regulatory, legal, and ethical challenges. It identifies five software development opportunities and various organisational, industry and market, and public value and ethical opportunities. Conclusion: The first contribution integrates previously fragmented literature on the SDV ecosystem transformation, demonstrating how SDVs are transforming the automotive industry through the four interrelated shifts driven by software advancements. Second, it proposes an SDV ecosystems model that integrates SDV architecture, stakeholder groups, collaboration structures, and governance levels to facilitate sustainable SDV ecosystems. Additionally, agendas for research and practice are outlined. © 2026 The Authors

title: Structural Determinants of Household Resilience in Earthquake-Affected Communities: A Case Study from Bawean Island
abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic impacts of the March 2024 earthquake on household resilience in Bawean Island, East Java, Indonesia. Data for this study were collected through a survey with a snowball sampling technique, with a total of 221 valid respondents from affected regions. Using a household survey across 12 affected villages and partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study identifies critical factors contributing to household resilience, namely social, economic, human, and physical capital assets. The findings can be explained in two ways. First, the result confirms social, economic, human, and physical capital as critical resilience determinants. Second, higher household resilience could reduce the impact of natural disasters. This study can be an input for policymakers to strengthen household resilience in disaster-prone areas to support sustainable development goals (SDGs). © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Participatory short film production and student well-being: A narrative review from media literacy and sociocultural perspectives
abstract: In an AI-driven media ecology, short-form video platforms have intensified interest in participatory filmmaking (PFM) as a learner-centered practice in higher education. However, the relationship between student-led short-film production and holistic well-being remains conceptually scattered and methodologically uneven. This narrative review examines how PFM may support student well-being through media literacy and sociocultural learning processes, with particular attention given to the transferability of these mechanisms to Chinese higher education. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2014 and 2025 were searched in Scopus, Web of Science, and CNKI using combinations of “participatory video,” “filmmaking,” “higher education,” and “well-being.” A total of 238 records were screened. Studies were excluded if they focused on non-higher-education settings, addressed media consumption rather than student production, contained no interpretable well-being-related outcomes, or lacked peer-reviewed empirical content. Fifteen studies were retained for full analysis. Data were extracted on context, modality, participants, methods, well-being domains, and pedagogical mechanisms and then coded through a hybrid deductive-inductive thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarke and sensitized by media literacy and sociocultural theory. Three recurring mechanisms emerged: reflective authorship, which supports meaning making, critical judgment, and psychological resilience; collaborative scaffolding, which strengthens belonging, shared regulation, and social confidence; and embodied practice, which connects tool-mediated action to attention, physical vitality, and situated learning. However, the evidence base remains small, course bound, and dominated by short-term qualitative designs, with limited work in non-Western settings. This review therefore proposes the participatory filmmaking well-being framework (PFWF) as an empirically anchored synthesis and outlines implications for curriculum design, student support, and future mechanism-testing research in Chinese universities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The fantasy of digital immateriality: AI, ecologically unequal exchange, and appropriation of lived human time
abstract: The purported immateriality of AI technologies is as illusory as the general understanding of conventional technologies as simply the application of politically neutral knowledge to nature. The materiality of technologies and their foundation in global inequalities has been illuminated by studies of ecologically unequal exchange (EUE). The aim of this article is to extend the applicability of EUE theory to digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) by highlighting how even the data that they process have an inevitably biophysical history. AI technologies represent a novelty mainly in the sense that, in addition to exploiting extractive areas through EUE, they are based on the appropriation of data from the public. We argue for understanding the materiality of data as derived from lived human time. AI's dependence on data can thus be regarded as representing and embodying biophysical processes and asymmetric transfers implicating issues of justice. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: The effect of rosé wine color: A conceptual replication and a generation-based extension
abstract: Recent research on crossmodal correspondences from Jaud et al. (2025) highlighted the role of rosé wine color in shaping consumer responses. Building on their work, this study aims to assess the robustness and generalizability of these findings while extending the original model in two ways. Specifically, by using a within-subjects experimental design conducted in the United States (N = 448), we replicate the model in a different cultural context by shifting from a French to a US sample. Further, we extend the underlying process by introducing perceived lightness as an additional mediating mechanism. Finally, we broaden the model by incorporating generational belonging (Generation Z vs. Generation Y) as a moderating variable. This approach enables us to assess both the robustness and the boundary conditions of previously identified effects of rosé wine color. Our findings contribute to the literature on crossmodal correspondences by demonstrating the stability of color-driven effects while highlighting generational differences in the relationship between perceived fruitiness and willingness to buy. They also offer practical insights for wine producers and distributors seeking to better align product presentation with the expectations of different generation-based consumer segments. © 2026
