title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises
abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. When such content is perceived as violating widely shared social values, brands increasingly attribute such incidents to AI errors. Prior research has mainly emphasized the responsibility-exemption role of AI attribution strategy, offering limited insight into its moral risks, mixed consequences, and underlying mechanisms. Drawing on the fact-value model, this study conducts five scenario-based experiments to examine how AI attribution strategy affects brand trust in this crisis context. The findings reveal a double-edged effect. At the factual level, this strategy increases consumers' perceived responsibility reduction, thereby producing an exemption effect that supports trust repair. At the value level, it also triggers perceived moral indifference, thereby producing a backfire effect that damages trust. This double-edged effect is moderated by public opinion and consumer traits. High negative electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) dispersion strengthens the perceived responsibility reduction path, whereas low negative eWOM dispersion strengthens the perceived moral indifference path. AI literacy strengthens the exemption effect by helping consumers understand AI-related technical limitations, whereas hostile attribution bias strengthens the backfire effect by leading consumers to question the moral motives behind the brand's technical explanation. This study advances crisis attribution research by examining AI attribution as a proactive brand communication strategy under attribution ambiguity and shows how it can reduce factual blame while raising value-based moral concerns. The findings offer guidance for using AI attribution carefully and reducing ethical communication risks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The organic halo effect: A systematic review of the influence of organic labels and claims on healthiness perceptions
abstract: Food labels and claims play an increasing role in shaping consumer perceptions in complex food environments. While claims about nutrients are known to influence judgements of food healthiness, less is known about whether organic cues can lead to similar halo effects. We performed a systematic review to examine how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. We searched Web of Science and PubMed for experimental studies examining the effect of organic cues on food healthiness perceptions. Studies were included if they compared products with and without organic cues and reported outcomes related to perceived healthiness or perceived nutritional content. Of the records screened, 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. We conducted a narrative synthesis following SWiM guidelines, examining differences by cue type and outcome. Most studies found that organic cues increased perceived food healthiness. This effect was observed across both general health evaluations and specific calorie or nutrient judgements. Effects were more consistent for certified organic labels, whereas unofficial claims showed somewhat greater variability across products. A smaller number of studies reported mixed or null results, often depending on consumer characteristics or informational context. This review provides a synthesis of evidence on how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. By clarifying how consumers translate this information into health- and nutrition-related judgements, it contributes to a coherent understanding of the mechanisms underlying health halo effects. These findings suggest that organic cues may simultaneously act as signals of production practices and triggers of broader inferences about healthiness. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: The impact of reverse wording on cross-cultural comparisons of food-related attitudes
abstract: Reverse-worded items (RWIs) are commonly used in multi-item scales to reduce acquiescence bias, yet their implications for cross-cultural food attitude measurement remain underexamined. This study compared positively worded items (PWIs) and RWIs across four established food-related attitude scales using data from 6300 adult consumers across ten countries. RWIs generally showed lower internal consistency and weaker inter-item correlations than PWIs. Items showing the largest cross-country variation in standardized loadings from multi-group confirmatory factor analysis were predominantly reverse-worded. RWIs also produced lower mean scores and generally greater response dispersion than PWIs. These wording-related differences varied by construct and country, followed no uniform pattern across measurement indicators, and may reflect the combined influence of item content, linguistic structure, and culturally patterned response tendencies. Across these indicators, PWI and RWI subsets did not consistently function as psychometrically equivalent components of the same scale. The findings suggest that the use of RWIs in cross-cultural food attitude measurement may introduce wording-related measurement instability, and that wording-direction effects require explicit consideration in the design and evaluation of international consumer research instruments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The grass is not always greener: The effects of local labor market information on search and employment
abstract: We examine how information about local labor market conditions shapes search and employment outcomes for Indian job seekers. Participants were randomly shown information about either job postings, job applicants, or both from a popular job portal for their preferred city and occupation. Treated respondents are more likely to be employed seven months later. This overall effect varies considerably by baseline employment status. Among the initially employed, treatments reduce search off the portal and increase employment, with suggestive evidence of higher persistence in baseline jobs. In contrast, among the initially unemployed, treatments increase search activity but do not raise employment. Employment gains are concentrated among job seekers with less optimistic beliefs about labor market conditions. These findings suggest that limited information about labor market fundamentals may contribute to job churn in lower-income countries. © 2026 The Authors

title: Exploring Lean-Integrated Circular Economy in the Built Environment Setting: Implications for Project Governance and Compliance
abstract: The current study establishes how lean tenets contribute to the circular economy (CE) with exploration of lean tools with circular economy core principles and framework development. While there seem to be synergies between the concepts of lean and CE, the construction management research fraternity has not fully tapped the huge research potential in this domain. To address this gap, a two-phased exploratory qualitative research design is proposed. The first phase involves mapping lean tools with 10 dimensions of CE in the context of the built environment sector through content analysis and expert validation (n=3). Continuous improvement and added value tools of lean attained maximum realization of CE dimensions. The second phase involves semistructured interviews of experts (n=9) on an understanding of the synergies between lean and CE through thematic analysis (TA). The current study identifies predominant lean tools that realize CE dimensions and develops a conceptual model of a lean-driven circular economy (LdCE) framework for construction projects. Also, the lean tenets and their allied tools enabled value optimization through effective mapping of non-value-added processes and minimizing wasteful aspects. These findings are intended to inform engineers, construction managers, and legal practitioners about actionable strategies for promoting sustainable, legally compliant project execution. This study proves to accelerate sustainable construction through a lean and CE integrated framework in developing nations. Analyzing the associativity of the lean tools in realizing the CE dimensions and the strategies of a lean-driven circular economy through models is a novel concept with this research. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Influence of environmental stimuli on sustainable food choices: the moderating role of AI-source disclosure
abstract: Reducing meat consumption is necessary for public health and environmental sustainability. However, while the benefits of positively-valenced nature have been explored, the comparative behavioral effects and mediational patterns of positively-valenced and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli remain unclear. Across three studies, we examined how positively- and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli influence food choices. Study 1 showed that both types of environmental stimuli reduced meat-heavy meal choices compared to the control. Study 2 tested serial mediation models within a dual-system framework, and the results showed that positively-valenced stimuli were associated with stronger nature connectedness and greater consideration of future consequences (CFC), whereas negatively-valenced stimuli were associated with higher guilt and greater CFC. Study 3 manipulated AI-source disclosure for the environmental stimuli. Although AI-source disclosure did not significantly interact with environmental stimuli condition in predicting meat-heavy choices, it significantly attenuated the link between negatively-valenced stimuli and guilt, but did not attenuate the association between positively-valenced stimuli and nature connectedness. Collectively, these findings suggest that the environmental stimuli valence may be associated with food choices through two partially overlapping yet distinguishable psychological pathways, offering insights for nudging sustainable eating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Text-driven causal mapping of PET/rPET circularity in Australia: A dynamic factor–network analysis
abstract: PET circularity is often evaluated by recovery volumes, although performance ultimately depends on whether recovered material can be converted into quality-assured outputs and absorbed by viable end markets. Yet the mechanisms connecting policy, markets, technology, and stakeholder behavior remain dispersed across heterogeneous evidence. We developed a source-attributed, time-stamped causal-network approach using 750 Australian government, industry and NGO, corporate, and media documents published during 2010–2025. Causal extraction, semantic normalization, sentiment assignment, and graph construction yielded 2794 factor nodes and 1588 unique causal edges. The network was strongly externalized: policy, market, and social factors were more numerous and highly connected than internal technical and operational factors. Persistent barriers combined cost and price volatility, inconsistent recyclate quality, infrastructure gaps, and weak policy implementation. Positive mechanisms clustered around standards and measurement, design for recyclability, operational capacity, and end-market development; their circular value depended on retained material quality and the end use reached. Source attribution revealed systematic framing differences, with media coverage concentrating negative implementation narratives. Temporal and regional analyses indicated a shift from limited attention to rapid expansion and subsequent consolidation, alongside national structural hubs and differentiated state pathways. A full-text academic shadow corpus preserved the broad problem domains but changed their hierarchy: academic evidence foregrounded material and processing mechanisms, whereas the primary corpus foregrounded institutional coordination and market implementation. The contribution is therefore not a universal ranking of Australian interventions, but an auditable framework for identifying how technical feasibility becomes, or fails to become, operational circularity under different institutional conditions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Creative or uncreative partner: Comparing humans and AI in collaborative creative tasks
abstract: Creativity is fundamentally a collaborative process. As generative AI becomes increasingly integrated into creative work, understanding how it reshapes collaboration becomes critical. This pre-registered study directly compares human-human and human-AI collaboration dynamics across two creative tasks: the Alternate Uses Task (AUT) and creative short story writing. Participants were randomly assigned to pairs in either human-human (N = 68 pairs) or human-AI (GPT-4o; N = 72 pairs) conditions, with partners alternating turns as first responders to examine how initiation order shapes the creative process. Our findings reveal that the apparent “AI advantage” in creative collaboration is illusory, driven primarily by increased AI verbosity rather than enhanced creativity. Critically, collaboration with AI partners negatively impacted humans' own creative responses compared to human-human partnerships, with human-AI collaboration failing to enhance idea originality or diversity relative to human-human collaboration. Human partners demonstrated higher collaborative creativity that strengthened over time, indicating that current generative AI systems, while producing more verbose outputs, do not replicate the collective creativity characteristic of human-human collaboration. These results challenge assumptions about AI's creative potential, with direct implications for AI system design and collaborative creative practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Navigating AI affective support: The cognitive-affective pathway from appraisal to emotional well-being in learners
abstract: As affective artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in educational contexts, understanding how learners emotionally engage with such systems is both timely and critical. Grounded in cognitive appraisal theory and the theory of affective bonding, this research examines how students interpret AI-delivered affective support during academic stress. Across two preregistered experiments (N = 202; N = 394), we find that AI affective support enhances emotional well-being via affective resonance, the perceived emotional alignment between learner and agent. Study 1 shows that affective resonance mediates the effect of AI affective support on positive and negative affect. title: Identifying a dynamic information trading zone framework via insights from full-scale emergency exercises
abstract: The article examines how the co-creation of a Common Operational Picture (COP) in multi-actor crisis response operations can be understood through the concept of Information Trading Zones (ITZ). The analysis is grounded in the theory of Situation Awareness (SA), including Endsley’s conceptualisation of individual, Team SA and Shared SA, and draws on Galison’s notion of trading zones as intercalation, the insertion of an intermediate concept or mechanism to bridge existing explanatory levels. In this study, ITZ is introduced as an intercalating construct linking information exchange, sensemaking, and coordinated action. Drawing on extensive qualitative analyses of five full-scale crisis exercises, the study traces the evolution of an operational framework that conceptualises ITZ as both a precondition for and an integral component of the co-creation of a COP. Within this framework, ITZ are positioned as socio-technical spaces where information is negotiated, interpreted, and stabilised across organisational boundaries, enabling the development of Shared and Team SA in the face of uncertainty. The article offers concrete recommendations for both researchers and practice, outlining how the interplay among ITZ, COP, and SA can inform the design of information systems that more effectively support coordination, sense-making, and decision-making in Emergency Management contexts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Research on the mechanism of linking time pressure to career growth among hotel employees
abstract: Research overlooks how and why identical cognitive appraisals of time pressure translate into divergent coping behaviors. Drawing upon the cognitive appraisal theory of stress, this study investigates the mechanisms linking time pressure to the career growth of frontline hotel employees. Utilizing a three-wave time-lagged design, we collected survey data from 323 frontline hotel employees in China and analyzed it using PLS-SEM via SmartPLS 4.0. The results reveal that challenge appraisal and hindrance appraisal play differentiated mediating roles between time pressure and career growth, with job crafting serving as a crucial behavioral bridge in the transformation from stress appraisal to career growth. Furthermore, achievement motivation significantly moderates this transformation from stress appraisal to job crafting behavior. This study provides empirical evidence for the hospitality industry to implement differentiated stress management and employee development interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Linking need for cognitive closure to cyberchondria among health information seekers: Disentangling the roles of uncertainty discrepancy, health worry and information processing evaluations
abstract: Despite growing research on online health information seeking behaviors, the psychological factors through which dispositional characteristics are linked to maladaptive information outcomes such as cyberchondria remain underexplored. Drawing on the Theory of Motivated Information Management (TMIM), this study establishes a conceptual framework to examine how the need for cognitive closure is associated with cyberchondria through interpretive constructs (i.e., uncertainty discrepancy and health worry) and evaluative assessments (i.e., perceived health information overload and self-efficacy). The study examines the pattern of associations among these information management constructs as theorized by TMIM. Analysis of data from 581 adults using structural equation modeling demonstrates that the need for cognitive closure was directly associated with cyberchondria and was also positively associated with uncertainty discrepancy and health worry. Uncertainty discrepancy and health worry were associated with perceived information overload and self-efficacy, and perceived information overload and self-efficacy were associated with cyberchondria. This research offers insights into the information management constructs associated with cyberchondria by illustrating how dispositional factors are linked to maladaptive information management outcomes in a pattern consistent with the structure theorized by TMIM. Because the data are cross-sectional, this structure reflects a theoretical ordering assumed by the framework rather than an empirically established temporal sequence. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Artificial general intelligence architectures and evaluation methodologies: A comprehensive review and future research roadmap
abstract: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) seeks to create machines with broad, human-like cognition. However, rapid advances in narrow AI make it clear that general intelligence remains unresolved. This systematic review synthesises AGI research in five dimensions: definitions, enabling technologies, envisioned applications, evaluation methodologies, and open challenges. We performed a systematic search of major academic databases and search engines up to January 2026. After deduplication, two reviewers independently screened 927 records and included 393 studies that met the predefined criteria. We extracted data to address five research questions for each dimension and conducted a qualitative synthesis, as the evidence base did not support a meta-analysis. Across the literature, AGI is primarily characterised by broad adaptability and cross-domain generalisation. The main approaches include symbolic knowledge-based methods, machine learning, cognitively inspired architectures, hybrid neuro-symbolic systems, and brain-inspired or theoretical models Raman et al. (2025) [302]; each contributes partial capabilities, but exhibits limitations in isolation. The proposed application areas include healthcare, education, finance, transportation, smart cities, defence, scientific research, and more. Evaluation practices span multidimensional scales, cognitive test batteries, and safety-oriented benchmarks for alignment and autonomy. However, many benchmarks are saturated rapidly and do not fully capture real-world generality. Persistent challenges include the absence of a unified empirical theory of intelligence; the integration and scalability of heterogeneous methods; symbol grounding and embodiment; value alignment and control of highly capable agents; and the development of rigorous yet comprehensive evaluation protocols. In general, AGI research remains fragmented, with no approach that demonstrates the full spectrum of general cognitive competence. We operationalise “integration” as a system-level property in which learning, reasoning, memory, and social-ethical constraints are coupled through shared representations and closed-loop control so that each component can shape the others during task execution. We also describe two integrative candidate architectures proposed in the literature: (i) a Self-Evolving Binary-Symbolic AGI framework and (ii) the Cohomological Active Inference Architecture (CAIA). Whether a proposed architecture achieves this integration can be measured empirically using multidimensional AGI benchmarks and safety or alignment evaluations discussed in AGI assessment methodologies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Fostering institutional trust and organ donation: Evidence from a randomized informational intervention in Tunisia
abstract: Organ transplantation saves lives and improves the quality of life of patients who would otherwise depend on costly and invasive treatments. The technology is becoming available in low- and middle-income countries, but the gap between the demand for and the supply of organ transplants remains large. In a randomized controlled trial at a Tunisian university, we evaluate an expert-led intervention designed to inform about organ donation and strengthen trust in medical institutions. The intervention consists of a short video testimonial from a heart transplant survivor, a presentation led by a medical doctor and a short Q&A session. We find that the intervention significantly increases deceased donor registration, with suggestive evidence of positive spillover effects on the control group. The survey data provides little support for changes in attitudes and social expectations as potential mechanisms. Instead, it reveals large and statistically significant increases in medical and legal knowledge, religious beliefs supportive of donation, and institutional trust among treated students. Finally, we show that treatment effects on organ donor registration are driven by male students and those whose families likely support organ donation. Targeting older segments of the population may further increase the impact and cost-effectiveness of this intervention. © 2026 The Authors

title: Research trends and conceptual foundations of religious moderation: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Although the concept of religious moderation has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years, comprehensive and globally integrative syntheses remain limited. In many Western scholarly traditions, similar ideas are often articulated through related concepts such as religious tolerance, pluralism, liberal pluralism, or collaborative secularism, resulting in fragmented conceptual discussions across disciplines and regions. This study therefore aims to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of research on religious moderation within global academic discourse. This study employs a hybrid approach combining Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, where the keyword “religious moderation” was searched in article titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search identified 901 publications (2009–2026). After applying the PRISMA screening procedure, 235 articles met the inclusion criteria and were selected for analysis. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, institutional affiliations, and thematic patterns within the field. The findings indicate that research on religious moderation has experienced gradual growth and increasing global visibility. However, the distribution of scholarly contributions remains highly concentrated in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia, suggesting that the concept has not yet diffused widely across Western, Middle Eastern, and African academic traditions. This geographical concentration reveals significant opportunities for comparative, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research. This study also, through an analysis of 235 articles indexed in Scopus, found several studies on the indicators and principles of religious moderation, which play an important role in fostering harmony amid social differences and diversity. In addition, the study proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework linking religious moderation to broader domains including social cohesion, conflict resolution, interfaith relations, family dynamics, and education, highlighting its relevance for sustaining inclusive and resilient communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Mother tongue as a tool for africanization of the curriculum
abstract: This paper explores the prospects of mother tongue education as a tool for the Africanization of the curriculum by addressing the research gap on the decline in the use of the mother tongue in educational institutions. The deliberation is targeted at promoting a more inclusive and culturally responsive education system in which the linguistic identity of learners is respected. Africanization in education aims at recentering African perspectives, values, and knowledge systems, challenging Western-dominated views that have long sidelined African cultures and languages in learning spaces. While many African countries continue to prioritize colonial languages such as English and French in education, the mother tongue remains a vital tool in assisting learners, as colonial languages often hinder learners’ academic success and reduce their engagement in the learning process. However, the African mother tongue remains at risk of becoming extinct as people continue to migrate in hopes of better economic opportunities. This paper reviewed the language policies of selected African countries, emphasizing the urgent need to prioritize mother tongue teaching and to develop African languages as effective instructional media across all subjects, going beyond just language classes to utilize it as a tool to Africanize the curriculum. The implications for the basic school curriculum are discussed, stressing that mother tongue integration not only supports language preservation but also enhances academic achievement and identity formation. The paper calls for curriculum designers, policymakers, and educators to collaboratively embed African languages and knowledge systems into the curriculum. This approach builds an education system that genuinely embodies and supports the values, cultures, and needs of African communities. The insights emerging from this discourse promise to nurture culturally grounded learners who are capable of addressing African challenges through an Afrocentric lens. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: An intelligent spectrum-aware trajectory data reduction approach for maritime decision support systems
abstract: High-quality Automatic Identification System (AIS) data is the cornerstone of modern Maritime Expert Systems and Intelligent Decision Support Systems (IDSS). However, the exponential growth of AIS data challenges the real-time situational awareness and storage capabilities of these systems. Conventional compression strategies face a dichotomy: offline algorithms ensure fidelity but suffer latency, while online methods support streaming but often exhibit “geometric blindness,” neglecting kinematic variations like speed changes along linear paths. This study proposes a novel online method, Frequency-Aware Improved Open Window (FA-IOPW). FA-IOPW uses localized spectral information within an evolving Opening Window to adapt the PED–TED weighting during online compression. To support the evaluation, we developed a visualization platform for trajectory query, compression, comparison, and adaptive-weight display. The platform was tested with historical AIS records and controlled application-level replay; live satellite AIS feeds, production Vessel Traffic Service environments, and shipborne hardware were not included in the present validation. Results demonstrate that FA-IOPW achieves a Pareto-optimal trade-off between compression ratio and reconstruction accuracy. Under high-compression regimes, it significantly reduces position and speed errors compared to mainstream methods. Furthermore, we integrated an AI agent module into the platform, lowering the usage threshold for regular users. As a robust online method, FA-IOPW offers a high-fidelity solution for real-time maritime monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Ethics, economics, and environmental stewardship: Religious moral frameworks as constraints for rational policy choice
abstract: Environmental policy often embeds ethical judgments implicitly in discount rates, welfare weights, prices, or informal constraints. This paper develops a constraint-based framework that makes major ethical commitments explicit before economic optimization begins. Drawing on convergent principles in Jewish, Islamic, Christian, Indigenous, Buddhist, and secular traditions, it identifies stewardship, restraint of waste, intergenerational responsibility, ecological limits, and institutional responsibility as candidate non-compensatory constraints. Economic analysis then compares costs, trade-offs, and institutional feasibility only among policies that satisfy the adopted constraints. Applied water-policy illustrations show how this approach can clarify minimum access, pricing, desalination, and wastewater-reuse choices without claiming that these policies were historically caused by the ethical framework. The contribution to ecological economics is methodological: moral commitments define the admissible policy space, while economics identifies efficient pathways within it. This division of labor improves transparency under moral pluralism and environmental scarcity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Accounting for the risk of restoration failure in ecosystem service valuation
abstract: While ecosystem recovery is widely recognized to vary, valuations of ecosystem services often assume guaranteed outcomes. We examine whether omitting information on restoration failure risk causes bias in the utility estimates of ecosystem services. Further, we examine how two personal attitudes (connectedness to nature and place attachment) influence risk perception. In comparison to previous studies, we integrate both risk (known outcomes and their probabilities of ecosystem service provision following grassland restoration) and uncertainty (unknown outcomes and probabilities) within a single framework. We find that omitting information on risk leads to overestimation of the utility derived from ecosystem services. Controlling for subjective uncertainty and risk aversion using a hybrid choice model, we find no influence of connectedness to nature on risk perception, whereas the negative effect of high restoration failure risk on utility becomes weaker when place attachment is high. Both latent attitudes decrease the utility of uncertainty, i.e., of the opt-out alternative no restoration. Given the substantial utility implications of restoration failure risk, the EU should complement Member State-level monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation with project-level monitoring, open data sharing, and transparent reporting of restoration outcomes to the public. © 2026 The Authors. title: Flying low for greener farms: Configurational pathways linking the low-altitude economy to agricultural green total factor productivity in China
abstract: The low-altitude economy is increasingly viewed as a new technological frontier for agricultural transformation, yet its relationship with agricultural green total factor productivity remains poorly understood. This study examines how low-altitude economy-related conditions are associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity in China. We develop an institutional-technological-scenario framework and apply a sequential mixed-method design that combines qualitative coding, necessary condition analysis and dynamic fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis. The empirical analysis uses a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2022, covering 270 province-year observations. The period is treated as a formative and pre-consolidation stage of the low-altitude economy rather than as a fully mature integrated system. The results show that no single condition constitutes a statistically supported necessary condition for high agricultural green total factor productivity. Exploratory bottleneck analysis nevertheless reveals descriptive threshold patterns at higher outcome levels. The dynamic configurational analysis identifies three pathways associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity, namely technology-application coupling, institution-innovation coupling and scale-application diffusion. The non-high productivity configuration further shows that enterprise development, policy support and market support may fail to translate into green productivity improvement when industrial application is absent. Regional and temporal analyses reveal substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity. The findings suggest that the low-altitude economy is better understood as an emerging socio-technical enabling system rather than as a single UAV-based technology, and that agricultural green transformation depends on the configuration of institutional support, technological capacity and application scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A physics-cognitive proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing collaborative framework for offshore wind farms under extreme met-ocean conditions
abstract: Reliable offshore wind operation requires maintenance decisions that account for multi-source uncertainty including stochastic degradation, environmental shocks, and incomplete condition information. Extreme met-ocean conditions also restrict maintenance access, coupling uncertainty in asset health with fragmented vessel operating windows and high operation and maintenance costs. To address these uncertain issues, this study proposes a proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing strategy. A physics-based competing failure model is developed to capture both cumulative degradation and shock-induced damage. To reduce the physics-cognitive divergence, defined as the inevitable divergence of state estimations from physical wear, an air–sea collaborative fleet using unmanned aerial vehicles enables active monitoring and dynamic replanning. A marginal-benefit-driven opportunistic maintenance strategy is introduced to exploit short and variable weather windows. A continuous weather filtering module proactively schedules critical tasks before adverse conditions, integrated with a bi-level mixed-integer non-linear programming model, which is solved by a bi-stage collaborative solution algorithm to co-optimize multi-vessel routing and maintenance bundling. Simulations on a 78-turbine offshore wind farm over a 90-day period show that the proposed strategy reduces total O&M costs by 96.4%, 46.4%, 19.4% and 46.2% compared to corrective, condition-based, non-opportunistic baselines and sequential scheduling and routing strategy, respectively. The framework offers a scalable and computationally efficient solution for multi-vessel routing and opportunistic maintenance, contributing to the development of cost-effective offshore asset management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The security unlock: How rural social pension makes people more entrepreneurial?
abstract: Previous literature on the determinants of entrepreneurship has not explored the role of social pension. Leveraging variation in the roll-out timing of a universal rural pension program across Chinese counties, our analysis, at both the individual and aggregate levels, reveals that pension provision led to an increase in entrepreneurship among the younger generation. We show that this effect operates through two primary channels: an intergenerational transfer channel and a local demand channel. Specifically, the pension program mitigates upward transfers from adult children to elderly parents, while boosting local consumer demand, which exerts a demand-side “pull” effect on enterprise establishment. Our findings may shed new light on the interplay between pension, intergenerational resource allocation, and entrepreneurial activity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Governance and renewable energy adoption: Assessing the state's role in solar energy uptake in Iran
abstract: This study investigates how government managers in Golestan Province, Iran, interpret and respond to national directives aimed at promoting solar energy adoption. Despite Iran's substantial solar potential and supportive national policies, the uptake of solar technologies within public institutions remains limited. Drawing on 28 semi-structured in-depth interviews with senior and mid-level government officials and employing thematic analysis, the study identifies two overarching themes: Managers' Actions and Managers' Orientations. The findings demonstrate that socio-political acceptance within the state is severely constrained by institutional decoupling. Provincial managers face conflicting mandates—such as national renewable targets that conflict with provincial security directives requiring diesel generators—leading to symbolic compliance (e.g., installation of decorative solar panels) while continuing reliance on fossil fuels. By integrating socio-political acceptance with institutional decoupling, the Technology Acceptance Model, and Diffusion of Innovations, this study extends renewable-energy acceptance research from public and market actors to acceptance and resistance within the state apparatus. The findings suggest that aligning national and provincial directives, strengthening inter-agency coordination, and improving managerial capacity are essential for renewable-energy implementation in centralized governance systems and other Global South contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Facilitator or hallucination trap? A social-cognitive account of AI-generated misinformation handling in GenAI-assisted L2 writing
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has demonstrated remarkable potential in second language (L2) learning, yet it is prone to hallucinations. Empirical research on how GenAI-generated misinformation is handled in educational contexts remains scarce. Accordingly, little is known about how these practices shape learning processes and outcomes. Guided by social cognitive theory, the current study frames students' GenAI-assisted L2 writing (using a tailored GenAI writing agent) in a hallucination-prone context in which misinformation was implanted. We examine AI literacy, higher-order thinking resources (i.e., critical thinking and creativity), L2 writing resources (i.e., L2 writing grit and self-regulatory writing strategies), English writing self-efficacy (EWSE), AI-generated misinformation detection (AI-MD), and L2 writing performance within this framework. Using a multi-method approach, combining a qualitative interview study (N = 35), two lab experiments (N = 140), and a large-scale questionnaire survey (N = 406), we find that critical thinking positively predicts GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance via AI-MD, and that negative priming on AI hallucinations significantly improves students’ AI-MD and their GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance, relative to neutral or positive priming. Furthermore, the cross-sectional survey focuses on personal factors and shows that AI literacy significantly predicts EWSE both directly and indirectly through a cognitive–generative pathway involving higher-order thinking resources and a motivational–regulatory pathway involving L2 writing resources. These findings extend social-cognitive accounts of GenAI-assisted L2 writing and inform instruction that helps learners evaluate AI outputs, manage misinformation risks, and sustain their own writing processes. © 2026

title: Self-disclosure to intelligent virtual agents: A scoping review and the disclosure affordance–actualization–governance framework
abstract: Intelligent virtual agents (IVAs) have become digital social objects to which people disclose personal, emotional, health-related, and other sensitive information. Yet similar cues—including anthropomorphism, social presence, empathy, gaze, anonymity, and structured questioning—are associated across studies with greater disclosure, refusal, impression management, socially desirable responding, or discomfort. Searches covered four bibliographic databases without publication-year restrictions through March 17, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar searching on May 20, 2026. This review, reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), maps 88 empirical studies and introduces the Disclosure Affordance–Actualization–Governance (DAAG) framework as a middle-range account linking specific empirical findings with broader explanations of IVA-mediated disclosure. DAAG distinguishes sociotechnical interaction ecology; perceived safety from judgment, relational receptivity, expressive latitude, and boundary agency; disclosure actualization; affective, relational, and functional consequences; governance; and evidential reach—the extent to which studies observe perception, behavior, consequences, time, and governance. The literature is most developed for disclosure onset, sensitive reporting, emotional expression, and immediate system acceptance, but remains thin on persistence, reciprocity, subjective–behavioral divergence, correction, revocation, and downstream data use. Recurrent patterns are consistent with IVA cues being interpreted through evaluation risk, partner responsiveness, observability, topic sensitivity, competence, privacy, and control. DAAG is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a framework for explaining when digital social interaction supports, redirects, or appropriately constrains self-disclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Journey to the bargaining table: Signaling, seeking, and screening
abstract: Negotiation scholarship has focused extensively on what happens at the bargaining table—how parties make offers, manage conflict, and reach agreements. Far less attention has been paid to how parties get to the table in the first place. In this article, we argue that the journey to the table deserves greater scrutiny. We organize pre-table dynamics around three behaviors: signaling (communicating whether and how negotiation might proceed), seeking (approaching a counterpart to propose bargaining), and screening (deciding whether to engage with or withdraw from a seeker). We review recent and foundational work bearing on each, identifying where the field has made progress and where significant gaps remain. These pre-table processes have important implications for negotiated outcomes, for negotiations that never occur, and for understanding how opportunity and bias operate before parties ever sit down together. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Disaster Management: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
abstract: This study presents an examination of artificial intelligence (AI) in the disaster management (DM) cycle to support human decision-making systems. There is an urgent need for holistic application strategies that support disaster risk reduction given the increasing frequency and severity of disaster events. This stems from the growing adoption of AI technologies, including machine learning (ML), deep learning, and natural language processing in transforming disaster management. This is to enable the development of high-performance tools for assessing disaster impacts and addressing un-met human needs. This study reviewed journals and conference proceedings articles from three different academic databases: Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Article selection and query refinement were conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to support methodological approach. The review explored scholarly perspectives on AI application in DM phases to support human-centered decision-making processes in reducing disaster impacts on human lives. Findings from the review indicate that most existing studies focus primarily on the AI application in the response phase. Despite its potential, integrating AI into disaster management remains challenging, particularly due to widespread misconceptions about adoption of AI, as well as ongoing ethical, trust, and security concerns. This study emphasizes the comprehensive application of AI to enhance planning, encourage proactive measures, and improve response and recovery efforts during disaster events. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Autonomy-supportive mediation and scam susceptibility: The role of literacy among middle-aged and older adults
abstract: Although online scams increasingly threaten middle-aged and older adults, existing research has largely focused on individual literacy and short-term interventions, leaving the development and application of scam literacy in everyday contexts less understood. Drawing on parental mediation theory and self-determination theory, this study conceptualizes autonomy-supportive mediation (ASM) as a family-based socialization context for developing aging parents' scam-related literacy. It also considers face concern, a personal orientation reflecting individuals’ motivation to protect their social image from potential social judgment. This study tested two complementary models that distinguish between the foundation of scam literacy (scam knowledge) and its activation (cyber-risk beliefs). Data were collected through a cross-sectional vignette-based survey of 404 middle-aged and older adults in China between February 13 and February 27, 2025, using a volunteer-assisted convenience sampling strategy. The results indicated that higher levels of ASM were linked to lower scam loss, with this association mediated by scam knowledge and moderated by face concern. Moreover, ASM was positively related to cyber-risk beliefs, which were subsequently linked to greater systematic information processing and suspicion toward potential scams. These findings suggest that effective scam prevention depends not only on what individuals know, but also on whether they recognize and respond to risks in real-world situations. This study highlights the importance of autonomy-supportive family communication in combating online scams. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Why and when does leisure-time physical activity enhance hospitality employees’ job satisfaction
abstract: Employee engagement in leisure-time physical activity has been associated with greater job satisfaction. However, the conditions under which and the reasons why leisure-time physical activity enhances job satisfaction need to be better understood. Drawing on the integrated perspective of proactivity and the work–home resources model, we propose that employees with lower levels of proactive personality particularly benefit from leisure-time physical activity because it helps them proactively manage their vitality, thereby increasing job satisfaction. Consistent with our expectations, the results from a sample of 197 hotel employees indicate that leisure-time physical activity positively predicted job satisfaction through proactive vitality management. Moreover, the mediating effect of proactive vitality management was more substantial among individuals with lower proactive personality. We discuss the theoretical and practical implications of these findings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Evolution of recommender systems: Approaches, advances, paradigm shifts, and future directions
abstract: Recommender systems are essential tools across numerous digital platforms, helping users discover relevant products, content, and services. Research has traditionally focused on prediction accuracy and relevance, relying primarily on collaborative filtering and matrix factorization techniques. With the increasing complexity of user behavior and data modalities, modern systems have moved beyond simple rating prediction to address additional objectives, including fairness, transparency, privacy, long-term engagement, and trustworthiness. This article systematically reviews the evolution of recommender systems, covering key stages from early predictive models to modern human-centered and trust-aware systems. Each stage is discussed in terms of methodological advances and practical applications. Emerging paradigms, including causal reasoning for bias mitigation, reinforcement learning for long-term optimization, federated and privacy-preserving learning, explainable recommendation techniques, and blockchain-based trust mechanisms, are analyzed. These developments illustrate a broader shift from static, correlation-driven predictions toward adaptive, context-aware, and human-centered intelligence. By organizing research into coherent clusters, this review provides a unified perspective on the field, highlights the connections between past and current approaches, and identifies promising directions for next-generation recommender systems that balance accuracy, user satisfaction, ethical considerations, and long-term system effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
abstract: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management. © 2026 The Authors

title: Generative AI use and sustainable pedagogical practices as predictors of 4Cs skill development: The mediating role of digital literacy among international postgraduate students in China
abstract: This study examines how Generative AI Use (GAU) and Sustainable Pedagogical Practices (SPP) are associated with international postgraduate students’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4Cs), with Digital Literacy (DL) examined as a mediator. Using survey data from 369 international Master’s and PhD students at China’s C9 League universities, this study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis. The 4Cs were modeled as a higher-order construct comprising four lower-order dimensions. The results show that both GAU and SPP are positively associated with students’ 4Cs, with SPP showing the largest standardized direct association. GAU and SPP are also positively associated with DL, which in turn is positively associated with the 4Cs. Significant indirect associations of both GAU and SPP with the higher-order 4Cs construct were observed through DL. The ANN results provide complementary predictive evidence, with SPP showing the highest normalized predictive importance, followed by GAU and DL. Together, the findings support a technology–pedagogy–capability perspective in which pedagogical design shows the largest standardized direct association with 4Cs development, while DL functions as a learner-side information-processing capability linking AI-supported and sustainability-oriented learning experiences with competence development. For practice, the findings suggest that universities may benefit from embedding generative AI within structured, sustainability-oriented learning activities that emphasize information verification, responsible use, and collaborative problem solving. These findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional, self-report design and the specific context of international postgraduate students at China’s C9 League universities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How media narratives shape public sentiment toward electric micromobility: Stronger effects for e-scooters than e-bikes
abstract: Public sentiment toward electric micromobility, particularly e-scooters and e-bikes, is increasingly shaping safety debates and regulatory responses; yet, these attitudes and perceptions have not been systematically evaluated within a unified framework, nor is it clear to what extent they reflect stable judgments versus sensitivity to external narratives. This study addresses these gaps by quantifying public sentiment toward e-bikes and e-scooters and evaluating their responsiveness to controlled negative media narrative exposure. A unified survey framework was developed to enable consistent evaluation, combining statement-based measures with image-based scenario assessments. Two complementary studies were conducted with Australian participants. Study 1 (N = 1027) established baseline sentiment in the absence of media exposure, and Study 2 (N = 1025) examined how responses shift following controlled exposure to negative news headlines. The results showed that public sentiment is multi-dimensional and mixed. While both modes received moderate recognition in terms of sustainability and legitimacy, practical acceptance remained lower, particularly for e-scooters. Exposure to negative media narratives produced broader and more consistent shifts toward less favorable sentiments for e-scooters, especially in perceptions of rider behavior and public-space interaction, whereas e-bike responses remained comparatively stable and more robust to media narrative exposure. In contrast, evaluations of concrete negative situations showed no systematic change following exposure, indicating that these evaluations are grounded in situational interpretation rather than external framing. The findings suggest that public sentiment should be used cautiously to inform policy development. While consistent concerns linked to observable safety issues justify targeted interventions, broader sentiment shifts may reflect narrative influence rather than actual conditions. Effective policy should therefore be informed not only by public sentiment but also by objective evidence on behavior, exposure, and risk. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Spatial optimization of land use for synergizing economic development and carbon neutrality based on an efficiency-driven PLUS model
abstract: Optimizing land-use allocation is important for achieving regional carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets. Existing land-use simulation studies generally incorporate carbon objectives through ex-post assessment or macro-level land-demand optimization, leaving historical grid-level carbon–economic performance disconnected from future spatial allocation. To further address this limitation, we developed LUCE-PLUS, a framework that links grid-scale land-transition accounting and efficiency evaluation with PLUS-based spatial simulation. Using Jiujiang City, China, as a case study, we quantified conversion costs, economic-output changes, and carbon emissions induced by observed land-use transitions from 2010 to 2020 at a 30-m resolution. A single-stage mixed-integer linear programming super-efficiency range-adjusted measure (Sup-RAM) model treated carbon emissions as a weakly disposable undesirable output and enabled discrimination among efficient grid-level transition units while ensuring Pareto-efficient projections. The resulting surfaces of economic efficiency and carbon–economic synergy efficiency were incorporated into PLUS as scenario-specific predictors of land-use expansion probabilities. Land-use patterns in 2030 were simulated under natural-development, economic-dominant, and carbon–economic dual-objective scenarios while aggregate land demand and planning constraints were held constant. Mean carbon–economic synergy efficiency was 20.5% lower than mean economic efficiency, indicating that economic efficiency alone may understate the carbon-related environmental costs of land-use transitions. Compared with the dual-objective scenario, the economic-dominant scenario increased the projected GDP increment by only 0.04% but raised land-use-change-induced carbon emissions by 7.3%. Impervious-land expansion under the dual-objective scenario also showed a stronger tendency toward locations associated with lower carbon-stock losses. LUCE-PLUS therefore provides a performance-informed approach to low-carbon spatial allocation under fixed land-demand targets. From an environmental impact assessment perspective, the framework could support alternatives analysis in strategic environmental assessment of territorial spatial plans by enabling ex ante comparison of projected land-use patterns, carbon-stock changes, and economic outcomes under consistent planning constraints. © 2026

title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
abstract: Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. Existing research provides valuable insights into individual hazards, infrastructure components, modeling methods, and resilience metrics, but these insights remain difficult to translate into preliminary decision support because they are organized across different hazard types, sectors, analytical scales, and decision contexts. This article presents a structured state-of-the-art review of natural hazards, CIS impacts, and resilience enhancement. A two-pathway review strategy was adopted. A Web of Science (WoS) core search was used to characterize the bibliometric landscape and identify WoS-sourced core synthesis studies, while a targeted anchor-search pathway was used to verify foundational concepts, hazard mechanisms, methodological approaches, resilience frameworks, and authoritative institutional sources. The review clarifies the conceptual distinction among dependencies, interdependencies, compound hazards, cascading failures, service disruption, and resilience; synthesizes cross-hazard infrastructure impact mechanisms; compares major method families for hazard-impact and resilience assessment; and develops a synthesis-derived rapid resilience assessment framework for preliminary screening and prioritization under constrained data and time conditions. The synthesis indicates that future CIS resilience assessment would benefit from moving beyond isolated asset-damage analysis toward integrated workflows that link hazard loading, component vulnerability, network functionality, service consequences, recovery capacity, uncertainty, and feasible intervention choices. The article contributes a more transparent evidence-source structure, an evidence-to-decision bridge, and a bounded decision-oriented framework for organizing future research and practical resilience screening. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: When imperfect food meets joint consumption: a social influence perspective
abstract: Drawing on social influence theory, this research examines the interaction effect of food appearance (imperfect vs. perfect) and consumption context (solo vs. joint) on consumers' preferences. Across five experiments, we show that a joint (vs. solo) consumption context exacerbates the reduction in consumers' purchase intention toward imperfect food. In addition, perceived risk and purchase embarrassment mediate this interaction effect on both purchase intention and willingness to pay (WTP). We further identify self-construal and discount information as boundary conditions. Regarding self-construal, for consumers with an interdependent self-construal, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. In contrast, for those with an independent self-construal, these amplifying effects are not significant. In terms of discount information, when it is displayed, joint consumption amplifies the effect of imperfect appearance on perceived risk, purchase embarrassment, and purchase intention. When it is absent, however, only the effect on purchase intention remains, albeit attenuated. Finally, the presence of discount information shifts the underlying mechanisms of the interaction toward greater reliance on indirect pathways. This research offers practical guidance for promoting suboptimal food in joint consumption contexts. © 2026

title: Teaching by example? Teacher ICT use and middle school students’ computer and information literacy across China and the United States
abstract: Background: In the digital era, Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) has become a crucial educational outcome. While teacher Information and Communication Technology (ICT) use is widely promoted to enhance student digital skills, its effectiveness may vary significantly across different national education systems. Aims: This study investigates the impact of teacher ICT use on middle school students' CIL in China and the United States. It aims to compare these cross-national effects and examine the mediating roles of school ICT resources and institutional support in shaping these relationships. Methods: Using nationally representative data from the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS) 2023, this research employs regression models and instrumental variable (2SLS) methods to address potential endogeneity. Mediation analyses further explore how school-level factors transmit teacher ICT effects. Results: The analysis reveals striking cross-country differences: in China, all dimensions of teacher ICT use significantly improved students' CIL, whereas these effects were statistically insignificant in the United States. School ICT resources and support fully mediated teacher ICT effects in China but only partially mediated ability effects in the U.S. Additionally, student background factors consistently influenced CIL across both countries. Conclusion: While teacher ICT experience demonstrates universal importance, the broader impact of instructional ICT practices depends critically on national context and institutional support systems. The findings highlight the complex interplay between teacher practices, school resources, and national educational environments in shaping digital literacy outcomes. © 2026

title: Exploring Italian consumer perceptions and acceptance of innovative foods and food technologies: insights from a national survey
abstract: Innovative foods and food technologies face barriers to adoption in Italy, where food plays a central role in identity and social life. This study investigates Italian consumer responses to seven innovative food products and technologies using a consumer survey (N = 2000), stratified by age, gender, and geographical region. The survey included psychometric scales assessing food neophobia, food technology neophobia, disgust sensitivity, trust, sensation seeking, and health interest. It measured perceptions of risk, benefit, familiarity, and emotions associated with each product. Findings indicate that Italian consumers show high levels of food and technological neophobia, coupled with low trust and strong health concerns. Acceptability varied significantly across sociodemographic groups: higher education and income were associated with higher trust and sensation seeking and lower neophobia, whereas female and older respondents exhibited higher disgust sensitivity and greater resistance to innovation. Exploratory clustering identified two broad clusters of aggregated consumer profiles. One cluster was associated with younger age, higher educational attainment and household income, together with greater trust and sensation seeking, whereas the other was associated with older age, lower educational attainment and household income, together with greater food and food technology neophobia and disgust sensitivity. Emotional responses emerged as correlates of acceptability, with curiosity most positively and disgust most negatively. Products most aligned with product ideals were plant-based proteins, algae, and unusual fruits, while insect-based proteins and cultured meat faced the greatest barriers. These findings highlight the importance of reinforcing trust and curiosity while addressing disgust to promote sustainable Italian food innovation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Gendering conversational AI in human–AI interaction: The role of interaction context and sexist ideology in shaping user evaluations
abstract: As human–AI interaction becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, users often infer social identities from AI systems, including gender. Moving beyond the conventional view of AI gender as a static, designer-assigned attribute, this study conceptualizes AI gender as a user-constructed perception shaped by contextual cues. Integrating social role theory, the stereotype content model, and ambivalent sexism theory, we conducted a 2 (AI gender cues: male vs. female) × 3 (interaction context: service-oriented, warm-authoritative, vs. serious-authoritative) between-subjects experiment with Chinese participants (N = 833) to examine how interaction context, perceived AI gender, and sexist ideology jointly shape evaluations of AI competence, warmth, and trustworthiness. The results showed that interaction context significantly influenced gender attribution, with the serious-authoritative condition eliciting stronger gender categorization and a masculinization bias regardless of assigned gender cues. The evaluative consequences of perceived AI gender were also context-dependent: perceived femininity consistently linked with warmth, but was associated with competence and trustworthiness primarily in the serious-authoritative condition. Hostile and benevolent sexism further moderated these relationships in distinct ways. By shifting attention from designed gender to perceived gender, this study offers a more process-oriented account of AI anthropomorphism and demonstrates the value of integrating the stereotype content model with ambivalent sexism theory to explain bias in human–AI evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Sensing the path forward: AI as amplifier in sensory and consumer science
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how sensory and consumer data are collected, analyzed, and used. A common fear is that algorithms will displace trained panels and that predictive models will replace expert judgment. We argue the opposite: as AI automates what is easy to formalize, the value of what only humans can do (embodied sensing, cultural interpretation, ethical judgment, and meaning-making) rises. This paper is not a systematic review. It advocates a particular perspective (AI as amplifier of sensory expertise), informed by on-the-ground experience through the recent rise of large language models, including what has worked and what has not in practice. Three industry case studies from PepsiCo, Danone, and Kenvue support that perspective. The principles (knowledge management, automation, predictive modeling, people-centered adoption; humans in the loop; culture before algorithms) are meant to apply beyond large companies, including academia and smaller groups. That perspective also guided a selective literature reading focused on Food Quality and Preference and related journals, mainly from 2022 to early 2026. We clarify what AI is and is not, trace the path from chemometrics to neuromorphic sensing, and describe a four-pillar framework from a Pangborn 2025 industry workshop. Self-reported case outcomes include up to 50% faster analysis and a 75% reduction in reporting time; calculation details were not disclosed to us and the figures are not independently validated. The three organizations built the same capabilities in different orders and met the same barriers (culture, talent, IT collaboration). We also propose narrative-driven analysis with large language models and a near-term research agenda. Central message: when machines predict, humans must decide. © 2026

title: Prioritizing configuration relevance via compiler-based refined feature ranking
abstract: Modern programming languages, most notably Rust, offer advanced linguistic constructs for building highly configurable software systems as aggregations of features—identified by a configuration. However, they pose substantial challenges for program analysis, optimization, and testing, as the combinatorial explosion of configurations often makes exhaustive exploration infeasible. In this manuscript, we present the first compiler-based method for prioritizing configurations. Our approach consists of four main steps: (1) extracting a tailored intermediate representation from the Rust compiler, (2) constructing two complementary graph-based data structures—a feature dependency graph capturing inter-feature code-level dependencies weighted by predicate structure, and an atom dependency tree encoding the extent of code governed by each feature—, (3) using centrality measures to rank features, and (4) refining the ranking by considering the extent of code they impact. A fixed number of most relevant configurations are generated based on the achieved feature ranking. The validity of the generated configurations is guaranteed by using a SAT solver that takes a representation of feature dependencies in conjunctive normal form. We formalized this approach and implemented it in a prototype, RUSTYEX, by instrumenting the Rust compiler. An empirical evaluation on higher-ranked open-source Rust projects shows that RUSTYEX efficiently generates user-specified sets of configurations within bounded resources, while ensuring soundness by construction. The results demonstrate that centrality-guided configuration prioritization enables practical exploration of large configuration spaces, and we discuss the implications and open challenges for future configuration-aware analysis and optimization. © 2026 The Authors

title: The neglected dimension: Arousal, emotions and product choices
abstract: This article presents an overview of the ways in which arousal may be an important influence on consumer product choices. It is recognised that the recent emphasis on measures of emotions in consumer studies has its origins in the limitations of measures of liking to predict choices, and that there is evidence that such measures have added value to traditional hedonic ratings. The possibility that this improvement derives from the fact arousal is implicitly included in emotion measures is considered. In addition, measuring arousal may avoid some of the uncontrolled aspects of measuring emotions, including those related to individual variability in language use. The research evidence for arousal being directly involved in consumer decision making is discussed. Finally, there is an overview of the ways in which arousal can be assessed in consumer studies. © 2026 The Author

title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: UK bioenergy policies and implications for global land use change
abstract: Bioenergy is central to UK decarbonisation policy, yet its reliance on imported biomass and crop-based biofuels raises concerns about land use change (LUC) and indirect land use change (ILUC) in supplier countries. This study provides a data-driven, ex-post assessment of land use implications associated with two UK bioenergy policy pathways: forestry-derived biomass supported by the Contract for Difference (CfD), and 1st generation biofuels supplied under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation (RTFO). Import data for 2015–2022 were linked to forestry biomass productivity and country-specific crop yields to estimate direct land use footprints in major supplier countries. Wider ILUC-consistent signals were then assessed using observed land use, production and trade trends from 2000 to 2022, with particular focus on the US and Brazil. Results show that UK-bound forestry-derived biomass was mainly associated with land footprints in the US, Canada, Latvia and Estonia, while UK-bound 1st generation biofuel land demand became increasingly concentrated in the US and Brazil by 2022. Sensitivity analysis showed that lower productivity assumptions increased estimated land requirements, but did not alter the main supplier-country patterns. Overall, UK bioenergy imports represented a small share of total land use in major supplier countries. The study found no persistent national-scale ILUC signal detected in the US or Brazil. The findings suggest that ex-post land use monitoring can complement model-based ILUC assessment and improve the evidence base for bioenergy sustainability policy. © 2026 The Authors.
