title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Large language model-based carbon emission forecasting: A sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework with transformer-long short-term memory networks
abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions from coal, oil, natural gas, cement, and total CO2 is critical for formulating effective emission reduction strategies and carbon trading policies. However, existing models are plagued by overemphasis on total CO2 prediction, overreliance on single-task learning that overlooks cross-source correlations, neglect of sentiment information in carbon-related texts, and the absence of domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) for carbon sentiment extraction, which severely impairs their prediction accuracy and generalization ability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a novel sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework for carbon emission forecasting, which integrates an LLM with a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) network. First, a domain-adapted LLM is developed based on DeepSeek-R1 and a multi-level fusion attention mechanism, enabling efficient sentiment feature extraction from carbon emission reports (e.g., policy, transaction, social awareness) with few-shot data. Second, a Transformer-LSTM-based multi-task learning model is designed to synergistically predict emissions from the five aforementioned sources by exploiting shared features and the complementary strengths of parallel computing and long-term dependency capture. Finally, a strengthened blood-sucking leech algorithm with Cauchy chaotic mutation and chaotic mapping is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of the multi-task model, thus avoiding local optima and enhancing convergence stability. Validated on real-world data from the International Energy Agency, the proposed framework reduces the root mean square error by 11.14 tons compared with benchmark models. Meanwhile, the developed LLM achieves a sentiment classification accuracy 0.145 higher than baseline methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of integrating sentiment information in carbon emission forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Visions, narratives and numbers: How roadmapping enables industrial transformation toward decarbonisation
abstract: The transformation to a low-carbon industry requires different actors to work together and align their strategies. To support this process, policy and industry in many European countries have been driving the development of industry technology roadmaps at sectoral and national levels. However, limited attention has been paid to how visions, narratives and quantitative modelling work together within roadmapping to enable alignment and transformation across organisational, industry and policy levels. We examine industry technology roadmaps in six selected European countries, using secondary material, survey responses and two focus groups. The analysis is based on a conceptual framework that integrates the design and process elements considered important for roadmap development and implementation, complemented by the requirements for promoting industrial transformation rooted in the literature on socio-technical change. While most roadmaps included sophisticated modelling techniques and quantified scenarios, the study shows that a well-articulated narrative is equally important in mobilising stakeholders toward long-term industrial decarbonisation goals. In addition, the case studies illustrate that strategic planning processes of industrial companies benefit from having a forum to assess the future potential of specific technologies with other companies and along the value chain, thereby helping them manage uncertainty in investment decisions. © 2026

title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was -1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately -6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of -6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects. © 2026 The author(s). title: Automatic binary security classification of arabic mobile app reviews using transformer models and active learning
abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. However, existing research has largely focused on English reviews and lacks systematic approaches for identifying security-related feedback in Arabic, a low-resource language in this domain. In this paper, we address this gap by developing an integrated approach for automated binary classification of security-related versus non-security-related Arabic mobile app reviews, grounded in a structured set of security requirement categories derived from software engineering literature. We collected 14,667,283 reviews from 56 mobile applications across multiple domains, including government, finance, and social platforms. Using natural language processing techniques and sentiment-based filtering, positive reviews were removed as a dataset-reduction step, while neutral and negative reviews were retained for subsequent analysis. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. The active learning process resulted in a final training dataset of 10,632 expert-validated reviews. In addition, 1000 expert-validated reviews were reserved as a held-out test set and excluded from model training. The training dataset was used to fine-tune three transformer models, namely CAMeLBERT, MARBERT, and Paraphrase, for binary classification of security-related and non-security-related reviews. CAMeLBERT achieved the highest performance among the fine-tuned models, with 95.76% accuracy and 95.77% F1-score under 10-fold cross-validation and 91.20% accuracy and 91.16% F1-score on the held-out test set. To support practical adoption, we developed a web-based interface integrated with a large language model to enable real-time classification and provide interpretable explanations. The resulting dataset and developed approach contribute to advancing security-aware analysis of Arabic user-generated content and support software engineers in identifying security-related concerns in mobile application reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Use of Social Network Analysis for community-led area-based fisheries management: The case of tropical lobster fisheries
abstract: Co-management is essential for successful community-based fishery reserves such as Mexico’s Fishing Refuge Zones (FRZs), but they can be hindered by gaps in institutional capacity that undermine collaborative governance. This study analyzes the governance networks underpinning FRZs in Punta Allen and Maria Elena, two small-scale fishing communities within the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Mexican Caribbean. Using a social-ecological system lens and social network analysis, we analyzed the structure, cohesion, and resilience of the governance networks of both communities, using semi-structured interviews and a weighted interaction index that integrates communication frequency and quality, trust, and collaboration. Results show structural differences between governance networks. Punta Allen exhibits a more decentralized, cohesive, and diversified network that links community actors, civil society organizations (CSOs), and government agencies, fostering multiple pathways for collaboration. María Elena presents a more centralized and segmented configuration, with strong dependence on CSOs and limited integration of governmental actors. Resilience simulations further demonstrate that decentralized structures maintain coordination under disturbance more effectively than centralized ones. Although FRZs are formally established by federal authorities, their local-level operational governance is sustained by informal social relationships that enable trust, reciprocity, and local coordination. Our findings show that FRZs can function as effective co-management instruments within MPAs, but their long-term viability requires strengthening institutional coordination, diversifying actor participation, and ensuring consistent governmental presence to reduce fragmentation. By diagnosing governance gaps and highlighting structural strengths, this study provides a transferable framework for improving the design, implementation, and policy uptake of community-based conservation and small-scale fisheries management initiatives. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Community participation intensity on asynchronous biodiversity and human well-being responses to ecological restoration in global drylands
abstract: Ecological restoration serves as a key strategy for addressing desertification and ecosystem degradation in global drylands. However, achieving synergistic benefits for both biodiversity and human well-being remains a significant challenge for sustainability. Although community participation is increasingly promoted, quantitative evidence remains limited on how participation intensity is associated with measured ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. A dataset encompassing 744 effect sizes from 41 independent studies across global drylands was constructed to conduct a meta-analysis. The synthesis indicated positive benefits relative to degraded baselines, while composite biodiversity and composite human well-being showed asynchronous responses across community participation intensity. For composite biodiversity, the pooled mean estimate corresponded to an average increase of 122.11% relative to degraded baselines. Limited community participation was associated with long-term positive patterns in the composite biodiversity (159.35%) and composite human well-being (130.71%), whereas extensive community participation showed an evidence-limited and marginally supported positive tendency in composite human well-being in the short term. Eventually, we propose an adaptive framework in which livelihood-support components may be emphasized during early restoration, followed by lower-disturbance stewardship considerations as biodiversity recovery stabilizes. Overall, our findings provide exploratory quantitative evidence for discussing how community participation may affect asynchronous ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. The findings also underscore the importance of shifting from instrumental approaches to a more systemic understanding of environmental communication. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and ecological determinants of cutaneous Leishmaniasis in Errachidia Province, southeastern Morocco: A 16-year municipality-level analysis with SARIMA forecasting
abstract: Leishmaniasis is a vector-borne parasitic disease transmitted by female sandflies of the genus Phlebotomus and affects approximately 1.2 million people annually in more than 90 countries worldwide. Morocco remains one of the most affected countries in North Africa, where the disease continues to represent a major public health concern. This study aimed to analyze the spatial and temporal trends of leishmaniasis incidence across all municipalities of Errachidia Province between 2010 and 2025 and to assess the influence of ecological, demographic, and socio-economic factors on its distribution. Also, the study aimed to predict the monthly CL cases using the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model. Epidemiological data on parasitologically confirmed cases obtained from the Errachidia Provincial Health Delegation were processed using geographic information system (GIS) tools and statistical methods to explore spatial patterns and correlations with environmental and socio-demographic variables. The models are trained and evaluated using monthly CL cases collected from 2010 to 2025, with the optimal model selected based on Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). During 16-years study period, 7034 cases were recorded in Errachidia Province, with the highest incidence reported in 2010 (860 cases per 100,000 inhabitants). Overall, the incidence showed marked temporal fluctuations but demonstrated a general decreasing trend over the study period. A pronounced spatial heterogeneity was observed between rural municipalities (Sid Ali, Melaab, and Ferkla) and urban municipalities (Errachidia, Arfoud, and Goulmima) ( p < 0.01). The disease was slightly more frequent in females (54.41%) than in males (45.59%), and a significant difference was observed among age groups ( p = 0.019), with the 0–9 and 10–19-year groups being the most affected. Seasonal analysis revealed a peak incidence during winter. In addition, higher incidence was associated with low- to medium-altitude municipalities, while no significant association was observed with poverty or vulnerability indices. The SARIMA (0,0,1)12 model demonstrated the best predictive performance. These findings highlight the heterogeneity and ecological determinants of leishmaniasis in southeastern Morocco and may support targeted surveillance and control strategies in high-risk areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Trends and directions in military professionalism research: A scopus-based bibliometric analysis
abstract: The current bibliometric analysis examines the evolution of research related to professionalism in the military based on the Scopus database. Author contributions, country-based production, institutional engagement, and co-occurrence analysis were reported. The biblioshiny in the R language was used to examine the data, and the Garza-Reyes was utilised to ensure the validity and reliability of the data. In this case, a total of 35 relevant publications were selected to be reported in the bibliometric analysis. Based on the finding, the USA is the most contributing country and has a steady increase in the number of publications, which peaked in 2023. However, even though the USA was indicated as the country with the most publications in this research theme, the United Kingdom was found to have the most impactful and influential publication, with a total cited score of 49. In terms of the most contributive affiliation, Uniformed Services University from the USA was dominant and followed by two universities from the Netherlands namely, VU University Medical Centre and the Netherlands Defence Academy. For the most contributive authors, Cole Rebekah and Rudinsky Sherri L were identified as the most productive authors. In this case, the author production over time analysis indicates Cole Rebekah, and Rudinsky Sherri L, are the most productive and influential authors in this research theme. In the thematic map analysis, the concepts of 'human', 'military personnel', and 'humans' emerge as well-developed and central, indicating that discussions around military professionalism are strongly anchored in the human dimension of service members. It was emphasised in the co-occurrence analysis that highlights the centrality of military personnel, humans, and humans, which appear as the most frequent and interconnected terms, indicating that research on military professionalism is predominantly framed around the human dimension and the role of personnel. Finally, the current research reveals three major military professional research directions through Multiple Correspondence Analysis namely, (1) education and social identity, (2) healthcare personnel and military health, and (3) professionalism and ethics, with demographic factors serving as a transversal element across clusters. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: QSRR-Based RP-HPLC Method Development for Antiviral Drug Analysis: Machine Learning, Design of Experiments, and Sustainable Analytical Strategies—A Review
abstract: Pharmaceutical quality control and research depend on the creation of effective, reliable, and sustainable analytical techniques for antiviral medication analysis. The development of conventional RP-HPLC methods frequently depends on lengthy experimental trials, which might raise the need for resources, analytical time, and solvent usage. A useful computational technique for connecting molecular structural characteristics to chromatographic retention behaviour and assisting in the advancement of predictive methods is Quantitative Structure–Retention Relationship (QSRR) modelling. The promise of QSRR-based approaches to comprehending retention processes, forecasting chromatographic behaviour, and improving chromatographic circumstances has been further increased by recent developments in machine learning (ML), chemometrics, and design of experiments (DoE). The latest developments in QSRR-based RP-HPLC method development for antiviral medication evaluation are covered in this review, with a focus on molecular descriptors, statistical and machine learning-based predictive techniques, DoE-assisted optimisation, and sustainability analytical strategies. Additionally, covered are pertinent databases, computing systems, and software tools for chromatographic optimisation, model creation, validation, and descriptor synthesis. The opportunity of combining QSRR with ML and DoE to lessen experimental workload, enhance prediction and optimisation, and support more effective chromatographic technique development is demonstrated by published works. The difficulties with data quality, descriptor selection, model interpretability, overfitting, validation, repeatability, and portability are further examined in the review. The application of QSRR in sustainable pharmaceutical evaluation could be further enhanced by explainable artificial intelligence, automated and high-throughput processes, sophisticated chemometric techniques, and green analytical principles, according to future viewpoints. All things considered, the integration of QSRR, ML, and DoE offers a viable foundation for developing RP-HPLC methods for antiviral drug analysis that are predictive, effective, and environmentally friendly. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Perceptions of biodiversity benefits of regional food: A Q-method study from a German biosphere reserve
abstract: Increasing consumer demand for food produced using biodiversity-friendly practices may create market incentives that support biodiversity conservation. However, there is limited understanding of consumer perspectives regarding the perceived biodiversity aspects of such products. This study represents an empirical approach to investigate how consumers perceive biodiversity-related attributes of regional products and how these perceptions influence purchase motivation in the context of the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve. Regional product criteria related to biodiversity protection and prevalence within the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve were assessed through a literature review. The Q-method was applied to determine their influence on consumer purchase motivation. Key findings include the determination of three prevalent consumer perspectives consisting of Traditional Regionalists valuing local community support and cultural identity, Environmental Pragmatists appreciating criteria with direct environmental protection benefits and Quality Seekers being motivated by concerns of food safety and transparency in the food industry. The regional product criteria were revisited regarding their importance for the individual consumer perspectives, providing insights into how each group relates to criteria associated with perceived biodiversity benefits. Equal to future research prospects extending on the relevance of demographic and economic variables, these insights suggest potential pathways for adapting and expanding the offering of biodiversity-friendly regional products, in combination with consumer-oriented communication and marketing approaches. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: The Economic Value of Animals Traded for Traditional Medicine in Ghana and Its Effect on Biodiversity Conservation
abstract: The trade and use of wildlife for traditional medicine are widespread in many developing countries and continue to expand. The increasing demand for high-value, endangered animals used in traditional medicine has raised important conservation concerns. In this first nationwide cross-sectional study of its kind in Ghana, we assessed the economic value of wildlife traded for traditional medicine through interviews with 133 vendors in 48 markets and examined its implications for biodiversity conservation. The mean annual sales per vendor were estimated at USD 15,123.6. Based on an estimated 1,074 vendors engaged in the trade of Animal-Based Medicine (ABM) nationwide, the annual economic value of the sector was approximately USD 16.2 million. We found that the vendors' sex, age and religious affiliation were not statistically associated with their annual trade values. However, vendors whose clientele consisted predominantly of females recorded significantly higher annual sales than those serving predominantly male clients (USD 247,852.8 vs. 59,765.6; p-value = 0.004). The most expensive animal parts included endangered species such as lion (Panthera leo), tiger (P. tigris), African savanna elephant (Loxodonta africana), and Home’s hinge-back tortoise (Kinixys homeana). Our findings showed that the ABM trade in Ghana provides employment and income for many actors along the supply chain, and contributes millions of dollars annually to the national economy. These findings highlight the need for stakeholders and policymakers to strengthen collaboration in regulating the harvest and trade of wildlife used in traditional medicine to promote both sustainable livelihoods and biodiversity conservation in Ghana and across sub-Saharan Africa. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Comparing AI chatbot users and non-users in Germany: Reasons for use, addictive AI chatbot use, mental health, and loneliness
abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots is becoming increasingly popular worldwide. To prevent potential negative consequences associated with the use at an early stage, it is crucial to understand its associations with mental health. Therefore, the present study compared people who use AI chatbots with those who do not engage in AI chatbot-interactions in terms of mental health and loneliness. Moreover, we investigated potential mechanisms associated with addictive AI chatbot use. Data of 7,312 persons (3,729 users: 42.1% men, 57.9% women; Mage = 42.23, SDage = 13.33; 3,583 non-users: 42.6% men, 57.4% women; Mage, = 54.28, SDage = 14.49) from the German adult population were collected via an online survey. AI chatbot users had significantly higher levels of loneliness, depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms, and significantly lower levels of life satisfaction than non-users. Users primarily engaged in AI chatbot-interactions for informational and practical reasons, such as obtaining information and inspiration, and receiving text-related assistance. The frequency of AI chatbot use to escape negative emotions was significantly positively associated with addictive tendencies. Loneliness statistically mediated the association between addictive AI chatbot use and the mental health variables. Most observed effect sizes were small. The present findings show that using AI chatbots for emotion regulation is positively associated with higher addictive tendencies and lower levels of mental health. Further experimental longitudinal research is urgently needed to clarify causal mechanisms of these associations. © 2026 The Authors

title: Divergent relationships between moral disengagement and cyberbullying bystander response behaviors: Examining the amplifying roles of humor and anonymity
abstract: While bystander response behaviors are pivotal for cyberbullying (CB) intervention, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding their correlates, partly because it has often treated diverse bystander responses as a monolithic construct and failed to distinguish constructive defense from aggressive defense. Furthermore, few empirical studies have examined how digital affordances interact with individual factors in relation to diverse bystander responses within a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) framework. To address these gaps, this study examined the main and interactive associations of individual moral disengagement (MD), perceived anonymity, and humor of CB with four distinct online bystander responses (constructive defense, aggressive defense, inaction, and reinforcement). A final analytic sample of 1201 Chinese secondary school students, selected via multi-stage random sampling, completed a survey assessing MD, CB contexts, and real online bystander responses. Multilevel analysis indicated that MD, perceived anonymity and humor were consistently and negatively associated with constructive defense but positively associated with inaction. Conversely, MD and anonymity were positively associated with aggressive defense, whereas humor showed no significant link. Regarding reinforcement behaviors, perceived anonymity and humor were positive predictors, whereas MD exerted a non-significant association. Moderation analyses revealed that anonymity strengthened MD's positive associations with inaction and reinforcement, whereas humor amplified MD's association solely with reinforcement. These findings underscore the necessity of distinguishing constructive from aggressive defense and integrating individual moral cognition with contextual cues for both exploring correlates of online bystander response and designing CB interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Enhancing situational awareness in health systems: A scoping review of technologies and cross-industry insights
abstract: Background: Situational awareness technologies are increasingly utilised in healthcare systems to facilitate timely and coordinated decision-making. Reported implementation considerations include data quality, governance, and integration into everyday workflows. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map technologies, systems, and methods used to enhance situational awareness in health service delivery and to identify approaches used in other industries that could be adapted for healthcare, particularly in regional and remote settings. Methods: We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance for scoping reviews. Electronic databases (PubMed and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between January 2000 and October 2025. Reference lists and citation searches in Google Scholar were also examined. Records meeting the inclusion criteria were screened and reviewed, with key data extracted using a structured charting form and synthesised into seven application domains. Results: Searches identified 744 records, of which 23 studies were included. These covered diverse technologies such as dashboards, forecasting models, alert systems, and geospatial decision environments. Most studies were from high-income countries (n = 19). Studies reported potential benefits for visibility, coordination, and decision-making. However, most evidence was descriptive, with limited evidence of whether these systems improve service delivery. Recurrent implementation challenges included data fragmentation, limited interoperability, and misalignment between governance and workflow. Conclusions: This review highlights the need for more rigorous and context-sensitive evaluations of technologies used to enhance situational awareness in healthcare, especially in regional and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

title: Pyrolysis of biomass feedstocks for hydrogen-enriched syngas production: Cold gas efficiency modelling, latin hypercube uncertainty analysis, and parametric stress analysis
abstract: Biomass-derived syngas offers a viable pathway for producing renewable, hydrogen-rich fuel gas. However, its conversion performance is influenced by feedstock type, temperature, feed rate, and moisture content. This study develops a Cold Gas Efficiency (CGE) model for four agricultural feedstocks: wheat, barley, oilseed rape, and beans. Temperature-dependent regression correlations are developed for the main syngas components and gas flow rate using experimental data. Results show that CGE is highly sensitive to temperature, with low-temperature stress (0–5th percentile) reducing mean CGE by up to 22%. High-moisture stress (95–100th percentile) produced an even larger decline, lowering mean CGE from ∼44% to ∼35% for wheat and compressing the distribution into a low-performance regime. Regression-based tornado charts indicate that temperature is the strongest linear driver (coefficient = +0.44), while Spearman rank correlations highlight feed rate as the most monotonic negative driver (−0.41). Feedstock probability density functions (PDFs) show that wheat as the most efficient and least variable performer, while Oilseed Rape (OSR) and beans exhibited broader distributions due to higher ash-related inhibition of char reactivity. The thermochemical and statistical results demonstrate that operational uncertainty, such as temperature and moisture, dominates CGE variability. This underscores the need for robust control strategies in small-scale pyrolysis systems. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Proactive vs reactive destination revitalisation
abstract: Destinations evolve through lifecycles, with a very real risk of entering long-term decline in the post-maturity phase. Decline is not inevitable, though, for it depends on whether destination stakeholders recognise early symptoms and respond appropriately. Unfortunately, the literature suggests that timely, anticipatory responses are rare. Instead, most destinations fail to detect or act on early warning signals and only respond reactively after decline has set in. This paper develops a conceptual model that identifies and contrasts reactive and proactive responses to post-maturity decline. The model is derived from a systematic synthesis of case-study evidence of 50 case studies examining destination decline and attempts at rejuvenation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Personality engineering with AI agents: A new methodology for negotiation research
abstract: According to canonical negotiation theory, people's success in a negotiation depends on how well they balance competing demands—empathizing and asserting, demonstrating concern for other and concern for self, being soft on the people and hard on the problem. Yet people struggle to manage these tensions, so researchers have lacked the ability to rigorously test the field's prescriptions under controlled conditions. AI agents do not face the same limitations, and their precision, repertoire, consistency, and scalability enable a new class of experiments to contribute to negotiation theory. In this article, we introduce personality engineering—a methodology that precisely parameterizes the personas of AI agents based on established personality frameworks—and propose how this method can be used to study the traits and behaviors of negotiators. Given its relevance to negotiation theory, we propose the interpersonal circumplex—and its two core dimensions of warmth and dominance—as a foundational coordinate system for the field. This approach offers both a rigorous methodology for testing classic negotiation theories and a practical guide for designing the personas of AI negotiation agents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Creating markets for under-utilised fish species: Consumer valuation of a co-created fish finger
abstract: It is common practice to discarded under-utilised fish species that are caught as bycatch because of their low market value. In this paper, we examine whether locally co-created and produced fish fingers, made from locally sourced under-utilised fish species are valued by consumers by employing a discrete choice experiment (DCE). A novel feature of this study is that we consider three versions of the fish finger, sourced from three UK ports: Plymouth, Lowestoft and Grimsby. Our DCE employs a novel set of attributes to capture the unique characteristics of product design and development of the fish finger. Results reveal that all attributes are positively valued, with the largest for fish that are sustainably caught. We also find that distance to the product locality does not materially affected consumer valuation. Location comparisons indicate limited differences overall for the three versions of the fish finger. These results indicate that sustainability information is a primary driver of demand for processed seafood using species with historically low market uptake, while local cues add value without substituting for sustainability. Our findings can help inform efforts to reduce discarding of under-utilised fish species that remains a significant issue in many fisheries. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Analysis of retail resilience in Seoul's neighborhood commercial districts Amidst the COVID-19 shock
abstract: This study examines the economic resilience of neighborhood commercial districts in Seoul in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Moving beyond static before–after comparisons, we employ a Panel Interrupted Time Series (Panel ITS) design to separately identify (i) the immediate level shift at the onset of the shock, conceptualized as resistance, and (ii) the subsequent change in the growth trajectory as conditions transitioned toward the endemic phase, conceptualized as recoverability. The results show that structural diversity, operationalized via Shannon's entropy, functions as a key buffering mechanism: it attenuates initial revenue losses and is associated with a steeper post-shock recovery trend. Importantly, we also document pronounced spatial heterogeneity across Seoul's five major sub-markets. Central business districts exhibit heightened exposure and larger initial downturns, while recovery trajectories vary across sub-markets. Taken together, these findings imply that urban management should complement place-based physical upgrading with ecosystem-oriented strategies—specifically, “portfolio diversification” approaches that strengthen sectoral complexity and reduce systemic vulnerability within local commercial ecosystems. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. In the 90° case, VG orientation achieved the highest electrical efficiency at (Re = 11000), achieving an electrical efficiency of 16.9% and maximum achievable electrical power output of approximately 88 W, after accounting for DC fan power consumption, with the 90° VG configuration still showing the highest system electrical power. The 30° scenario, by contrast, resulted in the best thermal efficiency—nearly 80% and the greatest thermal power—over 420 W demonstrating practical merit in providing guidance for selecting PV cooling configurations based on specific electrical-output or thermal-recovery priorities. ©2027 The author(s). title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Research on online multi-step short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on selective representation-driven concept drift adaptation
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the secure operation and optimal scheduling of power systems. However, PV power data are highly non-stationary due to weather fluctuations, seasonal transitions, and changing operating conditions, which often cause concept drift in real-world scenarios. Most existing methods are developed in offline settings and lack the ability to adapt continuously to evolving data streams. To address this issue, this study proposes an online learning framework for multi-step short-term PV power forecasting. Specifically, a shared-parameter dual-branch Informer concept encoder is designed to capture concept discrepancies between historical and incoming data, while a mixture-of-experts adaptive parameter generator is introduced to produce targeted update parameters for different drift patterns. In addition, a selective segmentation mechanism is incorporated into the TimeBridge backbone to improve the modeling of critical temporal blocks. Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for drift-aware online PV forecasting and offers practical support for enhancing the reliability, stability, and dispatch efficiency of power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. title: Comparative evaluation of SRF-PLL and instantaneous-power LVRT control for a three-wire grid-connected PV system under ground faults
abstract: The performance of low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control depends on the voltage information used for synchronisation and current-reference generation, as well as the physical current paths of the converter. In this paper, four synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) and instantaneous power theory (IPT) implementations are compared on a common 1.504 MW photovoltaic simulation model under single line-to-ground and double line-to-ground faults. The three-wire converter is connected through a delta–grounded-wye transformer. Consequently, its zero-sequence line current is constrained to zero, although ground-fault current is present on the grounded transformer side. The current-control action is therefore confined to the two independent converter axes. The comparison uses conventional and positive-sequence-conditioned SRF and IPT implementations with a shared reactive-current-priority LVRT law, DC-voltage regulation and current-reference limits. For the double line-to-ground case, positive-sequence IPT provides 730.6 kvar at the low-voltage measurement point, compared with 376.1 kvar for instantaneous-voltage IPT, while its nonfundamental current residual decreases from 22.06% to 0.037%. However, the latter controller has a smaller 100 Hz active-power component, demonstrating a trade-off between power oscillation and current quality. Actual transient current reaches 1.234 pu despite a 1.2 pu reference ceiling. Sequence-extraction diagnostics against established DSOGI and DSC methods, together with transformer-side measurements, explain these outcomes. Hardware-in-loop captures document laboratory-platform observations; all quantitative controller comparisons are based on simulations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From generative AI usage to entrepreneurial intention: The sequential roles of task and social self-efficacy
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is rapidly evolving and creating new possibilities for supporting students' entrepreneurial development. However, limited research has examined how GAI usage is associated with entrepreneurial intention (EI) through specific psychological pathways. Drawing on self-efficacy theory, this study examines the relationship between GAI usage and EI, focusing on the mediating roles of task and social self-efficacy. Using survey data from 521 Chinese university students, this study empirically tests the proposed model. The results show that GAI usage is positively associated with students' task and social self-efficacy. However, task self-efficacy (TSE) is not directly associated with EI. In contrast, social self-efficacy (SSE) accounts for a significant indirect association between GAI usage and EI. Moreover, a significant sequential indirect association is observed, linking GAI usage with EI through TSE and SSE. By disentangling the distinct roles of TSE and SSE, this study shows that the association between GAI usage and EI is consistent with pathways that differ in their functions and proximity to entrepreneurial action. The findings also provide practical insights for entrepreneurship education and AI-supported learning environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Short-term emission pathways in India's iron and steel sector: A hybrid framework combining quantitative methods and bottom-up modelling
abstract: This study presents a hybrid assessment framework to quantify current greenhouse gas emissions and evaluate decarbonization pathways for India's iron and steel industry up to 2030. The framework establishes a sectoral emissions baseline and examines the impact of alternative mitigation scenarios, providing a foundation for long-term decarbonization planning beyond 2030. The industry was categorized into two segments: major integrated steel producers, representing more than 57% of national crude steel output, and other producers, comprising predominantly electric-route and small-to-medium-scale operations. Emission intensity estimates for major producers were derived from reported production and emissions data, whereas emissions from other producers were assessed using a bottom-up, process-based estimation. The study estimated the baseline emission intensity for financial year 2023–24 at 2.31 tCO₂/tcs, with major producers averaging 2.53 tCO₂/tcs and other (secondary) producers operating at a lower intensity of 2.02 tCO₂/tcs. Six scenarios were modelled through 2030, revealing that a combination of 30% scrap use and 50% renewable electricity offer the most effective short-term mitigation, reducing intensity to 1.66 tCO₂/tcs. While emissions from major producers remain largely stable, most reductions are driven by secondary producers, highlighting their greater decarbonization potential. Despite these improvements in carbon intensity, projected growth in steel production is expected to increase total sectoral emissions by approximately 20–74% by 2030, depending on the scenario considered. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: What Strategies Can Payers Use to Negotiate Medicine Prices Globally? Insights and Lessons for Low-Income Countries from a Scoping Review
abstract: Objectives No comprehensive global review has synthesized mechanisms, strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges of pharmaceutical pricing policies. This scoping review aimed to examine global pharmaceutical pricing policies and generate policy-relevant insights, particularly for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods Electronic searches were conducted in Medline, CINAHL, EconLit, and Embase using predefined inclusion criteria. Gray literature was identified through government publications and World Health Organization reports, and reference lists of relevant studies were screened. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines. Results Searches conducted up to May 2024 and updated in February 2026 identified 88 eligible studies. Reference pricing was the most commonly reported strategy, used in 85% of identified countries, offering simplicity and transparency through price benchmarking. Value-based pricing was widely adopted in high-income countries, aligning prices with health outcomes but requiring strong health technology assessment infrastructure. Managed entry agreements were reported in 56% of countries and were used to improve access to new medicines while mitigating financial risk. Indication-specific pricing was implemented in 9 countries but faced operational challenges. Compulsory licensing in several LMICs improved access to essential medicines at lower cost, although concerns regarding impacts on pharmaceutical innovation were noted. Most countries combined multiple pricing approaches to balance affordability, access, and innovation. Conclusions Although value-based pricing and managed entry agreements are common in high-income settings, simpler approaches such as reference pricing and compulsory licensing may be more feasible in LMICs. Context-specific strategies are needed to balance access, affordability, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

title: From waste to Watts: Causal evidence on AI-enabled waste-to-energy and financial performance in tourism and hospitality using an empirics-first investigation
abstract: This study examines whether artificial intelligence enabled waste to energy adoption improves financial performance in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms and identifies the mechanisms and conditions shaping these effects. Using an empirics first mixed methods design, we combine interviews with 41 managers and a firm year panel of United Kingdom listed tourism, travel, and hospitality firms from 2015 to 2025. Difference in differences models with firm and year fixed effects show that adoption is associated with significantly higher financial performance, particularly at greater levels of adoption intensity. The findings indicate that energy cost savings and operational efficiency partially explain these gains. Performance benefits are also stronger in firms with higher baseline waste intensity and during periods of elevated energy prices. The study demonstrates that AI enabled waste to energy functions as an operational capability that can generate measurable economic value when integrated into organisational routines and governance systems. © 2026 The Author.

title: Architected NiTi alloys with elastically dominated regions for efficient and stable elastocaloric cooling
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling based on stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) in NiTi alloys shows great potential for low-carbon thermal management, but the functional performance–cyclic stability trade-off remains unresolved. Here, an integrated strategy of macro–microstructure fabrication is proposed to mitigate this trade-off by architecting the NiTi alloy into elastically dominated buffering regions and phase-transforming regions. In situ experiments confirm that the designed structure spatially distributes stress and temperature. Microscopic analysis further reveals that preferential longitudinal-direction martensite growth and regular secondary twins can effectively suppress plastic damage accumulation and improve reversibility. title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Decarbonization within racial capitalism continues to reproduce extractivist inequalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Exploring the key drivers of biogas adoption: a business model for livestock farmers in developing countries
abstract: The increasing number of livestock farms, coupled with inadequate waste management infrastructure, has become a growing concern, contributing to environmental pollution and productivity loss. Biogas technology presents a viable solution to address these challenges by transforming waste into a sustainable energy source. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the key factors influencing the adoption intention of biogas technology as a business Model among livestock farmers. Employing a purposive sampling approach, this study gathered data from 336 livestock farmers. To ensure a comprehensive analysis, a combined methodological framework integrating both symmetric and asymmetric techniques was utilized, providing a profound understanding of the determinants impacting the intention to adopt biogas technology. This study observes a notable consistency between the findings derived from PLS-SEM and ANN. The analysis indicates that awareness of consequences (AOC) significantly influences ascription of responsibility (AOR). Additionally, findings indicate that personal norms are significantly shaped by herd mentality, initial cost, AOC, AOR, and self-esteem. Furthermore, herd mentality, personal norms, and self-esteem are significantly associated with biogas adoption. However, no significant association was found between perceived ease of use and personal norms. Meanwhile, findings from the fsQCA revealed eight distinct pathways leading to a strong intention to adopt biogas, highlighting herd mentality and AOC as critical prerequisites. Insights gained from this study will be instrumental for stakeholders involved in shaping policies, making investments, and providing technological assistance for the effective installation and operation of biogas technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Navigating travel paradoxes: Gen Z coping responses and implications for destination management
abstract: Paradoxes involve contradictory yet interdependent poles that persist rather than disappearing when one side is chosen. Tourism routinely exposes travelers to such tensions, but traveler-level paradoxes and the responses used to navigate them remain underexamined. Using the early tourism-recovery period of 2022 as the empirical context, this study examines paradoxical tensions perceived by young adult Gen Z student travelers and how they respond to them. A two-stage qualitative design was employed. Study A recruited 98 Norwegian Gen Z student travelers, of whom 95 provided useable responses; Study B recruited 48 Gen Z student travelers from the United Kingdom and the United States, of whom 46 provided useable responses. Online open-ended essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, with constant comparison used as an iterative coding technique. Four persistent traveler-perceived tensions emerged: personal travel fulfillment versus environmental responsibility, community economic benefit versus community livability, business recovery versus service-capacity strain, and travel maximization versus travel restraint. Responses clustered into four types: integrative or balancing, prioritization, avoidance or resignation, and externalization or delegation. These responses did not permanently resolve the paradoxes; instead, they temporarily stabilized the tension, privileged one pole, reproduced it, or displaced responsibility. The study therefore positions the 2022 recovery period as an external intensifying condition that made enduring tensions especially visible and connects traveler paradox management to destination governance and shared responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A robust energy management model for unbalanced microgrids under electricity price uncertainty considering central inverters and demand response for voltage unbalance mitigation
abstract: The increasing penetration of unbalanced loads, such as single-phase electric vehicles, in microgrids (MGs) can lead to significant Power Quality (PQ) issues, requiring demand response and ancillary services for mitigation. In this regard, an energy management model for renewable energy resources (RES) and energy storage (ES)-based buses is proposed, in which central inverters are used to support PQ and coordinate energy trading. An unbalanced IEEE 13-bus test system is used to evaluate the proposed framework, with particular emphasis on voltage unbalance mitigation and energy management. The results show that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage unbalance Indicator (VUI) from approximately 4% to below the 2%, with only a 0.35% increase in operating cost. In addition, a robust optimization approach is employed to address electricity price uncertainty, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework under uncertain operating conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: GenAI support to the rescue: Mitigating employees’ psychological stress following tourism service recovery
abstract: Growing evidence suggests that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has a notable impact on employees' attitudes and behaviors, yet its potential to mitigate psychological stress remains underexplored. Combining conservation of resources (COR) theory with the “computers are social actors” (CASA) paradigm, this study investigates whether and how GenAI support (emotional versus informational) reduces tourism employees' post-recovery psychological stress. The results show that: (1) GenAI support effectively alleviates such stress following tourism service recovery; (2) emotional (vs. informational) support exerts a stronger stress-alleviating effect, which is serially mediated by social presence and emotional energy; (3) framing GenAI as an assistant (vs. a friend) further amplifies the relative effectiveness of emotional over informational support. This study enriches the understanding of GenAI's benefits and extends the workplace support literature. It also offers actionable insights into leveraging digital support tools to manage employee stress in tourism workplaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Direct Technology Diffusion in Higher Education: Evidence from Doctoral Students
abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Using a quantitative survey of research scholars, the study finds that direct diffusion significantly improves outcomes. Similarity levels decreased substantially under direct diffusion, indicating more accurate application of plagiarism rules. Additionally, direct diffusion reduced the time required and lowered costs considerably. The findings suggest that direct access empowers users, minimizes intermediary-related inefficiencies, and enhances both effectiveness and efficiency. The study highlights cost-effectiveness as a key enabler and recommends that policymakers and institutions promote direct technology diffusion to improve adoption and strengthen academic integrity in higher education. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Assessment innovation in management education: Authentic assessment evaluation to develop workplace-ready graduates
abstract: Authentic assessment is increasingly seen as essential in management education for aligning assessment tasks with the complex, collaborative, and uncertain, multi-stakeholder demands of modern workplaces. This paper argues that, despite its popularity, the impact of authentic assessment on graduate preparedness remains poorly understood. To address this, the paper builds and evaluates an integrative model relating authentic assessment design, feedback and reflection, perceptions of assessment value, professional self-efficacy, and perceived workplace outcomes among management students. Drawing on literature about authentic assessment, experiential learning, situated cognition, assessment for learning, and employability, the paper frames authentic assessment as a holistic pedagogical system. A cross-sectional survey of 412 undergraduate and postgraduate students in business and management at four universities provides the empirical basis. The instrument was honed through expert review and a pilot test, and analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity checks, correlations, and hierarchical regression and mediation tests. The findings show that authentic assessment design strongly correlates with workplace readiness, especially when dialogic feedback, reflection, and professional self-efficacy are present. External audience group projects, live case analysis, simulations, and portfolio-based evaluation proved effective with clear criteria and guided post-task reflection. The paper contributes a process model and actionable design principles for educators to enhance employability through meaningful assessment, advancing the discourse on management education. © 2026

title: Time for challenge, money for relaxation: The resource-activity fit in tourism
abstract: Although money and time are essential resources that influence consumer decision-making, research has mostly ignored how resource concept activation affects tourists' decisions in the context of tourism. Drawing on mental simulation theory, this study investigates how activating time versus money resource concepts influences tourists' preferences for different types of tourism activities. Across three experiments, the results show that when the concept of time is activated, tourists report stronger preferences for challenging activities, whereas when the concept of money is activated, they report stronger preferences for relaxing activities. Outcome-focused simulation mediates the relationship between time activation and challenging activity preference, whereas process-focused simulation mediates the relationship between money activation and relaxing activity preference. These indirect pathways are further conditioned by maximization: the time-related pathway becomes stronger as maximization increases, whereas the money-related pathway becomes weaker. The results offer practical implications for tourism destinations that can tailor marketing strategies based on tourists’ decision-making tendencies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Blast Furnace Slag as an Alternative to Natural Mineral Materials in Pavement Engineering: A Review; [Доменный шлак как альтернатива природным минеральным материалам в дорожном строительстве: обзор]; [Жол құрылысында табиғи минералдық материалдарға балама ретіндегі домна қожы: шолу]
abstract: The presented literature review contains the results of the analysis of scientific articles for 2000-2026 years, considering the use of blast furnace slag in various areas of road construction. It has been established that there are clear differences between the application options for different types of blast furnace slag. Air-cooled blast furnace slag (ACBFS) is more often used as a coarse or fine aggregate for cement concrete and asphalt concrete, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) is used as an additional binder or as a mineral/reactive filler. When using blast furnace slag in the production of concrete, the highest results in a number of studies were achieved when replacing 20-40% of the aggregate with slag, although this indicator was not a universal optimal value. In some articles, it was pointed out that the use of blast furnace slag as part of the base of a highway or for soil stabilization was associated with an increase in CBR. Some authors point to a reduction in the consumption of Portland cement when using complex binders containing granular blast furnace slag. Data on the improvement of water resistance, fatigue resistance, Marshall stability, and rutting resistance of asphalt concrete with the introduction of ACBFS and GGBFS in various proportions are also presented. Pretreatment of porous ACBFS was also important: selective crushing and related separation methods reduced water absorption, crushing value, and the proportion of weak porous particles. The main practical conclusion is that BFS should not be treated as a single interchangeable material. Its use should be selected according to slag type, particle quality, the component being replaced, and the required pavement property. Further studies should examine whether improvements achieved by slag pretreatment at the aggregate level are retained in concrete, asphalt mixtures, and pavement-base materials under long-term service conditions. © 2026, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .
