title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Effects of a design thinking education program for kindergarteners: A mixed-methods study
abstract: Children as young as three can engage in oral and visual planning when creating tangible objects from materials, yet it remains unclear whether such design competencies can be systematically strengthened in early childhood to cultivate future design thinkers and innovative creators. To evaluate a research-informed design thinking (DT) education program, we conducted a mixed-methods study. The quantitative component involved a quasi-experiment with 133 children ( M age = 5.22, SD = 0.86) from a Chinese kindergarten (intervention group: n = 68; business-as-usual comparison group: n = 65), where the intervention group received an eight-week DT program. Each child’s DT competence was assessed immediately before and after the intervention, followed by play-based interviews with 12 children (six per group). Child-level analyses indicated a statistically significant improvement in overall DT competence favoring the intervention group (Cohen’s d=0.38). However, gains were uneven across specific DT dimensions. Children showed more apparent gains in Empathize, Define, and Prototype, whereas no significant gains were observed in Ideate and Test. Furthermore, the youngest children appeared to show larger gains, whereas gender did not significantly moderate the intervention effects. Qualitative interviews provided insight into the cognitive processes underlying these developmental variations. Together, these preliminary findings may inform DT education research and practice in early childhood settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Results confirm that biospheric values significantly shape awareness of environmental consequences, moral responsibility, and personal norms, which in turn directly influence behavioral intention. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. This research extends theoretical understanding by linking ethical and volitional determinants of sustainable consumption and offers managerial insights for airlines and policymakers to design effective carbon offset communication, education, and engagement strategies. title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Validity and Reliability of the Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle Method for Determining Masticatory Preference in Children Before Premolar Transition
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the validity and reliability of Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle (PFMA) method with a modified device compared to the clinical method as the gold standard for determining masticatory preference side in children. Material and Methods: Validity and reliability study of diagnostic tests. The study included 102 children, aged 6 to 9 years, before the transition to premolars. The outcome measures were the validity and reliability of the PFMA method compared to the clinical method as the gold standard. To measure the PFMA, a device was designed; for the direct clinical observation method, it was performed with a portion of baguette bread over seven mastication cycles. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values were measured; and reliability through intra-and inter-observer agreements using simple Kappa. Results: Sensitivity and negative predictive values were the highest percentages, being 88% with a 95% confidence interval, providing good validity, ruling out the condition of unilateral mastication with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.15. The interobserver agreement (reproducibility) was ideal (p=1.000), and the intraobserver agreement (repeatability) was significant, with an agreement percentage of 30.95%. Conclusion: The Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle with a modified device proved to be a method with good validity and a useful tool as a screening test to identify the masticatory preference side. This study contributes to the diagnostic evaluation in pediatric dentistry. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Dual boron‑coordinated active sites steering an “activation‑migration‑desorption” relay pathway in S‑scheme SubPc/Ag‑ZnIn2S4 for H2O2 photosynthesis from wastewater
abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) faces an intrinsic trade-off between activity and selectivity, primarily due to the lack of well-defined and functionally differentiated active sites. Herein, a SubPc/Ag–ZnIn2S4 (SubPc/Ag–ZIS) S-scheme heterojunction is constructed by coordinating subphthalocyanine (SubPc–Br) onto Ag cluster-decorated ZnIn2S4. Distinct from conventional dual-site catalysts, this work achieves atomic-precision site differentiation via boron coordination chemistry, where the electron-rich B–Ag site activates O2, and the B–S site lowers the H2O2 desorption barrier. More importantly, the interfacial potential difference drives directional migration of the activated ·O2− intermediate from B–Ag to B–S, establishing an unprecedented “activation–migration–desorption” relay pathway. Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) confirms that this dual-site synergy significantly prolongs the charge carrier lifetime, providing a favorable kinetic foundation. The optimal catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 1200 μmol g−1 h−1 with a 2e− ORR selectivity of 78%. In the presence of tetracycline (TC) wastewater, hole-driven TC degradation (reaching 93.5% within 60 min) further inhibits charge recombination and synergistically increases the hydrogen peroxide generation rate to 1579.8 μmol g−1 h−1. This work establishes a boron coordination chemistry-driven dual-site relay catalysis strategy, offering a new paradigm for integrating efficient H2O2 photosynthesis with pollutant degradation. © 2026

title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective
abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Analysis of 406 participants exposed to an AI-generated tourism video reveals that true-to-ideal and true-to-fact authenticity show significant direct effects on destination attractiveness, whereas true-to-self authenticity operates entirely indirectly, consistent with a meaning-making route. For parallel mediation, true-to-ideal and true-to-self authenticity exert significant indirect effects via both mediators, whereas true-to-fact authenticity does so only through place imagination. The sequential pathway from place imagination to mental simulation receives consistent support across all dimensions. Theoretically, this study advances the ERC framework from a static typology to a processual account by delineating the distinct cognitive routes of each referent and highlighting both the conceptual promise and measurement challenges of operationalizing true-to-self authenticity as perceived communicative sincerity in algorithmically generated portrayals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Micro-foundations of destination supply: A configural analysis of herders’ livelihood strategies in grassland tourism
abstract: Based on the revised Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis was used to investigate the combinatorial effects of social, human, cultural, policy, physical, natural, and financial capital on herders' livelihood strategies in Chen Barag in the Hulunbuir Grassland, to identify the key drivers of herders’ adoption of a tourism livelihood. The results identify six differentiated livelihood configuration types. Traditional pastoral livelihoods are associated with resource-constrained configurations and high thresholds for tourism participation under ecological, market, and institutional conditions. Conversely, mixed livelihoods are associated with configurations involving productive resource release, locational advantages, cultural commodification, and intergenerational labour division, while governance tensions between institutional arrangements and diversified livelihood needs may create additional constraints. These findings highlight the joint importance of asset-related thresholds and institutional conditions in shaping differentiated tourism participation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Data were collected from 389 graduate students in Chinese universities using a two-wave survey design, and the hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using hierarchical regression analyses supplemented by the PROCESS macro. The results indicate that illegitimate tasks exert opposing indirect effects on research creativity through distinct reflective cognitive pathways. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Supervisor-student relationship quality further shaped how illegitimate tasks were interpreted and which reflective pathway was activated. These findings clarify the cognitive mechanisms and relational conditions through which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity and contribute to understanding how task legitimacy shapes creative thinking in graduate research contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. At the concept level, government failure, incentives, and user-pays lay on the higher-difficulty side, while demand and costs, price discrimination, and public, private, and club goods fell on the lower-difficulty side. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. These patterns remained broadly stable in supplementary analyses assessing sensitivity to question selection. The findings add a question- and concept-level perspective to research on air transport management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Digital Literacy through a Web-Based Application: Addressing Polarization and Promoting Social Integration among Islamic Senior High School Students
abstract: Digital literacy encompasses not only technical skills but also an understanding of social dynamics such as polarization and the need for social integration in digital environments. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of a web-based Mobile Polarization and Social Integration application in improving students’ digital literacy. A quasi-experimental design with a control group was employed, involving students from an Islamic senior high school. Data were collected using a validated test and analyzed through comparative statistical methods. The application significantly enhances students’ digital literacy and supports their awareness of polarization and social integration. This study highlights the potential of web-based learning applications to strengthen digital citizenship and encourage responsible and inclusive participation in digital spaces. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. This paper addresses this fragmentation through the first systematic cross-domain seating assignment literature review, analyzing publications via bibliometric analysis and examining assignment methods (including optimization techniques) across transportation (airplanes and trains), dining establishments, entertainment venues, and classrooms. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. The review concludes that limited real-world implementation stems partly from researchers' inability to access successful approaches from adjacent fields, highlighting opportunities to advance seating assignment methods through integrated frameworks. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Multi-layered texture-heterogeneous architecture enabling strength-ductility synergy in Mg laminates
abstract: Achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys remains challenging because their inherent plastic anisotropy leads to a trade-off between texture-induced strengthening and strain accommodation. Here, we designed and fabricated texture-heterogeneous Mg laminates by accumulative roll bonding, comprising five alternating layers of Mg-Al-Zn with a strong basal texture (hard layer) and Mg-Al-Sn-Ca with a weaker basal texture (soft layer). Two texture-heterogeneous laminates with different stacking architectures have been constructed, i.e., hard-soft-hard-soft-hard (HSH-5L) and soft-hard-soft-hard-soft (SHS-5L). HSH-5L exhibits a yield strength of 192 MPa and fracture elongation of 22%, representing improvements of 8.1% and 27%, respectively, compared with SHS-5L. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, digital image correlation, and finite element simulation indicate that the improved mechanical response is associated with enhanced interfacial constraints and higher strain gradients in HSH-5L. These conditions facilitate <c+a> slip near interfaces and provide more nucleation sites for strain bands (SB). As deformation proceeds, dense SBs mainly dominated by basal <a> slip gradually intersect. The intersection regions induce local stress concentration and activate additional non-basal slip, which in turn restricts the further propagation of SBs and thereby contributes to sustained strain hardening in the HSH-5L sample. By contrast, in the SHS-5L sample, basal <a> slip initiates and propagates rapidly during deformation, forming long-range SBs that lead to local deformation instability and premature fracture. These findings provide insights for the design of heterogeneous Mg laminates with high strength and ductility. © 2026

title: Simultaneous giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability in PNZST ceramics via antiferroelectric phase boundary regulation
abstract: Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramics are promising candidates for precision actuators, but the trade-off between giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability has severely limited their practical applications. Here, we propose a dual-pathway phase boundary regulation strategy in perovskite AFE systems to synergistically optimize electrostrain magnitude and temperature stability by designing the electric-field-induced AFE-ferroelectric (FE) transition sequence under coupled temperature-electric-field conditions. Using the prototype system of Pb0.99Nb0.02[(Zr0.75Sn0.25)xTi1−x]0.98O3 (PNZST-100xZS), our results show that PNZST-99ZS and PNZST-97ZS exhibit giant electrostrains of 0.98% and 0.77%, respectively. Remarkably, over a wide temperature range of 25–155 °C, they maintain low electrostrain fluctuations of only 16.12% and 9.21%, significantly better than previously reported materials. The excellent performance stems from the electric-field-induced orthorhombic AFE (AFEO)-rhombohedral FE (FER) transition at low temperatures and the tetragonal AFE (AFET)-FER transition at high temperatures. Between these two temperature regions, the diffuse AFEO-AFET transition bridges the two field-induced pathways, ensuring a smooth evolution of the electrostrain response across the entire operating temperature range. This work provides a new route to high-performance AFE actuator materials with both large electrostrain and wide-temperature stability. © 2026

abstract: Grammarly is one of the most widely used software applications for the automatic detection of grammatical errors in texts translated from Persian into English. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Grammarly and to propose suggestions for improving its performance. To achieve this objective, a corpus consisting of English translations of booklets introducing works of resistance literature was analyzed. After grammatical errors had been identified by the researchers (human evaluators), the electronic versions of the booklets were submitted to Grammarly for error detection. The identified errors were then categorized, and the results obtained by the researchers were compared with those generated by the software. Following the qualitative and quantitative analyses of the errors and the presentation of the findings, recommendations were made to enhance Grammarly’s effectiveness. According to the findings, of the 98 instances identified by Grammarly as errors, 16 were not actual errors. In four cases (4.9%), Grammarly failed to correctly identify the type of error. The software demonstrated its weakest performance in the detection of spelling errors and the misuse of masculine and feminine pronouns. Overall, Grammarly exhibited a high level of effectiveness, correctly identifying 82.8% of the errors. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Synergistic enhancement of coercivity and saturation magnetization in Sm-Co alloys via multi-element doping
abstract: Multi-element doping represents the most effective approach for enhancing the performance of permanent magnetic alloys. However, the complex interdependencies among diverse doping elements, broad concentration ranges, and intricate element-matrix interactions present significant challenges in establishing appropriate composition-property relationships, impeding efficient development of high-performance multicomponent alloys. To address this fundamental limitation, this study introduced a data-driven framework incorporating high-throughput identification of key elemental features governing magnetic properties. Principal component and feature sensitivity analyses quantified feature contributions to distinct magnetic characteristics and evaluated comprehensive weighting factors for multi-objective optimization. This integrated methodology enabled efficient and appropriate design of multi-element doped alloys targeting simultaneous enhancement of competing magnetic properties. Demonstrated by the Sm-Co-based systems, the framework concurrently enhanced both saturation magnetization and coercivity, which effectively resolved the trade-off between these properties through multi-element doping. Experimentally validated designs across multiple matrix types exhibited superior comprehensive magnetic properties, with quantitative confirmation of the model predictions. The present study provides a novel strategy that is in principle broadly applicable for designing multicomponent alloys that overcome inherent property trade-offs. © 2026

title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. The findings demonstrate that structured, pedagogically guided AI integration transforms AI from a passive information source into an active learning scaffold. The SAIL approach, supported by RACE, offers a practical and transferable pathway for educators seeking to prepare students to navigate AI-augmented professional environments with critical, reflective, and responsible judgment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Waiting for Uganda’s first commercial ‘Pearl Sweet’ oil: Discourses on social and environmental impacts and safeguards
abstract: Uganda discovered approximately 3.5 billion barrels of commercially recoverable oil reserves in 2006 and is poised to become a major oil producer in Sub-Saharan Africa. In assessing progress towards full–scale oil production, expected by the end of 2026, Uganda’s President referred to the country’s commercial crude oil as “pearl sweet”, highlighting its medium-to-heavy, highly waxy characteristics, relatively low sulphur content, and ease of refining. Despite the anticipated economic benefits, considerable debate persists regarding the potential social and environmental impacts of oil development and the adequacy of safeguards ahead of full–scale production. Drawing on experiences from established oil–producing countries, this paper examines how environmental and social impacts are framed, how safeguards are prioritised, and what this implies for Uganda’s emerging oil sector. Anchored in environmental justice and political ecology, the study adopts a sequential integrative design combining a systematic literature review with empirical insights from twelve purposively selected stakeholders in Uganda’s oil-producing districts and national regulatory institutions. The literature review used Boolean search strings that connected terms within conceptual blocks using OR and combined blocks using AND, following a PRISMA-guided process across Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar and institutional data bases. Of 1800 records identified, 95 key sources were retained for analysis. The findings indicate that, although Uganda has initiated several safeguards measures including oil–spill preparedness training, buffer zone enforcement, afforestation, and resettlement programs – implementation remain fragmented, under–resourced, and heavily centralised. Comparative analysis further indicates limited integration of international climate frameworks, including the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, into national oil governance. We argue that Uganda’s challenge is not simply the absence of safeguards, but the persistence of centralised, uneven, and under–resourced governance arrangements that constrain the translation of international safeguard commitments into effective national practice. This study contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while also intersecting with SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Psychological safety as a driver of student learning outcomes in team-based learning environments: The mediating role of teamwork quality
abstract: With the rise of constructivist approaches, team-based learning (TBL) has gained popularity as an instructional design in the field of management education. The extant research indicates that the positive effects of TBL on student learning outcomes, which many studies report, might depend on individual as well as social-contextual drivers. In this paper, we introduce psychological safety and the quality of teamwork processes as two important social-contextual drivers of student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Based on research on team processes and TBL, we argue that psychological safety fosters student learning outcomes because of its positive effect on intrinsic motivation and group interaction. We further hypothesize that the relationship between psychological safety and student learning outcomes is mediated by the quality of teamwork processes within the student teams. A field study based on a computerized business simulation involving 169 undergraduate management students, nested within 44 teams, at a German university supports our hypotheses. We contribute to research on constructivist learning and TBL by introducing psychological safety as an important driver and the quality of teamwork processes as a mediating mechanism for student learning outcomes in TBL settings. Our study also has practical implications for the design, support, and facilitation of psychologically safe team-based learning environments. © 2026

title: The power of gastronomic cultural capital: How local food culture shapes residents' recommendation intention
abstract: While destinations increasingly leverage cultural capital for competitiveness, research predominantly focuses on top-down promotions of monument-centered heritage, neglecting the distinct social logic of gastronomic culture. Grounded in cultural capital theory, this study aims to examine how Hong Kong's tea restaurants food culture translates into residents' recommendation intentions toward culturally diverse individuals. It untangles the core inquiries: how everyday food culture fosters attachment; how this attachment subsequently shapes cultural identity and confidence; and how nostalgia and knowledge moderate these psychological pathways. Additionally, it identifies which specific tea restaurant's food culture dimensions serve as the primary drivers. Utilizing an empirical sample of 615 Hong Kong residents, this research adopts a PLS–SEM–ANN approach. The PLS–SEM analysis confirms that cultural identity and confidence act as pivotal mediators, while the complementary ANN analysis reveals that gastronomic identity, exceeding mere sensory flavour, is the predominant driving dimension. Empirically, nostalgia amplifies the culture–attachment link, and knowledge strengthens the attachment–confidence relationship. These findings advocate for a paradigm shift in destination marketing: beyond institutional campaigns, mobilizing residents as active cultural transmitters is crucial for gastronomic tourism, establishing a scalable mechanism for everyday cultural capital transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The power of morality: The effect of moral appeals on tourists’ attitudes in rural tourism destinations
abstract: Rural tourism has become an important tool for rural-revitalization and poverty alleviation, which has been increasingly framed as a moral narrative in public discourse. However, destination marketing often prioritizes utilitarian attributes while overlooking the role of moral appeals. Drawing on affective events theory, this study employs two experiments to examine the effects of moral appeals on tourists' attitudes, the underlying mechanism, and boundary conditions. The findings reveal that moral appeals significantly enhance tourists' visit intention and perceived value of rural destinations, with anticipated guilt mediating this relationship. Notably, these effects are more pronounced in low-quality destinations than in high-quality ones. Specifically, in rural destinations with low quality, high-intensity moral appeals are more effective than low-intensity ones in enhancing tourists’ visit intention and perceived value. This study contributes to the literature on rural tourism marketing and highlights the strategic value of moral appeals, particularly for rural destinations with limited resources. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge of the Arhuaco People on Water Management in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta
abstract: This article analyzes the role of Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) of the Arhuaco people in water management in the upper Ariguaní river basin, in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Colombia), in a context of accelerated socio-environmental transformation. From an ethnohydrological approach, the study adopts a mixed-methods design that integrates community surveys, participatory techniques, spatial analysis of land use change (2000–2023), and dynamic socio-hydrological modeling. A TEK Index was constructed to evaluate three dimensions of water management: cultural management, indigenous norms, and government norms. The results show that traditional water knowledge is mainly based on ritual practices and indigenous norms guided by indigenous spiritual authorities, while coordination with state institutional frameworks is limited. Spatial analysis shows a loss of forest cover and expansion of agricultural uses around the sacred sites that sustain TEK. Modeling indicates that, although indigenous norms slow the deterioration of the system, only co-governance scenarios can cushion pressures and avoid trajectories of collapse. Taken together, the findings show that the effectiveness of TEK depends on its articulation with multiscale governance arrangements. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Bridging the implementation gap in MCABC inventory management: from a taxonomy to practical archetypes
abstract: Despite increasing demands for resilient and sustainable supply chains, inventory management often relies on outdated single-criterion analyses. While multi-criteria ABC (MCABC) analyses provide a theoretically mature assessment of resilience-sustainability-benefit trade-offs in inventory, their adoption remains limited due to fragmented methodologies, lack of standardization, and unclear design guidance. This study addresses this gap by developing a taxonomy of eight dimensions and 25 characteristics to structure the MCABC analysis design space. Using a dataset of 108 configurations, cluster analysis identifies six recurring archetypes that serve as implementation-ready templates for inventory analysis. Archetype 2: artificial intelligence (AI)+-driven cluster minimalist enables rapid, cost-focused inventory structuring with minimal data and no expert input. In contrast, Archetype 1: AI+-driven complex ranker uses expert-weighted multi-criteria analysis to support holistic and sustainability oriented inventory strategies. The taxonomy and archetypes provide a unified framework for researchers to theorize inventory design trade-offs and for practitioners to apply scalable blueprints for mature inventory analyses. © 2025 The Author(s). title: A study on the site selection of pumped storage power plants based on GIS and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Models: A case study of China
abstract: Pumped storage power plants (PSPPs) are essential for enhancing power system flexibility and supporting renewable energy integration. However, PSPP site selection involves complex spatial constraints and multi-dimensional trade-offs among technical, economic, environmental, and social factors. This study proposes a two-stage GIS–MCDM framework for PSPP site selection. First, GIS-based spatial screening with veto criteria is applied to identify feasible candidate sites. Subsequently, an integrated AHP–entropy weighting approach and TOPSIS method are employed for comprehensive evaluation, with VIKOR, TODIM, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation used to verify robustness. A case study in Guangxi, China identifies the optimal site among seven alternatives, and the results demonstrate the stability of the proposed framework under different weighting scenarios. Furthermore, theoretical energy storage assessment and comparison with an approved PSPP project provide additional evidence for the engineering feasibility of the selected site. The proposed approach offers an effective decision-support tool for PSPP planning and clean energy development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Enhancing repeat patronage in beauty clinics: An integrated model of trust and consumer perceptions
abstract: This study aims to explain how trust drives repeat patronage in the beauty clinic industry by examining the roles of service quality, price fairness, and influencer credibility. A quantitative explanatory approach was applied using survey data from 360 beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS to test direct and indirect relationships among variables. The results show that perceived service quality, perceived price fairness, and influencer credibility each have positive and significant direct effects on both repurchase intention and brand trust, and that brand trust itself significantly and positively drives repurchase intention. Brand trust also partially mediates the effects of all three antecedents on repurchase intention, indicating that consumers' evaluations of service, price, and influencers shape repeat patronage both directly and through the trust these evaluations help to build. These findings suggest that improving service quality, price fairness perception, and influencer credibility can enhance consumer trust in a brand, which ultimately increases repurchase intention in beauty clinic services. This study is limited to beauty clinic consumers in the Jabodetabek area. Beauty clinic managers should focus on trust-building strategies through consistent service quality, transparent pricing, and collaboration with credible social media influencers to foster long-term consumer relationships. This study provides an integrated model that empirically demonstrates the mediating role of brand trust in the beauty clinic industry. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: IMPORTANCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS IN CAMPUS MANAGEMENT
abstract: Campus managers need to balance the competing claims of different stakeholders of higher education institutions (HEIs). Previous studies in general management have indicated that the decision-making processes are highly related to stakeholders’ attributes (power, legitimacy and urgency). However, such studies have not yet been conducted in the field of campus management. Therefore, this paper aims to identify the importance of key stakeholders in campus development and relevant key performance indicators (KPIs) that are essential for decisionmakers in determining and explaining how their efforts are progressing towards achieving various stakeholders’ goals. To explore the underlying importance of campus stakeholders, a theory on stakeholder salience and a questionnaire survey among Polish public HEIs were employed. In turn, to identify various KPIs, the content analysis of institutions’ strategies was conducted. Empirical research suggests that in Polish public HEIs, authorities and academic staff continue to be regarded as the most important stakeholders (at different stages of the building’s life cycle, respectively). This contrasts with the growing market-oriented approach seen in higher education globally. Moreover, the KPIs presented in HEIs’ strategies are predominantly result-focused and rarely user-centric (which have begun to be perceived as the most significant with respect to building performance). © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Research Competence of a Modern Teacher as a Factor in Improving the Quality of Education and Supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: This study examines teacher research competence as a factor in improving educational quality and supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Data from 10 secondary school teachers were collected through a questionnaire assessing professional competencies, temperament, motivation, stress resistance, and burnout. Communicative and methodological competencies were strongest, while research, managerial, digital, and inclusive competencies need further development. Research competence was positively related to intrinsic motivation and methodological competence. title: Breaking the cycle of malice: Influence mechanism and intervention of social exclusion on malevolent creativity in adolescents
abstract: Creativity is the core driving force for humans to break through existing boundaries and promote continuous social progress, and its positive impacts have been widely recognized. However, creativity also has a dark side, namely, malevolent creativity, which poses significant potential harm to society. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to conduct research on malevolent creativity to prevent its negative impacts. Based on the 4P model of creativity, this study explored the impact mechanism between social exclusion and malevolent creativity (Study 1) and the effectiveness of a group counseling intervention for self-concept clarity (Study 2). Study 1 conducted a field questionnaire survey (N = 1567). The results showed that social exclusion not only directly increased malevolent creativity, but also indirectly predicted it through the independent mediating effects of reduced self-concept clarity and heightened negative emotions, as well as through the serial mediating effect whereby reduced self-concept clarity led to increased negative emotions, which in turn predicted malevolent creativity. Trait mindfulness moderated the impact of social exclusion on self-concept clarity, with higher levels of trait mindfulness alleviating the negative effects of social exclusion on self-concept clarity. Study 2 utilized a group counseling intervention (N = 30) and demonstrated that the experimental group experienced a significant increase in self-concept clarity and a significant decrease in malevolent creativity after the intervention. The study's conclusions provide educators with references and insights for correctly understanding the impact of social exclusion and for offering interventions to enhance self-concept clarity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises: The roles of technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality in an ai-driven business environment
abstract: The tourism industry is experiencing unprecedented transformation driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and the rapid evolution of smart tourism ecosystems. At the same time, tourism enterprises face growing pressure to enhance service quality while controlling operational costs and improving managerial responsiveness. In this context, management accounting effectiveness has become a critical capability for supporting strategic decision-making and maintaining sustainable competitiveness. Although previous studies have examined digital transformation and accounting systems separately, limited attention has been paid to how technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality jointly influence management accounting effectiveness in tourism enterprises operating in emerging economies. Addressing this research gap, the present study investigates the effects of these three determinants on management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism enterprises. Grounded in the resource-based view, contingency theory, dynamic capabilities theory, and sociotechnical systems theory, the study adopts a mixed-method research design consisting of expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. Data were collected from 315 tourism enterprises, with chief accountants, general accountants, and management accounting personnel serving as key respondents. The data were analyzed using SPSS through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The empirical findings demonstrate that technology readiness, information technology infrastructure, and data quality all exert positive and statistically significant effects on management accounting effectiveness. Among these determinants, information technology infrastructure emerges as the strongest predictor, followed by technology readiness and data quality. These findings indicate that tourism enterprises equipped with integrated digital infrastructure, advanced technological capabilities, and high-quality accounting data are better positioned to generate timely, accurate, and strategically relevant management accounting information in AI-enabled business environments. This study extends the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy and contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital transformation and management accounting. The findings also offer practical implications for tourism managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital accounting capabilities, improve managerial decision-making, and enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of tourism enterprises in the era of AI-driven business transformation. title: An advanced integrated cross-sectoral model for formulating government strategies on energy consumption management to reduce greenhouse gas emissions toward achieving net-zero emissions in the future
abstract: This study aims to develop a model that identifies alternative scenarios for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by examining the interrelationships among the circular economy, socio-cultural, and environmental sectors, with the ultimate goal of supporting Thailand's net-zero emissions target. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study provides a foundation for developing integrated national management strategies that promote long-term sustainability. A novel model, referred to as the Path–Probit–Logit–ARx Model (Path Analysis–Probit–Logit Model based on Autoregressive with Exogenous Variables), was developed to address the study objectives. The findings reveal that, during the period 1992–2025, the circular economy sector experienced continuous growth, which directly contributed to the steady expansion of the socio-cultural sector. The growth of both sectors also exerted a positive influence on the environmental sector. Furthermore, the environmental sector was found to have a direct positive effect on the socio-cultural sector, indicating a bidirectional relationship between these two sectors. This finding suggests that environmentally responsible societies can promote long-term ecosystem development and that environmental and social development should progress concurrently. Based on the analysis, the study identified the adoption of electric vehicles as the most sensitive and effective scenario for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Under this scenario, the growth rate of final energy consumption is reduced to 33%, while greenhouse gas emission growth decreases to 53.73%, remaining below the critical threshold of 590.05 Mt CO2 equivalent and thereby meeting the government's target. To enhance the policy relevance and credibility of the findings, a focus group consisting of 15 experts was conducted to validate the results. The experts confirmed the appropriateness and accuracy of the proposed scenario and agreed that it is suitable for promoting sustainable development in Thailand. However, they emphasized the need for immediate action and strong governmental support to ensure effective implementation. Therefore, the findings of this study can support evidence-based decision-making and strategic planning, contributing to the development of Thailand's long-term national strategies through 2065. © 2026 The Authors. title: Human Factors and Safety Communication in Engineering Safety Performance: A Predictive PLS-SEM Model for Petrochemical Operations
abstract: Petrochemical operations are complex engineering systems in which safety performance depends not only on technical safeguards and process controls but also on human and organisational factors that influence how workers perceive, interpret, and respond to safety requirements. Despite advances in engineering controls and occupational safety management systems, incidents continue to occur, highlighting the need to integrate human factors into engineering safety management. This study develops and evaluates a predictive model of engineering safety performance by examining the effects of two culturally embedded human factors, religiosity and fatalism, together with safety communication effectiveness in Malaysian petrochemical operations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 463 employees and contractors from major petrochemical facilities in Malaysia. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. The structural model showed that religiosity significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.442, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while fatalism significantly influenced safety communication effectiveness (β = 0.451, p < 0.001) and safety performance (β = 0.378, p < 0.001). In contrast, safety communication effectiveness did not directly predict safety performance (β = −0.006, p = 0.954). The model explained 74.7% of the variance in safety communication effectiveness and 61.2% of the variance in safety performance. These findings demonstrate that engineering safety performance in high-risk petrochemical operations cannot be addressed solely through technical controls and communication systems. Integrating culturally embedded human factors with organisational safety mechanisms provides a more comprehensive approach to engineering safety management and supports the development of human-centred safety interventions for complex industrial operations. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. .

title: A graph-based direct association strategy with fuzzy interpretability for linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality
abstract: Existing coke quality prediction methods mainly rely on a two-stage prediction strategy, where blended coal properties are first estimated from individual coal properties and then used for coke quality prediction. This process inevitably introduces information loss and accumulated prediction errors, which limit the prediction accuracy and reliability of these models in practical coal blending applications. To address this challenge, this study proposes, for the first time, a graph-based direct association strategy linking individual coal properties in coal blending schemes to coke quality. Each coal blending scheme is transformed into a graph structure, where individual coal samples are regarded as graph nodes and their corresponding coal properties together with blending ratios are used as node features. Different graph neural network models are further investigated to directly learn the relationship between individual coal properties and coke quality indicators, namely Coke Reactivity Index (CRI) and Coke Strength after Reaction (CSR). A total of 306 coal blending schemes are used for model development and evaluation. Experimental results show that the proposed one-stage graph-based framework outperforms traditional two-stage prediction methods. Among different graph neural network models, the graph attention network achieves the best overall prediction performance, obtaining mean absolute errors of 2.06 and 2.60 for CRI and CSR prediction, respectively. The t-SNE visualization further demonstrates that the proposed one-stage framework can learn more discriminative feature representations than the traditional two-stage framework. In addition, the proposed framework demonstrates good robustness under blending conditions with different numbers of coal types and can provide interpretable analysis through feature importance and node importance visualization. Furthermore, fuzzy interpretability is introduced at the feature level to characterize the gradual contribution levels of different coal properties. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Temporal water-quality variability and its implications for environmental management of sand lobster aquaculture
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable management of sand lobster aquaculture is often limited by monitoring approaches that summarize environmental conditions using long-term averages, obscuring short-term extremes and spatial variation. The study objectives were to characterize spatial and temporal variations in water quality within a floating net cage aquaculture system, identify their underlying physical drivers, evaluate whether longitudinal growth is governed more by culture duration, initial size, and stocking density than by environmental exposure alone, and translate these empirical relationships into a transferable environmental monitoring framework. METHODS: The study collected longitudinal growth and environmental data from floating net cage culture in Indonesia. Monitoring covered temperature, salinity, oxygen concentration, potential of hydrogen, and nutrient concentrations across three water depths and multiple sampling times. Non-parametric statistical tests were employed to evaluate depth-dependent variations in dissolved oxygen, while correlation and regression analysis assessed the relationships between wind speed, water temperature, and dissolved oxygen levels. Multivariate statistical ordination summarized dominant environmental gradients, and mixed-effects statistical models, compared through an information-theoretic model selection approach, captured longitudinal growth. FINDINGS: Dissolved oxygen concentration differed significantly among depths (test statistic 29.27, probability below 0.001), declining by close to a fifth from the surface to three and ten meters. Monthly wind speed closely tracked the concurrent decline in temperature closely (correlation coefficient -0.988, probability below 0.002) but exhibited no statistically significant association with dissolved oxygen, consistent with a wind-driven transition observed during this production cycle. Culture duration, initial size class, and stocking density together explained total length best, with an additive model carrying more than seventy percent of the statistical weight among six candidate models. Growth rate exhibited its strongest association with low-oxygen exposure, followed by temperature and potential of hydrogen condition, an interpretation that warrants caution given the limited independent exposure intervals available. CONCLUSION: Successful sand lobster aquaculture requires an adaptive environmental monitoring architecture that accounts for depth-related oxygen stratification and wind-driven seasonal variability, alongside coordinated management of culture duration, initial seed size, and stocking density. The analytical framework of integrated site assessment and management for lobster can be adapted to other marine aquaculture systems through the inclusion of species-specific biological indicators and management variables. © 2027 The author(s). title: Economic design of residential solar resources under uncertainty: An adaptive robust optimization approach for EV households
abstract: The integration of residential PV systems with electric vehicles (EVs) offers significant opportunities to enhance self-consumption, reduce reliance on the grid, and lower household energy costs. Effective PV system sizing, however, is challenged by uncertainties in PV generation, household electricity demand, and EV charging behavior. While traditional approaches often ignore uncertainties or assume predefined values for uncertainties, this paper develops an adaptive robust optimization framework for sizing residential PV systems in EV-integrated households, explicitly accounting for operational uncertainties and calibrating the uncertainty parameters using a Genetic Algorithm. The proposed model explicitly incorporates multi-source uncertainty using a budgeted adaptive robust optimization approach. Investment decisions, such as PV capacity, are modeled as here-and-now variables, while operational variability is captured as wait-and-see decisions responding to uncertainty realizations. To mitigate the inherent conservatism of robust optimization and identify optimal uncertainty settings, a Genetic Algorithm–based calibration is integrated. The GA iteratively searches for the best combination of uncertainty parameters through simulation-based evaluation, balancing robustness and economic efficiency. The results show that calibrated uncertainty parameters provide a cost-effective and resilient system design, avoiding oversized PV capacities while improving household energy performance by reducing the cost of energy up to 18%. © 2026

title: Transforming value of sustainability in urban development: Reconfiguring logistics service in the construction industry
abstract: Urban development depends on construction activity to improve sustainability, yet the logistics required to move materials, equipment, waste, and workers remains insufficiently integrated into urban planning. This paper examines how construction logistics can be integrated into municipal urban planning by analysing how actor groups perceive its impacts and coordinate value creation across fragmented urban systems. The study applies a qualitative interactive research design based on a Swedish construction logistics project. Data were collected between August 2022 and March 2024 through eight semi-structured group interviews, joint workshops, actor-specific validation workshops, and a final synthesis workshop with developers, main contractors, suppliers, and trade organizations. The analysis combines iterative thematic coding with value configuration theory. The findings show that suppliers emphasize efficiency and climate savings, main contractors focus on project efficiency and safety, developers stress sustainability, accessibility and accountability, while trade organizations highlight knowledge-building and sector coordination. These differences create misalignment because societal benefits are often separated from project-level costs. Four conditions are identified as central: clearer procurement requirements, stronger logistics knowledge, scalable logistics service designs, and systematic follow-up of time, cost, and emission effects. The paper concludes that municipalities should use procurement, planning requirements and follow-up mechanisms to enforce construction logistics values in urban planning. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Hot war tourism: The touristification of unresolved conflict
abstract: This article conceptualises hot war tourism as the touristification of unresolved conflict: configurations in which conflict continues materially to shape civilian vulnerability, security and visitor access while conflict-affected places and experiences acquire experiential, representational or market value. A critical integrative review clarifies its boundaries with dark, battlefield, military, risk, recovery and solidarity-oriented tourism and identifies five dimensions: temporal immediacy, spatial proximity, commodification, moral and motivational ambiguity, and governance and responsibility. Ukraine and Syria illustrate contrasting active-war witnessing and recovery–normalisation configurations. A relational framework locates war-related tourism according to the degree of unresolved conflict and the intensity of touristification, while a multi-actor governance framework specifies responsibilities for access, risk disclosure, representation, consent, platform accountability, humanitarian non-interference and escalation. The concept links tourism value production to unresolved harm and provides a basis for analysing when conflict-related visitation requires facilitation, restraint or restriction. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java: The roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, innovation capability, and ESG
abstract: This study examines the determinants of social enterprise sustainability in Java by analyzing the roles of intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) implementation, innovation capability, and organizational performance. Social enterprises in emerging economies increasingly face challenges in maintaining long-term sustainability due to resource limitations, institutional uncertainty, and dynamic social demands. Although previous studies have explored intellectual capital, entrepreneurial orientation, ESG practices, and innovation capability separately, limited empirical research has integrated these variables into a comprehensive sustainability model within the context of social enterprises in emerging economies, particularly Indonesia. Therefore, this study seeks to address this gap by developing and testing an integrated model of social enterprise sustainability. This research adopts a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data were collected from 200 owners and managers of social enterprises operating across six provinces on Java Island. The findings reveal that entrepreneurial orientation has a strong and significant effect on innovation capability (β = 0.699, p < 0.001), while ESG implementation significantly influences social enterprise performance (β = 0.402, p < 0.001). Intellectual capital and entrepreneurial orientation significantly contribute to innovation capability, whereas ESG implementation directly improves organizational performance and sustainability. Furthermore, innovation capability acts as a crucial mediating variable that strengthens the relationship between strategic organizational resources and sustainability outcomes. Social enterprise performance also demonstrates a significant mediating role in achieving long-term sustainability. These findings highlight the importance of innovation-driven strategies, knowledge-based resources, and ESG-oriented governance in strengthening the resilience and sustainability of social enterprises. This study contributes to the development of sustainability and social entrepreneurship literature while providing practical implications for managers and policymakers in building a more sustainable social enterprise ecosystem in emerging economies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From eco-signals to green trust: How tourists evaluate sustainability credibility through online reviews
abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. This study examines how tourists interpret environmental practices by analyzing 138,683 online reviews from major Southeast and East Asian coastal and island destinations. Drawing on signaling theory and attribution theory, the study proposes that observable sustainability cues are associated with eco-authenticity inference, which is linked to green trust and, in turn, more positive review sentiment. Using natural language processing, topic modeling, regression analysis, mediation analysis, and robustness checks for sparse text-derived variables, the findings show a positive association between eco-signal richness and eco-authenticity inference, as well as a significant indirect association from eco-authenticity inference to sentiment through green trust. Eco-authenticity inference is not directly associated with more positive sentiment once green trust is included. Because the focal sustainability, authenticity, and trust expressions are infrequent and have median values of zero, the findings identify a consistent but sparse textual pattern rather than a large or pervasive psychological effect. Because the Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner (VADER) is English-oriented, VADER-based sentiment models were also checked using the English-language subset; the qualitative pattern remained consistent. Topic modeling provides supplementary contextual evidence that sustainability discourse in reviews is episodic and grounded in concrete visitor experiences. Practically, the findings suggest that destinations and tourism providers should make sustainability practices visible, verifiable, and experience-based rather than relying on abstract promotional claims. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

abstract: This study investigates the simultaneous utilization of mineralized mass (MM) from Central Kyzylkum phosphorite waste and acidic wastewater (AWW) from the soapstock processing industry for efficient fluoride removal. The MM was chemically activated by AWW under controlled conditions, leading to surface modification, increased porosity, and enhanced active site heterogeneity. The chemical interaction between H⁺ ions from AWW and fluorapatite in MM resulted in ion exchange, dissolution of phosphate groups, and the formation of volatile HF. Adsorption experiments were conducted at various MM: AWW ratios to determine the optimal operating parameters. Equilibrium data were fitted to the Freundlich isotherm model, confirming multilayer adsorption on heterogeneous surfaces. Kinetic analysis indicated that the pseudo-second-order (PSO) model provided the best fit, suggesting that chemisorption is the dominant rate-limiting mechanism. The Weber–Morris intra-particle diffusion model revealed that pore diffusion contributes to fluoride uptake but is not the sole controlling step. The synergy between isotherm and kinetic results supports a two-stage adsorption process involving rapid surface chemisorption followed by slower intraparticle diffusion. The developed method offers a dual environmental benefit by valorizing two industrial waste streams and reducing their ecological footprint. The produced sorbent showed high fluoride removal efficiency under simulated operational conditions. The process is simple, cost-effective, and compatible with existing industrial infrastructures. Large-scale application has the potential to reduce operational costs and promote circular economy principles. These findings provide a sustainable approach to water treatment in fluoride-affected regions while addressing industrial waste management challenges. © 2027, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Can a transversal adaptation of teaching materials foster students’ entrepreneurial intentions? A quasi-experimental exploration in a statistics course setting
abstract: We propose that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content within other curricula may be an effective approach to foster students' entrepreneurial intentions. We embedded entrepreneurship content in an otherwise unrelated statistics course targeting the theory of planned behavior constructs of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms in relation to entrepreneurship. 350 Swiss students (193 intervention group, 157 control group) participated in a nine-week quasi-experiment to explore the effects of this intervention. Structural equation modeling suggests that being in the intervention group affected students' attitude toward entrepreneurship, which in turn was associated with higher entrepreneurial intentions by the end of the intervention. The intervention did not affect perceived behavioral control nor subjective norms and changes in these variables were neither associated with change in entrepreneurial intentions. Unexpectedly, the intervention did not improve students' attitude ratings but appeared to prevent their decline over time. A qualitative follow-up exploration with seven participants suggested that the data collection itself may have prompted students to reassess their attitude toward entrepreneurship. We conclude that a transversal integration of entrepreneurship content into university curricula could play a key role in enhancing students’ entrepreneurial mindset and may, over time, support conditions conducive to innovation and creativity. © 2026 The Authors

title: When static Volt–VAr control helps and when it does not: Operational and planning lessons from a weak radial distribution feeder
abstract: Long radial distribution feeders are increasingly exposed to sustained undervoltage as electrification-driven load growth outpaces reinforcement. Static inverter Volt–VAr curves are attractive because they can be deployed through existing controller settings, but standard curves may be too conservative for electrically weak feeders. This paper evaluates the operational and planning value of feeder-specific static Volt–VAr settings under data conditions commonly available to distribution system operators: sparse voltage measurements, hourly feeder-level inputs, and offline parameter updates. The study applies the slope-selection procedure developed in [1] to a predefined BESS Volt–VAr curve and evaluates the resulting setting through quasi-static time-series power flow for a real 22 kV radial feeder in Northern Norway. During the constructed 168 h high-load/no-generation stress period, the model-based, condition-matched comparison produced 153 h within the adopted target band with the full feeder-specific setting, compared with 8 h under the IEEE 1547-type setting and 1 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. An independent 2025 operating period was used for quantitative comparison with field measurements. The model reproduced the average voltage and voltage-band occupancy, while the disagreement in hourly variation limits its use to comparative screening rather than point-by-point prediction. The transferred feeder-specific setting produced 0 h outside the target band, compared with 16 h under the IEEE-type curve and 55 h without BESS Volt–VAr support. Higher-resolution measurements from the BESS and hydropower plant were used separately to examine interaction between the two local controllers. Under the 59% industrial-growth stress scenario, 4 MVAr was the smallest tested reactive-power rating that kept all 168 hourly voltages at or above the lower limit of the adopted target band after feeder-specific slope selection. The results provide a practical DSO screening procedure: test static tuning first, then identify whether the remaining limitation is curve setting, VAr headroom, or interaction between independently controlled assets. © 2026 The Authors
