title: Machine Learning-Assisted optimization of acetylene Dual-Fuel combustion using Copper oxide (CuO) Nano-Enhanced waste Plastic Oil in Compression Ignition (CI) Engine
abstract: In this study, an experimental and machine learning-assisted investigation was conducted on a modified single-cylinder direct-injection Compression Ignition (CI) engine operating in acetylene dual-fuel mode using copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticle-enhanced waste plastic oil (WPO) blends. The proposed approach integrates waste-to-energy fuel utilization, catalytic nano-additives, high-reactivity gaseous combustion, and data-driven predictive modelling within a unified sustainable combustion framework. Experimental investigations were performed using WPO10 and WPO20 blends containing 50 and 100 ppm CuO nanoparticles under acetylene flow rates of 5 and 10 LPM. Among all tested fuel combinations, A5WPO10Cu100 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a maximum brake thermal efficiency of 33.12 %, corresponding to an 8.27 % improvement over diesel, together with a 21.03 % reduction in brake specific energy consumption. The optimum fuel also reduced HC, CO, and smoke opacity by 41.46 %, 47.62 %, and 43.58 %, respectively, while A10WPO10Cu100 produced the highest combustion intensity with a peak heat release rate of 68.9 J/°CA, maximum cylinder pressure of 90.5 bar, and minimum ignition delay of 8.75 °CA, indicating enhanced premixed combustion and catalytic oxidation. Although NOx emissions increased under higher acetylene induction due to elevated combustion temperatures, the overall combustion efficiency and emission trade-off were significantly improved. To further establish predictive capability, Linear Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models were developed using the experimental dataset. Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated the highest prediction accuracy with R2 values ranging from 0.995 to 0.999 and prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, confirming its robustness in predicting nonlinear combustion, performance, and emission characteristics. The integrated experimental and machine learning framework demonstrates that CuO nano-enhanced WPO coupled with acetylene induction is a promising strategy for improving CI engine efficiency while simultaneously advancing intelligent combustion optimization for sustainable transportation applications. To further enhance predictive capability and intelligent engine diagnostics, advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF) were developed using experimentally measured combustion, performance, and emission parameters. The Random Forest model demonstrated superior nonlinear prediction capability with prediction accuracy exceeding 98 %, coefficient of determination (R2) approaching 0.995–0.999 for major engine responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The viral deviation: a quantitative analysis of social media engagement metrics on non-compliant flight deck behaviors
abstract: Background Normalization of Deviance (NoD) is a well-documented organizational failure mode in aviation, yet its propagation through digital ecosystems remains unexplored. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) highlights a critical mentorship vacuum due to pilot retirements, and social media platforms increasingly serve as informal training environments. This study introduces the concept of Algorithmic Normalization of Deviance- ANoD, hypothesizing that recommendation algorithms systematically reward and amplify “gray-zone” cockpit behaviors that erode sterile flight deck protocols. Method We conducted a stratified netnographic analysis of 150 high-visibility aviation videos (N = 150) across Instagram Reels, split between algorithmically recommended content (n = 100) and curated influencer content (n = 50). A novel coding framework operationalized compliance (Compliant vs. Gray Zone vs. Deviant) and incentive structures. Engagement metrics were analyzed to quantify the algorithmic advantage of non-compliant behavior. Results The analysis reveals a directionally consistent “Viral Deviation” pattern rather than a statistically decisive one. Gray-zone recordings (i.e., technically legal but procedurally borderline) comprised 57% of the sample and attracted higher engagement than compliant content, although this difference was small and did not reach conventional significance (d = 0.24, p = 0.11). The clearest signal emerged between content sources: algorithmically surfaced posts showed significantly higher interaction rates than curated influencer posts (d = 0.31, p = 0.029), a small but statistically significant per-view advantage for content promoted directly by the recommendation system. Structural incentive analysis further indicates that monetization pressures co-occur with increased gray-zone production, structurally analogous to a parallel, shadow curriculum associated with conditions that may facilitate drift. Conclusion The study identifies statistical associations, not causal relationships, and the downstream behavioural impact on pilots is hypothesised from the algorithmic-pattern evidence rather than directly measured. Within those bounds, social media algorithms constitute a structurally unmonitored distribution channel whose observed associations with gray-zone content amplification are consistent with a normalisation-of-deviance feedback mechanism operating beyond current regulatory oversight — an association that warrants urgent empirical validation and proactive governance. We propose a shift from prohibition to risk-stratified governance, recommending that regulators distinguish between handheld (high-risk) and mounted (managed-risk) devices, and integrate digital algorithmic literacy into ab-initio pilot training to counter this new systemic threat. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Decoding entrepreneurial intention: A systematic review, theoretical framework synthesis, and research trajectories
abstract: Entrepreneurial intention (EI) is a critical psychological construct for understanding the precursors of entrepreneurial behavior. Despite a surge in empirical research over the past decade, the literature on EI remains fragmented across theoretical frameworks, methodological approaches, and contextual applications. This study systematically reviews 53 peer-reviewed articles on entrepreneurial intention published between 2018 and 2025 to synthesize theoretical frameworks, methodological patterns, key findings, and future research directions. Guided by the PRISMA approach, the review reveals the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) as the predominant model, frequently integrated with constructs from Social Cognitive Theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and moral or contextual frameworks. Quantitative cross-sectional designs dominate the methodological landscape, often involving university student samples and the use of structural equation modelling techniques for hypothesis testing. Findings consistently confirm the central role of attitude, perceived behavioral control, and self-efficacy in predicting EI, while more recent studies highlight the growing significance of emotional intelligence, cultural influences, institutional support, and entrepreneurship education. However, the review identifies key limitations, including the overreliance on student-based samples, a lack of longitudinal and experimental designs, and limited generalizability to actual entrepreneurial behavior in real-world settings. Additionally, contextual diversity across emerging and developed economies remains underexplored. In response, the study proposes five future research trajectories: theoretical expansion beyond dominant models, increased adoption of behavioral and longitudinal approaches, broader contextual and demographic inclusion, pedagogical innovation in entrepreneurship education, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration. By mapping evolving trends and gaps in EI research, this review provides a foundation for more dynamic, inclusive, and practically relevant scholarship in entrepreneurship studies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: HAD-TAM: Health insurance anomaly detection via truncated affinity maximization with degree-normalized scoring
abstract: Substantial financial losses are incurred annually as a result of medical insurance fraud, driven by subtle behaviors such as false diagnoses and over-prescription. Although heterogeneous graph structures can be exploited by existing graph neural network-based methods, they often rely on manually selected meta-paths, and the identification of structural anomalies remains a persistent challenge. To address these challenges, Health insurance Anomaly Detection via Truncated Affinity Maximization (HAD-TAM) is proposed as a health insurance fraud detection method, wherein degree-normalized anomaly score-guided meta-path selection is first combined with dual-threshold edge pruning to capture structural anomalies. First, the meta-graph with the highest degree-normalized anomaly score is selected by the model to highlight structures potentially indicative of fraud. Second, non-homophily edges are iteratively pruned by the model using both global and local thresholds to suppress noise and preserve meaningful structure. Finally, the neighborhood affinity of normal nodes is maximized by the model to better separate them from anomalies and improve fraud detection accuracy. Experimental results show that HAD-TAM outperforms eleven advanced baseline methods on two real-world medical insurance datasets, achieving a 2.41% improvement in AUROC and a 1.06% improvement in AUPRC. Furthermore, it exhibits good generalization to public datasets such as Amazon and Reddit. © 2026

title: Determination of discount rates in business valuation and public project evaluation: A systematic review from the perspective of international finance and financial theory
abstract: The discount rate plays a central role in business valuation and public project appraisal because it links risk to the valuation of future cash flows and guides the efficient allocation of resources. However, the global literature lacks methodological consensus and shows significant divergences between private and social approaches, as well as between developed and emerging economies. The present study aims to synthesize the main theoretical and empirical approaches used to determine discount rates from the perspective of international finance. A systematic literature review was conducted following the prisma protocol. Searches were conducted in scopus, web of science, sciencedirect, ssrn, and jstor, using boolean search strings related to “discount rate”, “wacc”, “capm”, “social discount rate”, and “country risk premium”. Studies published from 2000 to 2025, in english and spanish, were included. Only studies with a clear methodological foundation in finance and economics were considered. The analysis was carried out through a qualitative thematic synthesis. The reviewed literature indicates the predominance of the wacc and asset pricing models as the primary references for estimating private discount rates, and reports the increasing use of multifactor models and country risk premiums in the international context. For public projects, the literature identifies two main approaches: the social rate of time preference and the social opportunity cost of capital. The studies also suggest substantial heterogeneity across countries, with generally higher discount rates in emerging economies. No single discount rate is universally applicable; instead, its estimation depends on the local institutional context, the objectives of the investment, and the nature of the risks being evaluated. These findings should be interpreted in light of the qualitative nature of the synthesis. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives
abstract: Despite broad agreement on the urgency of sustainability transitions that protect biodiversity, conservation conflicts continue to rise. This paper examines environmental conflicts in protected areas (PAs), highlighting the overlooked link between conflict and justice. Existing frameworks often fail to distinguish between conflict manifestations and determinants, or to integrate justice theories with economic perspectives. This study provides a comprehensive review of the literature to support the analysis of PA conflicts and develops a robust framework that integrates justice considerations with the economic perspective. Conflicts are viewed as inherent to complex social–ecological systems, shaped by social relations and rights over ecosystem services. The framework is structured around three analytical axes: substance (what the conflict is about), process (how it unfolds), and relation (who is involved with-whom). It differentiates between how conflicts appear (i.e., manifestation) and what causes them (i.e., determinants), framed through distributive, procedural, and recognition justice. This perspective challenges linear assumptions that conflicts always stem from injustices, emphasizing their potential to drive institutional change. The framework offers a novel approach to assessing justice-conflict dynamics in PAs governance, providing comprehensive toolkit for promoting equitable conservation strategies. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. As a case, this paper traces the historic development of one of safety’s most influential and iconic safety concepts, the accident triangle, over nearly a century through successive cycles of replication, variation, and selection. Knowledge of factors that influence the adoption of safety concepts can contribute to the design of more effective concepts that attract attention and of social and organisational environments that are receptive of these concepts. In the end, provided the concepts in question are useful, this can contribute to enhancing safety and reducing harm. In addition, the insights gained in this paper can help safety professionals and academics to critically reflect on the development of safety concepts, to help them better understand how safety concepts evolve and can change meaning leading to various interpretations and reflect on what this means for their own adoption of concepts and eventually their practice. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Influencer beware: The buffering role of sponsor–influencer fit in the commercialization-authenticity trade-off
abstract: As social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly commercialize their online presence through sponsored content, understanding how sponsorship intensity shapes consumer responses has become important. Drawing on attribution and congruence theories and the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how sponsorship levels influence audience engagement and purchase intentions through perceived personal authenticity (PPA) and whether these effects depend on sponsor–SMI fit. Three experimental studies were conducted to test the proposed relationships. The results show that higher sponsorship levels reduce consumers’ intention to follow influencers and share their content. Sponsor–SMI fit attenuates the negative effect of sponsorship intensity on PPA. Thereby mitigating its adverse effects on consumer engagement and purchase intentions. We further demonstrate that sponsorship level affects consumer responses indirectly through PPA and that this indirect effect is contingent on sponsor–SMI fit. These findings advance the influencer marketing literature by applying the ERC framework to distinguish the different authenticity types and their impact on consumer behavior. The study also extends attribution and congruence theories by explaining how and when commercialization influences consumer responses and offers practical guidance for balancing monetization and authenticity in influencer marketing. © 2026 The Authors

title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process
abstract: Digital technologies influence consumers across need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase activity. This study examines how six features of digitally mediated promotion—informativeness, personalisation, interactivity, entertainment, credibility, and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)—shape attitudes and subsequent behavioural responses among Albanian consumers. It also evaluates attitude as a mediator, media literacy as a moderator, and differences across decision-journey stages. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 487 valid responses from adults residing in Albania who had recently used online channels in purchase-related activity. The conceptual model integrates the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the Theory of Planned Behaviour, and the customer-journey perspective. Measurement and structural relationships were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples; supplementary analyses tested mediation, moderation, age-group differences, and stage-specific effects. Results: Credibility was the strongest predictor of attitude (β = 0.291), followed by positive eWOM (β = 0.245) and informativeness (β = 0.230). Attitude positively predicted purchase intention (β = 0.597), online engagement (β = 0.467), and recommendation intention (β = 0.517), while purchase intention predicted self-reported purchasing (β = 0.553). Attitude mediated the effects of all six promotional features on purchase intention. Media literacy strengthened the informativeness–attitude relationship (β = 0.109), whereas age-group differences were not significant. Influence was greatest during information search and alternative evaluation. Conclusion: Effective online communication depends more on usefulness, credibility, and authentic social evidence than on entertainment alone. The findings extend evidence from a Southeast European setting and show that favourable attitudes translate into purchases only when perceived value, affordability, payment, and delivery conditions permit conversion. Managers should therefore combine transparent information and trustworthy reviews with financially clear offers and sustained post-purchase support. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: River tourism based on community participation and regional linkages for sustainable livelihoods: The case of Can Tho City, Vietnam
abstract: This study examines the role of community-based river tourism and regional linkages in supporting sustainable livelihoods in Can Tho City, Vietnam. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining surveys of 385 tourists, 47 local households, and 18 tourism officials and community representatives with 36 semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), cluster analysis, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were integrated through thematic coding, triangulation, and SWOT analysis. The findings indicate that community-based river tourism contributes to livelihood diversification, income generation, skill development, and social capital formation. Participating households reported relatively high livelihood stability (mean = 3.87) and moderate government support (mean = 3.59), whereas regional linkage participation remained low (mean = 1.79). EFA results revealed a common factor linking government support, regional cooperation, and livelihood outcomes, with factor loadings ranging from -0.64 to -0.51. For tourism officials and community representatives, EFA identified two governance dimensions—regional coordination and community-enterprise synergy—which explained 84.83 of the total variance. Tourists reported high overall satisfaction (mean = 4.35), strong community interaction (mean = 4.61), positive perceptions of cultural preservation (mean = 3.71), and willingness to pay for tourism services (mean = 3.98). Regression analysis showed that cultural preservation perception was the only statistically significant predictor of tourist satisfaction ( β = 0.146, p = 0.004 ). Open-ended responses highlighted key development priorities, including reducing crowding ( 29.6 ), increasing the availability of tour guides ( 26.8 ), enhancing cultural activities ( 23.9 ), and extending tour duration ( 19.7 ). Overall, sustainable livelihood outcomes depend not only on community participation but also on effective governance, cultural preservation, and stronger regional integration. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical implications for sustainable tourism planning in riverine destinations of the Mekong Delta. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Toward a relational typology: Mapping social entrepreneur-resident interactions in community-led tourism social entrepreneurship
abstract: Research on tourism social entrepreneurship has focused on exogenous models while overlooking host communities' agency. The aim of this study was to examine interactions between social entrepreneurs and residents in the context of community-led tourism social entrepreneurship. The exploratory qualitative study design involved three fieldwork phases. We used two dimensions—the initiator's primary motivation and the embeddedness forms in the responder's actions—to identify four relationship types: traditional bonding ties, instrumental ties, patron–client ties, and value-congruent alliances. The social action and embeddedness theories guided our examination of relational formation. Findings further reveal a model of power shift and relationship dynamics. This model suggests that a power shift involves three principal stages centered around dependence. In summary, we provide here a typological framework for analyzing social entrepreneur–resident interactions and offer practical insights into sustainable community development. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A bibliometric review of farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia: A two-decade study
abstract: Farmer livelihood resilience is crucial given the sector's contribution to the national economic resilience, particularly in Indonesia. Despite its importance, a comprehensive synthesis of how this field has evolved over the past two decades remains limited. The objectives of this study are to provide an overview of the circumstances and challenges related to farmer resilience by examining research on farmer livelihood resilience in Indonesia. Employing a hybrid methodology that combines bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by PRISMA protocols, this research analyzed 184 articles, 94 conference papers, and 2 review papers indexed in the Scopus database from 2005 to 2025. VOSviewer software was utilized to visualize co-occurrence networks and publication patterns. The results demonstrate a substantial increase in academic interest over the last decade, with a significant peak in publications after 2015. The analysis identified five dominant thematic clusters: (1) Smallholder Farmers’ Climate Change Adaptation in Indonesia; (2) Sustainable Agriculture and Land Conversion Policy; (3) Social Capital and Collective Action for Sustainable Agriculture; (4) Livelihood Strategies of Oil Palm and Agroforestry Farmers; (5) Sustainability of Palm Oil Smallholders. This study fills a critical research gap by bridging quantitative mapping with qualitative insights, offering a strategic roadmap for future scholarly inquiry. The findings emphasize that strengthening farmer resilience in Indonesia requires integrated policy frameworks that prioritize institutional support and optimized social capital. Ultimately, these results provide vital evidence for policymakers to design more inclusive and sustainable agricultural development strategies. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The psychology of AI-mediated communication across languages
abstract: Communication across languages is increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence (AI). This creates opportunities for people with different language backgrounds to communicate in their respective native languages. AI-mediated communication can therefore reduce cognitive effort, disfluency, and social stigma associated with speaking a non-native language. At the same time, non-native language use influences cognitive, emotional, and social processes that go beyond the accurate transmission of meaning. By affecting these processes and introducing new cues, AI-mediated communication could also have unintended effects on communication effectiveness and social evaluations between interlocutors. We examine the conditions under which these effects may help or hinder cross-linguistic interactions and identify directions for research on the psychology of cross-linguistic communication as AI language tools become prevalent. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Beyond Technology Readiness Levels: Developing and Evaluating an Industry 5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework for Regulated Life Sciences Manufacturing
abstract: Purpose: Regulated life sciences manufacturing organisations face increasing pressure to adopt Industry 5.0 (I5.0) innovations while maintaining patient safety, product quality, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. Existing assessment models provide useful perspectives on technical maturity, expectation dynamics, and organisational innovation capability, but do not fully assess whether an innovation is ready to progress responsibly in a regulated, multi-stakeholder environment. This paper develops an I5.0 Innovation Readiness Framework and presents a preliminary practitioner-informed evaluation of its use in regulated life sciences manufacturing. Methods: This paper uses design science research structured through the Double Diamond process. The framework was developed through literature review, advisory feedback, subject matter expert input, practitioner workshops, case-based application, surveys, and thematic analysis. Evaluation was conducted with a small, purposively selected cohort of 16 practitioners from a single educational-industry programme. Results: The framework comprises three linked tools: the Innovation Maturity Assessment, Innovation Maturity Rubric, and Innovation Readiness Levels. Across two exploratory workshops involving 16 experienced practitioners, participants reported that the framework supported clearer discussion of readiness and improved visibility of adoption risks. In Workshop 2, descriptive feedback indicated that 91% of respondents viewed Innovation Readiness Levels as clearer than Technology Readiness Levels, 82% found the framework useful for comparing innovation timelines, and 75% would recommend it. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary practitioner feedback rather than sector-wide validation. Conclusion: The findings support the conceptual distinction between innovation readiness and technology readiness and indicate the need to assess technical, regulatory, organisational, stakeholder, and societal dimensions together when evaluating I5.0 innovation in regulated manufacturing. Further evaluation with broader industry cohorts, quality and regulatory professionals, and regulatory stakeholders is required. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Examining perceptual spillover effects in social media influencer marketing effectiveness: A PLS-SEM and fsQCA approach
abstract: Social media influencers (SMIs) play a pertinent role in shaping brand evaluations, yet how influencer-level perceptions translate into brand-level evaluations and SMI marketing effectiveness remains unclear. Drawing on spillover effects as a theoretical lens, a two-stage quantitative approach was adopted. Results from the Stage 1 serial mediation model suggest that SMI social attractiveness is directly associated with purchase intention and indirectly associated with purchase intention through brand attitude. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, perceived SMI authenticity does not mediate the relationship between social attractiveness and purchase intention. Consistent with a spillover interpretation, perceived SMI authenticity serves as an evaluative facilitator associated with brand-level evaluations rather than directly with purchase intention. In a separate Stage 2, fsQCA was used to explore configurations associated with SMI marketing effectiveness, which, in this study, encompasses both transactional and non-transactional dimensions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. This research extends passion theory by highlighting its interpersonal signaling effects and reframes silence as a strategic emotion-regulation response. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Investigations of the cascading effect of hotel entrepreneur's optimism on employees’ work behaviors and customers evaluations in small and medium hospitality enterprises
abstract: Given the significant proportion of small and medium hospitality enterprises (SMHEs) in the hospitality and tourism industry, this study focuses on the influential role and the power of entrepreneurs. Integrating optimism theory and social learning theory, we delineate how the entrepreneur's attributes and leadership exert a cascading effect across hierarchical levels, impacting both employees and customers. A multisource field study (248 entrepreneurs, 681 employees, and 1179 customers) shows that an entrepreneur's optimism drives adaptation to new leadership styles, i.e., e-leadership and green leadership, crucial for achieving the organization's goals regarding digital transformation and sustainability. An entrepreneur's e-leadership positively affects employees’ creative performance, while green leadership has a crossover effect on employees’ green behaviors, ultimately increasing customer satisfaction and ratings. We discuss new implications for understanding both the emergence and the profound effects of new leadership styles, especially in the context of SMHEs in the hospitality and tourism industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Assessing the viability of urban rooftop photovoltaic systems under new regulatory frameworks in Brazil via an evolutionary real options approach
abstract: The transition towards decentralized and sustainable urban energy systems requires robust decision-making frameworks that account for policy changes, market uncertainties, and investment flexibility. This study applies an Evolutionary Real Options Approach (EROA) to evaluate the economic viability of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems in Brazil under the New Mark of Distributed Generation (NMDG), a regulatory change that alters incentives for net metering. By incorporating stochastic volatility models, such as the Heston model and Geometric Brownian motion (GBM) with jumps, this work quantifies the impact of regulatory changes on investment timing and system sizing decisions. Results indicate a significant reduction in financial returns and a delay in investment decisions under the new regulation. The introduction of the new regulation has led to reductions in returns of approximately 18% and 23% for the Heston and GBM with jumps models, respectively. In terms of decision sequences, the Heston model presents increased opportunities for phased investment due to its greater flexibility. On the other hand, the GBM with jumps model encourages immediate investment in a complete solar system. The new regulation results in a delay of 6 to 12 months at entry points, regardless of the chosen model. These findings contribute to the understanding of urban energy transitions, policy impacts on decentralized generation, and investment dynamics in sustainable urban infrastructure. © 2026 The Authors

title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Second, we explore how ambitious and flexible first offers should be. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Abandonment is better explained by institutional distrust and multidimensional attachment than by cohort labels, but generation remains consequential for where users go next. Platforms seeking retention should repair credibility and cultivate wanted attachment rather than relying on lock-in or age targeting alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Negotiating the contested: A framework for studying social issue negotiations
abstract: Negotiation research has yielded useful insights on how to manage economic and business interactions by highlighting the importance of information sharing, trade-offs, and integrative solutions in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. However, these approaches inadequately explain why negotiations over social issues such as immigration reform and climate change can remain deadlocked despite sustained efforts to reach agreement. Drawing upon recent research, we introduce an organizing framework that identifies three common features of such negotiations: moralization, identity threat, and public contestation. Moralization frames issues as matters of right and wrong, reducing willingness to compromise; identity concerns transform policy disagreements into threats to group membership and self-concept; and public scrutiny increases reputational risks and constrains flexibility. Together, these dynamics hinder engagement, value creation, and the quality of agreements. We review emerging interventions—including moral reframing, perspective sharing, high-quality listening, informal dialogue, and third-party mediation—that may mitigate these barriers. We conclude by highlighting the need for research examining how moral, identity, and public pressures interact across levels of analysis to shape social issue negotiation processes and outcomes. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. By conceptually and empirically distinguishing ambassadors from testimonials, this study shows that social proof is not a uniformly positive force but a context-dependent mechanism conditioned by authenticity, with implications for transparency-oriented digital marketing strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The evolution of remote operating centres: Towards a new geography of mining
abstract: In mining ‘remoteness’ was once a measure of isolation from other activities and communities. With the adoption of new digitalization technologies, ‘remote operations’ now more often refers to the management, monitoring and control of mining equipment, processes and infrastructure from locations which are geographically separate from the immediate extraction site. This paper reviews the evolution of remote operating centres in the sector and explores the nature and implications of the new geography of mining that they are helping to create. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Nature- versus non-nature-based recreation: A comparative assessment of self-reported anxiety alleviation
abstract: Nature-based recreation delivers vital ecosystem services that shape human physical and psychological well-being, representing a core category of nature's contributions to people within urban and peri-urban social-ecological landscapes. While non-nature-based recreational activities can also improve people's quality of life by mitigating anxiety, the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based recreation to people's mental health, and the factors that influence them, remain largely unknown. Here, we conducted a survey of 15,522 respondents across China and applied structural equation modeling to show that nature-based recreation is associated with significantly stronger self-reported anxiety alleviation than non-nature-based recreation. A longer time allocation to nature-based recreational activities during holidays and weekends was also associated with greater self-reported alleviation of anxiety from nature-based recreation. Furthermore, predictors including environmental pressure, anxiety-related attributes, and socioeconomic status were associated with the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based anxiety alleviation, with these associations partly mediated via recreation engagement. This empirical evidence improves integrated landscape and urban planning frameworks by providing context-specific guidance for sustainable urban recreational space design and cross-regional governance focused on public health. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
abstract: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets. © 2026

title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. These findings provide insights for organizations seeking to integrate AI into employee selection while maintaining justice and inclusion. As AI becomes more prevalent in hiring, organizations should prioritize human oversight, ensuring that AI supports rather than replaces human. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Driving police engagement through talent management: Evidence from Abu Dhabi
abstract: This study examines the relationship between talent management practices and employee engagement, as well as the moderating role of business analytics and the subsequent impact on employee performance within the Abu Dhabi Police. Specifically, the research explores how talent attraction, retention, learning and development, and career management influence employee engagement, which in turn affects job performance. Drawing on social exchange theory, dynamic capability theory, and Aon Hewitt's employee engagement model, a quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to senior officers across various departments. A total of 383 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.3.9. The findings reveal that all four dimensions of talent management (talent attraction, talent retention, learning and development, and career management) have significant positive effects on employee engagement. Furthermore, employee engagement strongly and significantly influences employee performance, underscoring its pivotal role in organizational effectiveness. The results of the moderation analysis indicate that business analytics significantly strengthens the relationships between talent attraction, learning and development, and career management and employee engagement, with learning and development and talent attraction showing the strongest moderating effects, whereas the moderating effect on talent retention is statistically insignificant. The model explains 53.8 of the variance in employee engagement, indicating satisfactory predictive power. These findings contribute to the literature by integrating business analytics into the talent management—engagement—performance nexus, particularly within a public sector policing context. Practically, the results highlight the strategic importance of leveraging data-driven and analytics-enabled HRM practices to personalize talent management interventions, enhance perceived fairness, and improve engagement outcomes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that while business analytics enhances most talent management dimensions, its influence is not uniform across all practices, particularly in the case of talent retention. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers and HR leaders seeking to build agile, high-performing, and engaged workforces in dynamic environments. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. This study systematically identifies and prioritizes the key determinants shaping the planning of fast-charging infrastructure in China. A two-round Delphi process was conducted with 30 experts drawn from government, industry, and academia to establish consensus on critical influencing factors. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the central role of policy coherence, sustainable financial models, and interoperability in accelerating the diffusion of infrastructure and reducing regional inequality. The study advances a theoretically informed prioritization framework to support strategic infrastructure planning in rapidly electrifying economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. label: Social Sciences
title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. Overall, the reform reduced measured aggregate productivity in China's registered, above-scale industrial sector by 3.3 percent, with entry into the above-scale industrial sector accounting for about 45 percent of the estimated decline. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. It identifies young adults’ support-seeking motivations and models their associations with two interaction processes (Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity) and two psychological outcomes (Resilience and AI Dependence). In Study 1, we developed the Motivation Scale for Generative AI (MS-GAI) through theory-driven item generation and interviews and validated it with a survey of Korean young adults (N = 300). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported an eight-factor, 40-item structure grounded in four social-support domains and supplemented by context-specific motivations. In Study 2, structural equation modeling showed that Emotional Support and Self-Enhancement were positively associated with both Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity. Objective Advice Seeking was positively associated with Perceived Authenticity, whereas Learning Assistance, Daily Problem-Solving, and Entertainment/Mood Diversion were positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Perceived Authenticity was also positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Both interaction processes were positively related to self-reported Resilience and AI Dependence, with Interaction Intensity showing the stronger association with AI Dependence. These findings identify distinct but overlapping interaction pathways through which support-seeking motivations are associated with adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. The study extends understanding of social support in human–AI interaction by providing a validated motivation measure and showing how shared interaction processes relate to both short-term perceived recovery and dependence. The findings are consistent with the Paradoxes of Technology perspective and highlight the need for emotionally supportive yet balanced design and policy safeguards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

label: Social Sciences
title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. This exhaustion-driven withdrawal is amplified rather than buffered by correction confidence, suggesting that individual motivation alone is insufficient in hostile environments. These findings highlight emotional exhaustion as a key psychological constraint on citizen-led fact-checking and suggest that platform-level moderation targeting hostile comments is critical to protect the emotional resources required for a resilient democratic debate in digital environments. © 2026 The Authors

title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and sociotechnical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
