title: Management control systems and organizational innovation: A bibliometric analysis of the literature (1977–2026)
abstract: Management control and organizational innovation are widely recognized as major determinants of firm performance and long-term competitiveness in contemporary business environments. Nevertheless, these two dimensions are frequently perceived as conflicting, as management control is traditionally associated with formalization, standardization, and performance monitoring, whereas innovation requires flexibility, experimentation, and organizational adaptability. This apparent tension has led several scholars to question the compatibility between management control systems and innovation processes, encouraging innovative organizations to explore new governance and coordination mechanisms. Against this backdrop, the present study aims to examine the evolution, role, and effectiveness of management control within innovation-oriented organizational contexts. To address this objective, the research adopts a bibliometric approach combined with a structured literature review in order to analyze the scientific production related to management control and innovation. The study investigates the conceptual transformations and practical reconfigurations of management control in response to contemporary organizational changes and emerging managerial challenges. Using 433 scientific articles published in the fields of economics, management, and organizational studies, the analysis identifies the main publication trends, influential authors, dominant research themes, and evolving theoretical perspectives within the literature. The findings reveal a significant and continuous growth in academic interest concerning the relationship between management control and innovation, particularly in relation to organizational agility, strategic performance, digital transformation, and dynamic capabilities. The study also highlights the progressive shift from traditional control mechanisms toward more flexible and interactive forms of management control adapted to innovation-driven environments. Furthermore, this bibliometric review contributes to ongoing debates by identifying emerging research streams and proposing future theoretical and methodological directions for scholars interested in the interaction between management control systems and organizational innovation. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Physiological and behavioral modeling of stress and cognitive load in web-based question answering
abstract: Time pressure and question difficulty can trigger stress and cognitive overload in web-based surveys, compromising data quality and user experience. Most stress detection methods are based on low-resolution self-reports, which are poorly suited for capturing fast, moment-to-moment changes during short online tasks. Addressing this gap, we conducted a 2 × 2 within-subjects study (N = 29), manipulating question difficulty and time pressure in a web-based multiple-choice questionnaire. Participants completed general knowledge and cognitive questions while we collected multimodal data: mouse dynamics, eye tracking, electrocardiogram, and electrodermal activity. Using condition-based and self-reported labels, we used statistical and machine learning models to model stress and question difficulty. Our results show distinct physiological and behavioral patterns within very short timeframes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of rapidly detecting cognitive-affective states in digital environments, paving the way for more adaptive, ethical, and user-aware survey interfaces. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: CFD Investigation of Thermal and Electrical Behavior of Photovoltaic Modules Equipped with Heat Sinks and Vortex Generators
abstract: The Photovoltaic (PV) modules suffer performance losses at high operating temperatures, especially in hot and low-wind conditions, making effective cooling essential. This study numerically investigates a fan-assisted PV cooling duct equipped with heat sinks and vortex generators (VGs) using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The novelty of the work lies in the integrated evaluation of duct height, fin spacing, VG height, inclination angle, and attack angle within a single forced-convection framework. The model was validated against published benchmark data with deviations below 5%. The results demonstrate that the reduction of duct height from 200 mm to 100 mm can decrease the PV surface temperature by 10 °C and among all finned cases, the array with 22 fins exhibited maximum cooling whilst the best compromise between heat-transfer enhancement and pressure drop was provided by using an arrangement with 18 fins in a given area. Thermal performance improved with increasing VG height, but the 40 mm VG gave the greatest heat-transfer coefficient at the cost of relatively high-pressure loss. title: Research on online multi-step short-term photovoltaic power forecasting based on selective representation-driven concept drift adaptation
abstract: Accurate short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the secure operation and optimal scheduling of power systems. However, PV power data are highly non-stationary due to weather fluctuations, seasonal transitions, and changing operating conditions, which often cause concept drift in real-world scenarios. Most existing methods are developed in offline settings and lack the ability to adapt continuously to evolving data streams. To address this issue, this study proposes an online learning framework for multi-step short-term PV power forecasting. Specifically, a shared-parameter dual-branch Informer concept encoder is designed to capture concept discrepancies between historical and incoming data, while a mixture-of-experts adaptive parameter generator is introduced to produce targeted update parameters for different drift patterns. In addition, a selective segmentation mechanism is incorporated into the TimeBridge backbone to improve the modeling of critical temporal blocks. Experimental results on two real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best overall forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods. The proposed framework provides an effective solution for drift-aware online PV forecasting and offers practical support for enhancing the reliability, stability, and dispatch efficiency of power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources. title: Comparative evaluation of SRF-PLL and instantaneous-power LVRT control for a three-wire grid-connected PV system under ground faults
abstract: The performance of low voltage ride-through (LVRT) control depends on the voltage information used for synchronisation and current-reference generation, as well as the physical current paths of the converter. In this paper, four synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) and instantaneous power theory (IPT) implementations are compared on a common 1.504 MW photovoltaic simulation model under single line-to-ground and double line-to-ground faults. The three-wire converter is connected through a delta–grounded-wye transformer. Consequently, its zero-sequence line current is constrained to zero, although ground-fault current is present on the grounded transformer side. The current-control action is therefore confined to the two independent converter axes. The comparison uses conventional and positive-sequence-conditioned SRF and IPT implementations with a shared reactive-current-priority LVRT law, DC-voltage regulation and current-reference limits. For the double line-to-ground case, positive-sequence IPT provides 730.6 kvar at the low-voltage measurement point, compared with 376.1 kvar for instantaneous-voltage IPT, while its nonfundamental current residual decreases from 22.06% to 0.037%. However, the latter controller has a smaller 100 Hz active-power component, demonstrating a trade-off between power oscillation and current quality. Actual transient current reaches 1.234 pu despite a 1.2 pu reference ceiling. Sequence-extraction diagnostics against established DSOGI and DSC methods, together with transformer-side measurements, explain these outcomes. Hardware-in-loop captures document laboratory-platform observations; all quantitative controller comparisons are based on simulations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From generative AI usage to entrepreneurial intention: The sequential roles of task and social self-efficacy
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is rapidly evolving and creating new possibilities for supporting students' entrepreneurial development. However, limited research has examined how GAI usage is associated with entrepreneurial intention (EI) through specific psychological pathways. Drawing on self-efficacy theory, this study examines the relationship between GAI usage and EI, focusing on the mediating roles of task and social self-efficacy. Using survey data from 521 Chinese university students, this study empirically tests the proposed model. The results show that GAI usage is positively associated with students' task and social self-efficacy. However, task self-efficacy (TSE) is not directly associated with EI. In contrast, social self-efficacy (SSE) accounts for a significant indirect association between GAI usage and EI. Moreover, a significant sequential indirect association is observed, linking GAI usage with EI through TSE and SSE. By disentangling the distinct roles of TSE and SSE, this study shows that the association between GAI usage and EI is consistent with pathways that differ in their functions and proximity to entrepreneurial action. The findings also provide practical insights for entrepreneurship education and AI-supported learning environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Short-term emission pathways in India's iron and steel sector: A hybrid framework combining quantitative methods and bottom-up modelling
abstract: This study presents a hybrid assessment framework to quantify current greenhouse gas emissions and evaluate decarbonization pathways for India's iron and steel industry up to 2030. The framework establishes a sectoral emissions baseline and examines the impact of alternative mitigation scenarios, providing a foundation for long-term decarbonization planning beyond 2030. The industry was categorized into two segments: major integrated steel producers, representing more than 57% of national crude steel output, and other producers, comprising predominantly electric-route and small-to-medium-scale operations. Emission intensity estimates for major producers were derived from reported production and emissions data, whereas emissions from other producers were assessed using a bottom-up, process-based estimation. The study estimated the baseline emission intensity for financial year 2023–24 at 2.31 tCO₂/tcs, with major producers averaging 2.53 tCO₂/tcs and other (secondary) producers operating at a lower intensity of 2.02 tCO₂/tcs. Six scenarios were modelled through 2030, revealing that a combination of 30% scrap use and 50% renewable electricity offer the most effective short-term mitigation, reducing intensity to 1.66 tCO₂/tcs. While emissions from major producers remain largely stable, most reductions are driven by secondary producers, highlighting their greater decarbonization potential. Despite these improvements in carbon intensity, projected growth in steel production is expected to increase total sectoral emissions by approximately 20–74% by 2030, depending on the scenario considered. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From waste to Watts: Causal evidence on AI-enabled waste-to-energy and financial performance in tourism and hospitality using an empirics-first investigation
abstract: This study examines whether artificial intelligence enabled waste to energy adoption improves financial performance in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms and identifies the mechanisms and conditions shaping these effects. Using an empirics first mixed methods design, we combine interviews with 41 managers and a firm year panel of United Kingdom listed tourism, travel, and hospitality firms from 2015 to 2025. Difference in differences models with firm and year fixed effects show that adoption is associated with significantly higher financial performance, particularly at greater levels of adoption intensity. The findings indicate that energy cost savings and operational efficiency partially explain these gains. Performance benefits are also stronger in firms with higher baseline waste intensity and during periods of elevated energy prices. The study demonstrates that AI enabled waste to energy functions as an operational capability that can generate measurable economic value when integrated into organisational routines and governance systems. © 2026 The Author.

title: Architected NiTi alloys with elastically dominated regions for efficient and stable elastocaloric cooling
abstract: Elastocaloric cooling based on stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) in NiTi alloys shows great potential for low-carbon thermal management, but the functional performance–cyclic stability trade-off remains unresolved. Here, an integrated strategy of macro–microstructure fabrication is proposed to mitigate this trade-off by architecting the NiTi alloy into elastically dominated buffering regions and phase-transforming regions. In situ experiments confirm that the designed structure spatially distributes stress and temperature. Microscopic analysis further reveals that preferential longitudinal-direction martensite growth and regular secondary twins can effectively suppress plastic damage accumulation and improve reversibility. As a result, the NiTi structure exhibits significant elastocaloric performance, with a stable coefficient of performance of ∼18.7, a mechanical loss factor (ζloss) of ∼0.11 over 103 cycles, and a first recovery strain of 7.3%. This study demonstrates that macroscopic structural programming can improve elastocaloric functional performance by regulating local stress distribution and transformation behavior, offering a new approach to solid-state cooling materials beyond micro-control material optimization. © 2026

title: Uncorrelated Inequalities: A Multiproxy Measure for Household Archaeology
abstract: Inequality has received increased attention in the social sciences since the 1990s, in part because of the harm it causes and because massive inequality is avoidable. Bolstered by the Gini coefficient, a quantitative measure of unevenness in a distribution that enhances comparative studies across time and space, archaeologists have expanded the study of inequality in recent years. Many of these investigations use multiple variables to assess inequality. A challenge of such multi-proxy studies is that simply averaging Gini coefficients for multiple variables can over-represent inequality in societies where variables for inequality are not correlated. This paper provides an experimental measure—the Domain Sensitivity Gini (DSG)—and applies it to a sample of Maya archaeological case studies with extensive domestic excavations. The DSG helps disambiguate societies where wealth variables are aligned from societies where such variables are not aligned. In cases where variables do not align, different forms of wealth are not strongly correlated: a household that is poor in one domain might be wealthy in other domains. The DSG also suggests that inequality is lower than estimates based on averaged variables. This finding is valuable when set within a broader comparative context because it shows that high inequality seen today is not natural and that ancient case studies are relevant. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Critical minerals and the U.S. industrial strategy: resource security, environmental justice, and the contradictions of decarbonization
abstract: The United States has rapidly implemented a critical minerals industrial policy to support the clean energy transition and to advance national and economic security, using the Inflation Reduction Act, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Defense Production Act to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on China. This review examines whether this strategy represents decarbonization, a new phase of green industrial policy, green extractivism, a geopolitical resource-security approach, or a contradictory project that advances climate goals while perpetuating inequalities. Drawing on 65 peer-reviewed articles, books, and policy reports, the Critical Minerals Justice Dilemma framework clarifies persistent tensions among decarbonization, supply security, industrial competitiveness, environmental justice, and geopolitical resilience. Evidence from Indigenous sovereignty research, conflict mapping in the Americas, and political economy analysis shows that U.S. policy accelerates green extractivism, overrides Tribal consent through crisis-driven measures, uses techno-legal solutions that undermine democratic governance, and shifts environmental and social burdens to Global South sacrifice zones. The analysis identifies three main gaps: limited theorization of racial capitalism and settler colonialism in domestic contexts, insufficient attention to epistemic justice, and a lack of demand-side political economy. The findings suggest techno-optimistic views on green transitions do not address structural inequalities. Achieving a just strategy requires prioritizing Free, Prior, and Informed Consent, Indigenous co-governance, and demand reduction as central political imperatives rather than technical solutions. Decarbonization within racial capitalism continues to reproduce extractivist inequalities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Evaluating visitor satisfaction in protected areas: a case study of Samaria National Park
abstract: This study examines visitor satisfaction in the Samaria National Park, Crete, Greece, focusing on the pre and post-COVID-19 pandemic periods. Utilizing data from 2018 to 2022 and employing the Multi-Criteria Satisfaction Analysis (MUSA) method, we evaluated various aspects influencing visitor experiences, such as available time, landscape quality, safety, and local businesses. The findings indicate a consistently high overall satisfaction, with notable variations in the importance and satisfaction levels of specific criteria across different years since the pandemic brought a shift in visitor priorities. This paper also discusses the implications of these findings for park management, highlighting the need for tailored strategies to maintain high visitor satisfaction and promote sustainable tourism. The study underscores the critical role of protected areas in offering safe and enriching experiences. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Exploring the key drivers of biogas adoption: a business model for livestock farmers in developing countries
abstract: The increasing number of livestock farms, coupled with inadequate waste management infrastructure, has become a growing concern, contributing to environmental pollution and productivity loss. Biogas technology presents a viable solution to address these challenges by transforming waste into a sustainable energy source. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the key factors influencing the adoption intention of biogas technology as a business Model among livestock farmers. Employing a purposive sampling approach, this study gathered data from 336 livestock farmers. To ensure a comprehensive analysis, a combined methodological framework integrating both symmetric and asymmetric techniques was utilized, providing a profound understanding of the determinants impacting the intention to adopt biogas technology. This study observes a notable consistency between the findings derived from PLS-SEM and ANN. The analysis indicates that awareness of consequences (AOC) significantly influences ascription of responsibility (AOR). Additionally, findings indicate that personal norms are significantly shaped by herd mentality, initial cost, AOC, AOR, and self-esteem. Furthermore, herd mentality, personal norms, and self-esteem are significantly associated with biogas adoption. However, no significant association was found between perceived ease of use and personal norms. Meanwhile, findings from the fsQCA revealed eight distinct pathways leading to a strong intention to adopt biogas, highlighting herd mentality and AOC as critical prerequisites. Insights gained from this study will be instrumental for stakeholders involved in shaping policies, making investments, and providing technological assistance for the effective installation and operation of biogas technology. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Navigating travel paradoxes: Gen Z coping responses and implications for destination management
abstract: Paradoxes involve contradictory yet interdependent poles that persist rather than disappearing when one side is chosen. Tourism routinely exposes travelers to such tensions, but traveler-level paradoxes and the responses used to navigate them remain underexamined. Using the early tourism-recovery period of 2022 as the empirical context, this study examines paradoxical tensions perceived by young adult Gen Z student travelers and how they respond to them. A two-stage qualitative design was employed. Study A recruited 98 Norwegian Gen Z student travelers, of whom 95 provided useable responses; Study B recruited 48 Gen Z student travelers from the United Kingdom and the United States, of whom 46 provided useable responses. Online open-ended essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, with constant comparison used as an iterative coding technique. Four persistent traveler-perceived tensions emerged: personal travel fulfillment versus environmental responsibility, community economic benefit versus community livability, business recovery versus service-capacity strain, and travel maximization versus travel restraint. Responses clustered into four types: integrative or balancing, prioritization, avoidance or resignation, and externalization or delegation. These responses did not permanently resolve the paradoxes; instead, they temporarily stabilized the tension, privileged one pole, reproduced it, or displaced responsibility. The study therefore positions the 2022 recovery period as an external intensifying condition that made enduring tensions especially visible and connects traveler paradox management to destination governance and shared responsibility. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A robust energy management model for unbalanced microgrids under electricity price uncertainty considering central inverters and demand response for voltage unbalance mitigation
abstract: The increasing penetration of unbalanced loads, such as single-phase electric vehicles, in microgrids (MGs) can lead to significant Power Quality (PQ) issues, requiring demand response and ancillary services for mitigation. In this regard, an energy management model for renewable energy resources (RES) and energy storage (ES)-based buses is proposed, in which central inverters are used to support PQ and coordinate energy trading. An unbalanced IEEE 13-bus test system is used to evaluate the proposed framework, with particular emphasis on voltage unbalance mitigation and energy management. The results show that the proposed strategy reduces the voltage unbalance Indicator (VUI) from approximately 4% to below the 2%, with only a 0.35% increase in operating cost. title: GenAI support to the rescue: Mitigating employees’ psychological stress following tourism service recovery
abstract: Growing evidence suggests that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has a notable impact on employees' attitudes and behaviors, yet its potential to mitigate psychological stress remains underexplored. Combining conservation of resources (COR) theory with the “computers are social actors” (CASA) paradigm, this study investigates whether and how GenAI support (emotional versus informational) reduces tourism employees' post-recovery psychological stress. The results show that: (1) GenAI support effectively alleviates such stress following tourism service recovery; (2) emotional (vs. informational) support exerts a stronger stress-alleviating effect, which is serially mediated by social presence and emotional energy; (3) framing GenAI as an assistant (vs. a friend) further amplifies the relative effectiveness of emotional over informational support. This study enriches the understanding of GenAI's benefits and extends the workplace support literature. It also offers actionable insights into leveraging digital support tools to manage employee stress in tourism workplaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Direct Technology Diffusion in Higher Education: Evidence from Doctoral Students
abstract: This study compares direct and indirect technology diffusion in higher education, focusing on plagiarism detection software in Indian doctoral education. Using a quantitative survey of research scholars, the study finds that direct diffusion significantly improves outcomes. Similarity levels decreased substantially under direct diffusion, indicating more accurate application of plagiarism rules. Additionally, direct diffusion reduced the time required and lowered costs considerably. The findings suggest that direct access empowers users, minimizes intermediary-related inefficiencies, and enhances both effectiveness and efficiency. The study highlights cost-effectiveness as a key enabler and recommends that policymakers and institutions promote direct technology diffusion to improve adoption and strengthen academic integrity in higher education. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Assessment innovation in management education: Authentic assessment evaluation to develop workplace-ready graduates
abstract: Authentic assessment is increasingly seen as essential in management education for aligning assessment tasks with the complex, collaborative, and uncertain, multi-stakeholder demands of modern workplaces. This paper argues that, despite its popularity, the impact of authentic assessment on graduate preparedness remains poorly understood. To address this, the paper builds and evaluates an integrative model relating authentic assessment design, feedback and reflection, perceptions of assessment value, professional self-efficacy, and perceived workplace outcomes among management students. Drawing on literature about authentic assessment, experiential learning, situated cognition, assessment for learning, and employability, the paper frames authentic assessment as a holistic pedagogical system. A cross-sectional survey of 412 undergraduate and postgraduate students in business and management at four universities provides the empirical basis. The instrument was honed through expert review and a pilot test, and analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity checks, correlations, and hierarchical regression and mediation tests. The findings show that authentic assessment design strongly correlates with workplace readiness, especially when dialogic feedback, reflection, and professional self-efficacy are present. External audience group projects, live case analysis, simulations, and portfolio-based evaluation proved effective with clear criteria and guided post-task reflection. The paper contributes a process model and actionable design principles for educators to enhance employability through meaningful assessment, advancing the discourse on management education. © 2026

title: Time for challenge, money for relaxation: The resource-activity fit in tourism
abstract: Although money and time are essential resources that influence consumer decision-making, research has mostly ignored how resource concept activation affects tourists' decisions in the context of tourism. Drawing on mental simulation theory, this study investigates how activating time versus money resource concepts influences tourists' preferences for different types of tourism activities. Across three experiments, the results show that when the concept of time is activated, tourists report stronger preferences for challenging activities, whereas when the concept of money is activated, they report stronger preferences for relaxing activities. Outcome-focused simulation mediates the relationship between time activation and challenging activity preference, whereas process-focused simulation mediates the relationship between money activation and relaxing activity preference. These indirect pathways are further conditioned by maximization: the time-related pathway becomes stronger as maximization increases, whereas the money-related pathway becomes weaker. The results offer practical implications for tourism destinations that can tailor marketing strategies based on tourists’ decision-making tendencies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Blast Furnace Slag as an Alternative to Natural Mineral Materials in Pavement Engineering: A Review; [Доменный шлак как альтернатива природным минеральным материалам в дорожном строительстве: обзор]; [Жол құрылысында табиғи минералдық материалдарға балама ретіндегі домна қожы: шолу]
abstract: The presented literature review contains the results of the analysis of scientific articles for 2000-2026 years, considering the use of blast furnace slag in various areas of road construction. It has been established that there are clear differences between the application options for different types of blast furnace slag. Air-cooled blast furnace slag (ACBFS) is more often used as a coarse or fine aggregate for cement concrete and asphalt concrete, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) is used as an additional binder or as a mineral/reactive filler. When using blast furnace slag in the production of concrete, the highest results in a number of studies were achieved when replacing 20-40% of the aggregate with slag, although this indicator was not a universal optimal value. In some articles, it was pointed out that the use of blast furnace slag as part of the base of a highway or for soil stabilization was associated with an increase in CBR. Some authors point to a reduction in the consumption of Portland cement when using complex binders containing granular blast furnace slag. Data on the improvement of water resistance, fatigue resistance, Marshall stability, and rutting resistance of asphalt concrete with the introduction of ACBFS and GGBFS in various proportions are also presented. Pretreatment of porous ACBFS was also important: selective crushing and related separation methods reduced water absorption, crushing value, and the proportion of weak porous particles. The main practical conclusion is that BFS should not be treated as a single interchangeable material. Its use should be selected according to slag type, particle quality, the component being replaced, and the required pavement property. Further studies should examine whether improvements achieved by slag pretreatment at the aggregate level are retained in concrete, asphalt mixtures, and pavement-base materials under long-term service conditions. © 2026, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Low-Temperature All-Solid-State Batteries
abstract: Reliable battery operation in sub-zero environments is critical for polar exploration, military missions, and space applications. However, conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face inherent limitations at low temperatures by intrinsic hurdle of poor ionic mobility in liquid electrolytes. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), which replace liquid electrolytes with non-flammable and non-freezing solid electrolytes, are considered promising alternatives because these solid electrolytes provide high ionic conductivity at low temperatures, superior temperature stability, and exceptional safety. ASSBs still face practical limitations at extremely low temperatures due to degradation caused by interfacial side reactions and mechanical instabilities that increase resistance and polarization. Addressing these challenges is critical to realize the advantages of ASSBs and enable their practical deployment in low-temperature applications. This review provides an overview of historical developments, critical challenges, and recent progress in advancing the low-temperature performance of ASSBs. The key components of ASSBs, including solid electrolytes, cathodes, and anodes, are systematically investigated to develop strategies for improving ASSBs at low temperatures. By highlighting future perspectives, we emphasize both the potential and necessity of ASSBs to overcome the intrinsic limitations of LIBs and ensure reliable energy storage in harsh environments. title: Environmental health conditions associated with childhood stunting during the first 1000 days of life
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Child stunting is increasingly recognized not only as a nutritional disorder but also as a complex environmental health issue. Household environmental determinants, particularly safe potable water and advanced sanitation infrastructure, exert a fundamental influence on minimizing children's susceptibility to environmental health hazards that compromise linear growth trajectories. Using the transtheoretical model as a behavioral framework, the study objectives were to examine how household environmental conditions, including access to improved drinking water and sanitation, together with maternal environmental health-related behaviors, are associated with child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life in Indonesia. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the fifth wave of the Indonesian Family Life Survey. Maternal behaviors related to nutrition, healthcare utilization, and environmental conditions were operationalized as proxies for advanced stages of behavioral change. Child stunting was defined using height-for-age z-scores based on the World Health Organization Child Growth Standards. A binary logistic regression model was utilized to evaluate the multivariate associations linking maternal behavioral patterns, socio-environmental covariates, and socio-demographic indicators to the latent risk of linear growth retardation in children. FINDINGS: The prevalence of stunting among children aged 0 to 23 months was 30.32 percent. Low birth weight and higher birth order significantly increased the odds of stunting. Maternal behaviors reflecting progression to the action and maintenance stages were protective, including routine antenatal care attendance, with an odds ratio of 0.642, and delivery assisted by a skilled birth attendant, with an odds ratio of 0.707. Findings indicate that higher maternal educational attainment, improved sanitation facilities, and safe drinking water sources significantly decreased the likelihood of stunting. In contrast, maternal under nutrition elevated the associated risk by 26.5 percent. CONCLUSION: Household environmental conditions constitute fundamental determinants of child stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. Maternal progression toward advanced stages of stunting prevention behavior, reinforced by adequate health services and enabling environments, plays a critical role in reducing stunting during the first 1,000 days of life. The findings underscore the efficacy of the transtheoretical model as a robust conceptual paradigm for mitigating childhood stunting. By integrating maternal behavioral stages of change with healthcare access and environmental determinants, the research delineates a nuanced, stage-sensitive and contextually grounded architecture for analyzing early childhood growth dynamics. © 2027 The author(s). title: Prioritizing resilience criteria and indicators in urban disadvantaged areas using the Best-Worst Method (BWM)
abstract: Urban disadvantaged areas are highly vulnerable to natural hazards due to physical, social, economic, and institutional deficiencies. These areas-such as historic residential area, decayed residential areas, informal settlements, and social housing-experience distinct challenges that necessitate tailored resilience strategies. Considering Iran's high hazard proneness, strengthening resilience in such areas is an urgent priority. Existing resilience literature often adopts a generalized, city-wide perspective, lacking the granularity for effective local-level resource allocation in diverse disadvantaged areas. This study aims to identify and prioritize resilience criteria and indicators across the four types of disadvantaged areas. A comprehensive literature review extracted potential resilience criteria, refined and validated using the Delphi method with 16 experts engaged via snowball sampling. The Best-Worst Method (BWM), an MCDM approach, weighted and ranked criteria for each area type. Results show economic capacity is most critical in informal settlements. Physical-environmental aspects (building quality, infrastructure) dominate historical and decayed areas. Institutional dimensions (governance, accountability, policy support) are most influential in social housing resilience. Cross-area comparison reveals shared and context-specific determinants, underscoring the need for integrated, area-sensitive resilience planning. Findings offer a framework for urban planners to prioritize targeted interventions, balancing physical upgrades with social empowerment, economic capacity building, and institutional strengthening for sustainable and inclusive resilience. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Developing and validating a scenario-based evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services
abstract: As population aging and digital transformation advance, IPTV has become an important media platform for older adults. However, mismatches between interface design and older users’ capabilities continue to limit effective use. This study develops and validates a contextualized evaluation framework for age-friendly IPTV services. Policy review, interviews with older users, and regional case analysis were conducted to identify eight typical IPTV usage scenarios and construct an initial indicator pool. A two-round Delphi consultation refined the framework, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) determined indicator weights. The final framework comprises five primary dimensions and 22 secondary indicators. Evaluation of three provincial IPTV projects showed that security management, functional operation, and service quality are the highest priorities for improving user experience, whereas content format and product characteristics support initial adoption. Interviews further revealed that limited stakeholder coordination and delays between user feedback and system updates constrain age-friendly implementation. The proposed framework quantifies the alignment between older users’ capabilities and large-screen interaction while tracing usability problems to specific usage contexts. It also informs optimization through hierarchical support, progressive capability support, and social support mechanisms. The scenario-based indicators can be adapted to local technical infrastructures, service processes, and user behaviors, supporting localized application across diverse large-screen media ecosystems. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Solar Photovoltaic Adoption in East Java Non-Profit Organizations
abstract: Non-profit organizations in East Java need dependable electricity for service continuity, daily operations, and cost control, yet face capital, regulatory, behavioral, and tropical-climate barriers to rooftop solar photovoltaic adoption. This study combines a focused literature review, bibliometric mapping of 25 verified domain studies selected from 79 unique Scopus records, a random-effects synthesis of five Global Solar Atlas locations, and a 50,000-iteration Monte Carlo model for a common 12 kWp system. The 25 studies met predefined adoption, finance/policy, governance/behavior, and tropical-performance criteria and passed metadata verification. Modeled annual output ranges from 17.231 to 18.227 MWh; pooled yield is 4.03 kWh/kWp/day (95% CI: 3.92–4.14). Median NPV is IDR 40.7–54.9 million, with a conditional positive-NPV probability of 86.4–92.5%. Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate, tariff escalation, capital cost, avoided electricity value, and self-consumption as the dominant drivers of NPV. The five-city results are screening evidence, not a representation of all tropical climates or roofs. A 30% grant or blended-finance contribution raises positive-NPV probability above 99.8% and reduces median payback to 5.8–6.2 years. © 2027, Semarak Ilmu Publishing. .

title: Inclusive education as organizational inclusion: Creating inclusive business schools through co-curricular learning
abstract: Knowing how to create inclusive business schools is crucial for the development of leaders navigating the workforce. This research examines co-curricular First-Year Experience (FYE) programming as an approach to supporting student integration, learning, and experiences. Using a quasi-experimental design, two studies examined academic performance and perceived transition success, belonging, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and time management behaviours across in-person and online learning contexts. In Study 1, in-person students demonstrated higher academic performance and perceived transition success than online students. At the end of the semester, online and in-person students were comparable in outcome expectations, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management. General belonging was lower among online students across the two measurement occasions however, this difference was already present at baseline and did not change significantly over time. General belonging, university belonging, self-efficacy, and time management were positively associated with perceived transition success, whereas outcome expectations were not a significant unique correlate. Study 2 identified exploratory within-format patterns across co-curricular in-person, bespoke in-person, and bespoke online course formats, with university belonging emerging as a significant correlate of perceived transition success across all three. Together, these findings position co-curricular and bespoke FYE approaches as promising frameworks for supporting inclusive business education while highlighting the central role of belonging in students’ transition experiences. © 2026 The Authors

title: Navigating the successful digital transformation of correctional services: Challenges, good governance, and a hybrid framework
abstract: Digital transformation initiatives are essential for advancing correctional services toward digital maturity in Macao. However, the absence of a well-defined overarching strategy presents a significant impediment to the effective implementation of reforms. Due to the fact that the intelligent construction of the penal system has not yet been integrated with the extant eGovernment, the governance of the correctional system and its capabilities necessitate rigorous enhancement. Good governance encompasses legitimacy, accountability, transparency, capacity, fairness, responsiveness, participation, and consensus, which are widely considered core principles of public administration and are well-suited to linking the vision of digital transformation and smart correction initiatives. Based on the practice of eGovernment in Macao, which aspects can facilitate the digital transformation of correctional services to enhance the modernization of governance systems and capabilities, and achieve good governance? This study employs qualitative research methods, including a comprehensive literature review, secondary data collection, and analysis of legal documents, regulations, and sentencing policies within the Macao penal system. A SWOT-Plus analysis is conducted to assess potential internal and external trends and identify extant challenges. A hybrid framework is proposed that incorporates the incentives for eGovernment and the fundamental principles of good governance, including key governance beliefs and values such as organization, process, regulation, and culture. The findings also outline a series of expected impacts on correctional services that navigate the transformation ideology and foster successful implementation, thereby coordinating the vision of smart government. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Deterministic branch-and-bound global MPPT using surrogate-derived power bounds for partially shaded PV arrays
abstract: Partial shading fragments the power–voltage characteristic of series-connected photovoltaic (PV) arrays into multiple local peaks, rendering conventional trackers ineffective and exposing the reliance of metaheuristic global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) methods on random initialization and empirical tuning coefficients. This paper proposes TSB-GMPPT, a deterministic tanh-surrogate branch-and-bound GMPPT algorithm that eliminates both dependencies. A control-oriented hyperbolic-tangent surrogate of the PV I–V characteristic admits a non-iterative Lambert W asymptotic approximation for the maximum power point voltage. During discovery, a single saturation-region measurement per candidate is sufficient to construct a calibrated optimistic bound, safely pruning the search space before final peak localization. An offline polynomial calibration recovers the remaining parameters from short-circuit current. During discovery, an optimistic branch-and-bound rule maintains an upper power bound for each unconfirmed layer and permanently discards candidates that cannot exceed the incumbent confirmed power, contracting the admissible search space without exhaustive probing. A five-state finite-state machine governs initialization, shading-topology detection, discovery, winner refitting, convergence, and adaptive reinitialization. Experimental validation using a Chroma 62150H solar array simulator and a dSPACE DS1104 platform on five-module benchmark cases and additional eight-module complex multi-peak shading cases demonstrates average tracking efficiencies of 99.94% under partial shading and 99.98% under uniform irradiance, with corresponding average convergence times of 0.25 s and 0.21 s, respectively, for the five-module test set. title: Fabrication of bioactive hydrogels stabilized by gluten amyloid fibrils and ε-polylysine: Effects of fibril morphology and blending ratios
abstract: The introduction of ε-Polylysine (PL) provides additional functional activities for hydrogels. However, it simultaneously impairs their mechanical properties to a certain extent. To address this trade-off, we hypothesized that gluten protein amyloid fibrils (GAFs) with distinct topological morphologies—long rigid fibrils (LRF), long flexible fibrils (LFF), and fibril networks (FN) differentially modulate PL hydrogels through site-specific molecular bridging and spatial cross-linking. Driven by strong electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding, GAFs and PL underwent ratio dependent systemic reorganization and assembly. The physicochemical properties of GAFs/PL hydrogels were primarily governed by the combined regulation of GAFs morphology and blending ratios. Specifically, at the same GAFs/PL ratio, FN exhibited superior spatial connectivity, contributing to enhanced water immobilization within the hydrogel network. Meanwhile, LRF and FN were more effective in constructing continuous force transmission pathways, thereby improving hardness and dynamic viscoelasticity. These findings demonstrate that the functional performance of GAFs/PL hydrogels can be tailored by selecting appropriate fibril morphologies and blending ratios according to specific application requirements. However, the network formed by LFF was more susceptible to deformation, resulting in a relatively limited mechanical reinforcement effect on the hydrogel skeleton. Ultimately, this study aims to clarify the assembly pathway driven by the cooperative contribution of GAFs and PL. This study provides a theoretical foundation and design strategies for developing food-grade composite materials with tunable mechanical properties and bioactive functionalities. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Amplified strain partitioning driven by multiple heterostructures enables superior strength-ductility in Ti-reinforced Mg composites
abstract: The strength-ductility trade-off remains a long-standing challenge for magnesium matrix composites (MMCs). Herein, we develop a novel strategy to fabricate multi-heterostructured MMCs with simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement, using a Ti/Mg-6Zn-1.5Mn composite prepared via ultrasonic-assisted semi-solid stirring, homogenization heat treatment, and hot extrusion. The constructed multi-level heterostructures consist of three key features: (i) non-uniform coarse/fine grain (CG/FG) mixed structure, (ii) nanophases with density differences between FGs and CGs, and (iii) Ti particles preferentially distributed adjacent to the nanophases. The composite exhibits exceptional comprehensive mechanical properties, with an ultimate tensile strength of 366 MPa, yield strength of 239 MPa, elongation of 20.6%, and a superior strength-ductility product of 66.29 MJ/m3. The excellent performance originates from multi-heterostructure-driven amplified strain partitioning, which induces hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening and hardening via geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation. Meanwhile, activated non-basal slip systems enable efficient intergranular slip transfer for uniform plastic deformation, and CGs effectively delay plastic instability and suppress crack propagation. This work provides new insights into the deformation mechanisms of heterostructured MMCs and offers a feasible pathway for developing advanced lightweight structural materials. © 2026

title: Learn AI with AI: Designing conversational agents to support older adults in learning about AI
abstract: Older adults are motivated to develop AI literacy and consider it important. Prior research suggests that conversational agents can support older adults’ AI literacy learning by simplifying AI concepts and providing interactive learning experiences. However, little is known about how such agents should be designed to address the learning challenges older adults face. To address this, we interviewed nine older adults to explore their challenges and identify design opportunities. Findings revealed affective barriers related to confidence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of peer-like characteristics in agents, such as reciprocal knowledge sharing. Guided by these insights, we designed a peer-like agent and compared it with a website and an assistant agent in a between-subjects study with 45 older adults learning about deepfakes. Results showed that the peer agent fostered higher engagement and supported confidence more than the others. We conclude with design recommendations for conversational agents to support older adults’ AI learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Analysis of environmental and social impacts of quarry mining for bridging stakeholder perception gaps–a case study from Padukka, Sri Lanka
abstract: This study investigates stakeholder perceptions of the environmental and social impacts associated with the China Harbour Aggregate Quarry in the Padukka Division of the Colombo District, Sri Lanka. Despite growing concerns about the impacts of quarrying on host communities, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how different stakeholder groups perceive and experience these impacts in the Sri Lankan context. A mixed-methods case study design integrated qualitative and quantitative approaches to examine stakeholder perspectives. The study involved 31 community members near the quarry, 3 quarry site professionals, and 4 officers from a technical services company, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews with all stakeholder groups and structured questionnaires comprising open- and closed-ended questions administered to community members. Thematic analysis was used to analyze interview and open-ended questionnaire data, while descriptive analysis was applied to closed-ended questionnaire responses. Findings indicate that vibration was the dominant impact, reported by all community participants (100%), with concerns about noise, water dry out, dust, and occasional flyrock events. Community responses revealed high perceived annoyance (93.5%) and opposition to the mining site (87.1%), although all respondents were unwilling to relocate, highlighting sociopsychological constraints. Comparative analysis revealed convergence and divergence between community perceptions and quarry personnel perspectives, with mitigation measures implemented but challenges persisting due to spatial constraints, communication gaps, and disputed compensation claims. The study contributes context-specific evidence on stakeholder perceptions of quarrying impacts and provides practical insights for strengthening community engagement, impact mitigation, and socially responsible quarry management in Sri Lanka. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From sustainability awareness to practical agency: Translating institutional activity into meaningful student learning
abstract: The Principles for Responsible Management Education initiative calls upon business schools to embed sustainability and responsible management within their curricula. Although higher education institutions have made progress, student perspectives remain underrepresented in Education for Sustainable Development research. Drawing on an integrated theoretical framework comprising Transformative Learning Theory, the sustainability competency framework, social learning and students-as-partners pedagogy, this exploratory study reports a mixed-methods survey of 130 Business and Management students across two UK higher education institutions. The findings indicate generally favourable sustainability attitudes among the participating students, consistent with previous responsible management education research. Exploratory comparisons found broadly similar patterns across two contrasting UK cohorts: full-time undergraduate students and employed degree apprentices. The more distinctive finding concerns an institutional-to-educational translation gap. Students acknowledged aspects of current provision but indicated that institutional sustainability activity did not always become visible, participatory or educationally meaningful within their programmes. Across both cohorts, students called for stronger collaboration, practice-oriented education and solutions-focused learning through which sustainability knowledge could be connected with authentic organisational and societal challenges. These findings underpin a student-informed conceptual framework, Towards Transdisciplinary and Transformative Sustainability Education, which identifies conditions through which institutional sustainability activity may become visible, participatory and educationally meaningful to students. The study does not directly assess institutional transformation, transformative learning or behavioural change, nor does it test whether favourable attitudes persist when sustainability entails difficult financial, professional or lifestyle trade-offs. The Framework should therefore be understood as a conceptual proposition for supporting meaningful engagement rather than as evidence that transformative or behavioural outcomes have occurred. © 2026 The Authors

title: Energy trading and demand response strategies for energy flexible manufacturing systems under temporary electricity shortages: A noise-robust multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
abstract: This paper investigates the energy management of energy flexible manufacturing systems (EFMS) under temporary electricity shortages (TES). TES disrupt the real-time balance of energy supply and demand. Meanwhile, multi-source measurement noise can degrade dynamic state estimation and affect scheduling decisions. To address these challenges, a hybrid approach integrating a generalized loss cubature Kalman filter (GLCKF) and a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is proposed. First, a dynamic pricing model based on the real-time demand-supply ratio, retail price, and feed-in tariff is designed to keep local trading prices within the grid price bounds. Second, GLCKF is used to suppress the effects of non-Gaussian measurement noise and random outliers. The resulting state estimates are used by MADDPG to jointly optimize real-time energy trading and demand response (DR) strategies. The framework is evaluated using a simulated four-EFMS cluster over a one-day scheduling horizon. The case incorporates industrial load profiles, photovoltaic generation, energy storage parameters, and time-of-use electricity prices. Comparative results show a 53.76% reduction in state-estimation root mean square error relative to CKF-MADDPG under the selected mixed-Gaussian noise setting. The results indicate that the framework improves economic performance and supports supply-demand balance in the tested TES scenarios. © 2026

title: Optimizing equity and efficiency in the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem
abstract: This study addresses the aerial firefighting resource allocation problem, formulated as the strategic prepositioning of a heterogeneous aerial firefighting fleet across capacity-constrained airbases. A novel bi-objective model is proposed that simultaneously optimizes efficiency (aggregate risk-weighted accessibility) and equity (minimized regional service disparities). The model employs an enhanced spatial accessibility method with a distance-decay function to evaluate coverage effectiveness and distribution fairness. A multi-objective genetic algorithm is implemented to generate Pareto-approximate solutions, revealing quantifiable trade-offs. Applied to a national-scale case study in Greece using 25 years of wildfire data, results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides significantly wider coverage than current practices, thereby extending protection to underserved regions while reducing redundant overlap. Sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across various real-world conditions, such as different budget levels and aircraft availability. This transferable tool enables policymakers to make data-driven decisions by quantifying the balance between response effectiveness and social fairness in wildfire-prone regions. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Sour grapes or strategic choice? Socially disadvantaged tourism entrepreneurs' pursuit of ‘break out’
abstract: While structural conditions impacting immigrant entrepreneurs' ‘break out’ are well-documented in tourism research, the underlying psychological processes remain underexplored. Informed by self-determination theory and adaptive preferences, this ethnographic study conducted between December 2024 and May 2025 explores how socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs negotiate structural constraints and individual agency while pursuing ‘break out’. Drawing on 345 h of ethnographic observation, digital data from two focal Nepali tourism entrepreneurs in Hong Kong SAR, and longitudinal object-oriented interviews with nineteen stakeholders, it reveals a psychological mechanism where frustration of basic psychological needs triggers adaptive preferences, hindering ‘break out’ efforts. It also shows how tourism's experiential nature enables entrepreneurs to counter stigma and negotiate autonomy. Practically, the findings highlight the need for psychologically informed support that goes beyond traditional skill-based training. While focused on Hong Kong's Nepali diaspora, the study offers broader insights into entrepreneurial ‘break out’ among socially disadvantaged immigrant tourism entrepreneurs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A game-theoretic approach for the retailer-third party multiple market-site capture competition in an end-of-life product collection system
abstract: This paper introduces a bi-level game-theoretic model for competition between two players collecting End-Of-Life (EOL) products within a circular economy framework. The model focuses on strategic market targeting in a geographically segmented market dominated by an established retailer. A new entrant (third party) acts as the leader, selecting a subset of nodes to capture. The incumbent retailer responds as the follower, recapturing lost nodes under its own budget. Due to NP-hardness, a Benders cut-based solution approach is developed. The model is extended to a partial interdiction formulation with continuous capture decisions, allowing gradual market entry. A genetic algorithm has also been developed for large-scale instances. A case study on EOL mobile phone collection in Tehran illustrates the practical application. Entry points and defensive and offensive strategies are derived under various budget scenarios. Results show that entry is not always advantageous. As the retailer’s budget increases, the third party faces higher financial barriers to entry, requiring a disproportionately larger budget to remain competitive. In the partial interdiction setting, the model captures nodes fully when the budget permits, reserving fractional capture only when resources are insufficient. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Tackling cold-start emissions: an integrated strategy of active thermal management and oxygenated fuel formulation
abstract: This study investigates the integration of bio-oxygenated fuel formulation with an electrically heated catalytic system to mitigate low-temperature cold-start emissions in compression-ignition engines. Four 20 % v/v oxygenated blends, comprising linear alcohols (butanol, pentanol) and cyclic compounds (cyclopentanol, cyclopentanone), were evaluated in a single-cylinder research engine coupled to a diesel oxidation catalyst. Linear alcohol blending reduced the CO light-off threshold (T50,CO) by 26 °C (butanol) and 16 °C (pentanol) relative to neat diesel by suppressing heavy hydrocarbon precursors and limiting active-site blocking on platinum group metals, whereas engine-out measurements showed that cyclic fuels yielded an initial particulate number reduction exceeding 85 % (reaching up to 90 % for cyclopentanone) compared to neat diesel. Active thermal management at DOC inlet temperatures of 355 °C to 415 °C achieved approximately 99 % CO conversion and 72 % total hydrocarbon reduction and increased the downstream NO2/NOx ratio up to 0.34. Catalytic post-treatment further reduced total particle number concentration by 41.1 % to 57.2 % with a simultaneous increase in count median diameter. These results, constrained by the single-cylinder steady-state operating conditions and specific engine loads evaluated, indicate that coupling tailored fuel formulations with active electrical heating offers an integrated methodological framework with the potential to resolve cold-start emissions limitations in low-exhaust-temperature applications. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: An integrated framework of emergy analysis and LMDI for assessing sustainability: a case study of tobacco production system
abstract: To tackle the challenges of resource consumption and environmental pressure in agricultural production systems, quantifying sustainability performance and identifying its driving mechanisms are critical. This study introduces an integrated framework based on emergy analysis and the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI), covering production investigation, system analysis, sustainability evaluation, and driver exploration, and ultimately guiding targeted production recommendations. The results reveal that tobacco energy output rose from 3.5 × 10^16 J in 2004 to 5.1 × 10^16 J in 2013, before declining to 3.3 × 10^16 J in 2021. Total emergy input exhibited a similar pattern, peaking at 2.2 × 10^22 sej in 2013. From 2004 to 2021, the environmental sustainability index increased from 0.46 to 0.54, while the environmental loading ratio decreased from 3.36 to 3.00, indicating a steady improvement in sustainability. Significant spatial variability was observed across provinces. LMDI decomposition revealed that economic efficiency contributed significantly to the sustainability improvement (0.53), while changes in renewable resource dependency offset -0.52 of this gain. Based on this framework, targeted strategies are proposed to optimize curing energy utilization, refine fertilizer management, and enhance economic efficiency. These findings offer practical support for promoting the sustainable transformation of the tobacco production system. © The Author(s) 2027. Published by Higher Education Press. title: Artificial intelligence disclosure and the value relevance of earnings
abstract: This study investigates the effect of AI disclosure on the value relevance of earnings using Chinese listed companies from 2013 to 2022. We find that AI disclosure significantly enhances earnings’ value relevance. Mechanism tests show that AI disclosure increases firms’ earnings quality and boosts investor attention, thus elevating the value relevance of earnings. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that this effect is more pronounced in firms in advanced manufacturing industries, firms in highly competitive industries and non-SOEs. Overall, this study highlights the important role of AI disclosure in the price discovery of both fundamental and unexpected earnings, and contributes to a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms through which AI affects the value relevance of earnings. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Mixed methods research: Critical review and guidelines for stronger design, integration, and contribution
abstract: Mixed methods research has a prominent place in tourism and hospitality scholarship, yet adoption has advanced faster than methodological selectivity, which leaves many studies combining qualitative and quantitative strands without explaining why both strands were necessary, how the strands were related, or what integrated inference their combination alone made possible. Drawing on a critical review of 222 mixed methods studies published in leading tourism and hospitality journals, this article identifies dominant patterns, strengths and weaknesses, and underused possibilities. In response, the article offers a stage-based guide that links problem formulation, purpose selection, design fit, sampling bridges, strand roles, integration, divergence handling, reporting architecture, and contribution development. In doing so, the article advances a more demanding standard for mixed methods scholarship and argues that the next phase of tourism and hospitality research should shift from routine method combination toward integrated inferences that are conceptually sharper, methodologically clearer, and practically more useful. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Fostering creativity through interdisciplinary teaching: A meta-analysis of effectiveness
abstract: Interdisciplinary teaching is widely promoted to cultivate students’ creativity, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis synthesized 55 quantitative studies (70 effect sizes, 7490 students) from 2013 to 2024, applying random-effects models using Hedges’ g. Creativity outcomes were decomposed into three theoretically grounded dimensions: creative thinking process, creative practice ability, and creative personality and psychology. Results indicated a large overall positive effect ( g + = 1.090, 95% CI [0.913, 1.266]), with very high heterogeneity ( I 2 = 96.017%). Dimensional analysis revealed significant variations: the strongest effects on creative practice ability ( g + = 2.164), followed by creative thinking process ( g + = 1.253), while effects on creative personality and psychology were smaller ( g + = 0.478). Moderator analyses revealed that educational stage, dominant subject, pedagogical approach, intervention duration, and group activities significantly influenced outcomes, while class size and instructional setting did not. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Balancing economic and environmental goals in green supply chains through a multi-objective optimization on financing and coordination contract
abstract: This study aims to develop a green supply chain management (GSCM) framework that integrates buyer-backed purchase order financing (BPOF), advance payment discounts (APD), and coordination agreements to enhance sustainability and financial stability. This research work applies Stackelberg game theory and multi-objective optimization to investigate how BPOF and APD can be used to promote both economic stability and environmental performance. The combination of these financing options with revenue-sharing and cost-sharing agreements provides a comprehensive view that is frequently lacking in green supply chain models. The main innovation is that financial mechanisms and multi-objective goals are considered simultaneously within a coordinated framework. The effect of coordinating contracts and funding mechanisms on the overall performance of the supply chain is evaluated using numerical analysis. The results indicate that BPOF improves financial flexibility for manufacturers, promoting higher green investment levels. Among financing strategies, advance payment discount (APD) appears as the most effective, delivering around 10–20% larger profits than other mechanisms, while buyer-backed purchase order financing (BPOF) is a viable option under liquidity restrictions. The findings have significant management and industrial consequences. Manufacturers should prioritize low-cost financing solutions, such as APD, to support green developments, especially in areas with high environmental awareness. The model is especially applicable in industries like electric automobiles, battery recycling, and sustainable manufacturing, where companies must strike a balance between economic performance and environmental responsibility. This paper presents a practical decision-making framework for increasing profitability and sustainability in modern supply chains. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: The impact of entrepreneurship education on sustainable entrepreneurial intentions: A quasi-experimental study
abstract: In this paper, we examine how a semester-long sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship course shapes sustainable entrepreneurial intention (SEI) through individual sustainability orientation (ISO). Grounded in an adaptation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, ISO is conceptualized as a multidimensional construct encompassing sustainability-oriented (SO) values, SO motivation, awareness of sustainability issues, and SO self-efficacy, dimensions expected to mediate educational effects on SEI with different temporal sensitivities. We implemented a quasi-experimental design across two graduate introductory entrepreneurship courses at two Canadian universities: one redesigned around sustainability mechanisms (treatment, N = 112) and one covering standard content (comparison, N = 47). Pre- and post-test surveys were conducted. Results show no direct effect of the treatment on SEI and no change in SO values, which were high at baseline. However, the treatment significantly increased students’ sustainability awareness, self-efficacy, and, unexpectedly, motivation. Among these, changes in awareness and self-efficacy were positively associated with changes in SEI. These findings indicate that semester-long interventions can reliably influence proximal cognitions (awareness and self-efficacy), while deeper dispositions such as values, and to a lesser extent motivation, likely require longer-term or more immersive exposure. Theoretically, this study conceptualizes ISO as a temporally layered construct that helps explain why prior findings on education–SEI links are mixed. Methodologically, it demonstrates the value of coupling quasi-experimental designs with pedagogical reporting. Practically, it highlights workable mechanisms, such as sustainability-anchored projects, sustainable business modeling, and impact-oriented pitches, that strengthen awareness and SO self-efficacy. These insights encourage moving beyond outcome-level evaluations toward understanding how entrepreneurship education can foster SEI. © 2026 The Authors

title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention networks for multi-regional load forecasting in modern power systems with missing data
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy and multi-regional power system operation creates new challenges for short-term load forecasting (STLF), particularly under missing data, dynamic spatial dependencies, and uncertainty. Existing approaches often separate data imputation from forecasting, rely on static spatial structures, and provide deterministic predictions, limiting their applicability in risk-aware power system operation. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Graph Attention Network (UA-DGAT) for multi-regional load forecasting under incomplete and uncertain data conditions. The proposed framework integrates probabilistic masked self-attention imputation, uncertainty-aware dynamic graph attention, and multi-scale temporal modeling based on discrete wavelet transform within an end-to-end architecture. Unlike conventional pipelines, UA-DGAT explicitly propagates imputation uncertainty, spatial dependency uncertainty, and predictive uncertainty throughout the forecasting process. Extensive experiments on NYISO and ISO-NE datasets demonstrate that UA-DGAT achieves superior performance in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting metrics, reducing MAE and RMSE while attaining approximately 87% prediction interval coverage. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each component and confirm the significant role of uncertainty-aware conditioning. Furthermore, the proposed framework maintains robust forecasting performance under missing data rates up to 50%, with particularly improved resilience under block missing patterns. The results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware modeling of data reconstruction and spatial dependency learning enables more accurate, reliable, and risk-aware load forecasting for modern power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
