title: Exploring the linkage between entrepreneurial education and entrepreneurial intentions among university students in Morocco
abstract: The Moroccan labor market continues to struggle with the incorporation of its university graduates and the interest in entrepreneurship as an employment option is growing. Higher education institutions are an essential part of developing students' entrepreneurial competencies and intentions. This research investigates the effects of entrepreneurship education on students' entrepreneurial intention as based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The research also investigates how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, creativity, proactive behavior, and family background influence entrepreneurial intention. A self-administered questionnaire was used to collect data from 226 students at the Faculty of Economics and Management at Beni Mellal, Morocco, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that entrepreneurship education is positively related to entrepreneurial intention both directly as well as indirectly through attitudes toward entrepreneurship and perceived behavioral control; also, creativity and family background were found to positively influence entrepreneurial intention. In contrast, subjective norms and proactive behavior do not show a significant effect in this context. These findings highlight the importance of entrepreneurial education in strengthening students' entrepreneurial orientation while suggesting that social influences and individual proactivity may operate differently within the Moroccan context. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence from a developing country context and offers implications for policymakers and educators seeking to enhance entrepreneurship education programs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Will this time be different? Just transition pathways in eastern and Southern Africa’s critical minerals sector
abstract: The global energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for critical minerals required for renewable energy technologies like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems. However, the future translation of mineral reserves into equitable socio-economic development in the region depends on policy frameworks and governance systems that promote inclusive participation, recognition, and benefit-sharing. This paper examines pathways for inclusive economic transformation, analyzing the conditions required to ensure mining-affected communities benefit equitably from the critical minerals boom. We employ a justice-centered framework of distributional, procedural, recognition and restorative justice to analyze five countries (Democratic Republic of Congo, South Africa, Zambia, Malawi, and Burundi) through stakeholder interviews with 43 actors and document and policy analysis, including Malawi and Burundi, whose emerging sectors are largely absent from the peer-reviewed record. Across the five cases the four dimensions are not encountered as separate problems. Findings suggest that employment opportunities do not always reach local populations, revenue mechanisms face transparency challenges, consultation processes have limited influence over outcomes, customary tenure is inconsistently recognized, and environmental legacies often persist without adequate remediation. Ensuring that the substantial economic opportunities created by critical mineral demand are realized inclusively will require simultaneous interventions across all four justice dimensions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A coupled oxidation-damage model for cross-layer ablation failure in HfC/SiC bilayer coatings on C/C composites
abstract: HfC/SiC bilayer coatings provide exceptional ultra-high-temperature ablation protection for Carbon/Carbon composites. However, the complex cross-layer chemo-mechanical interactions, specifically between the oxidation-induced cracking of the HfC outer layer and the active oxidation of the SiC inner layer, remain poorly understood. In this work, a comprehensive oxidation-damage coupling ablation model is proposed based on continuum damage mechanics and chemical reaction kinetics. Oxyacetylene ablation experiments were conducted to characterize the ablation depths and layer-specific damage evolution. To handle the severe material discontinuity at the bilayer interface, an interfacial node-decoupling method is implemented, ensuring multiphysics continuity while preserving the independent chemical kinetics. The proposed model is successfully validated against experimental results with an average relative error of 15.7%. The numerical results clarify a mutually exacerbating failure mechanism: Stress-driven HfC cracking creates preferential oxygen pathways that accelerate localized SiC depletion, while the resulting material loss undermines the mechanical support of the overlying HfC layer. Furthermore, parametric analysis uncovers a non-monotonic evolution of the anti-ablation performance when varying the SiC layer thickness (10–30 μm). A thicker SiC layer imposes a more severe mechanical constraint that prematurely drives outer-layer microcracking, whereas it provides a superior secondary oxygen barrier during extended ablation. This chemo-mechanical trade-off offers crucial guidelines for the structural optimization of advanced multilayer anti-ablation coatings. © 2026

title: Not that simple: How can generative artificial intelligence be used to develop college students’ entrepreneurial ability?
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become increasingly relevant to entrepreneurship education, yet its association with college students' entrepreneurial ability remains contested. To address this gap, we conceptualize GenAI as encompassing both routine and innovative uses, providing a more comprehensive understanding of its role in entrepreneurial ability. Based on questionnaire data, our empirical findings show that both routine and innovative use of GenAI are positively associated with entrepreneurial ability. Moreover, we find that potential and realized absorptive capacity mediate this relationship, while interaction analyses indicate that these associations are stronger at higher levels of design thinking. These findings contribute to the entrepreneurship education literature by revealing the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which GenAI use enhances college students’ entrepreneurial ability. The study also provides insights into how college students can use GenAI more effectively in complex business contexts to strengthen their entrepreneurial ability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Determining the robust drivers of CO2 emissions in Africa: Machine learning and panel econometric evidence on the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis
abstract: One of the primary greenhouse gases linked to global warming is carbon dioxide. This study investigates the determinants of carbon dioxide emissions in 29 African countries over the period 1990–2023 using a two-stage machine learning and econometric framework. In the first stage, Classification and Regression Trees, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms are employed to identify the most important drivers of carbon dioxide emissions. The results indicate that Random Forests provide the highest predictive performance among the machine learning models. In the second stage, the variables identified by the machine learning analysis are incorporated into second-generation panel estimators that account for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity. Specifically, long-run and short-run relationships are examined using the Common Correlated Effects Autoregressive Distributed Lag estimator, while Augmented Mean Group, Common Correlated Effects Mean Group estimators, and Fixed Effects with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors are employed as robustness checks. The findings reveal that oil consumption is positively associated with carbon dioxide emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption is negatively associated with carbon dioxide emissions. The results provide limited but supportive evidence for the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis, with income and income-squared terms exhibiting the expected signs and the estimated turning point falling within the observed income range. Robustness analyses based on oil-exporting and non-oil-exporting country groups, as well as an alternative carbon-intensity measure, confirm the central role of fossil fuel dependence and renewable energy adoption in shaping environmental outcomes across Africa. These findings highlight the importance of accelerating renewable energy deployment, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable development strategies to achieve long-term environmental sustainability in African economies. © 2026 The Authors. title: Driving sustainable development goal alignment through green consumption marketing and public mind
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sustainable development demands synchronized efforts across socioeconomic and environmental domains, specifically targeting poverty alleviation, food security, and environmental stewardship. Although sustainable consumption patterns and ecological marketing act as established catalysts for environmental transitions, the specific socio-civic pathways translating micro-level pro-environmental behaviors into macro-level policy alignment remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, the study objectives were to evaluate the direct and indirect pathways through which green consumption behavior and green marketing drive local alignment with the sustainable development goals through the mediating role of the public mind among residents in Nonthaburi Province, Thailand. METHODS: A quantitative survey design was executed to gather data from 400 residents across administrative districts in Nonthaburi Province using proportionate stratified random sampling. The researchers collected primary data through structured questionnaires employing a 5-point Likert scale. Analytical procedures encompassed descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to validate construct relationships and assess overall structural model fit. FINDINGS: The results of structural equation modeling indicate that both green consumption behavior and green marketing significantly influence the realization of local sustainable development goals, operating through both direct pathways and indirect pathways mediated by public consciousness. The public mind demonstrated the strongest direct influence on sustainable development goals realization (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), followed by direct impacts from green consumption behavior (β = 0.35, p < 0.01) and green marketing (β = 0.28, p < 0.01). Additionally, green consumption behavior was the primary driver of public mind activation (β = 0.37, p < 0.01), surpassing green marketing (β = 0.27, p < 0.01). The validated structural model accounted for substantial variance in sustainable development goals alignment (R^2 = 0.97) and the public mind (R^2 = 0.77). CONCLUSION: Green consumption behavior and green marketing are critical precursors to cultivating a collective public mind, which bridges individual eco-conscious actions with macro-level alignment of Sustainable Development Goals. Municipal authorities ought to embed the mobilization of public ecological awareness into environmental governance policies. Furthermore, this structural framework offers a scalable model adaptable to other rapidly urbanizing provinces in Southeast Asia. title: Meta-operation-assisted optimization for execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning
abstract: Existing robotic disassembly sequence planning (RDSP) studies mainly optimize operation ordering under precedence constraints, whereas robot configurations and local operation parameters are typically treated separately or represented by fixed or simplified operation costs. To bridge this gap, this paper formulates an execution-parameterized robotic disassembly sequence planning (EP-RDSP) problem that jointly considers disassembly sequencing, robot configuration selection, and disassembly operation parameter optimization. In contrast to task-level RDSP, EP-RDSP evaluates a plan through the coupled effects of its operation sequence, selected inverse kinematics (IK) configurations, joint-space transitions, and local operation parameters. EP-RDSP contains heterogeneous and tightly coupled decisions, making direct optimization of the full mixed decision space computationally challenging. To address this challenge, a meta-operation-assisted (MOA) optimization framework is proposed to support multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA)-based search. The framework exploits meta-operation knowledge for operation-parameter generation before online optimization, allowing MOEA to focus on globally coupled planning decisions such as operation ordering, IK candidate selection, and joint-configuration and speed-ratio decisions. Experiments on 15 generated problem instances show that, across the four underlying optimizers and three instance scales, the MOA variants reduce the mean online runtime required to reach the target hypervolume (HV) by 16.45%–83.01%. Under fixed online time budgets, the MOA framework improves the mean HV by 31.13%–80.04% relative to five comparison methods and achieves the lowest mean inverted generational distance (IGD) on 14 of the 15 instances. title: Dual-Objective Design of Broadband Rectenna and Anchor Node Optimization for Energy Harvesting and High-Accuracy UWB Localization
abstract: Wireless sensor networks and portable devices face two major challenges: sustainable energy supply and high-precision indoor localization. While far-field wireless power transfer (WPT) offers energy solutions, it suffers from low power density and environmental sensitivity. To mitigate these drawbacks, the proposed system incorporates polarization diversity and a wideband impedance matching strategy. Simultaneously, GPS fails in indoor environments, driving the need for ultra-wideband (UWB) localization to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. This paper presents a dual-objective framework to tackle both issues. First, it designs a broadband antenna array (1–20 GHz) with multi-polarization reception, combined with an optimized matching network and Schottky-based rectifier to enhance RF-to-DC conversion under low power. Second, it introduces an anchor placement optimization algorithm for UWB that uses probabilistic target behavior models to minimize positioning errors. Simulation results confirm that the energy harvester remains effective across various incident angles and frequencies, while the localization error is consistently reduced to around one centimeter. The integrated approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation WSNs, overcoming power management bottlenecks while elevating localization accuracy to approximately one centimeter. © 2027 The author(s). title: TikTok as a stage: How short video creators’ identity performance drives engagement with tourism experiences
abstract: Destinations are increasingly collaborating with short-form video creators to engage consumers. Through Goffman's dramaturgical lens, this study explores how creators' performed identities in travel videos relate to audience responses. Combining machine learning and AI-powered analyses of over 10k short-form videos and 176k viewer comments with a controlled experiment, we identified four identities that creators performed in these videos (the “showman,” “diarist,” “docent,” and “photographer”) and classified them at scale. Results showed that identity performance is associated with distinct configurations of audiences' behavioral engagement. The “docent” generated more audience engagement than other identities, including audiences' learning, endorsing, and intending to participate dimensions. Guided by the knowledge gap theory, a subsequent experiment showed that the “docent” identity increased engagement by sparking curiosity. These findings guide content creators in adopting effective identity performance strategies, destinations in partnering with well-aligned content creators, and platforms in using algorithmic curation to achieve desired marketing outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Recursive self-regulation in genAI-assisted experiential learning: A task-contingent model
abstract: Existing literature on generative AI (genAI) in business education has examined students’ attitudes, motivation, and the ethics of genAI use, alongside ongoing debate about whether genAI over-reliance may diminish self-regulated learning (SRL). However, how students self-regulate their learning while working with genAI during authentic tasks remains under-explored. This study addresses this gap by examining (RQ1) how students' self-regulatory strategies manifest during genAI-assisted learning and (RQ2) how these strategies change through genAI interaction. A thematic analysis was conducted of 34 metacognitive reflections generated across two scaffolded, four-stage experiential learning activities in a Lean Startup unit. Findings inform a three-stage AI-mediated recursive loop model, comprising monitoring, strategic adoption, and limitation identification, that extends cyclical models of self-regulated learning by showing how regulation may be initiated within the task by genAI-generated suggestions. Within this structured, reflective learning context, students indicated evaluative judgement and metacognitive regulation, providing preliminary evidence that scaffolded genAI activities can elicit active rather than passive engagement. GenAI-supported cognitive deepening was task-contingent, emerging most strongly during applied refinement tasks. The model offers management educators a pedagogical process model for designing scaffolded genAI-assisted activities that elicit monitoring, selective adoption, and critical reflection. © 2026 The Authors

title: Complex adaptive governance for sustainable tourism villages: Explanatory insights from combined polycentric and chaos theoretical perspectives
abstract: Sustainable tourism villages face complex governance challenges because they must simultaneously support economic development, protect local culture, preserve ecological resources, and respond to changing social conditions. Existing studies have examined sustainable tourism governance mainly from administrative, community-based, or institutional perspectives, but less attention has been given to how distributed authority interacts with nonlinear adaptive dynamics in village-level governance systems. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated framework that combines polycentric governance theory and chaos theory. Using a quantitative explanatory design, survey data were collected from 590 stakeholders involved in tourism village governance across four regencies and one city in Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that institutional diversity has the strongest association with sustainable tourism village governance, followed by decentralization and local autonomy, bifurcation and cosmology, community participation, flexibility and adaptability, edge of chaos and the butterfly effect, and self-organization and strange attractors. The model yields a very high coefficient of determination, which suggests a close within sample fit between the proposed constructs and the observed perception data. This result is interpreted cautiously because the study is cross-sectional and several constructs are conceptually proximate. The study contributes to governance theory by showing that sustainable tourism village governance can be understood as both polycentric and complex-adaptive. Practically, the findings suggest that policymakers and tourism village managers should strengthen multi-actor coordination while maintaining flexibility to respond to uncertainty and local change. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Retreat in monastery stay tourism: the role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ connectedness and behavioural intention
abstract: Monastery stay tourism is an emerging niche within spiritual and transformative tourism, offering immersive experiences that facilitate personal and emotional growth. Despite its rising popularity, limited research has explored how such experiences shape tourists' emotional bonds, identity formation, and revisit intention. Drawing on mindfulness theory, this study examines the role of mindfulness cultivated during Buddhist monastery retreats in influencing emotional solidarity, experience self-connection, place identity, and behavioural intention. Data were collected from 430 visitors and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM results underscore the critical role of mindfulness in shaping tourists’ social interactions, emotional attachment to the destination, and self-connection, all of which significantly impact their intention to engage in spiritual retreats. Emotional solidarity and self-connection are found to significantly influence place identity and future behavioural intention. The MGA findings indicate that generational and experiential segmentation reveals that Generation Z is more responsive to mindfulness and experience self-connection, while older cohorts are more influenced by emotional solidarity. Repeat visitors report stronger mindfulness effects across all outcomes, whereas first-time visitors rely more on emotional bonding. These insights underscore the value of tailoring mindful retreat experiences to foster deeper engagement and sustained support for religious tourism destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Employee cybersecurity awareness impact on cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada
abstract: This study investigates the impact of employee cybersecurity awareness on the cybersecurity posture of business organizations in Canada, as the prevalence of cyber threats, such as ransomware, phishing, and data breaches, continues to rise. The study adopts Servant Leadership (SL) theory as the analytical framework, with particular emphasis on SL’s attributes of employee empowerment, training, and organizational culture as factors in building resilience against cyber threats. A systematic literature review (SLR) methodology was employed, drawing on peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 from databases including Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science. The review process followed PRISMA guidelines, with rigorous application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the AMSTAR and CASP tools, resulting in 30 articles for the SLR. The findings reveal that organizations with strong servant leadership attributes, employee empowerment and training, combined with a cybersecurity-conscious culture, enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and training. The study further found that clear and consistently enforced policies are critical for guiding employee behaviour and fostering long-term adherence. The study recommends adopting targeted role-based and scenario-driven training approaches on cybersecurity for employees to improve their knowledge retention and threat response to cyberattacks for strengthening organizational cybersecurity posture in Canada. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Multi-objective optimization and decision-making for renewable energy production and enhancement of wind turbine selection in Morocco
abstract: Selecting an appropriate wind turbine for a specific location requires the simultaneous evaluation of energy output, cost, and site-specific deployment constraints. This research introduces a comprehensive framework that integrates simulation, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), and hybrid deep learning to enhance the selection of turbines for various sites. One year of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis version 5 (ERA5) reanalysis data and geographical information from satellite and elevation datasets was used to model the energy output of 40 commercial turbines in 15 Moroccan cities. A weighted scoring procedure was developed to evaluate turbines based on their capacity factor, annual energy production (AEP), capital and operating expenditures (CAPEX/OPEX), topographical constraints, and proximity to infrastructure. Two hybrid models, convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural network-Transformer (CNN–Transformer), were trained on structured inputs that included meteorological, topography, and spatial data to enhance decision assistance. The CNN–Transformer model outperformed the CNN–LSTM model in predictions and closely aligned with the expert rankings derived from simulations. Constraint-aware filtering and cost-performance trade-offs were employed to enhance the final turbine suggestions. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning for large-scale energy planning at specific locations. This framework supports future upgrades to renewable energy systems, including AI-based digital twins, real-time monitoring, and use across more locations. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Behavioral Economics as a Driver of Healthcare System Reform: Methodological Approach
abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to develop and apply the Behavioral Economics in Health index as a methodological tool for assessing the role of behavioral strategies in healthcare reform, with particular attention to their impact on healthcare expenditure, life expectancy, and system-level adaptation in countries with varying levels of institutional maturity and economic capacity. Methods The research used system-dynamics-based simulation modeling using behavioral and economic parameters, followed by statistical analysis of the results. Results The AnyLogic simulation results showed that, under an intensive behavioral integration scenario for 2024 to 2034, per-capita health expenditure decreased by USD 200 in Ukraine and USD 190 in Poland. In these countries, the initial levels of behavioral integration were the lowest—0.51 and 0.59, respectively—and the 10-year increase was 0.30. This fact ensured a steady reduction in expenditure throughout the entire modeling period without significant fluctuations. In Denmark, where the initial behavioral integration level was higher (0.88), the decrease amounted to only USD 26 per person, indicating a limited effect of further behavioral interventions in an already prevention-oriented healthcare system. Conversely, in the United States, where the integration index was even higher (0.91), expenditure increased by USD 20.72 per capita. Conclusions These findings indicate that the maximum economic effect of behavioral strategies is achieved in countries with low initial levels of integration and limited resources. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Broad-spectrum chromaticity and high color fastness of polyimide fibers via intrinsic coloration
abstract: Due to the exceptional thermal stability, radiation resistance, and mechanical properties, polyimide (PI) fibers are widely used in various extreme environments. However, the intrinsic monochromatic golden hue and chemically inert surface of PI fiber give rise to a natural barrier to dyeing and low color fastness. Herein, a facile and transformative intrinsic coloration strategy for the dyeing of PI fibers is proposed by directly incorporating a perylene-based chromophore monomer into the backbone of PI. By tuning the concentration and categories of perylene derivatives, various intrinsic colors of PI fibers are afforded, constructing a diverse chromatic PI fiber library with a broad color gamut (spanning from warm tones to slate-grey). Significantly, the strategy successfully overcomes the long-standing trade-off between dyeing and mechanical integrity. Moreover, the incorporation of perylene-based chromophores exhibits excellent structural compatibility with the PI backbone, acting as reinforced components rather than stress-concentrating defects. Consequently, the fibers exhibit simultaneous enhancements in mechanical properties and exceptional color fastness against harsh environments. This work establishes a cost-effective and scalable paradigm for the functionalization of PI fibers, contributing to the expanding application of PI fibers in high-end textiles and smart wearables. © 2026

title: Electrical performance assessment of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid power system for EV charging applications
abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure with renewable-based autonomous power systems presents a promising approach for distributed energy deployment. This study evaluates the electrical performance of an off-grid solar-wind hybrid system designed to supply EV charging and lighting loads in Urla, Izmir, Türkiye. Optimal system sizing is performed using HOMER, followed by detailed electrical modeling and time-domain simulations in ETAP under realistic operating conditions. The system comprises photovoltaic arrays, a wind turbine, battery energy storage with bidirectional converters, supplying EV charging and lighting loads. A deterministic time-scheduled load profile is adopted to ensure reproducibility. Scenario-based analyses across multiple operating conditions, including reduced solar irradiance, wind turbine outage, and load curtailment, are conducted over three representative days corresponding to winter, summer, and transitional conditions. Results demonstrate sustained power balance and full supply reliability, achieving 0% unmet load across all scenarios. Voltage levels remain within tight operational limits, confirming electrical stability, while battery state-of-charge profiles indicate adequate energy availability and effective storage utilization. The findings validate the operational feasibility and electrical robustness of the proposed system under variable generation and dynamic loading conditions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Curriculum greenwashing in business statistics education: Institutional decoupling in responsible management education
abstract: Business schools increasingly state commitments to responsible management education (RME), yet institutional commitment may not be consistently reflected in pedagogical change. This study examines curriculum greenwashing as a possible divergence between RME language in curriculum artifacts and corresponding evidence in teaching practice and student learning, without assuming deliberate intent. Drawing on institutional theory and decoupling, we test whether signatory status in the Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME) is associated with declarative, procedural, and consequential integration in undergraduate business statistics courses. Longitudinal multilevel data were collected from 215 students and 45 faculty members across 30 institutions across three waves. PRME status was positively associated with RME content in syllabi, whereas associations with reported teaching and student learning gains were not detected. Faculty-reported practices were positively associated with student learning gains. The PRME status × faculty quantitative teaching self-efficacy interaction was positive but did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory probing indicated a positive PRME association only at high self-efficacy. The study contributes a three-level audit framework for evaluating how institutional RME commitment is reflected across curriculum representation, reported teaching practice, and student learning, while underscoring the value of evidence beyond syllabus language alone. © 2026

title: Recurrent and eroding challenges in creative tourism: A longitudinal study of entrepreneurial resilience among urban handicraft artisans
abstract: Despite the growing importance of creative tourism in emerging economies, the temporal nature of the challenges facing artisans—and the resilience strategies they employ—remains poorly understood. Grounded in the processual entrepreneurial concept, this study explores how handicraft artisans understand the challenges they face and how they enact resilience in response. Adopting a longitudinal interpretivist approach, the study examines the entrepreneurial resilience of urban handicraft artisans in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, across a period of compounding crises, including the pandemic, political instability, and socioeconomic volatility. The study identifies a novel “recurrent–eroding” dichotomy as a framework for understanding challenge temporality and three resilience enablers, namely personal resources, social support networks, and operational responses. Theoretically, the study introduces new typologies of entrepreneurial challenges and extends resilience theory in creative tourism. Practically, it provides critical insights for policymakers, advocating for institutional shifts from crisis-response measures to strengthening accountable support mechanisms, market linkages, and protections for cultural work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Embodied cognition and the luxury hospitality experience of in-flight wine in premium cabins
abstract: This study explores how first- and business-class passengers experience in-flight wine as luxurious, even though flying reduces taste and smell. Drawing on embodied cognition theory, we argue that passengers do not simply judge wine by its quality. They build a sense of luxury by noticing how the airline tries to compensate for sensory limits, by feeling that the service fits their bodily experience, and by responding emotionally. We surveyed 500 premium-cabin passengers and used two analytical approaches: structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis. The results show two related paths to luxury: a cognitive path, in which the service feels consistent with the passenger's bodily state, and an affective path, in which the service creates positive emotions. For first-class passengers, both paths had to reach a minimum level for luxury to emerge. For business-class passengers, the cognitive path was more important, and positive emotions were less essential. These findings help airlines design in-flight wine service that still feels luxurious despite the sensory challenges of air travel. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Beyond participation: Creativity and entrepreneurial mindset across instructional modes and learner-level digital conditions in entrepreneurship education
abstract: Entrepreneurship education is often examined as a uniform educational exposure, although its associations with student development may depend on instructional mode and learner-level digital conditions. This study compares six entrepreneurship education formats and examines their associations with two self-perceived outcomes—creativity and entrepreneurial mindset—while assessing whether these relationships vary by perceived digital literacy and functional social media use. Drawing on survey data from 1181 graduating students at a multidisciplinary university in Guangdong, China, we use propensity score matching to improve comparability between participants and non-participants on observed characteristics and estimate interaction models to assess conditional relationships. The results indicate that entrepreneurship education is more consistently associated with entrepreneurial mindset than with creativity. Business plan competitions, training programs, and practical workshops generally show comparatively strong associations, particularly relative to entrepreneurship courses, although public lectures are also notably associated with entrepreneurial mindset. Perceived digital literacy displays a selective and format-dependent moderating relationship with creativity but does not consistently moderate the relationship with entrepreneurial mindset. Functional social media use shows no stable moderation in the primary binary models, while supplementary continuous-measure models reveal some operationalization-sensitive patterns. These findings indicate that entrepreneurship education is best understood as a heterogeneous set of learning experiences whose associations with student development vary across instructional modes, developmental outcomes, and learner-level digital conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Optimal telepresence experience in heritage tourism: A multidimensional scale and its impact on tourist behavior
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being integrated into on-site heritage tourism, yet little is known about how visitors evaluate hybrid experiences combining physical heritage environments with VR-mediated reconstructions. To address this gap, drawing on telepresence and flow theory, this study conceptualizes and validates Optimal Telepresence Experience (OTE) as a higher-order experiential construct reflecting visitors' overall technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Using a multi-stage scale development process with data collected at a heritage museum in Hue, Vietnam, the study develops and validates the OTE measurement instrument. The findings show that OTE, reflected through emotional, cognitive, and functional dimensions, strengthens visitors’ memory formation and revisit intention. Theoretically, the study advances immersive tourism research by conceptualizing and validating OTE as a higher-order experiential construct for hybrid technology-enhanced heritage experiences. Practically, the validated OTE scale provides a tool for designing and evaluating VR-enhanced heritage experiences that foster deeper visitor engagement and behavioral outcomes. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Designing sustainability communication across behavioral effort levels: How AI-generated micro-videos shape pro-environmental intentions
abstract: The sustainability communication literature treats communication formats as functionally substitutable, overlooking how effectiveness may depend on the effort required to perform targeted behaviors. Drawing on processing fluency theory, this research uses perceived behavioral effort and procedural demands as an organizing lens for examining message effectiveness. Focusing on AI-generated micro-videos, the study examines how different formats influence hotel guests’ perceptions and pro-environmental intentions. Across three experiments, Study 1 demonstrated that dynamic AI-generated videos outperformed static signage, although the effect could not be attributed solely to AI generation. In Study 2, instructional clips enhanced perceived message fluency and task–technology fit for lower-effort behaviors, but not pro-environmental intentions. In Study 3, instructional clips significantly enhanced all three outcomes for higher-effort, rule-based behaviors. The study enriches sustainability communication theory by highlighting the value of explicit instructional guidance and offers actionable recommendations for designing hospitality sustainability initiatives in unfamiliar tourism service settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread
abstract: The dissemination of epidemic-related information can effectively enhance public awareness of preventive measures and decrease infection risks. However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility. To address this gap, this study develops a three-layer metapopulation network coupled model that integrates online information dissemination, epidemic spreading, and offline information dissemination. The proposed model systematically investigates the patterns of information dissemination through both online and offline channels, as well as the epidemic reaction–diffusion process driven by individual migration. Furthermore, the social interactions dynamics of both information channels are influenced by migration, manifested as migrated individuals acquire offline information in destination patches and establish online connections with individuals residing there. Theoretical analysis using the Microscopic Markov Chain Approach (MMCA) derives epidemic thresholds, while Monte Carlo (MC) simulations validate the model and examine factors influencing propagation dynamics. Results indicate that migration enhances individuals’ offline information acquisition, and accelerates cross-patch online information dissemination. Both online and offline information interactions exert inhibitory effects on epidemic spread, effectively increasing the infection threshold and reducing the outbreak scale. Furthermore, increasing the connectivity and dissemination rate of online information, particularly the information dissemination via weak relationships between patches, can effectively inhibit epidemic outbreaks. Notably, when the suppression effect of information on the epidemic is weak, population migration facilitates epidemic spread. In contrast, when the suppression effect is strong, migration-driven information dissemination significantly reduces the probability of infection, thereby further suppressing the outbreak. title: Individual entrepreneurial orientation in Spanish university students: The role of critical thinking disposition and intellectual styles in entrepreneurship education
abstract: This study proposes a model that links students' disposition toward critical thinking (DTCT), Type I intellectual styles (oriented toward creativity, cognitive complexity, and autonomy) and Type II intellectual styles (oriented toward structure, conformity, and rule adherence), and individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) in higher education. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 208 students enrolled in entrepreneurship-related courses at a Spanish public university, and the data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that DTCT is a strong positive predictor of IEO; Type I intellectual styles are positively related to both DTCT and IEO, whereas Type II styles display negative relations with entrepreneurial orientation. DTCT improves the effect of Type I styles on IEO, but not with Type II styles. These findings suggest that strengthening DTCT is a central pathway through which entrepreneurship education can enhance students' IEO. The study argues that entrepreneurship courses should explicitly treat DTCT and IEO as learning outcomes and intentionally adapt tasks, scaffolding, and assessment to diverse intellectual style profiles in order to support more inclusive and opportunity-oriented entrepreneurial learning. © 2026 The Authors

title: Integrated system dynamics modeling for sustainable fisheries provisioning services
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fisheries provisioning services deliver food production, livelihoods and ecosystem functions, but are increasingly under pressure from environmental degradation, declining fishery resources and socio-economic stressors. Traditional paradigms in fisheries governance often exhibit a deficiency in accounting for the multidirectional feedback loops linking ecological systems with socio-economic dynamics. The objectives of this study were to develop an integrated system dynamics model to assess interactions between these dimensions and identify management options to improve fisheries provisioning services through long-term scenario simulations. METHODS: A system dynamics model was integrated, consisting of social, environmental, and economic sub-models using primary and secondary data from 2018-2023. The model includes population, fishermen, floating net cages, alternative employment, willingness to be a fisher, water quality and aquatic conditions, fish restocking, capture fisheries production, fisheries productivity, fish processing innovations, income, costs, and fisher's income. The model was verified and validated using the mean absolute error and average variation error metrics. Subsequently, predictive simulations were projected to 2045 under current, moderate, and optimistic scenarios. FINDINGS: Actual capture fisheries production declined by 88.9 percent, from 588,100 kilograms in 2018 to 65,035 kilograms in 2023 and was projected to decline to 31,179 kilograms by 2045 under current conditions. Under the moderate and optimistic scenarios, the number of floating net cages was modeled with an annual reduction rate of 30% and 35%, respectively. Production recovery commenced in 2027 under the moderate scenario and in 2026 under the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, target water quality conditions were achieved by 2041 and 2037, respectively, while fisher's net income reached positive values by 2034. CONCLUSION: The integrated system dynamics model underscores the potential for the sustainability of fishery production services through coordinated actions across social, environmental, and economic dimensions. The faster realization of target outcomes under the optimistic scenario highlights that proactive, coordinated interventions effectively expedite ecological restoration, fisheries output, and socioeconomic progress. This model offers a decision-support framework for assessing long-term fisheries management strategies. © 2027 The author(s). title: Teaching AI governance in management education: A serious game for accountable decision-making under uncertainty
abstract: Management education increasingly needs ways to prepare students for AI governance, yet students have limited opportunities to practise the organisational judgement involved in deployment decisions. This paper presents “Leading in the Age of AI”, a card-based serious game in which student teams assume asymmetric C-suite roles, make AI deployment decisions under constraints, and document their reasoning in Model Cards adapted from AI documentation practice. Conceptually, the paper frames AI governance education as accountable decision-making under uncertainty: students negotiate competing priorities, allocate scarce safeguards, respond to disruption, and prepare written accounts for scrutiny. The paper contributes a reusable game design, a pedagogical adaptation of Model Cards as justification artefacts, and design patterns for management-education contexts involving accountable decisions under uncertainty. An exploratory evaluation across two undergraduate cohorts used matched pre-test/post-test data (N=67), post-session evaluations, and descriptive artefact analysis of team-produced Model Cards (n=15). Students evaluated the activity positively and reported immediate confidence gains across knowledge, ethics, and governance composites (dz=0.44 to 1.00), while quiz gains were modest and not statistically significant. Model Card analysis suggests the activity generated inspectable governance reasoning, while leaving causal learning, retention, and transfer for future research. © 2026 The Author

title: Dance as destination infrastructure: Toward a progress agenda
abstract: Tourism destinations increasingly seek embodied, multisensory, and culturally meaningful experiences whose significance extends beyond immediate consumption. Yet tourism management still has a limited vocabulary for explaining how embodied cultural practices generate value across destination systems. This Progress paper uses dance as a focused and theoretically revealing case to address this gap. Rather than treating dance merely as entertainment, heritage representation, or event programming, we conceptualize it as relational, embodied cultural infrastructure through which patterned movement can organize encounters, carry cultural meaning across generations, and contribute to the character and capabilities of destinations. Drawing on tourism's anthropological lineage and interdisciplinary dance scholarship, we develop the Dance Ecosystem for Destinations—a seven-biome framework that distinguishes encounter-level value realization, portfolio-level accumulation and circulation, and cross-cutting technological mediation. The framework expands tourism management's conceptual and diagnostic capacity by linking these biomes to questions of experience design, stewardship, governance, value distribution, and evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Integrating theory of planned behavior and value-belief-norm framework to explain voluntary carbon offsetting intentions in aviation: Evidence from Vietnamese air passengers
abstract: The aviation industry faces growing environmental criticism for its high greenhouse gas emissions, necessitating both technological and behavioral solutions to mitigate climate change. This study examines passengers’ willingness to pay for voluntary carbon offsetting programs by developing and empirically testing an integrated model combining the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Values-Beliefs-Norms (VBN) framework. Using data from 342 Vietnamese airline passengers, the study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze both direct and indirect relationships among key constructs. Results confirm that biospheric values significantly shape awareness of environmental consequences, moral responsibility, and personal norms, which in turn directly influence behavioral intention. Within the TPB framework, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control are strong predictors of the intention to participate in voluntary carbon offsetting, with perceived behavioral control exerting the largest effect. Mediation analysis reveals that attitudinal and normative pathways bridge moral and cognitive antecedents with behavioral intention, underscoring the complementary roles of rational and moral motivations. The integrated TPB-VBN model demonstrates considerable explanatory power, providing a useful framework for understanding pro-environmental behavior in aviation. This research extends theoretical understanding by linking ethical and volitional determinants of sustainable consumption and offers managerial insights for airlines and policymakers to design effective carbon offset communication, education, and engagement strategies. title: Carbon coordination-driven regulation of reactive species pathways in Fe-N-C catalysts for enhanced activity and stability
abstract: Fe-N-C catalysts featuring Fe-N4 active sites are promising yet exhibit structurally similar Fe-N4 first-shell coordination environments that evolve distinct reaction pathways with unclear origins. Herein, carbon coordination in Fe-N4 single-atom is found to reprogram interfacial electronic and spin structures, enabling bifurcated reactive species evolution and reshaping activity-stability trade-off. Specifically, M-FeNC catalyst exhibits superior activity compared to M-HFeNC (0.2998 vs 0.266 min−1), yet inferior stability (67.6% vs 87.5%) after ten cycles, with high-valent iron species predominating in M-FeNC and 1O2 prevailing in M-HFeNC. 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with theoretical calculations reveals that FeN4C10 possesses a balanced electronic distribution, facilitates well-matched spin exchange and promotes PMS coupling. This configuration enables efficient 1O2 generation while minimizing structural reconstruction, thereby preserving high catalytic stability. In contrast, FeN4C12 exhibits enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized HOMO-LUMO coupling, which favors high-valent iron formation, but induces pronounced Fe-N bond fluctuations and local carbon reconstruction, ultimately compromising stability despite high activity. Furthermore, CPET-driven high-valent iron species-mediated polymerization pathway for phenolic pollutants was unveiled. This work provides molecular-level insight into how carbon coordination regulates reactive species pathways and thereby governs the activity-stability balance in Fe-N-C catalysts, establishing essential design principle for rational catalyst engineering. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Validity and Reliability of the Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle Method for Determining Masticatory Preference in Children Before Premolar Transition
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the validity and reliability of Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle (PFMA) method with a modified device compared to the clinical method as the gold standard for determining masticatory preference side in children. Material and Methods: Validity and reliability study of diagnostic tests. The study included 102 children, aged 6 to 9 years, before the transition to premolars. The outcome measures were the validity and reliability of the PFMA method compared to the clinical method as the gold standard. To measure the PFMA, a device was designed; for the direct clinical observation method, it was performed with a portion of baguette bread over seven mastication cycles. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values were measured; and reliability through intra-and inter-observer agreements using simple Kappa. Results: Sensitivity and negative predictive values were the highest percentages, being 88% with a 95% confidence interval, providing good validity, ruling out the condition of unilateral mastication with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.15. The interobserver agreement (reproducibility) was ideal (p=1.000), and the intraobserver agreement (repeatability) was significant, with an agreement percentage of 30.95%. Conclusion: The Planas’ Functional Masticatory Angle with a modified device proved to be a method with good validity and a useful tool as a screening test to identify the masticatory preference side. This study contributes to the diagnostic evaluation in pediatric dentistry. © 2027, Association of Support to Oral Health Research (APESB). .

title: Dual boron‑coordinated active sites steering an “activation‑migration‑desorption” relay pathway in S‑scheme SubPc/Ag‑ZnIn2S4 for H2O2 photosynthesis from wastewater
abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) faces an intrinsic trade-off between activity and selectivity, primarily due to the lack of well-defined and functionally differentiated active sites. Herein, a SubPc/Ag–ZnIn2S4 (SubPc/Ag–ZIS) S-scheme heterojunction is constructed by coordinating subphthalocyanine (SubPc–Br) onto Ag cluster-decorated ZnIn2S4. Distinct from conventional dual-site catalysts, this work achieves atomic-precision site differentiation via boron coordination chemistry, where the electron-rich B–Ag site activates O2, and the B–S site lowers the H2O2 desorption barrier. More importantly, the interfacial potential difference drives directional migration of the activated ·O2− intermediate from B–Ag to B–S, establishing an unprecedented “activation–migration–desorption” relay pathway. Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) confirms that this dual-site synergy significantly prolongs the charge carrier lifetime, providing a favorable kinetic foundation. The optimal catalyst delivers a H2O2 production rate of 1200 μmol g−1 h−1 with a 2e− ORR selectivity of 78%. In the presence of tetracycline (TC) wastewater, hole-driven TC degradation (reaching 93.5% within 60 min) further inhibits charge recombination and synergistically increases the hydrogen peroxide generation rate to 1579.8 μmol g−1 h−1. This work establishes a boron coordination chemistry-driven dual-site relay catalysis strategy, offering a new paradigm for integrating efficient H2O2 photosynthesis with pollutant degradation. © 2026

title: Predictors of Death Related to Drug Use Disorder and Interpersonal Violence in North Africa
abstract: Fatal interpersonal violence and deadly drug use disorder are serious social issues resulting from criminal behavior, which require effective intervention policies. Prior research on African countries is limited, and the potential association between the two issues, as described in the literature, has not been investigated. In this study, a statistical analysis was performed with R packages to identify factors that predict the death patterns related to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence, and to show empirical evidence for the association between drugs and violence in North Africa. Data on annual counts of deaths attributed to drug use disorder and interpersonal violence between 1990 and 2023 were collected, and a bivariate copula modeling approach was adopted to account for the dependence of the two counts. The findings show that socioeconomic factors, including per-capita gross domestic product, youth unemployment rate, and urban population, are significant predictors of these death counts, and statistical tests show a positive relationship between deaths related to drug use disorder and deaths caused by interpersonal violence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Perceived authenticity of AI-generated tourism video and destination attractiveness: An entity-referent correspondence perspective
abstract: Grounded in the entity-referent correspondence (ERC) framework, this study examines how three authenticity dimensions of AI-generated destination portrayals, true-to-ideal, true-to-fact, and true-to-self, relate to destination attractiveness via parallel and sequential pathways of place imagination and mental simulation. Analysis of 406 participants exposed to an AI-generated tourism video reveals that true-to-ideal and true-to-fact authenticity show significant direct effects on destination attractiveness, whereas true-to-self authenticity operates entirely indirectly, consistent with a meaning-making route. For parallel mediation, true-to-ideal and true-to-self authenticity exert significant indirect effects via both mediators, whereas true-to-fact authenticity does so only through place imagination. The sequential pathway from place imagination to mental simulation receives consistent support across all dimensions. Theoretically, this study advances the ERC framework from a static typology to a processual account by delineating the distinct cognitive routes of each referent and highlighting both the conceptual promise and measurement challenges of operationalizing true-to-self authenticity as perceived communicative sincerity in algorithmically generated portrayals. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Micro-foundations of destination supply: A configural analysis of herders’ livelihood strategies in grassland tourism
abstract: Based on the revised Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis was used to investigate the combinatorial effects of social, human, cultural, policy, physical, natural, and financial capital on herders' livelihood strategies in Chen Barag in the Hulunbuir Grassland, to identify the key drivers of herders’ adoption of a tourism livelihood. The results identify six differentiated livelihood configuration types. Traditional pastoral livelihoods are associated with resource-constrained configurations and high thresholds for tourism participation under ecological, market, and institutional conditions. Conversely, mixed livelihoods are associated with configurations involving productive resource release, locational advantages, cultural commodification, and intergenerational labour division, while governance tensions between institutional arrangements and diversified livelihood needs may create additional constraints. These findings highlight the joint importance of asset-related thresholds and institutional conditions in shaping differentiated tourism participation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Cognitive appraisal of illegitimate tasks and research creativity: dual reflective processing pathways in graduate education
abstract: Although graduate students frequently encounter illegitimate tasks—assignments perceived as inconsistent with their research roles—little is known about how such tasks influence research creativity and through what cognitive mechanisms. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), a dual-pathway model is proposed in which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity through problem-solving pondering and affective rumination, with supervisor–student relationship quality as a moderator. Data were collected from 389 graduate students in Chinese universities using a two-wave survey design, and the hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using hierarchical regression analyses supplemented by the PROCESS macro. The results indicate that illegitimate tasks exert opposing indirect effects on research creativity through distinct reflective cognitive pathways. Illegitimate tasks were associated with increased affective rumination, which interfered with sustained creative engagement. However, under high-quality supervisor-student relationships, illegitimate tasks were more strongly related to problem-solving pondering, which facilitated creative thinking. Supervisor-student relationship quality further shaped how illegitimate tasks were interpreted and which reflective pathway was activated. These findings clarify the cognitive mechanisms and relational conditions through which illegitimate tasks influence research creativity and contribute to understanding how task legitimacy shapes creative thinking in graduate research contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Applied economic reasoning in air transport management: A question- and concept-level analysis of an airport business course
abstract: Economic reasoning underpins business decision-making. Yet how it is taught and assessed in air transport management education remains underexplored. Drawing on final-exam data from an Airport Business course for non-specialists at a Japanese university, this study identifies aspects of assessed economic reasoning that appeared relatively more demanding. At the question level, the higher-difficulty side concerned airport network financing, restructuring, and public support, whereas the lower-difficulty side addressed charge pass-through, the club-good characteristics of small-airport services, and concession-contract risks. At the concept level, government failure, incentives, and user-pays lay on the higher-difficulty side, while demand and costs, price discrimination, and public, private, and club goods fell on the lower-difficulty side. This concept-level pattern did not follow a simple foundational–advanced distinction, with positions varying across institutional contexts and concept co-occurrence. These patterns remained broadly stable in supplementary analyses assessing sensitivity to question selection. The findings add a question- and concept-level perspective to research on air transport management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Digital Literacy through a Web-Based Application: Addressing Polarization and Promoting Social Integration among Islamic Senior High School Students
abstract: Digital literacy encompasses not only technical skills but also an understanding of social dynamics such as polarization and the need for social integration in digital environments. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of a web-based Mobile Polarization and Social Integration application in improving students’ digital literacy. A quasi-experimental design with a control group was employed, involving students from an Islamic senior high school. Data were collected using a validated test and analyzed through comparative statistical methods. The application significantly enhances students’ digital literacy and supports their awareness of polarization and social integration. This study highlights the potential of web-based learning applications to strengthen digital citizenship and encourage responsible and inclusive participation in digital spaces. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Inner-supportive destinations for psychologically vulnerable solo travelers: A framework of narrative reconstruction and reintegrative stabilization
abstract: This study examines how inner-supportive destination experiences support psychological reconstruction among solo visitors reporting self-identified emotional disruption. Drawing on constructivist grounded theory and 30 in-depth interviews with domestic solo visitors to Da Lat, Vietnam, the research identifies a process through which pre-travel emotional disruption is gradually reorganized through destination experience. Findings show that participants did not travel merely for leisure or stress relief, but because burnout, grief, relational rupture, life transition, or identity uncertainty had unsettled their self-understanding. Inner-supportive affordances, including temporal deceleration, sensory softness, perceived safety, and supported solitude, reduced defensive pressure and created conditions for regulated emotional exposure. This exposure enabled narrative re-authoring, through which distressing experiences were reinterpreted and integrated into a more coherent self-understanding. Based on these accounts, the study proposes the inner-supportive destination framework, explaining how destination affordances, regulated emotional exposure, narrative re-authoring, participant-attributed reintegrative stabilization, and boundary conditions relate within a contingent process. Theoretically, the study extends destination marketing and management by distinguishing narrative reconstruction from restoration, healing, or emotional elevation. Practically, it offers guidance for designing vulnerability-sensitive destinations that support autonomy, low-pressure engagement, and safe solitude without making therapeutic claims. The findings invite broader applications of inner-supportive design across wellness, cultural, nature-based, and urban retreat contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From airplanes to classrooms: A cross-domain literature review of seating assignment models and methods
abstract: Seating assignments play an important role in customer-focused managerial decisions, yet existing studies are frequently limited in scope to isolated application domains. This paper addresses this fragmentation through the first systematic cross-domain seating assignment literature review, analyzing publications via bibliometric analysis and examining assignment methods (including optimization techniques) across transportation (airplanes and trains), dining establishments, entertainment venues, and classrooms. Co-citation analysis reveals that research communities operate in separate networks despite addressing similar challenges using mathematical programming, heuristic approaches, stochastic simulation, and other operational research methods. Our cross-domain synthesis identifies technique transfer opportunities previously invisible due to research silos, such as applying restaurant group-seating strategies to airline passengers traveling together or entertainment venue considerations to dining table assignments. The review concludes that limited real-world implementation stems partly from researchers' inability to access successful approaches from adjacent fields, highlighting opportunities to advance seating assignment methods through integrated frameworks. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Multi-layered texture-heterogeneous architecture enabling strength-ductility synergy in Mg laminates
abstract: Achieving strength-ductility synergy in Mg alloys remains challenging because their inherent plastic anisotropy leads to a trade-off between texture-induced strengthening and strain accommodation. Here, we designed and fabricated texture-heterogeneous Mg laminates by accumulative roll bonding, comprising five alternating layers of Mg-Al-Zn with a strong basal texture (hard layer) and Mg-Al-Sn-Ca with a weaker basal texture (soft layer). Two texture-heterogeneous laminates with different stacking architectures have been constructed, i.e., hard-soft-hard-soft-hard (HSH-5L) and soft-hard-soft-hard-soft (SHS-5L). HSH-5L exhibits a yield strength of 192 MPa and fracture elongation of 22%, representing improvements of 8.1% and 27%, respectively, compared with SHS-5L. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction, digital image correlation, and finite element simulation indicate that the improved mechanical response is associated with enhanced interfacial constraints and higher strain gradients in HSH-5L. These conditions facilitate <c+a> slip near interfaces and provide more nucleation sites for strain bands (SB). As deformation proceeds, dense SBs mainly dominated by basal <a> slip gradually intersect. The intersection regions induce local stress concentration and activate additional non-basal slip, which in turn restricts the further propagation of SBs and thereby contributes to sustained strain hardening in the HSH-5L sample. By contrast, in the SHS-5L sample, basal <a> slip initiates and propagates rapidly during deformation, forming long-range SBs that lead to local deformation instability and premature fracture. These findings provide insights for the design of heterogeneous Mg laminates with high strength and ductility. © 2026

title: From duality to triadic structuration: Coupling Agile agency, generative technology, and regulatory structure
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) increasingly permeates software development, Agile organizations face growing pressure to achieve continuous lifecycle compliance amid rapidly evolving regulatory demands. Classical Structuration Theory and its derivatives account for technology as either an instantiation of social structure or a medium for human agency; neither pole adequately captures GenAI's quasi-autonomous capacity to reshape organizational practices and give rise to new regulatory obligations. This study addresses this gap by developing Triadic Structuration Theory. Following an incremental design science research (DSR) paradigm, we develop this abstract design artifact through cycle-level intermediate artifacts, with cross-cycle knowledge accumulation. Cycle 1 derives a problem backlog of GenAI-induced tensions in Agile practice. Cycle 2 conceptualizes RegOps, showing how Agile agency adapts under regulatory pressure. Cycle 3 designs an EU AI Act-aligned model card template, showing how regulatory structure becomes embedded in generative technology. Cycle 4 explores GenAI-enabled solutions to ISO-related compliance barriers in an Agile company. Together, the evidence and knowledge accumulated within and across the cycles position generative technology as a third construct rather than a medium between agency and structure. Regulatory structure is embedded directly into it; it reshapes Agile agency through quasi-autonomous action, and its use to meet existing obligations may recursively generate new ones. The study extends Structuration Theory as a middle-range theory to Agile and GenAI contexts, and demonstrates how nested DSR with intermediate artifacts can support theory development. For practitioners, it offers guidance on leveraging GenAI for compliance, cautioning that it is a structural intervention rather than a one-off fix. © 2026 The Authors

title: Simultaneous giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability in PNZST ceramics via antiferroelectric phase boundary regulation
abstract: Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramics are promising candidates for precision actuators, but the trade-off between giant electrostrain and wide-temperature stability has severely limited their practical applications. Here, we propose a dual-pathway phase boundary regulation strategy in perovskite AFE systems to synergistically optimize electrostrain magnitude and temperature stability by designing the electric-field-induced AFE-ferroelectric (FE) transition sequence under coupled temperature-electric-field conditions. Using the prototype system of Pb0.99Nb0.02[(Zr0.75Sn0.25)xTi1−x]0.98O3 (PNZST-100xZS), our results show that PNZST-99ZS and PNZST-97ZS exhibit giant electrostrains of 0.98% and 0.77%, respectively. Remarkably, over a wide temperature range of 25–155 °C, they maintain low electrostrain fluctuations of only 16.12% and 9.21%, significantly better than previously reported materials. The excellent performance stems from the electric-field-induced orthorhombic AFE (AFEO)-rhombohedral FE (FER) transition at low temperatures and the tetragonal AFE (AFET)-FER transition at high temperatures. Between these two temperature regions, the diffuse AFEO-AFET transition bridges the two field-induced pathways, ensuring a smooth evolution of the electrostrain response across the entire operating temperature range. This work provides a new route to high-performance AFE actuator materials with both large electrostrain and wide-temperature stability. © 2026

abstract: Grammarly is one of the most widely used software applications for the automatic detection of grammatical errors in texts translated from Persian into English. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Grammarly and to propose suggestions for improving its performance. To achieve this objective, a corpus consisting of English translations of booklets introducing works of resistance literature was analyzed. After grammatical errors had been identified by the researchers (human evaluators), the electronic versions of the booklets were submitted to Grammarly for error detection. The identified errors were then categorized, and the results obtained by the researchers were compared with those generated by the software. Following the qualitative and quantitative analyses of the errors and the presentation of the findings, recommendations were made to enhance Grammarly’s effectiveness. According to the findings, of the 98 instances identified by Grammarly as errors, 16 were not actual errors. In four cases (4.9%), Grammarly failed to correctly identify the type of error. The software demonstrated its weakest performance in the detection of spelling errors and the misuse of masculine and feminine pronouns. Overall, Grammarly exhibited a high level of effectiveness, correctly identifying 82.8% of the errors. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Synergistic enhancement of coercivity and saturation magnetization in Sm-Co alloys via multi-element doping
abstract: Multi-element doping represents the most effective approach for enhancing the performance of permanent magnetic alloys. However, the complex interdependencies among diverse doping elements, broad concentration ranges, and intricate element-matrix interactions present significant challenges in establishing appropriate composition-property relationships, impeding efficient development of high-performance multicomponent alloys. To address this fundamental limitation, this study introduced a data-driven framework incorporating high-throughput identification of key elemental features governing magnetic properties. Principal component and feature sensitivity analyses quantified feature contributions to distinct magnetic characteristics and evaluated comprehensive weighting factors for multi-objective optimization. This integrated methodology enabled efficient and appropriate design of multi-element doped alloys targeting simultaneous enhancement of competing magnetic properties. Demonstrated by the Sm-Co-based systems, the framework concurrently enhanced both saturation magnetization and coercivity, which effectively resolved the trade-off between these properties through multi-element doping. Experimentally validated designs across multiple matrix types exhibited superior comprehensive magnetic properties, with quantitative confirmation of the model predictions. The present study provides a novel strategy that is in principle broadly applicable for designing multicomponent alloys that overcome inherent property trade-offs. © 2026

title: Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) in business and management education for developing AI and prompt literacy
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into organizational practice has created an urgent need for business and management education to move beyond tool exposure toward meaningful skill development. This study develops and implements a Structured AI-Integrated Learning (SAIL) approach that embeds GAI within active learning environments to support students' AI literacy and prompt literacy. A central feature of the approach is the use of structured scaffolds, particularly the RACE framework (Role–Action–Context–Explanation), which guides students in designing prompts, evaluating AI outputs, and linking responses to theoretical concepts. The approach was implemented in an undergraduate Organizational Behavior course (n = 93) using an explanatory mixed-methods design. Quantitative results indicate significant improvements in both AI literacy and prompt literacy, including gains in knowledge, application, and ethical awareness. Qualitative findings show that students engaged with AI iteratively and reflectively, using it as a “co-thinker” to refine prompts, assess output quality, and connect AI-generated insights with course theories. Cognitive and metacognitive engagement emerged as dominant, while collaborative and ethical dimensions, though less prominent, contributed to students’ developing awareness of responsible AI use. The findings demonstrate that structured, pedagogically guided AI integration transforms AI from a passive information source into an active learning scaffold. The SAIL approach, supported by RACE, offers a practical and transferable pathway for educators seeking to prepare students to navigate AI-augmented professional environments with critical, reflective, and responsible judgment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
