label: Social Sciences
title: When crowds converge: Link between events and crime
abstract: This study draws on environmental criminology to conceptualize planned events as bounded opportunity contexts that temporarily reshape urban activity. Using high-dimensional fixed-effects Poisson models and a panel of 154,561 events in Houston, Texas, we estimate reduced-form associations across event attributes and offense types. The event-crime association is statistically detectable but economically modest. Formal comparisons reveal selective offense heterogeneity, with the Crimes Against Society coefficient exceeding the Violent Crime coefficient. Public opportunistic crime also shows stronger associations than private opportunistic and non-opportunistic crime, but not Other Crime. Event size exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the largest events showing stronger associations than those in all lower-attendance categories. Event type, day-type context, duration, and recurrence are not statistically distinguishable. Adjustment for contemporaneous foot traffic attenuates the event coefficient. The findings suggest proportionate, targeted situational prevention rather than generalized security escalation in urban destination safety planning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Energy security risks and democratic vulnerability in the European Union
abstract: Over the past decade, growing vulnerabilities in the global energy system have affected both economic stability and the quality of democratic governance. The COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine war have intensified energy security risks, imposing new pressures on democratic processes and public accountability. Structural imbalances in energy markets, particularly within the European Union (EU), have necessitated the redefinition of energy policies and the reduction of external dependency. This study empirically investigates the impact of energy security risk on democratic governance using data from 25 EU countries for the period 2008–2023. The Voice and Accountability indicator from the World Bank’s World Governance Indicators serves as the measure of democratic governance, while dynamic interrelationships are analyzed through a Panel Vector Autoregression model estimated via the generalized method of moments (Panel GMM-VAR). The findings indicate that energy security risk has predictive precedence over democratic accountability. Granger causality analysis shows a unidirectional relationship running from energy security risk to Voice and Accountability, with no significant reverse effect. The cross-sectional association between the two is negative, although the dynamic responses are modest in magnitude and conditional on the identification ordering. At the policy level, energy supply diversification and resilience-building measures should be prioritised in efforts to protect democratic stability. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

title: Experimental comparison of dual-stage organic Rankine cycle and organic Rankine flash cycle for low-temperature geothermal power generation
abstract: Organic Rankine cycle (ORC) has gained increasing attention in thermal power generation, but with a relatively low efficiency due to the irreversible loss of the evaporation process. In order to improve the performance of ORC, dual-stage ORC (DORC) and organic Rankine flash cycle (ORFC) were proposed. Previous numerical studies have demonstrated that DORC and ORFC can indeed enhance the system performance. However, experimental verification is lacking. This study designed and established an experimental setup to achieve the switching of the DORC and ORFC systems via valve start-stop operation, using R245fa as the working fluid. The power generation performance of ORFC is tested and compared with that of the DORC. Experimental results reveal that the working fluid of ORFC undergoes incomplete evaporation before entering the scroll expander, which can effectively reduce the irreversible loss of between the heat source and the working fluid. Compared with DORC, ORFC achieves a higher specific power output due to the further reduction the injection temperature. The thermal efficiency of ORFC is almost the same as that of DORC. Nevertheless, ORFC exhibits lower net power generation and exergy efficiency due to higher power consumption of the working fluid pumps. © 2026 The Authors. title: Overcoming geothermal development barriers in Indonesia: A narrative policy review of sedimentary basin-based geothermal development
abstract: Indonesia possesses the world's largest geothermal resource potential, yet its utilization remains disproportionately low. This study conducted a narrative policy review and strategic assessment using the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) framework to identify the key barriers to geothermal development and formulate strategic recommendations using the TOWS (Threats, Opportunities, Weaknesses, Strengths) matrix. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach based on a narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2011 and 2026. The analysis identified four major constraints to conventional volcanic geothermal development: high exploration risk and capital expenditure (CAPEX), land-use conflicts with protected forests, electricity tariff policies linked to coal-based generation costs, and persistent social resistance (NIMBY/Not in My Backyard syndrome). The findings indicated that diversifying geothermal development toward non-volcanic back-arc sedimentary basins, particularly through co-production with mature Oil and Gas (O&G) fields, provided a practical pathway to reduce exploration risk, lower infrastructure costs, minimize permitting conflicts and social resistance, and improve project economics. This approach could potentially reduce the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) to below USD 0.07/kWh. Based on the TOWS analysis, the study recommended a dual-track geothermal development strategy combining continued volcanic exploration with accelerated sedimentary basin development, supported by binary-cycle technology, brownfield O&G infrastructure reuse, Feed-in Tariff (FiT) reform, and international green financing. Collectively, these strategies could strengthen investment attractiveness and accelerate Indonesia's transition toward its Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 target. © 2026 The Authors. title: Career plateau and multifaceted turnover pathways in the airline industry: Evidence from full-service and low-cost carrier cabin crew
abstract: This study examines how career plateau influences stress, burnout, and multifaceted turnover intentions among airline cabin crew members by comparing full-service carriers (FSCs) and low-cost carriers (LCCs). Career plateau was categorized into hierarchical and job content career plateaus, and their psychological and behavioral impacts were assessed. Data were collected through a survey of 382 Korean cabin crew members with at least three years of experience and in-depth interviews with 14 participants. Quantitative results showed that a job content career plateau significantly heightened stress, leading to burnout. LCC crew members reported stronger turnover intentions, whereas burnout among FSC crew members did not necessarily translate into turnover intentions, suggesting that its effects may be constrained by organizational and labor market conditions. Qualitative findings revealed coping strategies such as goal adjustment and highlighted carrier-specific interpretations of turnover. Social support moderated the burnout–turnover link, buffering negative outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A simulation-informed machine learning framework for integrated energy and thermal comfort assessment in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings under hot-arid climates
abstract: Adaptive reuse of heritage courtyard buildings as boutique hotels creates a complex balance between energy performance, thermal comfort, and cultural conservation in hot-arid regions. However, existing studies commonly address energy performance and thermal comfort separately and often depend on computationally intensive simulation workflows. This study develops a simulation-informed machine-learning surrogate framework for simultaneous prediction of end-uses energy consumption and thermal comfort indicators in adaptively reused heritage courtyard buildings. A comprehensive hourly dataset was generated from full-year simulations of twelve heritage courtyard buildings modelled in DesignBuilder using representative meteorological data for the hot-arid climate of Kashan, Iran. Building-specific heat-transfer characteristics represented by overall heat-transfer coefficient values, geometric attributes, operational parameters, indoor environmental conditions and weather were used as predictors. Seven end-uses energy outputs, namely cooling electricity, heating gas, lighting, appliance energy, system fan energy, system pump energy, and auxiliary energy, were evaluated alongside three thermal comfort indicators: predicted mean vote, predicted percentage of dissatisfied, and comfort percentage. Twenty-eight machine-learning algorithms were attempted, of which 22 successfully converged and were assessed using a leave-one-building-out validation strategy to evaluate cross-building generalization. In addition, an independently simulated heritage building, excluded from all training and validation procedures, was used for external testing to further assess model transferability. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean squared error, and predictor importance was examined using a Shapley-value-based feature-importance analysis. Ensemble Bagged Trees achieved the highest predictive performance for eight of the ten evaluated outputs, while the two system-level end-uses, system fans and system pumps, were predicted less accurately (coefficients of determination of 0.397 and 0.839, respectively). Thermal comfort analysis revealed substantial seasonal discomfort, ranging from cold winter stress to severe summer overheating, while annual comfort levels remained below the adopted comfort benchmark. The Shapley-value-based analysis indicated that climatic variables (e.g., solar irradiation and outdoor temperature) and building-scale geometric/envelope variables (e.g., orientation, façade area, window-to-wall ratio, and envelope thermal properties) were among the most influential predictors across the evaluated outputs. Although courtyard-specific geometric parameters were not included as explicit inputs, building-scale variables partly reflect the influence of courtyard configuration. The independent test case further demonstrated the framework's ability to predict several energy and thermal comfort outputs for a previously unseen building, while indicating lower transferability for some system-level end-uses. Although the framework is based on simulation-generated rather than measured data, it provides a computationally efficient basis for preliminary retrofit assessment and scenario exploration. Overall, the framework enables integrated and interpretable assessment of energy performance and thermal comfort to support heritage-sensitive retrofit planning in hot-arid climates. © 2026 The Authors. title: Zwitterionic Ionogels Resolving the Trade-Off Between Mechanical Strength and Autonomous Self-Healing for Iontronics
abstract: Simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness and autonomous self-healing in ionogels remains a fundamental challenge for durable, skin-like electronics. Conventional approaches often improve mechanical strength by introducing rigid or densely cross-linked polymer networks, but such strategies inevitably restrict polymer chain mobility and hinder dynamic bond reconfiguration required for healing. Here, a zwitterionic side-chain engineered tough ionogel (ZESTI) is developed to overcome this trade-off through molecular-level design. Hydrophilic zwitterions are covalently grafted onto a hydrophobic polyurethane backbone to preferentially interact with the ionic liquid through ion–dipole interactions and thereby regulate its distribution. This architecture simultaneously facilitates dipole–dipole interactions for mechanical reinforcement and ion–dipole coordination for efficient self-healing under ambient conditions. As a result, ZESTI exhibits an exceptional combination of tensile strength (10.40 MPa), stretchability (1606%), toughness (56.03 MJ m−3), and ambient self-healing efficiency exceeding 83%, while maintaining high ionic conductivity via enhanced ion hopping. When constructed as a self-reporting packaging interface, ZESTI provides stable protection and state perception under sharp contact and restores signal output after mechanical damage through self-healing. This work offers a generalizable design strategy that reconciles mechanical toughness with dynamic functionality in ionogels, establishing a general design paradigm for next-generation self-sustaining iontronic devices. title: Alginate-induced structural modification of high-moisture extruded soy and pea protein scaffolds for cultivated meat applications
abstract: Producing plant-based scaffolds through high-moisture extrusion offers a promising approach for cultivated meat. However, the influence of hydrocolloid incorporation on scaffold structure and functionality remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated alginate incorporation during high-moisture extrusion of pea and soy protein concentrates and evaluated its effect on structure, material properties, and cell distribution.Protein source was associated with differences in processing behavior and extrudate appearance, with soy exhibiting higher specific mechanical energy and darker extrudates than pea. Increased directional alignment was observed in pea extrudates upon alginate addition, whereas soy extrudates only showed moderate structural changes. Mechanical characterization of soy extrudates showed increased stiffness and cohesion compared to pea extrudates, while alginate-containing formulations generally reduced stiffness and increased deformability, potentially reflecting both alginate incorporation and the associated reduction in protein content. Protein extraction differed between pea and soy protein and was altered by alginate addition, indicating changes in protein accessibility, potentially reflecting both altered protein-polysaccharide interactions and the decreased protein content. Scaffold preparation altered surface morphology, with observed increased porosity upon ethanol treatment, especially in alginate-containing scaffolds. Cell experiments showed heterogeneous cell distribution, with observed localized cell accumulation in grooves and cavities.Overall, differences between protein sources were observed in processing behavior, structure, mechanical properties, and protein solubility, while alginate addition altered these properties to varying extents. These findings provide first insights into how formulation composition and scaffold preparation may influence scaffold architecture and cell distribution, for cultivated meat applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Bi-level coordinated day-ahead dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat–hydrogen integrated energy system with endogenous hourly vehicle-to-grid pricing interaction
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy and large-scale EV integration poses new challenges to the optimal scheduling of regional integrated energy systems (RIESs) by intensifying source-load uncertainty and affecting operational flexibility and economic performance. To address this issue, a bi-level optimal dispatch model is developed to coordinate the economic interaction between the RIES operator and EV users through price-based source-load interaction. The upper-level RIES operator minimizes its net operating cost, while the lower-level EV users minimize their net charging/discharging cost. Three EV participation modes, namely disorderly charging, orderly charging, and vehicle-to-grid (V2G), are compared to quantify their impacts on load smoothing, multi-energy coordination, and system-user economics. Scenario generation and reduction are used to construct expected renewable profiles, while Monte Carlo sampling provides heterogeneous EV travel inputs for the deterministic day-ahead bi-level dispatch. Under the zero-degradation-cost setting, the V2G strategy reduces the RIES operator net cost, EV user net cost, and combined resource cost by 5.56%, 47.74%, and 10.99%, respectively, compared with disorderly charging. When battery degradation compensation is considered, the EV-side economic benefit decreases but remains positive; for example, the EV user cost reduction decreases to 42.41% at a degradation cost of 0.10 CNY/kWh. The proposed strategy balances the interests of EV users and the RIES operator while improving load smoothing and flexible coordination of multi-energy flows. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: The impact of environmental, economic, and social sustainability under intensive agriculture
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intensive agriculture has substantially increased agricultural productivity but is increasingly associated with environmental degradation, resource depletion, and socio-economic challenges. The study objectives were to evaluate the sustainability impacts of intensive agricultural practices across environmental, economic, and social dimensions in Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu, India, with particular emphasis on resource utilization, ecological stress, and the factors influencing sustainable agricultural development. METHODS: Primary data were collected during 2025 from 663 eligible farmers selected through multistage stratified random sampling across eight taluks of Namakkal District using a structured questionnaire. Farms were classified as traditional or intensive based on cultivation practices. Relationships among the study variables were examined using correlation analysis, analysis of variance, regression analysis, and non-parametric statistical tests. FINDINGS: The findings revealed a strong positive relationship between landholding size and family size (correlation coefficient = 0.7214), indicating close structural and demographic linkages within farming systems. Intensive agriculture was significantly associated with land expansion (correlation coefficient = 0.658), environmental pollution (correlation coefficient = 0.519), and declining health conditions among farming communities (correlation coefficient = 0.412). Approximately 63 percent of respondents reported land degradation, while 65 –78 percent reported salinity and nutrient depletion, reflecting perceived ecological stress. The regression model explained 7.1 percent of the variation in agricultural production (coefficient of determination = 0.071), indicating modest explanatory power. Questionnaire reliability was satisfactory (Cronbach's alpha = 0.824), supporting the internal consistency of the survey instrument. CONCLUSION: Intensive agriculture is associated with higher short-term agricultural productivity but is also associated with environmental degradation, increases health risks, and places greater pressure on natural resources. These findings may inform strategies to improve the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of agricultural sustainability through sustainable soil management, balanced agrochemical application, efficient irrigation, and policy support. While the study is limited to a single district and cross-sectional data, it provides empirical evidence to inform future longitudinal and multi-regional investigations. ©2026 The author(s). title: Beyond green claims: a social-ecological assessment of cruise tourism sustainability
abstract: Cruise tourism sustainability discourse prioritises vessel level innovation, marginalising destination level social ecological impacts. To address this, we develop a structured literature based conceptual model of cruise mobility as a coupled global and local social ecological system. Supported by AI assisted extraction and synthesis of multidisciplinary literature, this paper constructs a governance-oriented framework. The analysis identifies two interacting dynamics: a reinforcing expansion loop where revenues stimulate infrastructure and deepen dependency, and a degrading acceptance loop where cumulative stress erodes tolerance. Presented as heuristic formalisation devices, these loops help explain why vessel efficiency alone cannot prevent destination level degradation. We translate these findings into a five-pillar governance framework featuring capacity thresholds, social monitoring, economic diversification, power rebalancing, and multi-level coordination. This shifts attention from ship focused compliance towards destination embedded sustainability governance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ethical reasoning and responsible use of ChatGPT in higher education: Integrating technology acceptance and moral cognition
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has raised important questions about how students evaluate the ethical implications of AI-assisted academic practices and whether those evaluations are linked to intentions to use these tools responsibly. While previous research has largely focused on technology adoption and acceptance, it has paid less attention to the relationship between ethical reasoning and intentions to use these tools responsibly. This study develops and tests an integrated framework that combines the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and moral cognition theory to examine how technology perceptions and academic and cognitive factors relate to students’ ethical reasoning and intentions to use ChatGPT responsibly. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design among business and management students in Oman and analysed the data using structural equation modelling. The findings indicate that perceived ease of use, academic pressure, and moral disengagement are positively associated with ethical reasoning, whereas perceived usefulness is not significantly associated with ethical reasoning. Ethical reasoning is positively associated with behavioural intention to use ChatGPT responsibly. In contrast, ChatGPT usage does not significantly moderate the relationship between academic pressure and ethical reasoning. These findings suggest that students’ responsible-use intentions are associated with their ethical evaluations of ChatGPT-assisted academic practices, while conventional technology acceptance perceptions and usage frequency alone offer a more limited explanation of ethical reasoning. The study contributes to emerging research on responsible generative AI use by extending TAM beyond conventional adoption outcomes and integrating it with a moral cognition perspective. It highlights the relationship between ethical reasoning and responsible-use intentions while distinguishing ethical evaluation from technology acceptance and usage frequency. The findings also provide context-specific evidence from Omani higher education, while recognising the limitations of the cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, and a context-specific sample. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Supporting initial teacher education student creativity and critical thinking using active constraints in assessment: A scoping review
abstract: Assessment design plays a critical role in shaping student learning in higher education, particularly in disciplines where creativity is both a learning outcome and a pedagogical approach. In Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this role is intensified, as assessment tasks often function as the primary site of learning for time-poor students and simultaneously model pedagogical practice for future teachers. While constraints are frequently embedded within assessment tasks, their role in supporting creativity remains under-theorised and inconsistently articulated in the literature. This scoping review examines how constraints are used within assessment tasks that aim to foster creativity and/or critical thinking in social sciences, humanities, education and creative arts courses in higher education in order to consider implications for enhancing creativity through assessment tasks in ITE. Using a scoping review framework, 28 empirical studies published since 2000 were identified and analysed thematically. Six key themes emerged: the role of prior experience, constraints as catalysts for creativity, task design and flexibility, rubrics and scaffolding as support structures, the domain-specificity of creativity, and the presence of “invisible architectures” in task design. Findings indicate that constraints function as powerful pedagogical mechanisms when they are intentionally designed, aligned with disciplinary practices, and calibrated to student readiness. However, many studies prioritise creative outcomes without sufficiently detailing the task conditions that shape them. Drawing on these findings, the paper positions constraints as active contributors to assessment design and introduces a design-oriented framework to support educators in making constraints explicit and pedagogically purposeful. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Artificial intelligence and generative AI in entrepreneurship education: A systematic review of competency development, entrepreneurial intention, and the sustainability disconnect
abstract: Entrepreneurship education increasingly deploys artificial intelligence (AI), yet claims that it builds entrepreneurial competence and advances sustainability rest on an unexamined evidence base. This review asks what that evidence supports, and what it does not. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus and Web of Science searches yielded 21 empirical studies with approximately 7800 unique participants across 14 countries. Studies were stratified as generative, broader or analytical AI, quality was appraised item by item with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and every conclusion was tested by sensitivity analysis. CIMO logic specified the question; TCM-ADO organised the synthesis. AI was positively associated with entrepreneurial intention in every study that measured it, but its magnitude cannot be established: the largest estimates come from the lowest-quality studies, and few report uncertainty estimates. Competency development, the assumed mechanism, rests almost entirely on non-generative AI studies and is untested for generative systems. Self-efficacy operates as a boundary condition, raising an equity concern no study measures. Nominal relevance to the Sustainable Development Goals is widespread, yet none measured a sustainability outcome or named an environmental goal. It supplies a stratified, quality-weighted evidence base and shows that closing the sustainability gap requires theory and instruments, not more intention surveys. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Toward vulnerability-friendly destinations: A relational framework for inclusive destination governance
abstract: Tourism research has generally located vulnerability in particular travelers and treated inclusion as an extension of accessibility provision. This paper reframes vulnerability as a relational destination-level condition produced, intensified, or reduced through interactions between heterogeneous human capacities and destination-system demands. A structured integrative conceptual synthesis connects public health equity, human factors engineering, and tourism management. The resulting framework explains how unequal exposure creates person-system mismatch, how destination arrangements produce vulnerability through recurring interfaces, and how inclusive-governance capability operates both preventively by shaping system properties and responsively by coordinating intervention. Risk redistribution is specified as a distinct mechanism that follows risk reduction and the allocation of responsibility, workload, and cost, and concerns the pooling, transfer, or absorption of residual risk by actors with greater capacity. Five recurring exposure interfaces and four intervention dimensions are organized in an analytical matrix. The framework distinguishes proximal outcomes (participation, safety, dignity, trust, and wellbeing) from conditional destination outcomes such as legitimacy, loyalty, and competitiveness. The paper extends relational vulnerability logic to the destination-system level and provides a research agenda for inclusive destination governance. © 2026

title: Investigating the interplay between public art, urban design, and national identity: Case of the UAE
abstract: Public art and culturally responsive urban environment play a crucial role in shaping national identity, particularly in culturally diverse and rapidly evolving societies like the UAE. This study examines how different forms of public art, their integration into urban spaces, and digital platforms influence perceptions of national identity. Grounded in Social Identity Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and Public Space Theory, it employs structural equation modeling (SEM) and thematic analysis using data from 543 respondents across UAE emirates. The SEM model explains 40.3% of the variance in Perceived National Identity (PNI), emphasizing the significant role of public art and digital platforms in cultural engagement. Mediation analysis highlights the importance of interactive experiences in strengthening cultural connections, while thematic analysis identifies cultural integration, community involvement, and sustainability as key themes. Findings suggest that combining traditional Emirati artistic elements with modern digital technologies enhances inclusivity and engagement. However, the limited direct impact of urban design on national identity highlights the need for culturally relevant elements to maximize its effectiveness. By integrating quantitative and qualitative insights, this study offers clear implications for policy and practice by recommending participatory planning, integration of heritage-based design elements and use of digital platforms to enhance cultural visibility and engagement. It provides a practical framework for urban planners, cultural policymakers, and designers to develop inclusive public spaces that reinforce national identity in the UAE. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Motivations in Chinese costume travel photography: An evolutionary psychology perspective
abstract: Tourist photography has shifted from passive sightseeing to active narrative construction. Existing research has revealed the proximate motives of such behavior centered on identity construction, but the ultimate motives remain underexplored. Using a qualitative research design, this study explores motivations in Chinese costume travel photography by applying three interpretive lenses derived from evolutionary psychology, namely performative affiliation, temporary status, and scripted exploration. The findings indicate that participants' motivations are satisfied in Chinese costume travel photography as follows: temporary immersion and affiliation are gained from symbolic imitation and contextual co-performance; contextualized status enhancement is acquired by enacting ideal identities and collecting digital validation; and novelty seeking is met through experiences grounded in symbolic imagination and pre-arranged scripts. This study provides insights into the ultimate drivers of tourists’ surface motivations and the possible satisfaction mechanisms of deep evolutionary motives in Chinese costume travel photography. It also offers practical insights for tourism experience design and marketing by focusing on the satisfaction of deep motives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From fragmentation to integration: Rethinking the measurement of responsible management education
abstract: Responsible Management Education (RME) has become a central agenda within business schools, as institutions seek to prepare graduates capable of addressing complex sustainability and societal challenges. Despite its growing prominence, approaches to evaluating RME remain fragmented, with studies measuring diverse educational, institutional and societal outcomes using inconsistent conceptualisations and indicators. This study systematically reviews the contemporary literature to examine how RME is currently measured and develop a more coherent conceptual framework for evaluation. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review of 62 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 using the Scopus database—an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop thematic synthesis identified and consolidated 328 measurement-related concepts. The synthesis identified five complementary measurement domains: implementation, learning, behaviour, performance and impact, alongside five stakeholder groups: students, educators, institutions, industry and society. Building on these findings, the study proposes the Integrated Responsible Management Education Measurement Framework (IRMEF) as a multidimensional conceptual evaluation architecture that organises these domains and stakeholder perspectives. Rather than representing an empirically validated measurement model, the IRMEF provides a common conceptual vocabulary for organising existing approaches and guiding future evaluation and empirical validation. It provides a foundation for greater theoretical coherence and methodological consistency while supporting business schools, accreditation bodies, and policymakers seeking more balanced, multidimensional, and contextually appropriate approaches to RME evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Advancing family bonding: A conditional framework from immersion to communitas
abstract: A gap still exists between mobile social media-embedded modern family tourism and family relationship improvement. From a communitas perspective, this study proposes a conditional immersion-communitas relationship improvement framework to address this gap. Evidence from multi-wave surveys, an eye-tracking experiment, focus group interviews, and multiple field experiments shows that: (1) social media notification management is a key precondition for relationship improvement; compared with notification-off, visual, or auditory models, haptic notifications better sustain relationship improvement through the full chain mediation of immersion and communitas; (2) happiness experience type (eudaimonia vs. hedonia) moderates the immersion maintenance mechanism, with hedonia family members relying more on notification management; (3) family structure (intragenerational vs. intergenerational) also moderates the process: the positive effect of communitas on family relationship improvement is stronger in intergenerational families than in intragenerational ones. This study advances understanding of modern family tourism and offers practical implications for both individual management and external intervention. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Adaptive energy management of storage-enabled microgrids using emission-aware demand-side flexibility aggregation
abstract: Microgrids play a key role in distributed energy systems by facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining system reliability, and creating economic value. However, optimising their operation remains challenging, as it requires balancing conflicting objectives under operational constraints. This paper presents a novel customer-centric adaptive microgrid energy management framework using a two-stage ε-constraint multi-objective optimisation approach to balance competing objectives: minimising operational costs and emissions, enhancing technical performance through load factor improvement, and maximising customer benefits via dynamic reward allocation. The proposed two-stage response mechanism, formulated as a non-convex MINLP, exploits the flexibility of both economic- and comfort-oriented consumers within a coordinated system optimisation framework. The first stage models consumer participation using a coefficient of participation (CoP) and an incentive-based structure, enabling significant load adjustments. In the second stage, the microgrid operator exploits the aggregated flexibility of comfort-oriented consumers to solve the multi-objective problem and generate feasible optimal solutions. To improve computational efficiency, this paper reformulates the model as an MIQP using the Big-M method and McCormick relaxation. The framework is validated against real-world data from an Australian grid-connected microgrid. Results indicate that, relative to a no-flexibility baseline, economic-oriented consumers reduce individual energy consumption by up to 33%, with load factor improvements of up to 10%. The analysis also reveals clear trade-offs among the objectives by generating solutions with an average computation time of approximately 3 seconds per feasible solution, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated energy management in balancing technical, economic, and social objectives in microgrid operation. © 2026 The Authors

title: Traditional or simplified Chinese? Exploring the use of linguistic variants in tourism linguistic landscape
abstract: By employing a two-phase mixed-method research design (i.e. survey and interviews), this study investigates residents' and tourists' perceptions of the effectiveness of language variants of Chinese characters in public signage within Macao's tourism landscape. The findings reveal that while simplified Chinese may be favored for its practicality, traditional Chinese retains significant cultural and identity values among residents and enhances the travel experiences by signally authenticity. Additionally, the research highlights perceived cultural erosion among the local community and concerns over prioritizing tourists' needs at the expense of local identity. This study extends linguistic landscape scholarship by illustrating how script variants within a shared language carry distinct practical and symbolic meanings for different stakeholders. Finally, this research proposes an exploratory needs–affect–attachment framework and a theoretically informed model of tourism power relations to conceptualize these dynamics. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Uncovering creative metacognition patterns in TVET innovation education: insight from an epistemic network analysis of students’ self-reflective assessments
abstract: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) increasingly position creativity as a teachable competence in innovation and entrepreneurship education, yet little is known about how Creative Metacognition (CMC) elements are structurally interconnected and activated to facilitate creativity in TVET learners. To address this gap, this study provides an exploratory epistemic network analysis on structural mapping of CMC in TVET innovation and entrepreneurship course. Forty TVET learners completed a three-stage authentic Creative Problem-Solving task focused on venture design for a remote region. Their self-reflective assessments were segmented into 1,506 theory-driven semantic fragments and coded into Creative Strengths (CS), Creative Restrictions (CR), and Creative Contextual Knowledge (CK). Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA) was employed to model the co-activation patterns and relational intensity among CMC elements. Results show that students with high scores exhibited a stronger connection between CS and CK, suggesting that contextual knowledge was framed as creative affordances. In contrast, low-scoring students demonstrated a stronger connection between CR and CK, suggesting that situational reasoning was more often associated with perceived barriers and may reflect constrained idea development despite contextual awareness. The study also provides evidence of associations between reflective CMC configurations and creative performance, offering implications for reflective scaffolding and TVET entrepreneurship task design. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Synergistic strength-ductility in wire arc additive manufacturing of Al-Cu-Mg alloys via Sc microalloying and in-situ multi-scale precipitation
abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) of high-strength 2xxx series Al-Cu-Mg alloys is severely restricted by the intrinsic strength-ductility trade-off, severe mechanical anisotropy, and inadequate microstructure control under non-equilibrium solidification. This work addressed these challenges by developing a novel Sc microalloyed 2024 Al alloy wire and systematically investigating its microstructural evolution and mechanical properties in both as-deposited (AD) and T6-treated conditions. The results indicated that the non-equilibrium solidification during WAAM induced the in-situ transformation of primary Al3Sc into the highly stable Al8Cu4Sc (W-phase) at grain boundaries. The introduction of Sc and Mn synergistically mitigated the conventional bimodal grain structure by inhibiting interlayer recrystallization, reducing the microstructural anisotropy to 9.1%. Following T6 treatment, the intergranular T-phase (Al20Cu2Mn3) networks were largely dissolved and reprecipitated as nanoscale rod-like intragranular T-phase, while the coarse W-phase remained thermally stable at the boundaries. This cross-scale hierarchical microstructure enables a remarkable synergy of strength and ductility. The ultimate tensile strength and yield strength reached 453.0 and 313.9 MPa, respectively, with an extraordinary elongation of 10.1% (a 115% increase compared to the AD conditions). Quantitative calculation indicated that Orowan strengthening from nano-scale T- and W-phases dominated the yield strength (108.2 MPa), while uniform distribution of non-shearable precipitates promoted homogeneous dislocation slip and delayed strain localization, accounting for the improved ductility. This work provides fundamental insight into Sc microalloying in high-Cu Al alloys for WAAM, and offers a facile strategy for developing high-performance additively manufactured aluminum alloys. © 2026

title: A framework for transmission line ice thickness prediction integrating physics-informed feature engineering, attention networks, and causal inference
abstract: Accurate prediction of ice thickness on transmission lines is essential for effective anti-icing and de-icing strategies. Existing methods predominantly rely on "black-box" models lacking physical interpretability, and correlation analysis alone cannot distinguish direct causal effects from mediated transmission among meteorological factors. This paper proposes a three-layer progressive analytical framework for high-altitude heavy-icing sites that integrates physics-informed feature engineering, an attention-based prediction network, and causal inference, progressively addressing prediction accuracy, feature-level interpretability, and causal mechanism discovery. A key finding is the synergistic effect between physics-informed feature engineering and the attention mechanism—neither component alone improves prediction accuracy, yet their combination yields a significant performance gain, with the proposed model achieving competitive performance among deep learning methods. Computational analysis further shows that the proposed model achieves a compact parameter count (12,321) and 40× faster inference than Random Forest, while providing interpretability. SHAP cross-model consistency analysis identifies humidity-related features as the dominant predictors across architecturally distinct models, a conclusion driven by data patterns rather than model bias. Causal inference further reveals that humidity exhibits a nonlinear inverted-U effect on ice thickness (peak at ∼82% RH), temperature serves as a necessary threshold condition, and wind speed exerts a modest direct effect (+0.21 mm/(m/s)) that is not mediated by temperature or humidity. These findings provide a scientific basis for a three-tier icing early-warning framework—temperature gating, humidity severity assessment, and wind intensification—rather than relying on temperature alone. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Voltage fluctuation source localization in distribution systems using a signature-based approach with minimal monitoring points
abstract: Reducing or eliminating voltage fluctuations, a key power quality issue that causes many problems such as flicker, hinges on accurately identifying their sources. The complexity of distribution systems adds further challenges to this task. On the other hand, there is a limitation in providing power quality measurement devices (PQMDs) compared to the number of buses in these systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a simulation-based approach for pinpointing voltage fluctuation sources (VFSs) in distribution systems, specifically for frequencies up to three times the network frequency, using a limited number of PQMDs. The proposed method simulates potential VFS locations and applies a trial-and-error approach, comparing a defined signature from the simulated system with that of the real system to find the closest match to the observed network behavior. Additionally, this method employs a novel carrier signal estimation technique for demodulation and a pulse-wave approximation method for decomposition of rectangular amplitude modulation. To validate the method, simulations were performed under various scenarios on the 15-bus system, the IEEE 33-bus standard test system, and the 70-bus test system. The simulation results demonstrate 99.4%, 97.8%, and 99.5% accuracy in identifying the VFS location in the 15-bus, 33-bus, and 70-bus test systems, respectively, while using only 3, 4, and 14 PQMDs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: From diagnosis to explanation: An integrated framework for examining spatially heterogeneous associations between temporary industrial-land use and neighborhood gentrification
abstract: As Chinese megacities transition to post-industrialism, the socio-spatial consequences of temporary industrial land reuse—a pivotal urban renewal strategy—remain under-theorized. This study integrates Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR), Geodetector, and Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) to examine associations between four functional types of temporary use and a Standardized Gentrification Index (SGI) capturing changes in educational and floating-population composition across 134 Beijing subdistricts. The results reveal differentiated and context-dependent patterns. Technology-oriented use density exhibits a stable and spatially widespread positive association with SGI. Cultural-use area is positively associated with SGI across most subdistricts, whereas cultural-use density is predominantly negative. Production-service area is significant only in a limited set of locations, while consumer-service measures show no statistically significant local MGWR coefficients. Cultural and technology clustering recur as the principal correlates of coefficient heterogeneity, whereas production clustering, transport-accessibility growth, and housing-price change matter in specific relationships. These findings suggest a state-mediated, technology-oriented pathway of demographic upgrading and a more conditional cultural pathway. Methodologically, the framework moves from mapping spatial non-stationarity to interpreting its contextual correlates, providing evidence for differentiated urban-renewal governance. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Embedding ESG, sustainability and ethics in accounting assessment: Bridging global standards and educational practice
abstract: The growing prominence of environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, sustainability, and ethical accountability is reshaping expectations of accounting and management graduates. While these competencies are increasingly embedded within global professional standards and competency frameworks, their translation into educational assessment remains underexplored. This study examines how ESG, sustainability, and ethics are embedded in documented assessment across global standards, professional competency frameworks, and Australian university accounting education. Using qualitative comparative document analysis, the study analyses the International Federation of Accountants’ International Education Standards, the competency frameworks of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and assessment documentation from 104 undergraduate accounting units across 26 Australian universities. The findings reveal partial and uneven alignment. Although sustainability and ethics are explicitly articulated within global and professional frameworks, they are frequently embedded implicitly within technically oriented assessment tasks rather than explicitly assessed as judgement-focused competencies. To explain this pattern, the study introduces the concept of differential assessability, which explains why some professional competencies are more readily translated into assessment than others despite comparable prominence within professional standards. By reframing ESG integration as an assessment design challenge, the study extends assessment theory and offers practical implications for responsible management and accounting education. © 2026

title: Designing ethical negotiation simulations for measurable metacognitive development: Boundary conditions in SCELM
abstract: Ethical negotiation simulations generate strong engagement but often fail to produce measurable metacognitive development in students. This boundary condition design study argues that the problem is structural: many simulation formats are misaligned with the consolidation phase through which disruption becomes learning. We evaluated two implementations of Structured Cross-Cultural Ethical Leadership through Multilateral Negotiations (SCELM): a multicultural rotating format (N = 84 responses; matched n = 26) and a bilateral intercultural format (N = 39; Battle 1 n = 30) across four high-institutional-distance dyads in this study. Paired t-tests and thematic analyses of 124 reflections (κ = 0.81) were conducted in parallel. The rotating format produced no significant within-person changes across any metacognitive index (all d ≤ 0.17). In contrast, the bilateral format generated greater baseline assumption disruption, as indicated by a significant Welch's t-test (p = .028) and marginally higher role tension (p = .063). Qualitative findings showed that perspective revision occurred primarily during structured intra-team consolidation rather than during negotiations, indicating that immediate post-battle surveys underestimate learning. We propose four educator-facing design principles and a dual-timepoint Assurance of Learning protocol, recommending that perspective-shift outcomes be assessed after structured consolidation rather than immediately following negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From influence to empowerment: Unpacking capacity building and social learning in virtual communities
abstract: This study explores how independent travel empowers women travel influencers and how meanings of empowerment are negotiated through interactions with their followers by examining the empowerment process at both individual and social levels. Drawing on capacity building theory and social cognitive theory, it investigates how travel experiences and digital content creation contribute to personal agency, skill development, and socially mediated expressions of empowerment. Using an interpretive paradigm and a netnographic approach, the study analyses the social media practices of 17 female travel influencers. Findings show that independent travel fosters self-efficacy, confidence, and the acquisition of skills and knowledge among influencers, while followers express inspiration, aspiration, identification, and negotiation of constraints in response to shared narratives of empowerment. The study underscores the dynamic interplay among digital influence, community engagement, and gendered empowerment, offering insights into virtual capacity building within contemporary travel cultures. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Consensus and flocking with transmission and reaction delays
abstract: We investigate consensus formation and flocking behavior in multi-agent systems subject to two distinct types of delay: a transmission delay accounting for information exchange between agents, and a reaction delay representing the processing time before agents adjust their states. For a simplified linear two-agent system, we analyze how these delays affect asymptotic stability. We then derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic consensus and flocking in the general multi-agent setting with a nonlinear, globally positive influence function. These conditions require the delays to be sufficiently small relative to the initial data and the decay rate of the influence function. The analysis is based on a Lyapunov functional approach combined with a Grönwall–Halanay-type inequality. Our results establish rigorous sufficient conditions under which collective behavior emerges in delayed multi-agent systems where both communication and reaction lags are non-negligible, with applications to biological, social, and engineered systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Generative AI communications and firm value: Evidence from digital innovation in tourism, travel, and hospitality firms using deep learning
abstract: This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. The final sample includes 177 firms from 2018 to 2024, comprising 68 firms with verified WeChat official accounts and 109 firms retained with zero-valued communication measures. From 105,429 archived posts, we develop a bilingual annotation scheme and supervised deep-learning classifiers to identify GenAI communication and distinguish implementation-salient disclosures from generic mentions. Our preferred measures are share-normalized, capturing both GenAI communication intensity and implementation emphasis relative to total posting activity. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Digital innovation partially mediates this relationship, while industry dynamism and complexity strengthen it, but munificence does not. The study contributes a tourism-specific measure of GenAI capability signaling and clarifies the value relevance of implementation-oriented communication in service-intensive digital contexts. © 2026 The Author.

title: Assessing salinity intrusion risk from coastal flooding through a spatial multi-criteria approach in Satkhira district of Bangladesh
abstract: Bangladesh's coastal zones face compounding threats from climate change, sea-level rise, and the resulting intensification of salinity intrusion, critically jeopardizing freshwater security, agriculture, and local livelihoods. This study presents a spatial multi-criteria analysis using a Geographic Information System (GIS) integrated with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to systematically assess and map the hazard, vulnerability, and exposure dimensions driving flood-induced salinity intrusion risk in Satkhira District. The comprehensive assessment utilized 17 thematic criteria, revealing distinct spatial patterns of susceptibility. The Hazard analysis demonstrated that 35.21% of the total area is classified under the combined High and Very High zones, predominantly concentrated in the south-western and south-eastern coastal areas. The biophysical vulnerability assessment indicated a high degree of intrinsic sensitivity, with 36.59% of the district categorized as very highly vulnerable. Conversely, the Exposure analysis identified a substantial 28.19% of the land as highly and very highly exposed, reflecting the high density of valuable assets even in inland Upazilas. The final composite risk map reveals that 27.95% of the study area is subjected to either high or very high salinity intrusion risk, with the highest risk observed in Satkhira sadar. These empirically derived risk maps and quantitative findings offer crucial, evidence-based insights for policymakers, providing a foundational tool for the design and implementation of targeted adaptation strategies, sustainable land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction programs in vulnerable deltaic environments globally. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Comparative assessment of distribution network robustness against wind and solar uncertainties using information gap decision theory
abstract: To address the challenges posed by source‑load multiple uncertainties to the stable operation of power systems, this paper explores adaptive control strategies for energy storage system (ESS) and investigates differences in system sensitivity to uncertainties in wind and solar power generation. Based on Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) for uncertainty quantification, a three-layer robust optimization model is formulated to maximize the uncertainty radius under a predefined power loss target. By incorporating the worst condition defined as minimized power generation coupled with maximized load, the original three-layer model is converted into a two-layer model for efficient solution. Furthermore, the Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm (RVEA) is employed to solve the model, obtaining a Pareto solution set that reflects the trade‑off between robustness and economy. Simulations based on the IEEE 33‑bus system demonstrate that ESS forms differentiated charging and discharging strategies for different operating scenarios, and the system exhibits higher sensitivity to wind power fluctuations. These results verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in identifying uncertainty impact pathways and optimizing ESS strategies. © 2026

title: Designing a Data-Driven E-Learning Module for Teaching English to Young Learners: Integrating Needs Analysis and the ISAV Learning Model
abstract: This study designed a data-driven e-learning module for Teaching English to Young Learners by integrating needs analysis with the Interactive, Somatic, Auditory, and Visual learning model. Using a design-based research approach, the study focused on the analysis and design phases. Data were collected from elementary school English teachers and pre-service English teachers through a structured questionnaire addressing necessities, lacks, and wants. The findings identified vocabulary, reading, and oral communication as key learning necessities, alongside difficulties in sentence structure and broader instructional constraints. Respondents also preferred interactive and multimodal learning activities. These findings informed an ISAV-based e-learning module prototype integrating interactive, somatic, auditory, and visual features to support learner-centered, multimodal, and contextually responsive English instruction for young learners in digital environments. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Hand clearances in ergonomic design: A scoping review of types, methods, and measurements
abstract: Hand clearances, the space available for hand access and operation, are essential for manual workspace design. However, clearance types lack systematic characterization, unified methods, and standardized criteria for defining adequate space during manual tasks. This scoping review analyzed 26 records published between 1960 and 2026. Ninety-four unique clearances were identified and organized into four categories: Openings, Operational Clearances, Object-Specific Clearances, and PPE Allowances. Four methodological approaches and eight methodological gaps were identified, including reliance on static measurements, inadequate treatment of PPE, small or outdated samples, and limited reporting standards. Widely cited clearance values originate from small, demographically narrow 1960s studies and have propagated with limited re-validation. The review introduces the functional clearance margin as a conceptual proposition describing the additional space beyond hand dimensions required for functional operation rather than fit alone. These findings provide a foundation for developing more representative, dynamic, and standardized approaches to hand clearance design. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modeling the propagation of risk in large-scale power outages: Integrating ETA, directed-weighted CN, and risk chain mining
abstract: To understand the systemic propagation and interdependencies of various risk factors in large-scale power outages, a novel risk evolution framework is proposed, incorporating Event Tree Analysis (ETA), directed-weighted Complex Network (CN), and risk chain mining. A network comprising 37 nodes and 130 edges is constructed using data from 29 large-scale power outages spanning from 1965 to 2025. Topological analysis identifies critical propagation nodes, including power plant failures and grid instability. Robustness tests reveal the network's resilience to random disruptions but also expose its vulnerability to targeted attacks. Furthermore, high-risk causal chains are directly extracted and classified from the network, and path mining further uncovers 24 high-risk six-node chains, which are categorized into four distinct propagation patterns. This integrated framework offers a data-driven methodology for characterizing large-scale power outage risks, yielding structurally suggestive priorities to inform prevention and mitigation strategies for power systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Workplace management of musculoskeletal and mental health risks: translating evidence into practice
abstract: There is a large body of research evidence identifying the biomechanical and psychosocial hazards that can affect work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and stress-related mental health problems (MHPs). The APHIRM Toolkit was developed to facilitate more effective translation of this evidence into workplace risk management practices. Using APHIRM survey data from three occupations in the healthcare sector, this project compared hazard ‘riskiness’ profiles: (a) at occupational versus local workgroup levels, and (b) using hazard constructs versus individual hazard items. It was concluded that effective risk management is likely to require: risk assessment and prioritisation of control actions separately for each local workgroup; assessment of specific hazards rather than the generic constructs used by researchers. Results highlight the value of managing MSD and MHP risks together, because both were affected by both psychosocial and biomechanical hazards in combinations that varied widely between workgroups. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Urbanisation, gender vulnerability, and ecovocation among migrant women in prostitution
abstract: This study examines how rapid metropolitan transformation in Jakarta produces structural vulnerability and social inequality among female migrants involved in covert sexual labour within the SPA industry. It investigates the relevance of the right to the city and an eco-vocational educational approach within Population and Environmental Education as critical frameworks for understanding exclusion, agency, and citizenship. Using a qualitative multi-sited case study design, the research draws on in-depth interviews, limited participant observation, and document analysis involving women workers, SPA managers, community actors, civil society representatives, and policymakers. The data were analysed thematically through critical urban studies and feminist perspectives. The findings show that women's involvement in covert sexual labour cannot be understood simply as an individual moral failure or fully voluntary decision. Rather, it reflects constrained agency shaped by unequal labour markets, limited educational capital, family economic responsibilities, debt relations, migration pressures, and regulatory ambiguity surrounding the SPA sector. Participants experienced layered forms of exploitation, symbolic violence, stigma, and disconnected citizenship: they contributed to the city's informal service economy but remained socially marginalised, politically unrecognised, and institutionally underprotected. Urban governance practices tended to intensify this vulnerability by emphasising surveillance, raids, and moral regulation rather than social protection, labour justice, and inclusive public policy. The study argues that the right to the city offers a useful analytical lens for revealing spatial injustice and the denial of substantive citizenship among marginalised women. It further proposes eco-vocational education as a transformative framework for restoring dignity, strengthening capabilities, expanding livelihood alternatives, and promoting more inclusive, just, and humane urban futures. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Energy transition materials, climate knowledge, and the imagined supply chain: Escaping the productive paradox of necessary mining
abstract: Much scholarship, public discourse, and policymaking on ‘energy transition materials’ (ETMs) imagines a supply chain from material production to climate mitigation, despite the absence of any mechanism ensuring that mined materials will become an electrification technology, let alone replace fossil fuels or avoid warming impacts. Scholarship about energy transition material (ETM) discourse, including criticism, largely neglects this material-discursive contradiction and truncates final analyses to paradoxes productive toward extractive futures. Leveraging a review of 99 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013-2025, this article brings mining scholarship into conversation with climate knowledge politics. It charts the dematerialization of climate knowledge from warming impacts to values negotiated along three spectra (urgency, scale, and sacrifice) and rematerialization reflected in extractive rationales (developmental, Indigenous rights, nature, and futures). Most ETM discourse is enclosed in three narrative boundaries, which lean on the imagined supply chain and foreclose non-extractive possibilities: (1) The contingencies that link climate policy and mining, such as materials science, technological manufacturing and use, are taken for granted; (2) Scalar formulations separate and compare anthropogenic climate change and mining impacts; and (3) ETMs wield climate knowledge itself as a supply chain, dialectically illustrating a problem to its own solution. Pathways to overcome the boundaries can center the materiality of mining and climate change over the abstractions of supply chains and imagined climate benefits, critically reflect on the relationships between material production and technopolitical knowledge, and take seriously actually occurring alternative livelihoods. © 2026 The Authors.

title: LLM-agent-based explicit-implicit interaction fusion for human-robot collaborative Assembly
abstract: In human-robot collaboration (HRC), explicit and implicit interactions typically follow distinct workflows: explicit interactions are actively initiated by the operator to convey task objectives, while implicit interactions are continuously perceived and responded to by the system to adapt robot behavior to the current collaboration context. Existing HRC systems often handle these interaction types separately, lacking a unified cognitive and decision-making mechanism, which can lead to interaction conflicts, execution interruptions, or delayed safety responses in complex scenarios. Although large language models (LLMs) demonstrate tremendous potential in reasoning, they have yet to effectively integrate explicit and implicit interactions into robotic decision-making. To address this, this paper proposes an LLM-Agent-based framework for explicit-implicit interaction fusion, which models both types of input within a unified semantic space and incorporates a two-stage fusion decision mechanism in LLM reasoning. This framework helps robots maintain consistent responses to task objectives and mitigate potential collaborative safety risks. Preliminary small-scale experimental results on representative HRC tasks reveal favorable trends in task completion ratio, collaborative safety performance and decision consistency when compared with the baseline scheme without explicit-implicit fusion. The proposed method provides an interpretable and scalable approach for deploying LLM-based HRC systems in real-world settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Numerical approximation in discrete portfolio optimization using DeFi as a new asset frontier: Risk contribution and correlation dynamics in a minimum-risk portfolio
abstract: The introduction of decentralized finance (DeFi) as an innovative asset class necessitates a reevaluation of the conventional framework for portfolio optimization. Traditional continuous-time models are challenged by the complex and non-linear features of DeFi tokens, such as discontinuous trading, high volatility, heteroskedasticity, and regime-switching behavior. The use of numerical approximation is examined in this article, optimizing portfolios with discrete techniques, including DeFi assets in a framework with low risk. We use and compare several optimization techniques, such as mean variance, Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and a number of Risk Parity (RP) strategies are at the core of our analysis. We used a dataset of ten well-known DeFi tokens for our empirical investigation. DeFi tokens from 2021 to 2024 show a fundamental trade-off. Concentration-based models (mean-variance and CVaR) generate highly concentrated weights portfolios, leading to extreme volatility, large drawdowns, and prohibitively high portfolio turnover, which would be severely affected by real DeFi transaction fees, such as gas fees. In contrast, Risk Parity models consistently demonstrate superior practical performance. They produce well-diversified portfolios that deliver smoother results and significantly lower compound return paths and more stable rolling volatility and drastically reduced turnover. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Impact of Livelihood Capital on Farmers’ Adoption of Sustainable Crop Residue Management Practices: Empirical Evidence from Punjab Province, Pakistan
abstract: Sustainable crop residue management can increase agricultural productivity and reduce farming-related carbon emissions, yet adoption of sustainable crop residue management practices (SCRMPs) remains limited. This study investigates how farmers’ livelihood capital shapes SCRMP adoption in Punjab, Pakistan, using survey data from 500 farmers in three agro-ecological zones. A multivariate probit model, weighted with the entropy-TOPSIS method, estimates the effects of human, social, natural, physical, and financial capital on practices including on-farm use, livestock feed, residue retention, and biogas production. Human, social, financial, and physical capital positively influence on-farm residue use, while all five forms of capital significantly promote biogas production. Although livestock feed remains the most common use, many farmers are willing to adopt alternatives such as biofertilizer production and biogas. These findings indicate substantial potential to expand sustainable residue management in the region. Policymakers should prioritize farmer training, credit access, rural infrastructure, biogas technologies, extension services, and farmer cooperatives to encourage environmentally and economically sustainable practices. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Balancing the mechanical-corrosion performance via the in-situ alloying effects of commercial Al-Mg and Al-Zn powders during additive manufacturing
abstract: Corrosion-mechanical performance trade-off is a key issue for engineering application of Al-Mg alloy. The main restriction is the contradicted performance variation and sensitization phenomenon. Current research has achieved prominent progress in performance optimization of casting Al-Mg alloy, by in-situ alloying, post treatment, etc. Whereas, the performance evolution in hot-spot additive manufacturing still needs systematic study. More importantly, the performance is vitally sensitive to microstructure variation, and their intrinsic mechanism still needs clearer elucidation. This work attempts to testify the influence of microstructure evolution on the strengthening-corrosion behaviors. Herein, an economic and efficient alloying approach is adopted by coupling commercial Al-Zn/Al-Mg system. The cooperation of Al3(Sc,Zr) and low-brittleness T-Mg32(Al,Zn,Cu)49 suppresses the sensitization effects and harmonizes the strengthen-deformation behaviors. Therefore, the novel Al-Mg-Zn-Cu alloy achieves a yield strength of 420.4 MPa and an elongation of 11.4%, and they retain 310.9 MPa and 29.4% at 200 °C, respectively. Moreover, the microstructure can restrain intergranular corrosion and promote pitting homogeneity. Zn addition promotes the passive film densifying, and T-phase shows a standard potential close to matrix, thus lowering the corrosion tendency. By regulating the plastic deformation-corrosion behaviors, the comprehensive performance is improved. The findings can provide a supplement for the performance regulation theory of Al-Mg alloy. © 2026

title: Genesis and evolution of metaverses as socio-technological realities; [پیدایش و تکامل متاورس در جایگاه واقعیتی اجتماعی و فناورانه]
abstract: This article focuses on exploring the evolution of metaverses as socio-technological virtual spaces, which, with further development, will lead to the growth of existing or potentially new forms of social interaction. Approaches to defining the key characteristics and stages of metaverse development are considered. Various forms of social activity within metaverses are analyzed with reference to specific examples, such as political activity, economic activity, and the implementation of socio-cultural projects. The article is based on a systemic analysis that enables the consideration of the technological and social aspects of metaverse development in their interrelation and dynamics, as well as scenario analysis to predict future forms of social interaction in virtual spaces. The emergence of increasingly new forms of social interaction may lead to the manifestation of a confrontational political potential, expressed in virtual protests, rallies, calls for a change of power, etc. The derived conclusions highlight the importance of developing inclusive mechanisms and models for managing and regulating metaverses in terms of social, public, and political risks. © 2026, University of Tehran. .

title: Beyond Digitalization: A Conceptual and Institutional Framework for Digital Transformation in Higher Education
abstract: Digital transformation in higher education has emerged as a strategic priority for universities worldwide over the past decade. Despite the rapid growth of scholarly interest in this field, the existing literature remains conceptually fragmented, disproportionately focused on technological aspects, and limited in providing integrated frameworks to guide digital transformation processes. This study aims to systematically synthesize the digital transformation literature in higher education, identify dominant trends, key dimensions, challenges, and research gaps, and develop an integrated conceptual framework to address these limitations. Using a systematic literature review approach in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, 145 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2026 were analyzed. Data were examined through systematic content analysis across multiple levels, including temporal and geographical trends, methodological characteristics, thematic classifications, and conceptual integration of findings. The results reveal a clear shift in the literature from technology-centered perspectives toward a multidimensional, institutional, and strategic understanding of digital transformation in higher education. Three interrelated dimensions, digital technologies and infrastructure, human resources and digital skills, and leadership, culture, and policy were identified as the core components of effective digital transformation. The findings further highlight persistent research gaps related to organizational readiness, institutional implications, change management, and the contextual localization of digital transformation frameworks, particularly in developing country contexts. In response to these gaps, this study proposes an integrated conceptual framework that conceptualizes digital transformation in higher education as a dynamic four-stage process encompassing readiness and assessment, pilot implementation, scaling and integration, and continuous optimization and innovation. The proposed framework offers both an analytical foundation for future research and a practical reference for university leaders and policymakers seeking to design and implement sustainable digital transformation initiatives. © 2027 The author(s). title: Hierarchically woven covalent organic framework hydrogels with programmable hydrogen-binding domains for adaptive human–machine interfaces
abstract: Hydrogels are among the most promising materials for wearable sensors in human–machine interaction, but the pursuit of high mechanical strength and resilience in hydrogels often leads to a trade-off with conductivity, which significantly limits their practical applications; thereby, balancing energy dissipation and ion transport in hydrogels remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop molecularly woven hydrogels by non-covalently threading linear polymers into thiadiazole-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs), in which the thiadiazole dihydrazide units in the COFs function as hydrogen-binding domains, fostering multiple non-covalent interactions between the COFs and linear polymers. This unique configuration facilitates energy dissipation while simultaneously enhancing ion transport. The resulting hydrogels exhibit a tensile strength of 0.41 MPa, resilience of 99%, an ionic conductivity of 1.27 ± 0.18 S m−1, and limited crack propagation, ranking among the highest values reported for hydrogel materials. Furthermore, the hydrogel-based sensor demonstrates a rapid strain response of 12.5 ms, excellent cyclic stability, and superior environmental weatherability, enabling accurate monitoring of human activities and gesture recognition for dexterous robotic manipulation. This work holds great promise for developing intelligent human-machine interfaces to perform dangerous and high-precision tasks. © 2026

abstract: The study provides compelling evidence of why a children dimension should be included in hospitality and tourism curriculum. Having said that, the suggested development of hospitality and tourism education curriculum is coming with challenges such as the emergence of hidden curriculum and opportunities such as augmented profile of students.
