title: Modelling and Solving Problems of Sustainable Efficiency of Technological Processes in Metallurgy; [Металлургиядағы технологиялық процестердің тұрақты тиімділігі мәселелерін модельдеу және шешу]; [Моделирование и решение задач устойчивой эффективности технологических процессов в металлургии]
abstract: Through a comparative analysis, this study investigates the development, simulation, and application of mathematical models for integrated analysis of copper rod production in order to improve product quality, reduce costs, and minimize risks. The purpose of this article is achieved by creating mathematical descriptions of real processes, which are then used to conduct computer experiments. In contrast to the traditional molecular dynamic methods, this study used information technology to obtain the characteristics of the flow field in technological equipment. The novelty lies in: integration of thermomechanical modeling with an optimization algorithm; introduction of a criterion minimizing mechanical property variation; consideration of reduction and redistribution effects on roll wear; possibility of adaptive real-time control. An information analysis of the profiles of copper melt flow velocities in a wide range of temperatures in the Copper Rod Production Plant Kazkat is presented. Information Technology fulfils the need to address the problem of determining the optimal values of temperature, rolling speed, and other parameters to achieve the best quality and productivity of copper rod production processes. Based on these findings, this study proposes the optimization directions for the temperature field profile in the rolling rolls, which leads to a decrease in roll wear and an increase in the uniformity of the wire rod structure, focusing on improving microstructural properties. © 2028, Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation JSC. .

title: Business simulation games and ethical decision making confidence and intentions: The role of self-efficacy, reflective practice, and teamwork
abstract: This study examines the potential associations between experiential learning via participating in a business simulation game and business students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. While simulation games have been widely recognized for their effectiveness in developing business competencies, their associations with ethical decision making confidence and intentions in a non-ethics related environment remain underexplored. Drawing on Kolb's experiential learning theory, we carried out a quantitative survey with the use of a structured questionnaire. We collected data from 251 undergraduate students in a UK university and analyzed them using structural equation modeling. Our findings suggest that participation in simulation games is associated with higher levels of students' teamwork and reflective practice capabilities that, in turn, were found to be positively associated with their ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Moreover, students who participated in simulation games reported higher self-efficacy which, however, was not found to have a significant relationship with ethical decision-making confidence and intentions. Our findings highlight the potential value of integrating experiential learning tools, such as simulation games, into business education suggesting an association with improvements in students' ethical decision making confidence and intentions. Theoretical and practical implications for researchers, universities, and practitioners are discussed. © 2026 The Authors

title: Seven Sisters tourism under siege: Hybrid neural insights into stakeholder resilience
abstract: Tourism stakeholders in insurgency-affected destinations navigate persistent insecurity that shapes their perceptions, adaptive behavior, and support for tourism in nonlinear ways. This study investigates how security-related perceptions influence tourism support in Northeast India's Seven Sisters region, a politically fragile zone characterized by prolonged insurgency. Using a mixed-method hybrid design, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), artificial neural network (ANN) modeling, sensitivity analysis, and content analysis were applied to 584 stakeholder surveys and 25 in-depth interviews. EFA identified four latent constructs: security forces concern, moral panic, social stability, and cognitive concern, which collectively explain 57% of tourism support variance. ANN modeling revealed a nonlinear inverted-U relationship between security visibility and stakeholder support, interpreted as a “ security-skepticism dilemma” grounded in Prospect Theory. Security forces concern (35%) and moral panic (24%) were the most influential predictors. These findings advance tourism resilience theory and provide actionable governance guidance for conflict-affected destinations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Congestion management in electric distribution systems through flexibility services: a bibliometric and analytical review
abstract: Electricity systems are rapidly evolving toward decentralized architectures with high shares of variable renewable energy sources and distributed energy resources (DERs), increasing congestion in medium- and low-voltage networks. This paper presents a structured mixed-source review combining bibliometric mapping and targeted analytical synthesis on flexibility services for congestion management in electric distribution systems. Analysis of the quality-controlled Q3 corpus (n = 1827) identifies China as the leading national contributor and substantial collective European participation, with 79.6% of records published from 2018 onward. Author-keyword mapping reveals five streams: distribution-network optimization, market-based congestion management, uncertainty-aware active-network operation, flexibility-service coordination, and demand-response smart-grid control. Novelty lies in keeping the validated bibliometric corpus separate from an independently assembled, question-driven evidence base until interpretation. The analytical synthesis shows that distributed locational marginal pricing (DLMP), particularly in iterative formulations, can internalize network constraints and provide locational signals for DER coordination, although its effectiveness depends on adequate network modeling, uncertainty treatment, and flexible-demand participation. The review also identifies converging trends toward multilayer coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs), local flexibility procurement, and digital platforms for ancillary-service provision. Across jurisdictions, explicit remuneration, interoperable data, and coordinated governance recur, but uneven implementation precludes causal comparisons or effectiveness rankings. The paper concludes by identifying research gaps related to cost–benefit validation, regulatory standardization, data interoperability, and large-scale implementation in distribution systems. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: How autonomy-supportive environments and growth mindset foster creativity efficacy in middle school students? Evidence from a large-scale survey in China
abstract: This study examines the associations between multi-source autonomy-supportive environments, growth mindset, and creative self-efficacy among Chinese middle school students, with particular attention to the mediating role of growth mindset and individual heterogeneity in these associations. Using large-scale survey data from 6146 middle school students in Suzhou, China, and drawing on Bandura's (1997) social cognitive theory and Self-Determination Theory, we employed structural equation modeling and quantile regression to investigate these relationships. The SEM results indicate that teacher, parental, and peer autonomy support are all positively associated with creative self-efficacy, with teacher and peer support showing stronger total associations than parental support. Growth mindset mediated all three associations, with the indirect effect proportion being highest for teacher autonomy support, followed by parental autonomy support and peer autonomy support. Quantile regression analyses revealed meaningful heterogeneity across the creative self-efficacy distribution: teacher and parental autonomy support showed stronger associations at lower quantiles, peer autonomy support peaked at moderate quantiles, and all associations weakened at higher quantiles. These findings contribute to the cross-cultural understanding of how multi-source autonomy-supportive environments relate to creative self-efficacy in a collectivist educational context, and offer practical implications for differentiated educational interventions targeting students at different levels of creative self-efficacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
abstract: Generative AI tools can now create photorealistic destination images at low cost, yet whether such images motivate travel as effectively as human-generated images remains unclear. Drawing on the heuristic-systematic model, this research examines differences between AI-generated and human-generated tourism images through three studies. Study 1 shows that AI-generated images receive higher ratings of perceived aesthetics but lower ratings of perceived authenticity, narrative transportation, and visit intention than human-generated images. Study 2 identifies 19 computable visual indicators across three dimensions and finds that AI-generated images exhibit stronger visual schema characteristics, whereas human-generated images show richer visual structure. Study 3 uses XGBoost and SHAP analysis to identify the visual features associated with different psychological responses. These findings connect computational visual analysis with tourism consumer research by identifying differences in audience responses to AI-generated and human-generated images and the visual features associated with those responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Feelings of ease in generating ideas: My loyal companion that guides my mental action but does not help me generate more creative ideas
abstract: The ability to generate creative ideas is an important skill for education. This study examined how feelings of ease in generating ideas act as a cue that allowed individuals to have information to monitor their mental action and make important metacognitive decisions while generating creative ideas. Participants were asked to generate four ideas to help deal with the problem of empty work offices during and after the pandemic of COVID-19. After generating each idea, participants reported their feelings of ease and evaluated the creativity of each idea. Participants then reported their confidence in the ideas generated and selected their most creative idea. Results showed negative, curvilinear trajectories of feelings of ease and self-evaluations of the creativity of each idea. Feelings of ease in generating ideas were positively related to self-evaluations and the decisions to continue generating ideas and negatively related to choosing the first idea as the most creative. In addition, feelings of ease were indirectly and positively related to post-task confidence through their relationship with self-evaluations. These findings provided initial, empirical evidence that feelings of ease acted as cues to inform relevant judgments and decisions in the process of ideation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Modified DEA-SBM efficiency-based diversion risk proxy assessment with peer similarity for decision support in aircraft diversion management
abstract: Aircraft diversion is a critical component of aviation safety management, requiring close coordination among pilots, air traffic controllers, and airline operations teams. Although established procedures guide the process, diversions remain complex and time-sensitive due to operational and logistical constraints, and there is no universal framework for selecting the most suitable alternate airport. This paper proposes a decision support system to assist diversion decision-making through a modified data envelopment analysis–slack-based measure (DEA-SBM) efficiency-based proxy model. The model evaluates the efficiency-based diversion risk proxy (EDRP) index for airports using relevant input and output variables associated with the diversion process. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, three real diversion cases in the Philippines are used as baseline scenarios. The resulting model outputs are consistent with the actual diversion decisions implemented in operational practice. This alignment provides empirical support that the model can function as a reliable decision support tool for diversion management, particularly in replicating observed operational judgment under real-world constraints. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Task value, effort regulation and critical thinking: Towards a unified learning configuration in financial management education
abstract: Financial Management requires students to integrate motivational, behavioural, and cognitive competencies to solve financial problems. However, existing research has predominantly examined these learner characteristics independently, providing limited understanding of how they coexist to shape learning. This study adopted a person-centred approach to identify distinct learning configurations based on task value, effort regulation, and critical thinking among Business students studying Financial Management. A cross-sectional survey design was employed to collect data from 168 students using validated measures, and Latent Profile Analysis identified naturally occurring learning profiles. Four distinct learning configurations emerged: Low Learning Orientation (10.1%), Developing Learning Orientation (11.9%), Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation (31.0%), and Integrated Learning Configuration (47.0%). The Integrated Learning Configuration represented the largest group. Notably, the Motivated but Cognitively Emerging Orientation profile reflected students with stronger task value and effort regulation relative to critical thinking. This finding suggests that valuing learning and regulating effort alone may be insufficient for developing higher-order financial reasoning. Profile membership differed by programme of study but not by sex or age. The study advances management education by conceptualising learning in Financial Management as an integrated configuration of motivational, behavioural, and cognitive dimensions rather than isolated learner characteristics, informing pedagogical connoisseurship in practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Data-driven calibration sample selection and forecast combination in electricity price forecasting: An application of the ARHNN method
abstract: Calibration sample selection and forecast combination are two simple yet powerful tools used in forecasting. They can be combined with a variety of models to significantly improve prediction accuracy, at the same time offering easy implementation and low computational complexity. While their effectiveness has been repeatedly confirmed in prior scientific literature, the topic is still underexplored in the field of electricity price forecasting. In this research article we apply the Autoregressive Hybrid Nearest Neighbors (ARHNN) method to three long-term time series describing the German, Spanish and New England electricity markets. We show that it outperforms popular literature benchmarks in terms of forecast accuracy by up to 10%. We also propose two simplified variants of the method, granting a vast decrease in computation time with only minor loss of prediction accuracy. Finally, we compare the forecasts’ performance in a battery storage system trading case study and propose a new automated trading strategy. We find that using a forecast-driven strategy can consistently achieve a substantial share of theoretical maximum profits while trading, demonstrating business value in practical applications. © 2026

title: Gender Representation and Intercultural Competence in Iranian EFL Coursebooks from the 1960s to 2020s
abstract: This study aims to investigate the representation of gender and intercultural competence in the images and texts of 15 Iranian secondary school English coursebooks, published over six decades. Gender representation was investigated using the framework proposed by Dahmardeh and Kim (2020), and the scale developed by Solhaug and Kristensen (2020) was used as the criteria for investigating intercultural competence. The data were coded and counted using manifest content analysis. The results showed that Iranian English coursebooks mentioned males and females unequally in their texts across different decades, with one gender being represented more in each decade. Regarding gender representation in the images, males were represented more than females in almost all decades. The representation of males and females in the books published in the 1970s was almost equal, followed by extreme and sudden changes in gender representation in the 1980s. However, the books published in and after the 2000s presented a balanced picture of males and females. The coursebooks dealt with intercultural competence in their texts and images very rarely, limiting this concept to religious issues and neglecting other aspects. In fact, the coursebooks addressed only one category out of the 11 categories. Finally, the study ends with implications for coursebook authors, materials designers, teachers, students, and teacher trainers. © 2027, Tarbiat Modares University. .

title: Perceived social entrepreneurship education and entrepreneurial intention in times of crisis: Where moral obligation matters
abstract: Social entrepreneurship education is widely promoted; however, the reflection of students' educational experience in social entrepreneurial intention remains insufficiently understood, particularly in institutionally fragile contexts. Drawing on survey data from 299 Lebanese university students, this study tests a moderated mediation model grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). Specifically, it examines whether personal attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control mediate the relationship between students' perceived social entrepreneurship education experience and entrepreneurial intention, and whether moral obligation conditions these pathways. More positive perceptions of the educational experience are associated with stronger intention indirectly through personal attitude and perceived behavioural control, while subjective norms show no significant effect, reflecting weakened normative reference points under prolonged crisis. Moral obligation operates selectively, strengthening the attitudinal pathway while leaving the control and the normative pathways unchanged. This study extends the mediated view of educational influence to social entrepreneurship education in a crisis setting, suggests that moral obligation may function as a conditional ethical amplifier, and shows how institutional fragility can affect the salient dimensions of TPB. In fragile settings, such education should cultivate reflective attitudes and moral engagement alongside structural reforms that enable normative support for socially oriented careers. © 2026

title: Emotional preferences in LoRA-driven AI-generated urban vitality spaces: A study using discrete choice models
abstract: China's transition toward urban stock renewal has heightened the focus on the emotional quality of urban vitality spaces. While AI generative design offers new approaches, whether AI-generated images as visual representations for specific spaces can meet people's emotional needs remains insufficiently examined. This study examines whether AI-generated visual representations of such spaces evoke image-based emotional preferences comparable to those for real photographs, and identifies which spatial attributes drive these preferences. Using THE BOX in Beijing as a case, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)-fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models generated visual representations of seven chosen scenes. Emotional preferences were measured through validated scales completed by 115 participants. A discrete choice model was used to compare participants' preferences between photographs of the real space and AI-generated images and identified influential attributes. Results showed that participants with design-related backgrounds preferred real photographs. Positive affect toward AI-generated images was the strongest predictor of preference. Real-scene color, natural elements, and uniqueness reduced the odds of choosing AI-generated versions, whereas AI-generated form and structure, natural elements, and changeability increased them. The study contributes a replicable workflow linking generative AI with emotional preference measurement, offering a structured approach for evidence-based design review. The findings are preliminary due to the single case, modest sample, and reliance on static images. Future work should extend to diverse urban contexts and multimodal evaluation. © 2026 The Authors.

title: A bibliometric and systematic analysis of artificial intelligence and the transition towards smart geotourism
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of tourism has positioned artificial intelligence as a key enabler of destination intelligence, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable tourism management. Although artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in smart tourism research, its application to geotourism remains fragmented, particularly regarding geoheritage conservation, geodiversity management, and territorial planning. Employing a retrospective approach, this study delineates the developmental trajectory of artificial intelligence applications in sustainable tourism while interrogating their integration into the paradigm of smart geotourism. An integrated bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review were conducted to evaluate scientific developments and empirical applications of artificial intelligence within geotourism contexts. Such findings delineate a burgeoning field of inquiry structured through the convergence of three intersecting axes: technological advancement, analytical intelligence, and visitor-focused experiential paradigms. The review study identified four principal domains through which artificial intelligence contributes to geotourism: predictive analytics, smart destination management, geoheritage interpretation, and environmental monitoring and geoconservation. The findings further highlight significant regional differences in technological adoption and reveal a limited integration between artificial intelligence, geoheritage conservation, and sustainable territorial governance. Based on these findings, the study proposes a smart geotourism framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning within a unified conceptual structure. By delivering an integrated appraisal of artificial intelligence within geotourism, this study contributes to extant scholarship by conceptualizing artificial intelligence beyond its technical dimensions—positioning it as a fundamental enabler of empirical territorial planning, destination analytics, and the sustainable preservation of geological resources. The study objectives were to propose an integrated conceptual framework that connects artificial intelligence, smart tourism, geoheritage conservation, and territorial planning to support the development of smart geotourism. © 2027 The author(s). title: Scenic spot crowd flow prediction: Combining large language model semantic understanding and spatio-temporal network
abstract: Accurate forecasting of tourist flows is crucial for urban planning, transportation management, and overcrowding prevention. Tourism demand is highly sensitive to external stimuli, often leading to abrupt and irregular fluctuations that are difficult to quantify using existing methods. To address this issue, we propose an event-aware dynamic spatiotemporal network (EAD-STN) that integrates large language model embeddings with dynamic spatiotemporal graph modeling. External factors are encoded into high-dimensional representations to capture their impacts on visitor demand. The model further incorporates both dynamic spatial adjacency and LLM-derived semantic adjacency among attractions, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of inter-attraction relationships. Experiments on real-world datasets from Beijing and Shanghai demonstrate that EAD-STN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. By leveraging large language models to quantify complex external influences and semantic relationships, this framework provides a new perspective for improving the accuracy and interpretability of tourism flow forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Silent Valleys: Unraveling the Causes and Strategic Pathways for Reverse Migration in Hilly Regions of Uttarakhand
abstract: This study examines out-migration and the prospects for sustainable reverse migration in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand, addressing three objectives: identifying the main drivers of migration, synthesizing reinforcement strategies to reduce distress migration and support return, and linking causes and responses within a human-environment systems perspective. We conducted a scoping review of 68 studies (2010–2025) using a structured screening and synthesis process. Findings show that migration results from interacting economic, infrastructural, geographical, policy, and social pressures rather than a single employment factor, with reinforcing feedback effects such as land abandonment, declining agricultural viability, weakened local services, and heightened human-wildlife conflict that can intensify future migration. The study synthesizes an evidence-graded portfolio of interventions: livelihood diversification, agri-value-chain strengthening, digital access and skills, climate-resilient infrastructure, community-based and eco-tourism, and improved local service delivery and governance support, contributing an integrated conceptual framework linking drivers, feedback loops, and intervention levers for coordinated, place-based mountain-region planning. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Mapping the intellectual structure of digital transformation research in SMEs: A decade of performance-oriented studies
abstract: Despite their vital contribution to worldwide economic progress, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vulnerable to environmental fluctuations, resource limitations, and swift technological shifts. In this context, digital transformation has emerged as a critical strategic mechanism through which firms seek to enhance competitiveness, resilience, and organizational outcomes. Although this topic has attracted considerable scholarly attention in recent years, the available literature is dispersed across different academic fields, theoretical viewpoints, and methodologies, making it difficult to gain a holistic understanding of the area's intellectual organization and progression. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to examine digital transformation and firm-level outcomes in small business contexts from January 2016 to January 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix through its Biblioshiny interface and VOSviewer. A final dataset of 186 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined using descriptive statistics, keyword co-occurrence analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation analysis, thematic mapping, and research trend analysis. The results indicate a strong and accelerating publication trend, with an annual growth rate of 17.46, particularly since 2020, highlighting the increasing strategic importance of digital technologies in response to economic disruptions and uncertainty. The analysis identifies four major thematic clusters: (1) performance-oriented outcomes, (2) technology - and capability-driven transformation, (3) organizational and sustainability-related performance, and (4) strategic and Industry 4.0-oriented transformation. In addition, emerging themes include digital readiness, dynamic capabilities, and business model innovation. While the literature frequently associates digital transformation with improved organizational outcomes, the findings also reveal persistent heterogeneity in results and highlight substantial risks and failure rates, especially among resource-constrained firms. By mapping the intellectual foundations, thematic structure, and evolution of this research domain, the study provides an integrative overview that supports theory development and informs future empirical research. The results also offer valuable insights for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers who seek to understand and guide digital transformation initiatives in small business contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: The impact of technological developments on the changing role of HR(M): A scoping review and research agenda
abstract: Due to technological developments, jobs disappear, new jobs arise, and existing jobs change. This leads to opportunities and challenges regarding human resource management (HRM) and the role of the HR function in the future of work. In this article, we explore how technological developments such as the use of smart technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and robotics influence HRM and the role of the HR function. Through a scoping review, we highlight the influence of technological developments across macro (societal), meso (organization/HRM) and micro (individual workers) level work themes. We specifically focus on the dynamic interplay between technological developments and HRM. At the meso level, the analysis zooms in on how technological developments influence HRM at the strategic, tactical, and operational levels within organizational contexts. Our findings inform a future research agenda comprising avenues aimed at deepening our understanding of the challenges and opportunities associated with technological change in the context of HRM. More specifically, we propose future research to explore how the HR function can prepare the organization, itself, and other stakeholders, including line managers and workers, for the impact of technological developments to enhance HRM for the greater good. title: A tri-objective goal programming approach to generator maintenance scheduling
abstract: The generator maintenance scheduling problem is a key decision-making task in power system planning, requiring schedules that ensure reliability while controlling operational costs. Motivated by reliability challenges and financial constraints in systems such as South Africa's, this paper proposes a tri-objective optimisation framework that simultaneously minimises generator failure probability, production cost, and reserve margin. The model is formulated using goal programming to balance these competing objectives and is solved using simulated annealing and constraint programming. It is evaluated on the IEEE reliability test system and a large-scale Eskom-inspired system with 157 generating units. The results characterise trade-offs among reliability, cost, and reserve margin objectives, approximate a Pareto frontier, and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a decision-support tool for practical generator maintenance planning. © 2026 The Authors

title: How to deal with AI technology anxiety and its negative consequences? The role of strengths-based leadership
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into hospitality operations, employees’ AI technology anxiety has emerged as a salient managerial concern. Drawing on social information processing theory, this study examines the effect of strengths-based leadership on AI technology anxiety and the subsequent influence of this anxiety on employees’ social loafing behavior. Across a time-lagged field study and an experiment, the findings reveal the following key results. First, strengths-based leadership effectively alleviated hospitality employees’ AI technology anxiety, thereby reducing their social loafing behavior. Second, job automation weakened the negative effect of strengths-based leadership on AI technology anxiety. In turn, the indirect effect of strengths-based leadership on social loafing behavior through AI technology anxiety was also attenuated under high levels of job automation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Extending ethanol energy fractions in ethanol-diesel dual-fuel combustion through EGR, intake conditions, and injection strategies
abstract: Misfire and excessive maximum pressure rise rates (MPRR) typically limit the ethanol energy fraction (EEF) in ethanol–diesel dual-fuel combustion. To extend the allowable EEF while maintaining combustion stability and acceptable MPRR, experiments were conducted on a medium-duty engine (1.1 L/cylinder) operating in intake-fumigation dual-fuel mode with ethanol and diesel. Tests at 6, 10, and 15 bar gross indicated mean effective pressure (IMEPg) evaluated the effects of EGR, intake conditions, diesel injection timing, rail pressure, and injection strategy on combustion, emissions, and efficiency. At 10 and 15 bar IMEPg, operation was primarily constrained by excessive MPRR. Under baseline conditions, maximum EEF was limited to 51 % at 10 bar IMEPg and 39 % at 15 bar IMEPg. Increasing EGR from 14 % to 48 % at 10 bar IMEPg reduced peak heat release rates, lowering MPRR below 5 bar/deg and extending achievable EEF to 82 %. Intake temperature influenced combustion phasing and burn rates; reducing intake temperature from 350 K to 330 K decreased MPRR and widened the allowable EEF range. At 6 bar IMEPg, operation was limited by misfire rather than MPRR. Stable combustion could not be sustained above 87 % EEF because high ethanol fractions suppressed diesel cool-flame reactivity. Increasing intake pressure improved combustion quality by advancing combustion phasing and increasing in-cylinder temperatures. Diesel injection timing and rail pressure were varied to assess diesel reactivity under high-EGR, high-EEF conditions. Lower rail pressures favored advanced injection timings because richer spray plumes promoted stronger early-stage reactivity, whereas higher rail pressures benefited from later injection timings to avoid excessive spray overmixing before ignition. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Ensuring eco-resilience in Physical Internet-enabled production routing problem under ripple effect: a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach
abstract: Abstract: Resilience and eco-friendliness have emerged as two pivotal objectives for modern supply chains facing increasing disruptions and sustainability demands. The Physical Internet (PI), characterized by interconnectivity, resource sharing, and adaptability, represents a transformative approach to enhancing supply chain flexibility while mitigating environmental impacts. This study develops a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer optimization model to design a PI-enabled resilient production-routing system under the ripple effect. Furthermore, the model evaluates the influence of four distinct carbon policies, capturing the trade-offs between resilience and eco-friendliness. To address hybrid uncertainties arising from parameters, objectives, and constraints, this study proposes a scenario-based robust possibilistic flexible programming approach. The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed model and solution approach are validated through a case study. The results demonstrate that the PI significantly enhances both resilience and environmental sustainability by optimizing vehicle utilization, a benefit that cannot be realized in traditional noncollaborative or collaborative supply chains. Moreover, the analysis reveals that as policymakers adopt more conservative approaches, both total costs and carbon emissions increase simultaneously. Furthermore, higher carbon prices and lower carbon emission caps do not always lead to lower carbon emissions. © 2025 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Do negative emotions mediate the association between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions to involuntary musical imagery? Testing an OCD-analogue cognitive model of distressing earworms
abstract: Purpose: Distressing involuntary musical imagery (INMI) or “earworms” are often experienced but rarely studied. Due to their similarity with obsessions, research can draw on models of obsessive-compulsive disorder. The present study followed a cognitive model and tested the hypothesis of a positive relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions, mediated by negative emotions. Methods: Individuals with OCD (n = 79) and students without OCD (n = 298) completed the Characteristics of Earworms Questionnaire (CEAR). The central hypothesis was tested using a mediation analysis. Results: The analysis revealed a significant direct effect of negative appraisals on dysfunctional reactions to INMI, but no mediation by negative emotions. Conclusions: These findings support the applicability of the cognitive OCD model to INMI, particularly the relationship between negative appraisals and dysfunctional reactions. However, the results question whether negative emotions mediate this relationship. If replicated, results may provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions for distressing INMI. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Do users trade performance for eco-visibility? Digital pollution awareness and stated preferences for social media platform configurations
abstract: Digital platforms face growing pressure to demonstrate environmental responsibility, yet users’ preferences for eco-visible features remain underexplored relative to functional attributes. Using a full-factorial rating-based within-subject conjoint survey with a UK sample (N = 345) recruited to match national census distributions of age, sex, and ethnicity, combined with hierarchical linear modelling, this study decomposes willingness to use social media platforms across four attributes: media quality, loading speed, eco-visibility, and advertising frequency. Results show that technical attributes — media quality (relative importance = 34.9%) and loading speed (34.5%) — jointly dominate eco-visibility (8.1%), revealing a persistent performance-over-sustainability hierarchy in elicited trade-off preferences. A full 4 × 4 cross-level moderation analysis incorporating all 16 attribute-by-moderator interactions with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction identifies advertising receptivity — rather than green self-identity or environmental awareness — as the strongest individual-difference moderator, showing a dual pattern: it simultaneously attenuates the reduced-ads utility and amplifies the loading-speed premium. Green self-identity attenuates the media-quality premium but does not amplify eco-visibility utility; none of the eco-visibility moderations — by green self-identity, social comparison orientation, or digital environmental attitude — is confirmed. Exploratory benefit segmentation identifies three preference profiles — Technical Optimizers, Eco-Aware Pragmatists, and Ad-Averse Minimalists — revealing a sign reversal in eco-visibility utility across profiles. Theoretical and practical implications for sustainable platform design, multiple-comparison practices in conjoint moderation research, and green digital marketing are discussed. © 2026 The Authors

title: Why they come (back): Motive clusters of seasonal employees and their multiple workplace commitments
abstract: This study develops seasonal employee typologies for the Alpine tourism and hospitality sector by connecting motives for seasonal work with varying levels of different workplace commitments and return intention. Conceptualizing the destination as an analytical lens rather than merely context, this study examines how employees’ social, economic, and leisure motives affect their commitment to the organization, coworkers, job, and destination. Drawing on survey data from 381 hospitality employees in an Alpine destination in Austria, cluster analysis, analysis of variance, and post hoc tests were applied. The analysis identified four employee clusters (lifestyle seekers, dedicated professionals, practical earners, and social contributors) that significantly differ in their motivational profiles, commitment patterns, and demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrate that commitment among seasonal employees extends beyond the organization and differs across motive-based segments. These differences may shape guest interactions and service delivery, ultimately impacting service quality, visitor satisfaction, and overall destination performance. By integrating a motive-based segmentation with a multi-target commitment perspective, this study advances research on seasonal tourism employment and underscores how destination-specific contexts impact employee attitudes and behaviors. The results offer insights for adapting recruitment and retention strategies to distinct employee profiles in seasonal hospitality settings. © 2026 The Authors

title: Not alone: How group photos enhance audience responses to virtual influencers
abstract: Although marketers increasingly use virtual influencers to engage consumers, concerns about authenticity continue to limit their effectiveness. This research examines whether group photos can make virtual influencers appear more socially connected and authentic, thereby improving audience responses. We propose that, compared with no-person images or solo photos, group photos provide visual social cues that place virtual influencers in recognizable interpersonal contexts and make them appear more socially connected in shared experiences. Across one large-scale field study and two experiments, we test this proposition. Study 1 draws on a large-scale Instagram dataset of 17,878 posts from 109 virtual influencers collected between 2023 and 2026, with the main analyses based on 8558 non-video posts and finds that group photos receive higher post engagement than no-person images and solo photos. Study 2 provides controlled experimental evidence consistent with this effect and suggests that perceived social connectedness and perceived authenticity sequentially account for the relationship between group photos and favorable post evaluations. Study 3 identifies virtual influencer type as an important boundary condition: group photos are more effective for human-like virtual influencers, whereas this advantage weakens for cartoon-like virtual influencers. These findings contribute to research on virtual influencer humanization and authenticity by showing that visual social connectedness can make virtual influencers appear more socially embedded, more authentic, and more favorably evaluated. The results also offer actionable insights for marketers and content creators seeking to design virtual influencer content that elicits more favorable audience responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: AI-driven cultural and creative packaging design and user purchase intention: AI-disclosure perspective based on SEM-ANN hybrid analysis
abstract: Generative AI has introduced new possibilities for cultural and creative packaging design. This study examines how cultural symbol compatibility, design innovation, and aesthetic experience are associated with purchase intention through functional value, emotional value, social value, and epistemic value. Perceived factual disclosure and perceived narrative disclosure are further incorporated as moderators. A combined SEM-ANN approach is used to examine the linear relationships and nonlinear predictive importance of the study variables. The results indicate that the three perceived design attributes are indirectly associated with user purchase intention through multiple consumption-value pathways, although statistical support varies across the specific indirect effects. The principal theoretical contribution is to identify AI disclosure as a differentiated boundary condition in the conversion of consumption value into purchase intention. Perceived factual disclosure does not significantly moderate the relationships involving functional value or social value. Perceived narrative disclosure is associated with a weaker relationship between emotional value and purchase intention and a stronger relationship between epistemic value and purchase intention. The study extends research on AI-assisted cultural packaging and provides practical implications for AI disclosure in high-end product contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A graph model for conflict resolution incorporating movement willingness intensity under linguistic uncertainty
abstract: In the graph model for conflict resolution (GMCR), decision-makers (DMs) are required to express their preferences over feasible conflict states. Under uncertainty, however, such preferences are often difficult to quantify precisely and are more naturally represented by linguistic preference relations. To address this issue, this study develops a linguistic GMCR framework. Four linguistic stability concepts, namely linguistic Nash stability, linguistic sequential stability, linguistic symmetric metarationality, and linguistic general metarationality, are defined in logical form for general multi-DM conflicts. Corresponding matrix-based representations are then derived to facilitate stability computation. To capture heterogeneity in DMs’ willingness to transition between states, the framework is further extended by introducing a two-degree linguistic preference structure with two flexible formulations of the linguistic satisficing threshold. This extension distinguishes strong and mild transition willingness and yields three classes of linguistic stability, namely general linguistic stability, strong linguistic stability, and weak linguistic stability. The proposed framework is applied to the Elmira groundwater contamination conflict to demonstrate its practical applicability. Sensitivity and comparative analyses show that the two-degree linguistic framework identifies differentiated stability patterns that cannot be captured by single-threshold approaches, thereby providing a more refined basis for conflict diagnosis and resolution under linguistic uncertainty and heterogeneous transition willingness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: MAGE: A structural-prior-guided graph-language multimodal framework for business process anomaly detection
abstract: Business process event logs record activities, resources, timestamps, and other process attributes, and therefore provide the basis for trace-level anomaly detection. Existing methods often lack a unified reference for normal behavior and do not explicitly coordinate structural deviations with semantic information. We propose MAGE, a structural-prior-guided graph-enhanced language embedding framework for business process anomaly detection. MAGE first constructs structural priors solely from normal traces in the training set, including normal directly-follows relations, trace-length statistics, and adjacent-event resource-switching statistics. It then compares each trace with these priors to generate structural deviation signals and constructs both an activity-resource-time-slice heterogeneous graph and a structure-aware textual representation. A heterogeneous graph Transformer extracts structural representations, while a LoRA-adapted Qwen3 model extracts semantic representations. Gated cross-attention fuses the two modalities for trace-level anomaly classification. The structural prior and graph self-supervised pretraining use only normal training traces, whereas the final multimodal classifier is jointly optimized on labeled training samples. Experiments on synthetic logs and public real event logs with controlled anomaly injection show that MAGE achieves the highest mean F1-scores of 0.872 and 0.860, respectively, among the compared methods under the evaluated settings. Ablation results further indicate that the structural prior, heterogeneous graph encoding, structure-aware prompting, and cross-modal fusion each contribute positively to F1-score under the evaluated settings. Together, these findings provide evidence for combining normal-process structural constraints with language-based semantic information in trace-level business process anomaly detection. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Home economics and sustainable futures: A systematic literature review
abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the development, thematic structure, and research trends in Home Economics from 2015 to 2024, with an emphasis on its contribution to a sustainable future. Through the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach with Scopus indexed article data sources, a total of 22 articles were analyzed using a combination of thematic synthesis methods and bibliometric visualization through the VOSviewer tool to identify developing research patterns, relationships, and clusters. The results of the analysis show that Home Economics research has shifted its focus from traditional discussions of household skills to a multidisciplinary approach that emphasizes sustainable education, family economic literacy, health, and social responsibility. The keyword mapping process uncovered to have five major clusters—education, sustainability, health, students, and digital literacy—that intersect to have within the broader framework of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). Quantitatively, publication trends show a significant increase over the past three years (2021–2024), reflecting to have the increasing global interest in issues concerning welfare and sustainability in the field of education. The main findings also suggest that Home Economics is increasingly being positioned as a transformative discipline that integrates economic literacy, environmental awareness and social responsibility. Theoretically, the results of this study expand the framework of Home Economics as a humanistic and ecological science, while practically, the implications confirm the need for contextual, collaborative, and project-based curriculum and pedagogy innovations to address the challenges of the 21st century. These implications are important for curriculum developers, educators, and policymakers in integrating sustainability values into the education system. In conclusion, this study confirms that Home Economics has a strategic role in shaping a sustainable future through education. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: What Strategies Can Payers Use to Negotiate Medicine Prices Globally? Insights and Lessons for Low-Income Countries from a Scoping Review
abstract: Objectives No comprehensive global review has synthesized mechanisms, strengths, limitations, and implementation challenges of pharmaceutical pricing policies. This scoping review aimed to examine global pharmaceutical pricing policies and generate policy-relevant insights, particularly for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Methods Electronic searches were conducted in Medline, CINAHL, EconLit, and Embase using predefined inclusion criteria. Gray literature was identified through government publications and World Health Organization reports, and reference lists of relevant studies were screened. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review framework and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews guidelines. Results Searches conducted up to May 2024 and updated in February 2026 identified 88 eligible studies. Reference pricing was the most commonly reported strategy, used in 85% of identified countries, offering simplicity and transparency through price benchmarking. Value-based pricing was widely adopted in high-income countries, aligning prices with health outcomes but requiring strong health technology assessment infrastructure. Managed entry agreements were reported in 56% of countries and were used to improve access to new medicines while mitigating financial risk. Indication-specific pricing was implemented in 9 countries but faced operational challenges. Compulsory licensing in several LMICs improved access to essential medicines at lower cost, although concerns regarding impacts on pharmaceutical innovation were noted. Most countries combined multiple pricing approaches to balance affordability, access, and innovation. Conclusions Although value-based pricing and managed entry agreements are common in high-income settings, simpler approaches such as reference pricing and compulsory licensing may be more feasible in LMICs. Context-specific strategies are needed to balance access, affordability, and sustainability. © 2026 The Authors.

title: International scaling of social innovations through digitalization: A 3D framework
abstract: Social enterprises that embed social innovations (SIs) play a critical role in advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), representing an estimated US$12 trillion market opportunity. Yet, how SIs internationalize in the presence of institutional voids remains underexplored in international business research. Using a history-to-theory and history-in-theory approach, this study examines how dynamic capabilities and digitalization enable the international scaling of SIs. We find that international diffusion depends on capabilities such as boundary spanning, international sensing, legitimacy building, business diplomacy, and market shaping. Digitalization accelerates scaling, contingent on factors including timing, resources, intellectual property ownership, purpose, and technology scope. Our findings also suggest that traditional internationalization metrics—such as exports, FDI, subsidiaries, and foreign sales—do not adequately capture SI internationalization. Instead, internationalization is reflected in the cross-border diffusion of innovations and social impact, alongside the ability to attract international funding, partnerships, talent, and legitimacy while balancing social impact with financial sustainability. title: Research trends and conceptual foundations of religious moderation: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Although the concept of religious moderation has received increasing scholarly attention in recent years, comprehensive and globally integrative syntheses remain limited. In many Western scholarly traditions, similar ideas are often articulated through related concepts such as religious tolerance, pluralism, liberal pluralism, or collaborative secularism, resulting in fragmented conceptual discussions across disciplines and regions. This study therefore aims to map the development, intellectual structure, and thematic evolution of research on religious moderation within global academic discourse. This study employs a hybrid approach combining Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database, where the keyword “religious moderation” was searched in article titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search identified 901 publications (2009–2026). After applying the PRISMA screening procedure, 235 articles met the inclusion criteria and were selected for analysis. Bibliometric mapping was conducted using VOSviewer to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, institutional affiliations, and thematic patterns within the field. The findings indicate that research on religious moderation has experienced gradual growth and increasing global visibility. However, the distribution of scholarly contributions remains highly concentrated in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia, suggesting that the concept has not yet diffused widely across Western, Middle Eastern, and African academic traditions. This geographical concentration reveals significant opportunities for comparative, cross-cultural, and interdisciplinary research. This study also, through an analysis of 235 articles indexed in Scopus, found several studies on the indicators and principles of religious moderation, which play an important role in fostering harmony amid social differences and diversity. In addition, the study proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework linking religious moderation to broader domains including social cohesion, conflict resolution, interfaith relations, family dynamics, and education, highlighting its relevance for sustaining inclusive and resilient communities. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Reservation-based intersection scheduling using dynamic programming with dominance pruning
abstract: Scheduling connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) at reservation-based intersections faces a fundamental trade-off: existing methods sacrifice either optimality for computational efficiency or real-time applicability for optimal solutions. We bridge this gap by proposing a dynamic programming (DP) algorithm with dominance pruning ((Formula presented.)) that simultaneously achieves optimal batch formation, polynomial-time complexity, and superior solution quality. (Formula presented.) introduces a novel dominance rule that eliminates suboptimal child nodes by comparing analytically derived lower bounds, enabling batch-based processing of CAVs while guaranteeing optimality. Unlike existing approaches that assume predetermined batches or sacrifice optimality, (Formula presented.) integrates optimal batching decisions directly into the scheduling algorithm. The proposed method achieves a substantial improvement over existing exact algorithms with (Formula presented.) worst-case and (Formula presented.) best-case time complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that (Formula presented.) reduces computation time by 91% and 99% compared to a state-of-the-art DP algorithm and Gurobi solver, respectively, while consistently delivering superior performance in makespan, average delay, and maximum delay metrics across diverse traffic scenarios. Furthermore, (Formula presented.) outperforms heuristic algorithms in achieving better solution quality and comparative computational efficiency. Sensitivity analysis reveals that (Formula presented.) ’s dominance rule remains effective across varying mean headways, CAV counts, and batch proportions, with performance benefits extending beyond simple batch processing to complex traffic patterns. © 2026 International Federation of Operational Research Societies.

title: Artificial intelligence systems distort upstream selection in human social learning
abstract: Humans are social learners who depend on observing others to acquire knowledge, norms, and behaviors, a capacity that underlies cumulative cultural evolution. Social learning unfolds in two stages: upstream selection determines what information becomes visible, and downstream selection determines what learners copy from that visible sample. Downstream selection occurs through biases such as conformity bias (copying what appears common) and prestige bias (copying those who appear highly respected). These downstream biases can be adaptive when upstream selection yields a sample that reflects the population's true distribution, so that what appears common is actually common and those who appear respected are actually competent. We argue that digital technologies disrupt this condition, creating an upstream selection problem. Engagement-based algorithms amplify the tails of the distribution, surfacing rare and extreme content, whereas generative AI collapses it toward the mode (of the population or the user), erasing the surrounding diversity. Crucially, in each system the optimization signal shapes both visibility and prestige. For engagement-based algorithms, the signal is engagement: creators who post extreme content become more visible and, through the likes, shares, and followers, appear more prestigious. For generative AI, the signal is statistical typicality: it makes a modal answer dominant and, with no alternatives shown, makes the model that produced it appear more prestigious. These distortions can give rise to emergent group-level phenomena, including pluralistic ignorance and illusory consensus. Synthesizing evidence across psychology, cultural evolution, and computational social science, we provide a framework for how digital technologies disrupt social learning and outline interventions for restoring functional cultural transmission. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: More alike than unalike: Contextually aligned authority arguments amplify sustainable choices across cultures
abstract: Most research is conducted in Western societies, with few studies from Latin America. This oversight has led to a narrow understanding of the effectiveness that various sustainability-oriented interventions have in countries with different cultural values. As consumers play a vital role in mitigating climate change issues, this behavioral field experiment investigates whether reliance on the authority and commitment-consistency principles from social influence increases individuals' inclination to choose sustainably, and whether the effectiveness of these principles is culturally contingent. Participants from Ecuador and Norway (N = 346) were randomized to one of three conditions (control vs. authority vs. commitment-consistency), with the latter two conditions containing a message tailored to its associated social influence principle. After replying to some survey items, participants made a choice between a more (vs. less) sustainable option. A chi-square test revealed that both social influence conditions jointly boosted choice likelihood of the more sustainable option relative to the control condition, supporting our initial preregistered hypothesis. However, contrary to our second preregistered hypothesis, a regression-based simple moderation analysis using the PROCESS macro (Model 1) showed no country moderation in the effectiveness of these social influence principles; instead, the results were largely attributable to the authority condition alone, which was considerably more effective than both other conditions across countries, regardless of participants' trust in authorities and their need for consistency. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of contextually aligned authority arguments as a viable way to foster pro-environmental behaviors. © 2026 The Authors

title: Trustworthy artificial intelligence in advanced manufacturing
abstract: Additive manufacturing is relying more and more on artificial intelligence for prediction, control, and real-time decisions. Deployment, however, is still difficult. The main reason is that the underlying thermal, flow, and microstructural behavior can shift as the process changes, which makes reliable model performance hard to maintain. This review examines how trustworthy artificial intelligence (TAI) can be used to close that gap in digital twins for additive manufacturing across both metallic and ceramic systems. It frames trustworthiness as a technical condition for deployment and translates it into an AM-specific operational framework. From that point onward, it examines how current workflows handle reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, explainability, robustness, generalizability, fairness, and transparency. A structured evaluation of sixty studies in metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing systems reveals a distinct trend. Robustness and generalizability receive much more attention than transparency, explainability, and fairness. The coverage is also stronger in metallic systems than in ceramic ones. To move beyond binary classification, the review further applies a structured evidence-depth rubric that distinguishes absent coverage, limited or implicit evidence, method-level evidence, and operational evidence for each TAI attribute. We further show that trustworthy deployment depends on more than predictive accuracy. It also depends on physically consistent models as well as updates that account for uncertainty. Decision support has to remain interpretable as well. Model transfer across machines and materials should be treated as controlled adaptation, where reusable physics, sensing, and validation elements are separated from material-specific features that require recalibration. The validation path must also support qualification and industrial deployment, leading to a more cohesive digital twin framework. It brings together physics-based models, reduced-order models, learning-based surrogates, multimodal sensing, and trust-aware evaluation. The main finding is that trustworthiness is the missing technical link between digital twins that can be confidently used in advanced manufacturing and promising AI-enabled demonstrations. © 2026 The Authors

title: Evolution and lifecycle mapping of research methods based on the Boston Matrix in library and information science from 1995 to 2025
abstract: Developing an evolution framework for research methods is essential for advancing Library and Information Science (LIS), but existing research method schemas remain fragmented and limited. This study proposes an automated framework combining AI-driven methods to mine, classify, and a temporal analysis based on the Boston Matrix to map the lifecycles of research methods. Using a comprehensive dataset of 31,913 articles from 21 LIS journals (1995–2025) as a validation corpus, the framework integrates semantic clustering for bottom-up entity extraction with generative top-down ontology mapping. This approach dynamically maps methods into a four-stage lifecycle schema: mainstream, emerging, marginalized, and mature, revealing distinct evolutionary trajectories and the broader computational turn within LIS. Validated through quantitative threshold testing and qualitative evaluation, the proposed framework significantly reduces manual coding subjectivity and enhances replicability. By empirically comparing the subfields of librarianship and information science, this study accounts for inherent thematic variations and uncovers their distinct paces of methodological adoption. Ultimately, this study offers a robust automated framework for longitudinal methodological tracking, theoretically demonstrating how diverse AI-driven and traditional methods synergistically coevolve and assume distinct scholarly roles within the emerging AI4Science paradigm. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The security unlock: How rural social pension makes people more entrepreneurial?
abstract: Previous literature on the determinants of entrepreneurship has not explored the role of social pension. Leveraging variation in the roll-out timing of a universal rural pension program across Chinese counties, our analysis, at both the individual and aggregate levels, reveals that pension provision led to an increase in entrepreneurship among the younger generation. We show that this effect operates through two primary channels: an intergenerational transfer channel and a local demand channel. Specifically, the pension program mitigates upward transfers from adult children to elderly parents, while boosting local consumer demand, which exerts a demand-side “pull” effect on enterprise establishment. Our findings may shed new light on the interplay between pension, intergenerational resource allocation, and entrepreneurial activity. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Algorithmic fairness as a human–technology interaction problem
abstract: Algorithms shape high-stakes decisions across society. While promising efficiency, algorithms also raise fairness concerns. This article proposes that algorithmic fairness is best understood as a human–technology interaction problem rather than a purely technical challenge. Algorithms can reproduce human biases, amplify them through feedback loops, or create new forms of unfairness through objectives, proxies, and seemingly neutral variables. Yet they can make decision processes more explicit, disparities more visible, and actively mitigate discrimination. Fairness depends not only on statistical properties but also on how algorithms are designed, used and experienced by those affected by their decisions. This article therefore offers an interdisciplinary perspective that integrates insights from social justice, psychology, computer science, judgment and decision-making, and management. © 2026 The Author

title: How have flight operations between China and Europe changed since the Russia–Ukraine war?
abstract: This study examines how direct flight services between China and Europe changed during the COVID-19 pandemic and after the Russia–Ukraine war began in February 2022. We use monthly airport pair–airline data from January 2014 to September 2024. Our baseline model is a panel regression with route fixed effects. As a robustness check, we also estimate a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) specification with route and period fixed effects. After February 2022, passenger traffic fell and yields rose on the sampled routes, and these changes differed between European and Chinese carriers. In the baseline route fixed-effects model, European carriers had approximately 32.7% lower revenue passenger miles and 14.4% lower yields than Chinese carriers during the war period, relative to pre-war differences. The TWFE specification gives interaction estimates of similar sign and magnitude. These differences arose at the same time as the closure of Russian airspace to European carriers and are consistent with the longer routings that other studies document, together with other concurrent factors. During the COVID-19 period, passenger traffic fell sharply. Yields rose in the pooled sample but not in either travel direction separately, which is consistent with unequal travel demand in the two directions. Taken together, these findings highlight persistent vulnerabilities in the China–Europe aviation market and point to potential airline strategies, including greater operational flexibility, service enhancements, code-sharing arrangements, and bilateral coordination, that may strengthen market resilience. title: From design attributes to social life: Modelling conviviality in urban underground spaces
abstract: From being infrastructure utilities, urban underground spaces (UUS) have developed into multipurpose public spaces that combine commercial, cultural, and transit functions. While their technical and spatial contributions to compact urbanism are evident, their capacity to foster conviviality, the experiential quality of inclusiveness, sociability, and shared belonging, is less understood. This study develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework that operationalizes conviviality in UUS by linking seven spatial-perceptual dimensions (safety and security, identity and meaning, accessibility, functionality, environmental comfort, aesthetics, and structure and form) to behavioral mediators of willingness to use and social interaction, culminating in perceived conviviality. Using the Theatre-Shahr underground complex in Tehran as a case study, data were collected through structured surveys and analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that although environmental factors generally have a positive indirect effect on perceived conviviality, social interaction emerges as the primary mechanism shaping conviviality in urban underground spaces, while willingness to use plays only a complementary and limited mediating role in this process. Among the environmental factors, accessibility, environmental comfort, and safety and security show the strongest effects. In contrast, some variables, particularly identity and meaning and structure and form, do not demonstrate statistically significant effects in certain pathways. These findings suggest that planning and design strategies for urban underground spaces should prioritize environmental qualities that support social interaction, to enhance perceived conviviality. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Production decisions of a leasing-selling closed-loop supply chain under different authorization strategies
abstract: Leasing or selling, when to choose which? This paper investigates the production decisions of a closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) considering authorized remanufacturing (royalty/fixed-fee authorization) under different business mode combinations. Furthermore, win–win authorization strategies for the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the third-party remanufacturer (TPR) are analyzed. The conclusion shows that: (1) Regardless of the business mode chosen by the OEM, the sensitivity of unit product authorization fee to consumer perceived value of remanufactured products (RPs) is always higher when the TPR chooses the selling mode than when it chooses the leasing mode. (2) For selling new products (NPs) and RPs mode and selling NPs and leasing RPs mode, the fixed-fee authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for selling is high and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range, and the royalty authorization strategy is a win–win strategy when this cost is low and the fixed authorization fee is within a certain range. The win–win authorization strategies for the leasing NPs and selling RPs mode and leasing NPs and RPs mode are affected by the manufacturing cost per unit of NP for leasing and the fixed authorization fee. (3) Under the royalty authorization strategy, the TPR is more profitable when the OEM chooses the leasing mode, but the OEM is more profitable when the TPR chooses the selling mode. Under the fixed-fee authorization strategy, when one of the two players chooses the leasing mode, the other is always more profitable. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Facilitator or hallucination trap? A social-cognitive account of AI-generated misinformation handling in GenAI-assisted L2 writing
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has demonstrated remarkable potential in second language (L2) learning, yet it is prone to hallucinations. Empirical research on how GenAI-generated misinformation is handled in educational contexts remains scarce. Accordingly, little is known about how these practices shape learning processes and outcomes. Guided by social cognitive theory, the current study frames students' GenAI-assisted L2 writing (using a tailored GenAI writing agent) in a hallucination-prone context in which misinformation was implanted. We examine AI literacy, higher-order thinking resources (i.e., critical thinking and creativity), L2 writing resources (i.e., L2 writing grit and self-regulatory writing strategies), English writing self-efficacy (EWSE), AI-generated misinformation detection (AI-MD), and L2 writing performance within this framework. Using a multi-method approach, combining a qualitative interview study (N = 35), two lab experiments (N = 140), and a large-scale questionnaire survey (N = 406), we find that critical thinking positively predicts GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance via AI-MD, and that negative priming on AI hallucinations significantly improves students’ AI-MD and their GenAI-assisted L2 writing performance, relative to neutral or positive priming. Furthermore, the cross-sectional survey focuses on personal factors and shows that AI literacy significantly predicts EWSE both directly and indirectly through a cognitive–generative pathway involving higher-order thinking resources and a motivational–regulatory pathway involving L2 writing resources. These findings extend social-cognitive accounts of GenAI-assisted L2 writing and inform instruction that helps learners evaluate AI outputs, manage misinformation risks, and sustain their own writing processes. © 2026

title: Self-disclosure to intelligent virtual agents: A scoping review and the disclosure affordance–actualization–governance framework
abstract: Intelligent virtual agents (IVAs) have become digital social objects to which people disclose personal, emotional, health-related, and other sensitive information. Yet similar cues—including anthropomorphism, social presence, empathy, gaze, anonymity, and structured questioning—are associated across studies with greater disclosure, refusal, impression management, socially desirable responding, or discomfort. Searches covered four bibliographic databases without publication-year restrictions through March 17, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar searching on May 20, 2026. This review, reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), maps 88 empirical studies and introduces the Disclosure Affordance–Actualization–Governance (DAAG) framework as a middle-range account linking specific empirical findings with broader explanations of IVA-mediated disclosure. DAAG distinguishes sociotechnical interaction ecology; perceived safety from judgment, relational receptivity, expressive latitude, and boundary agency; disclosure actualization; affective, relational, and functional consequences; governance; and evidential reach—the extent to which studies observe perception, behavior, consequences, time, and governance. The literature is most developed for disclosure onset, sensitive reporting, emotional expression, and immediate system acceptance, but remains thin on persistence, reciprocity, subjective–behavioral divergence, correction, revocation, and downstream data use. Recurrent patterns are consistent with IVA cues being interpreted through evaluation risk, partner responsiveness, observability, topic sensitivity, competence, privacy, and control. DAAG is not presented as a validated causal model, but as a framework for explaining when digital social interaction supports, redirects, or appropriately constrains self-disclosure. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
