title: When culture speaks through E-commerce chatbots: How collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles shape impulsive buying
abstract: E-commerce chatbots increasingly provide product advice during online shopping, yet it remains unclear how culturally framed recommendation language shapes impulsive buying. Drawing on cultural dimensions theory, cultural priming theory, and constructivist interpretation, this study conceptualizes collectivistic and individualistic persuasive styles as message-level cultural language cues rather than as measures of consumers’ stable cultural orientation. Across four experiments with 880 participants, we show that a collectivistic persuasive style increases impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as socially supported and behaviorally acceptable choices, which strengthens social conformity. By contrast, an individualistic persuasive style reduces impulsive buying by making recommendations more likely to be interpreted as choices requiring confirmation against personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit, which strengthens self-referencing. The findings further identify two boundary conditions. Human labeling strengthens the collectivistic pathway through social conformity by making group-oriented language more likely to be treated as socially relevant advice, whereas AI labeling shifts source perception toward algorithmic advice and strengthens the individualistic pathway through self-referencing by increasing attention to personal needs, usage situations, and product-feature fit. Low algorithm accessibility strengthens the collectivistic pathway, whereas high algorithm accessibility strengthens the individualistic pathway. These findings show that chatbot recommendations do more than transmit product information. They shape how consumers interpret the perceived source, social relevance, and personal applicability of recommendations, thereby influencing whether recommendations are quickly accepted as purchase decisions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Platform abandonment through push–pull–mooring: Trust, commitment, and generational patterns in U.S. social media
abstract: Generational frameworks frequently explain platform adoption, but rarely platform abandonment. Through a stratified survey of 990 U.S. adults, this study examines how age cohorts (digital natives vs. digital immigrants) respond to platform change and what predicts abandonment across Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, and TikTok. Using the push-pull-mooring (PPM) framework, we found that cohort labels did not predict exit in pooled models. Distrust was the strongest pooled push predictor. Affective and normative commitment reduced abandonment odds, whereas need-based commitment increased them. Generation did, however, structure post-exit destinations: among Twitter/X leavers, digital natives were more likely to name Instagram and TikTok, and older cohorts were more likely to name Facebook. Abandonment is better explained by institutional distrust and multidimensional attachment than by cohort labels, but generation remains consequential for where users go next. Platforms seeking retention should repair credibility and cultivate wanted attachment rather than relying on lock-in or age targeting alone. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Artificial intelligence in negotiation research: From computational negotiators to psychological evidence
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence are reshaping how negotiation is conducted and studied. AI systems increasingly enter negotiation research in two broad roles: as part of the negotiation process, either as negotiators or as support for human negotiators, and as research instruments that annotate, standardize, and simulate negotiation at scale. As negotiators, these systems range from theory-driven agents to data-driven and hybrid agents, each embedding different assumptions about negotiation. As instruments, they promise scale, consistency, and control, but also raise risks of circular inference, in which AI appears to reveal patterns in human negotiation while actually reproducing patterns learned from its own training data. This review organizes emerging work on AI and negotiation around these two roles and argues that their scientific value depends on psychological grounding. Used naively, AI becomes a mirror of its own assumptions. Used carefully, with grounding in theory and calibration against human evidence, AI can become a transformative tool for advancing negotiation science. © 2026 The Authors

title: Why and when customer-related social stressors impair service performance: A conservation of resources perspective
abstract: Building on the conservation of resources theory, we investigate how customer-related social stressors impact service performance among hospitality employees. To explore this, we gathered data from 350 supervisor-employee pairs across twelve hotels in China through a three-wave survey. The results show that customer-related social stressors detrimentally affect work engagement, which in turn reduces service performance. Furthermore, job social support and employees’ social skills emerge as two key moderators, buffering both the direct impact of customer-related social stressors on work engagement and the indirect effect on service performance via work engagement. These findings provide a nuanced understanding of the interactions among customer-related social stressors, work engagement, and service performance, offering significant implications for both theory and practice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Negotiating the contested: A framework for studying social issue negotiations
abstract: Negotiation research has yielded useful insights on how to manage economic and business interactions by highlighting the importance of information sharing, trade-offs, and integrative solutions in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. However, these approaches inadequately explain why negotiations over social issues such as immigration reform and climate change can remain deadlocked despite sustained efforts to reach agreement. Drawing upon recent research, we introduce an organizing framework that identifies three common features of such negotiations: moralization, identity threat, and public contestation. Moralization frames issues as matters of right and wrong, reducing willingness to compromise; identity concerns transform policy disagreements into threats to group membership and self-concept; and public scrutiny increases reputational risks and constrains flexibility. Together, these dynamics hinder engagement, value creation, and the quality of agreements. We review emerging interventions—including moral reframing, perspective sharing, high-quality listening, informal dialogue, and third-party mediation—that may mitigate these barriers. We conclude by highlighting the need for research examining how moral, identity, and public pressures interact across levels of analysis to shape social issue negotiation processes and outcomes. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: From image to action: How social proof turns brand image into repurchase intention
abstract: This study examines how social proof shapes the relationship between brand image and repurchase intention in an emerging digital marketplace, distinguishing three forms that operate through different mechanisms: user-generated content, brand ambassadors, and testimonials. Because online markets involve considerable information overload, consumers rely heavily on others' evaluations to reduce decision risk; however, forms of social proof vary in authenticity and persuasive effectiveness, and prior research has largely treated them as a single, uniformly positive construct. A two-study, mixed-methods design set in Vietnam addresses this gap. Study 1 applies a Vietnamese-optimized RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach) model to social media comments to surface authentic consumer sentiment, providing exploratory, triangulating context without constituting a direct hypothesis test. Study 2 tests the proposed relationships using moderated regression on survey responses from 394 active Vietnamese online shoppers. Results show that brand image exerts a strong positive direct effect on repurchase intention. User-generated content significantly strengthens this relationship, with the largest effect among consumers holding moderate brand-image perceptions. Brand ambassadors moderate the relationship but show a bounded pattern, with diminishing influence once brand image is already strong. Testimonials exert a dual effect: they amplify the brand image-repurchase link when perceived as credible, but, when seen as commercially motivated, they independently trigger skepticism and weaken repurchase intention. By conceptually and empirically distinguishing ambassadors from testimonials, this study shows that social proof is not a uniformly positive force but a context-dependent mechanism conditioned by authenticity, with implications for transparency-oriented digital marketing strategy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
abstract: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets. © 2026

title: Identifying and prioritizing key factors influencing electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure planning in China: A Delphi study
abstract: The rapid expansion of China's new energy vehicle market has intensified demand for a coordinated, equitable fast-charging infrastructure system. Despite substantial growth, regional disparities, technical incompatibilities, and fragmented governance arrangements continue to constrain the efficiency and long-term sustainability of network deployment. This study systematically identifies and prioritizes the key determinants shaping the planning of fast-charging infrastructure in China. A two-round Delphi process was conducted with 30 experts drawn from government, industry, and academia to establish consensus on critical influencing factors. Anchored in diffusion of innovation and institutional theory, the analysis integrates technological, economic, spatial, social, environmental, and governance dimensions into a coherent evaluative framework. Six principal factors emerged: governance and institutional coordination; economic and financial viability; technological integration and standardization; social equity and user-oriented considerations; spatial and urban planning; and environmental sustainability. Governance and institutional coordination ranked highest in importance, with strong consensus among participants (Kendall's W = 0.696, p < 0.001). The findings underscore the central role of policy coherence, sustainable financial models, and interoperability in accelerating the diffusion of infrastructure and reducing regional inequality. The study advances a theoretically informed prioritization framework to support strategic infrastructure planning in rapidly electrifying economies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Payroll taxes, firm dynamism, and aggregate productivity
abstract: This study examines the impact of payroll-tax enforcement on firm dynamism and its implications for aggregate productivity. We exploit China's Social Security Collection Agency Reform, which transferred responsibility for collecting social-insurance contributions from local social-insurance agencies to tax authorities, thereby strengthening enforcement. We show that the reform increased firms’ social-insurance contributions, shifted workers toward informal employment without reducing overall nonagricultural employment, and reduced new firm entry while weakening incumbent firms’ profitability and investment. title: Hidden dissatisfaction after agreement: Post-negotiation perceptual alignment
abstract: Negotiations continue to have consequences after an agreement or impasse. When parties reach a deal, value is often created only later, as they implement commitments, adapt to uncertainty, or decide whether to negotiate again. This review introduces post-negotiation perceptual alignment, how accurately a negotiator understands the counterpart's post-negotiation experience. Integrating research on subjective value, interpersonal perception, and post-agreement outcomes, I distinguish four states: recognized satisfaction, recognized dissatisfaction, overestimated dissatisfaction, and hidden dissatisfaction. Hidden dissatisfaction is consequential because it creates a false sense of success where one party treats agreement as evidence that the negotiation went well while the counterpart carries forward negative appraisals that remain unrecognized and unaddressed. Recent research suggests tactics that appear successful at agreement can impose unrecognized social and relational costs. I review why misalignment arises, emphasizing how negotiators’ imperfect inferences about counterparts’ experiences can combine with social pressures that discourage dissatisfied parties from speaking up. I conclude by outlining directions for measuring alignment and testing how negotiators can recognize and respond to dissatisfaction after negotiations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Corporate social responsibility and socio-economic impacts in the mining sector: A bibliometric review of local community empowerment and sustainable development
abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of the scholarly literature on corporate social responsibility (CSR) and its socio-economic implications in the mining sector, with a focus on local community empowerment and sustainable development outcomes. Using the Scopus database, a systematic search yielded 217 documents published between 2015 and 2025, which were then refined into 182 articles and reviews through structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study covers three main dimensions: (1) the evolution of mining-related CSR publication trends over the period 2015–2025; (2) the identification of dominant countries, institutions, and authors along with evolving collaboration patterns; and (3) thematic clusters that shape the intellectual architecture of the field, specifically how these clusters reflect the tension between corporate interests and stakeholder rights as theorized by Stakeholder Theory. The analysis was conducted using VOSviewer and the Bibliometrix package in R to map publication trends, author productivity, international collaboration networks, and thematic keyword clusters. The findings show a progressive growth in publications, reaching a peak of 37 documents in 2023, reflecting increasing academic and regulatory attention to corporate accountability in the extractive industries. Five thematic clusters were identified: CSR and indigenous peoples, economic sustainability and the resource curse, artisanal mining and local livelihoods, coal mining and occupational health, and a methodological cluster related to data mining in computer science. The United States and Australia lead in publication volume, while Ghana records the highest citation-per-document ratio. Indonesia, while present in the corpus, exhibits limited citation visibility, indicating significant room for increased global research engagement. The study identified critical gaps, including a dearth of longitudinal CSR assessments, limited multinational accountability research, and underrepresentation of Southeast Asian perspectives as urgent research priorities for advancing equitable mining governance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Generative AI as a social partner for young adults: Dual pathways to resilience and AI dependence
abstract: This study examines LLM-based AI chatbots as social interaction partners. It identifies young adults’ support-seeking motivations and models their associations with two interaction processes (Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity) and two psychological outcomes (Resilience and AI Dependence). In Study 1, we developed the Motivation Scale for Generative AI (MS-GAI) through theory-driven item generation and interviews and validated it with a survey of Korean young adults (N = 300). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported an eight-factor, 40-item structure grounded in four social-support domains and supplemented by context-specific motivations. In Study 2, structural equation modeling showed that Emotional Support and Self-Enhancement were positively associated with both Perceived Authenticity and Interaction Intensity. Objective Advice Seeking was positively associated with Perceived Authenticity, whereas Learning Assistance, Daily Problem-Solving, and Entertainment/Mood Diversion were positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Perceived Authenticity was also positively associated with Interaction Intensity. Both interaction processes were positively related to self-reported Resilience and AI Dependence, with Interaction Intensity showing the stronger association with AI Dependence. These findings identify distinct but overlapping interaction pathways through which support-seeking motivations are associated with adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. The study extends understanding of social support in human–AI interaction by providing a validated motivation measure and showing how shared interaction processes relate to both short-term perceived recovery and dependence. The findings are consistent with the Paradoxes of Technology perspective and highlight the need for emotionally supportive yet balanced design and policy safeguards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From hostile feedback to withdrawal: Emotional exhaustion as a barrier to social media misinformation correction
abstract: User-driven misinformation correction is essential for sustaining the integrity of democratic discourse on social media, yet the emotional costs that discourage engagement remain understudied. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how the emotional tone of other users' feedback affects correctors' emotional exhaustion and subsequent willingness to engage in future corrections in a social media environment. In a cross-national experiment (N = 2001) across Austria, Bulgaria, Denmark, and Poland, utilizing a single-factor, four-level between-subjects design, participants corrected misinformation and received feedback varying in valence and arousal. Results show that angry, high-arousal feedback uniquely depletes emotional resources, producing higher exhaustion than civil disapproval or positive feedback. This indicates that critical feedback does not inherently exhaust correctors, but it is the hostile tone, not the negativity itself, that drives depletion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, predicts avoidance of future corrective engagement. This exhaustion-driven withdrawal is amplified rather than buffered by correction confidence, suggesting that individual motivation alone is insufficient in hostile environments. These findings highlight emotional exhaustion as a key psychological constraint on citizen-led fact-checking and suggest that platform-level moderation targeting hostile comments is critical to protect the emotional resources required for a resilient democratic debate in digital environments. © 2026 The Authors

title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and sociotechnical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Mental Health and Neurodivergence Disclosure Risk Mitigation in Private Higher Education Institutions: An Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to Support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: This study examines mental health and neurodivergence disclosure risk mitigation in private higher education institutions through an Integrated Risk-Protection Framework to support Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 297 academic and non-academic staff from selected private higher education institutions in Selangor, Malaysia. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Structural power asymmetry, institutional trust deficit, stigma anticipation, and absence of safeguards reduce psychological safety in disclosure. Perceived enforceability of protection moderates these relationships and strengthens the explanatory power of the model. This study highlights perceived enforceability of protection as a key risk mitigation mechanism for developing inclusive, psychologically safe, and sustainable higher education governance. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Exploring socioeconomic associations of crisis information processing via large language models and explainable AI
abstract: Social media evolution has restructured corporate crisis communication, yet extracting regional intelligence from unstructured data remains a significant computational challenge. This study proposes an integrated AI-Spatial Information Framework to analyze provincial-level discourse patterns during a major corporate crisis. Using the DeepSeek R1 671B model with few-shot learning, we classified 225,515 social media comments from Douyin into five theory-driven categories and an “Other” category, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.67% against stratified human reference labels (Cohen’s kappa = 0.828). We then employed LASSO-based feature selection and FDR-corrected OLS regression to examine associations between provincial-level socioeconomic indicators and consumer discourse patterns across 31 Chinese provinces. Statistical results suggest that provincial socioeconomic factors account for a substantial portion of the observed variation in digital discourse. Life expectancy was positively associated with brand anthropomorphism, while tertiary education showed a tentative negative association with health risk perception. More importantly, these associations suggest that regional variation in brand-supportive discourse is closely related to socioeconomic conditions and is theoretically consistent with cognitive buffering processes. By integrating theory-driven LLM classification with spatial analysis, the proposed framework connects computational linguistics and spatial social computing, providing a replicable approach for examining regional heterogeneity in digital crisis discourse. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Integrating Computational Thinking and Islamic Values in Geometry Learning: Effects on Pre-Service Primary Teachers’ Conceptual Understanding
abstract: This study examines the integration of computational thinking and Islamic values in geometry learning for Primary School Teacher Education (PSTE) students. Using a quantitative descriptive approach, the research involved 70 PSTE students at Universitas Islam Riau. Data were collected through tests, observations, and interviews, and analyzed using triangulation to ensure validity. This integration significantly improves students’ conceptual understanding, as reflected in the increase in post-test scores. The one-sample t-test yielded a significance value, confirming a meaningful difference between pre-and post-test results. In addition, students internalized Islamic values such as honesty, cooperation, and spiritual awareness during learning activities. This study responds to the need for educational models that balance cognitive skills and character development. The integration of technology and Islamic principles creates a holistic learning experience, contributing to the development of competent, ethical, and responsible future educators. © 2027 Bumi Publikasi Nusantara.

title: Understanding work well-being: A systematic review and future research agenda on multilevel influences
abstract: Work well-being has become an important topic in organizational research, as it is beneficial to employee performance and job satisfaction. Although studies on work well-being have increased recently, existing literature remains fragmented, with prior reviews predominantly focusing on general employee well-being or single-level analyses. This limitation constrains both theoretical clarity and the development of targeted organizational interventions. In particular, there is a need to systematically review how individual, group, and organizational factors shape employees’ well-being at work. To address this gap, the present study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing evidence from 53 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025, retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. This study has two key implications: It identifies knowledge gaps in the literature and supports evidence-based decision-making. By synthesizing findings across the individual, group, and organizational levels, this review develops a broad and integrated understanding of the drivers of work well-being. The findings suggest that work well-being is driven by the dynamic interaction between individual and social resources, and broader organizational conditions. These factors operate in combination rather than independently, shaping employees’ psychological experiences across work contexts. This study contributes to the literature by providing a structured and integrative multilevel framework, clarifying conceptual boundaries of work well-being, and identifying underexplored research areas. It also offers a more analytically grounded synthesis that advances theoretical development and informs evidence-based organizational practices. In addition, the study highlights directions for future research, offering valuable insights for policymakers, managers, and scholars seeking to promote work well-being. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Cities under pressure: Tourism intensity and the erosion of social capital in Italy
abstract: This research note reconceptualizes tourism intensity as a structural stressor capable of undermining the social capital that sustains urban life. Drawing on a 15-year longitudinal panel data of 42 Italian cities (2009-2023) and employing a dynamic System GMM estimator, our study analyses how varying levels of tourism intensity affect social capital, operationalized through a multi-indicator civic engagement index. The results reveal a non-linear erosion process, where social capital remains stable at low and moderate levels of tourism intensity but declines sharply once cities surpass high-intensity thresholds. Our findings provide a quantifiable basis for understanding overtourism as a threshold-based social phenomenon, extending beyond resident perceptions to the structural weakening of civic cooperation, trust, and engagement. The present study advances theoretical debates by positioning tourism intensity as a civic destabilizer and highlights the need for governance models that protect social capital as a critical urban asset. Without such safeguards, cities risk transitioning from vibrant, participatory communities into socially depleted Non-places. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A dynamic graph query-based data pricing method via multi-armed bandits
abstract: Graph query-based data pricing is promising for pricing answer subgraphs in graph databases according to diverse buyer queries. However, existing methods provide limited support for adaptive price updates when the broker must balance transaction revenue with transaction success rate under incomplete buyer-valuation information. To bridge this gap, we propose GQPRM, which includes: (1) a vertex-edge pricing mechanism that prices a first-time queried answer graph through non-negative atomic prices; (2) a multi-armed bandit (MAB)-based strategy that discretizes repeated-query prices into candidate actions and uses historical acceptance/rejection records for exploration and exploitation; (3) an entropy-weighted feedback update that allocates the observed subgraph-level price variation to vertices and edges in a demand-sensitive manner, rather than assuming that binary feedback uniquely identifies a single overpriced element; and (4) a smart contract-based incentive allocation mechanism that records ownership and supports auditable reward allocation between the data broker and data owners. Experiments on three typical datasets demonstrate that GQPRM improves cumulative transaction value and transaction success rate over the static baseline under the evaluated settings. © 2026

title: An adaptive-problem structure framework for survival relevance in temporal processing
abstract: Research on survival-relevant cues and subjective time often groups stimuli into immediate-survival, reproductive, and social categories. These labels do not explain why cues within one category recruit different temporal processes across contexts and perceivers. The Adaptive-Problem Structure (APS) Framework characterizes the adaptive problem indicated by a cue through two separable appraisals: ecological urgency, the time sensitivity and cost of delaying a response, and interpretive indeterminacy, the extent to which adaptive meaning and the appropriate response remain unresolved. APS predicts when these appraisals recruit established arousal, attention, information-sampling, and memory processes, how diagnostic context changes those links, and which personality differences strengthen them. Temporal consequences depend on the timing paradigm, interval, and response format. We outline independent ratings, selective within-domain manipulations, process measures, and staged construct validation. Five predictions specify task conditions, personality mappings, comparison baselines, and non-supporting outcomes. APS offers testable constraints on mechanism recruitment and prediction for new stimuli; the framework itself remains to be empirically validated. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The role of citizen science in engaging older adults with age-friendly green spaces
abstract: This project addresses the global challenges of an ageing population and rapid urbanisation by exploring how citizen science can support the engagement of older adults in shaping age-friendly green spaces. Conducted in the City of Unley, South Australia, the study engaged 30 older residents (aged 60+) as citizen scientists to trial a multi-format audit tool and co-reflect on its use in practice for creating age-friendly environments, generating practical insights for future research and design practice. Integrating audits into participants’ daily routines and everyday life spaces ensured that findings reflected lived experiences. Citizen science was not merely a data collection tool but a sustained dialogue, with regular workshops and informal café sessions supporting motivation, peer learning, and collaborative analysis. Participants reported challenges such as sustaining long-term motivation, but also highlighted opportunities for empowerment, confidence-building, and strengthened community ties. Importantly, many older adults described shifts in how they experienced their environments—becoming more observant, extending their walking habits, and growing more confident in voicing ideas. Several participants continued their civic engagement beyond the project, illustrating the lasting impact of participation. The study contributes methodological insights into designing inclusive citizen science initiatives, offering guidance on recruitment, tool development, and engagement strategies tailored to older populations. Overall, this study demonstrates the power of citizen science not only to generate grounded data but also to empower older adults and co-produce inclusive urban knowledge. Findings provide process-focused insights into age-friendly engagement and illustrate the broader potential of citizen science in shaping equitable, community led public spaces. Overall, this research demonstrates how citizen science can move beyond data collection to become a co-creative process that empowers older adults and informs age-friendly urban transformation. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Anchoring sustainability: A new paradigm for maritime clusters
abstract: The environmental footprint of maritime transport, combined with growing social and regulatory pressure to tackle pollution, has brought the shipping industry to the forefront of the sustainability agenda. The role of industry clusters is becoming increasingly relevant to this discourse, given their influence across all dimensions of sustainability. Surprisingly, although this profound relationship is well documented, it has not received sufficient scholarly attention. This study analyses the highly fragmented literature on maritime clusters and sustainability using a novel combination of bibliometrics and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven thematic analysis. On this basis, a framework is developed that captures the interaction between clusters and the key components of sustainability. The findings suggest that sustainability should not be treated as an isolated strategic initiative or the outcome of regulatory pressure, but as a key dimension of cluster competitiveness. Overall, this study provides actionable insights for maritime practitioners and policy makers alike. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Perceived placeness in creative tourism: Conceptualization, scale development and implications for transformative experiences
abstract: Creative place-making combines cultural heritage, spatial design, creative symbolism, and experiential affordances to cultivate distinctive destinations, yet what tourists holistically perceive in these places remains underexplored. Drawing on atmospheric aesthetics theory, this study conceptualizes perceived placeness in creative tourism as tourists' holistic perception of the environmental and atmospheric qualities that make creative tourism destinations experientially distinctive. To operationalize this construct, content analysis was used to identify its dimensions and initial items. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses refined these items into a 20-item, five-dimensional scale comprising environmental qualities, historical-cultural embeddedness, creative-symbolic ambiance, restorative affordance, and emotional affordance. The nomological relevance of the scale was further established by examining its implications for transformative experiences via authenticity. Theoretically, this study positions perceived placeness as an integrative perceptual field between place-making and tourists’ psychological responses, and contextually elaborates atmospheric aesthetics theory in creative tourism. Practically, the scale provides a timely tool for evaluating and planning creative place-making efforts and curating meaningful tourist experiences. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: From growth mindset to social-emotional skills in early and mid-adolescence: A educational-cultural examination of an integrated mind-body-behavior framework
abstract: Background: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is a core educational goal, yet little is known about how adolescents’ cognitive beliefs, body-related self-perceptions, and everyday health behavior jointly relate to social-emotional skills across diverse cultural contexts and school stages. Objective: Based on mindset theory and self-regulation perspectives, we examined an integrated Mind-Body-Behavior framework in which growth mindset, positive body image, and health behavior show a theoretically specified pattern of associated with adolescents’ social-emotional skills. Sample: Participants were 62,105 adolescents from 15 regions where data were drawn from the OECD 2023 Study on Social and Emotional Skills. Methods: A two-stage quantitative design combined structural equation modeling and machine learning. Results: Growth mindset was associated with social-emotional skills both directly and indirectly associations via body image and health behavior. The direct association was substantially stronger than the combined indirect associations, indicating partial rather than complete support for the full proposed pattern. Scalar invariance across the seven clusters was not supported, so cluster-level comparisons were treated as descriptive. Associations differed between cohorts: the association between growth mindset and body image was stronger in the younger cohort, whereas the association between health behavior and social-emotional skills was stronger in the older cohort. Conclusions: The study contributes an integrated view of how beliefs, body-related self-perception, and health behavior relate to social-emotional skills. The framework shows that cognitive, body-related, and behavioral domains each relate to adolescents’ social-emotional skills and that these relations change between school stages. © 2026 The Authors

title: Greenhouse gas emission under a dual-disposability approach: Assessing environmental technical efficiency in the airline industry
abstract: This study provides a robust analysis of environment-adjusted airline efficiency under a dual-disposability assumption for undesirable output. It employs also a two-stage methodology to investigate the complex and heterogeneous relationships between airline operational profiles and their environmental efficiency. Technical efficiency is estimated in the first step using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) based on the Directional Distance Function (DDF) under both assumptions of the technological characterization of gas emissions, contractible versus non-contractible. In the second step, to analyze the factors influencing the estimated efficiency scores, a Tobit second-stage regression is employed. Results show that efficiency scores under strong disposability are systematically and significantly higher than those obtained under weak disposability, with an average difference of 11.9 percentage points. The findings also indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between the LCC variable and technical efficiency, implying that airline groups with LCC subsidiaries achieve higher efficiency levels. Based on their specific trade-off between operational and environmental inputs, the analysis of technical efficiency elasticities classifies airlines into five groups. These range from “Strong Proactive Environmental Performers” to “Low Efficiency High-Cost” groups, whose efficiency improvements are structurally linked to either an optimization or a deterioration of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions performance. The technical efficiency elasticity with respect to revenue share and to fuel efficiency are parallel across all airlines, while the elasticity for GHG consistently exhibits the opposite sign. We provide one of the few systematic comparisons of efficiency scores under weak versus strong disposability. This comparison allows us to quantify the systematic contraction in measured efficiency that occurs when greenhouse gas emissions are modeled as a technologically costly output rather than a costless byproduct. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Going green to compete: Male-biased operational sex ratio, status motivation, and men's relative green product preference
abstract: Motivating men to choose environmentally preferable products remains an important challenge. Across six studies, this research examines how operational sex ratio (OSR), defined as the ratio of reproductively available men to women, is associated with men's relative preference for green products over conventional alternatives. OSR can characterize a broader demographic environment or serve as a population cue in a local social setting. A cross-level analysis in China showed that men living in provinces with more male-biased OSRs assigned greater priority to environmental protection, whereas women showed no corresponding association. Randomized experiments showed that perceived male-biased OSR increased men's relative green product preference; perceiving a female-biased OSR did not produce a corresponding increase among women. Among men, the subsequent studies provided complementary evidence consistent with mediation by status motivation, linked male-biased OSR cues more closely to intrasexual competition motivation than to mate-attraction motivation, and showed that audience publicness moderated the indirect effect through status motivation. These findings extend sustainable-consumption research by identifying population composition as a social-environmental condition relevant to men's green product evaluations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: ResGAT: A residual graph attention network for technology transfer prediction in Chinese universities
abstract: University patent transfer in China remains sparse, and only a small fraction of university patents are licensed or assigned. Technology-transfer offices must still judge which patents are worth promoting and which enterprises are plausible recipients. Existing matching methods rely on content similarity, collaborative filtering, or shallow heterogeneous graphs. They rarely model patent–patent, patent–entity, and entity–entity relations together with patent attributes when positive transfer labels are extremely scarce. This study proposes a residual graph attention network (ResGAT) for technology-transfer object recognition. Built on three meta-paths, ResGAT uses relation-specific attention together with a shared feature transformation. It stacks residual graph-attention layers on the homogeneous branches to limit over-smoothing, and it uses a shallow cross-type branch to pass entity information to patents. A two-stage procedure then estimates transfer probability and ranks candidate transferees by dot-product similarity. On a civil-engineering patent graph from a Chinese university, and on seven strategic-emerging-industry subsets, ResGAT outperforms heuristic, linear, and multi-relational graph baselines under the same 10-fold protocol. The model also returns ranked enterprise lists for high-potential patents, so transfer offices receive a concrete shortlist rather than only a transfer score. © 2026

title: Descriptive or injunctive? The interactive effects of influencer type and social norms on alternative protein purchase intention
abstract: As alternative protein products attract increasing attention, understanding how social norm messages and influencer type jointly shape consumers’ purchase intention has become increasingly relevant. Drawing on schema congruity theory, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments with Chinese panel participants. The studies manipulated influencer type (human vs. virtual) and social norm framing (descriptive vs. injunctive), with regulatory-mode message priming introduced in Study 3. The results showed significant interactions between influencer type and norm framing. In Study 1, human influencers elicited higher purchase intention than virtual influencers under injunctive framing, whereas virtual influencers elicited higher purchase intention under descriptive framing. However, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention than injunctive framing within both influencer conditions. Study 2 provided evidence of moderated mediation through information processing fluency: the conditional indirect effect was significant for virtual influencers but not for human influencers. In Study 3, injunctive framing generated higher purchase intention than descriptive framing for human influencers under assessment-oriented priming, whereas this difference was not significant under locomotion-oriented priming. For virtual influencers, descriptive framing generated higher purchase intention under both priming conditions. These findings extend research on influencer marketing and social norms by identifying how influencer type and norm framing interact, highlighting information processing fluency as a potential explanatory mechanism and regulatory-mode priming as a boundary condition. They also provide practical guidance for selecting influencers and designing social norm messages in alternative protein marketing. © 2026 The Authors

title: Meaning in the age of AI: Experiencing less, needing more
abstract: What does it mean to be human when artificial intelligence (AI) can simulate human thought and creative labor with increasing fidelity? Unlike AI, humans experience meaning in life. Yet AI may create a paradox for meaningfulness. AI may reduce people's ability to experience meaning by disrupting selfhood (loss of effort and self-efficacy), social relationships (reduced mattering and connection), and culture (erosion of value and stability). At the same time, it may heighten people's need for meaning by challenging human exceptionalism and increasing the need for coherence amidst upheaval. This paradox—experiencing less while needing more—is what we term the AI Meaning Gap. Yet meaninglessness is not inevitable. If developed and used intentionally, AI could become a tool for reflection, understanding, and self-growth, thereby enhancing meaning. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Use of Social Network Analysis for community-led area-based fisheries management: The case of tropical lobster fisheries
abstract: Co-management is essential for successful community-based fishery reserves such as Mexico’s Fishing Refuge Zones (FRZs), but they can be hindered by gaps in institutional capacity that undermine collaborative governance. This study analyzes the governance networks underpinning FRZs in Punta Allen and Maria Elena, two small-scale fishing communities within the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve, Mexican Caribbean. Using a social-ecological system lens and social network analysis, we analyzed the structure, cohesion, and resilience of the governance networks of both communities, using semi-structured interviews and a weighted interaction index that integrates communication frequency and quality, trust, and collaboration. Results show structural differences between governance networks. Punta Allen exhibits a more decentralized, cohesive, and diversified network that links community actors, civil society organizations (CSOs), and government agencies, fostering multiple pathways for collaboration. María Elena presents a more centralized and segmented configuration, with strong dependence on CSOs and limited integration of governmental actors. Resilience simulations further demonstrate that decentralized structures maintain coordination under disturbance more effectively than centralized ones. Although FRZs are formally established by federal authorities, their local-level operational governance is sustained by informal social relationships that enable trust, reciprocity, and local coordination. Our findings show that FRZs can function as effective co-management instruments within MPAs, but their long-term viability requires strengthening institutional coordination, diversifying actor participation, and ensuring consistent governmental presence to reduce fragmentation. By diagnosing governance gaps and highlighting structural strengths, this study provides a transferable framework for improving the design, implementation, and policy uptake of community-based conservation and small-scale fisheries management initiatives. © 2026 The Authors.

title: When ads look worth keeping: Screenshotable design increases ad saving and Facebook ad liking
abstract: As social media advertising increasingly competes in fast-scrolling feed environments, an important but understudied question is whether some ads succeed by functioning less as transient persuasive messages and more as saveable information objects. Drawing on affordance theory and uses and gratifications reasoning, this research examines whether screenshotable ad design increases preservation-oriented engagement by making ads seem useful for later use. Across five studies, including controlled online experiments and a naturalistic simulated-feed experiment, screenshotable ads were associated with higher ad saving intention and Facebook ad liking relative to non-screenshotable ads. The results are consistent with perceived future utility as a mediating mechanism: screenshotable design increased perceived future utility, which in turn was associated with higher saving-related responses and Facebook ad liking intention. The process was stronger when consumers anticipated a future rather than immediate need, such that perceived future utility translated more strongly into ad saving and liking under future-need conditions. In addition, screenshotable design more strongly increased perceived future utility when information density was high rather than low, indicating that saveable structure is most effective when the ad contains enough substantive content to justify preservation. The findings contribute to consumer research on digital advertising response by identifying screenshotable ad design as a distinct visual structure that can shape consumers’ interpretation of an ad as a later-use resource, and they offer guidance for managers designing social media ads intended to be kept, revisited, and positively engaged with over time. © 2026

title: Corporate environmental credit rating and social stability: Evidence from capital-labor conflicts in China's polluting industries
abstract: Mitigating capital-labor conflicts is essential for maintaining social stability. Using China's Enterprise Environmental Credit Evaluation System (EECES) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the impact of corporate environmental credit rating on capital-labor conflicts. The results indicate that EECES reduces capital-labor conflicts in polluting industries by approximately 17.63%, although its effect weakens over time. Channel tests show that EECES mitigates capital-labor conflicts by reducing workers' pollution exposure risk, improving corporate environmental information transparency, and enhancing social trust in corporations. Moreover, in cities with weaker social governance capacity, EECES exerts a stronger restraining effect on capital-labor conflicts, suggesting that it effectively compensates for deficiencies in social governance. Further analysis reveals that although EECES reduces industrial output, it significantly promotes economic transformation. Overall, these findings highlight EECES as an effective policy tool for safeguarding social stability. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Beyond the accession event: Joint regional membership duration and completion of cross-border acquisitions
abstract: Cross-border acquisition (CBA) completion is often hindered by institutional barriers, imposing substantial costs on deal participants. While regional integration aims to reduce such barriers, prior research predominantly treats regional integration as a discrete accession event, leaving post-accession adaptation dynamics and their underlying mechanisms underexplored. Drawing on new institutional economics and social learning theory, we argue that joint regional membership duration increases CBA completion likelihood, with country-dyadic M&A stock serving as the mediating carrier via the sequential pathways of institutional alignment and social learning. We further examine how initial regulatory distance and cultural distance condition this mechanism. Using a sample of 8009 announced CBAs across the European Union (2010–2022), we find support for the mediation pathway and show that both regulatory and cultural distance weaken this indirect effect. This study advances the literature by moving beyond discrete event-based integration framing and refines the understanding of cross-national distance within integrated regional blocs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Community participation intensity on asynchronous biodiversity and human well-being responses to ecological restoration in global drylands
abstract: Ecological restoration serves as a key strategy for addressing desertification and ecosystem degradation in global drylands. However, achieving synergistic benefits for both biodiversity and human well-being remains a significant challenge for sustainability. Although community participation is increasingly promoted, quantitative evidence remains limited on how participation intensity is associated with measured ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. A dataset encompassing 744 effect sizes from 41 independent studies across global drylands was constructed to conduct a meta-analysis. The synthesis indicated positive benefits relative to degraded baselines, while composite biodiversity and composite human well-being showed asynchronous responses across community participation intensity. For composite biodiversity, the pooled mean estimate corresponded to an average increase of 122.11% relative to degraded baselines. Limited community participation was associated with long-term positive patterns in the composite biodiversity (159.35%) and composite human well-being (130.71%), whereas extensive community participation showed an evidence-limited and marginally supported positive tendency in composite human well-being in the short term. Eventually, we propose an adaptive framework in which livelihood-support components may be emphasized during early restoration, followed by lower-disturbance stewardship considerations as biodiversity recovery stabilizes. Overall, our findings provide exploratory quantitative evidence for discussing how community participation may affect asynchronous ecological and social outcomes in dryland restoration. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Mapping the evolution of communication research in aquatic conservation: A systematic literature review of emerging patterns and research opportunities (2015–2025)
abstract: This review examines the development of communication research in aquatic conservation through a systematic literature review. Although communication is increasingly recognized as crucial for environmental governance, promoting aquatic conservation remains underexplored and often treated instrumentally. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this review analyzed eleven articles (n = 11) published between 2015 and 2025, drawn from Scopus and Web of Science databases. Findings indicate that existing studies are predominantly presented in the Global North and tend to emphasize media representation, message framing, and individual behavioral change. These patterns suggest that communication is often conceptualized as a tool for disseminating information rather than as a broader social process. Most of the research described is qualitative, further strengthening the exploratory nature of the evidence. This review identifies limited engagement with systemic perspectives in understanding how communication shapes environmental responses. To address this, this study introduces Niklas Luhmann's social systems theory as an analytical lens for reinterpreting communication in aquatic conservation. From this perspective, communication is understood as a process of systemic resonance in which environmental issues are selectively interpreted across different social systems. This study contributes to the field by providing an exploratory synthesis of existing research and highlighting the need for more methodologically robust, geographically diverse, and theoretically grounded studies. The findings also underscore the importance of shifting from instrumental approaches to a more systemic understanding of environmental communication. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Expand or carve up? Evaluating market dynamics of premium airline entry with extended synthetic control methods: Evidence from STARLUX airlines
abstract: This study examines the effects of STARLUX Airlines' entry as a newly established premium full-service carrier on Taiwan's international air transport market. Using the synthetic control method (SCM) and an extended SCM framework, the analysis evaluates changes in passenger demand following the airline's entry, encompassing both single and multiple treated units, including individual routes and interconnected markets. A conditional growth model was subsequently employed to distinguish market expansion from demand redistribution. Results indicate that although only 9 out of 24 treated markets showed statistically significant expansion, STARLUX's entry still revealed latent demand and contributed meaningfully to overall market growth despite the relatively small size of STARLUX as compared to its primary competitors, China Airlines and EVA Airways. This effect was particularly evident in business-oriented and transfer-focused segments, while some tourism-driven and politically sensitive markets saw limited or negative responses. title: Mobile internet connectivity and climate change literacy in Africa
abstract: Addressing climate change requires individual behavioral shifts and a deep understanding of its impacts, yet the role of information and communication technologies (ICT), a powerful driver of social movements and cultural shifts, in shaping climate change literacy remains underexplored. This study addresses a critical gap by exploring how ICT, particularly mobile Internet connectivity, influences climate change literacy in Africa. I provide the first systematic evidence on the impact of mobile Internet connectivity on climate change literacy by exploiting variations in peer-based Internet connectivity in an instrumental variable strategy. Using newly georeferenced individual-level data on climate change literacy from over 42,000 respondents across 31 African countries, I show that mobile Internet connectivity has a modest yet robust effect on climate literacy, raising it by approximately 0.57 points for a typical adopter. Heterogeneity analysis shows that mobile Internet access primarily enhances the knowledge-based dimensions of climate literacy, particularly climate awareness and understanding, while also improving risk perceptions to a lesser extent. This suggests that mobile Internet contributes to climate literacy mainly by expanding access to factual information and knowledge about climate change. Suggestive evidence reveals that Internet connectivity can help close climate-related information gaps, among socio-economically disadvantaged groups, such as women, farmers, and those without formal education. Although Internet connectivity increases the frequency of using Internet and social media for news, there is no strong evidence that these platforms serve as channels linking Internet connectivity to climate literacy. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A Malatya Centrality-based algorithm for optimal solutions to maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover problems in lattice graphs
abstract: A lattice graph constitutes a fundamental graph type utilized across various domains and for addressing distinct challenges. The literature acknowledges a plethora of lattice graphs, each characterized by unique structures and attributes. Among the problems defined on lattice graphs are the Maximum Independent Set Problem (MISP) and the Minimum Vertex-Cover Problem (MVCP). MISP entails identifying the largest set of vertices in a graph that are not adjacent via edges. Conversely, MVCP involves determining the smallest set of vertices necessary to encompass all edges between nodes. Numerous methodologies have been suggested to resolve these issues within the context of lattice graphs. This research introduces an algorithm to address both MISP and MVCP on lattice graphs, leveraging the Malatya centrality algorithm. The algorithm calculates the centrality values of nodes within a lattice graph based on their degrees. Initially, it identifies the optimal solution set for MISP by employing the Malatya centrality values of the nodes. Subsequently, it ascertains the optimal solution set for MVCP based on the solution derived for MISP. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm was verified through its application to sample lattice graphs of varying sizes and configurations. It offers an efficient and robust solution in polynomial time across different lattice graph categories. Mathematical analysis and empirical studies on prevalent lattice graphs in the literature affirm that the algorithm yields optimal and effective resolutions for MISP and MVCP. Moreover, it generates solutions that are not contingent on constraints such as the number of iterations or initial conditions, and it produces effective outcomes in scenarios where integer linear programming methods fall short. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: DNA authentication of shark meat products from a major Chinese e-commerce platform reveals trade-name opacity and traceability limitations
abstract: Shark meat products are subject to a variety of regulatory and conservation frameworks, yet their characterization at the retail level is often constrained by the use of umbrella terms and limited species-specific information. In this context, the present study was designed as an exploratory case study examining shark meat products commercialized through a major Chinese e-commerce platform within a defined sampling period. Product descriptions, labeling information (including trade name, processing type, product presentation, declared production origin, and price), and molecular species identification obtained through DNA barcoding were jointly examined to characterize shark-derived products marketed through the platform. A total of 63 products were screened, and 165 tissue samples were analysed using COI and cytb markers. All products were marketed under generic umbrella terms, without scientific nomenclature, and prepackaged products showed variable labeling completeness. Molecular analyses detected at least one shark taxon in 61 of the 63 products examined, whereas the remaining two products contained billfish and batoid taxa. At the tissue level, 160 of 165 samples (97%) were assigned to shark taxa. Across all analysed samples, molecular identification revealed 12 species-level taxa, comprising 10 shark species (Alopias pelagicus, A. superciliosus, Carcharhinus brevipinna, C. limbatus, C. sorrah, Galeocerdo cuvier, Isurus oxyrinchus, Mustelus griseus, Prionace glauca, and Sphyrna lewini), one batoid species (Rhynchobatus australiae), and one billfish species (Istiophorus platypterus), together with three genus-level assignments including shark and billfish taxa (Scoliodon sp., Carcharhinus sp., and Kajikia sp.). The identified taxa include species listed as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, and Critically Endangered according to the IUCN Red List. The two products containing non-shark taxa represented cases of non-conformity between molecular identity and the available product information and therefore warrant discussion in relation to labeling practices. Overall, the findings illustrate the utility of molecular approaches for documenting species composition in online retail settings and provide an exploratory baseline for future investigations into species-level transparency, product information practices, and shark product commercialization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The allure of imperfection: How ugly-cute aesthetics drive purchase intentions
abstract: The rise of social media has increased both aesthetic diversity and consumer attention to product appearance and emotional appeal. This research examines the commercially successful yet under-researched “ugly-cute” aesthetic, exemplified by products like Pop Mart's LABUBU. Moving beyond traditional approaches that treat beauty (or ugliness) and cuteness as separate dimensions, we investigate their interactive effects through four studies: one field experiment and three online experiments, involving participants from both China and the United States. Our findings show that the combination of ugly-cute configurations can attenuate the purchase-intention disadvantage associated with ugliness-related aesthetic deviation, with this effect explained by perceived social value and moderated by consumption setting (public vs. private). Specifically, this effect is more pronounced in public consumption settings, where consumers are more likely to seek social approval and positive evaluation from others, thereby amplifying perceived social value in purchase decisions. These results advance the literature on product design and consumer aesthetics by identifying a psychological explanation underlying consumer responses to atypical aesthetics, and provide practical insights for designing products that generate perceived social value (e.g., feeling accepted, gaining approval, or being positively regarded by others). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Encountering the “familiar stranger”: Activating latent cultural identification among Vietnamese tourists in China
abstract: Tourism studies have largely examined cultural identification through encounters with difference, while paying less attention to culturally proximate travel contexts. Drawing on schema theory, this study examines how latent cultural identification (LCI) emerges when sedimented cultural meanings become perceptible and interpretable during travel. Based on interviews with 41 Vietnamese tourists traveling in China, the findings indicate that material, social, and mediated cues make routinized meanings noticeable, while internalized cultural schemata help tourists interpret them in relation to their cultural self-understanding. Affective resonance amplifies this process by intensifying the salience and self-relevance of interpreted meanings. Behavioural responses vary across compliance, inquiry, reinterpretation, and co-creation, reflecting different degrees of self-reflection and social embeddedness. By highlighting the role of cultural schemata in LCI, this study extends tourism identity research and shows how LCI can help tourists locate their own culture within the wider world-cultural landscape, enrich personal meaning-making, and foster intercultural exchange. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: From perceived attractiveness to visitation: Multi-scale measurement and influencing factors across 143 Chinese historic cities
abstract: Effective tourism management requires understanding how attraction attributes and supporting factors shape tourists’ perceived attractiveness, and how these in turn translate into visitation. We develop a tourist-centered framework using 610,136 reviews across 2128 heritage attractions in 143 cities, measuring multi-scale perceived attractiveness with a large language model pipeline and visitation with review volume, then identifying the factors that influence both metrics using XGBoost and SHAP. Results show that (1) perceived attractiveness and visitation share a multi-core spatial structure, while visitation displays a polarized long-tail distribution; (2) attraction attributes, especially official designation, visual quality, and ticket pricing, dominate both metrics but shape them differently; (3) positively perceived social, economic, scientific, historic and aesthetical values increase visitation, whereas political value is negatively associated; and (4) accessibility and spatial agglomeration also contribute positively. Practically, multi-scale benchmarking identifies underperforming attractions, while attraction-scale value profiles and the identified influencing factors guide targeted strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Beyond technological determinism: A multidimensional framework and research agenda for consumer trust in blockchain applications
abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly integral to domains such as finance, supply chain, commerce and tourism, yet consumer trust remains a pivotal barrier to its widespread adoption. Studies on trust in blockchain contexts have significant conceptual and contextual limitations that inhibit a holistic understanding of trust formation. In this study, we draw on the antecedents, decisions, outcomes and theory, context, methods (ADO-TCM) framework to systematically review 53 high-quality multidisciplinary studies. We identify three critical issues: (1) technological determinism that conflates technical capability with consumer trust, marginalising psychological, social and institutional factors; (2) theoretical convergence around acceptance models that obscures blockchain-specific trust phenomena; and (3) a narrow geographic and domain scope that creates self-reinforcing knowledge hierarchies limiting generalisability across applications and cultures. To address these gaps, we propose a multidimensional trust framework integrating three dimensions: technological architecture trust, information source trust and social actor trust, reflecting blockchain's sociotechnical structure. Central to this framework is a four-paradigm typology that classifies trust into interpersonal, technology, institutional, and sociotechnical perspectives, revealing that the prevalence of technological determinism reflects theoretical inertia rather than genuine consensus. We complement this with three research themes: multi-level theoretical integration, innovative methodologies and contextual expansion. This study contributes to the information systems discourse by providing a theoretical foundation for understanding trust in complex sociotechnical systems beyond acceptance models. By conceptualising consumer trust as a dynamic, multidimensional construct shaped by interactions between users, technology, and institutions, we offer a research agenda with actionable directions for advancing blockchain trust theory and practice. © 2026 The Authors

title: Registered Report Stage I: Signaling green, securing greenbacks: Sustainability claims and venture funding in hospitality & tourism start-ups
abstract: Tourism's sustainable transition increasingly depends on startups capable of scaling credible innovations. Yet to lead this transformation, they must convince investors that sustainability claims reflect genuine commitment rather than symbolism. This study tests whether, and under what conditions, startups' sustainability communication on X (Twitter) attracts external funding. Integrating signaling and legitimacy theory, we argue that costly, externally validated messages (e.g., stakeholder collaborations or investment-backed actions) enhance pragmatic legitimacy and capital inflow. Analyzing 3869 startups across 94 countries, we link few-shot-classified social-media posts with Crunchbase funding data using a multilevel hurdle model. The study positions startups as the vanguard of tourism's sustainable future, introduces investor funding as an outcome of sustainability communication, and demonstrates a scalable machine-learning approach for field-wide analysis. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: The adopter's conundrum: Institutional drivers and performance outcomes of innovation in travel distribution
abstract: This paper investigates the link between institutionally driven innovation and firm performance within the travel distribution sector. Focusing on the adoption of the New Distribution Capability (NDC), we employ a Difference-in-Differences (DID) methodology on a proprietary dataset of travel agency sales spanning four years. The results provide causal evidence that adoption leads to improved sales performance. Moreover, we identify a clear premium for early adoption, with dynamic effects accelerating over time, indicating that firms faster to adopt obtain superior results. The study contributes to the literature by validating the economic benefits of technological innovation using objective market data rather than subjective measures, offering key insights for managers navigating industry-wide technological shifts. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Inside and out: Exploring how internal and external CSR perceptions influence hospitality employees’ service sabotage
abstract: Although corporate social responsibility (CSR) has been shown to exert positive effects on hospitality organizations and their stakeholders, the interactive effect of internal CSR (ICSR) and external CSR (ECSR) perceptions on employees’ subsequent service behaviors remains unclear. Drawing on social cognitive theory and cue consistency theory, this study aims to explore how the interaction between ICSR and ECSR perceptions influences employees’ service sabotage. Time-lagged data were collected from 366 hotel employees at two time points and analyzed using hierarchical regression. The results indicate that the ICSR × ECSR interaction has a significant effect on employee service sabotage. Specifically, ECSR perceptions suppress service sabotage only when ICSR perceptions are high. This relationship is mediated by perspective taking. Furthermore, corporate reputational identification strengthens the negative effect of perspective taking on service sabotage. This study offers valuable insights for CSR practices in the hospitality industry and points to promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Structural Determinants of Household Resilience in Earthquake-Affected Communities: A Case Study from Bawean Island
abstract: This study examines the socioeconomic impacts of the March 2024 earthquake on household resilience in Bawean Island, East Java, Indonesia. Data for this study were collected through a survey with a snowball sampling technique, with a total of 221 valid respondents from affected regions. Using a household survey across 12 affected villages and partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study identifies critical factors contributing to household resilience, namely social, economic, human, and physical capital assets. The findings can be explained in two ways. First, the result confirms social, economic, human, and physical capital as critical resilience determinants. Second, higher household resilience could reduce the impact of natural disasters. This study can be an input for policymakers to strengthen household resilience in disaster-prone areas to support sustainable development goals (SDGs). © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.
