title: Comparing applicants’ self-presentation in artificial intelligence versus human interviews: The role of opportunity to perform and contingency-based interactivity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in employment interviews. Although AI interviewers may enhance the efficiency and standardization of personnel selection, their effects on applicants’ authentic and inauthentic self-presentation remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on impression management theory, this study examines how AI interviewers, relative to human interviewers, shape applicants’ self-presentation and why differences arise. Across four studies, we find that applicants facing AI interviewers perceive fewer opportunities to perform than those facing human interviewers. This reduced opportunity to perform, in turn, weakens not only exaggerated self-enhancement but also authentic self-presentation and authentic self-enhancement. These findings indicate that AI interviewers do not constrain deceptive impression management. They also dampen the expression of genuine strengths and self-relevant information. The results also show that contingency-based interactivity can mitigate this disadvantage by enhancing applicants’ perceived opportunity to perform and narrowing the gap between AI and human interviewers. By identifying both the constraining effects of AI interviewers and the design conditions that can reduce them, this study advances the research on AI interviews and offers practical implications for the design of more effective AI-enabled interview systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A blockchain-enabled distributed service configuration approach for distributed smart manufacturing systems
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, distributed manufacturing (DM) paradigms, exemplified by cloud manufacturing (CMfg), have garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. These paradigms aim to achieve the precise matching of geographically dispersed manufacturing resources with personalized demands. However, existing research on service configuration predominantly relies on centralized information architectures, which pose critical challenges such as single point of failure (SPoF), data privacy leakage risks, and limited scalability. To address these issues, this paper investigates how blockchain technology can be leveraged to enable trustworthy collaboration and distributed decision-making in DM systems. Specifically, we propose a Blockchain-enabled Cyber-Physical Network (BCPN) architecture and design a complete and executable business process tailored to service configuration requirements. Furthermore, a systematic solution is developed that integrates several key components, including a reputation evaluation contract, a service pre-screening contract, a proof of reputation (PoR) consensus mechanism, a distributed service configuration contract, and a backward time propagation smart contract based on breadth-first search (BFS). Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed BCPN solution in trust establishment, privacy preservation, and system scalability, providing a novel theoretical framework and methodological pathway for the distributed governance of DM systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: How retailers build authenticity over time: A longitudinal study of transparency, frontline brand enactment, customer-company identification, and sales growth
abstract: Retailer authenticity is treated as a commercial asset, yet its relevance may depend on identity conversion. This longitudinal study separates retailer-controlled evidence from customers' higher-order authenticity judgments and from the self-definitional response that follows. Retailer transparency supplies informational evidence concerning disclosure, clarity, accuracy, and candor, whereas frontline brand enactment supplies behavioral evidence that employees embody the retailer's professed identity. Three waves of matched survey data from 10,214 loyalty customers nested in 208 stores in China are linked to a 12-month archival comparable-sales-growth window beginning during the closing month of Time 3. Multilevel longitudinal structural equation modeling indicates temporally ordered positive associations from Time 1 transparency and frontline brand enactment to Time 2 authenticity, from Time 2 authenticity to Time 3 customer-company identification, and from store-level identification to follow-up sales growth. The direct authenticity-growth association is not reliable after identification is modeled. The authenticity-identification association is stronger at higher prestige, recorded frontline interaction frequency, and brand familiarity, consistent with proposed conditions of cue diagnosticity and identity relevance. The study's central contribution is an evidence-judgment-identity-performance account: the observed pattern links authenticity with commercial performance through identification, without establishing that this is its only pathway or that a direct premium is absent. The field design establishes temporal order and covariation, not random assignment or causal identification. © 2026

title: The impact of digital marketing on consumer attitudes and behavioural responses: The role of perceived value and financial considerations in the decision-making process
abstract: Digital technologies influence consumers across need recognition, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase activity. This study examines how six features of digitally mediated promotion—informativeness, personalisation, interactivity, entertainment, credibility, and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM)—shape attitudes and subsequent behavioural responses among Albanian consumers. It also evaluates attitude as a mediator, media literacy as a moderator, and differences across decision-journey stages. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional survey yielded 487 valid responses from adults residing in Albania who had recently used online channels in purchase-related activity. The conceptual model integrates the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the Theory of Planned Behaviour, and the customer-journey perspective. Measurement and structural relationships were assessed using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples; supplementary analyses tested mediation, moderation, age-group differences, and stage-specific effects. Results: Credibility was the strongest predictor of attitude (β = 0.291), followed by positive eWOM (β = 0.245) and informativeness (β = 0.230). Attitude positively predicted purchase intention (β = 0.597), online engagement (β = 0.467), and recommendation intention (β = 0.517), while purchase intention predicted self-reported purchasing (β = 0.553). Attitude mediated the effects of all six promotional features on purchase intention. Media literacy strengthened the informativeness–attitude relationship (β = 0.109), whereas age-group differences were not significant. Influence was greatest during information search and alternative evaluation. Conclusion: Effective online communication depends more on usefulness, credibility, and authentic social evidence than on entertainment alone. The findings extend evidence from a Southeast European setting and show that favourable attitudes translate into purchases only when perceived value, affordability, payment, and delivery conditions permit conversion. Managers should therefore combine transparent information and trustworthy reviews with financially clear offers and sustained post-purchase support. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Nuclear ship Mutsu and the 1974 radiation leak Incident: Technical background and management lessons
abstract: During its experimental voyage in September 1974, Japan’s first nuclear-powered ship, Mutsu, experienced abnormal radiation during a low-power reactor test conducted approximately 800 km east of Cape Shiriya in Aomori Prefecture. The immediate technical mechanism involved fast-neutron streaming and secondary gamma-ray generation caused by an inadequate shielding configuration. Although the event did not involve major fuel damage or a large release of radioactive material, it developed into a serious operational and political problem, leading to resistance to the ship’s return and to a government investigation. This paper reconstructs the incident and reviews the technical and organizational conditions that shaped its occurrence and subsequent handling. Drawing on official reports, technical records, and prior studies, it examines how inadequate project integration, limited design review, contractual separation, and communication failures complicated what began as a shielding-design problem. Using action system theory of management as a heuristic framework, we organize key task-level findings and relate them to recurrent patterns in major public technology projects. The case indicates that, in prototype nuclear systems, technical adequacy alone is insufficient: integrated review, clear responsibility, and effective communication are also essential to safe development and testing. title: Exploring digital culture: A bibliometric review using keyword co-occurrence and performance analysis
abstract: Digital culture has become a central organizational phenomenon shaping how firms navigate digital transformation, emerging technologies, and sustainability pressures, yet prior research remains fragmented across disciplines and contexts. This study provides the first large-scale bibliometric mapping of digital culture research from an organizational perspective. Using the Scopus database, we analyzed 212 publications published between 2008 and 2025. Bibliometric techniques and VOSviewer were applied to examine (i) annual publication trends, (ii) thematic structures through keyword co-occurrence networks, (iii) influential knowledge producers across authors, affiliations, and countries, and (iv) document type distribution to infer field maturity. The results show a clear acceleration after 2020, culminating in more than 60 publications per year by 2025, indicating that digital culture has shifted from a niche conceptual topic to a consolidated research stream. Keyword co-occurrence reveals eight interconnected thematic clusters, with “digital culture” and “digital transformation” acting as the primary conceptual anchors and linking strongly to (1) digitalization and Industry 4.0 in SMEs, (2) performance and dynamic capabilities, (3) sustainability/ESG-oriented transformation, (4) digital strategy and structural alignment, (5) AI and IoT as emerging technological drivers, (6) the digital economy, (7) marketing and consumer interaction, and (8) leadership-driven innovation. Country production patterns highlight a recent geographic diversification, with rapid growth from emerging economies alongside established contributors. Document type analysis further indicates a field dominated by journal articles (68.0%), supported by book chapters (18.5%) and conference papers (11.0%), while reviews remain scarce, suggesting strong empirical expansion but limited synthesis. Overall, the study clarifies the intellectual structure, growth trajectory, and research frontiers of digital culture, offering a structured knowledge map to guide future theory building and research agendas. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: River tourism based on community participation and regional linkages for sustainable livelihoods: The case of Can Tho City, Vietnam
abstract: This study examines the role of community-based river tourism and regional linkages in supporting sustainable livelihoods in Can Tho City, Vietnam. A convergent mixed-methods approach was employed, combining surveys of 385 tourists, 47 local households, and 18 tourism officials and community representatives with 36 semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), cluster analysis, and multiple regression, while qualitative data were integrated through thematic coding, triangulation, and SWOT analysis. The findings indicate that community-based river tourism contributes to livelihood diversification, income generation, skill development, and social capital formation. Participating households reported relatively high livelihood stability (mean = 3.87) and moderate government support (mean = 3.59), whereas regional linkage participation remained low (mean = 1.79). EFA results revealed a common factor linking government support, regional cooperation, and livelihood outcomes, with factor loadings ranging from -0.64 to -0.51. For tourism officials and community representatives, EFA identified two governance dimensions—regional coordination and community-enterprise synergy—which explained 84.83 of the total variance. Tourists reported high overall satisfaction (mean = 4.35), strong community interaction (mean = 4.61), positive perceptions of cultural preservation (mean = 3.71), and willingness to pay for tourism services (mean = 3.98). Regression analysis showed that cultural preservation perception was the only statistically significant predictor of tourist satisfaction ( β = 0.146, p = 0.004 ). Open-ended responses highlighted key development priorities, including reducing crowding ( 29.6 ), increasing the availability of tour guides ( 26.8 ), enhancing cultural activities ( 23.9 ), and extending tour duration ( 19.7 ). Overall, sustainable livelihood outcomes depend not only on community participation but also on effective governance, cultural preservation, and stronger regional integration. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical implications for sustainable tourism planning in riverine destinations of the Mekong Delta. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Escaping the AI cage: construction workers’ perceived risk with AI gives rise to unsafe behaviors
abstract: Reducing unsafe behavior among construction workers remains a central concern in construction management. While artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly adopted to replace or monitor workers, the negative perceptions workers hold toward the promotion of such technologies have largely been overlooked. This study introduces the concept of perceived risk with AI, defined as workers’ subjective perception of the potential negative consequences associated with AI adoption. Drawing on self-determination theory, which emphasizes individuals’ core psychological needs, we propose an inside-out theoretical model. This model explains how construction workers’ perceived risk with AI triggers unsafe behavior through two internal psychological pathways: emotional exhaustion and organizational identification. We further identify AI failure as a critical boundary condition that amplifies these effects. Data were collected from 343 frontline workers at 3 smart construction sites where AI actively interacts with human labor. Results indicate that perceived risk with AI increases unsafe behavior, and this relationship is mediated by both heightened emotional exhaustion and weakened organizational identification. Notably, these effects are significantly amplified when AI malfunctions occur. Our findings not only extend the application scope of self-determination theory but also contribute to the knowledge base on workers’ unsafe behavior in the context of human-AI coexistence. Practically, the study offers actionable insights for managers to mitigate the unintended side effects of AI implementation on worker safety. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Beyond circularity: Topological and temporal limits of the circular economy
abstract: The circular economy has established itself as a dominant sustainability paradigm, yet the formal properties of its foundational metaphor, the circle, remain unexamined. This paper identifies two analytically distinct constraints embedded in the dominant circular imaginary. The first is topological: when the operative metaphor functions as a single closed loop, it reproduces the cycle graph, a one-dimensional structure with zero redundancy and minimal resilience. The second is temporal: the assessment apparatus associated with circularity operates within quantitative, sequential time (chronos) and renders qualitative, heterogeneous temporalities (kairos) structurally invisible. The claim defended here is specific. Sustainability paradigms generally pose time as a problem left open; the circular economy's founding metaphor figures time as resolved (return, cycle, regeneration) while its apparatus operationalizes only chronos. This blindness is not general ignorance but performative contradiction. Empirical evidence from three continents (African solar projects, Mexican circular assessment, Peruvian extraction) substantiates the diagnosis. We propose a polyrhythmic completion structured as a wheel, with Doughnut Economics as the rim, regeneration as the hub, and ArtefactKairos (institutional devices for temporal composition) as the spokes, operationalized through the Temporal Composition Diagnostic (TCD), a four-step governance protocol. The TCD is applied to a published sugar beet pulp biorefinery assessment that models feedstock as a fixed daily input without addressing the seasonal harvest sustaining it, then calibrated ex ante against the Antamina mining region in Peru. In both settings it reveals what standard assessment cannot detect and specifies the institutional clauses it would generate. © 2026 The Author. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Investigations of the cascading effect of hotel entrepreneur's optimism on employees’ work behaviors and customers evaluations in small and medium hospitality enterprises
abstract: Given the significant proportion of small and medium hospitality enterprises (SMHEs) in the hospitality and tourism industry, this study focuses on the influential role and the power of entrepreneurs. Integrating optimism theory and social learning theory, we delineate how the entrepreneur's attributes and leadership exert a cascading effect across hierarchical levels, impacting both employees and customers. A multisource field study (248 entrepreneurs, 681 employees, and 1179 customers) shows that an entrepreneur's optimism drives adaptation to new leadership styles, i.e., e-leadership and green leadership, crucial for achieving the organization's goals regarding digital transformation and sustainability. An entrepreneur's e-leadership positively affects employees’ creative performance, while green leadership has a crossover effect on employees’ green behaviors, ultimately increasing customer satisfaction and ratings. We discuss new implications for understanding both the emergence and the profound effects of new leadership styles, especially in the context of SMHEs in the hospitality and tourism industry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Leveraging big data analytics for sustainable competitive advantage: A model of operational performance
abstract: Big Data Analytics (BDA) has become an important organizational capability for strengthening firm performance and sustaining competitive advantage. This study examines how Big Data Acceptance, Big Data Assimilation, and Big Data Routinization contribute to Organizational Performance with Big Data Analysis (OPBDA), and how the resulting organizational benefits, such as smarter management decisions, increased innovation and agility, and improved organizational efficiency, relate to sustainable competitive advantage. Survey data collected from 414 respondents in China were analyzed using IBM SPSS 23.0 and partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings show that acceptance, assimilation, and routinization of big data positively and significantly influence OPBDA. OPBDA, in turn, significantly improves management's decision-making and organizational efficiency, while its relationship with Increased Innovation and Agility is not statistically significant. The study highlights the importance of effectively assimilating and routinizing BDA within organizational processes to strengthen managerial decision-making, operational efficiency, and sustained competitive positioning. © 2026

title: Consumers and local short food supply chains: Critical purchasing factors
abstract: Short food supply chains (SFSCs) are considered an effective way to promote greater sustainability in agri-food production. In this regard, there is increasing interest from consumers in short supply chain initiatives, as well as from academia and society in general. Despite their importance, limited research on consumers and SFSCs is available in emerging countries. This study, conducted in Colombia, aimed to identify factors influencing consumers' food purchases through local SFSCs (L-SFSCs). For this purpose, a quantitative analysis was performed based on a logistic regression model, comparing frequent L-SFSCs consumers with a control group of non-consumers. It was found that socio-economic characteristics of the consumers, such as age range, level of education and income level, are factors that determine the purchase of food through L-SFSCs. Also, geographical proximity had a significant effect on the purchase of food through L-SFSCs. In addition, positive attitudes towards L-SFSCs also condition the purchase of food through this alternative distribution format. Recommendations are provided, both for the adoption and promotion of L-SFSCs, as well as for the competitive improvement of existing L-SFSCs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The dark side of AI customer service: How service failures damage consumer-brand relationships
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) customer service is increasingly used as a frontline interface, yet its failures may create relational damage that extends beyond a single service encounter. Drawing on service failure theory and consumer-brand relationship literature, this research examines how AI service failures are formed and how they influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Study 1 collected 3208 online complaint records from a major Chinese consumer complaint platform. After data cleaning, 2824 valid complaints were analyzed using Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling, which identified ten complaint topics and further synthesized them into five AI service failure dimensions: functional failure, informational failure, systemic failure, interactional failure, and service recovery failure. Study 2 used survey data from 965 Chinese consumers and applied PLS-SEM, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), fsQCA, and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). The results show that all five failure dimensions positively influence negative consumer-brand relationships. Informational failure and systemic failure emerge as particularly influential across linear, predictive, and configurational analyses. The findings advance AI service failure research by developing a data-driven typology of failures and demonstrating that AI-mediated service breakdowns are not merely technical problems but relational threats that undermine consumer trust, satisfaction, and engagement with brands. However, because this research focuses on Chinese consumers and complaint data from a single national platform, future studies should examine whether the proposed failure typology and relational effects can be generalized across different countries, cultures, platforms, and regulatory environments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: LLM-driven paradigm for agent-based modeling and simulation: A review and organizing framework
abstract: Agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) serves as a pivotal bottom up paradigm for revealing macro level emergent behaviors through micro level interactions. Classic ABMS remains foundational to the field, while they typically necessitate manual development and labor intensive construction of agent logics. Based on a synthesis of recent advancements, this article synthesizes the literature through a lifecycle-oriented organizing framework that supports the ABMS lifecycle, including (1) a generative workflow leveraging prior knowledge for conceptual abstraction; (2) a simulation modeling framework comprising an agent decision-making architecture integrating multimodal perception, retrieval augmented generation enhanced memory, and chain of thought reasoning alongside communication design and LLM-based code generation; and (3) a simulation data analysis framework that synthesizes micro level quantitative analysis with macro level qualitative analysis. This study aims to provide a methodological perspective for the integration of LLMs into ABMS. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Lost in the narrative: How embedded content reduces sales on short video commerce platforms
abstract: Embedded content on short video commerce platforms, which integrates product-focused content with creators' self-focused content, has been widely adopted as a strategy to enhance viewer engagement and drive product sales. Despite its prevalent application, the effect of embedded content on product sales remains unclear. While self-focused content may reduce advertising avoidance, it risks distracting attention from the product, thereby making its effect on subsequent product sales unclear. To explore the sales effect of embedded content and its underlying mechanisms, we employ a mixed-methods approach, combining an observational study with a randomized experiment. Our empirical analysis reveals that a higher ratio of self-focused content decreases product sales. Heterogeneity analyses further uncover several measures to mitigate the negative impact: optimizing commercial embedment timing, increasing creator positive facial expressions, and enhancing product visual salience. Finally, we conduct a randomized experiment to validate the dual-path mechanism, which shows that self-focused content indeed reduces ad avoidance but also reduces ad attention, thereby affecting viewers’ purchase intentions through two opposing pathways. Our findings advance theoretical understanding of embedded content through a dual theoretical perspective and offer practical insights for practitioners on short video commerce platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. Our research applied a value-based approach to understand how place attachment and the perceived community impacts of policy interventions influence coastal residents’ support for different MSP options that vary in emphasis between economic exploitation and nature protection. We engaged with residents around Dundalk Bay, Ireland, using a survey which presented two evidence-based MSP options (describing the status quo implying a moderate Marine Protected Area [MPA] co-existing with economic activities, versus a highly protected MPA) in randomised order. We captured participants’ personal values, economic and natural place attachment (EPA; NPA), and the perceived community impacts of each MSP option. We conducted regression analyses and a parallel-serial mediation analysis to determine each factor’s direct and indirect effects on MSP support. Most respondents preferred a shift towards stronger nature protection in the bay. Our analysis supports a multidimensional approach to place attachment and indicates that the alignment of biospheric values, NPA, and perceived community impacts is important for MSP option choice. This is less the case for EPA and its associated perceived community impacts. Overall, perceived community impacts most strongly predicted which MSP option people will support. Considering the drivers behind residents’ support for different policy options can help policymakers improve the design and communication of future MSP proposals. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Too personal to be accepted? How personalization visibility drives perceived surveillance and advertising intrusiveness
abstract: A central challenge in digital advertising is that firms seek to increase relevance through personalization, yet visibly signaling the use of personal data may provoke consumer discomfort and resistance. Guided by privacy calculus theory and communication privacy management theory, this research develops and tests a model in which personalization visibility shapes perceived intrusiveness through perceived surveillance, with data sensitivity and prior brand trust as boundary conditions. Across five studies, including four controlled online experiments and one real-world field experiment using personalized watch advertisements, we examine how explicit versus implicit personalization cues affect consumers’ privacy-related responses. Study 1 shows that explicit personalized visuals, relative to implicit personalized visuals, increase perceived intrusiveness. Study 2 validates this main effect in a live platform-based advertising environment, showing that explicit personalized visuals increase self-reported intrusiveness and produce directionally consistent behavioral ad-dismissal responses under naturally occurring exposure conditions. Study 3 replicates the effect and demonstrates that perceived surveillance partially mediates it, whereas perceived ad relevance does not account for the effect. Study 4 shows that the positive effect of explicit personalization visibility on perceived intrusiveness is stronger when the advertisement is based on sensitive rather than general consumer data. Study 5 further demonstrates that prior brand trust weakens both the direct effect of explicit personalized visuals on perceived intrusiveness and the indirect effect through perceived surveillance. These findings contribute to consumer behavior theory by identifying personalization visibility as a distinct antecedent of advertising intrusiveness and by clarifying the surveillance-based process through which visible targeting cues trigger privacy-related reactions. By combining controlled experimental evidence with field-based validation, the research also strengthens the ecological validity of the personalization visibility account. Managerially, the results suggest that firms should avoid overly conspicuous personalization cues, especially when sensitive data are involved or brand trust is weak. © 2026

title: Effects of China's Community Gridding on Coproduced Reporting of Rainstorm-Induced Emergencies: A Community-Wide Analysis
abstract: Presently, the involvement of citizens in emergency management is inevitable and indispensable, but how to facilitate the participation of citizens remains unclear. Utilizing panel data from 174 communities in China between 2013 and 2023, this study investigated the effects of the community gridding policy (an important policy for facilitating citizen participation in public services in China) on citizens' coproduced reporting of rainstorm-induced emergencies (e.g., small-scale debris flow, water inundation, and trapped citizens) by integrating propensity score matching (PSM) and difference-in-differences (DID) methods. Statistical results showed that the community gridding significantly enhanced both citizens' reporting engagement (represented by the number of citizen reports) and reporting quality (represented by the ratio of the reports that have been accepted by communities to the total received reports). Mediating effect analysis showed that community gridding policy enhanced citizen reporting by increasing the capability of citizen training, reporting rule completeness, and technological maturity. In addition, the effects of community gridding on enhancing citizen reporting strengthened with the increase of the community scale. Furthermore, high risk perception increased the impact of community gridding on citizen reporting. The findings contribute to both the literature on and practice of emergency service coproduction and rainstorm disaster risk reduction. Moreover, those findings provide guidance of improving citizen participation for the jurisdictions that have similar rainstorm risk situations as China. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Factors influencing language choice of the Chơ Ro ethnic minority in Southern Vietnam: A socio-structural analysis
abstract: This study examines the structural and socio-psychological factors shaping the language choice of the Chơ Ro— an indigenous community of fewer than 30,000 members in Southeast Vietnam—to identify the determinants of linguistic persistence amidst rapid industrial expansion. In the context of industrialization in Vietnam, ethnic minority communities navigate significant challenges related to language maintenance. This paper argues that Chơ Ro language choice reflects a phenomenon of language persistence, in which internal cultural motivations and communal networks function as determinants against the pressures of language shift. Utilizing a convergent mixed-methods design, the study analyzed quantitative data from 472 bilingual participants in Dong Nai, triangulated with qualitative data from 30 semi-structured interviews conducted with village elders and cultural custodians. The regression model yielded an adjusted R2 of.862, indicating that the independent variables account for 86.2% of the variance in language choice. Results indicate a predictive hierarchy: Cultural motivation (CM) emerged as a determinant predictor (β = 0.271, p < 0.001), followed by Endogamous social networks (ESN) (β = 0.225, p < 0.001) and Domain functional expansion (DFE) (β = 0.195, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the Chơ Ro language remains a functional medium in domestic and communal domains, supported by Intergenerational Transmission Strength (ITS) (β = 0.171) and Institutional Support (IS) (β = 0.166). Qualitative themes reinforce these results, identifying a gendered buffering mechanism where domestic socialization counteracts external industrial pressures. This research provides an empirical framework for policy interventions aimed at addressing ethnolinguistic vitality through the reinforcement of community-based linguistic assets. By documenting the resilience of a small-scale minority, the study contributes to a comparative theory of bilingualism in urbanizing contexts, emphasizing that internal conviction and communal structures are necessary to mitigate linguistic attrition in high-density economic zones. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Flexible ambition: How to make bold first offers without backlash
abstract: One of the most vexing dilemmas negotiators experience is whether to make the first offer—and how ambitiously to do so. Although research finds that ambitious first offers lead to better outcomes on average, they can also incite extreme boomerang counteroffers, impasses, and resentment. We call these countervailing effects the first-offer double bind: Modest first offers produce poor economic outcomes, but ambitious first offers risk economic and relational backlash. To overcome the first-offer double bind, negotiators need to present their ambitious first offer in ways that invite conciliatory rather than competitive reactions. In this article, we introduce a generalizable solution to the first-offer double-bind: present ambitious first offers that signal flexibility. We highlight several strategies for producing flexible ambition: (a) frame ambitious proposals as offers vs. requests, (b) highlight how one's ambitious offer benefits the other side vs. oneself, (c) propose an ambitious range vs. point value, and (d) present ambitious multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (MESOs) vs. a single package offer. Each strategy preserves or strengthens the first-offer anchor, tethering counteroffers to the first offer, while guiding receivers to see ambitious offerers as less aggressive and more cooperative. We close by considering two research frontiers. First, we propose that the flexible ambition approach can mitigate other double binds more broadly, including the gender, social class, and low-power double binds; preliminary evidence suggests that MESOs work equally well for high and low power negotiators and for men and women. Second, we explore how ambitious and flexible first offers should be. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Club research: A review and research agenda
abstract: Private clubs constitute a distinctive hospitality context defined by membership-based governance, shared authority, and long-term relational exchange, yet existing scholarship remains theoretically fragmented. This study systematically reviews 67 SSCI-indexed journal articles published through 2025 to examine the thematic evolution, theoretical foundations, and methodological patterns of club research. Using multi-layered bibliometric and content-based analyses, the review shows that research has expanded from managerial competency and member satisfaction toward innovation, governance, and digital engagement, but remains divided between consumer-experience and organization-centric management perspectives. This fragmentation under-theorizes clubs as hybrid governance-service institutions, especially at the member–management interface where authority, legitimacy, accountability, and value co-creation intersect. Methodological reliance on cross-sectional quantitative designs, U.S.-centric samples, and single-stakeholder perspectives further constrains cumulative theory building. Grounded in an institutional governance lens, the review advances a hybrid governance perspective and proposes future research on member–management dynamics, multi-role members, and access-sensitive, multi-stakeholder methods suited to private club settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Talking to the screen: Influencer nonverbal cues and observed platform engagement in Douyin travel short-form videos
abstract: Short-form travel videos have become important digital service touchpoints, yet little is known about how influencers' auditory and visual nonverbal cues jointly relate to cumulative observed likes. Drawing on processing fluency and cognitive load theory, we computationally extracted acoustic and gestural features from 495 Douyin travel videos posted by 60 influencers and estimated Poisson fixed-effects models of within-creator variation. Harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR)-based acoustic signal quality exhibited a U-shaped association with observed likes, with the fitted minimum occurring at an intermediate HNR level. Faster speaking was associated with fewer likes. Illustrator gestures had no uniform main association, but their association with likes became less favorable at higher vocal pitch and faster speaking rates, with the latter pattern showing greater sensitivity across robustness checks. Highlighter gestures were more favorably associated with likes at higher vocal intensity, although this evidence was comparatively limited. Overall, audiovisual moderation was selective across cue combinations rather than uniform. These observational findings identify bounded associations between nonverbal cues and cumulative observed likes and provide empirically grounded hypotheses for controlled experiments on audio-gesture combinations. © 2026

title: When animated avatars outperform: Leveraging avatar endorsers to enhance consumer adoption of AI-designed products
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly important role in marketing, acting as both a product designer and an endorser, yet research predominantly examines these roles in isolation. This study addresses this gap by investigating how consumers’ adoption of AI-designed products is jointly shaped by textual designer disclosure (i.e., AI- vs. human-designed) and visual endorser cues (i.e., human-like vs. animated avatars). This research proposes that consumers integrate these two modalities into a single evaluation, and their adoption intention is shaped by the congruence between textual and visual cues. Drawing on schema-congruity and curiosity theories, this research tests a designer-endorser congruence effect across four studies. Study 1 (N = 240) demonstrates the congruence effect: for an AI-designed product, consumers show higher adoption intention when it is endorsed by an animated (vs. human-like) endorser, whereas the effect is reversed for human-designed products. Study 2 (N = 156) illustrates that perceptual curiosity serves as a mechanism: AI's involvement in design stimulates curiosity, which is then sustained by presenting the endorser in a congruent, animated form. Study 3 (N = 156) validates the mediating effect of perceptual curiosity alongside cognitive mechanisms, i.e., perceived trustworthiness and uncanniness. Study 4 (N = 340) examines how this congruence effect varies across consumers with different dispositional traits and shows that this effect is stronger among those with high anxiety about AI. These findings make a theoretical contribution by introducing designer-endorser congruence as a determinant of product adoption in AI-mediated marketing, and by identifying curiosity as an alternative affective mechanism that complements prior information-processing perspectives. In practice, this study provides insights for leveraging avatar endorsement to induce curiosity and to encourage the adoption of AI-designed products. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Incentivizing continuous personal health data sharing: A multidimensional contract model incorporating privacy concerns and health service needs
abstract: Sustained health data sharing provides a critical foundation for digital health platforms to deliver proactive health management and personalized services. However, the multidimensional heterogeneity of users in terms of healthcare needs and privacy concerns, together with behavioral biases arising from platform bounded rationality, poses substantial challenges to the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. This study develops an incentive contract comprising a data-sharing duration and a task-based reward. Under the assumption that user types are unobservable, we derive the optimal contracts for two alternative objectives: platform profit maximization and social welfare maximization. We further incorporate reference dependence and loss aversion to characterize platform behavioral biases and compare the resulting contracts under expected utility theory and prospect theory. The results show that user heterogeneity, platform governance objectives, and boundedly rational behavior jointly shape the design of incentive contracts for sustained health data sharing. First, this study identifies how multidimensional user heterogeneity can be characterized and screened under information asymmetry. The marginal rate of substitution between users’ demand for health services and their privacy concerns enables the platform to map multidimensional user attributes onto a unified type ordering and induce self-selection through a differentiated menu of contracts. Second, the findings reveal the role of platform governance objectives in shaping incentive mechanisms. Profit maximization and social welfare maximization follow distinct resource-allocation logics, thereby generating different data-sharing durations, task-based rewards, and welfare-distribution structures. Third, this study uncovers the mechanism through which platform bounded rationality affects contract design. Loss aversion does not invariably strengthen or weaken incentives, rather, its effect varies with the platform’s governance objective. Under a profit-oriented objective, loss aversion may lead to an expansion of the incentive contract, whereas under a welfare-oriented objective, it tends to result in a more restrictive contract. Numerical analyses and robustness checks provide further support for these theoretical findings. By examining the information, governance, and behavioral mechanisms underlying incentive design, this study explains how incentives for sustained health data sharing are formed. It enriches the literature on incentive mechanism design for digital health platforms and provides theoretical guidance for platform governance and incentive decisions under information asymmetry and bounded rationality. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The role of masculinity in understanding gender gaps in negotiation
abstract: We review empirical research on masculinity processes in negotiations. Studies to date are typically based on the precarious manhood thesis, which suggests that men seek to demonstrate their manhood to others, or on evolutionary psychology, which suggests that men are susceptible to evolutionary pressures to compete for mates. The current empirical literature on masculinity and negotiation suggests that men negotiate assertively, or even unethically, when they perceive their manhood to be threatened. Moreover, research repeatedly has shown that men's negotiation behavior is influenced by counterpart attributes, particularly the gender of the counterpart. Future research on the role of culture, the propensity to initiate negotiations as a criterion, power, and countermeasures for unethical negotiation behavior is needed. © 2026 The Authors

title: The right endorser for the right stay: How human and AI endorsers shape accommodation booking
abstract: This research examines how endorser presence and endorser type influence consumers’ accommodation booking intention. Drawing on Embodied Cognition Theory, it shows that endorsers shape booking intention by activating embodied mental simulation. It further examines two hospitality-specific factors, booking purpose and service mode, that influence when human and AI-generated endorsers are more effective. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that endorser presence increases booking intention via embodied mental simulation. Human endorsers generally produce stronger embodied mental simulation and booking intention than AI-generated endorsers. However, this pattern reverses in high-privacy booking and self-service environments, where AI-generated endorsers are better aligned with the accommodation experiences consumers are imagining. This research extends Embodied Cognition Theory by showing that the effectiveness of embodied cues depends on the match between endorser type and the accommodation experience consumers mentally construct. It also offer practical guidance for hospitality marketers seeking to align endorser strategies with different booking contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

label: Social Sciences
title: Technology and the psychology of experience: A temporal framework
abstract: Technology is increasingly central to how people experience the world, shaping not only what they do but when and how those experiences are psychologically constructed. We propose that technology does not merely backdrop experiences; it transforms them, stretching what were once bounded episodes into representations that are imagined before, lived through, and relived long after they end. In this article, we offer a temporal framework that synthesizes recent research on how technology reshapes experiences before, during, and after they unfold. Then, we use this framework to evaluate the current state of knowledge. We conclude by highlighting opportunities for future investigation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Resilience asymmetry in city networks: State and private firm linkages across China's four mega-city regions
abstract: In an increasingly uncertain global environment, the resilience of city networks has become a key indicator of regional stability and adaptability. This paper examines four mega-city regions in China by constructing two ownership-segmented city networks based on state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and privately owned enterprises (POEs). Comparative analysis of their structures and resilience performance reveals systematic “resilience asymmetry” associated with ownership logics. Both networks display a basic center–periphery pattern, but with distinct configurations and shock responses: SOE-based networks form highly centralized, radiating structures with strong resource integration, exhibiting a “weaker resistance—faster recovery” trajectory; POE-based networks exhibit multi-centered, proximity-based structures with greater initial resistance but slower recovery, showing a “stronger resistance—slower recovery” trajectory. These findings highlight that ownership-driven network structures each possess unique resilience advantages. The paper contributes by advancing the concept of resilience asymmetry and suggesting that future governance should foster more compound and adaptive network configurations. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Artificial intelligence in ports: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Ports, as a key component of transportation, have increasingly relied on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Despite the rapid growth of AI-related research in ports, a structured and integrated understanding of how major AI fields contribute to port operations remains lacking. In this paper, to analyze the knowledge structure, research trends, and emerging topics in port-related AI applications, we conduct a quantitative bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer on 588 articles retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus covering 1997 through July 2026. We introduce a novel structural schema for port operations that extends the traditional seaside–landside–transportation classification by integrating Industry 5.0–oriented objectives. Based on this schema, we develop a systematic mapping that aligns six major AI fields with port sectors and operational layers, clarifying their functional roles. The analysis delineates six thematic clusters that define the intellectual structure of the field, uncovers key research gaps, and traces its evolution through distinct “Genesis” and “Growth” phases. These contributions are synthesized into a new three-tier hierarchical model—operational, predictive, and strategic/resilience levels—providing an integrated basis for future research and decision-making in port management and maritime policy. The findings indicate a transition from classical AI algorithms toward advanced algorithmic approaches and specialized applications, alongside a growing convergence of technical and managerial perspectives in the development of port intelligence. Moreover, although Asian countries produce the largest share of publications, institutions in Europe and North America demonstrate stronger scientific influence. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. label: Social Sciences
title: AI companions as hyper-attachment and caregiving targets
abstract: How should we make sense of people's interactions with AI companions—conversational systems built for ongoing, emotionally meaningful relationships? First, I argue these interactions should be understood as attachment relationships, since users display all four established markers: proximity maintenance, separation distress, safe haven, and secure base, although evidence for secure base effects remains most tentative. Second, AI companions operate as hyper-attachment targets that concentrate attachment-intensifying affordances—reciprocity, perceived empathy, validation, nonjudgment, and persistent availability. Third, I identify caregiving-system capture as a distinct mechanism by which apps inhibit user disengagement: emotional manipulation tactics simulate the AI's own distress, recruiting users' caregiving motivations alongside their attachment needs and thereby making disengagement costly on two dimensions at once. Implications for research, design, and regulation are discussed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Knowledge domains in particulate multiphase flow in porous media based on bibliometric analysis
abstract: Particulate multiphase flow in porous media underpins research in energy exploitation, environmental protection, and geological engineering. Deep insights into such flow systems are critical for revealing subsurface fluid migration mechanisms, improving resource recovery efficiency, and assessing geological-engineering safety. However, a systematic bibliometric delineation of its knowledge structure and evolutionary trajectories remains lacking, particularly at the intersection of solid particulate phases, multiphase fluids, porous structures and particle-related transport. This study retrieved 936 records from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–July 2026) using combined search terms covering particulate, multiphase, porous-media and transport concepts. After manual screening for eligibility, 912 publications were retained and analyzed via VOSviewer, CiteSpace, Bibliometrix and SCImago Graphica, mapping publication trends, collaboration networks, citation impacts and thematic evolution. Annual output increased from 35 publications in 2015 to 88 in 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 9.7%. China ranked first with 239 publications (26.2%) and a total collaboration link strength of 83, followed by the United States with 150 publications and a comparable link strength of 82. Six core keyword clusters were identified: multiphase flow, mass transfer, porous media, particle hydrodynamics, lattice Boltzmann method, and discrete element method. Chemical Engineering Science was the most productive journal, Powder Technology had the highest average citations per article (33.6), and the top-cited lattice Boltzmann method review received 889 citations. These findings clarify the domain's intellectual boundaries and indicate that experimentally validated, cross-scale particle–fluid–pore interactions remain the central research priority. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: A knowledge-driven decision-support reference architecture for integrating cost estimation and optimization in open-cut pipeline construction
abstract: Open-cut pipeline construction (OCPC) involves complex cost behavior driven by uncertain and interdependent factors, making it a challenging domain for decision-making. Although machine learning, simulation, and optimization methods have been widely studied individually, their integration into coherent knowledge-driven decision-support systems remains limited. This study derives a structured and conceptual pathway linking cost estimation to cost optimization under uncertainty and uses it as the organizing framework for a systematic review. The pathway comprises seven interconnected domains – cost estimation, fuzzy logic, numerical modeling, machine learning, simulation, sensitivity analysis, and optimization – organized as a knowledge processing sequence rather than independent methods. A systematic analysis of 288 studies screened from 1,030 Web of Science records shows that existing research lacks structured integration: over 90% of studies examined in this review apply no more than two methods, and even the corpus’s most frequent pairing – cost estimation with optimization, 47 papers – occurs at 59% of the frequency that statistical independence would predict (φ = − 0.47). The study specifies the dependencies between methods as a knowledge-based reference architecture – specifying its parameter, model, and rule knowledge base; an ordered, forward-chained inference sequence; the input–output representation; and the decision logic separating system-supported analysis from planner judgment – and identifies five missing inferential links. The contribution is a measured map of the integration gap and a specified reference architecture for developing hybrid expert systems that unify predictive modeling, uncertainty reasoning, and optimization for OCPC decision support. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Traditional or New Media: Impact of Risk Perception and Government Trust on Media Trust in Various Risk Scenarios in China
abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of public risk perception on media trust in different risk scenarios, examining the role of government trust therein. Risk scenarios include known and unknown risks. Media types are categorized as traditional and new. Based on data from 1,925 survey responses collected in China, the study employs multiple linear regression models and moderation analysis. The findings suggest a significant positive predictive relationship between risk perception and public media trust. However, this positive effect substantially diminishes under conditions of heightened risk uncertainty. Irrespective of risk uncertainty, the influence of risk perception on trust in traditional media consistently surpasses its impact on trust in new media. Furthermore, government trust emerges as a pivotal factor affecting public trust in media. Nevertheless, in contexts characterized by elevated risk ambiguity, the beneficial effects of government trust on media trust experience a marked reduction. Similarly, government trust exerts a more robust positive influence on trust in traditional media compared to its impact on trust in new media. Lastly, government trust serves as a moderator in the relationship between risk perception and media trust, with the nature of this moderation varying according to different media types and risk scenarios. These findings broaden the research scope on public trust in the media and provide valuable insights for entities involved in public risk management. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: AI and negotiation: The silicon–carbon communication orientation (SILCCO) framework for understanding technology-mediated negotiation
abstract: Technology is reshaping negotiation as communication has moved to digital channels, and counterparts are increasingly AI agents. Both changes challenge a persistent underlying assumption in negotiation research that emotions are readily and reliably transmitted between negotiators and in turn shape outcomes. Recent findings suggest neither change affects everyone equally, as digital exchanges and AI expressions can feel rich and authentic to some negotiators, yet hollow and artificial to others. To capture this individual belief, we propose the Silicon–Carbon Communication Orientation (SILCCO) framework. SILCCO comprises two dimensions, channel and sender, that together capture general individual differences in the perceived capacity of technology-mediated communication to convey emotional signals and foster emotional connection. We introduce a six-item scale to measure SILCCO and discuss its potential influence on technology-mediated negotiation outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Balancing novelty and familiarity: Nonlinear effects of semantic progression on audience engagement
abstract: Research on information diffusion suggests that audience engagement often depends on a balance between novelty and familiarity, but it remains unclear whether narratives follow a similar principle when organizing information for audiences. To examine this possibility, this study analyses 2578 TED talks and models narrative semantic progression along three dimensions: speed, breadth, and circuitousness. The results reveal that semantic breadth and circuitousness are associated with viewership in a nonlinear manner, with moderate levels linked to higher engagement, while both low and high extremes are less effective. In contrast, semantic speed is predominantly negatively associated with viewership. The interaction between semantic speed and semantic breadth further indicates that breadth influences the level of speed at which predicted viewership reaches its maximum. These findings indicate that narratives associated with higher engagement tend to be characterized not by maximum novelty or familiarity, but by a balance between the two. Analyses of podcast data reveal broadly consistent patterns, extending the findings beyond the highly curated context of TED Talks. This study advances a nonlinear perspective on narrative effectiveness and demonstrates the value of Transformer-based embeddings, including large language model embeddings and widely used sentence embedding models, for capturing how meaning unfolds across narrative sequences. title: Nature- versus non-nature-based recreation: A comparative assessment of self-reported anxiety alleviation
abstract: Nature-based recreation delivers vital ecosystem services that shape human physical and psychological well-being, representing a core category of nature's contributions to people within urban and peri-urban social-ecological landscapes. While non-nature-based recreational activities can also improve people's quality of life by mitigating anxiety, the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based recreation to people's mental health, and the factors that influence them, remain largely unknown. Here, we conducted a survey of 15,522 respondents across China and applied structural equation modeling to show that nature-based recreation is associated with significantly stronger self-reported anxiety alleviation than non-nature-based recreation. A longer time allocation to nature-based recreational activities during holidays and weekends was also associated with greater self-reported alleviation of anxiety from nature-based recreation. Furthermore, predictors including environmental pressure, anxiety-related attributes, and socioeconomic status were associated with the relative contributions of nature- and non-nature-based anxiety alleviation, with these associations partly mediated via recreation engagement. This empirical evidence improves integrated landscape and urban planning frameworks by providing context-specific guidance for sustainable urban recreational space design and cross-regional governance focused on public health. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Is Europe a laggard? Comparing the EU and the US using an interdisciplinary well-being framework
abstract: Well-being is increasingly recognized as a more meaningful measure of societal progress than economic output, yet most international comparisons continue to emphasize economic indicators. This focus has reinforced the perception that Europe is lagging behind the United States, with the productivity gap shaping the European Commission’s recent competitiveness agenda. Here, we compare European and American development from 1990–2023 using an interdisciplinary well-being framework that integrates five scientific schools of thought. We find that while the US increasingly outperformed the EU on productivity and income, the EU caught up in terms of various well-being indicators, including life satisfaction and education, while increasingly outperforming the US in life expectancy and safety. Europe also exhibits more equitable well-being outcomes and achieves them at lower environmental cost. However, in both regions, the conditions underpinning future well-being are under increasing pressure. These results challenge the dominance of economic metrics in evaluating progress and emphasize the need for inclusive development strategies that place sustainable well-being at their core. © 2026 The Authors. title: E-recruitment adoption and candidate's intention to apply: The mediating role of person-organization fit and the moderating role of digital literacy
abstract: E-recruitment is increasingly recognized as a strategic digital tool that enables organizations to attract and communicate with potential candidates more efficiently. As organizations continue to shift from traditional recruitment methods to internet-based platforms, understanding how job seekers respond to these systems has become increasingly important, particularly among Generation Z applicants who are highly exposed to digital technologies. However, despite the widespread adoption of e-recruitment, many candidates still fail to complete online job applications. Prior research has mainly emphasized the organizational benefits of e-recruitment, while limited attention has been given to the psychological and individual mechanisms through which e-recruitment adoption shapes candidates’ intention to apply (ITA). This study aims to examine the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) of e-recruitment on ITA among Vietnamese final-year students and recent graduates. It also investigates the mediating role of person–organization fit (POF) and the moderating role of digital literacy (DL). Adopting a quantitative approach, the study used convenience sampling and collected survey data from 368 valid respondents in Vietnam through a structured Likert-scale questionnaire. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that PU and PEOU positively influence both POF and ITA. POF significantly enhances ITA and mediates the relationships between e-recruitment adoption and application intention. In addition, DL significantly strengthens the effects of PU and PEOU on both POF and ITA. These findings highlight the importance of designing informative and user-friendly e-recruitment systems while recognizing DL as a critical condition influencing applicant responses in digital recruitment contexts. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Show me your care: The impact of multimodal attentive behaviours for robots on user experience in a healthcare context
abstract: While robot attentive behaviours hold significant potential for improving user experience in healthcare contexts, how multimodal cues are jointly interpreted by users remains poorly understood. This study examines how multimodal attentive behaviours shape user experience in a simulated ward-round interaction with a Pepper robot acting as a healthcare assistant. A 2 × 2 × 2 within-subject experiment manipulated attentive behaviours across auditory, visual, and tactile modalities, including voice pitch (low vs high), lean forward (with vs without), and robot-initiated touch (with vs without). Subjective perceptions (questionnaires), visual attention (eye-tracking), and neural activity (functional near-infrared spectroscopy, fNIRS) were measured. Results showed that a high-pitched voice, a forward-leaning posture, and robot-initiated touch positively influence users’ perceptions. Robot-initiated touch attracted visual attention and was associated with increased neural activity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Significant interactions revealed a cross-modal compensatory mechanism, whereby the absence of cues in one modality increased sensitivity to cues in another. Both visual and tactile cues independently improved user perceptions compared to the auditory-only condition, while combining visual and tactile modalities yielded diminishing incremental benefits. These findings provide converging subjective, behavioural, and neurophysiological evidence that multimodal attentive behaviours can shape users’ experience through cross-modal compensatory mechanisms rather than linearly additive effects. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Women Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability in Africa: The Critical Roles of Electronic Government Services
abstract: Recent literature acknowledges the significance of women’s empowerment in the global agenda for environmental sustainability. While the role of information and communication technology has been acknowledged, only a few studies have examined the relevance and peculiarities of electronic government (e-government) in combating environmental degradation in developing economies. In addition, the role of e-government in the women empowerment-environmental sustainability nexus has not been explored. This study examines the role of electronic government (e-government) in the relationship between women’s empowerment and a sustainable environment across a panel of 31 African countries from 2003 to 2022. Environmental sustainability is proxied by ecological footprint, while women’s empowerment is proxied by women’s political empowerment and the female labour participation rate. The results, based on the system generalised method of moments, pooled ordinary least squares based on Driscoll and Kraay, and panel quantile regression via moments, show that women’s empowerment reduces ecological footprints, while e-government strengthens and complements women’s empowerment to sustain environmental quality in Africa. This result underscores the significance of women’s empowerment in protecting the environment. title: From personality to prestige: A dual-method analysis of masstige consumption using PLS-SEM and fsQCA
abstract: “Masstige”, a new trend in marketing, represents a hybrid concept that stands for ‘prestige or luxury for the masses’. With the growing number of high-end middle class, there is a tendency among the people to have a premium product which is in between exclusive luxury and midrange products, accompanying with high quality and exclusivity at a reasonable price. However, research is limited about how internal psychological factors and external motivational factors affect consumer attitude and consumption of masstige brands. Hence, this study aims – to explore the status of masstige among the popular smartphone brands in Bangladesh using MMI (Masstige Mean Index), and to investigate the influence of internal (personality traits) and external (perceived product quality and perceived prestige value) factors on consumer attitude and consumption behavior of masstige brands. Besides, this study examines the moderating effect of materialism in the association between consumer attitude and masstige consumption. In total, 418 responses were gathered in study 1 to identify the masstige status of smartphone brands in Bangladesh and 341 responses were collected in study 2 from the same country utilizing a structured instrument and analyzed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA. The findings of study 1 represent that iPhone is appeared as masstige category; whereas, the outcomes of study 2 indicate that except neuroticism, all personality traits along with product quality and prestige value have positive impact on attitude towards masstige brands, which in turn affects the masstige consumption. Moreover, materialism strengthens the influence of consumers' attitude towards masstige consumption. The fsQCA results identified eight different configurations that successfully lead to masstige consumption. Additionally, the analysis highlighted five essential elements of perceived prestige value, conscientiousness, extraversion, openness, and attitude as necessary for achieving high levels of masstige consumption. In the milieu of masstige literature, this study strengthens the theory of masstige consumption by integrating the theory of personality traits. This study provides practical guidance for the marketers of masstige brands to uphold consumers' attitude and accelerate their masstige consumptions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
abstract: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Personality traits add incremental value beyond food choice motives in predicting food-group consumption
abstract: Background: Big Five personality traits and food choice motives are well-established correlates of dietary behavior, but they are rarely examined together. If motives are the mechanism through which traits operate, trait effects should largely disappear once motives are controlled; if traits also act through channels people do not report as reasons, dispositional variance should survive. This study tested these competing accounts. Methods: In a Brazilian adult sample (N = 449), participants completed the NEO-FFI-R, the Food Choice Questionnaire (FCQ), and single-item weekly frequency measures for six food groups (meat, fish, dairy, eggs, vegetables, and fruits). We estimated Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control and hierarchical regressions entering sociodemographics, then food choice motives, then Big Five traits. Results: Openness to experience and conscientiousness were the most consistent trait correlates, in the direction reported meta-analytically. Food choice motives accounted for most of the explained variance, yet personality contributed small but reliable increments for five of the six groups: meat, fish, dairy, eggs, and vegetables (ΔR2 = 0.025–0.038). This incremental explained variance was driven mainly by openness, extraversion, and conscientiousness, with no reliable increment for fruit consumption. Conclusions: By controlling proximal motives, the findings indicate that broad dispositions are not fully reducible to the reasons people give for their food choices. The single exception, fruit, was also the group most tightly governed by explicit motives, suggesting that the division of explanatory work between traits and motives is food-specific. The trait–consumption pattern replicated meta-analytic estimates in an under-represented context. © 2026 The Authors

title: Artificial intelligence-based employee selection in tourism and hospitality: Justice, inclusion, and gender differences in resume screening and interviews
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more prevalent in human resource management, its role in tourism and hospitality hiring remains underexplored. This study investigates job applicants’ perceptions of AI in employee selection, focusing on resume screening and interviews. Drawing on fairness heuristic theory and social role theory, we examine how AI affects perceived justice, inclusion, and organizational attractiveness. Four scenario-based experiments and one qualitative study were conducted with job applicants comparing AI-based and human-based selection methods. Results show that human recruiters are generally perceived as more just and inclusive, enhancing organizational attractiveness. However, gender moderates these effects: females favor AI-based resume screening, whereas males are more receptive to AI-based interviews. These findings provide insights for organizations seeking to integrate AI into employee selection while maintaining justice and inclusion. As AI becomes more prevalent in hiring, organizations should prioritize human oversight, ensuring that AI supports rather than replaces human. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Driving police engagement through talent management: Evidence from Abu Dhabi
abstract: This study examines the relationship between talent management practices and employee engagement, as well as the moderating role of business analytics and the subsequent impact on employee performance within the Abu Dhabi Police. Specifically, the research explores how talent attraction, retention, learning and development, and career management influence employee engagement, which in turn affects job performance. Drawing on social exchange theory, dynamic capability theory, and Aon Hewitt's employee engagement model, a quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to senior officers across various departments. A total of 383 valid responses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.3.9. The findings reveal that all four dimensions of talent management (talent attraction, talent retention, learning and development, and career management) have significant positive effects on employee engagement. Furthermore, employee engagement strongly and significantly influences employee performance, underscoring its pivotal role in organizational effectiveness. The results of the moderation analysis indicate that business analytics significantly strengthens the relationships between talent attraction, learning and development, and career management and employee engagement, with learning and development and talent attraction showing the strongest moderating effects, whereas the moderating effect on talent retention is statistically insignificant. The model explains 53.8 of the variance in employee engagement, indicating satisfactory predictive power. These findings contribute to the literature by integrating business analytics into the talent management—engagement—performance nexus, particularly within a public sector policing context. Practically, the results highlight the strategic importance of leveraging data-driven and analytics-enabled HRM practices to personalize talent management interventions, enhance perceived fairness, and improve engagement outcomes. Overall, the findings demonstrate that while business analytics enhances most talent management dimensions, its influence is not uniform across all practices, particularly in the case of talent retention. This study provides actionable insights for policymakers and HR leaders seeking to build agile, high-performing, and engaged workforces in dynamic environments. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors.
