title: Designing the waiting experience: How order tracking shapes consumer engagement and loyalty
abstract: The post-purchase waiting period is an important yet underexamined stage of the digital customer journey. Consumers increasingly interact with order tracking systems during this phase, yet research has treated tracking primarily as a logistics tool rather than an experiential touchpoint. This study examines how tracking experience design shapes consumer engagement and loyalty through two psychological mechanisms: perceived control and anticipation. Drawing on perceived control theory and anticipatory utility theory, we develop a framework proposing that richer tracking interfaces enhance consumers' sense of predictability and forward-looking excitement, which in turn strengthen post-purchase engagement and loyalty. We test this framework using a three-study design combining scale validation (N = 240), a between-subjects experiment (N = 180), and structural equation modeling with a large field sample (N = 920) of online shoppers. Across all studies, richer tracking experiences consistently increase perceived control and anticipation, both of which stimulate engagement during the waiting period and contribute to customer loyalty. Engagement further mediates the effects of perceived control and anticipation on loyalty. These findings extend customer experience research, contribute to the psychology of waiting literature, and provide actionable guidance for retailers designing post-purchase interfaces. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Forecasting Approaches to Pharmaceutical Supply Management Across Healthcare Settings: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Drug shortages remain a persistent global issue affecting essential medicines across healthcare settings. In healthcare settings, inadequate pharmaceutical forecasting and inventory management may lead to suboptimal medicine availability, treatment disruption, and patient harm. Despite advances in automated inventory systems, forecasting practices remain fragmented across healthcare contexts with varying demand conditions and implementation requirements. Objectives: This scoping review aimed to map forecasting methods used in pharmaceutical supply management and examine their application across operational contexts. Methods: Studies reporting forecasting or prediction models in pharmaceutical healthcare settings were included. Studies unrelated to pharmaceutical forecasting, non-healthcare logistics, qualitative designs, editorials, and inaccessible full texts were excluded. Searches were conducted in Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. Extracted data on forecasting methods, implementation contexts, and operational outcomes were synthesised narratively. A proposed conceptual framework integrating forecasting approaches and contextual triggers was developed through interpretive synthesis. Results: Twenty-four studies (2007–2026) were included, representing 13 identified countries. Four forecasting approaches were identified: rule-based, traditional/statistical, machine learning/artificial intelligence (ML/AI), and hybrid approaches. Traditional/statistical methods were most frequently reported (n = 8), followed by ML/AI approaches (n = 7), hybrid approaches (n = 5), and rule-based approaches (n = 4). Forecasting approaches were reported across operational contexts with differing demand patterns, data availability, and implementation requirements. Conclusions: ML/AI and hybrid approaches were also reported in studies involving uncertainty and demand variability. However, comparative superiority cannot be established, and the proposed conceptual framework remains an interpretive evidence synthesis structure requiring empirical validation. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

title: Modular microgrids and their deployment: Aligning technological interoperability with integrators’ customization
abstract: Modularity is recognized as a strategic instrument for advancing microgrid deployment and development. However, this potential is often constrained by a complex interplay of factors, including fragmented standards and site-specific requirements. In addressing these challenges, practitioners have taken different positions or priorities, which may lead to different paths and outcomes in microgrid deployment. This study employs Q methodology to explore practitioners’ subjective perspectives on this issue, aiming to reconcile the inherent tension between standardization and customization in leveraging modular microgrids. Drawing on insights from 17 Chinese experts with extensive experience in microgrid deployment, four distinct viewpoints were identified: (1) prioritizing the establishment of interoperability, (2) demand-oriented customization, (3) techno-economic optimization, and (4) industrial synergies. The findings suggest that aligning interoperability with customization can facilitate the deployment of modular microgrids. The proposed framework provides practitioners with a strategic tool to optimize negotiations and mitigate microgrid deployment risks, while offering policymakers a basis for formulating policy guidance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Staff interactions and individual influences on complaint behaviour in restaurants
abstract: This study examines the influence of early staff interactions and individual characteristics on customer complaint behaviour during restaurant dining. A two-stage mixed-methods design was employed: Study 1 surveyed 790 diners, measuring sociodemographic and personality variables alongside self-reported propensity to complain. Study 2 applied these findings in a longitudinal design tracking 98 customers across 994 restaurant visits over one year, capturing individual and situational factors, including staff interactions. Drawing on voice/exit theory and cognitive appraisal frameworks, findings identify redress orientation as a consistent predictor of complaint propensity, whilst empathy reduces both the likelihood of perceived dissatisfaction and willingness to raise issues verbally. Early staff interactions, particularly making customers feel special upon arrival, significantly reduced complaint propensity, as did service quality and friendliness. These findings contribute to the understanding of the individual and situational determinants of complaint behaviour in the UK hospitality industry. © 2026

title: Striking the right balance: How sanctions and consequences of customer misbehavior shape hotel guests’ fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions
abstract: Customer misbehavior in hospitality has attracted attention, yet little is known about how observer guests interpret sanctions imposed on misbehaving guests as rule-enforcement signals. Because observers often outnumber offenders and judge a hotel's response, their reactions may shape fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions. We investigate this through a scenario-based online experiment with U.S. participants (Study 1) and a scenario-based framed field experiment with hotel guests in Senegal (Study 2), manipulating sanction severity and observer guest impact. Across studies, moderate sanctions were judged fairer on average than no or severe sanctions, suggesting that observers do not simply prefer stronger sanctions. Effects on rebooking intentions were more mixed: in Study 1, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than no sanction but did not differ significantly from severe sanctions; in Study 2, moderate sanctions produced higher rebooking intentions than severe sanctions but did not differ significantly from no sanction. Observer guest impact shaped evaluations and moderated sanction effects in Study 1 but had no significant effects in Study 2. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Towards ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented research with small-scale fishing communities: a multi-scalar call to action
abstract: Small-scale fisheries underpin food security, livelihoods and cultural identity for hundreds of millions of people worldwide, yet remain marginalised within dominant ocean governance and research agendas. Recent shifts toward justice-, equity- and rights-based approaches in ocean governance and policy signal important progress, but their rapid uptake risks remaining largely rhetorical if not grounded in meaningful changes to research practice. This paper draws on the experiential knowledge of researchers working across diverse geographical and institutional contexts to critically examine the structural conditions that shape research with small-scale fishing communities. We identify seven tensions that are recurring and cross-cutting within funding architectures, institutional incentive systems, and global policy agendas that constrain the ability of researchers to conduct ethical, co-produced and justice-oriented work. These include misalignments between global priorities and local realities, knowledge hierarchies, rigid funding models, and academic metrics that undervalue relational and collaborative processes. In response, we propose six principles to enable and guide more equitable research practices with small-scale fishing communities. We emphasise the need for the recognition of diverse knowledge systems and creative outputs, institutional reforms that value long-term partnerships and local impact, and strengthened training in reflexive and ethical research approaches. Framed as a multi-scalar call to action, this paper highlights the shared responsibilities of research funders, academic institutions, policy agencies, NGOs, and researchers in reshaping the systems that govern knowledge production that inform ocean governance. Advancing ocean sustainability requires not only new ideas but structural transformation to ensure that research with small-scale fishing communities is inclusive, accountable and just. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Digital finance momentum and indonesian government bond yields: Evidence from an augmented affine term structure model
abstract: This study examines the determinants of the Indonesian government bond yield curve by incorporating a digital finance momentum (DFM) factor into an augmented affine term structure model (ATSM). The study is motivated by the persistent inflation puzzle in Indonesia, where conventional inflation indicators frequently exhibit a weak empirical relationship with government bond yields despite their central role in macrofinance theory. To address this issue, the study introduces a novel DFM index constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) from high-frequency indicators of digital financial activity, including QRIS transaction values, fintech peer-to-peer lending, and e-money transactions. The first principal component explains 82.3% of the total variance across these indicators, supporting the validity of the DFM index as a unified single-factor measure of digital financial expansion. The empirical analysis uses monthly Indonesian data from January 2015 to December 2024 and estimates the model using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques. The results show that the DFM factor significantly affects both the level and slope of the Indonesian yield curve and explains a substantial share of forecast error variance, particularly for medium- and long-term bond yields. In contrast, core inflation remains statistically weak in explaining yield dynamics. Impulse response analysis further indicates that shocks originating from digital financial activity generate persistent increases in government bond yields comparable to those produced by monetary policy shocks. These findings suggest that digital financial development has become an important transmission channel influencing macroeconomic expectations, liquidity conditions, and systemic risk in Indonesia. Under the rational expectations hypothesis, investors incorporate high-frequency digital financial signals into expectations of future inflation more rapidly than conventional macroeconomic indicators. The paper uses quantum-inspired vocabulary in a strictly conceptual rather than mathematical sense; the empirical model is a classical no-arbitrage ATSM augmented with the DFM factor. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Strategic decision-making in negotiation: Lessons from behavioral game theory
abstract: Game theory provides a language and a set of tools for analyzing behavior in a wide range of strategic interactions, including negotiation. Here, we illustrate behavioral game theory's contributions to the study of negotiation, with a particular focus on the role that communication and emotion play in negotiation. We explain how researchers can use games to study various negotiation phenomena, including the effects of power, information asymmetry, and identity on negotiation processes and outcomes. The concepts, methods, and findings we review offer insights and tools that negotiation scholars and practitioners can harness to advance their understanding of negotiation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Enhancing customer decision-making through 3D body-scan-enabled personalization in brick-and-mortar stores: The moderating roles of human support and technology intrusiveness
abstract: Brick-and-mortar stores remain vital in today's retail landscape. To stay competitive, they must deliver experiences that go beyond what online retailers offer, increasingly relying on technology-driven personalization and convenience. Although retailers are investing in technology-enabled personalization (TEP), empirical evidence of its effectiveness remains limited. Across three scenario-based experiments and one field experiment in two product categories (lingerie and jeans), we demonstrate that TEP, specifically 3D body-scan technology, enhances decision convenience and subsequently fosters word-of-mouth (WOM) intentions, but only when human-enabled personalization (HEP) is absent. However, when HEP is present, TEP does not seem to offer additional customer benefits in this study's context. Although we hypothesized that perceived intrusiveness would further qualify the interaction between TEP and HEP, this three-way interaction was not supported. Instead, the findings indicate that perceived intrusiveness directly qualifies the effectiveness of TEP. Specifically, when technology intrusiveness is perceived as low, TEP enhances decision convenience, which in turn fosters WOM intentions. Conversely, high perceived intrusiveness of the technology used reverses this effect, diminishing convenience and indirectly reducing WOM intentions. These findings advance retail personalization research in brick-and-mortar stores by identifying when the examined form of TEP, a 3D body-scanning technology, is most effective in a fashion retail setting and offer managerial guidance for strategically implementing this technology alongside HEP to optimize in-store experiences while safeguarding retailers' cost efficiency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Exploring livelihood assets among inland fishing communities: Evidence from the Sungai Pahang, Malaysia
abstract: The Inland fishing community consisted of Inland fishermen and cage fish farmers. They are among the vulnerable rural groups that require economic assistance. Their dependence on natural resources results in unstable income and increased vulnerability. The vulnerability affects their well-being and livelihoods. Therefore, this study helps by addressing livelihood assets that help minimise vulnerability among the inland fishing community. This paper aims to identify and explore the livelihood assets of inland fishermen and cage fish farmers along the Sungai Pahang. The study employs the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) to identify five livelihood assets: human, natural, financial, physical, and social assets. A survey was conducted among 521 respondents, including 261 inland fishermen and 260 cage fish farmers, using a structured questionnaire. The study was conducted in five districts along the Sungai Pahang Jerantut, Temerloh, Bera, Maran, and Pekan. The data was then analysed through exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to identify the main dimensions of the five livelihood assets within the inland fishing community groups. The data were also checked with reliability coefficients (Cronbach’s alpha). The findings show that inland fishermen depend heavily on financial assets 79.53% variance and physical assets 76.48% variance, highlighting the importance of access to credit and fishing gear for their livelihoods. In contrast, cage fish farmers mainly rely on social assets, accounting for 77.96% of the variance, and human assets, accounting for 69.67 of % variance. This reflects the cage fish farmers' reliance on relevant government institutions for support, training & skills, health, and experience to sustain cage fish production. Although both community groups share the same river ecosystem, their needs is differ, highlighting the diverse in main livelihood assets within riverine communities. However, both communities identify natural assets as a weak livelihood dimension, reflecting their shared vulnerability. Policy interventions in Malaysia should therefore prioritise river conservation, stricter pollution control, sustainable fishing and aquaculture practices, and community-based environmental awareness programmes. Relevant agencies, including the Department of Environment Malaysia, should collaborate with inland fishing communities to implement integrated, participatory environmental management strategies that enhance livelihood resilience and ensure the long-term sustainability of the Sungai Pahang ecosystem. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Faking feelings: Emotional deception in negotiation
abstract: Emotional deception – the intentional misrepresentation of emotions – is pervasive in negotiations and everyday interactions. In this article, we review and extend theory and research on emotional deception in negotiations. We argue that emotional deception is a distinct form of deception with important economic, relational, and psychological consequences for both deceivers and their targets. Specifically, we define emotional deception, examine how it is perceived, and review its antecedents and consequences. We conclude by identifying promising directions for future research on emotional deception. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity under extreme heat: Evidence from 550 global cities
abstract: Extreme heat has become a key factor affecting urban residents’ quality of life, existing studies on urban forest have focused on their average cooling effects, overlooking whether and how variations in cooling efficiency affect heat exposure inequity. To address these gaps, this study selected 550 cities worldwide with a main urban area exceeding 100 km2 to analyze the relationship between urban forest cooling efficiency and heat exposure inequity over the past 24 years. We found that although tree coverage increased in most cities, the enhanced vegetation index (EVI) deteriorated in nearly half of them, revealing a polarizing pattern: “High coverage turning green, low coverage turning brown.” Notably, tree coverage and EVI were particularly fragile in tropical climates and low Human Development Index (HDI) cities. We found that each 1 % increase in tree coverage reduces the average land surface temperature during extreme heat by 0.31 °C. However, this cooling efficiency is distributed extremely unevenly. The study utilized the population-weighted temperature Gini coefficient to represent the inequity of urban heat exposure. About 25.2 % of cities experienced increased heat exposure inequity, particularly in developed cities, as increasing tree coverage unintentionally exacerbated spatial inequity. At the same time, about 5.6 % of cities even exhibit a forest warming effect, especially in the desert climate zones and low HDI areas. About 66 % of the cities showed that as the cooling efficiency of urban forest increased, there was a corresponding increase in heat exposure equity. The study proposed the concept of the equity potential index and compared the possibility of achieving equity potential for the cooling efficiency of urban forest under the three scenarios: SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP3-7.0. The study showed that SSP1-2.6 is more favorable for temperate climate zones and low-HDI cities, whereas SSP2-4.5 is more beneficial for tropical, continental climates, and very high HDI cities. This study provides a scientific, equity-oriented framework for designing place-specific urban forest strategies that enhance thermal resilience and social sustainability. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Artificial intelligence and public sector transformation: A systematic literature review on applications, governance and acceptability factors
abstract: The public sector is undergoing a profound digital transformation characterised by the increasing integration of artificial intelligence into its management control practices. Concurrently, the optimisation of public performance and accountability has emerged as a central concern among scholars, particularly within the broader context of digital transition. This period of structural change calls for renewed forms of governance and organisational steering grounded in innovative and adaptive approaches. Research on artificial intelligence in public administration has developed significantly since the early 2020s, although the effective adoption of these technologies continues to present substantial challenges. This article offers a systematic review of the literature published between 2020 and 2025, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines to ensure methodological rigour and reliability. The content analysis is based on a corpus of twenty-five selected articles. The findings indicate that the adoption of artificial intelligence in public management control remains a critical issue. AI has contributed to innovation across five principal domains: financial auditing, budget forecasting, operational optimisation, public health, and legal support. These developments open promising avenues for enhancing the quality of public management, particularly through the effective implementation of technological innovations, the strengthening of institutional adaptability and resilience, the development of essential digital competencies, the cultivation of critical engagement with algorithmic systems, and the reinforcement of digital literacy among public officials. Nevertheless, significant ethical challenges persist, including algorithmic opacity, discriminatory bias, and tensions between efficiency and equity. Addressing these concerns requires the establishment of appropriate governance frameworks and the consolidation of broader societal acceptance. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Quantifying the prestige of scientific awards: A network-bibliometric framework
abstract: Scientific awards play a central role in recognizing excellence and shaping research trajectories, funding priorities, and disciplinary visibility. Yet despite their importance, scalable and reproducible quantitative frameworks for assessing award prestige remain limited, with prior efforts relying largely on small-scale or perception-based evaluations. This study introduces a data-driven framework for quantifying the prestige of scientific awards by integrating network centrality measures derived from inter-award linkages with bibliometric indicators of prize-winners’ research profiles. Using a dataset of 1352 research-related award records across seven disciplines, we treat award prestige as a latent construct approximated by two external reference dimensions: public attention (crowd-sourced engagement) and professional reputation (expert survey responses). Across three complementary modeling approaches and repeated cross-validation, the framework recovers rankings that are broadly consistent with conventional perceptions of scientific prestige, with awards such as the Nobel Prize, Abel Prize, and Turing Award consistently appearing near the top across external reference dimensions. Among the examined features, network prominence, as measured by eigenvector centrality, emerges as the most consistently important signal, followed by recent bibliometric activity and authorship leadership. The proposed framework offers a scalable and transparent approach to quantifying scientific recognition, providing empirical insights into the structure of academic prestige and informing future evaluations of emerging or underrecognized awards. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: When do sustainability-related fashion reviews become helpful? The credibility role of verified purchase in online retailing
abstract: Online reviews are an important source of information in digital retailing, yet not all reviews are equally useful to consumers. This study examines whether sustainability-related content is associated with online review helpfulness and whether verified purchase status conditions this relationship. Using 1,680,956 Amazon Fashion reviews, sustainability-related content is identified through a two-stage procedure combining a keyword pre-filter with large language model–assisted semantic classification and is integrated with review-, product-, and reviewer-level information. The main analysis employs a full-sample Negative Binomial model with product-level clustered standard errors, review-age exposure and review-specificity controls, and an empirically estimated NB2 dispersion parameter. Sustainability-related content is negatively associated with expected helpfulness among unverified reviews (β=−0.763), whereas verified purchase status is positively associated with helpfulness (β=0.596). The interaction between sustainability-related content and verified purchase status is positive and statistically significant (β=0.958). A formal linear-combination test shows that the combined sustainability effect among verified reviews is positive (β,=0.195p=0.023), corresponding to approximately 21.5% more expected helpful votes. Binary Logit and OLS models, year and month fixed effects, and product-type proxy fixed effects support the same credibility-contingent pattern. The findings indicate that sustainability-related user-generated content is not uniformly associated with greater helpfulness; its informational value is contingent on the transaction-based credibility cue attached to the review. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
abstract: Algorithmic management is increasingly embedded in hotel operations, raising questions about how employees interpret managerial authority and voice concerns. Drawing on organisational justice and trust perspectives, this study examines relationships among perceived algorithmic control, perceived algorithmic fairness, and employee voice intention. An explanatory sequential mixed methods design combined structural equation modelling with semi-structured interviews. Perceived algorithmic control was negatively associated with procedural justice, interactional justice, and voice intention, whereas perceived algorithmic fairness was positively associated with trust in the employer and voice intention. Procedural justice, interactional justice, and trust were positively related to voice intention. The indirect-association analysis showed that algorithmic control was negatively associated with voice through procedural and interactional justice, while algorithmic fairness was positively associated with voice through trust. Qualitative findings highlighted explainability, reviewability, and managerial discretion. The study positions algorithmic management as relational governance and distinguishes control and fairness as separate pathways associated with employee voice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Halo or horn? The role of prior attitudes in shaping consumer responses to high-protein food labels
abstract: Front-of-pack nutrition claims can shape consumers' perceptions of food products by triggering inferences about their overall healthfulness. Among these claims, “high-protein” labels have rapidly expanded across food categories, yet their influence on consumers' nutritional judgments remains underexplored. The present study investigated whether a high-protein label induces a health halo effect and examined the role of product characteristics and individual differences in shaping these perceptions. In an online experiment (N = 218), participants evaluated five food products presented either with or without a high-protein label. For each product, participants rated perceived calories, healthiness, sugar content, additives, level of processing, and purchase intention. Individual differences in drive for muscularity and attitudes toward protein products were also measured. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that the high-protein label did not produce a generalized positive halo effect: it did not significantly affect perceived healthiness, caloric content, sugar content, or purchase intention. However, products labeled as high protein were perceived as containing more additives and as being more industrially processed, consistent with a horn effect. The influence of the label on calorie and sugar estimations was moderated by the caloric content of the product, with effects emerging primarily for high-calorie products. Attitudes toward protein products moderated the label's effect across nutritional judgments, whereas drive for muscularity did not moderate labeling effects. These findings highlight the central role of individual predispositions in shaping responses to nutrition claims and suggest that high-protein labels may generate complex and sometimes contradictory perceptual biases, with implications for dietary behavior and public health. © 2026 The Authors

title: Do narcissistic personality traits and immature defense mechanisms hinder communication and cooperation in pilots?
abstract: This study examines the safety operation behaviors of pilots within the framework of communication and cooperation, compares how these behaviors are affected by narcissistic personality traits, and compares the results for the correct evaluation and management of immature ego defense mechanisms, which are thought to be a factor triggering this relationship. The data were collected from 150 pilot participants working at airlines in Turkey using a survey data collection tool. It was observed that the participants frequently used the defense mechanisms of rationalization, isolation, and acting out. This result shows that pilots continue to exhibit the same behavior by providing acceptable reasons rather than trying to eliminate negative situations by discussing them realistically. It was also observed that they tend to focus only on the objective aspects of events and avoid discussing the parts that negatively affect them psychologically. In addition, it was found that narcissistic personality traits negatively affect the communication and cooperation behaviors of pilots, and immature ego defense mechanisms are a precursor that strengthens the narcissistic personality. It is thought that examining narcissistic personality traits within the framework of immature ego defense mechanisms and managing these mechanisms effectively will contribute greatly to aviation psychology research to prevent risks related to the human factor, which airline companies and authorities view as an important risk within safety management systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Digital transformation policy and production efficiency in state-owned electric power enterprises: Evidence from China
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly used to modernize public utilities, but its efficiency effects remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the effect of China's 2020 digital transformation policy for state-owned enterprises on the production efficiency of listed electric enterprises. Treating the policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a super-efficiency data envelopment analysis model to measure production efficiency and a difference-in-differences model to examine the policy effect. The results show that the policy significantly improves the production efficiency of state-owned electric enterprises relative to non-state-owned enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis shows stronger effects among utilities in eastern China, labor-intensive firms, and large firms. Mechanism analysis further shows that increased R&D investment is an important channel through which the policy generates efficiency gains, while managerial equity incentives strengthen policy effectiveness. The findings provide policy implications for utility digitalization, differentiated policy support, innovation incentives, and governance reform. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The long-term effects of teachers’ gender stereotypes on labor outcomes
abstract: This paper links a teacher-level measure of gender-stereotyped grading — validated against their Implicit Association Test (IAT) scores — to the later schooling and labor-market outcomes of 1.6 million Peruvian students. Exposure to a more stereotyped teacher widens the gender gaps in high-school completion, formal-sector employment, and earnings, driven by boys’ lasting gains rather than by girls’ smaller, short-lived losses. A single year with a math teacher one standard deviation more stereotyped than average raises boys’ on-time graduation by 0.9 percentage points and lowers girls’ by 0.6. Over the five years after high school (ages 17–22), it raises boys’ formal employment by 4%–12% of the mean employment rate and widens the gender pay gap by about 11% in the first two years, while girls’ losses fade thereafter. These effects run through high-school completion, not test scores or college enrollment. The widening gap in male-dominated industries mainly reflects men's entry rather than women's exit, and students show little sign of adopting the stereotypes themselves. Where structural barriers already constrain access to higher education, teachers’ stereotypes shape who finishes school and their early labor-market outcomes, rather than who reaches college. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Transformative leadership models and styles to improve the quality and development of Muhammadiyah school education in Blora Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to investigate models and leadership styles that are effective in improving the quality of education in Muhammadiyah Schools in Blora, Indonesia. The research method used is a case study with a focus on qualitative data analysis, including interviews, observations, and analysis of related documents. This research identifies various leadership models that have been applied in Muhammadiyah Schools, including transformational, transactional, and participatory leadership. In addition, this study explores stakeholder preferences and perceptions of the most effective leadership styles in the context of Islamic education in the Muhammadiyah school environment in Blora. The results showed that transformational leadership models and styles play a key role in designing strategic vision and driving educational innovation in Muhammadiyah Schools. The implementation of transactional and participatory strategies has also proven important in day-to-day management and consensus-based decision-making. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for policymakers and education leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools, to optimize leadership strategies to improve the quality of Islamic education in Blora. The novelty of this study lies in the identification of a combination of transformational and participatory leadership as an optimal leadership model in the context of Islamic education. This research also adds a new perspective on stakeholder preferences in the implementation of leadership styles in Muhammadiyah schools. The implication of this study is the need for educational leaders in Muhammadiyah Schools to consider the application of a combination of flexible and innovative leadership models, in order to achieve continuous improvement in the quality of Islamic education. This can be a reference for policymakers to formulate more effective leadership strategies in facing future educational challenges. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: A survey of information retrieval and recommender systems in the era of large language models: Two sides of the same task
abstract: The fields of information retrieval and recommender systems have long evolved as distinct disciplines, each with its own methodologies and theoretical foundations. This survey provides a perspective on the convergence of these fields, a transformation catalyzed by the advent of large language models. We maintain that this convergence is far from a trivial overlap of tools, but it embodies a substantial conceptual and architectural unification. Our central contribution is a novel three-part taxonomy that explains the mechanisms of this merger leveraging large language models as (1) an embedded engine, (2) a semantic re-ranker, and (3) a response generator. We show how this trajectory culminates in a paradigm inversion, from weak to strong inversion, where the information-seeking task itself is reshaped. The unification is structurally consolidated through joint search and recommendation architectures and contextually curated by retrieval-augmented generation frameworks. This hypothesis is substantiated by a rigorous, quantitative analysis of scholarly publication trends, which provides empirical evidence of this rapid evolution. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a convergence operating at different velocities dictated by domain-specific latency constraints, while acknowledging critical operational vulnerabilities regarding hallucination and bias. A companion GitHub repository is publicly available and offers the complete data collection methodology, dynamic trend analyses, and a comprehensive, categorized list of the surveyed papers, which will be actively maintained as a living resource for the research community. We conclude that the distinction between retrieval and recommendation is becoming a historical artifact and call for the formal recognition of a new, integrated science of information discovery. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). To address this deficiency, this study, conducted in the Republic of Ireland, adopts a sequential research design in which expert workshops and focus groups were used to develop a nationally representative discrete choice survey (n = 970) to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for environmental improvements and to enhance the effectiveness, legitimacy, and practical uptake of SEA. Our findings reveal strong public support for planning scenarios that include greater public participation, substantial increases in local green space (10–30%), and acceptance of short procedural delays (1–2 years) in SEA processes to ensure comprehensive environmental assessment. Model estimates indicate that respondents expressed a WTP of approximately €48–€63 per year for a 30% increase in green space, with the lower estimate derived from the multinomial logit (MNL) model and the higher estimate from the random parameters logit (RPL) model. Results also indicate limited public familiarity with SEA instruments and relatively low trust in governmental environmental decision-making. The study presents a methodological framework for integrating ecosystem service valuation and measurable forms of public participation into SEA processes to support more effective and legitimate environmental decision-making. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Adult-only: When excluding children reveals a flaw in hospitality management approach
abstract: This research note explores social servicescape in hospitality settings, considering recent regulatory debates questioning the exclusion of children. Although children are often positioned as either sovereign consumers or a marginalised group, their impact on guest satisfaction remains largely unexplored. Drawing on 90,045 TripAdvisor reviews from 72 international resorts, we applied advanced natural language processing techniques, including BERT-based sentiment analysis and child-reference classification using a local Large Language Model to examine whether references to children influence customer evaluations. By comparing satisfaction scores across reviews that mention or omit children, we explore whether these differences reflect broader managerial, academic, and policy-related challenges. This study contributes to ongoing debates on adult-only vs inclusive hospitality by highlighting how children's presence is addressed in guest feedback, and by raising questions about the potential limitations in current hospitality management practices. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Fixed or flexible: How product formats affect consumer redemption behavior for live-streamed food and beverage (F&B) products
abstract: With the rapid growth of live-streaming e-commerce in the food and beverage industry, low redemption rates despite high sales volumes have become a critical challenge for merchants. This research investigates how product formats and familiarity affect consumer redemption behavior and identifies the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions. Through five studies using one archival-data study, three scenario-based experiments, and one field experiment, we find that: product formats and familiarity interact significantly: set meals yield higher redemption under low familiarity, while vouchers perform better under high familiarity. This relationship is mediated through a dual-pathway mechanism: at low levels of familiarity, a loss-avoidance pathway prevails through perceived risk, whereas at high levels of familiarity, a gain-seeking pathway dominates through perceived preference fit. Purchase type further moderates this interaction, such that the effect emerges only under impulse purchase conditions. This research extends the theoretical understanding of the “purchase-redemption” process in live-streaming commerce and offers actionable insights for F&B firms to optimize product strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Trust patterns in food chain actors in the European region over a six-year period (2019-2024): an exploratory analysis
abstract: We analyse consumer trust in food chain actors, both commercial and authorities, in 12 European countries and Israel over a period of 6 years, including the years of the Covid-19 pandemic, based on data from the EIT Food TrustTracker® yearly data collection. While we find considerable differences in consumer trust between countries, an analysis over time shows that trust levels have been remarkably stable. However, in some countries there was a change in trust level during the Covid-19 years. In some countries, trust in commercial actors increased slightly during Covid-19, and stayed at this higher level after the pandemic. Also, trust in authorities increased slightly in some countries during Covid-19, but mostly regressed to pre-Covid levels afterwards. These changes are interpreted in terms of disruptions in the food supply chain during Covid-19 and their perception by consumers, and in terms of governmental reactions to the pandemic. © 2026 The Authors

title: Helpfulness and enjoyment in eWOM: A dual-value perspective for hedonic digital products
abstract: As the digital economy increasingly pivots toward the experience sector, electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) serves not merely as a decision-support tool but as an intrinsic source of entertainment. Yet, the literature remains overwhelmingly anchored to a unidimensional metric: review helpfulness. Challenging this utilitarian bias, this study establishes a dual-value evaluative paradigm that encompasses both diagnostic helpfulness and enjoyment to decode peer evaluations of hedonic digital product reviews. Grounded in processing fluency theory, we investigate how cognitive stimuli (product informativeness) and affective stimuli (emotional richness) synergistically yet distinctly drive these dual dimensions. Leveraging a dataset of 12,823 reviews from Steam, we deploy a rigorous methodological triangulation: extracting deep semantic features via Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and VADER sentiment analysis, estimating causal mechanisms via Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) regressions, and validating predictive robustness using Random Forest algorithms. The empirical findings reveal that review breadth and thematic distribution divergence concurrently enhance both outcomes. Review thematic density exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship across both dimensions. While the negative sentiment rate enhances utilitarian risk-mitigation but severely disrupts hedonic gratification. The study advances eWOM literature by establishing a dual-value evaluative paradigm, providing actionable guidelines for digital platforms to optimize content distribution for review helpfulness and enjoyment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Political activism and indulgent preferences: Perceived moral contribution and deservingness
abstract: Political activism is commonly conceptualized as a form of collective action that promotes individual empowerment, collective efficacy, and societal well-being. However, this research demonstrates that activism focused on the pursuit of a collective goal can also have paradoxical consequences by increasing subsequent indulgent preferences. Drawing on moral licensing theory, when high-effort, in-person activism is grounded in moral conviction, actors may interpret their effortful involvement as a morally meaningful contribution to a collective cause, enhancing a sense of perceived moral contribution, which heightens perceived deservingness and, in turn, indulgence. Across four experimental studies (n = 852) in emerging and developed economies, the results highlight that participants exposed to high-effort, in-person activism scenarios subsequently demonstrated higher levels of indulgence than those in low-effort online actions or the control condition. These effects are moderated by consumer type in emerging markets, with the effect of high-effort activism on indulgence being stronger among bottom-of-the-pyramid (BOP) consumers. Our findings caution advocacy organizations against assuming that effortful civic participation consistently reinforces prosocial behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: EXPLORING THE HEALTH KNOWLEDGE CO-CONSTRUCTION ON SHORT VIDEO PLATFORMS
abstract: Short video platforms have become an important channel for doctors to conduct health science popularization. This study aims to explore the factors influencing health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms. Based on arousal theory, we develop an empirical model to examine the effects of video vividness, video complexity, emotional attitudes, and doctor popularity on health knowledge co-construction. We collected data from the largest short video platform in China, comprising a total of 4,009 videos and 1,040,230 comments for empirical analysis. This study combined machine learning, large language models, and econometric models to test the theoretical model. The results show that: (1) video vividness has a significant positive effect on health knowledge co-construction; (2) video complexity has a negative effect on health knowledge co-construction; (3) there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between emotional attitude and health knowledge co-construction; (4) doctor popularity positively moderates this curvilinear relationship. This study contributes to the literature on knowledge co-construction, expands the understanding of health knowledge co-construction on short video platforms, and provides practical guidance for platform managers and doctors. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. .

title: Mapping the research landscape of generative artificial intelligence in education with implications for teacher education: A bibliometric analysis
abstract: The rapid emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models, has significantly transformed educational research and practice, resulting in a rapidly expanding yet fragmented body of literature. This study aims to systematically map the research landscape of GenAI in education and examine its implications for teacher education through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using the Scopus database, 16,250 documents published from 2021 to 2025 were analyzed through performance analysis and science mapping techniques, including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship network analysis, and citation analysis to capture the structural and intellectual development of the field. The findings reveal a sharp increase in publication output beginning in 2023, indicating a transition from an emergent to a high-growth phase of research development. Research productivity and scholarly influence are concentrated among a limited group of authors, institutions, and countries, particularly the United States and China, reflecting uneven global participation. Collaboration networks exhibit a multi-clustered structure, suggesting active yet fragmented research communities with limited cross-group integration. Citation patterns indicate that a small number of recent publications exert strong influence and serve as foundational references in the field. Thematic analysis further identifies three dominant and interconnected areas: core technological developments, educational applications, and domain-specific implementations, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of GenAI in education. The field is expanding rapidly but remains structurally fragmented and is still undergoing intellectual consolidation. These findings emphasize the need for more cohesive research efforts, stronger international collaboration, and greater integration across thematic domains. Implications for teacher education include the integration of AI-related competencies into pre-service programs, the adoption of pedagogically grounded and context-sensitive approaches, and the provision of continuous professional development to support teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Food souvenir SMEs performance: Digital marketing, branding, innovation, and Hexa Helix moderation
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), particularly in the food souvenir sector, play a vital role in supporting local economic development. However, increasing competition and rapid digital transformation require SMEs to strengthen their strategic capabilities in order to maintain their marketing performance. Previous research has largely examined digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation separately, with limited attention to the combined effects of these three factors and the moderating role of collaborative ecosystems such as the Hexa Helix model. This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing capabilities, branding, and product innovation on marketing performance, while also examining the moderating role of Hexa Helix collaboration. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 335 SMEs owners, and the data were analyzed using Warp Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (WarpPLS-SEM). The results indicate that branding has the strongest positive effect on marketing performance ( β = 0.318, p < 0.001 ), followed by digital marketing capabilities ( β = 0.289, p < 0.001 ) and product innovation ( β = 0.117, p = 0.015 ). Regarding the moderating role, the findings indicate that the Hexa Helix does not significantly moderate the relationship between digital marketing capabilities and marketing performance, nor between branding and marketing performance. However, the Hexa Helix significantly strengthens the relationship between product innovation and marketing performance ( β = 0.217, p < 0.001 ). These findings suggest that while internal strategic capabilities are the primary drivers of SMEs performance, external collaborative support through the Hexa Helix is highly effective in amplifying the impact of product innovation rather than uniformly strengthening all strategic relationships. This study contributes to the literature by providing a deeper understanding of the conditional role of collaborative ecosystems in SMEs performance. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Large language model-based carbon emission forecasting: A sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework with transformer-long short-term memory networks
abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions from coal, oil, natural gas, cement, and total CO2 is critical for formulating effective emission reduction strategies and carbon trading policies. However, existing models are plagued by overemphasis on total CO2 prediction, overreliance on single-task learning that overlooks cross-source correlations, neglect of sentiment information in carbon-related texts, and the absence of domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) for carbon sentiment extraction, which severely impairs their prediction accuracy and generalization ability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a novel sentiment-enhanced multi-task learning framework for carbon emission forecasting, which integrates an LLM with a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) network. First, a domain-adapted LLM is developed based on DeepSeek-R1 and a multi-level fusion attention mechanism, enabling efficient sentiment feature extraction from carbon emission reports (e.g., policy, transaction, social awareness) with few-shot data. Second, a Transformer-LSTM-based multi-task learning model is designed to synergistically predict emissions from the five aforementioned sources by exploiting shared features and the complementary strengths of parallel computing and long-term dependency capture. Finally, a strengthened blood-sucking leech algorithm with Cauchy chaotic mutation and chaotic mapping is proposed to optimize the hyperparameters of the multi-task model, thus avoiding local optima and enhancing convergence stability. Validated on real-world data from the International Energy Agency, the proposed framework reduces the root mean square error by 11.14 tons compared with benchmark models. Meanwhile, the developed LLM achieves a sentiment classification accuracy 0.145 higher than baseline methods, which fully verifies the effectiveness of integrating sentiment information in carbon emission forecasting. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Creative thinking ability: A hybrid systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: This study explores the development of creative thinking ability over the past few decades using a interdisciplinary approach in a global context. Various studies have investigated creative thinking ability over the past several decades, but the search is still fragmented in each field. Therefore, there is a significant gap in our understanding of how these concepts of creative thinking overlap and interact across disciplines. So that, in-depth research on this subject remains necessary. This study is a systematic literature review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis of creative thinking ability based on empirical studies that have been conducted. The methodology used in this study is a systematic literature review using term “creative thinking ability” in the article title, abstract, and keywords from the Scopus database, resulting in 4,487 publications from 1968 to 2025. The evaluation was conducted on January 5, 2026. The collected data were analyzed bibliometrically using the VOS (visualization of similarities) viewer. This study found that creative thinking intersects various disciplines, including psychology, education, and business, which holistically intersect with the cognitive dimension, the affective dimension, and the socio-cultural dimension. In psychology, an individual’s creative capacity can be optimized through cognitive stimulation aligned with their personality characteristics. In the business sector, a climate of innovation is encouraged through structured training programs adaptively designed based on employee perceptions and needs. title: Rethinking institutional support for migrant businesses in Sweden: A strategic management– oriented scoping review
abstract: Migrant entrepreneurship has become an increasingly important contributor to Sweden’s economic and social landscape; however, the institutional environment supporting migrant-owned businesses remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. This study conducts a scoping review to map existing knowledge on the opportunities, barriers, and systemic gaps affecting migrant entrepreneurs in Sweden. The review draws on peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and grey literature published between 2020 and 2026, identified primarily through the Scopus database and complementary manual searches. A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using a thematic synthesis approach. The findings reveal that migrant entrepreneurs contribute significantly to job creation, innovation, and regional development, particularly in sectors such as retail, hospitality, and services. However, they face persistent barriers including limited access to finance, bureaucratic complexity, language constraints, and weak integration into institutional support networks. The analysis further shows that although Sweden possesses a wide range of support mechanisms, these are often poorly coordinated, resulting in duplication, inefficiencies, and limited accessibility for migrant entrepreneurs. Guided by the resource-based view (RBV) and contingency theory, this study develops a strategic pathways model consisting of three interrelated pillars: resource mobilization, adaptive strategy, and collaborative alignment. The model provides a conceptual framework for enhancing institutional effectiveness and improving the inclusiveness of entrepreneurial support systems. The study highlights the need for a more integrated, flexible, and strategically coordinated support ecosystem. It also identifies critical gaps in empirical research and calls for future studies to test the proposed model in real-world institutional settings. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Turning climate concern into climate courage: Female parliamentarians, environmental taxation and SDG13
abstract: Environmental issues, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and air pollution, have received heightened international attention following the adoption of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which aim to promote global sustainable development. The presence of women in parliament has proven to be highly effective in advancing environmental tax policies that help reduce vulnerability to climate change. Using panel data from G20 and N11 economies between 2002 and 2022, this study provides evidence that women's presence in parliament is a critical determinant of achieving environmental sustainability. The models' results show that female parliamentarians with significant representation are more effective, and they reach the ‘Climate Action’ goal by reducing CO2 and GHG emissions, among other environmental targets. Notably, the country's ecological achievements can be intensified by implementing more efficient environmental taxation policies. We mitigate endogeneity by using Lewbel-IV and GMM estimation. Moreover, this study also highlights the significance of this relationship when the government invests more in renewable energy, emits less CO2, has a significant forest reserve, and offers better employment opportunities. © 2026 The Authors. title: A reciprocal perspective on internationalization and ESG in EMNEs: The role of digitalization
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) has become a critical measure of multinational enterprises’ global competitiveness, yet emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs) face distinct legitimacy challenges due to weak home-country ESG regulations, known as the liability of home origin. Although prior studies have examined the relationship between internationalization and ESG, they have largely treated the two directions separately, leaving unclear whether they operate as competing explanations or as mutually reinforcing processes. Drawing on legitimacy theory, this study conceptualizes internationalization and ESG performance as exhibiting mutually reinforcing associations over time. Using longitudinal data from 2460 Chinese listed firms between 2009 and 2020, we examine the reciprocal relationship between internationalization and ESG performance, and the moderating role of digitalization. Findings indicate that internationalization is consistently associated with stronger ESG performance, suggesting EMNEs use ESG to mitigate liabilities of origin and build legitimacy abroad. The reverse association is weaker but most robust for foreign-country scope, indicating that ESG performance may support international expansion by signaling alignment with international sustainability expectations. The moderating associations of digitalization are uneven and are concentrated in visible foreign organizational and geographic presence, such as overseas subsidiaries and foreign-country scope, rather than overseas revenues. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Visions, narratives and numbers: How roadmapping enables industrial transformation toward decarbonisation
abstract: The transformation to a low-carbon industry requires different actors to work together and align their strategies. To support this process, policy and industry in many European countries have been driving the development of industry technology roadmaps at sectoral and national levels. However, limited attention has been paid to how visions, narratives and quantitative modelling work together within roadmapping to enable alignment and transformation across organisational, industry and policy levels. We examine industry technology roadmaps in six selected European countries, using secondary material, survey responses and two focus groups. The analysis is based on a conceptual framework that integrates the design and process elements considered important for roadmap development and implementation, complemented by the requirements for promoting industrial transformation rooted in the literature on socio-technical change. While most roadmaps included sophisticated modelling techniques and quantified scenarios, the study shows that a well-articulated narrative is equally important in mobilising stakeholders toward long-term industrial decarbonisation goals. In addition, the case studies illustrate that strategic planning processes of industrial companies benefit from having a forum to assess the future potential of specific technologies with other companies and along the value chain, thereby helping them manage uncertainty in investment decisions. © 2026

title: Digitalising waqf for sustainable development growth: Investigating user intentions through technology readiness and ethical commitment
abstract: The digitalisation of cash waqf represents a promising avenue within Islamic social finance, offering substantial potential to enhance the welfare and socio-economic development of Muslim communities. Through digital platforms, cash waqf can be collected, managed and distributed more efficiently, transparently and widely compared to traditional methods. Despite these advantages, the level of public participation and contributions to digital cash waqf platforms remains significantly below expectations. This gap highlights the need to better understand the factors that influence individuals’ willingness to adopt digital channels for charitable giving. This study aims to explore the determinants that influence individuals’ intentions to contribute to cash waqf via digital platforms by employing the Technology Readiness framework. Specifically, the study examines the roles of optimism, innovativeness, insecurity, discomfort, and moral obligation in shaping users’ behavioural intentions toward online waqf contributions. Data were collected through an online survey involving 211 Muslim respondents in Malaysia who have experience with digital financial services. The data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings reveal that optimism, insecurity, and moral obligation have a positive and significant influence on individuals’ intentions to donate cash waqf through digital platforms. In contrast, discomfort demonstrates a significant negative effect, indicating that feelings of technological anxiety and lack of confidence in using digital systems may discourage adoption. Given the limited empirical research on digital cash waqf, this study contributes valuable insights into the psychological and behavioural factors influencing online donation behaviour. The findings provide practical implications for waqf institutions and policymakers to design strategies that reduce technological barriers while strengthening moral and religious motivations, thereby encouraging wider adoption of digital cash waqf platforms, particularly in developing countries with similar socio-economic environments. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Experiential and symbolic pathways to luxury fashion brand equity: The contingent role of brand attachment and subjective norm
abstract: The study develops and tests an integrated moderated mediation model to explain how emotional attachment, shaped by experiential and symbolic brand stimuli, is associated with consumer-based brand equity (CBBE) in the luxury fashion context, and the role of consumers’ social environment, drawing on Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour. Data were collected from 544 luxury fashion consumers and were analysed using Hayes' PROCESS Model 15. Both brand experience and brand mystery were positively associated with brand attachment. Brand attachment was also positively associated with CBBE and significantly mediated the indirect associations between experiential and symbolic brand resources and CBBE. Furthermore, subjective norm moderately weakens the positive relationship between brand attachment and CBBE, indicating that while subjective norm weakens the relationship between emotional attachment and consumers' evaluations of luxury fashion brands, it does not replace it. This study advances luxury branding research by showing how an identity-based relational mechanism is associated with broader CBBE, with experiential encounters and symbolic meanings relating to brand equity through emotional attachment. By integrating Attachment Theory, the Lovemarks framework, and the Theory of Planned Behaviour within a unified framework, the study shows that experiential and symbolic brand resources are associated with luxury brand equity through complementary relational pathways. © 2026

title: Balanced Risk Assessment and Management in Development of Hard-To-Recover Reserves Using Example of Heavy Oil
abstract: Depletion of conventional oil fields and increasing requirements for the economic justification of investment projects enhance the significance of developing hard-to-recover reserves, including heavy oil, which is characterized by technological complexity, high energy intensity, and multifactor uncertainty. This study proposes a balanced risk assessment framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system. Quantitative project parameters are modeled as random variables, while poorly formalized geological, technical, operational, environmental, social, and political-regulatory risks are aggregated into an integral fuzzy risk index. The proposed framework is tested using open data for a heavy oil project and four integration variants: a baseline Monte Carlo model without fuzzy risk adjustment, a model with risk-adjusted mean values, a model with risk-adjusted standard deviations, and a combined model. The fuzzy inference system produced a high integral risk index, Rhtr = 0.782. In the baseline model, expected NPV was -1.79 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV was 66.52%. When the integral risk index was incorporated through shifts in expected values, expected NPV decreased to approximately -6.76 billion USD and the probability of negative NPV increased to 89.90%. The combined model produced a similar central shift, with expected NPV of -6.75 billion USD and P(NPV < 0) of 89.44%, while also reflecting increased distributional uncertainty. The results show that the main economic effect of integral risk is associated with systematic changes in expected CAPEX, OPEX, production rate, and decline rate, whereas variance-only adjustment has limited influence on central project metrics. The proposed approach provides a transparent tool for linking qualitative risk assessment with probabilistic economic evaluation and supports more conservative investment decision-making in heavy oil development projects. © 2026 The author(s). title: Auditing TikTok’s recommendations: Understanding the prevalence of misinformation on the platform
abstract: Short video platforms have rapidly increased in popularity, bringing forth a concerning trend: widespread dissemination of misinformation partially owing to the persuasive nature of the rich media these platforms support. However, little research has systematically investigated the role of algorithmic recommendations in this phenomenon. Our study addresses this gap by auditing the recommendation algorithm of TikTok, the leading short video platform, through four experiments. We explore the prevalence of misinformation in TikTok’s auto-complete suggestions, search results, and For You Page (FYP) recommendations. Our audits yielded a novel dataset comprising 8535 auto-complete suggestions, 1606 search queries, and 2893 videos labelled by stance (promoting misinformation, neutral in nature, or debunking misinformation). Our analysis reveals that TikTok’s algorithm exhibits sensitivity to user behaviours, often in unexpected ways. We find the algorithm recommends substantially more misinformation to newly created accounts lacking search histories, potentially shaping the tone of the content these accounts engage with. We also find that watching and engaging with videos (e.g., liking and favouriting) dynamically influence misinformation prevalent on the platform, potentially reinforcing existing beliefs and contributing to echo-chambers. Further, we emphasise how engaging with misinformation on one topic serves as a gateway, prompting the algorithm to recommend misinformation spanning both related and unrelated topics. Our work stands as the first large-scale, systematic, and empirical assessment of misinformation in TikTok’s recommendations, contributing valuable insights on the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on TikTok and also underscoring the pressing need for responsible auditing practices across digital platforms. © 2026 The Authors. title: Automatic binary security classification of arabic mobile app reviews using transformer models and active learning
abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. However, existing research has largely focused on English reviews and lacks systematic approaches for identifying security-related feedback in Arabic, a low-resource language in this domain. In this paper, we address this gap by developing an integrated approach for automated binary classification of security-related versus non-security-related Arabic mobile app reviews, grounded in a structured set of security requirement categories derived from software engineering literature. We collected 14,667,283 reviews from 56 mobile applications across multiple domains, including government, finance, and social platforms. Using natural language processing techniques and sentiment-based filtering, positive reviews were removed as a dataset-reduction step, while neutral and negative reviews were retained for subsequent analysis. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. The active learning process resulted in a final training dataset of 10,632 expert-validated reviews. In addition, 1000 expert-validated reviews were reserved as a held-out test set and excluded from model training. The training dataset was used to fine-tune three transformer models, namely CAMeLBERT, MARBERT, and Paraphrase, for binary classification of security-related and non-security-related reviews. CAMeLBERT achieved the highest performance among the fine-tuned models, with 95.76% accuracy and 95.77% F1-score under 10-fold cross-validation and 91.20% accuracy and 91.16% F1-score on the held-out test set. To support practical adoption, we developed a web-based interface integrated with a large language model to enable real-time classification and provide interpretable explanations. The resulting dataset and developed approach contribute to advancing security-aware analysis of Arabic user-generated content and support software engineers in identifying security-related concerns in mobile application reviews. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Personalizing AI voice agents: How voice agents with similar voices shape trust, self-congruency, and behavior
abstract: As voice agents become embedded in products as well as service interactions, firms increasingly seek personalization strategies that strengthen consumers' acceptance and engagement. This research examines whether voice agents that sound more similar to users' own voices elicit more favorable behavioral responses. Moreover, we investigate through which psychological mechanisms these effects occur. Across two experiments, we manipulate voice similarity using (1) pretested similar versus dissimilar AI voices and (2) individualized voice cloning that replicates users' voices. Results consistently show that higher voice similarity increases purchase intention, use intention, and willingness to disclose personal information. Mediation analyses indicate that voice similarity operates via two parallel mechanisms: self-congruency and trust. Our research advances research on voice agent-consumer relationships and demonstrates that increasing voice similarity is a robust personalization strategy that enhances consumers’ behavioral responses. © 2026 The Authors

title: When plateware shape matters: The congruence effects between food pungency and plateware shape on food preference
abstract: Although considerable attention has been paid to enhancing the visual appeal of food, less is known about how plateware design should align with the sensory characteristics of food. Drawing on shape-taste correspondence research and processing fluency theory, this research examines the congruence between plateware shape and food pungency. Across four online experiments with Chinese participants, we obtained 754 valid responses covering all seven major geographic regions of China. The results show that pungent foods elicit more favorable consumer responses when served on angular rather than round plateware, whereas mild foods are evaluated more favorably when served on round rather than angular plateware. Processing fluency mediates the effects of plateware shape and food pungency congruence on food evaluation and ordering intention. These findings extend research on shape-taste correspondences and demonstrate that simple, low-cost plateware design can improve consumer responses to foods with different sensory profiles. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrated cognitive processing model of phishing detection: Mood state as moderating factor in the mindful cognition mediated detection process
abstract: Previous studies have shown that security awareness alone is not consistently associated with phishing detection accuracy, yet the processes through which awareness is associated with detection remain underexplored. Existing phishing research has also predominantly adopted a cognitive perspective, despite the interdependent nature of affect and cognition in decision-making. To address these gaps, this study adopts an affect-integrated cognitive processing perspective and examines a proposed cognitive process involving security awareness, domain mindfulness, cognitive processing, and mood state, with particular attention to the conditional role of positive mood in performance-focused phishing judgments. Our findings show that security awareness is not directly associated with phishing detection accuracy; rather, a significant indirect association is observed through domain mindfulness and cognitive processing. Although temperament is not directly associated with detection accuracy, it is positively associated with mood state. Positive mood is negatively associated with detection accuracy, and the estimated beneficial indirect associations involving domain mindfulness and cognitive processing are weaker at higher levels of positive mood. Together, the results are consistent with a phishing-detection process involving both cognitive and affective factors. This study extends cognition-focused phishing-detection models by integrating affective boundary conditions into the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
