title: Store coolness in luxury fashion: Antecedents, outcomes, and the moderating role of price consciousness
abstract: In the context of luxury fashion stores, this study investigates the mediating role of the dimensions of store coolness (extraordinary, subcultural, iconic, and high status) in linking service quality of employees, store display, and store creativity with customers' behavioral intention and positive word-of-mouth (WOM). Additionally, the study examines whether price consciousness moderates any of these relationships. To gain a deeper understanding of how coolness is perceived in luxury fashion stores, we collected customer insights through interviews with 16 frequent store visitors. We then tested our proposed model using a survey administered to shoppers immediately after they visited luxury stores (N = 213). Our results indicate that the extraordinary and subcultural dimensions of coolness positively mediate the effects of store display and creativity on behavioral intention and positive WOM. However, the iconic dimension did not play a mediating role, while the high status dimension negatively mediated these paths, including those involving service quality. Finally, we found that price consciousness weakens the path from store creativity to the studied outcomes via the extraordinary dimension. Building on these findings, we provide managerial insights for designing luxury fashion store experiences that foster store coolness and positive customer responses. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Unveiling research trends in artificial intelligence adoption based on the UTAUT: A bibliometric analysis supporting SDGs and future outlook
abstract: The development of AI adoption across disciplines has become a major global concern, especially with the UTAUT model that runs concurrently. This study aims to map research trends on AI adoption within the UTAUT model in conceptual, intellectual, and social structures. The research utilises a bibliometric approach from the Scopus database for the period 2018-2025 on related topics. Data analysis was conducted descriptively using Biblioshiny (Rstudio). The study found a very positive and significant development in research on AI adoption within the UTAUT model across various disciplines, aligning with the SDGs, particularly points four, nine, and seventeen. The countries that contributed most were China and the USA. Interesting themes for studying the development of UTAUT model implications include social influence, performance expectancy, behaviour, perceived risk, digital literacy, and AI anxiety. In SDG 4, the adoption of AI in higher education is crucial by incorporating perceived risk and digital literacy to achieve effective personalised learning. In SDG 9, organisational and corporate levels within managerial structures are important for combining structural and psychological factors that influence AI adoption. AIMDSS in the healthcare sector is essential for supporting health innovation and infrastructure. Meanwhile, for SDG 17, discovering best practices for AI adoption across various fields needs to be accelerated, particularly in Africa, South America, and most of Eastern Europe. The implications of this research point to the development of institutional guidelines for AI adoption and the exploration of the UTAUT model. By highlighting the evolving role of contextual, ethical, and governance-related factors, this study provides a foundation for aligning AI adoption strategies with sustainable development objectives and informs future empirical and policy-oriented research. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Tell me the truth: Consumer responses to feedback solicitation with robots versus humans
abstract: Advanced technologies enable service robots to handle a broader range of tasks than ever before. Among these, this research examines the potential of service robots to solicit and collect high-quality consumer feedback. This research, comprising four experimental studies, including a field study in a hotel, demonstrates that unsatisfied consumers are more likely to provide honest feedback to service robots than to human employees. Drawing on the theory of mind perception, the present research finds that such an effect is attributed to consumers’ concern for others' feelings (i.e., empathetic concern). Moreover, the proposed effects are diminished when the robot has a high (vs. low) level of emotional capability but are more pronounced among consumers with interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal. This research offers practical insights that enable advanced robotic technologies to be useful beyond simple physical tasks: consumer feedback management. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: CONSENT IS NOT JUST ABOUT ASKING: HOW YOU REQUEST CONSUMERS’ AGREEMENT TO COOKIES MATTERS
abstract: Website cookie notices influence consent decisions by configuring multiple design cues within the privacy calculus consumers apply when evaluating data disclosure. Results of an online experiment (N = 776) suggest that freedom of choice and cookie notice placement influence consumers’ perceived power. In addition, technical language influences perceived risk. Perceived power, perceived risk, and consumers’ emotions influence behavioral intentions toward cookie notices. The findings show that cookie notice cues operate configurally rather than independently, revealing a configurational privacy calculus in which the impact of any single design element depends on the broader configuration of cues in which it appears. © 2027 California State University, Long Beach. .

title: Trends and directions in military professionalism research: A scopus-based bibliometric analysis
abstract: The current bibliometric analysis examines the evolution of research related to professionalism in the military based on the Scopus database. Author contributions, country-based production, institutional engagement, and co-occurrence analysis were reported. The biblioshiny in the R language was used to examine the data, and the Garza-Reyes was utilised to ensure the validity and reliability of the data. In this case, a total of 35 relevant publications were selected to be reported in the bibliometric analysis. Based on the finding, the USA is the most contributing country and has a steady increase in the number of publications, which peaked in 2023. However, even though the USA was indicated as the country with the most publications in this research theme, the United Kingdom was found to have the most impactful and influential publication, with a total cited score of 49. In terms of the most contributive affiliation, Uniformed Services University from the USA was dominant and followed by two universities from the Netherlands namely, VU University Medical Centre and the Netherlands Defence Academy. For the most contributive authors, Cole Rebekah and Rudinsky Sherri L were identified as the most productive authors. In this case, the author production over time analysis indicates Cole Rebekah, and Rudinsky Sherri L, are the most productive and influential authors in this research theme. In the thematic map analysis, the concepts of 'human', 'military personnel', and 'humans' emerge as well-developed and central, indicating that discussions around military professionalism are strongly anchored in the human dimension of service members. It was emphasised in the co-occurrence analysis that highlights the centrality of military personnel, humans, and humans, which appear as the most frequent and interconnected terms, indicating that research on military professionalism is predominantly framed around the human dimension and the role of personnel. Finally, the current research reveals three major military professional research directions through Multiple Correspondence Analysis namely, (1) education and social identity, (2) healthcare personnel and military health, and (3) professionalism and ethics, with demographic factors serving as a transversal element across clusters. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Advancing bibliometric analysis: Evidence-based guidelines with insights from senior journal editors
abstract: Bibliometric analysis is a powerful means of evaluating research. This article employs a sequential mixed-methods approach to enrich the understanding of bibliometric analysis and presents a structured guide to maximize the technique's benefits. A thematically synthesized narrative commentary on bibliometric review papers, based on input from 53 senior editorial members of leading hospitality and tourism journals, constitutes the study's foundation. Cutting-edge literature comprising 195 bibliometric investigations is also considered. Our evidence-based guidance provides scholars with a roadmap for conducting state-of-the-art bibliometric analyses. These suggestions are intended to improve the method's quality and accessibility, affirming its utility. Ultimately, this paper seeks to enhance bibliometric studies’ clarity, rigor, and efficacy by presenting forward-looking, real-world insights. Its step-by-step guide will facilitate decision-making and advance the field's theoretical and managerial understanding. © 2026

title: Should generative AI be responsible to users? Developing and validating the user-generative AI psychological contract scale
abstract: As GenAI becomes increasingly embedded in AI-enabled service interactions, users' evaluations of AI are extending from functional performance to expectations regarding responsibility and obligation. Drawing on Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) theory and psychological contract theory, this study defines the user–generative AI psychological contract (AIPC) as users' beliefs about the responsibilities and obligations GenAI should fulfill toward them during ongoing interaction and develops a corresponding scale. Study 1 used purposively recruited interviews (N = 26) to identify the construct content domain. Study 2 used two nonprobability online-panel samples of active GenAI users (N = 507 and N = 506) to develop the items and examine the factor structure, reliability, and construct validity. Study 3 used the same 506-case sample employed for structural validation in Study 2 to provide an initial test of the nomological network among AIPC, AI anthropomorphism, and co-creation intention. Results indicate that AIPC consists of three dimensions—the functional support contract, relational collaboration contract, and ethical safety contract—and forms a 16-item scale. Users reported the strongest expectations regarding ethical safety. Anthropomorphism was indirectly associated with co-creation intention through functional support and relational collaboration, but not through ethical safety. The findings extend psychological contract theory to user–AI relationships and provide a measurement tool for studying responsibility expectations toward GenAI. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Factors affecting public transport adoption in Riyadh- case study
abstract: Riyadh's greenhouse gas emissions and urban climate risks are likely heightened by accelerated urbanization and profound dependence on private cars. Despite the government's investment in public transportation, societal resistance to giving up private cars and using public transit persists due to cultural and traditional factors. Within the Gulf context, this study is the first to investigate the unique socio-cultural and urban context of Riyadh to understand university students' mobility behavior, identify four factors that significantly are associated with their travel choices, and quantitatively rank the relative influence of these factors. Surveys (n = 710) were used to assess four key factors, analyzed via multiple regression, chi-square, and t-tests. Results indicate that, in descending order of influence, psychological factors (explaining 23% of the variance) have the most significant association with students' willingness to switch to public transport in Riyadh, followed by trip characteristics (13%), urban factors (12%), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (12%). The result suggests that, alongside infrastructure improvements, coordinated strategies are required to change social norms, enhance environmental awareness, and create culturally responsive incentives. The findings support the implementation of place-based policies for sustainable mobility. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Hungry for change: Inclusive dining for travelers with dietary restrictions
abstract: Dining is central to tourism experiences, yet for travelers with dietary restrictions, it can become a source of exclusion rather than enjoyment. Guided by stigma theory, this study examines how dietary restrictions function as a form of concealable stigma in tourism dining contexts. Using a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design, the study combines Critical Incident Technique interviews with 32 individuals and text mining of 3,165 traveler Yelp reviews. Findings reveal that stigma manifests through internal (self-burden, anticipatory anxiety) and external (public, structural, associative) forms producing psychological and behavioral consequences that constrain participation in dining experiences. Individuals employ a range of voluntary and involuntary coping responses to navigate such challenges. Building on these findings, the study proposes a mutual reinforcement model in which internal and external stigma recursively sustain one another across repeated dining encounters, highlighting the anticipatory and cumulative nature of dietary stigma in tourism and offering theoretical and practical insights. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Recommend or not? Investigating the effectiveness of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising
abstract: Online charitable platforms are important channels through which the public participates in micro-donations, and these platforms have increasingly leveraged algorithmic recommendation technologies to deliver personalized charitable advertisements to potential donors. Nonetheless, whether personalized algorithmic recommendations enhance or undermine consumers’ micro-donation intentions remains unclear. Drawing on moral identity theory, our research addresses this gap through five online scenario-based experiments. The results show that consumers exhibit lower micro-donation intentions when exposed to micro-donation advertisements with personalized algorithmic recommendations, and that this negative effect is driven primarily by perceived identity value threat. Furthermore, we find that the negative effect of personalized algorithmic recommendations in micro-donation advertising is attenuated in the presence of legitimization cues or among consumers with low scores on the moral identity scale. Our findings not only extend the literature on the antecedents of micro-donations and the economic consequences of algorithmic personalization in the charitable advertising context, but also offer actionable guidance for charitable platforms seeking to optimize their algorithmic recommendation strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Perceptions of biodiversity benefits of regional food: A Q-method study from a German biosphere reserve
abstract: Increasing consumer demand for food produced using biodiversity-friendly practices may create market incentives that support biodiversity conservation. However, there is limited understanding of consumer perspectives regarding the perceived biodiversity aspects of such products. This study represents an empirical approach to investigate how consumers perceive biodiversity-related attributes of regional products and how these perceptions influence purchase motivation in the context of the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve. Regional product criteria related to biodiversity protection and prevalence within the Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve were assessed through a literature review. The Q-method was applied to determine their influence on consumer purchase motivation. Key findings include the determination of three prevalent consumer perspectives consisting of Traditional Regionalists valuing local community support and cultural identity, Environmental Pragmatists appreciating criteria with direct environmental protection benefits and Quality Seekers being motivated by concerns of food safety and transparency in the food industry. The regional product criteria were revisited regarding their importance for the individual consumer perspectives, providing insights into how each group relates to criteria associated with perceived biodiversity benefits. Equal to future research prospects extending on the relevance of demographic and economic variables, these insights suggest potential pathways for adapting and expanding the offering of biodiversity-friendly regional products, in combination with consumer-oriented communication and marketing approaches. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Appliance-level energy assessment and its implications for the environmental impact of household energy conservation: Evidence from urban China
abstract: Accurate appliance-level energy judgments may help households identify and prioritize meaningful electricity-saving opportunities, with potential implications for the environmental benefits of household conservation. Using survey and experimental data from 2592 residents in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, this paper assesses how accurately urban households estimate the electricity consumption of 11 common appliances, whether their judgments exhibit patterns consistent with availability-based reasoning, and whether a randomized heat-related information cue improves relative appliance-energy judgments. The results reveal substantial misalignment between perceived and benchmark electricity use: (1) respondents tend to overestimate the energy use of low-energy, frequently used appliances (e.g., televisions) while underestimating high-energy, infrequently interacted devices (e.g., water heaters); (2) appliance use frequency is positively associated with perceived energy consumption, a pattern consistent with greater cognitive accessibility of frequently used appliances; (3) random assignment to the heat-related cue increases perceived energy use for heat-producing appliances and improves respondents' measured relative correspondence with the benchmark; and (4) further analyses show that higher educational attainment is associated with closer benchmark alignment and that closer alignment is associated with lower reported household electricity expenditures. These findings document systematic deviations in appliance-level energy judgments and show that a targeted information cue can improve such judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: What drives hybrid cultivated meat acceptance? Evidence from a controlled real-product tasting
abstract: Despite growing interest in cultivated meat, most consumer-related evidence remains based on hypothetical assessments rather than real product exposure, limiting understanding of actual sensory-driven acceptance. To address this gap, the present study investigated consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated chicken product through a controlled affective sensory evaluation with young Singaporean consumers. Participants (n = 82) evaluated overall liking and sensory liking for appearance, smell, taste, texture, and aftertaste, completed Just-About-Right (JAR) diagnostics and were segmented according to Net Promoter Score (NPS) responses. JAR penalty analysis suggested that deviations from optimal sensory intensity systematically affected overall liking, with excessive intensity perceived in taste, smell, and aftertaste generating the largest penalties. Across sensory dimensions, oral attributes exerted a stronger influence on liking than appearance, with taste emerging as the primary driver of acceptance and texture showing a secondary contribution. Multiple regression analysis confirmed taste liking as the strongest predictor of overall liking, whereas the remaining sensory aspects showed weaker or non-significant effects. NPS segmentation further revealed clear differences in recommendation behaviour across detractors, passives, and promoters, closely mirroring hedonic liking patterns and supporting consistency between sensory evaluation and recommendation-oriented behavioural responses. Overall, this study provides an initial empirical benchmark of consumer responses to a commercially available hybrid cultivated meat product under controlled conditions, highlighting the central role of taste quality and sensory balance in shaping hedonic responses and consumer satisfaction. The findings offer a reference point for future research as cultivated meat products potentially enter broader markets. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Digital influences on green economic participation: The role of eWOM in shaping circular consumption among young vietnamese consumers
abstract: Circular business models (CBMs) are increasingly recognized as a strategic mechanism for advancing sustainable consumption and supporting green economic growth, particularly in emerging economies where rising consumption intensifies pressures on natural resources and waste management systems. Concurrently, the rapid expansion of social media and digital commerce has elevated electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to a central role in shaping how young consumers interpret, evaluate, and normalize sustainability-oriented business practices. Despite this growing intersection, limited empirical evidence explains how specific attributes of eWOM translate into consumers’ intentions to participate in CBMs, especially in developing-market contexts such as Vietnam. Addressing this gap, the present study adopts a quantitative approach using survey data from 1,142 young Vietnamese consumers to examine how core dimensions of eWOM influence information acceptance and, subsequently, participation intentions in CBMs within the retail sector. A rigorous multi-stage analytical procedure was employed, including reliability testing, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to validate the measurement model, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to assess the structural relationships among latent constructs. The results indicate that all four eWOM attributes positively influence information acceptance, which in turn significantly drives participation intention. Among these factors, relevance emerges as the most influential attribute, suggesting that sustainability-related messages are most effective when aligned with consumers’ personal needs, values, and decision contexts. The findings also confirm the mediating role of information acceptance in translating eWOM quality into behavioral intention. By validating both the measurement and structural models, this study enhances the robustness of IAM-based explanations in the context of circular consumption and extends the literature on digital influence in emerging markets. Practically, the study highlights the importance of designing relevant, credible, and comprehensive sustainability communication strategies. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted with caution due to the cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling approach. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: When loyalty points become donations: The effects of redeemability, point expiration, and descriptive norm information
abstract: Although loyalty programs and checkout charity are widely implemented across retail industries, the integration of reward point donations into online checkout charity remains rare, and consumer behavior in this context is not yet fully understood. While a few studies have explored reward point donations and generally reported positive consumer responses, to the best of our knowledge, little research has examined how reward point characteristics and situational factors influence consumers' willingness to donate. To address this gap, the present research examines, across three studies, the effect of point redeemability on consumers’ donation intention through online checkout charity, as well as the moderating roles of point expiration and descriptive norm information. Study 1 shows that consumers exhibit higher donation intention when their reward points are non-redeemable than when they are redeemable. Study 2 demonstrates that the interaction between point redeemability and point expiration significantly influences donation intention, while Study 3 shows that the interaction between point redeemability and descriptive norm information also significantly affects donation intention. The findings provide actionable insights for retailers seeking to design more effective reward point donation programs and enhance social impact through online checkout charity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A framework integrating topological potential and semantic embeddings for identifying scientific research clusters in scholarly collaboration networks
abstract: Multi-team collaboration is essential for addressing major scientific challenges. Previous methods focus predominantly on individuals or single teams, making it difficult to capture the structure of multi-team collaborative innovation systems. To address this, this study conceptualizes a research cluster as a multi-team system formed through inter-team relationships and related research goals within complex collaborative research environments. We further introduce a four-phase Topological Potential–Semantic Embedding Research Cluster Identification (TPSE-RCI) framework to identify scientific research clusters. First, research teams are detected and a team collaboration network is constructed. Second, team feature vectors are generated via topological potential–enhanced Node2Vec and initial clusters are identified with HDBSCAN. Third, team publications are analyzed using BERTopic with BGE-M3 semantic embeddings to derive hierarchical research goals. Fourth, validity criteria are applied to filter scientific research clusters. Using medical informatics publications as a case study, we detected 4262 research teams from 81,557 publications by 269,598 authors. At the structural level, 702 initial scientific research clusters were identified. At the thematic level, 319 topics were extracted from the team publications and consolidated into 21 secondary and 7 primary research goals. By integrating structural and thematic results, we ultimately identified 239 scientific research clusters. Comparative and ablation analyses indicate that incorporating topological potential improves team representation and structural-clustering quality within this empirical setting. The identified research clusters can provide decision support for practical tasks such as organized research management, major project coordination and optimization, domain expert identification, and research resource allocation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Repairing trust in AI: Attribution, anthropomorphism, and the illusion of difference
abstract: Trust repair between humans and AI systems is an emerging area of inquiry that builds on a well-established literature in human–human (HH) interactions. This review examines how key HH findings, particularly the differential effectiveness of repair strategies following competence versus integrity violations, generalize to human–robot interaction (HRI). While some patterns hold, important divergences exist. The paper argues that better operationalizations of integrity violations and increased anthropomorphism can align HRI findings more closely with HH research. However, enduring challenges remain regarding the ethics of anthropomorphic design, the moral values AI should adopt, and how AI should extend trust to humans. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Online dating paradox: Why lonely hearts choose to ghost
abstract: This study examines the differential associations of state and trait loneliness with ghosting behavior in online dating, considering self-presentation strategies and dating fatigue as potential explanatory pathways. Survey data from 881 Chinese mobile dating app users were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that state loneliness was negatively associated with ghosting, whereas trait loneliness was positively associated with ghosting. Dating fatigue was positively associated with ghosting and statistically mediated the associations between both forms of loneliness and ghosting in opposite directions. Acquisitive self-presentation was positively associated with state loneliness and negatively associated with trait loneliness; unexpectedly, it was negatively associated with dating fatigue. Authentic self-presentation was not significantly associated with loneliness or dating fatigue. These findings suggest that temporary and chronic loneliness may correspond to different patterns of engagement and disengagement in online dating. The study contributes to mobile dating research by distinguishing state and trait loneliness and by identifying dating fatigue as an important correlate of ghosting behavior. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. The paper reflects on epistemic justice in energy- and ocean governance, and asks whether and how United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) facilitates that such justice is sought in the regulatory process of deep sea mining by focusing on procedural rules for the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and the representation of different knowers in the decision-making process, including its Council's structure, authority, and composition. It concludes that a very small number of individuals has the power to bring about a very large change in deep sea mining regulations, currently without legal requirements to include experiential, traditional or other forms of knowledges beyond the scientific method in the decision-making process. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Technostress in the age of digital transformation and AI: A bibliometric–systematic literature review for HRM research
abstract: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are reshaping human resource management through algorithmic recruitment, automated evaluation, predictive analytics, and generative tools. While these systems improve efficiency, they also intensify technostress through opacity, surveillance, reduced control, and digitally intensified work arrangements. Responding to a fragmented literature spanning both AI-enabled and broader digital work systems, this study provides a B-SLR that maps technostress in digital transformation while identifying AI-specific stressors as a key emerging stream for HRM research. Drawing on 194 Scopus-indexed articles, we combine performance analysis and science mapping to identify publication trends, dominant themes, and intellectual structures. The review shows how AI-specific stressors extend established technostress mechanisms and shift attention toward transparency, control, fairness, and responsible HRM design. We conclude with actionable implications for researchers and practitioners aiming to design more transparent, responsible, and sustainable digital and AI-enabled HRM systems. © 2026 The Authors

title: Familiar faces, honest answers? The impacts of enumerator familiarity and modality on survey responses
abstract: Survey data can be distorted through mistrust, discomfort, or demand effects on the part of respondents. We test whether familiar enumerators – those with whom a respondent has completed a prior survey – influence data quality in a panel survey with small business owners in Uganda. We randomly assign respondents to a familiar or a new enumerator and cross-cut a second randomization to an in-person or phone-based interview modality. Across a broad set of outcome types, we observe few impacts of either survey method on means, distributions, or attrition. However, respondents are significantly more likely to give norm-congruent answers to new surveyors compared to familiar ones. The effect of familiarity does not interact significantly with a prior experiment conducted with the same sample, suggesting that familiarity influences estimates of levels but not of treatment impacts. These findings suggest that surveys by familiar enumerators can improve the measurement of sensitive beliefs. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Comparing AI chatbot users and non-users in Germany: Reasons for use, addictive AI chatbot use, mental health, and loneliness
abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots is becoming increasingly popular worldwide. To prevent potential negative consequences associated with the use at an early stage, it is crucial to understand its associations with mental health. Therefore, the present study compared people who use AI chatbots with those who do not engage in AI chatbot-interactions in terms of mental health and loneliness. Moreover, we investigated potential mechanisms associated with addictive AI chatbot use. Data of 7,312 persons (3,729 users: 42.1% men, 57.9% women; Mage = 42.23, SDage = 13.33; 3,583 non-users: 42.6% men, 57.4% women; Mage, = 54.28, SDage = 14.49) from the German adult population were collected via an online survey. AI chatbot users had significantly higher levels of loneliness, depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms, and significantly lower levels of life satisfaction than non-users. Users primarily engaged in AI chatbot-interactions for informational and practical reasons, such as obtaining information and inspiration, and receiving text-related assistance. The frequency of AI chatbot use to escape negative emotions was significantly positively associated with addictive tendencies. Loneliness statistically mediated the association between addictive AI chatbot use and the mental health variables. Most observed effect sizes were small. The present findings show that using AI chatbots for emotion regulation is positively associated with higher addictive tendencies and lower levels of mental health. Further experimental longitudinal research is urgently needed to clarify causal mechanisms of these associations. © 2026 The Authors

title: Divergent relationships between moral disengagement and cyberbullying bystander response behaviors: Examining the amplifying roles of humor and anonymity
abstract: While bystander response behaviors are pivotal for cyberbullying (CB) intervention, prior research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding their correlates, partly because it has often treated diverse bystander responses as a monolithic construct and failed to distinguish constructive defense from aggressive defense. Furthermore, few empirical studies have examined how digital affordances interact with individual factors in relation to diverse bystander responses within a Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) framework. To address these gaps, this study examined the main and interactive associations of individual moral disengagement (MD), perceived anonymity, and humor of CB with four distinct online bystander responses (constructive defense, aggressive defense, inaction, and reinforcement). A final analytic sample of 1201 Chinese secondary school students, selected via multi-stage random sampling, completed a survey assessing MD, CB contexts, and real online bystander responses. Multilevel analysis indicated that MD, perceived anonymity and humor were consistently and negatively associated with constructive defense but positively associated with inaction. Conversely, MD and anonymity were positively associated with aggressive defense, whereas humor showed no significant link. Regarding reinforcement behaviors, perceived anonymity and humor were positive predictors, whereas MD exerted a non-significant association. Moderation analyses revealed that anonymity strengthened MD's positive associations with inaction and reinforcement, whereas humor amplified MD's association solely with reinforcement. These findings underscore the necessity of distinguishing constructive from aggressive defense and integrating individual moral cognition with contextual cues for both exploring correlates of online bystander response and designing CB interventions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When GAI backfires: Understanding the process mechanism of consumers’ avoidance of generative AI conversational recommendation agents from a misaligned affordance perspective
abstract: Generative AI-enhanced conversational recommendation agents (GCRAs) are being widely deployed on e-commerce platforms; however, consumers increasingly avoid these advanced recommendation tools. Prior research has not systematically identified which specific features of GCRAs drive such avoidance, nor has it clearly articulated the underlying process mechanisms through which avoidance emerges. To address these gaps, this study draws on affordance actualization theory and misaligned affordance theory to systematically investigate consumers’ perceived GCRA misaligned affordances and to model the complete pathways from these misaligned affordances to consumer avoidance behaviors. We employed a sequential mixed-methods approach. First, a qualitative interview research (N = 19) combined with a simple experiment identified three key GCRA misaligned affordances: limited choices, iterative dialogue, and hallucinated information. Second, a quantitative research (N = 538) validated that these misaligned affordances trigger cost-based comparative appraisals (opportunity and transaction costs), which in turn lead to negative experiences (both outcome-related and process-related), ultimately driving consumer avoidance. Finally, by integrating the findings across studies, we developed a comprehensive framework explaining consumers’ avoidance of GCRAs. Theoretically, this research advances the misaligned affordance actualization theory by highlighting the novel comparative appraisal stage, moving the theory from qualitative conceptualization to process-level mechanisms. Collectively, these findings provide new theoretical insights and practical guidance for improving the design and deployment of GCRAs. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Effects of AI-based chatbot coaching on goal attainment, self-efficacy, and stress: A longitudinal randomized experiment
abstract: Students in higher education face a range of academic challenges, which leads to high levels of stress among many students. While coaching has been shown to help students address these challenges, it is resource-intensive and therefore not broadly accessible. AI-based chatbots may help broaden access by providing interactive and personalized guidance at scale, yet empirical evidence on their effectiveness remains limited, particularly from longitudinal experimental studies. Addressing this gap, we conducted a longitudinal between-subjects experiment with four measurement points across an academic semester, randomly assigning 101 students to one of three conditions: AI-based chatbot coaching, literature-based self-study (active control), or a waitlist control condition. Students in the chatbot coaching and literature study conditions engaged in repeated interactions with the intervention, averaging approximately 100 min of cumulative interaction time accumulated across four sessions of 23–28 min each. We examined how students’ goal attainment, university-related self-efficacy, and stress developed over the course of the study. Results showed that students in the AI-based chatbot condition achieved significantly stronger increases in goal attainment over time compared to students in both control conditions. Self-efficacy also increased in the AI-based chatbot condition over time; however, between-condition differences were not consistent across time points, suggesting that the intervention had a more limited impact on self-efficacy relative to goal attainment. Furthermore, no significant effects were found for university-related stress. The findings suggest that AI-based chatbot coaching can effectively support students in achieving university-related goals and strengthening their self-efficacy, while its impact on stress reduction may be limited. © 2026 The Authors

title: Enhancing situational awareness in health systems: A scoping review of technologies and cross-industry insights
abstract: Background: Situational awareness technologies are increasingly utilised in healthcare systems to facilitate timely and coordinated decision-making. Reported implementation considerations include data quality, governance, and integration into everyday workflows. Objective: This scoping review aimed to map technologies, systems, and methods used to enhance situational awareness in health service delivery and to identify approaches used in other industries that could be adapted for healthcare, particularly in regional and remote settings. Methods: We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance for scoping reviews. Electronic databases (PubMed and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between January 2000 and October 2025. Reference lists and citation searches in Google Scholar were also examined. Records meeting the inclusion criteria were screened and reviewed, with key data extracted using a structured charting form and synthesised into seven application domains. Results: Searches identified 744 records, of which 23 studies were included. These covered diverse technologies such as dashboards, forecasting models, alert systems, and geospatial decision environments. Most studies were from high-income countries (n = 19). Studies reported potential benefits for visibility, coordination, and decision-making. However, most evidence was descriptive, with limited evidence of whether these systems improve service delivery. Recurrent implementation challenges included data fragmentation, limited interoperability, and misalignment between governance and workflow. Conclusions: This review highlights the need for more rigorous and context-sensitive evaluations of technologies used to enhance situational awareness in healthcare, especially in regional and resource-limited settings. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

title: Conflict expression: A decade of group conflict research
abstract: The conflict expression framework was developed to generate new practical and theoretical insights into how conflict communication affects group processes and negotiated outcomes. The framework proposes that conflict expressions vary along two dimensions: directness and oppositional intensity. The framework suggested that the effects of different types of conflict on group processes and outcomes likely depend on how the conflict is expressed, that conflict within groups is likely perceived differently by different members of the same social unit, and that conflict affects negotiation processes dynamically through reciprocated statements and responses. We review research building on the framework – including empirical tests of the main propositions, methodological advances, and as a theoretical foundation for conflict communication research more broadly – and identify directions for the future. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Performative narratives and destination image in cross-cultural tourism livestreaming
abstract: Tourism livestreaming allows global audiences to encounter destinations in real time, yet how livestreamers’ expressive behaviors shape audiences’ destination evaluations across cultures remains unclear. Drawing on a performative perspective, this research conceptualizes expressed destination image formation as a temporally situated process generated through live narrative enactment. Using multimodal cross-cultural livestream data, the study shows that emotional expression is positively associated with expressed affective destination image, explicit self-disclosure is positively associated with expressed cognitive image, and interactive engagement shows partial evidence of an inverted U-shaped relationship with expressed cognitive destination image. Cross-cultural proximity further operates unevenly: cultural distance reshapes the interaction–cognition pathway, whereas linguistic accessibility improves destination image expression but does not consistently amplify performative cues. Finally, post-livestream destination image expression attenuates over time, with affective impressions fading faster. Overall, this research clarifies how destination image expression is performatively activated, cross-culturally conditioned, and temporally attenuated in tourism livestreaming. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Emotional interaction and conversion value in live streaming E-commerce
abstract: Multi-agent emotional interaction constitutes a core characteristic of live streaming e-commerce. Nevertheless, prior research has yet to build a unified analytical framework incorporating streamers, viewers and live streaming assistants, and rarely explored how emotional dynamics shape live streaming performance. Based on minute-level panel data of 4671 min retrieved from 40 Taobao live streaming sessions, this study adopts sentiment analysis to quantify the emotional expressions of streamers and viewers. Applying the Panel Vector Autoregression (PVAR) model and impulse response analysis, this study constructs a tripartite emotional interaction system among streamers, viewers and assistants, and investigates its dynamic linkage with core operational performance, including product sales and new follower growth. The empirical results are consistent with a unidirectional streamer-to-viewer emotional association, whereby streamer emotions are closely associated with viewer interaction and purchase decisions. By contrast, intra-viewer emotional association is not statistically supported, whereas viewer emotions are positively associated with new follower growth. Higher frequency of live streaming assistant intervention shows a dual association pattern: it is positively associated with viewer interaction frequency, but negatively associated with product sales. This study extends the application scope of emotional contagion theory in the live streaming context, enriches the role configuration of the live streaming e-commerce ecosystem, and offers practical and targeted operational strategies for live streaming management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The temporal shift in consumer hue preferences in hotel booking
abstract: Despite the hospitality industry's ongoing pursuit of optimal color marketing strategies, it remains unclear whether consumers respond more favorably to cool or warm hues. This research investigates how consumers' hue preferences in digital marketing imagery shift as a function of time of day. Through a case coding analysis (n = 4510), an eye-tracking experiment (n = 105), three online experiments (n = 981), and a quasi-experimental field survey with real tourists (n = 316), this research reveals temporal shifts in hue preference in hotel booking contexts, such that consumers prefer hotel room photos with cool hues in the morning and warm hues in the evening. These preferences are mediated by the need for uniqueness and the need for belonging, respectively. Furthermore, the effect is moderated by visual temporal cues (window view) and individual circadian rhythms (chronotype). Our findings challenge static perspectives on color psychology and offer actionable guidance for time-adaptive visual marketing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Assessing the environmental–economic viability of expressway photovoltaics in China: A spatio–temporal life cycle perspective
abstract: Expressway corridors are increasingly considered for distributed photovoltaic deployment, but their environmental–economic viability depends strongly on local solar resources, infrastructure availability, grid structure, and future decarbonization pathways. This study develops an integrated framework that combines spatio–temporal assessment with environmental life cycle costing to evaluate the deployment potential and comprehensive benefits of expressway photovoltaic systems across 351 prefecture–level cities in China. The assessment covers service areas, rest areas, and expressway slopes under business-as-usual and carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenarios. Results indicate that expressway slopes provide the greatest installation potential, with 49.71% of cities supporting more than 200 MW. At the national-average level, expressway photovoltaic systems yield a net internal benefit of 317.05 USD/kW and a net environmental benefit of 249.48 USD/kW under the business-as-usual scenario. Inverter and monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic module production are the main contributors to environmental costs. Under the carbon-neutrality-by-2060 scenario, grid decarbonization reduces the avoided environmental burden of photovoltaic electricity and delays the transition to positive net environmental benefits from 2035 to 2037. These findings support a shift from capacity-oriented expansion to region-specific life cycle planning, prioritizing corridors where solar resources, expressway availability, grid displacement benefits, and recycling infrastructure are jointly favorable. © 2026

title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Screening out ethics: How technology enables ethical fading in negotiations
abstract: Negotiations are rife with opportunities and temptations to engage in unethical negotiating behavior. Such behavior is not always strategic or even intentional; rather, it can emerge from situational characteristics of the negotiation environment. One psychological process through which situational characteristics influence unethical behavior is ethical fading, a process that limits one's ability to recognize the ethical aspects of the situation and behave in line with one's ethical values. As technologies such as email, video conferencing, and artificial intelligence (AI) become increasingly common in negotiations, an important question is whether these technologies facilitate ethical fading. In this review, we explore the impact that technology and AI have on ethical fading and unethical negotiating behavior. We propose that technology and AI use in negotiations promotes three cognitive processes that facilitate ethical fading: psychological distance, cognitive offloading, and displaced accountability. We review how technology may serve as an antecedent to each of these processes and explain why these processes may facilitate ethical fading in negotiation contexts. Because research on the relationship between technology and unethical negotiating behavior remains limited, we conclude by identifying promising directions for future research. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: When does AI design help or hurt? Brand positioning and the dual effects of homogeneity and trend relevance in fashion retailing
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in fashion design to generate product aesthetics and forecast trends. While prior research has separately examined algorithmic homogeneity risks or efficiency gains, how consumers simultaneously process these opposing signals, and whether this processing differs from human-generated design, remains unclear. This study investigates how the attribution of design to AI (vs. human) influences consumer evaluations via dual pathways—perceived homogeneity and trend relevance—and examines brand positioning as a boundary condition. A 2 (design source: AI vs. human) × 2 (brand positioning: avant-garde vs. mainstream) between-subjects experiment with 412 consumers reveals that AI-attributed designs simultaneously heighten both perceptions. Multi-group analysis demonstrates that these perceptions operate through perceived manipulative intent, a mechanism significantly stronger for AI- than human-attributed designs. The two pathways exert opposing effects on brand sincerity and purchase intention. Brand positioning moderates these effects asymmetrically: the negative homogeneity pathway is amplified for avant-garde brands, while the positive trend-relevance pathway is strengthened for mainstream brands. These findings identify perceived manipulative intent as the core mechanism translating AI design attribution into consumer responses, and demonstrate that aligning AI adoption with brand positioning can either help or hurt brand sincerity. For fashion retailers, the implications are clear: communicate AI usage as value-creating rather than cost-cutting, and tailor AI strategies to brand positioning—avant-garde brands should emphasize human-AI collaboration, while mainstream brands should leverage AI's trend-sensing capabilities while guarding against stylistic sameness. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Who eats matters: How eating-agent identity in short-form retail videos influences consumers’ purchase intentions
abstract: Short-form retail videos frequently depict food consumption, yet little is known about whether the identity of the visible eater shapes how consumers evaluate the product. We conceptualize eating-agent identity as a contextual product cue and develop a cue-based inference account in which a pet eater makes nature-related meaning salient and, through visible consumption, connects that meaning to the focal food. Consequently, consumers infer greater product naturalness and greater healthiness, increasing purchase intention. This inference depends on how the consumption episode is structured: visible human assistance attenuates the pet advantage by altering the product-use relationship, whereas sponsorship disclosure changes the surrounding commercial context without necessarily disrupting that relationship. Five preregistered online experiments with 2462 retained participants from Chinese consumer panels support this account. Study 1 establishes the effect and examines alternative explanations. Study 2 demonstrates the sequential pathway through perceived naturalness and perceived healthiness. Study 3 manipulates naturalness information to provide causal evidence for the perceived naturalness component of the proposed pathway, Study 4 identifies eating autonomy as a boundary condition, and Study 5 shows that the focal pathway remains evident in the sponsorship disclosure context. The findings distinguish visible product users from promotional sources and reveal a scene-based route through which the contextual features of consumption episodes shape food attribute judgments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Mapping the global landscape of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship: A bibliometric review (2000–2025)
abstract: Mentorship is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of women’s entrepreneurial participation and success. However, existing scholarship remains fragmented, conceptually inconsistent, and unevenly distributed across global contexts. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of mentorship in women’s entrepreneurship, examining peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2025 globally. To enhance methodological robustness and address limitations associated with narrow keyword selection, a multi-stage search strategy was employed using the Scopus database. A total of 878 records were identified through the Scopus database. The final dataset includes 621 articles, allowing for a detailed analysis of publication trends, geographic distribution, authorship patterns, and thematic development within the field. The findings reveal a significant concentration of research output in the Global North, particularly in the United States and the United Kingdom, with comparatively limited representation from developing regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa. Thematic analysis indicates strong clustering around mentorship, coaching, entrepreneurial ecosystems, and capacity building, highlighting both conceptual convergence and fragmentation. Furthermore, the results show that mentorship is frequently embedded within broader entrepreneurial support frameworks rather than examined as a standalone construct. In response, this study advances a Gendered Social Capital and Learning framework to provide a more integrated understanding of mentorship processes in women’s entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the literature by offering a robust, data-driven overview of the field, identifying key gaps in geographic and theoretical coverage, and highlighting the methodological implications of keyword selection in bibliometric research. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to design more inclusive and contextually relevant mentorship interventions for women entrepreneurs. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: WISE: An interpretable word intensity framework for emotion-aware conversational systems
abstract: Emotion-aware conversational systems are increasingly adopted in healthcare, yet most emotion detection approaches rely on sentiment polarity, which fails to capture emotional nuance and intensity in short, informal chat messages. To overcome these limitations, this study develops an interpretable emotion-aware framework called Word Intensity Scoring Engine (WISE) that explicitly models emotional intensity in short-form conversational text. Grounded in Plutchik's Wheel of Emotions, WISE integrates lexicon-based emotion labeling, synonym expansion, semantic similarity using word embeddings, and negation-aware feature extraction to calculate intensity-weighted emotion scores at the word level. The WISE framework is evaluated through experimental benchmarking and an expert review involving practicing healthcare professionals. Results show that WISE enhances the performance of ML and LLM-based classifiers. Further, expert evaluations indicate that WISE-derived responses are perceived as professional, contextually appropriate, and empathetic. This study contributes a transparent, theoretically grounded design artifact that advances affective computing research and informs the deployment of emotion-aware conversational agents in healthcare. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Shared value vs plural values. Contesting renewable energy projects of the Enel Group
abstract: The energy transition triggers urgent questions about what values are important, who controls transitional processes, and who has the power to define the answers to the climate crisis. Energy companies claim their central role in the development of renewable energy as the ultimate solution. However, communities affected by large-scale renewable energy projects have extensively raised environmental and social justice concerns and denounced the industry's poor practices and abuses.In this article, we analyse 15 socio-environmental conflicts around renewable energy projects owned by the Enel Group, one of the world's largest energy utilities, through the values and valuation languages of the affected communities. We map them onto five dimensions: environmental, health-related, socio-economic, ontological, and political. We build on environmental justice and ecological economics literature on valuation languages and employ counter-accounting to gather bottom-up evidence of grievances.We argue that, while the company claims that RE is the ultimate solution and the ‘Creating Shared Value’ approach is beneficial to all parties, those impacted by Enel's projects question the corporate model of energy transition and defend a plurality of values embedded in relational worldviews that are systematically misrecognised. We eventually criticise the corporate self-attributed moral and value-centred mandate in the energy transition and call for inclusive research about desirable energy futures rooted in plural and relational value systems. title: From precarious work to occupational health outcomes in hotel housekeepers: a narrative review with meta-synthesis
abstract: Introduction: Hotel housekeepers sustain the core functioning of the hospitality industry yet perform demanding, repetitive, and undervalued work associated with substantial physical and psychosocial risks. Understanding how working conditions shape health, motivation, and lived experience is essential for informing prevention strategies and promoting decent work. Methods A sequential narrative review and qualitative meta -synthesis were conducted to integrate and reinterpret evidence across disciplines and study designs. Searches covered five academic databases and gray literature without year or language limits. Studies were screened using predefined criteria, appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and synthesized through narrative, tabular, and meta -analytical thematic analysis, with findings interpreted through the JD-R framework. Results Findings revealed employment precarity, work intensification, musculoskeletal pain, chemical and biological hazards, and elevated stress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Time pressure fostered coping strategies such as skipping meals and delaying bathroom use. Gendered labor divisions, discrimination, and negative supervision contributed to invisibility and limited autonomy. Workers also expressed pride, intrinsic motivation, and collective action to make their contributions visible. Conclusions This review demonstrates that housekeeping is characterized by structural precarity and cumulative health burdens alongside resilience and emerging activism. Improving occupational health requires organizational and policy transformations: realistic workloads, safer equipment, secure contracts, participatory risk management, and leadership practices grounded in dignity and fairness; rather than reliance on individual coping. Structural change is essential to advance safer, more equitable, and sustainable workplaces in the hospitality sector. The JD-R framework highlights the need to reduce demand and strengthen resources. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Material use and its relationship with per capita income. A panel data analysis at the global level
abstract: Global use of materials has significantly increased over recent decades, causing a wide range of environmental and social concerns. In this study, we use the latest available data from the UN database on global material flows to investigate the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for two widely used material flow indicators, Domestic Material Consumption and Material Footprint, for a dataset of 147 countries. Using both semiparametric and parametric methods over a longer period than any previous study (1970–2019), we find no evidence in support of the EKC hypothesis. A concerning result is that material-income elasticities are higher after 1989, implying that the situation has not improved. We conclude that major changes have not yet occurred in the income-material use relationship and that strong policy measures remain necessary to reduce material consumption. title: Personality engineering with AI agents: A new methodology for negotiation research
abstract: According to canonical negotiation theory, people's success in a negotiation depends on how well they balance competing demands—empathizing and asserting, demonstrating concern for other and concern for self, being soft on the people and hard on the problem. Yet people struggle to manage these tensions, so researchers have lacked the ability to rigorously test the field's prescriptions under controlled conditions. AI agents do not face the same limitations, and their precision, repertoire, consistency, and scalability enable a new class of experiments to contribute to negotiation theory. In this article, we introduce personality engineering—a methodology that precisely parameterizes the personas of AI agents based on established personality frameworks—and propose how this method can be used to study the traits and behaviors of negotiators. Given its relevance to negotiation theory, we propose the interpersonal circumplex—and its two core dimensions of warmth and dominance—as a foundational coordinate system for the field. This approach offers both a rigorous methodology for testing classic negotiation theories and a practical guide for designing the personas of AI negotiation agents. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors' Takeaways for Future Pandemics
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors' perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. title: From sound to resonance: Club anthem attractiveness and fan–brand relationships
abstract: Auditory branding plays an increasingly important role in sensory service experiences; however, limited research has examined how recurring auditory brand cues relate to consumer–brand relationship outcomes. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework as an organizing logic, this study examines associations among club anthem attractiveness (CAA), positive emotion (PE), post-exposure brand cognition (BC), and fan–brand resonance (FBR) in sports leisure services. Data were collected from a screened nonprobability online sample of 468 respondents in China. Participants listened to one of three standardized 90-s club anthem excerpts before evaluating CAA, PE, BC, and FBR. CAA was positively associated with both PE and BC, and these responses were positively associated with FBR. The two prespecified coefficient products were positive, whereas the residual direct CAA–FBR association was not significant. A separate balanced validation study (N = 450) supported CAA's empirical distinction from simple anthem liking, PE, BC, FBR, and prior brand attitude. CAA explained additional variance in PE and BC beyond simple liking and pre-exposure controls, while its incremental association with FBR was small. The findings indicate that evaluations of recurring auditory brand cues covary with consumer–brand relationship outcomes alongside affective and cognitive responses. This study extends auditory branding and sensory service literature by conceptualizing recurring branded sound as a service-embedded cue and examining theoretically ordered affective and cognitive associations. Because CAA was measured and the focal constructs were self-reported within one session, the findings support an association-based interpretation and do not establish temporal mediation or causality. © 2026

title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Perceived organizational support buffers these effects. The study contributes to workplace incivility research in collectivist and high power-distance cultures and offers practical implications for hotel management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Incompetence or deception: Unraveling the asymmetric mechanisms of AI hallucinations on trust and distrust
abstract: Reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) for knowledge work is increasing, yet confidently presented hallucinations can elicit strong negative user reactions. Existing literature frames hallucinations as technical failures that reduce trust, conflating the decline of trust with the emergence of distrust. However, trust and distrust are theoretically distinct constructs rather than opposite ends of a single continuum. Drawing on information manipulation theory (IMT), this study reconceptualizes AI hallucinations as violations of conversational norms. It proposes a model linking hallucination cues to perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially related to trust and distrust. It further examines whether perceived AI autonomy moderates the relationship between hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The model was tested using a sequential mixed-methods design that combined qualitative semi-structured interviews with a two-wave survey of 506 GenAI users. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA). The findings revealed that hallucination cues were differentially associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, with the former more strongly associated with trust and the latter with distrust. Perceived AI autonomy moderated the associations between some hallucination cues and perceived source deception. The PLS-SEM–NCA analysis provided complementary evidence on net effects and necessary conditions that neither method could offer alone. Overall, this study extends research on AI hallucinations by conceptualizing them as distinct forms of conversational norm violations and explaining how different hallucination cues are associated with perceived communicative incompetence and perceived source deception, which are differentially linked to trust and distrust. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Creating markets for under-utilised fish species: Consumer valuation of a co-created fish finger
abstract: It is common practice to discarded under-utilised fish species that are caught as bycatch because of their low market value. In this paper, we examine whether locally co-created and produced fish fingers, made from locally sourced under-utilised fish species are valued by consumers by employing a discrete choice experiment (DCE). A novel feature of this study is that we consider three versions of the fish finger, sourced from three UK ports: Plymouth, Lowestoft and Grimsby. Our DCE employs a novel set of attributes to capture the unique characteristics of product design and development of the fish finger. Results reveal that all attributes are positively valued, with the largest for fish that are sustainably caught. We also find that distance to the product locality does not materially affected consumer valuation. Location comparisons indicate limited differences overall for the three versions of the fish finger. These results indicate that sustainability information is a primary driver of demand for processed seafood using species with historically low market uptake, while local cues add value without substituting for sustainability. Our findings can help inform efforts to reduce discarding of under-utilised fish species that remains a significant issue in many fisheries. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The fantasy of digital immateriality: AI, ecologically unequal exchange, and appropriation of lived human time
abstract: The purported immateriality of AI technologies is as illusory as the general understanding of conventional technologies as simply the application of politically neutral knowledge to nature. The materiality of technologies and their foundation in global inequalities has been illuminated by studies of ecologically unequal exchange (EUE). The aim of this article is to extend the applicability of EUE theory to digital technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) by highlighting how even the data that they process have an inevitably biophysical history. AI technologies represent a novelty mainly in the sense that, in addition to exploiting extractive areas through EUE, they are based on the appropriation of data from the public. We argue for understanding the materiality of data as derived from lived human time. AI's dependence on data can thus be regarded as representing and embodying biophysical processes and asymmetric transfers implicating issues of justice. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier B.V. title: Exemption or backfire? The double-edged effect of AI attribution strategy on brand trust in digital content moral crises
abstract: Human-AI collaboration has become central to brand content production, but AI's black-box nature obscures responsibility in digital content moral crises. When such content is perceived as violating widely shared social values, brands increasingly attribute such incidents to AI errors. Prior research has mainly emphasized the responsibility-exemption role of AI attribution strategy, offering limited insight into its moral risks, mixed consequences, and underlying mechanisms. Drawing on the fact-value model, this study conducts five scenario-based experiments to examine how AI attribution strategy affects brand trust in this crisis context. The findings reveal a double-edged effect. At the factual level, this strategy increases consumers' perceived responsibility reduction, thereby producing an exemption effect that supports trust repair. At the value level, it also triggers perceived moral indifference, thereby producing a backfire effect that damages trust. This double-edged effect is moderated by public opinion and consumer traits. High negative electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) dispersion strengthens the perceived responsibility reduction path, whereas low negative eWOM dispersion strengthens the perceived moral indifference path. AI literacy strengthens the exemption effect by helping consumers understand AI-related technical limitations, whereas hostile attribution bias strengthens the backfire effect by leading consumers to question the moral motives behind the brand's technical explanation. This study advances crisis attribution research by examining AI attribution as a proactive brand communication strategy under attribution ambiguity and shows how it can reduce factual blame while raising value-based moral concerns. The findings offer guidance for using AI attribution carefully and reducing ethical communication risks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd
