title: The organic halo effect: A systematic review of the influence of organic labels and claims on healthiness perceptions
abstract: Food labels and claims play an increasing role in shaping consumer perceptions in complex food environments. While claims about nutrients are known to influence judgements of food healthiness, less is known about whether organic cues can lead to similar halo effects. We performed a systematic review to examine how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. We searched Web of Science and PubMed for experimental studies examining the effect of organic cues on food healthiness perceptions. Studies were included if they compared products with and without organic cues and reported outcomes related to perceived healthiness or perceived nutritional content. Of the records screened, 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. We conducted a narrative synthesis following SWiM guidelines, examining differences by cue type and outcome. Most studies found that organic cues increased perceived food healthiness. This effect was observed across both general health evaluations and specific calorie or nutrient judgements. Effects were more consistent for certified organic labels, whereas unofficial claims showed somewhat greater variability across products. A smaller number of studies reported mixed or null results, often depending on consumer characteristics or informational context. This review provides a synthesis of evidence on how organic labels and claims influence perceived food healthiness. By clarifying how consumers translate this information into health- and nutrition-related judgements, it contributes to a coherent understanding of the mechanisms underlying health halo effects. These findings suggest that organic cues may simultaneously act as signals of production practices and triggers of broader inferences about healthiness. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: The impact of reverse wording on cross-cultural comparisons of food-related attitudes
abstract: Reverse-worded items (RWIs) are commonly used in multi-item scales to reduce acquiescence bias, yet their implications for cross-cultural food attitude measurement remain underexamined. This study compared positively worded items (PWIs) and RWIs across four established food-related attitude scales using data from 6300 adult consumers across ten countries. RWIs generally showed lower internal consistency and weaker inter-item correlations than PWIs. Items showing the largest cross-country variation in standardized loadings from multi-group confirmatory factor analysis were predominantly reverse-worded. RWIs also produced lower mean scores and generally greater response dispersion than PWIs. These wording-related differences varied by construct and country, followed no uniform pattern across measurement indicators, and may reflect the combined influence of item content, linguistic structure, and culturally patterned response tendencies. Across these indicators, PWI and RWI subsets did not consistently function as psychometrically equivalent components of the same scale. The findings suggest that the use of RWIs in cross-cultural food attitude measurement may introduce wording-related measurement instability, and that wording-direction effects require explicit consideration in the design and evaluation of international consumer research instruments. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Text-driven causal mapping of PET/rPET circularity in Australia: A dynamic factor–network analysis
abstract: PET circularity is often evaluated by recovery volumes, although performance ultimately depends on whether recovered material can be converted into quality-assured outputs and absorbed by viable end markets. Yet the mechanisms connecting policy, markets, technology, and stakeholder behavior remain dispersed across heterogeneous evidence. We developed a source-attributed, time-stamped causal-network approach using 750 Australian government, industry and NGO, corporate, and media documents published during 2010–2025. Causal extraction, semantic normalization, sentiment assignment, and graph construction yielded 2794 factor nodes and 1588 unique causal edges. The network was strongly externalized: policy, market, and social factors were more numerous and highly connected than internal technical and operational factors. Persistent barriers combined cost and price volatility, inconsistent recyclate quality, infrastructure gaps, and weak policy implementation. Positive mechanisms clustered around standards and measurement, design for recyclability, operational capacity, and end-market development; their circular value depended on retained material quality and the end use reached. Source attribution revealed systematic framing differences, with media coverage concentrating negative implementation narratives. Temporal and regional analyses indicated a shift from limited attention to rapid expansion and subsequent consolidation, alongside national structural hubs and differentiated state pathways. A full-text academic shadow corpus preserved the broad problem domains but changed their hierarchy: academic evidence foregrounded material and processing mechanisms, whereas the primary corpus foregrounded institutional coordination and market implementation. The contribution is therefore not a universal ranking of Australian interventions, but an auditable framework for identifying how technical feasibility becomes, or fails to become, operational circularity under different institutional conditions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Developing a cyber-resilience framework for UAVs: insights from expert interviews on addressing cybersecurity challenges
abstract: Rapid technological advances have greatly enhanced the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their potential for beneficial uses. Such uses, however, have been limited by cybersecurity concerns. Despite considerable research attention, threat levels are increasing, and this is likely to further inhibit UAV use. A different approach is therefore required, one that marks a change from reactive mitigation to proactive prevention. This study proposes a holistic cyber-resilience framework for UAVs based on five resilience features, which are redundancy, flexibility, modularity, diversity, and tightness of feedback loops. Such a change, called for by several authors but yet to be achieved, can come through the components of a framework that are supported by expert perspectives. The study employs a mixed-methods design with in-person interviews of 32 expert professionals across eight sectors (aviation, military, security, insurance, aerospace, cybersecurity, logistics, and academia). A total of 261 vulnerabilities ranging across five threat categories are identified, with those related to communication facilitating a point of entry for cascading attacks. Drawing on expert evaluations of five resilience features, the novelty of this study is its proposed lifecycle-based framework that shifts UAV security from mitigation to embedded resilience. Practical trade-offs that include weight, power and relative costs as well as the position of the framework in relation to existing standards such as NIST CSF and MITRE frameworks are discussed. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Explainable spatiotemporal modeling in crime analytics: Robbery prediction via graph neural networks
abstract: Urban crime prediction is a critical task for ensuring public safety, yet it faces challenges related to model accuracy and transparency. While crime is an inherently temporal phenomenon, its embedding within the city’s structure suggests that integrating spatiotemporal dependencies via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can improve model robustness, particularly in data-sparse environments. Traditional grid-based methods often fail to capture the complex network topology of cities, while the “black-box” nature of advanced models raises ethical concerns for predictive policing. This study proposes an explainable spatiotemporal framework to predict robbery risk by uniquely integrating three elements: (1) fine-grained, citizen-sensed data from a public safety application in Santiago, Chile; (2) a tailored graph neural network to learn how to represent the urban environment as a graph; and (3) an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) component using Integrated Gradients to ensure transparency. We evaluate the model’s performance against traditional classifiers across various prediction horizons (1, 3, and 7 days) and spatial granularities. The results show that the tailored architecture dramatically improves predictive accuracy (average area under the receiver operating characteristic curve -AUC- ≈ 0.85) compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, the XAI analysis provides novel empirical evidence that citizen reports of “suspicious activity” are highly significant predictors of future burglaries, often more so than prior robbery incidents themselves. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Quantifying Regulatory Bottlenecks in South Korea’s Clinical Trial Approval Process Through an Analytic Hierarchy Process Framework
abstract: Purpose: Drug lag is a critical issue limiting South Korea’s pharmaceutical competitiveness and patient access, and it has been linked to delays in the Investigational New Drug (IND) review process. This study aimed to identify key barriers affecting IND review efficiency in South Korea by analyzing real-world industry experience and to propose concrete strategic actions to mitigate drug lag. Methods: We employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. First, we used grounded theory to identify problematic factors within the IND process through semi-structured interviews. We then applied the Analytic Hierarchy Process to evaluate these factors, followed by a quadrant analysis of importance and urgency to identify top-priority tasks. Results: Three core categories (rationality and patient-centricity, professional review, and operational efficiency), were identified as key domains for enhancing IND efficiency. Rationality and patient-centricity emerged as the most important and urgent criterion, followed closely by professional review. Within rationality and patient-centricity, four sub-criteria placed in the first quadrant (highly important and highly urgent): integration of patient needs into evaluation, global regulatory harmonization, acceptance of scientific evidence for new modalities, and adoption of overseas regulatory standards. Two sub-criteria within professional review (expert team review and standardized review guidelines) were also pinpointed in the first quadrant. Although operational efficiency ranked lowest, simplified Korean translation requirements stood out as the most critical factor within this category. Conclusion: Transitioning from focusing on procedural speed toward embracing regulatory flexibility to enhance scientific rationality and patient access is a viable pathway for mitigating drug lag in South Korea. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Empirical Stage-Damage Functions for SME Content Losses in Australian Flood Vulnerability Assessment
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) dominate Australian business activity, yet empirically calibrated functions for nonresidential flood-related contents losses remain limited. Postevent surveys of 185 SMEs across 12 business types and 14 towns affected by the February-April 2022 Northern Rivers floods were used to derive stage-damage functions for stock, equipment, and fit-out. Contents-specific damage indices combined peak internal flood depth (0-6 m, relative to finished-floor level) with self-reported losses and preevent replacement values. Pooled curves were fitted using LOESS and a beta-family generalized additive model (Beta-GAM); a hierarchical Beta-GAM (HBGAM) generated business-type functions under partial pooling, while random forest and XGBoost provided depth-only predictive benchmarks. Across the pooled models, performance on the corresponding within-event 25% holdout sets was moderate (R2=0.57-0.69; RMSE=0.23-0.27), and neither machine-learning benchmark consistently improved performance. The Beta-GAM was retained because it provided smooth, bounded, interpretable relationships, model-based and bootstrap uncertainty intervals, and extractable threshold depths. title: Towards a datafication framework for higher education institutions student success: A systematic review
abstract: Customer success is key to customer retention. Seemingly, this is equally true in the higher education space, as students are customers of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and, therefore, the primary reason for HEIs' existence. In view of this, it is important to understand and improve student success, which is dependent on different data indicators. Being guided by student success data indicators in HEI administration is necessary as it’s beneficial to both HEIs and their students, as through it, students can complete their qualification on time, and HEIs generate revenue. In the South African context, with its high unemployment rate and high dropout rates, understanding HEI student success is vital. However, HEIs are accustomed to collecting data rather than utilizing it for transformational activities, there has been an increase in research/publications on student success datafication frameworks in higher education in South Africa. However, these studies in isolation do not give the complete picture. This paper aims to systematically review the South African-based HEI student success data-related frameworks, including their underlying principles, trends, challenges, gaps, and future opportunities for improvement. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses method was used. Based on a clearly outlined search strategy, 508 publication abstracts were considered for review. Of these abstracts, 40 were selected for further review based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, and thereafter, 16 publications were included in the final review. The systematic review findings indicated that mostly data point indicators exist as compared to datafication frameworks. Furthermore, limited studies have been conducted on private higher education institutions in South Africa. Additionally, public sector studies have focused on first-year students; therefore, no segmentation. The implication of this study is that it sets the tone for future work within datafication, student success, and higher education, potentially enabling HEIs to approach transformational data. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Cultural value configurations and guests’ evaluations of AI-enabled service technologies
abstract: As Artificial Intelligence reshapes hospitality service delivery, understanding how culturally diverse guests evaluate AI-enabled encounters is critical. This study examines how cultural value configurations shape evaluations of service robots in hotels. Cultural value configurations are coherent combinations of orientations that jointly influence how individuals interpret and assess service encounters. Using more than 3000 robot-related hotel reviews from guests across 77 countries, we integrate Hofstede's dimensions with Schwartz's value theory to explain cross-cultural differences in sentiment. Masculinity and uncertainty avoidance predict more negative sentiment, individualism shows a positive association that is sensitive to model specification, and power distance shows no direct effect. One configuration is robust: masculinity combined with uncertainty avoidance amplifies dissatisfaction, and this interaction holds under multilevel and combined estimation and survives correction for multiple testing. Two further configurations remain suggestive: power distance combined with uncertainty avoidance attenuates risk aversion, and individualism combined with masculinity increases tolerance for imperfection. Both are marginal and do not persist under multilevel or joint estimation, so we report them as patterns for replication rather than as established effects. Hofstede's indices provide the measurement, while Schwartz's value theory serves as an interpretive lens rather than as a measured individual-level construct. Findings position culture as a configurational system and provide guidance for AI service design and communication. © 2026 The Authors

title: Understanding grey sheep users in recommender systems: A systematic and critical review of detection, modeling, and evaluation
abstract: Grey sheep users (GSUs), characterized by weak or unstable alignment with the broader user population, remain a challenge in collaborative filtering-based recommender systems. Despite extensive efforts devoted to their detection and treatment, a clear and consistent understanding of GSUs is still lacking. Existing studies typically adopt model-dependent definitions and often assume that GSUs necessarily reduce recommendation quality. This paper presents a systematic and critical review of GSUs, covering their definition, detection strategies, modeling paradigms, and evaluation practices. We revisit the classical similarity-based interpretation and show that the effect of GSUs depends on model design rather than being inherently harmful. Based on this observation, we introduce a refined conceptual perspective that describes GSUs as users with consistently misaligned preference patterns, and further propose a dynamic view that distinguishes between short-term irregular behavior and stable preference differences. We then provide a comprehensive taxonomy of existing approaches, including detection-dependent methods and detection-free strategies, and analyze their underlying assumptions and limitations. We further show that the form in which a detection result is expressed constrains which handling strategies are available, and that this correspondence is rarely exploited in practice. A key finding of this study is that current research is limited by weak evaluation practices. In particular, the absence of ground truth, inconsistent definitions, and dependence on aggregate performance metrics lead to circular reasoning and unreliable conclusions. Finally, we outline future research directions toward more robust modeling frameworks and user-centered evaluation protocols, with the aim of establishing a clearer conceptual foundation and guiding the development of more reliable and inclusive recommender systems. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Understanding event tourism competitiveness: From stakeholder-constructed attributes to visitor valuation
abstract: This study examines event tourism competitiveness by integrating stakeholder-constructed competitiveness attributes with visitor valuation. Using Hong Kong as the primary empirical context and London as a validation context, the study combines thematic analysis, confirmatory composite analysis (CCA), and a discrete choice experiment (DCE). The thematic analysis identifies six competitiveness dimensions, including Resource Synergies, a novel dimension capturing cross-sector and cross-boundary integration. The DCE results show that Resource Synergies functions as a direct destination selection criterion for MICE participants, whereas its direct effect is not significant among leisure-event visitors. Professionalism and Facilities emerges as a universal competitiveness driver for both groups, while leisure-event visitors prioritise experiential distinctiveness and international content. These findings advance event tourism competitiveness research by explaining how competitiveness attributes are constructed by stakeholders and differentially valued in the event tourism context. title: How does empowering leadership shape employee service innovation behavior? The roles of employee adaptability and job crafting
abstract: Based on conservation of resources theory, this paper examines how empowering leadership (EL) predicts service innovation behavior (SIB) through employee adaptability. The present paper also investigates job crafting (JCR) as a moderator between EL and employee adaptability. The proposed moderated mediation model was tested with multiple sources of data in the hotel industry. The results based on partial least squares structural equation modeling suggest that EL boosts employee adaptability that in turn engenders heightened SIB. The positive effect of EL on adaptability is stronger among employees high on JCR. More importantly, the positive indirect impact of EL on SIB via employee adaptability is stronger among employees who craft their jobs and optimize the work environment. The originality of this study is evident in its focus on employee adaptability and JCR as critical factors that shape the relationship between EL and SIB. Furthermore, it offers significant theoretical and practical implications. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Engaging consumers with varying budgets for battery electric vehicles in the post-subsidy era
abstract: China's BEV market must now engage the early majority to sustain broader penetration in the post-subsidy era. However, existing research inadequately explores how manufacturer-led strategies and psychological factors differentially shape the adoption decisions of this emerging consumer segment, particularly across varying budget levels. To address this gap, this study develops an integrated choice and latent variable (ICLV) model to jointly examine the effects of psychological determinants and multiple manufacturer-led strategies on BEV adoption. The analysis draws on 1200 stated-preference responses from prospective BEV buyers in Beijing and Shenzhen. Findings indicate that budget level significantly drives consumer heterogeneity in psychological drivers, while the relative effectiveness of manufacturer-led strategies remains consistent across groups: bundled insurance packages yield the largest marginal effects, followed by advanced intelligent driving services and lottery-based discounts, with price discounts being the least effective. These insights support the design of targeted, cost-effective manufacturer-led strategies in a post-subsidy context, facilitating electrification and sustainability goals. © 2026

title: Spatial trajectories and land-use potential of China's utility-scale photovoltaic expansion toward 2035
abstract: China aims to reach 3600 GW of combined wind and solar capacity by 2035, requiring substantial expansion of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) deployment. Quantifying the geospatial footprint of this expansion is essential for sustainable land-use planning and ecological protection. This study develops a nationwide assessment framework that integrates multi-source remote sensing observations, Random Forest (RF) suitability modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for model interpretation, and scenario-based spatial allocation. Historical PV data from 2000 to 2025 show that China's utility-scale PV farms expanded to 13,800 km2, with growth concentrated in northwestern mega-bases and emerging decentralized installations in central-eastern regions, indicating a dual-track spatial trajectory. Scenario projections suggest that Scenario B (NDC Update-Aligned Pathway) requires an additional 21,420 km2, whereas Scenario C (Wind-Slowdown Compensation) increases land demand moderately to 24,405 km2. Scenario A (Business as Usual) could require up to 63,990 km2 and would disproportionately affect croplands and forests. However, China retains more than 206,000 km2 of high-potential land, indicating that ecological conflicts are driven mainly by spatial mismatch rather than absolute land scarcity. These findings underscore the need for integrated spatial governance, optimized ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transmission, and distributed PV deployment. By linking observed spatial trajectories, interpretable suitability modeling, and capacity-to-land translation, this study provides a transferable framework for assessing the land-use potential of utility-scale PV expansion toward 2035. © 2026

title: Too much of a good thing? The curvilinear effects of job clarity on career satisfaction and creativity among hospitality employees
abstract: This study challenges the assumption that greater job clarity always benefits service employees. Drawing on self-determination theory and the Too-Much-of-a-Good-Thing framework, we test a moderated curvilinear mediation model linking job clarity, career satisfaction, and creativity, with career calling as a boundary condition. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 164 supervisor–employee dyads in Chinese hotels, results reveal inverted U-shaped relationships between job clarity and both career satisfaction and supervisor-rated creativity. Career satisfaction mediates this curvilinear effect. Moreover, career calling amplifies the curvature—employees high in calling gain greater motivational and creative benefits as clarity increases but experience sharper losses at very high clarity levels. These findings position job clarity as a dynamic and context-dependent resource, offering theoretical and managerial insights for fostering creativity and well-being among hospitality employees. © 2026 The Authors

title: An intelligent spectrum-aware trajectory data reduction approach for maritime decision support systems
abstract: High-quality Automatic Identification System (AIS) data is the cornerstone of modern Maritime Expert Systems and Intelligent Decision Support Systems (IDSS). However, the exponential growth of AIS data challenges the real-time situational awareness and storage capabilities of these systems. Conventional compression strategies face a dichotomy: offline algorithms ensure fidelity but suffer latency, while online methods support streaming but often exhibit “geometric blindness,” neglecting kinematic variations like speed changes along linear paths. This study proposes a novel online method, Frequency-Aware Improved Open Window (FA-IOPW). FA-IOPW uses localized spectral information within an evolving Opening Window to adapt the PED–TED weighting during online compression. To support the evaluation, we developed a visualization platform for trajectory query, compression, comparison, and adaptive-weight display. The platform was tested with historical AIS records and controlled application-level replay; live satellite AIS feeds, production Vessel Traffic Service environments, and shipborne hardware were not included in the present validation. Results demonstrate that FA-IOPW achieves a Pareto-optimal trade-off between compression ratio and reconstruction accuracy. Under high-compression regimes, it significantly reduces position and speed errors compared to mainstream methods. Furthermore, we integrated an AI agent module into the platform, lowering the usage threshold for regular users. As a robust online method, FA-IOPW offers a high-fidelity solution for real-time maritime monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: The increasing sensory richness of digitally-mediated experience
abstract: Digital interfaces were once sensorially sparse. Contemporary technologies have changed this dramatically, expanding the sensory richness of digital interfaces across visual, auditory, haptic, olfactory, and even gustatory modalities, collectively narrowing the perceptual gap between digital and physical worlds. We present findings from a growing, multidisciplinary body of evidence examining how these evolving sensory affordances shape individuals' perceptions, judgments, and behaviors. We conclude by offering a selection of future research directions with particular attention to those whose implications extend beyond any single sensory channel into more fundamental questions about human experience. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: Forecast-guided multi-task scheduling for autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets under charging and maintenance constraints
abstract: Autonomous electric ride-hailing fleets require real-time coordination among passenger dispatching, proactive repositioning, charging, and maintenance. This paper proposes a forecast-guided rolling framework that combines an attention-based spatial-temporal graph convolutional network (ASTGCN) with Enhanced Kuhn-Munkres (EKM) multi-task assignment. ASTGCN predicts grid-level demand, while a virtual-node (VN) mechanism converts forecasted regional shortages into bounded point-level relocation tasks at feasible points of interest (POIs). Passenger orders, VN-based repositioning, charging, and maintenance are then coordinated in a common vehicle-task graph after infeasible vehicle-task pairs are filtered according to battery, health, time-window, charging-capacity, and maintenance-capacity constraints. A residual-based search mechanism reduces the computational burden introduced by graph expansion. Experiments using real-world ride-hailing data show that the proposed framework achieves a system matching rate of 79.76%, which is 5.52 percentage points higher than the classical Kuhn-Munkres matching baseline. It reduces average passenger waiting time to 6.68 min, corresponding to a 14.41% reduction compared with the non-predictive scheduling variant. It also improves spatial supply-demand balance, reducing the normalized demand-supply difference to 0.128, and completes each rolling scheduling decision within 1.42 s on average. The incremental ablation study further shows that virtual-node-based forecast conversion mainly improves service quality and spatial balance, while the residual-based search mechanism reduces computation time from 22.45 s to 1.42 s without observed degradation. These results indicate that the main value of the proposed framework lies in converting demand forecasts into executable multi-task assignments for real-time autonomous electric fleet operation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Exploring Technology Probe applications in software engineering practice
abstract: Background: The development of software systems relies on user feedback, which can be captured with Validation Sessions (VS); however, VS are often conducted in an ad hoc manner. Technology Probe (TP) offers a participatory design method for capturing user perception; however, its application in software engineering lacks structure. Aim: This study consolidates evidence on TP applications in software engineering and identifies practices that support the systematic use of TP. Methods: A Literature Study, inspired by Rapid Reviews, was conducted in Scopus using backward and forward snowballing, screening 530 studies and selecting 53 primary works across the trials that support the results. Thematic analysis was employed to extract motivations, outcomes, and challenges associated with the use of TP in software engineering. Results: Through thematic analysis and open coding, 11 evidence-based characteristics were identified describing the use of TP in software engineering. These characteristics formed the foundation of an evidence-based checklist developed to assess and guide the development of TP techniques. Conclusion: It was found that TP has been applied across a variety of domains, with diverse techniques being crafted. Therefore, the checklist developed in this research aims to assist future researchers in crafting their techniques and supporting their decisions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Accounting for the risk of restoration failure in ecosystem service valuation
abstract: While ecosystem recovery is widely recognized to vary, valuations of ecosystem services often assume guaranteed outcomes. We examine whether omitting information on restoration failure risk causes bias in the utility estimates of ecosystem services. Further, we examine how two personal attitudes (connectedness to nature and place attachment) influence risk perception. In comparison to previous studies, we integrate both risk (known outcomes and their probabilities of ecosystem service provision following grassland restoration) and uncertainty (unknown outcomes and probabilities) within a single framework. We find that omitting information on risk leads to overestimation of the utility derived from ecosystem services. Controlling for subjective uncertainty and risk aversion using a hybrid choice model, we find no influence of connectedness to nature on risk perception, whereas the negative effect of high restoration failure risk on utility becomes weaker when place attachment is high. Both latent attitudes decrease the utility of uncertainty, i.e., of the opt-out alternative no restoration. Given the substantial utility implications of restoration failure risk, the EU should complement Member State-level monitoring under the Nature Restoration Regulation with project-level monitoring, open data sharing, and transparent reporting of restoration outcomes to the public. © 2026 The Authors. title: Emotional Factors in Quality Negligence: A Study of Residential Real Estate Construction Professionals
abstract: Quality negligence in the construction industry, a significant originator of legal crises, is predominantly attributed to technical and procedural failures. However, the pivotal role of construction professionals' emotions as a precipitating factor remains a critically unexamined research area. This study addresses this gap by investigating the influence of specific emotions on quality negligence and its subsequent escalation into legal crises for construction firms. The research employed an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Initially, a comprehensive literature review and unstructured interviews with industry experts identified seven prominent emotions (anxiety, guilt, pride, shame, elevation, injustice, and gratitude). Subsequently, a quantitative phase involved distributing a self-administered questionnaire to 162 Indian construction professionals within the Indian residential construction sector to assess their emotional states and quality negligence levels. Data analysis using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) indicated a statistically significant positive relationship between quality negligence and five emotions. The effects, in descending order of magnitude, were elevation (β=0.406, p<0.001), shame (β=0.405, p<0.001), gratitude (β=0.321, p<0.001), pride (β=0.261, p=0.009), and anxiety (β=0.179, p=0.047). In the final phase, consultations and brainstorming sessions with industry experts were used to identify the resulting legal crises and to establish a novel emotion-quality negligence-crises framework. This framework models the pathway from emotional antecedent to quality negligence and its culmination in a legal crisis. The study provides a critical diagnostic tool for practitioners in the real estate sector to mitigate risk and offers a new theoretical model for academics analyzing this psycho-legal connection. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: A physics-cognitive proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing collaborative framework for offshore wind farms under extreme met-ocean conditions
abstract: Reliable offshore wind operation requires maintenance decisions that account for multi-source uncertainty including stochastic degradation, environmental shocks, and incomplete condition information. Extreme met-ocean conditions also restrict maintenance access, coupling uncertainty in asset health with fragmented vessel operating windows and high operation and maintenance costs. To address these uncertain issues, this study proposes a proactive opportunistic maintenance and routing strategy. A physics-based competing failure model is developed to capture both cumulative degradation and shock-induced damage. To reduce the physics-cognitive divergence, defined as the inevitable divergence of state estimations from physical wear, an air–sea collaborative fleet using unmanned aerial vehicles enables active monitoring and dynamic replanning. A marginal-benefit-driven opportunistic maintenance strategy is introduced to exploit short and variable weather windows. A continuous weather filtering module proactively schedules critical tasks before adverse conditions, integrated with a bi-level mixed-integer non-linear programming model, which is solved by a bi-stage collaborative solution algorithm to co-optimize multi-vessel routing and maintenance bundling. Simulations on a 78-turbine offshore wind farm over a 90-day period show that the proposed strategy reduces total O&M costs by 96.4%, 46.4%, 19.4% and 46.2% compared to corrective, condition-based, non-opportunistic baselines and sequential scheduling and routing strategy, respectively. The framework offers a scalable and computationally efficient solution for multi-vessel routing and opportunistic maintenance, contributing to the development of cost-effective offshore asset management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Emotion-aware retailing: Using biometrics to decode consumer experience in physical–digital environments
abstract: The physical retail space, when blended with digital touchpoints, has created a multi-sensory consumer experience that cannot be fully measured in real time using legacy survey-based approaches. The work examines the opportunities offered by biometric technologies, such as electrodermal activity (EDA), facial action coding, eye-tracking, and heart-rate variability (HRV), to decode shoppers' affective experiences in a phygital retail space. The study is based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and affective computing theory, and has a mixed-methods experimental design that involved 312 study participants, who were offered four types of retail formats: department store, grocery hypermarket, experiential flagship store, and click-and-collect hub. All participants were given biometric sensors to wear and were monitored across three consecutive stages: browsing, assessment, and purchase decision. Behavioral and transactional data were used in real time and fused with multimodal biometric responses to create emotion maps for spatial retail areas. The findings show statistically significant positive relationships among high EDA arousal, positive facial affect, and conversion rates at digital interface points. Quantitatively, an optimal engagement window was identified at moderate stimulation levels (EDA = 2.10 μS), yielding a peak conversion rate of 41.2%. In contrast, HRV suppression was associated with decision paralysis at higher stimulation levels. Demographic cohorts and segmentation analysis showed that younger consumers reacted with much more emotion to augmented reality features and individualized digital signs. Eye-tracking and facial action coding confirmed that younger shoppers (<35) sustained an 8.42-s fixation duration with high positive affect (0.74) in flagship zones, whereas older cohorts (≥35) exhibited severe sensory avoidance. The article contributes to the theoretical understanding of emotion-behavior relationships in the store setting and offers practical guidance for store designers, digital experience architects, and consumer psychologists. Embargoes on biometric retail analytics that protect privacy are also discussed. Keywords: biometric sensing, emotion-aware retailing, phygital retail, electrodermal activity, consumer experience, affective computing, eye-tracking, heart-rate variability. The updated structural framework successfully bridges the gap between environmental retail inputs and transactional behavioral choices through intermediate biometric telemetry. Phygital spaces with heavy digital footprints create pronounced shifts in physiological processing, where elevated electrodermal activity predicts transaction completion up to an threshold point, beyond which severe heart-rate variability suppression signals choice paralysis. © 2026

title: When do hedonic appeals backfire? Credibility, scepticism and the disconnect between emotional engagement and pro-environmental intention
abstract: This study examines why emotional engagement with hedonic sustainability communication does not always translate into pro-environmental behavioural intention. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and Truth-Default Theory, it investigates consumer responses to pleasure- and comfort-based hotel food-waste messages. A sequential mixed-method design combined a laboratory experiment, projective interviews, and a follow-up online experiment testing green scepticism. Findings show no robust statistically significant physiological differentiation across message types, but substantial differences in perceived credibility, sincerity and emotional meaning. Pleasure-based appeals were interpreted as enjoyable but superficial and less trustworthy; comfort-based appeals were warmer and more relational, yet both hedonic appeals produced lower behavioural intention than the control message. Green scepticism strengthened this negative effect, particularly for comfort-based appeals. The findings suggest that hedonic sustainability communication operates less through heightened physiological arousal than through interpretive credibility evaluation, particularly among sceptical consumers. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Identification of subgroup causal effects in randomized trials under nonignorable missingness of covariates and outcome variables simultaneously
abstract: Randomized experiments are widely regarded as the gold standard for causal inference. However, identifying subgroup causal effects becomes particularly challenging when pretreatment covariates and outcome are subject to simultaneous nonignorable missingness. The study investigates the identifiability of subgroup causal effects under five increasingly complex missing data mechanisms, ranging from an ignorable mechanism to nonignorable mechanisms in which missingness depends on different combinations of treatment, covariates, and outcome. Identification is established under several nonignorable mechanisms without imposing restrictive parametric assumptions. For the most challenging mechanism, identification is established under a parametric model with specific assumptions on the outcome distribution and the missingness mechanism. For estimation and inference, a fractional-imputation Expectation-Maximization algorithm is developed to maximize the observed-data likelihood. Simulation studies compare the proposed estimator with complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, and a full-data oracle estimator, demonstrating satisfactory finite-sample performance across the considered missingness mechanisms. The practical utility of the proposed method is further illustrated using data from the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Workplace responses to perpetration of family and domestic violence: a global scoping review
abstract: Introduction Family and domestic violence (FDV), which includes intimate partner and family violence, affects workplace safety through spillover impacts on workers, organisations, and occupational health systems. To date, workplace interventions addressing the issue of FDV have predominantly concentrated on providing support to victim-survivors, while there is limited research regarding employer responses to employees who perpetrate such violence. Method A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which examined existing evidence from workplace policies, practices, and organisational mechanisms addressing FDV perpetration by workers. Peer-reviewed studies and high-quality grey literature on workplace responses to perpetration of FDV were systematically searched across multiple databases and online sources, and 28 documents on workplace responses to FDV perpetration were analysed. Results Findings from the scoping review reveal four dominant insights across the literature: 1. Perpetration of FDV is a major workplace problem, yet responses are under-researched; 2. Workplaces employ wide-ranging and varied responses, from zero tolerance dismissal of perpetrators to responsibility avoidance; 3. Responses lack a solid evidence-base and regulatory frameworks to address the problem remain weak; 4. Practical strategies are provided to better manage risk, strengthen safety, and reduce violence. Conclusion Our findings underscore the need for clearer organisational guidance, evidence-based strategies, and robust regulatory frameworks to strengthen workplace responses to FDV perpetration and improve occupational safety outcomes. Practical applications Effective workplace responses to perpetration of FDV should consider work design factors, referral pathways and confidentiality protections which are guided by graduated accountability models and regulatory frameworks. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The value of lost load in electricity intensive industry – combining and comparing stated and production value approaches
abstract: The value of lost load (VoLL) is a monetary metric quantifying the cost of unsupplied energy (€/kWh) during outages, providing valuable insights for policymakers, utility providers, and industrial stakeholders. Leveraging a mixed-method approach that integrates and compares survey data with publicly available microeconomic data insights, results show how value-added based measures significantly underestimate the financial impact of power outages. Shorter outages are found to be disproportionately costly, primarily due to high fixed costs associated with initial disruptions. Businesses report that the effects of a 1-h outage could linger for months, with some unable to fully recover even 12 months after the event. These extended disruptions underscore the enduring consequences of power outages, particularly for electricity-intensive industries. In a regression type of approach, the cost of power interruptions is not significantly influenced by the type of industry. Instead, the economic impact of an outage is more closely tied to the volume of electricity consumed, duration and production hours. Highlighting sectoral aspects and methodological sensitivities, the paper offers relevant insights for setting reliability standards, designing compensation schemes, and for guiding infrastructure investment. © 2026 The Authors. title: Why and when does leisure-time physical activity enhance hospitality employees’ job satisfaction
abstract: Employee engagement in leisure-time physical activity has been associated with greater job satisfaction. However, the conditions under which and the reasons why leisure-time physical activity enhances job satisfaction need to be better understood. Drawing on the integrated perspective of proactivity and the work–home resources model, we propose that employees with lower levels of proactive personality particularly benefit from leisure-time physical activity because it helps them proactively manage their vitality, thereby increasing job satisfaction. Consistent with our expectations, the results from a sample of 197 hotel employees indicate that leisure-time physical activity positively predicted job satisfaction through proactive vitality management. Moreover, the mediating effect of proactive vitality management was more substantial among individuals with lower proactive personality. We discuss the theoretical and practical implications of these findings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: What impacts can intertemporal trading have on carbon markets across different development stages? An economy-wide analysis
abstract: Carbon markets have encountered challenges such as limited flexibility and substantial price volatility. Intertemporal trading mechanisms, as one of the important ways of green finance, have been proposed as a potential solution to improve market efficiency. However, existing studies frequently overlook whether the intricate internal mechanisms of carbon markets are suitable for introducing intertemporal trading. To comprehensively analyze the effect of intertemporal trading, this study employs a computable general equilibrium model incorporating an intertemporal dynamic mechanism and a carbon market module. This study designs scenarios focusing on total quotas, sectoral coverage, quota allocation, and intertemporal trading to simulate and compare their macroeconomic impacts. The results suggest that intertemporal trading is particularly beneficial in carbon markets that prioritize later-stage reduction, experience rapid sectoral coverage, or have a high auction rate. Under these conditions, introducing intertemporal trading can help reduce long-term carbon prices while promoting the development of cumulative GDP and household welfare. It is noted that the output of sectors covered by the carbon market undergoes an initial contraction in the early stage, followed by a gradual increase in the later stage. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: Evolution of recommender systems: Approaches, advances, paradigm shifts, and future directions
abstract: Recommender systems are essential tools across numerous digital platforms, helping users discover relevant products, content, and services. Research has traditionally focused on prediction accuracy and relevance, relying primarily on collaborative filtering and matrix factorization techniques. With the increasing complexity of user behavior and data modalities, modern systems have moved beyond simple rating prediction to address additional objectives, including fairness, transparency, privacy, long-term engagement, and trustworthiness. This article systematically reviews the evolution of recommender systems, covering key stages from early predictive models to modern human-centered and trust-aware systems. Each stage is discussed in terms of methodological advances and practical applications. Emerging paradigms, including causal reasoning for bias mitigation, reinforcement learning for long-term optimization, federated and privacy-preserving learning, explainable recommendation techniques, and blockchain-based trust mechanisms, are analyzed. These developments illustrate a broader shift from static, correlation-driven predictions toward adaptive, context-aware, and human-centered intelligence. By organizing research into coherent clusters, this review provides a unified perspective on the field, highlights the connections between past and current approaches, and identifies promising directions for next-generation recommender systems that balance accuracy, user satisfaction, ethical considerations, and long-term system effectiveness. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: GenAI-enabled human–AI collaboration: An integrative review of local augmentation, hidden work, and governable synergy
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming part of everyday knowledge work, where it can accelerate drafting, coding, summarization, ideation, customer communication, and other language-intensive tasks. Yet the organizational problem is conversion: local GenAI gains create organizational value only when they survive the full work system, including verification, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Drawing on 251 academic and practice-facing sources across information systems (IS), management, human–computer interaction, human factors, organizational theory, and responsible AI, this article synthesizes why GenAI-enabled work often produces local augmentation but less often yields governable organizational synergy. The review develops three findings. First, GenAI shifts the relevant unit of collaboration from a one-step task interaction to a recurrent production-and-revision workflow in which human framing, prompting, verification, correction, and reuse become part of the value-producing system. Second, the augmentation-to-synergy boundary is net work-system value: visible task gains and reallocation benefits must exceed work displaced across roles and time into verification, rework, coordination, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability. Third, durable synergy requires behavioral embedding and multi-outcome governance: prompts, memory, feedback traces, review routines, and escalation rules must improve local fit while keeping reliance, learning, ownership, risk, and accountability observable. The article contributes a work-system conversion account that distinguishes substitution, augmentation, and synergy as different organizational states; a trace-centered behavioral-embedding view of how recurring GenAI use becomes a persistent, history-dependent workflow state within established sociotechnical IS theory; and a governance-instrumentation account that evaluates visible gains together with hidden labor, learning, ownership, risk, reviewability, and accountability. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: A socio-technical maturity framework for design firms to enable the transition to design-out-waste in Indonesia's construction sector
abstract: The construction sector remains a major driver of resource depletion and solid waste generation, with a substantial share traceable to early design-stage decisions. Design-out-Waste (DoW) strategies, including waste-efficient documentation, modern construction methods, and prefabrication, represent a proactive approach to enhancing lifecycle resource efficiency. However, their implementation remains fragmented, particularly in developing-country contexts, partly due to the lack of a structured framework for assessing organisational maturity. This study addresses this gap by developing an empirically grounded socio-technical maturity framework for DoW implementation in building design firms. The framework integrates five socio-technical dimensions into a single operational model encompassing processes & procedures, people & culture, industry structures, technology, and goals & incentives. Using data from 116 construction professionals, Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to validate the measurement and structural relationships, while Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) provided empirical importance values for weighting the maturity dimensions and attributes. These weights were subsequently integrated with a five-level maturity scoring scheme to operationalise the assessment framework. The results reveal an interdependent socio-technical structure, with Industry Structure emerging as the most influential dimension and an important upstream driver of other organisational capabilities. The resulting framework provides an empirically weighted basis for assessing organisational readiness, identifying capability priorities, and guiding DoW implementation towards circular construction. It also provides a structured basis for informing environmental assessment, project appraisal, and policy interventions aimed at improving resource efficiency and waste prevention. © 2026

title: “Crossing the river by feeling the stones”: Sub-national agency in China's highway maintenance marketisation
abstract: Marketisation reforms in China are often described as an extension of Western New Public Management (NPM), yet their meanings and effects vary substantially across regions and remain poorly understood from the perspective of policymakers themselves. Drawing on document review and interviews with sub-national officials and practitioners involved in highway maintenance in two underdeveloped provinces, this study examines how marketisation is interpreted, justified, and enacted through a "learning by doing" process shaped by administrative legacies, political incentives, and constrained market environments. The analysis shows that NPM-related principles, such as competition and performance management, are selectively adapted rather than directly transplanted, producing hybrid arrangements that combine bureaucratic control with quasi-market practices dominated by state-owned enterprises. The study identifies four narrative frames through which policymakers explain and evaluate reforms, as well as the recurring strategy of deliberate inaction, which emerges as a pragmatic response to tensions between central expectations and local socio-economic realities. It also considers the broader implications of marketisation for highway service performance, public satisfaction, fiscal sustainability, and technical capacity, pointing to uneven outcomes and persistent governance tensions. By foregrounding sub-national agency and context-sensitive adaptation, the article contributes to understanding policy transfer, the institutional logics shaping China's state-led market reforms, and the prospects for more sustainable infrastructure governance in less developed regions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: The impact of omni-channel strategies on consumer behavior in sport product purchases
abstract: This study addresses the gap in understanding sports consumers' behavior regarding omni-channel strategies, with a focus on the moderating roles of customer experience and brand trust. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and commitment-trust theory, a quasi-experimental omnichannel retail setting was utilized with a sample of 166 sports product consumers. The results indicate that consumer outcomes differ significantly across strategies for repurchase intention, customer satisfaction, and brand loyalty (p < .001, partial η2 ranging from 0.454 to 0.521). Specifically, following the logical progression of the consumer journey, Webrooming emerged as the primary driver for repurchase intention (M = 4.94), whereas the Online-to-Offline configuration was most effective in enhancing customer satisfaction (M = 4.96) and brand loyalty (M = 4.96). Scheffé's post-hoc tests revealed several significant pairwise differences, confirming that channel advantages are outcome-specific: digital research excels in driving intent, while integrated physical touchpoints are essential for securing relational outcomes. Customer experience and brand trust both significantly moderated the effects of omni-channel strategies on all three outcomes. In both cases, differences between strategies were more pronounced among consumers with lower experience and trust.This study elucidates the differential impacts of omni-channel strategies on sports product consumers and highlights the importance of methodological rigor, specifically post-stratification weighting as a robustness check, in enhancing the generalizability of retailing research. title: One count, three processes: Rethinking administrative stability in Korea's fuel-cell and renewable licensing pipeline
abstract: Administrative amendment counts conflate recurrent filings, schedule revisions, and changes in project ownership or specification. This article develops a Frequency-Magnitude-Type framework for interpreting incomplete development records and identifying the additional information needed for monitoring. Applied to Korea's RPS-era generation-licensing pipeline, it combines action-specific filing counts, planned-deadline displacement, and filing types over common project-age windows. Rebuilding the April 2001-June 2026 ledger yields 4804 records and a dated panel of 1813 projects; principal comparisons use 1018 projects with closed three-year windows. Fuel cells and onshore wind show no statistically detectable difference in extension incidence or intensity, whereas onshore wind has 1.44 times the adjusted deadline displacement among projects with positive movement. Project-level joint analysis adds distinctions that separate technology comparisons conceal. Twenty projects record positive deadline movement without a preparation-period extension, and projects with exactly one extension exhibit different displacement distributions. Ownership-transfer tags further distinguish administrative histories within the same frequency groups. Missing deadlines are retained as missing information rather than unchanged schedules. The resulting profiles describe administrative activity, not commissioning, and direct attention to the records needed to investigate it. The historical case thus provides a recording and interpretation framework for monitoring emerging development regimes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Generative AI use and sustainable pedagogical practices as predictors of 4Cs skill development: The mediating role of digital literacy among international postgraduate students in China
abstract: This study examines how Generative AI Use (GAU) and Sustainable Pedagogical Practices (SPP) are associated with international postgraduate students’ critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, and communication (4Cs), with Digital Literacy (DL) examined as a mediator. Using survey data from 369 international Master’s and PhD students at China’s C9 League universities, this study applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) analysis. The 4Cs were modeled as a higher-order construct comprising four lower-order dimensions. The results show that both GAU and SPP are positively associated with students’ 4Cs, with SPP showing the largest standardized direct association. GAU and SPP are also positively associated with DL, which in turn is positively associated with the 4Cs. Significant indirect associations of both GAU and SPP with the higher-order 4Cs construct were observed through DL. The ANN results provide complementary predictive evidence, with SPP showing the highest normalized predictive importance, followed by GAU and DL. Together, the findings support a technology–pedagogy–capability perspective in which pedagogical design shows the largest standardized direct association with 4Cs development, while DL functions as a learner-side information-processing capability linking AI-supported and sustainability-oriented learning experiences with competence development. For practice, the findings suggest that universities may benefit from embedding generative AI within structured, sustainability-oriented learning activities that emphasize information verification, responsible use, and collaborative problem solving. These findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional, self-report design and the specific context of international postgraduate students at China’s C9 League universities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: From expectations to experience: How tasting plant-based fermented foods shapes consumption intentions
abstract: Increasing consumption of plant-based fermented foods (PBFF) is beneficial for both public health and environment, yet intake among Western meat-eaters remains low. This study examined how sensory exposure to PBFF (sourdough bread, plant-based fermented dairy and meat alternatives), the timing of sensory exposure, and expected and actual liking influence intentions to increase PBFF consumption, and whether food neophobia moderates these effects. Data were collected over three weeks via an online pre-survey (n = 143), a laboratory experiment (n = 143), and an online post survey (n = 127). In the laboratory, participants were randomly assigned to either report their consumption intentions before tasting PBFF (n = 70) or after tasting PBFF (n = 73). Results showed that tasting PBFF attenuated the negative association between food neophobia and intention to increase consumption of PBFF. Patterns in the data suggested that intentions shifted at the first measurement following sensory exposure: participants who tasted before reporting intentions, changed intentions in the laboratory, whereas for those who reported intentions prior to tasting, changed intentions at follow-up. Product-specific patterns were observed: tasting increased intentions for the well-liked sourdough bread, but decreased intentions for the lesser-liked plant-based fermented meat. Sensory liking of the specific PBFF product was the strongest predictor of intentions for sourdough bread and plant-based fermented dairy, beyond expectations, whereas effects for plant-based fermented meat were weaker and less consistent. These findings highlight the importance of positive sensory experiences in shaping intentions to increase consumption of plant-based fermented foods, particularly among more food-neophobic meat-eaters. © 2026 The Authors

title: Shared but feared: A vulnerability-sensitive account of consumer responses to post-crisis service environments
abstract: Shared service environments are typically designed to facilitate comfort, efficiency, and positive consumer experiences. In post-crisis contexts, however, these environments may also be appraised through concerns about exposure, controllability, and personal vulnerability. Building on a context-specific refinement of the organismic component within the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this research examines how residual infection-related fear is associated with consumer responses to shared service environments in a post-pandemic context. A two-study design was implemented within a single French-language survey (N = 425). Study 1 tested whether residual infection-related fear was associated with avoidance of public service environments through differentiated forms of health anxiety. Structural equation modeling showed that residual infection-related fear was positively associated with both personal and interpersonal health anxiety, but only personal health anxiety was associated with avoidance, yielding a significant indirect effect through the self-focused pathway. Study 2 experimentally manipulated store density (high vs. low) and sanitary signals (present vs. absent) to examine how servicescape cues influenced perceived crowding and shopping satisfaction. Results showed that higher density reduced satisfaction, but this negative effect was attenuated when sanitary signals were present. Perceived crowding did not mediate the density–satisfaction relationship. A separate exploratory analysis indicated that the overall association between sanitary signals and satisfaction was more positive among individuals reporting higher residual infection-related fear. Taken together, the findings suggest that post-crisis responses to shared service environments may reflect the interplay between situational cues and heterogeneous vulnerability orientations, consistent with a vulnerability-sensitive appraisal system. The research offers a context-specific contribution to servicescape theory by suggesting that, under residual health-threat salience, organismic processes may require a more differentiated specification in contexts marked by residual threat, and by highlighting how visible safety-related cues may improve evaluations of dense service environments. Exploratory evidence further suggests that the overall association between such cues and satisfaction is more positive among consumers who remain more sensitive to infection-related risk. © 2026 The Authors

title: When perception meets reality: explaining measured food waste through consumer behavior in a university dining hall
abstract: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigates the determinants of consumer FW by integrating individual plate-waste measurements with behavioral and dining-related factors in a university dining hall setting. Data were collected from 422 diners using a 31-item questionnaire, along with individual measurements of avoidable plate waste after meals. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Kruskal–Wallis tests were applied to examine behavioral relationships and differences across demographic and meal-related groups. Average plate waste reached 51.5 g per person, with higher waste levels observed during lunch and among female diners. Self-perceived waste behavior, intention to reduce FW, and sensory satisfaction were directly associated with the measured amount of discarded food. In contrast, consumer knowledge, portion size perception, and available eating time influenced only perceived waste behavior, revealing a disconnect between awareness and objectively measured PW. The findings highlight the importance of dining context and meal satisfaction in shaping consumer FW and demonstrate the value of integrating subjective perceptions with objective waste measurements. By combining behavioral evidence with direct waste quantification, this study advances methodological approaches to consumer FW research and provides insights for designing more effective waste reduction strategies in institutional food services. © 2026 The Authors

title: The impact of consumer culture positioning on multinational brand premium: The moderating role of global identity
abstract: Multinational brands often charge higher prices in emerging markets than in their home markets. Although such multinational brand premiums can improve profitability, they may also invite consumers to compare prices across countries and evaluate the premium as unfair. This research examines how consumer culture positioning (CCP) shapes consumers' willingness to pay a multinational brand premium through price fairness perceptions, operationalized as perceived price unfairness, and how this process depends on consumers' global identity. Across a pretest and three experiments in China, we compare Global Consumer Culture Positioning (GCCP) with Local Consumer Culture Positioning (LCCP) in a multinational restaurant-brand context. Experiment 1 establishes the main effect of CCP and the mediating role of perceived price unfairness. Experiment 2 replicates this pathway and examines chronic global identity as a boundary condition. Experiment 3 further tests the moderation through situationally activated global versus local identity. The results generally show that GCCP, relative to LCCP, reduces perceived price unfairness and increases willingness to pay a premium. The fairness-based indirect effect becomes stronger as chronic global identity increases and when global identity is situationally activated. The findings integrate global branding and pricing research by showing when cultural positioning can make a higher price appear more acceptable rather than merely enhance brand image. The study also provides managerial implications for multinational and local brands operating in emerging retail and service markets. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Geopolitical risk and tourism firm resilience: Global evidence
abstract: This paper analyzes how geopolitical risk affects the performance of tourism firms and identifies the conditions under which its adverse effects are mitigated. Using a global panel of 1438 firms across 39 countries from 2007 to 2021, we find that heightened geopolitical risk significantly reduces firms’ market valuations. Drawing on risk perception theory, network theory, and institutional theory, we show that this effect is conditional rather than uniform. Specifically, firms located in countries with stronger international tourism network embeddedness experience weaker negative effects, as network connectivity facilitates demand diversification and adaptive responses. Similarly, higher institutional quality reduces the adverse impact of geopolitical risk by enhancing stability and policy credibility. These findings are robust to alternative measures and estimation methods. The paper provides new evidence on the transmission of geopolitical risk and highlights the role of structural and institutional factors in shaping resilience in the global tourism sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Predicting the future of retail services: Trends, technologies, and strategic imperatives for 2025–2035
abstract: The rapid convergence of digital platforms and shifting consumer behaviors is driving an unprecedented structural transformation across the global retail landscape. This paper examines the systemic evolution of retail channel revenue distributions and operational capabilities, establishing the critical strategic imperatives required to navigate market disruption over the 2025–2035 horizons. The primary objective of this study is to empirically model the longitudinal shifts between traditional physical retail, e-commerce, and physical channels, while concurrently diagnosing the capability gaps across diverse corporate scales. Methodologically, this research deploys a mixed-methods empirical framework, integrating a quantitative survey of 418 retail industry professionals with qualitative interviews from 32 senior executives across six countries, analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA. The empirical findings reveal a definitive market polarization: traditional physical retail is projected to contract significantly from 54.3% to 30.8%, while e-commerce expands to claim a dominant 52.7% revenue share by 2035. Our multi-method analysis validates that digital-physical integration and AI-driven personalization (β = 0.38, p < .001) directly resolve post-pandemic operational vulnerabilities, emerging as the primary drivers of future performance outcomes. Longitudinal analysis confirms a steady decline in traditional commodity metrics, while scenario simulations warn that small and medium-sized enterprises face a severe (66.5%) market share loss under unmitigated polarization. To address this structural market polarization, this study provides a rigorous, data-driven defense by establishing the Retail Evolution Framework (REF) to explain how systemic retail survival requires aligning operational tools with shifting institutional norms. The study bridges the dynamic capabilities gap under the Resource-Based View while offering actionable strategies for ethical data governance. Practically, these insights provide an actionable investment roadmap for corporate managers to redirect capital allocations from physical footprint expansion into automated data ecosystems and cloud-based logistics architectures to maintain long-term competitive viability. © 2026

title: Survival of Contractor Consortiums in the Road Construction Industry during Economic Crisis
abstract: Road construction industries worldwide are periodically exposed to economic crises, which are cyclical in nature and often characterized by high inflation, currency depreciation, resource shortages, and institutional inefficiencies. In such conditions, traditional procurement methods frequently struggle to maintain project continuity, prompting the emergence of local contractor consortiums as a more resilient alternative. This study examines how contractor consortiums in the road construction sector adapted to recent economic crises and sustained operations amid unprecedented challenges. A qualitative research approach was adopted, involving 14 semistructured interviews with industry experts. Manual content analysis identified key adaptive measures, including financial pooling, shared equipment and labor, agile internal coordination, and proactive engagement with public authorities. These mechanisms enabled many consortiums to continue project delivery despite severe economic and operational constraints. However, the effectiveness of these measures was constrained by rigid legal and contractual frameworks, limited digital integration, fragmented stakeholder collaboration, and delayed institutional responses. To enhance future resilience, the study recommends modernizing contractual systems, strengthening digital adoption, and improving public-private coordination. The findings contribute to construction management research in crisis contexts by demonstrating the viability of consortium-based procurement and providing practical guidance to support the long-term sustainability of local contractor consortiums in the road construction sector. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Institutional resilience and land-acquisition governance: Participation and conflict-management mechanisms in the Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway project
abstract: This study examines governance performance during infrastructure land acquisition and the role of institutional resilience in supporting implementation. Using survey data from 108 public-sector implementers involved in the Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway project in Indonesia, the relationships among institutional resilience capacities, participatory governance, conflict-management mechanisms, and governance performance were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Learning capacity and adaptive capacity were positively related to participatory governance, while buffering capacity was positively related to conflict-management mechanisms. Participatory governance showed no direct relationship with governance performance but its indirect relationship through conflict-management mechanisms was statistically significant. Buffering capacity and adaptive capacity were positively related to governance performance, while learning capacity showed no significant relationship. The findings reveal differentiated governance roles across resilience capacities and distinguish direct capacity–performance relationships from process-based relationships involving stakeholder participation and conflict-management mechanisms. In conflict-prone land acquisition, conflict-management mechanisms emerged as an important governance process linking stakeholder participation with governance performance. The study shows how different resilience capacities support different governance functions during land-acquisition implementation. © 2026

title: Context matters in just culture: Translating formal just culture into lived near-miss reporting experience in maritime transportation
abstract: In onboard environments characterised by high operational risk, near-miss reporting is an important mechanism for identifying latent risks, preventing accidents and supporting organisational improvement. However, there remains limited empirical understanding of whether the just culture advocated in formal systems can be translated into the lived reporting experience of seafarers who are willing, able and motivated to report near-miss incidents on a sustained basis. To address this issue, this study draws on semi-structured interviews with seafarers and shore-based managers. Six interrelated themes are identified: ease of reporting, motivation to report, trust, reporting independence, feedback and acknowledgement. The findings indicate that near-miss reporting is more likely to occur in organisational contexts where reporting is accessible, safe and worthwhile. Complicated procedures, paperwork burdens and hierarchical pressure weaken seafarers’ willingness to report, whereas simplified procedures, fair management, low exposure communication channels, timely feedback and positive acknowledgement help strengthen reporting willingness and promote experience sharing. This study provides context-specific empirical evidence on how formal just culture is translated into frontline reporting practice and offers practical insights that may inform efforts to improve near-miss reporting, reduce reporting concerns and strengthen closed-loop feedback in comparable organisational or cultural settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
