title: Anger regulation scale for adolescents (ARS-A): Psychometric properties of the Portuguese version and its associations with emotion regulation, depression, and anxiety
abstract: Adolescence is marked by difficulties in anger regulation, which are linked to internalising and externalising problems. Despite this, the instruments currently available to measure anger regulation in adolescents have a limited evidence base and require further investigation. The present study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Anger Regulation Scale for Adolescents (ARS-A) in the Portuguese context. A sample of 432 adolescents aged 11 to 18 (M = 13.73, SD = 1.61) from different regions of Portugal participated in this study. The factor structure and model fit were assessed through Principal Component Analysis and Confirmatory Factor Analysis, using the Solomon method for equivalent sample splitting. All subscales demonstrated acceptable internal consistency and fit indices, confirming the original three-dimensional structure after two items were removed. Pearson correlations with other measures of behavioural and cognitive emotion regulation were consistent with theoretical expectations, although not all associations were as expected. Correlations between anger regulation, depression and anxiety corroborated the relationship between dysfunctional anger regulation and emotional distress. The ARS-A is a reliable and valid measure of anger regulation for adolescents. © 2026 The Authors.

title: When health labels increase indulgent food purchase intention
abstract: Health labels are widely used in front-of-package communication and are generally expected to facilitate healthier decisions. We examine whether such labels can also increase consumers' indulgent food purchase intention. Across six studies, health labels attached to indulgent products were associated with greater attentional or motivational salience (Study 1a), higher digital-ad click-through rates (CTRs) (Study 1b), a higher likelihood of selecting an indulgent product in an incentive-compatible raffle (Study 1c), and stronger purchase intentions (Studies 1d–3). Study 2 provides statistical support for a serial indirect effect involving justification for purchase and perceived guilt, whereas perceived healthfulness did not mediate purchase intention in the models tested. Study 3 identifies brand equity as a boundary condition of the claim effect on purchase intention. The observed pattern raises concerns that health labels on indulgent foods may unintentionally lower consumers' psychological restraint, potentially increasing overall favorable responses to indulgent foods in real-world settings. Practically, the results suggest that health labels should be evaluated in relation to products' overall nutritional profiles and brand contexts. © 2026

title: UK bioenergy policies and implications for global land use change
abstract: Bioenergy is central to UK decarbonisation policy, yet its reliance on imported biomass and crop-based biofuels raises concerns about land use change (LUC) and indirect land use change (ILUC) in supplier countries. This study provides a data-driven, ex-post assessment of land use implications associated with two UK bioenergy policy pathways: forestry-derived biomass supported by the Contract for Difference (CfD), and 1st generation biofuels supplied under the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation (RTFO). Import data for 2015–2022 were linked to forestry biomass productivity and country-specific crop yields to estimate direct land use footprints in major supplier countries. Wider ILUC-consistent signals were then assessed using observed land use, production and trade trends from 2000 to 2022, with particular focus on the US and Brazil. Results show that UK-bound forestry-derived biomass was mainly associated with land footprints in the US, Canada, Latvia and Estonia, while UK-bound 1st generation biofuel land demand became increasingly concentrated in the US and Brazil by 2022. Sensitivity analysis showed that lower productivity assumptions increased estimated land requirements, but did not alter the main supplier-country patterns. Overall, UK bioenergy imports represented a small share of total land use in major supplier countries. The study found no persistent national-scale ILUC signal detected in the US or Brazil. The findings suggest that ex-post land use monitoring can complement model-based ILUC assessment and improve the evidence base for bioenergy sustainability policy. © 2026 The Authors. title: DCET: Multi-scale decomposition and channel clustering enhanced multivariate time series forecasting
abstract: Existing multivariate time series forecasting methods address multi-scale structures and channel heterogeneity by either enhancing model expressiveness with deeper and wider network architectures or by preprocessing sequences to attenuate certain frequency components. However, these approaches often lead to increased training costs, instability from over-reliance on model capacity, difficulty in handling multiple scales, and failure to consider differing structural relationships between channels. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel framework called DCET (Decomposition and channel Clustering Enhanced multivariate Time series Forecasting), which integrates a cascading two-stage decomposition process, channel clustering, and a ChebyKAN residual head within a single unified model. The main contribution of DCET lies in its ability to directly address multi-scale and channel heterogeneity in a more efficient manner by simplifying the model structure while preserving its expressiveness. Specifically, DCET introduces an unsupervised learning-based module for parameter sharing among similar variates, and applies the two-stage decomposition to capture multi-scale features. Nonlinear models are used to represent complex fluctuations, while linear models capture long-term trends. Moreover, a multi-objective training approach minimizes both the overall prediction error and the errors of decomposed components. We validate DCET through experiments on eight public datasets, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy, robustness, and flexibility in handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous time series with manageable model complexity. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: A fairness-aware TabTransformer framework for credit scoring with high-cardinality regional bias
abstract: This study examines whether fairness constraints must come at the expense of performance in credit risk models. We introduce a deep learning framework rooted in the TabTransformer architecture, integrating a Normalized Covariance Penalty into the loss function to mitigate regional bias over a high-cardinality sensitive attribute, the 27 Brazilian states. A real-world mortgage dataset of 1,529,211 contracts, under a strict unawareness-at-inference protocol and calibrated using Platt scaling, is benchmarked against industry standards and against fairness-aware alternatives from the pre-, in-, and post-processing families. The fairness-constrained model achieved an AUC of 0.751, above its unconstrained counterpart (0.745; DeLong p < .001) and Random Forest (0.735), while reducing the maximum True Positive Rate (TPR) gap across states to 0.445, against 0.499 for XGBoost, and reaching the lowest Demographic Parity difference among all evaluated models. XGBoost retains a statistically significant advantage in raw discrimination (ΔAUC (Formula presented)); among models that keep inference blind to the regional attribute, however, the proposed framework offers the most favorable fairness–performance profile and dominates the equity-constrained region of the empirical Pareto frontier. A decomposition across the 27 states shows that the penalty compresses the regional TPR distribution in both directions, raising the mean TPR of the three worst-served states, and a leakage audit confirms a measurable reduction in the regional information carried by the scores. Sensitivity analyses over the penalty weight and training seeds, module ablations, and replications on public credit datasets support the robustness of these findings. © 2026 The Authors. title: Urban economic resilience and low-altitude logistics industrial agglomeration: Implications for reliable deployment
abstract: Low-altitude logistics (LAL) is a complex urban cyber-physical freight system comprising uncrewed aerial vehicles, eVTOL aircraft, airspace management, and ground infrastructure. Reliable deployment requires technical validation, regulatory compliance, and commercially sustainable operations, while urban socioeconomic conditions may provide supporting resources. This paper develops an interpretable causal learning framework to evaluate how urban economic resilience influences LAL industrial agglomeration, measured by the log-transformed stock of registered LAL-related enterprises. Utilizing panel data from 296 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2010–2024, we quantify urban economic resilience via an improved entropy-weighted TOPSIS model and integrate panel fixed-effects, double machine learning, causal forests, and SHAP attribution to estimate average effects under identifying assumptions and examine spatial heterogeneity and nonlinear predictive contributions. The results indicate that urban economic resilience significantly fosters LAL enterprise concentration, yet reveals a distinct resilience saturation pattern: mid-resilience cities exhibit the largest estimated effects on LAL industrial agglomeration, whereas marginal returns diminish in highly resilient metropolitan centers. SHAP decomposition reveals that household wealth accumulation, income levels, and fixed-asset investment are primary contributors to industrial presence. These findings identify urban economic conditions associated with LAL industrial agglomeration and offer implications for the economic foundations supporting reliable deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Optimising construction health and safety training: the role of training design and firm size
abstract: Background The construction industry is one of the most hazardous sectors globally, responsible for a disproportionate share of work-related injuries and fatalities. Construction health and safety (H&S) training is widely recognised as a critical component for improving workers’ H&S competence and reducing accident rates. Despite extensive investment in training programmes, research indicates that learning effectiveness varies across construction firms and may be associated with differences in training design and organisational context. However, empirical understanding of whether firm size moderates the relationship between specific training design dimensions and learning effectiveness is limited. Objective This study investigated the relationships between training design dimensions (training content relevance, facilitator competence, opportunity for practice, and learning environment) and learning effectiveness in construction H&S training while assessing the moderating role of firm size. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 80 construction professionals from medium- and large-scale firms. Data were collected using 5-point Likert scales to measure training design dimensions and learning effectiveness. Correlation analysis, multiple regression analysis, and moderation analysis using PROCESS were performed to test the hypothesised relationships. Results Multiple regression showed that the four training design dimensions jointly explained 64% of the variance in learning effectiveness ( R2 = 0.64, adjusted R2 = 0.62), with all four dimensions showing significant positive associations. Moderation analysis showed that firm size significantly moderated the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness (interaction B = 0.19, p = 0.033), with a stronger conditional effect among large firms ( b = 0.62) than medium-sized firms ( B = 0.43). Conclusions This study extends the training effectiveness literature by showing that the relationship between training design quality and learning effectiveness varies according to organisational context, with firm size representing a potential boundary condition. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Organisational capability for digital health transformation in long-term care: development of a conceptual framework
abstract: Background: Digital health transformation in long-term care (LTC) involves more than the adoption of digital technologies. Organisations must coordinate leadership, workforce capability, infrastructure, governance and implementation processes to sustain digital systems within continuing care environments. Existing implementation and digital maturity approaches address important aspects of digital transformation but provide less explanation of how organisational capabilities interact as a system within LTC. Objective: This study develops an evidence-informed organisational capability framework for digital health transformation in LTC and proposes relationships among capabilities potentially relevant to sustained digital system use. Methods: An evidence-informed framework development approach was used. Published evidence from digital health, healthcare management, implementation and organisational research was examined to identify recurring organisational mechanisms associated with digital transformation. Related mechanisms were grouped into capability domains, and proposed relationships among the domains were conceptualised. The resulting domains were integrated into the Long-Term Care Digital Capability and Alignment (LTC-DCA) framework. Results: LTC-DCA comprises seven interdependent organisational capability domains: strategic digital leadership, organisational readiness, workforce development systems, technology and data infrastructure alignment, governance and ethical oversight, implementation and integration mechanisms, and performance and learning systems. The framework conceptualises these domains as a connected capability system in which changes in one domain may influence others. Performance and organisational learning are proposed as feedback mechanisms that may support continued adjustment and alignment. Conclusions: LTC-DCA shifts attention from technology adoption towards the organisational capabilities potentially involved in integrating, sustaining and adapting digital systems within long-term care. The framework is evidence-informed and conceptually specified rather than empirically validated. Future research could examine its domains, proposed relationships and indicators across different LTC settings and investigate whether they are associated with sustained digital system use and organisational performance. © 2026 Fellowship of Postgraduate Medicine

title: Leaning into risk: How slanted typeface logos increase perceived risk of efficacious products
abstract: Marketing practice commonly uses slanted typeface logos on product packaging to convey movement and vitality, yet existing research has paid limited attention to the potential conflict between this low-level visual feature and the core claims of specific products. Drawing on the elaboration likelihood model (ELM), this research examines when and why slanted typeface logos on packaging increase consumers' perceived risk of efficacious products, revealing the underlying mechanism and boundary condition. Across three controlled experiments and one incentive-compatible experiment, this research manipulates the form of typeface logos on packaging and evaluates its effects and subsequent behavioral responses. Study 1 shows that, compared with an upright typeface logo, a slanted typeface logo increases consumers' perceived risk of efficacious products. Study 2 supports the mediating role of design instability: a slanted typeface logo triggers a visually perceived sense of imbalance, which further induces consumers’ risk inferences about the product; meanwhile, arousal, perceived movement, and perceptual fluency do not emerge as significant mediating mechanisms. Study 3 identifies the moderating role of cognitive load, showing that high cognitive load amplifies the effect of a slanted typeface logo on perceived risk. Study 4 further provides behavioral evidence through an incentive-compatible experiment, showing that consumers are less likely to choose the product in the slanted typeface logo condition. Overall, this research reveals a boundary of the visual marketing principle that “slanting implies vitality” in the context of efficacious products. These findings enrich theoretical understanding of the boundary conditions under which peripheral visual cues operate within the ELM framework and offer practical implications for the context-specific management of brand visual identity systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Regionalized life cycle assessment of NMC and LFP batteries across China-EU supply chain configurations under the EU Battery Regulation
abstract: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 introduces stringent life cycle carbon footprint requirements that are expected to influence the regional organization of battery production. However, the carbon footprint implications of alternative China-EU supply chain configurations remain insufficiently understood. This study develops a regionalized life cycle assessment framework to evaluate the life cycle carbon footprints of lithium nickel‑manganese‑cobalt (NMC) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries under alternative regional supply chain configurations between China and the EU. The analysis follows the latest EU methodological guidance and combines proprietary industrial data from leading Chinese electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturers. The boundary analysis showed that the calculated carbon footprints were sensitive to the life cycle stages included. Under the EU baseline, the carbon footprints of NMC and LFP batteries were 96.2 and 51.6 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 91/157/EEC-informed reference boundary, 95.9 and 81.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Directive 2006/66/EC-informed reference boundary, and 142.9 and 128.3 gCO2e/kWh under the Regulation (EU) 2023/1542-aligned full life cycle boundary, respectively. Scenario analysis further indicated that regional supply chain reconfiguration can substantially narrow carbon footprint differences relative to Baseline-EU. For NMC batteries, the difference decreased from 59.3 gCO2e/kWh under the export (EX) scenario to 49.3 and 47.7 gCO2e/kWh under the overseas battery production (TB) scenario and partial material pre-processing in the EU (TBM) scenario, respectively. For LFP batteries, the corresponding values decreased from 74.1 to 49.4 and 47.1 gCO2e/kWh. These findings suggest that the regulatory context may encourage supply chain configurations with lower life cycle carbon footprints by altering the regional allocation of production stages. The findings highlight the importance of aligning regional production characteristics with decarbonization potential and provide policy-relevant evidence for coordinated China-EU battery supply chain strategies. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

title: A Block-Wise Updating Strategy for Approximate Duplicate Detection
abstract: Approximate duplicate detection in data streams aims to determine whether an item is present within a small subsequence of the data stream. It is a fundamental query problem needed in several network applications, such as web crawling and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag management. Most of the existing algorithms are not space-efficient as they overlook the distributional information of query frequency and membership likelihood. In this paper, we propose CEll Bloom Filter (CEBF) algorithm, a space-efficient data structure designed by adopting a block-wise updating strategy, to solve this problem, and two typical distributions are considered: two typical distributions: (1) uniform query frequency of items, and (2) uniform membership likelihood of items. For an arbitrary sliding window size n and an arbitrary average false positive rate ε ∈ (0, 1), the proposed algorithm needs approximately O(nlog2(1/ε)) bits, which is significantly less than the number of bits used in existing methods. Space lower bound is also derived for these two typical distributions, which demonstrates that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal in terms of space consumption. Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, and the experimental results clearly demonstrate that the proposed method is clearly and significantly more effective and promising compared to existing other methods. © The author(s) 2027.

title: Where AI enters the product development process: Task orientation, human identity threat, and purchase intention
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly moving beyond analytical retail functions into product development, raising new questions about how consumers respond depending on where AI is positioned within the process. Across three studies with U.S. consumers in fashion-related contexts, this research examines how the task AI performs and how its role is framed shape consumer responses to products developed with AI involvement. Study 1 maps consumers’ perceptions of fashion-related tasks along a logic–intuition continuum and identifies trend forecasting as a logic-oriented task and design as an intuition-oriented task. Study 2 compares AI involvement in these two contrasting product-development tasks and finds lower purchase intention when AI is involved in design rather than trend forecasting, with heightened human identity threat accounting for part of this difference. Study 3 focuses on the intuition-oriented design context and shows that framing AI as complementing rather than replacing human designers is associated with lower identity threat and higher purchase intention. Together, the findings suggest that consumer responses depend not only on whether AI participates in product development, but also on where AI is positioned within the process and how its contribution relative to human creativity is framed. This research advances understanding of task-dependent responses to AI by identifying human identity threat as a mediator linking AI involvement to purchase intention and by showing how role framing can shape purchase intention when AI participates in creative work. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Integrating Business Impact Analysis, Scenario-Based FMEA, and Business Continuity Planning in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing: A Product-Level Case Study
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the product-level integration of Business Impact Analysis (BIA), scenario-based Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and Business Continuity Planning (BCP) for a selected finished medicinal product. Methods: A single-site case study was conducted for cefixime 400 mg film-coated tablets in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical organization. Data were collected over approximately six months through four structured questionnaires, documentary and operational-record review, facilitated interviews, and cross-functional consensus sessions. BIA established Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD), Recovery Time Objective (RTO), and Work Recovery Time (WRT). Twenty-five de-identified scenarios, were assessed using predefined 1–4 scales for severity, frequency, and detectability; RPN was calculated as S × F × D. Results: IT and Technology had the shortest recovery requirement (MTD 48 h, RTO 24 h, WRT 24 h). Twelve scenarios were low risk and 13 were medium risk; none was high or critical. Material-transport interruption and adverse commercial and market conditions had the highest RPN of 16. Thirteen scenarios required additional controls. Sensitivity analysis showed that selected medium risks could move to high risk after a one-level score increase. Conclusion: The integrated approach supported transparent recovery prioritization and translation into product-specific continuity actions. Findings are context-specific and require prospective testing and replication. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Corporate strategy for the green transition: Are executive incentives effective?
abstract: This paper examines whether green incentives embedded in executive compensation schemes are associated with a reorientation of firms' innovative activities toward environmentally sustainable technologies. Drawing on agency theory and the attention-based view of the firm, we conceptualize green incentives as governance and management-control devices that can mitigate managerial short-termism and channel executive attention toward long-horizon environmental objectives, thereby redirecting firms' technological search. Using a panel of publicly listed U.S. and European firms that participate in the Carbon Disclosure Project over the period 2010–2020, we analyse green innovation as a multi-stage process comprising the reorientation of technological search (the distance of firms' patent portfolios from green domains), knowledge recombination (the citation of green prior art in non-green patents), and realized green innovation output (green patent counts and shares). Firms adopting green incentives exhibit higher green innovation output, a significant repositioning of their knowledge portfolios toward green technological domains, and a greater integration of green knowledge into non-green technologies. These associations are weaker among firms experiencing a recent deterioration in carbon performance, and are strongest among continental European firms. Overall, the findings suggest that executive green incentives are associated with the direction, and not merely the volume, of firms' innovative activities, highlighting the role of internal governance mechanisms in sustainability transitions while recognising the limits of causal inference in observational data. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Institutional co-development cues in retail food choice: Reducing perceived risk in alternative protein acceptance
abstract: Alternative proteins are increasingly available to consumers through retail and online food channels, yet their unfamiliarity often heightens perceived risk at the point of product evaluation. This research examines whether identifying an alternative-protein product as co-developed with an official agricultural research institute (OARI) functions as a retail-facing institutional cue. Across four experiments with Chinese consumers, an OARI co-development cue generally increased acceptance of plant-based, cultured-meat, and insect-based products. Study 2 showed that the cue increased acceptance by reducing perceived risk. Study 3 showed that this risk-reduction pathway was stronger among consumers with greater food neophobia. Study 4 demonstrated that the cue reduced risk and increased acceptance when trust in the named institution was high, but not when it was low. The findings contribute to consumer retailing research by showing how institutional co-development cues can reassure consumers evaluating unfamiliar food innovations, and why such reassurance depends on both consumers' need for risk reduction and trust in the named institution. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Macroprudential policies and dollarization: implications for the financial system and a cross-exchange rate regime analysis
abstract: Macroprudential policy has gained prominence in promoting financial stability. This paper evaluates the effectiveness of macroprudential measures in curbing credit growth over a 22-year period across 129 countries. It further examines how macroprudential policy interacts with dollarization and other exchange rate regimes. Our findings indicate that tightening macroprudential measures are associated with lower credit growth within one quarter following implementation. The estimated associations are similar across the system and difference GMM specifications. Additionally, macroprudential policies are associated with significantly lower non-performing loan rates in dollarized economies compared to most other exchange rate regimes. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Evaluation of cost reduction effects by sector-coupling synergies in timber processing and bioenergy for sustainable forestry in Japan
abstract: The greenhouse gas sequestration capacity of forests is an important pillar in combating global warming; therefore establishing a forest resource circulation system is crucial. Forestry, which includes everything from cultivation to harvesting forests that store carbon dioxide as they grow, and the sawmill industry, which processes this timber, frequently face significant economic challenges. Consequently, proposals are needed to establish systems that improve these industries’ economic competitiveness while also ensuring the forest resources circulation. This study developed a model to evaluate the economic relationship between timber processing and energy consumption from a sector-coupling perspective using a prospective techno-economic analysis. It specifically defines wood utilization as a comprehensive forest resource circulation that includes production, planting, processing, energy utilization, and reforestation. It evaluates the economic interdependence between timber processing and energy utilization when all wood is harvested from forests and both uses are combined. The evaluation results show that combining energy utilization in sawmills processing over 36,000 m3 annually allows for full harvesting from forests, reducing forest residues, and lowering site preparation costs for reforestation. Additionally, using inexpensive electricity from biomass power generation for sawmilling lowers sawmill costs. It has become clear that, at sawmills of a certain size or larger, combining material utilization with energy utilization results in a slight decrease in sawmilling costs, while reducing forestry management costs; overall, this is an effective approach for wood utilization. © 2026 The Authors. title: Market-driven or state strategic-driven? A hybrid driving paradigm and evolution of mission-oriented innovation ecosystems in aerospace engineering
abstract: How national strategies and market forces jointly organize innovation for complex and uncertain space missions, such as deep space exploration, and why distinct driving logics retain their differences while incorporating governance mechanisms from one another remain important questions for research on mission-oriented innovation ecosystems. This study develops the Drive–Organization–Adaptation–Value (DOAV) analytical framework and conducts a longitudinal comparison of SpaceX's deep space exploration program and the China Manned Space Program, tracing stage-specific mission demands, local task gaps, mechanism entry, and coupling at task interfaces. The findings reveal a sequence of conditional relationships. First, mission mandates and resource conditions shape initial driving relations and produce distinct configurations of organization, adaptation, and value. Second, when stage-specific demands reach the configuration performance boundary, the leading actor can address local task gaps through internal adjustment or admit heterogeneous mechanisms when complementary capabilities and executable interfaces are available. Third, coupling at task interfaces links organization, adaptation, and value, encouraging convergence in governance mechanisms while leadership relations retain identifiable continuity at the defined long-term mission level. On this basis, the study distinguishes instrumental hybridization, asymmetric structural hybridization, and mission co-shaping according to mechanism embedding depth and the reach of governance feedback. Mission co-shaping is retained as a conditional theoretical extension within the process explanation of the DOAV dynamic adaptation mechanism. The findings inform the coordination of public objectives and firm innovation capabilities in major scientific and technological missions, including space exploration, and the design of collaborative rights, responsibilities, and verification arrangements in response to stage-specific tasks. © 2026 IAA. title: Automatic behavior tree generation for enhanced human–robot collaborative task planning in industry 5.0: A systematic review
abstract: In the context of Industry 5.0, scheduling heterogeneous resources, such as humans and robots, has become increasingly critical. Task allocation must balance human comfort, ergonomics, and trust with productivity and responsiveness to customer demands. This review explores recent advances and prospects in the automatic generation of schedules and action plans, particularly Behavior Trees (BTs), to improve human–robot collaboration. We examine the application of artificial intelligence techniques to classical production management problems, such as Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) and Assembly Line Balancing Problems (ALBP), for autonomous task scheduling and robotic behavior design. This includes highlighting innovative scheduling approaches and the advantages of Behavior Trees over traditional models such as Hierarchical Task Networks (HTN) and Finite-State Machines (FSM). Behavior Trees offer a modular and reactive programming structure essential for executing complex tasks assigned to robots. The review also discusses human operators’ perception of robotic actions and identifies best practices for implementing collaborative solutions that prioritize both efficiency and safety. © 2026 The Authors. title: What makes human service distinctly human in the AI era? Conceptualizing and measuring authentic relational service competency
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) service agents increasingly simulate human interaction, the basis for distinguishing human service has become theoretically ambiguous. While prior research consistently identifies authenticity as a key limitation of AI-enabled service, authenticity remains underdeveloped as a uniquely human service capability. Addressing this gap, we introduce Authentic Relational Service (ARS) as a distinct form of service through which frontline employees create genuine, contextually responsive, and relationship-centered customer interactions. We further conceptualize authenticity as a competency-based capability and develop a measure of Authentic Relational Service Competency (ARSC), which enables frontline employees to enact ARS. Using established scale-development procedures, this study identifies and validates four dimensions of ARSC: perspective-taking, patience, creativity, and agility. By conceptualizing and operationalizing Authentic Relational Service as a distinct human service capability, this research advances theory on human-AI service differentiation and provides a foundation for understanding uniquely human value creation in service contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Developing instrument to measure the glass ceiling phenomenon among female academics in Indonesia
abstract: The persistence of the glass ceiling phenomenon in academia indicates the necessity of developing a contextually valid and reliable measurement instrument, particularly within Indonesian higher education institutions. Instruments developed in different cultural settings are often unable to fully capture the structural and sociocultural dynamics influencing female academics' career advancement in Indonesia. This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive measurement instrument that reflects these contextual specificities and improves measurement accuracy in assessing career advancement barriers. A quantitative research design was employed using a survey approach. Instrument development was conducted through the integration of two established questionnaires originating from India and Europe, followed by contextual adaptation. Data were collected from female lecturers employed at Catholic universities in Indonesia. The two preliminary questionnaires were administered to the same initial group of female academics. For the final validation, the integrated instrument was administered to the initial respondents together with additional participants, resulting in a larger validation sample. The measurement model was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with SmartPLS. Reliability and validity were assessed through composite reliability, Cronbach's alpha, average variance extracted, and discriminant validity criteria. The findings indicate that the newly developed instrument demonstrates strong reliability and validity across all dimensions, with acceptable thresholds achieved for composite reliability and convergent validity. Compared to the adapted international instruments, the final instrument exhibits higher cultural relevance and improved measurement precision. Several dimensions were more accurately captured, particularly those related to organizational culture, informal networks, and discriminatory promotion practices, indicating a stronger alignment with the Indonesian academic environment. The study contributes to the refinement of measurement approaches in gender-related research by providing a robust and context-sensitive instrument. The instrument is expected to support future empirical studies and institutional policy evaluations aimed at reducing gender disparities in academic career advancement and leadership positions in Indonesia, while also enabling more accurate diagnosis of structural and cultural barriers. title: ST-AHM: a soft-threshold sparse-attention hypergraph model with contrastive learning for session-based recommendation
abstract: Session-based recommendation (SBR) predicts the next interaction from anonymous, short-lived behavioral sequences. A central challenge is to capture higher-order dependencies within sessions and collaborative information across related sessions while limiting weak contextual relations. We propose ST-AHM, a dual-channel model that jointly represents within-session and cross-session information. In the within-session channel, hypergraph convolution captures higher-order item dependencies. Hypergraph-specific sparse attention (HSPA) then averages scaled compatibility scores across attention heads before applying Sparsemax. This operation creates a consensus-based sparse support while retaining head-specific value projections, thereby reducing the propagation of weakly supported relations. An identity-free blank node summarizes the enhanced sequence and produces a context-dependent session-intent representation without relying directly on the last item. In the cross-session channel, Jaccard similarity between session item sets defines a relational graph. Relational graph convolution propagates collaborative information, and the blank-node representation acts as a blank-node-derived query for aggregating relevant cross-session context. A contrastive objective aligns valid interaction representations with the blank-node-augmented view of the same session and distinguishes them from shuffled representations. Across Tmall, Diginetica, and 30Music, ST-AHM outperformed the evaluated baselines, including DCL-BPM, DiffSBR, and MSGAT. Its average improvements were 19.23% for HR@10, 12.71% for HR@20, 23.19% for MRR@10, and 24.28% for MRR@20. These results support the joint modeling of within-session and cross-session information while reducing the influence of weak relations. title: Why (not) subscribe? Drivers and barriers of grocery replenishment subscriptions
abstract: Subscription models are gaining importance across retail sectors, yet a picture of consumers’ evaluations of replenishment subscriptions for regularly needed products, particularly groceries, is still lacking. Drawing on perceived value theory and technology acceptance research, this study proposes a value-risk framework for replenishment subscription adoption. It contrasts four value-related drivers (time efficiency, supply reliability, cognitive relief, and cost efficiency) with four corresponding risk-related barriers (time concerns, supply mismatch concerns, lock-in concerns, and financial concerns) and examines their effects on perceived usefulness, attitude, and ultimately usage intention. Two structural models, a ‘drivers model’ and a ‘barriers model’, were estimated using quota-representative surveys in Germany (N = 493) and the UK (N = 339), complemented by multigroup analysis. The results show that subscription evaluations are inherently ambivalent: positive and negative evaluations coexist, but drivers account for considerably more variance in perceived usefulness and attitude than barriers, while financial and supply mismatch concerns still exert strong negative effects. Convenience proves multidimensional: while cognitive relief outweighs time efficiency as a driver of perceived usefulness, distinct barrier facets also show different relevance. The cross-country comparison reveals common patterns alongside differences. Retailers are advised to communicate the benefits of subscriptions more concretely rather than through generic convenience claims. However, relying just on benefit communication is insufficient: adoption also hinges on actively mitigating perceived risks, with messaging tailored to a market's maturity and familiarity. © 2026 The Authors

title: Investigation of uncertainties associated with human judgment during the inspection and condition assessment of civil infrastructures
abstract: Inspection of civil infrastructure components is a critical task to assess their condition states and plan for appropriate maintenance actions. The process of inspection, however, involves several sources of uncertainty that can influence how a component is rated by an inspector. Despite potential consequences, such uncertainties have remained largely unexplored. This motivated the current study to develop a holistic framework to first measure the agreement and consistency of condition state predictions provided by various inspectors through the inter-rater reliability and intra-class correlation methods. The study then advanced to understand how the provided condition ratings can be analyzed, updated, and aggregated, taking into consideration possible interactions among inspectors during an inspection task. The outcome was quantified based on the inclination of participating inspectors to make more conservative, realistic, or less conservative assessments. The cumulative prospect theory was then utilized to quantify how the risk tolerance of individual inspectors can influence the decision making process, both at the time of inspection and during the service life of civil infrastructure components subjected to inspection. In the absence of similar studies, this investigation’s findings helped improve how condition state ratings received from inspectors can be processed and incorporated into a decision making framework. While the exploration of the psychological roots of why various inspectors rate the same component differently remained outside the scope of this study, the quantification of contributing uncertainties is expected to guide future training programs to further enhance the quality of condition assessment and management decisions made based on inspection reports. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Diversification or concentration? Supply chain configuration responses to decoupling risk
abstract: This study investigates corporate supply chain configuration strategies in the context of perceived decoupling risk. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2016 to 2023, we employ textual analysis to construct a firm-level index of perceived decoupling risk. Building on this index, we empirically examine its effect on corporate supply chain configuration strategies. The findings reveal that a higher level of perceived decoupling risk prompts firms to pursue greater supply chain diversification, leading to a significant decrease in supply chain concentration; notably, the diversification response is concentrated among firms facing high-intensity risk perception, while low-intensity risk perception is associated with minimal supply chain adjustment. Further analysis reveals that this negative association is attenuated by both executive risk preference and the level of corporate investment irreversibility. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the reduction in supply chain concentration is more pronounced for firms with high overseas revenue exposure, those in strategic emerging industries, and small-scale enterprises. Additionally, this impact is amplified during periods of heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly following the U.S.-China trade frictions in 2018, and is more pronounced in the upstream ends of supply chains. Finally, we find that the proactive supply chain diversification triggered by decoupling risk significantly enhances firms' operational resilience after a three-year adjustment period, demonstrating a long-term benefit for corporate stability. By quantifying firms’ subjective perception of decoupling risk and confirming its significant impact on supply chain configuration, this study provides novel micro-level evidence on firms’ supply chain behaviors in response to external environmental uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Target item identification for injection attacks in recommender systems via graph-enhanced user representations
abstract: Recommender systems are increasingly threatened by profile injection attacks. However, most existing defenses focus on detecting fake users, which becomes unreliable as modern attacks generate highly concealed profiles and operational platforms often lack attacker labels or attack priors. To address this limitation, we propose TIGER (Target Item Identification via Graph-Enhanced Representations), a hybrid auditing-oriented framework that reframes the final defensive output from user-level fake user labels to item-level suspicious target item candidates. Importantly, TIGER does not eliminate user-side analysis; instead, it uses unsupervised suspicious user discovery as an intermediate support step for downstream auditing. Specifically, TIGER first leverages a small trusted reference set to learn stable item embeddings and aligns unknown data into a shared semantic space. It then constructs graph-enhanced user representations by integrating rating statistics, preference patterns, and item semantics, enabling the extraction of informative suspicious user candidates for target item auditing. Finally, suspicious target item candidates are flagged through a rank-shift auditing strategy that compares recommendation outcomes before and after reintroducing suspicious users. Extensive experiments on three widely used datasets under ten representative attack scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of TIGER. Across ten attacks, TIGER achieves average DR@5/DR@10 values of 0.4430/0.6120, 0.5550/0.7500, and 0.2670/0.3400 on ML-100K, ML-1M, and Automotive, outperforming the average results of the best baseline selected for each attack by 106.20%/28.25%, 72.36%/64.84%, and 154.29%/111.18%, respectively. These results indicate that TIGER provides a reliable auditing tool for identifying high-risk target item candidates in adversarial recommender systems. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Bridging Transparency Gaps in Construction Claims through Blockchain Integration
abstract: The construction industry plays a vital role in Pakistan's economy, yet it continues to face persistent challenges in claim administration that hinder project performance, transparency, and trust among stakeholders. This study addresses these challenges by identifying the principal shortcomings of conventional claim management systems and developing a blockchain-based claims management application to improve security, traceability, and procedural efficiency. A three-stage research design was adopted. First, a systematic literature review was conducted to identify deficiencies in traditional claim management practices. This was followed by semistructured interviews with fifteen contract specialists involved in extension of time (EOT) claims to validate and refine the identified issues. Second, a decentralized application (DApp) was developed using React.js front-end and Solidity-based smart contracts and deployed on the Polygon test network to enable faster and more cost-effective transactions. Third, the developed system was evaluated through expert review involving 32 participants drawn from contracting, consulting, client organizations, and academia, followed by statistical analysis. The findings indicate that the proposed blockchain-based claims management system (B-CMS) improves data integrity, transparency, traceability, and timeliness in claim administration compared with traditional approaches. However, the system is not intended to replace professional judgment in highly subjective claim situations and is not suitable for capturing oral instructions or unstructured design and work-pattern changes. Despite these limitations, the study demonstrates the feasibility of B-CMS for construction claim administration in Pakistan and offers insights that may be relevant to comparable project environments internationally. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Using reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a wine tasting service in Italy: Findings from a life cycle assessment application experience
abstract: Wine tourism, including winery visits, tastings, and cultural events, boosts sustainable development but generates environmental impacts ranging from food and wine production to tasting services. This study applies Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), focused on Carbon Footprint (CF), to compare the use of reusable ceramic vs. disposable cellulose-pulp plates in a tasting service in an Apulian winery. A cradle-to-grave analysis reveals that, in baseline scenario, reusable plates showed a slightly higher CF than single-use plates (0.0668 vs. 0.0635 kgCO₂eq/person served, respectively). Based on the results obtained, process optimisation solutions were identified: it was found that using photovoltaic-powered energy-efficient dishwasher may reduce the CF of reusable plates by 67%, reducing the impact to 0.0179 kgCO₂eq/person served in the best-performing scenario. Five service configurations were then tested over a total of 2500 customers served in six months, assuming a constant optimal dishwasher loading efficiency (i.e., operating exclusively at full capacity). Whilst the absolute reuse rate of the plate stock inherently scales with customer volume (averaging approximately 73 uses per plate in the baseline period), the results showed that, without technological improvements, the lowest-impact option was to serve 500 people with reusable plates and 2000 with disposable plates. Overall, this study extends the application of Life Cycle Assessment from conventional production systems to experiential tourism services. The findings demonstrate that the environmental performance of tableware is not solely dictated by intrinsic material properties, but is fundamentally driven by the systemic operational configuration, including dishwashing efficiency, service volumes, and the carbon intensity of the electricity mix. Consequently, this study provides a novel, scalable methodological framework to support wineries and tourism operators in designing scientifically grounded, lower-impact tasting services. © 2026

title: Contextualizing negotiation research: The unique dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations
abstract: Effective buyer–supplier negotiations are important for organizations to attain their goals and for wider society to have a reliable supply of goods and services. These negotiations also have distinctive characteristics that differentiate them from other negotiation settings, such as personal buyer–seller negotiations, which have attracted much of the attention in the negotiation literature. Given the differences between professional buyer–supplier and personal buyer–seller negotiations, some findings from personal negotiations may have limited applicability in supply chain settings, while others hold across contexts. These findings have important implications for both negotiation research and education, calling for careful contextualization based on the type of negotiation. By reviewing recent studies in the supply chain management literature, this article highlights several common dynamics of buyer–supplier negotiations and how they affect negotiation outcomes. These dynamics are broadly categorized into the non-exhaustive themes of power in ongoing buyer–supplier relationships, other relational factors (supply network complexity, cross-cultural relations, and AI adoption), and negotiation strategies in buyer–supplier relationships (distributive, integrative, and mixed strategies), providing scholars with an overview of selected recent research on buyer–supplier negotiations. © 2026 The Author(s)

title: LLMs’ reshaping of people, processes, products, and society in software development: a qualitative exploration with early adopters
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping software development, but their impact across the full software development lifecycle is underexplored. Existing work tends to focus on isolated activities such as code generation or testing, leaving open questions about how LLMs affect developers, processes, products, and the broader software ecosystem. We address this gap through semi-structured interviews with sixteen early-adopter software professionals who integrated LLM-based tools into their day-to-day work in early to mid-2023. We treat these interviews as early empirical evidence and compare participants’ accounts with recent work on LLMs in software engineering, noting which early patterns persist or shift. Using thematic analysis, we organize our findings around four dimensions: people, process, product, and society. Developers reported substantial productivity gains from reducing mundane tasks, streamlining search, and accelerating debugging, but also described a productivity-quality paradox: they frequently discarded generated code and shifted effort from writing code to critically evaluating and integrating it. LLM use was highly phase-dependent, with strong uptake in implementation and debugging but limited influence on requirements gathering and collaborative work. Participants developed new competencies to use LLMs effectively, including prompt engineering strategies, multi-layered verification, and security-conscious integration to protect proprietary data. They also anticipated changes in hiring expectations, team practices, and computing education, while emphasizing that human judgment and foundational software engineering skills remain essential. Our findings, consistent with evidence from large-scale studies, offer actionable implications for developers, organizations, educators, and tool designers seeking to integrate LLMs responsibly into professional software practice. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: When stigmatized workers become consumers
abstract: Existing research on occupational stigma has focused primarily on workplace consequences, with less attention to how stigmatized service workers respond to service failures as consumers. Guided by cognitive appraisal theory, this sequential mixed-methods study integrates 20 interviews with a survey of 429 frontline workers in China. Qualitative findings show that perceived occupational stigma heightens sensitivity to disrespect and identity threat, whereas perceived work dirtiness shapes whether failures are attributed to situational constraints or preventable neglect. Quantitative results indicate that both constructs are positively associated with customer aggression and tolerance. Aggression may function as confrontational problem-focused coping, whereas tolerance reflects emotion-focused coping, and both are positively related to service recovery satisfaction. Service recovery performance strengthens these relationships. The study applies cognitive appraisal theory to an underexplored dual-role context and shows how distinct occupational perceptions shape appraisal, coping, and recovery evaluations. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Educational legacies of christian missions: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
abstract: This paper investigates the educational legacies of Christian missions established before independence, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, focusing on contemporary disparities in educational content, quality, access, and outcomes. Using georeferenced data from over 20,000 schools and two million students participating in the Examen National d’État (Exetat) between 2016 and 2019, as well as primary data from a phone survey of 624 school directors, we explore how proximity to Catholic and Protestant missions during the colonial period influences educational opportunities today. We find that schools near historical Christian missions offer a broader and higher-quality curriculum, with increased access to study tracks outside the basic Pedagogy section. Students attending these schools are more likely to pass the Exetat and achieve grades qualifying for university admission, although the magnitude of the effect is modest. Observable school-environment and quality characteristics attenuate the Catholic missionary-proximity coefficient by about half, while demand-side patterns point to additional differences in student composition. Our findings reveal that the strong partnership between missions and the colonial state entrenched spatial inequalities in educational access and quality, inequalities that persist to this day. © 2026

title: Financial leverage in business sector profitability: A review
abstract: This study examines the relationship between financial leverage and corporate profitability in a context of heightened economic uncertainty following the COVID-19 pandemic, a period during which organizations have been compelled to redefine their financing strategies in order to preserve sustainability and financial performance. The primary objective was to systematically analyze recent empirical evidence on the impact of financial leverage on corporate profitability. To this end, a systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using the Scopus database. The search strategy incorporated terms related to financial leverage, financing, profitability, and firms, while the 2020–2025 period and the explicit inclusion of key topic-related concepts were established as the main eligibility criteria. From an initial total of 7,587 identified records, a rigorous screening process was carried out based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in the final selection of 36 articles for qualitative analysis. The study employed synthesis matrices, bibliometric analysis, and keyword co-occurrence networks, which made it possible to identify trends, predominant methodological approaches, and the main findings. The results indicate that companies rely on a combination of internal and external financing sources, including bank credit, bond issuance, informal financing, and fintech tools. In general, financial leverage has a positive effect on indicators such as ROA, ROE, and ROI, provided that adequate financial planning, cost control, and efficient debt management are in place. However, in SMEs or firms with high levels of indebtedness and limited managerial capacity, the impact may be negative or statistically insignificant. It is concluded that financial leverage constitutes a strategic tool for enhancing profitability, provided that it is managed prudently and within a comprehensive financial risk management framework. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: Operational constraints in professional kitchens: A theory of constraints perspective on food waste reduction
abstract: Professional kitchens, where core foodservice operations occur, generate up to two-thirds of total food waste. Although recent research has increasingly acknowledged the managerial and operational dimensions of food waste, limited attention has been devoted to explaining how these constraints interact within an integrated operational system. Addressing this gap, this study applies the Theory of Constraints (TOC) and qualitative triangulation through structured observations and in-depth interviews with kitchen staff to identify and analyze waste reduction constraints across kitchen workflows. Four interrelated constraint dimensions were identified, and workflow-tracing analysis revealed a sequential constraint chain in which policy and market constraints appear to influence resource conditions that are reflected in behavioral constraints, where throughput constraints become most visible. Applying Goldratt's Five Focusing Steps across this chain generates prioritized interventions. The study reframes waste as a systemic outcome of upstream pressures and offers a structured diagnostic framework for effective intervention. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Audiovisual aesthetic matching enhances food evaluation by amplifying pleasure and perceived tastiness
abstract: Aesthetic experiences can shape the evaluations of consumers, including in the case of food. While matching multisensory cues can enhance perception, such interventions have not always been shown to promote consumption as effectively as predicted. The present study examined whether and how the multisensory aesthetic match of food plating and background music can enhance consumers' hedonic evaluations and purchase intentions. In two studies, participants viewed or tasted foods with varying plating aesthetics, either with music matched or mismatched in aesthetic value (e.g., ugly vs. beautiful). The participants provided food evaluations before or after tasting. The results revealed that matched audiovisual aesthetics produced enhancement effects on expected evaluations across different aesthetic levels among female participants, whereas men's ratings were enhanced only for the less-aesthetic plating. In contrast, actual evaluations were amplified only for healthy food with less-aesthetic and unhealthy food with relatively high-aesthetic plating. The multisensory enhancement of aesthetic value occurred through distinct pathways, influencing pre- and post-tasting evaluations through pleasure and perceived tastiness. These findings reveal that the mechanisms of audiovisual aesthetic matching in enhancing food consumption depend on the type of food and the gender of the participant. Aesthetic cues can be applied to nudge emotional engagement and enrich sensory experiences in daily routines, and to promote health-oriented consumption across different goal orientations (e.g., encouraging or curbing consumption). © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Paying for the future? Cross-season pre-sale product launch strategy in hotels
abstract: Traditional hotels face persistent seasonal demand imbalance, with weak off-peak demand and constrained peak-season capacity. Drawing on Contingency Theory, this study examines cross-season pre-sale as a context-dependent hotel revenue management configuration and investigates how different configurations (i.e., no pre-sale, self-run pre-sale, and platform-based pre-sale) fit varying operating conditions. Results show that cross-season pre-sale does not universally outperform conventional practices; its value depends on the balance among incremental demand, impacts on existing demand, and implementation costs. Moreover, neither self-run nor platform-based pre-sale always dominates, as their relative effectiveness depends on the trade-off between platform-enabled market reach and channel costs. The study identifies boundary conditions for effective cross-season demand coordination and offers practical guidance for configuration choice. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Driving impact? How imperfect displacement shapes heterogeneous rebound in carsharing
abstract: Green technologies, products, and services, such as carsharing, are commonly promoted as pathways to lower environmental impacts by increasing efficiency. Yet rebound effects, behavioral and economic responses to improved efficiency, may erode these environmental impact reductions. Many rebound studies assume perfect displacement, where a new technology or mode of service provision fully replaces an existing service on a one-to-one basis. While analytically convenient, this assumption overlooks real-world complexity and consumer heterogeneity. Using survey data from nearly 4500 Belgian carsharing users, we compare rebound estimates under perfect displacement with those based on reported shifts in mobility. Under the perfect displacement assumption, we find a 53% rebound effect. When accounting for imperfect displacement, however, rebound effects vary widely across users. While median effects remain positive (20%–46%), at the individual level rebound effects range from substantial net benefits to strong rebound (5th–95th percentile: −331% to 147%). A cluster analysis further reveals distinct user groups with systematically different impacts, underscoring that displacement patterns vary not only in scale but also in direction. These findings suggest that carsharing's environmental impact is highly user-dependent, and that relying on a single aggregate estimate may mask critical behavioral variations. As this case study demonstrates, accounting for imperfect displacement in rebound analysis is critical for advancing theory and for tailoring more effective policy interventions. © 2026 The Authors. title: Uncovering heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on stock returns using causal forest double machine learning
abstract: Global uncertainty has become an important source of financial market instability, yet its effects are inherently heterogeneous and difficult to identify using conventional econometric models. Existing empirical studies primarily rely on linear and average-effect estimators, which may conceal substantial heterogeneity across economic conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable causal machine learning framework that integrates Causal Forest Double Machine Learning (CF-DML) with SHAP explanations to estimate and interpret heterogeneous effects of global uncertainty on industry-level stock returns. Using a balanced panel of six major industries listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange from 2011 to 2022, global uncertainty is measured by the World Uncertainty Index (WUI), while macroeconomic and financial variables are incorporated as lagged covariates. The CF-DML framework enables robust causal inference under high-dimensional confounding and nonlinear relationships, whereas SHAP values identify the main drivers of treatment-effect heterogeneity. The results show that the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) of global uncertainty is statistically insignificant, yet substantial heterogeneity exists across observations. Differences across industries are relatively modest, indicating that global uncertainty is transmitted primarily through time-varying macro-financial conditions rather than fixed sectoral characteristics. SHAP analysis identifies exchange-rate volatility, inflation, and market valuation as the dominant factors explaining heterogeneous responses. The study contributes to the literature by combining causal inference, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified framework for financial analysis. The findings suggest that global uncertainty should be viewed as a state-dependent macro-financial phenomenon, providing practical insights for portfolio risk management, macro-financial surveillance, and the design of policies aimed at enhancing financial resilience in emerging economies characterized by persistent inflation and exchange-rate volatility. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Does retirement reduce household carbon emissions in China? Evidence from fuzzy regression discontinuity design
abstract: This study examines the causal effect of household-head retirement on household carbon emissions (HCEs) in China. Combining multi-wave data from the China Family Panel Studies with household carbon accounting, we construct household-level total carbon emissions (TCEs), distinguishing between direct carbon emissions (DCEs) from household energy use and indirect carbon emissions (ICEs) embodied in the goods and services purchased by households. We estimate the local causal effect of retirement using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design based on China's statutory retirement age of 60 for urban male household heads. The results show that retirement significantly reduces TCEs by approximately 7.4–9.0 tCO₂ per household. This reduction is driven primarily by lower ICEs, while the estimated effect on DCEs is statistically insignificant. Point estimates are larger for households headed by individuals without tertiary education and for low-asset households, but formal bootstrap tests do not reject equality across education or asset groups. The mechanism results suggest that the decline in ICEs is mainly associated with a contraction in overall household consumption, particularly reductions in non-subsistence and work-related expenditure, with limited evidence of a broad shift in consumption composition. Disaggregated results further show that the emission reductions are concentrated in clothing, household facilities and services, and transportation and communication. These findings provide local causal evidence that retirement reshapes HCEs mainly through reductions in consumption-based indirect emissions rather than through changes in direct household energy use, highlighting the importance of life-course transitions for understanding demand-side emission dynamics in aging societies. © 2026

title: An empirical study on the capability of LLMs in decomposing bug reports
abstract: Bug reports are essential to the software development life cycle. They help developers track and resolve issues, but are often difficult to process due to their complexity, which can delay resolution and affect software quality. This study investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can assist developers in automatically decomposing complex bug reports into smaller, self-contained units, making them easier to understand and address. We first conducted an empirical study using 127 resolved privacy-related bug reports collected from Apache Jira. We evaluated ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V1 using zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Under zero-shot prompting, the models correctly decomposed only 10 and 11 reports, respectively. Few-shot prompting increased their true decomposition rates by 140% (10 vs. 24) and 163.64% (11 vs. 29), respectively, although the overall accuracy remained limited. To examine whether the findings generalize beyond privacy-related reports and to expand the dataset size, we further analyzed 127 security-related bug reports using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. We compared zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and persona prompting. Few-shot prompting achieved the best performance for both models, correctly decomposing 89 reports with GPT-5.5 and 51 reports with DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Across the experiments, we identify a concrete failure taxonomy for LLM-based bug report decomposition, including over-decomposition, over-analysis, incorrect interpretation of solutions, lacking key information, and empty output. Over-decomposition is the most common failure mode, suggesting that LLMs often struggle to distinguish independent bug units from supporting information such as logs, code snippets, background context, and proposed fixes. Overall, LLMs show potential for automated bug report decomposition, but their reliability, prompt sensitivity, and adherence to decomposition instructions still require improvement. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: The public funding of the New Space Economy. Confronting public procurement and public-private partnership
abstract: This paper confronts public funding mechanisms in the New Space Economy (NSE). NSE refers to the rise of private actors’ activities in space; however, public funding remains crucial. Addressing this issue, this paper critically compares Public Procurement - an order from the public sector - and public-private partnership (PPP) - i.e., a long-term agreement between public and private actors for the provision of public services or goods - with the final aim of highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and applicability in the NSE. We compare both models to underline differences and benefits, and contend that public procurement is advantageous for both public and private actors. Governments retain public control over space programmes on the one side, while private firms reduce risks on the other. Our results inform public decision-makers with a critical discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of the two models in the context of the NSE. The paper concludes that the supposed privatization of space is far from happening and that private actors would not have entered the space economy without public procurement. © 2026 IAA. title: Disruption-induced spatial inequality in resilience loss of urban rail transit: A multi-agent simulation analysis
abstract: With the rapid expansion of urban rail transit networks in large cities, operational disruptions occur more frequently, causing varying degrees of accessibility loss and shaping station-level resilience. From the network and spatial perspective, these differences manifest as inequalities in the distribution of transport capacity. To investigate these relationships, this study proposes a scenario-based dynamic simulation analysis framework and applies it to the Beijing urban rail transit system as a case study. High-resolution passenger travel processes are first generated using multi-agent simulation. Then, within a dynamic accessibility and resilience evaluation framework, a multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) model is applied to examine accessibility, resilience, and equity under zero-load, normal operation, and disruption scenarios. The results show that variations in accessibility and resilience are highly sensitive to the location and characteristics of disruptions. Under severe disruptions, suburban corridors and key transfer segments form concentrated clusters of low resilience. MGWR analysis further reveals distinct spatial heterogeneity in the effects of structural attributes, passenger demand pressure, and spatial environmental factors, with different drivers operating at different spatial scales. Overall, this study provides quantitative evidence to inform planning, operational optimization, and equity-oriented governance of urban rail transit systems under complex disruption conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A domain-differentiated stress perspective on turnover intention
abstract: This study examines the associations of job stress and work–family conflict with turnover intention among lecturers employed in private higher education institutions in Yunnan Province, China. Drawing on conservation of resources theory and a dual-stressor perspective, job stress and work–family conflict are conceptualized as distinct but potentially interrelated sources of resource depletion that may contribute to withdrawal cognition. Lecturers in Chinese private higher education institutions may face substantial teaching responsibilities, administrative demands, performance expectations, limited institutional resources, and employment uncertainty, making this an important context for examining turnover intention. Using a quantitative survey design, data were collected through the Wenjuanxing online platform. After data screening, 374 valid responses were retained. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to assess the measurement model, test the hypothesized relationships, and evaluate the model’s predictive relevance. The results showed that both job stress and work–family conflict were significantly and positively associated with turnover intention. Work–family conflict showed the stronger association, suggesting that difficulties reconciling professional and family responsibilities may play a particularly important role in lecturers’ intentions to leave. However, the interaction between job stress and work–family conflict was not statistically significant. Thus, the findings did not provide evidence that the association between work–family conflict and turnover intention varied across different levels of job stress. The model explained 62.1% of the variance in turnover intention, indicating substantial explanatory power. This study contributes to the literature by comparing the direct associations of work-domain and work–family-interface stressors with turnover intention in private higher education. The findings also suggest that workload management, family-supportive policies, and institutional support should be considered as complementary intervention targets. Copyright (c) 2026 The Authors. title: Psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation influences safety behaviour: A moderated serial mediation of psychological safety climate, employee resilience, and ethical leadership
abstract: Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study examines the psychological mechanisms through which digital transformation is associated with employees’ safety behaviour in Ghana’s mining sector. Specifically, the study investigates the mediating roles of psychological safety climate and employee resilience, as well as the moderating role of ethical leadership. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 418 employees across ten mining sites. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that digital transformation is positively associated with psychological safety climate and employee resilience, which in turn relate to both safety compliance and safety participation. Psychological safety climate emerged as a stronger predictor of compliance, whereas employee resilience played a more critical role in fostering participatory safety behaviours. Furthermore, the results support a serial mediation pathway, demonstrating that digital transformation indirectly influences safety behavior through the sequential effects of psychological safety climate and resilience. Ethical leadership was found to moderate these relationships, strengthening the positive associations between digital transformation on psychological resources and behavioural outcomes. The study contributes to literature by extending conservation of resources theory to explain how technological, contextual, and personal resources interact in relation to safety behavior in high-risk work environments. Practically, the findings highlight the importance of integrating digital technologies with supportive psychological climates, resilience-building strategies, and ethical leadership practices to promote sustainable safety outcomes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
