title: “It's all just code”: How is responsibility embedded (or not) in the work of a team of software engineers?
abstract: Recent research has documented how software can sometimes contribute to harm and inequality, affecting individuals, societies, and the environment. We argue that human values embedded in software, consciously or unconsciously during design and development, play a significant role in producing these outcomes. In other words, to understand responsibility in software engineering, it is crucial to understand how Software Engineers (SEs) incorporate responsibility into their practices, and if or how they reflect on the potential impact of their work. The research reported here probes this assertion by focusing on a team of research SEs involved in developing a commercial source code clone detection tool. Through reflexive thematic analysis of in-depth interviews, with meta-reflections from the SEs Principal Investigator, we offer a detailed account of the practices and artefacts referenced when these professionals reflect on responsibility in their work. Our analysis suggests that the team does not consider responsibility as a singular, unified concept. Instead, reflections on potential negative software impacts and mitigation strategies vary depending on whether they relate to the institutional/organisational context, the specific task, or the intended use. Overall, these SEs tend to perceive software as neutral or inherently beneficial, which, in turn, feeds into a lack of practice of engaging in speculation about the broader implications of the technologies they work with. To address these gaps, we propose a paradigm shift toward an infrastructural view of responsibility - interdisciplinary, sociotechnical, and situated – embedded within the diverse practices and organisational cultures of SE teams operating in different contexts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Effect of AI authorship disclosure on purchase intention in cultural tourism souvenirs: The mediating roles of perceived effort and authenticity
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands in cultural tourism souvenir design and disclosure policies evolve, evidence remains limited on how AI authorship disclosure shapes responses across nationality groups and products. Drawing on signaling theory, two studies compared consumers from China and the U.S. across three disclosure conditions: unlabeled, human–AI co-created, and AI-generated. Study 1 used tourism postcard stimuli (N = 1110), and Study 2 used mug and tourism tote bag stimuli (N = 1255). Both studies found that disclosure affected purchase intention and interacted significantly with nationality. Differences across disclosure conditions were significant among participants from the U.S. but not among those from China. In Study 1, the unlabeled and human–AI co-created conditions did not differ, and both exceeded the AI-generated condition. In Study 2, the unlabeled condition exceeded both disclosed conditions for both products, whereas the latter two did not differ. AI-generated disclosure was consistently associated with lower purchase intention than no disclosure, whereas the relative position of human–AI co-created disclosure differed between studies. Parallel mediation analyses showed indirect effects through perceived effort and perceived authenticity. Perceived effort effects were significant for both comparisons with the unlabeled condition across three examined products, whereas the human–AI co-created versus unlabeled authenticity effect was nonsignificant in Study 1 but significant in Study 2. Nationality moderated some, but not all, indirect effects. Thus, firms should not assume that human–AI co-creation enhances responses and should consider clarifying human contribution and pretesting disclosure strategies across products and national markets. © 2026 The Authors

title: AI and negotiation: Facilitating learning or Fostering dependency?
abstract: AI is being used in negotiation teaching and training both to promote learning and to facilitate planning for and executing a negotiation. This is a review of current empirical research on the relationships between AI negotiation interventions and learning and dependency. It categorizes AI negotiation interventions by practice, coaching, and feedback. It evaluates their effects on learning with respect to knowledge, satisfaction, behavior, and outcomes. Socratic coaching and post negotiation feedback and reflection appear to facilitate learning. However, interactive explicit AI coaching during planning or negotiation may risk dependency. Rather than dependency due to laziness, motivated students may defer to AI expertise. Alternatively, they may be overloaded by dynamic AI advice. The review concludes that there are many opportunities for future research on the question of if, why, and how AI can facilitate negotiators’ learning versus dependency. Research that looks broadly at learning, that compares separate versus packages of AI interventions, and that identifies mechanisms behind learning versus dependency is especially needed. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Picard approximation and stability analysis of generalized ϱ-Caputo stochastic fractional differential equations with application to a Black–Scholes-type model
abstract: This paper investigates stochastic fractional differential equations involving the generalized ϱ-Caputo derivative of order β∈(1/2,1). Under global Lipschitz and linear growth conditions, existence and uniqueness are established through successive approximations. Explicit pointwise mean-square estimates are derived for the Picard approximation error and the continuous dependence of solutions on the initial data. Sufficient conditions for finite-time stability (F − T − S) and generalized Ulam–Hyers–Rassias (U − H − R) stability are also obtained, together with computable stability constants. For numerical illustration, a generalized Euler–Maruyama (E–M) scheme is adapted to time-dependent coefficients and applied to a stochastic fractional Black–Scholes-type model. The simulations are consistent with the theoretical estimates. © 2026 International Association for Mathematics and Computers in Simulation (IMACS).

title: Pathways to plant-based meal consumption: A two-wave test of the health action process approach (HAPA)
abstract: Despite well-documented health and environmental benefits, increasing plant-based meal consumption remains challenging in meat-centric societies, reflecting complex socio-cognitive processes in translating intention into action. Grounded in the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA), this study examined plant-based meal consumption among young adults from the USA, Portugal, and the Netherlands who had not fully adopted a plant-based diet (N = 266). Using two waves one week apart, we estimated three structural models of plant-based meal consumption, controlling for prior behavior and common method variance. Findings were broadly consistent with HAPA. Action self-efficacy was most strongly associated with intention, which in turn was associated with action planning. Coping planning and self-monitoring pathways were not supported. While past behavior remained most strongly associated with plant-based meal consumption, the parsimonious model reaffirmed action planning as the key intention-behavior mediator. The findings highlight this volitional process in translating motivation into action and suggest interventions may benefit from strengthening efficacy beliefs and concrete planning strategies to support plant-based dietary change. © 2026

title: Together or apart? Migration, education access, and intergenerational mobility in China
abstract: This paper studies how hukou-based education wedges and child-arrangement costs jointly shape welfare and intergenerational educational mobility in China. I develop a quantitative spatial model with overlapping generations in which households sequentially choose education, migration, and child arrangement, and estimate it using census and household-survey data. Under a common financing rule, two child-targeted policies raise the co-migration rate to a similar extent but differ sharply in welfare and mobility. Subsidizing co-migrating families in high-cost destinations generates 1.4 times as much welfare per unit of government revenue as removing migrant children's education-access wedges. These gains concentrate on recipients. Removing the education-access wedges delivers over four times the mobility gain per unit of revenue, and the resulting human capital generates growing welfare gains across generations. A broader reform that equalizes public-service access for all migrants is the most welfare-efficient but does not raise mobility. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Bibliometric study of environmental education: Scientific architecture and the transition toward micro-educational and behavioral approaches
abstract: Although scientific production in environmental education has grown steadily, fragmented approaches and limited interdisciplinary integration persist. Moreover, the transition from macronormative frameworks to microeducational approaches oriented toward behavioral change remains insufficiently characterized. The objective of this study was to comprehensively analyze the scientific architecture of environmental education, identifying its structural evolution, key actors, predominant sources, funding dynamics, thematic trends, and scientific production cycle, with particular attention to the shift toward microeducational and behavioral approaches. The study followed a rigorous and consolidated four-stage bibliometric method. A total of 4,952 documents indexed in Scopus were analyzed using the Bibliometrix software, examining six main indicators: (1) authors, (2) sponsors, (3) thematic evolution and conceptual structure, (4) sources, (5) documents, and (6) scientific production. The findings reveal sustained expansion in environmental education, with a productivity peak in 2025 and a projected stabilization toward 2032, confirming its advanced consolidation phase. An editorial structure concentrated in historical core journals—Environmental Education Research and Journal of Environmental Education—was identified, alongside growing interdisciplinary expansion toward sustainability, higher education, and technological innovation. Scientific leadership is concentrated in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, although emerging economies such as Brazil and China are gaining prominence. Thematically, macrostructural cores linked to sustainability and sustainable development persist; however, microeducational approaches such as pro-environmental behavior, outdoor environmental education, and environmental knowledge are emerging more strongly, indicating a shift toward the analysis of situated learning processes and behavioral change. Bibliometric findings were contrasted with evidence from other bibliometric studies and systematic reviews. It is concluded that environmental education has evolved from a paradigm centered on global normative frameworks toward a multidimensional model integrating experience, behavior, technological innovation, and community action. The study provides insights for educational policy and teaching practice. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: A survey on fake review detection: From pre-trained language models to large language models
abstract: Online reviews shape consumer decisions, platform governance, and corporate reputation. Fake reviews compromise this information channel by injecting deceptive evidence into rating systems, recommendation pipelines, and public trust mechanisms. The rise of large language models, or LLMs, has changed the problem in two directions. LLMs can generate fluent and context-aware deceptive reviews, while pre-trained language models, or PLMs, and LLMs also provide stronger semantic representations for detection. This survey reviews fake review detection from an information fusion perspective, covering 211 studies published from 2018 to early 2026. We organize existing work by evidence source and fusion level, covering review text, sentiment, rating behavior, temporal metadata, user-product graphs, multimodal content, external knowledge, and LLM-generated signals. We trace the development from traditional machine learning and deep learning to PLM-based and LLM-based methods, and examine how different approaches combine textual, behavioral, structural, and multimodal evidence. We also analyze reported performance trends on widely used Amazon, Yelp, and OpSpam benchmark families, while noting the limitations caused by different label construction procedures, data splits, and evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems in adversarial generation, cross-domain transfer, uncertainty-aware fusion, missing-source robustness, interpretability, and trustworthy evaluation for AI-generated deceptive content. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: How can hotels strategically enhance competitive performance? Investigating the dynamic roles and impacts of service attributes on customer satisfaction and dissatisfaction
abstract: This study examines the asymmetric impact of service attributes on customer satisfaction (CS) and dissatisfaction (DS) in the luxury and upper upscale hotel segments, utilizing Impact Asymmetry Analysis and Impact Asymmetry Competitor Analysis. Grounded by the two-factor theory, this study integrates insights from online review ratings and textual sentiment to gauge customer evaluations. The findings reveal that attributes have discrete impacts on CS and DS when comparing high and low performance consistency brands. Hotels exhibiting low performance consistency are advised to prioritize managing attributes such as rooms, followed by value and cleanliness in rating-based evaluations. Additionally, location is identified as a key competitive disadvantage requiring urgent action in sentiment-based assessments. This study extends the understanding of the two-factor theory by examining the distinct impacts of attributes on CS and DS under varying performance consistency, providing actionable insights for hoteliers to strategically enhance attribute-level performance that strengthens customer experience and competitive standing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Suppressed inquiry: The hidden toll of working with satisfaction-optimized AI
abstract: LLMs have become thinking companions for hundreds of millions worldwide, and they often do remarkable work. But their satisfaction-optimized design produces suppressed inquiry: the tendency for LLMs to inhibit rather than facilitate users' questioning process. LLMs appear fluent, confident, and seemingly all-knowing, their near-instant and polished output making non-LLM work feel unacceptably tedious and less eloquent. They affirm rather than interrogate users' assumptions, producing output that is deceptively adequate—shallower, less original, and less carefully reasoned than it appears. Seemingly competent systems also reduce vigilance and the monitoring impulse that independent judgment requires. Their responses also confine users within the frame they establish, narrowing what users think to ask. These costs are self-concealing: detecting them requires the very engagement that they suppress. And repeated delegation gradually atrophies users' capacity to reason independently. Three converging pressures make correction difficult: commercial incentives that reward satisfaction over substance, LLMs’ tendency to revert to satisfaction-optimized defaults even when users push back, and a societal drift toward less-effortful engagement. We propose a research agenda to deepen the understanding of suppressed inquiry and how to counter it, to move closer to the remarkable thinking partners LLMs promised to be. © 2026 The Authors

title: Bridging the Human-AI preference gap: A persuasion-oriented tripartite framework
abstract: The remarkable performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems on a wide variety of complex tasks has fueled its rapid adoption in recent years. Yet, many individuals still exhibit a human-AI preference gap, such that they prefer human-generated over AI-generated outputs and follow recommendations made by generative AI (GenAI) less than human advice. We conceptualize the rejection of a superior AI system in favor of an inferior human as a persuasion failure that necessitates psychological rather than technological resolution. Recent research has identified various interventions that compress the human-AI preference gap. We codify these interventions by introducing a persuasion-oriented tripartite framework that delineates three distinct paths by which the preference gap between humans and AI systems may be narrowed: (1) AI-centric interventions, which directly bolster perceptions and evaluations of AI systems; (2) human-centric interventions, which reduce the (often inflated) perceptions and evaluations of humans; and (3) hybrid interventions, which offer an integrated or reformulated alternative that combines human and AI elements. Ultimately, our tripartite framework illustrates how different persuasion tactics fundamentally reshape beliefs and attitudes about both AI and humans, thereby informing system design elements and communication strategies that can bridge the human-AI preference gap. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Techno-economic study and sensitivity analysis- benefits of complex petrochemical waste refining
abstract: For the petrochemical industry to maintain resource sustainability, complex waste must be treated effectively. In the previous work, the Aspen Hysys V12.0 modeling tool was used to analyze the regeneration of water, aromatics (BTX), and glycols (MEG, DEG, and TEG) from petrochemical effluent and the operating parameters were validated with experimental study. This study presents a techno-economic and environmental assessment of an integrated petrochemical wastewater treatment system with resource recovery. The process enables recovery of water (7.8 MM kg/year), aromatics such as benzene and toluene (468,000 kg/year each), and glycols (over 16.5 MM kg/year). The total capital investment is estimated at $42.4 MM, with annual operating costs of $8.46 MM and revenue of $18 MM. The system achieves a net present value (NPV) of $31.8 MM, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 19.9%, and a payback period of 4.87 years. Sensitivity analysis identified product price and electricity cost as key economic drivers. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) showed a 95% probability of positive NPV, indicating robust performance under uncertainty. The carbon footprint is estimated at 11,970 tons CO2/year (0.12 kg CO2/kg treated), representing an 87% reduction compared to conventional systems. Carbon pricing further enhances economic viability. The novelty of this work lies in integrating techno-economic analysis, uncertainty quantification, carbon footprint evaluation, and circular economy principles into a unified framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed system is a sustainable and economically viable solution for petrochemical wastewater management. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: A probabilistic model for situation awareness reliability assessment in uncertain environments
abstract: Human error remains a major contributor to accidents in safety-critical systems, partly because operators may fail to establish effective situation awareness (SA) within critical time windows. Existing approaches to situation awareness reliability (SAR) often use SAGAT scores directly as reliability measures, conflating observed single-trial performance with the probability of successful SA formation under repeated conditions. They also lack a unified probabilistic framework integrating individual cognitive ability, task uncertainty, and available time. To address these limitations, this study applies the stress-strength interference principle from reliability engineering and models SA formation as a stochastic competition between cognitive strength and cognitive demand. A closed-form SAR expression with interpretable parameters is derived, forming the SAR-SSI model. The model was evaluated in a controlled experiment involving 29 participants and 1740 trials. Trial-level AUCs were 0.8032 for the full-sample fit and 0.8011 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, indicating similar discrimination for held-out participants within the same experimental paradigm. Higher values of the task-related indicator C and longer available time were associated with higher SAR, whereas greater task uncertainty was associated with lower SAR and attenuated these relationships. The SAR-SSI model provides an interpretable probability-based tool for comparing how alternative information-presentation and task configurations may affect the likelihood of successful SA formation in controlled dynamic tasks. title: Measurement scale for push and pull factors of Chinese pedestrian streets
abstract: The concepts of push and pull theory have been proposed and extensively discussed in various studies, particularly in tourism research. However, push and pull theory in the field of pedestrian street is not addressed in the existing research. This study takes the perspective of pedestrian-street consumers, follows a systematic scale-development procedure, and uses samples from eight Chinese cities to develop and test a scale measuring perceived push and pull factors. The scale is composed of 11 dimensions for each of the push and pull domains. This study then examines the nomological validity by testing the associations between push and pull factors and revisit intention and recommendation intention. The results of the study support the nomological validity of the proposed relationships. This study does not propose push and pull as new constructs. Instead, it organizes and validates their context-specific manifestations within Chinese pedestrian streets and provides a culturally grounded measurement instrument for subsequent retail and consumer research. The evidence supports its initial applicability across the Chinese cities examined, while its cross-national applicability remains to be established. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Product visual form and customer satisfaction: Multimodal evidence on affective value and functional diagnosis
abstract: Product visual form conveys important aesthetic, quality, and use-related cues for functionally complex products. However, multimodal evidence from real-world retail settings remains limited regarding how product visual form relates to consumer evaluations in online reviews and satisfaction. Using data from 200 smart standing desks, 41951 valid reviews, and 200 product images, this study combined engineering-attribute encoding, CLIP image embeddings, and CLIP-text concept scores to construct a multilayer representation of product visual form. A large language model was used to extract affective and functional evaluations from the reviews, and the platform favorable rate served as a product-level proxy for satisfaction. Product-level path analysis showed that PC3 (Non-standard premium form) was positively associated with affective evaluation, and affective evaluation was positively associated with satisfaction. Together, these coefficients yielded a significant positive indirect association (indirect association = 0.075, 95% BCa CI [0.021, 0.156], FDR-Adj. p = 0.014). Functional evaluation, by contrast, was negatively associated with satisfaction (β = −0.254, p < 0.01). Further decomposition showed that this negative association was more closely related to functional-mention coverage than to overall polarity of functional evaluations. Noise control and Workspace size adequacy were the principal negative sources. These findings indicate that affective and functional evaluations relate to satisfaction in distinct ways. For online retailers and e-commerce platforms, combining analysis of product visual form with online-review monitoring can help identify design value, detect quality risks, and prioritize service recovery. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Experimental and simulation studies on plasma gasification of medical waste for the co-production of ammonia and urea
abstract: This study explores the novel integration of plasma gasification and urea synthesis using medical waste as a feedstock, a research area largely unexplored compared to conventional plasma gasification applications. This investigation is designed to evaluate the technical and economic viability of producing hydrogen-rich syngas followed by the synthesis of ammonia and urea via advanced process simulation and experimental validation. Medical waste gasification occurs under a CO2 environment to increase syngas quality when using medical waste such as syringes, gloves, surgical masks, and drip sets. Although, the maximum value of lower heating value (LHV) (12.4 MJ/m3) was achieved by utilizing plasma at 1.25 kW, the highest energy efficiency of 53.8 % was obtained at 1.00 kW due to lower energy input. Residue content decreased from 19 wt% (0.75 kW), 14 wt% (1.0 kW), and 11 wt% (1.25 kW). A sensitivity analysis of the simulation indicates that increasing feed rates and plasma power improve syngas quality: CO reaches a maximum of 69 vol% and H2 rises to 31.1 vol%. Ammonia and urea units show N2 and CO2 conversion efficiencies of 87.6 % and 81.56 %, respectively, with maximum urea production of 2853 kg/h. Techno-economic analysis shows that a CAPEX of $32.9 million and OPEX of $4.49 million/year result in a competitive urea cost of $0.49/kg and annual revenue of $6.7 million. The cost analysis showed that a strong positive cash flow and net earnings in a period of 10 years confirm the long-term economic viability and sustainability of this waste utilization for fertilizer production. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Threats to food security in rice farming: A scientific mapping of climate change impacts
abstract: Climate change is severely disrupting many aspects of human life worldwide, particularly rice farming, as it feeds many people worldwide. In the absence of stable rice production, food security will is threatened for the global population. This paper examines how climate change is related to rice farming and what it means for overall food security. I used bibliometric analysis to examine the literature on this topic from 1998 to 2024, a 26-year period. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using specific keywords, yielding 549 matching documents. Using VOSviewer helped visualize connections and identify trends in the research. Researchers have consistently focused on climate change, rice farming, and food security over time, but have not yet mapped the interrelationships between these variables. The findings suggest a reciprocal relationship. Agriculture produces greenhouse gases that exacerbate climate change, but climate change subsequently reverses itself and harms agricultural productivity. It is particularly difficult for rice to respond to changing temperatures, unusual rainfall patterns, and recurring extreme weather events. As a result, when crop yields decline, the availability of rice as a staple food decreases, directly impacting food security. These findings directly relate to Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger, making it urgent to find better ways to adapt agriculture to climate change and make it more sustainable. This necessary adaptation in rice farming aligns with Sustainable Development Goal 13, Climate Action. Therefore, this Action requires support from the government and the agricultural sector workforce to achieve food security and sustainable rice farming. © 2027, Malque Publishing. .

title: TKAM: A temporal-availability-aware encoder-decoder framework for multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices
abstract: Accurate multi-step forecasting of soybean futures prices is important for hedging, inventory management, and agricultural market risk management. Existing soybean futures price forecasting studies often organize heterogeneous predictors as a unified input sequence and overlook differences in their temporal availability at the forecasting origin. In addition, how complex forecasting models use information across forecast horizons remains insufficiently explained. This study proposes TKAM, an interpretable framework for multi-step soybean futures price forecasting. TKAM separates past-observed market variables from future-known time features, uses a Mamba-based encoder to represent historical market dynamics, and employs a Temporal Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (TKAN) decoder with a multi-output forecasting strategy to generate forecasts for multiple future trading days. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used to examine horizon-specific feature contributions. The empirical analysis uses 4165 daily observations from the No. 1 yellow soybean futures contract listed on the Dalian Commodity Exchange in China, covering the period from May 9, 2008, to June 27, 2025. The results show that TKAM achieves competitive and stable point-forecasting accuracy compared with twelve benchmark models, particularly for biweekly and monthly forecasts. The ablation results indicate that the branch-based input organization contributes substantially to forecasting performance and that the Mamba encoder is effective within this structure. The SHAP analysis shows that related agricultural futures prices, domestic spot prices, and time features contribute differently across forecast horizons. These findings provide methodological insights for multi-step agricultural futures price forecasting and empirical evidence for understanding the horizon-specific forecasting behavior of complex models in agricultural markets. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and ecological determinants of cutaneous Leishmaniasis in Errachidia Province, southeastern Morocco: A 16-year municipality-level analysis with SARIMA forecasting
abstract: Leishmaniasis is a vector-borne parasitic disease transmitted by female sandflies of the genus Phlebotomus and affects approximately 1.2 million people annually in more than 90 countries worldwide. Morocco remains one of the most affected countries in North Africa, where the disease continues to represent a major public health concern. This study aimed to analyze the spatial and temporal trends of leishmaniasis incidence across all municipalities of Errachidia Province between 2010 and 2025 and to assess the influence of ecological, demographic, and socio-economic factors on its distribution. Also, the study aimed to predict the monthly CL cases using the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model. Epidemiological data on parasitologically confirmed cases obtained from the Errachidia Provincial Health Delegation were processed using geographic information system (GIS) tools and statistical methods to explore spatial patterns and correlations with environmental and socio-demographic variables. The models are trained and evaluated using monthly CL cases collected from 2010 to 2025, with the optimal model selected based on Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). During 16-years study period, 7034 cases were recorded in Errachidia Province, with the highest incidence reported in 2010 (860 cases per 100,000 inhabitants). Overall, the incidence showed marked temporal fluctuations but demonstrated a general decreasing trend over the study period. A pronounced spatial heterogeneity was observed between rural municipalities (Sid Ali, Melaab, and Ferkla) and urban municipalities (Errachidia, Arfoud, and Goulmima) ( p < 0.01). The disease was slightly more frequent in females (54.41%) than in males (45.59%), and a significant difference was observed among age groups ( p = 0.019), with the 0–9 and 10–19-year groups being the most affected. Seasonal analysis revealed a peak incidence during winter. In addition, higher incidence was associated with low- to medium-altitude municipalities, while no significant association was observed with poverty or vulnerability indices. The SARIMA (0,0,1)12 model demonstrated the best predictive performance. These findings highlight the heterogeneity and ecological determinants of leishmaniasis in southeastern Morocco and may support targeted surveillance and control strategies in high-risk areas. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

title: Chatbot service quality in omnichannel retailing: Effects of ChatbotSQ on decision confidence and customer behavior
abstract: AI chatbots are increasingly being embedded in omnichannel retail ecosystems; however, research on how chatbot service quality relates to customer behavior is limited. In this paper, we conceptualize chatbot service quality (ChatbotSQ) as a formative construct comprising six dimensions: functional, integration, interface, safety, emotional, and personalization quality. Drawing on means-end chain theory, we examine decision confidence as a mechanism underlying the association between chatbot service quality and customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in and explore the moderating role of chatbot comfort level. We use partial least squares structural equation modeling, importance-performance map analysis, and necessary condition analysis to analyze survey data from the United States (N = 345) and Saudi Arabia (N = 302). The results show that chatbot service quality is positively associated with customers' share of time with the chatbot and omnichannel ecosystem lock-in in both countries. These relationships are mediated by decision confidence, which also emerged as a necessary condition for achieving both behavioral outcomes. Chatbot comfort level significantly moderates the relationship between ChatbotSQ and decision confidence in Saudi Arabia but not in the United States, indicating that this boundary condition is context-sensitive across the two samples examined. We also validate a condensed six-item ChatbotSQ measure that provides a parsimonious alternative for research and practice. These findings advance retailing research by showing that AI chatbot service quality is associated with behavioral outcomes through customers’ decision confidence. © 2026 The Authors

title: QSRR-Based RP-HPLC Method Development for Antiviral Drug Analysis: Machine Learning, Design of Experiments, and Sustainable Analytical Strategies—A Review
abstract: Pharmaceutical quality control and research depend on the creation of effective, reliable, and sustainable analytical techniques for antiviral medication analysis. The development of conventional RP-HPLC methods frequently depends on lengthy experimental trials, which might raise the need for resources, analytical time, and solvent usage. A useful computational technique for connecting molecular structural characteristics to chromatographic retention behaviour and assisting in the advancement of predictive methods is Quantitative Structure–Retention Relationship (QSRR) modelling. The promise of QSRR-based approaches to comprehending retention processes, forecasting chromatographic behaviour, and improving chromatographic circumstances has been further increased by recent developments in machine learning (ML), chemometrics, and design of experiments (DoE). The latest developments in QSRR-based RP-HPLC method development for antiviral medication evaluation are covered in this review, with a focus on molecular descriptors, statistical and machine learning-based predictive techniques, DoE-assisted optimisation, and sustainability analytical strategies. Additionally, covered are pertinent databases, computing systems, and software tools for chromatographic optimisation, model creation, validation, and descriptor synthesis. The opportunity of combining QSRR with ML and DoE to lessen experimental workload, enhance prediction and optimisation, and support more effective chromatographic technique development is demonstrated by published works. The difficulties with data quality, descriptor selection, model interpretability, overfitting, validation, repeatability, and portability are further examined in the review. The application of QSRR in sustainable pharmaceutical evaluation could be further enhanced by explainable artificial intelligence, automated and high-throughput processes, sophisticated chemometric techniques, and green analytical principles, according to future viewpoints. All things considered, the integration of QSRR, ML, and DoE offers a viable foundation for developing RP-HPLC methods for antiviral drug analysis that are predictive, effective, and environmentally friendly. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Persuasive triggers and psychological pathways: Unplanned purchase behavior in live-streaming blind box commerce
abstract: Unplanned purchasing is increasingly embedded in digital experiences in which consumers encounter commercial opportunities without a prior intention to shop. This study examines how such opportunities become valued and actionable in live-streaming blind-box commerce. Using survey data from 231 Chinese consumers with experience purchasing blind boxes through livestreams, we test a process model linking scarcity messages, time pressure, economic benefits, and fear of missing out (FOMO) with perceived value, emotional and cognitive self-efficacy, and unplanned purchase behavior (UPB). All four conditions were positively associated with perceived value, which was positively associated with both forms of self-efficacy; emotional and cognitive self-efficacy were, in turn, positively associated with UPB. Streamer persuasiveness strengthened the relationships between all four antecedent conditions and perceived value. The findings show that an unplanned purchase need not arise simply from impulsive responding. Consumers may encounter an unexpected opportunity, judge it to be worthwhile, and feel capable of acting even when the purchase was not previously planned. The study extends research on livestream commerce by explaining how persuasive conditions relate to value appraisal and perceived capability, providing a process-based account of UPB in an uncertain and interactive retail setting. For practitioners, the findings highlight the importance of combining persuasive communication with clear and transparent presentation of purchase conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: The Economic Value of Animals Traded for Traditional Medicine in Ghana and Its Effect on Biodiversity Conservation
abstract: The trade and use of wildlife for traditional medicine are widespread in many developing countries and continue to expand. The increasing demand for high-value, endangered animals used in traditional medicine has raised important conservation concerns. In this first nationwide cross-sectional study of its kind in Ghana, we assessed the economic value of wildlife traded for traditional medicine through interviews with 133 vendors in 48 markets and examined its implications for biodiversity conservation. The mean annual sales per vendor were estimated at USD 15,123.6. Based on an estimated 1,074 vendors engaged in the trade of Animal-Based Medicine (ABM) nationwide, the annual economic value of the sector was approximately USD 16.2 million. We found that the vendors' sex, age and religious affiliation were not statistically associated with their annual trade values. However, vendors whose clientele consisted predominantly of females recorded significantly higher annual sales than those serving predominantly male clients (USD 247,852.8 vs. 59,765.6; p-value = 0.004). The most expensive animal parts included endangered species such as lion (Panthera leo), tiger (P. tigris), African savanna elephant (Loxodonta africana), and Home’s hinge-back tortoise (Kinixys homeana). Our findings showed that the ABM trade in Ghana provides employment and income for many actors along the supply chain, and contributes millions of dollars annually to the national economy. These findings highlight the need for stakeholders and policymakers to strengthen collaboration in regulating the harvest and trade of wildlife used in traditional medicine to promote both sustainable livelihoods and biodiversity conservation in Ghana and across sub-Saharan Africa. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. First, a regional tourism-pressure screening index is constructed for Euro-Mediterranean NUTS-2 regions to identify broader high-pressure contexts. Second, an Overtourism Vulnerability Index (OVI) is implemented for the main tourism hotspots in Apulia, Italy, using eight normalized indicators capturing direct tourism pressure, air accessibility, accommodation platformisation, economic dependence and heritage attractiveness. Rather than treating the OVI as a ranking device, the framework decomposes vulnerability into three diagnostic dimensions: direct pressure, structural fragility and gateway/heritage amplification. These dimensions identify four regimes: critical overload and fragility, gateway/heritage pressure, coastal fragility and platformisation, and monitor-and-prevent contexts. Robustness checks and an external waste-based plausibility check support the diagnostic interpretation. The resulting toolbox links each regime to assessment, monitoring and candidate intervention priorities, helping planners move from regional pressure screening to municipal scoping and targeted environmental and carrying-capacity assessment. © 2026 The Authors

title: Pyrolysis of biomass feedstocks for hydrogen-enriched syngas production: Cold gas efficiency modelling, latin hypercube uncertainty analysis, and parametric stress analysis
abstract: Biomass-derived syngas offers a viable pathway for producing renewable, hydrogen-rich fuel gas. However, its conversion performance is influenced by feedstock type, temperature, feed rate, and moisture content. This study develops a Cold Gas Efficiency (CGE) model for four agricultural feedstocks: wheat, barley, oilseed rape, and beans. Temperature-dependent regression correlations are developed for the main syngas components and gas flow rate using experimental data. Results show that CGE is highly sensitive to temperature, with low-temperature stress (0–5th percentile) reducing mean CGE by up to 22%. High-moisture stress (95–100th percentile) produced an even larger decline, lowering mean CGE from ∼44% to ∼35% for wheat and compressing the distribution into a low-performance regime. Regression-based tornado charts indicate that temperature is the strongest linear driver (coefficient = +0.44), while Spearman rank correlations highlight feed rate as the most monotonic negative driver (−0.41). Feedstock probability density functions (PDFs) show that wheat as the most efficient and least variable performer, while Oilseed Rape (OSR) and beans exhibited broader distributions due to higher ash-related inhibition of char reactivity. The thermochemical and statistical results demonstrate that operational uncertainty, such as temperature and moisture, dominates CGE variability. This underscores the need for robust control strategies in small-scale pyrolysis systems. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. title: Modeling Japanese consumers' acceptance and rejection of tech-enhanced foods
abstract: To maintain the well-being of the global population, strengthening the food supply system is necessary. A promising solution is the development of new food manufacturing technologies related to the production, processing, and preservation of food. Foods produced with such technologies are referred to as tech-enhanced foods. While the promotion of tech-enhanced foods is important, they have yet to be widely used in Japan. An understanding of consumers' psychological reactions and related factors is considered useful when designing and promoting tech-enhanced foods. Thus, this research aimed to construct a model explaining the psychological factors pertaining to consumers' acceptance and rejection of four types of tech-enhanced foods: genetically modified (GM) foods, meat alternatives, cultured meats, and edible insects. The proposed psychological model was based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework and supplemented with elements from the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The analysis revealed that positive and negative affects emerge as the most significant factors associated with intake intention and rejection, respectively. Moreover, the potential damage and benefits of tech-enhanced foods, along with reliability of regulation, were found to be associated with emotional responses, rejection, and intake intention. These findings may provide useful insights for designing interventions aimed at promoting the acceptance of tech-enhanced foods. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Activating competing goals: The dual effect of environmental fee
abstract: While economic intervention is increasingly used to support environmental protection, its effectiveness in tourism contexts remains unclear. By introducing symbolic interactionism, this research examined how environmental fee cues influence tourists’ environmentally responsible behavior across different attraction types and quality levels. We conducted a field observation study (N = 500), two field surveys using questionnaires (total N = 765), and one online experiment (N = 293). Results showed that environmental fee cues increased environmentally responsible behavior in resource-based attractions by activating moral norm goals, but decreased environmentally responsible behavior in market-based attractions via thrift goal activation. Moreover, this study further refined the environmental fee strategy and examined its effectiveness and mechanism across all attraction quality levels. The findings provide novel theoretical insights and practical implications for designing adaptive environmental fee strategies. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Barriers and enablers to circular economy implementation in 3D concrete printing: A fuzzy decision-making approach
abstract: The circular economy (CE) is increasingly emphasised in 3D concrete printing (3DCP), yet evidence remains limited on the key barriers to its implementation and the enablers needed to support practical uptake. This study addresses that gap through a sequential mixed-methods design combining a literature-informed review to identify initial barriers, ten semi-structured expert interviews to refine them and elicit corresponding enablers in the 3DCP context, and a questionnaire survey of 58 academic and industry specialists from multiple regions to prioritise their relative importance using a fuzzy synthetic evaluation approach. The findings show that CE implementation in 3DCP is constrained less by isolated technical limitations than by wider system conditions shaping approval, investment, knowledge translation, and supply-chain coordination. Regulatory and standardisation issues emerged as the most critical barrier theme, followed by financial and market constraints, while the gap between low-TRL academic research and high-TRL industrial implementation was identified as the most prominent item-level barrier. The most influential enablers were CE-oriented standards, cost-effective process maturation, targeted R&D support, and stronger validation and implementation pathways. By revealing convergence between academia and industry on the main priorities, the study contributes a context-specific methodological approach for investigating CE implementation in 3DCP and establishes a prioritised evidence base on the barriers and enablers shaping circular 3DCP. It also provides practical guidance for researchers, industry stakeholders, and policy actors by identifying where intervention is likely to be most effective, particularly in standards development, technology validation, investment support, and supply-chain coordination, to scale circular 3DCP in support of net-zero and zero-waste ambitions. © 2026 The Authors

title: Respect your privacy: An identifiable and authorized privacy-preserving data retrieval protocol through decentralized identifier
abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requires personal data processing to satisfy both the principles of lawfulness and data minimization. However, existing privacy-preserving data retrieval protocols rarely meet both principles, especially at the batch scale. To solve these problems, we present IAPDR, an Identifiable and Authorized Privacy-Preserving Data Retrieval protocol that builds on Decentralised Identifier (DID) that focuses on data-subject privacy under GDPR compliance. IAPDR uses DIDs to provide verifiable, globally unique identities while preserving anonymity and self-sovereign management. It uses non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKs) for anonymous authorization. The data controller can verify the lawfulness of each retrieval request without learning any personally identifiable data, thereby upholding data minimization. For scalable retrieval, IAPDR employs Private Set Intersection with Payload (PSI-Payload) to execute large-batch matching while keeping both identifiers and associated records confidential. We prove anonymity and unforgeability, and give a Universal Composability (UC) security analysis in the semi-honest model. Under the same dataset sizes and network settings on public benchmarks, IAPDR achieves an average 1.36 × improvement in computational efficiency and an average 3.62 × reduction in total communication compared with state-of-the-art schemes. These enhancements make GDPR compliant privacy-preserving data retrieval practically feasible. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Automotive warranty intelligence through evidence-grounded graph retrieval and agentic reasoning
abstract: Automotive warranty records contain detailed evidence on field failures, repeated repairs, and repair actions, but heterogeneous fields and fragmented vehicle–part–fault relations make reliability-oriented synthesis difficult. We introduce a confidential industrial protocol for automotive warranty intelligence and evaluate an evidence-grounded framework over 16,948 anonymized after-sales records. The evaluated framework combines GraphRAG evidence packs from a 2500-record test-reference-enriched index, Dynamic ACE-Agent governance with an evidence workspace and frozen procedural memory, and retrieval-aware supervised fine-tuning. Eight system configurations were tested on a locked 150-item set covering single-record diagnosis, multi-record fault reasoning, and global reliability-evidence synthesis. The full system achieved the highest blind-judge integrated quality score (4.224/5 versus 3.272 for the Flat Hybrid-RAG baseline) and reduced the hard-error rate from 48.7% to 22.0%. In a stratified double-rated expert review of 45 items, it also achieved the highest weighted score (4.237), exceeding the strongest competing configuration by 0.199 points (95% confidence interval, 0.115–0.281; Holm-adjusted p=0.0131). Within this controlled protocol using a test-reference-enriched GraphRAG index, the integrated configuration produced the strongest observed traceable warranty responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Is state fragility a hindrance to trade openness in Africa?
abstract: This paper analyses the effects of state fragility on trade openness in Africa, using panel data for 50 African countries over the period 1995–2018. We use the recent de facto trade openness indicators developed by Squalli and Wilson (2011) because it reflects the actual degree of trade and the Fraser Institute’s de jure Trade Freedom index. Estimates obtained using the feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and the system generalized method of moments (system GMM) show that the inability of African states to provide basic public services and ensure high-quality institutions has a negative effect on these countries’ trade openness. However, the magnitude of the estimated effects varies considerably according to the different measures of trade openness used. Furthermore, the quantile regression approach shows that the effect of state fragility and its dimensions varies across the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th quintile. The results are also robust when distinguishing other measures of state fragility and trade openness. Based on these results, it would be worthwhile for African countries to strengthen state capacity and the quality of their institutions in order to ensure an effective and sustainable improvement in trade transactions. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: Achieving emotionally and factually grounded interactive comments through a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine
abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce, online product comments have become a major reference point for consumers in making purchase decisions. However, current comment systems are challenged by uneven comment quality, limited accuracy in sentiment expression, and a lack of verification for factual information, which together reduce the usefulness and credibility of the comments. Grounded in dual process theory and adaptive control theory, this study proposes a large language model-driven adaptive dialogue engine framework that enables intelligent generation of interactive comments through an emotion-fact dual-anchoring mechanism. The framework dynamically adjusts its interaction strategy according to the dialogue state and user feedback, while preserving authentic emotional expression and ensuring the reliability of objective information. The findings show that interactive comments generated by large language models perform well in terms of content authenticity, emotional consistency, user satisfaction, and readability. This study offers an innovative solution to key limitations in e-commerce comment systems and is of significant importance for improving comment quality and user engagement on digital commerce platforms. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Do platform and seller cues improve price prediction? A study on online food delivery platforms using machine learning
abstract: This study investigates value-based pricing on online food delivery platforms by examining the role of beyond-core service attributes—platform brand and Observed Restaurant Activity Duration—as observable platform- and restaurant-level cues. Drawing on signaling theory as a conceptual lens, we adopt a theory-guided predictive modeling approach to assess whether these cue-related variables improve the prediction of the final price paid per order under varying levels of order urgency. Using a dataset of 1536 cross-platform transactions in Vietnam and applying a broader model-benchmarking strategy, including Random Forest, linear regression, XGBoost, and other machine-learning models, we show that nonlinear machine-learning models provide stronger out-of-sample predictive accuracy than traditional linear estimation. XGBoost achieves the strongest overall predictive performance and is therefore used as the primary model for permutation feature-importance and hypothesis analyses, while Random Forest serves as a robustness benchmark. Both platform brand and restaurant activity duration emerge as meaningful predictive contributors beyond core service attributes. Importantly, platform brand shows a substantial increase in predictive importance under high-urgency conditions, whereas restaurant activity duration remains comparatively stable across urgency levels. title: Knowledge graph–based data governance for small and medium-sized enterprises: A systematic literature review and socio-technical framework
abstract: Established data governance frameworks provide valuable guidance for large enterprises, yet their assumptions about stable funding, dedicated governance teams, and mature infrastructure often do not reflect the realities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Recent research has explored the use of semantic technologies and knowledge graphs to automate governance tasks, improve traceability, and support policy enforcement. Yet, whether these approaches effectively address SME-specific needs remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic literature review of knowledge-graph-based data governance approaches, focusing on their relevance to SMEs. Following the PRISMA method, we analyzed evidence from 43 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 through multiple lenses, including core data governance activities (Define, Implement, Monitor), components of the Data Governance Institute framework, and stages of the data lifecycle. Using thematic network analysis we synthesize recurring limitations and structural patterns across the literature. Our findings show that while semantic technologies demonstrate strong potential for automating policy enforcement, metadata integration, and interoperability, most approaches are designed for mature enterprises. They commonly assume formal governance hierarchies, specialized expertise, and sustained operational capacity, conditions that are often absent in SMEs. As a result, governance designs are skewed toward technical controls and early lifecycle stages, with limited attention to monitoring, organizational roles, decision rights, and end-to-end governance. Building on these findings, this study advances a socio-technical perspective on data governance in SME contexts by reframing governance as a lifecycle-embedded and practice-oriented capability rather than a purely technical implementation. It further conceptualizes knowledge graphs as boundary objects that mediate between governance intent, technical enforcement, and organizational practice. Our key contributions include a structured synthesis of knowledge-graph-based data governance research, identifies eight recurring gaps that hinder SME applicability, and derives nine design principles alongside a conceptual research framework to guide future research and the development of SME-suitable governance solutions. © 2026

title: Fuel vs. food? Climate shocks, biofuel expansion, and the future of global food security
abstract: The expansion of biofuel production has generated debate over its potential trade-off with food security, particularly regarding land diversion, rising food prices, and climate-related agricultural stress. This study utilizes panel data from 5 emerging (BRICS) and 7 advanced economies (G7) employing Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) and Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for robustness to examine the association between biofuel production and agricultural total-factor productivity, crop value, and global food security during the period 2012-2022. Grounded in bioeconomy transition theory, induced innovation theory, the Porter hypothesis, and sustainable intensification, the empirical evidence indicates that biofuel expansion does not create a homogeneous food–fuel trade-off; instead, its associations vary across development and performance regimes. Biofuel production is positively associated with crop value in both groups but shows contrasting productivity associations, particularly across quantiles. Temperature anomalies exhibit heterogeneous associations with agricultural outcomes, while food prices are more strongly associated with food security. In line with induced innovation theory, innovation capacity is positively associated with several agricultural outcomes, while the climate–innovation interaction indicates heterogeneous adaptive associations across country groups. The differing associations of environmental policy stringency are broadly consistent with the conditional predictions of the Porter hypothesis, rather than indicating uniform regulatory benefits. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between biofuel expansion and food-system performance is conditional on development stage, climate exposure, innovation capacity, environmental policy stringency, and food-price conditions. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: What counts as urban smartness? A longitudinal thematic analysis of smart city indexes
abstract: Smart city indexes increasingly influence urban governance, policy benchmarking, and investment narratives, yet their conceptual evolution remains insufficiently examined. This article investigates how major smart city evaluation frameworks changed between 2017 and 2022 through a longitudinal thematic analysis of six prominent smart city indexes selected from an initial inventory of sixteen. The findings suggest a shift in the smart city index landscape from more technocentric assessment frameworks toward more integrated evaluation logics that give greater attention to governance capacity, economic conditions, and societal dimensions. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Research on interruption risk propagation in aircraft supply chain network: A multi-layer network coupling model
abstract: The aircraft supply chain (ASC) is a core component of national high-end equipment manufacturing systems, which have complex network characteristics of strong coupling. Once an interruption occurs at any node, it will propagate to relevant enterprises along the supply-demand relationship. However, the propagation process of interruption risks is not merely a matter of physical transmission, it is typically accompanied by the spread of risk information and the adoption of preventive measures. Therefore, investigating the dynamic coupling characteristics among risk information diffusion, adoption of preventive measures, and interruption risk propagation is of great significance for exploring the interruption risk propagation mechanisms in ASC. Considering the above facts, this paper proposes a three-layer coupled network model. This model divides enterprises into multiple different states and innovatively proposes different network layer propagation mechanisms and interlayer coupling methods. Subsequently, the microscopic Markov chain approach is employed to establish state transition Eqs., and the mathematical characteristics of interruption risk outbreak are derived through theoretical deduction. The proposed model is applied to the risk propagation analysis of real ASC networks, and the proposed method and key findings were visually demonstrated. The research results provide decision-making references for risk management in the aviation industry chain. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Proactive vs reactive destination revitalisation
abstract: Destinations evolve through lifecycles, with a very real risk of entering long-term decline in the post-maturity phase. Decline is not inevitable, though, for it depends on whether destination stakeholders recognise early symptoms and respond appropriately. Unfortunately, the literature suggests that timely, anticipatory responses are rare. Instead, most destinations fail to detect or act on early warning signals and only respond reactively after decline has set in. This paper develops a conceptual model that identifies and contrasts reactive and proactive responses to post-maturity decline. The model is derived from a systematic synthesis of case-study evidence of 50 case studies examining destination decline and attempts at rejuvenation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

title: Trends in access to basic sanitation services across Brazilian municipalities under a new legal framework
abstract: Federal Law No. 14,026/2020 updated Brazil's sanitation legal framework, reinforcing universalization targets for water supply and sewage services. It mandates that by the end of 2033, sanitation contracts must ensure 99% of the population has access to potable water and 90% to sewage collection and treatment. Given Brazil's vast territory and regional disparities, achieving these targets across all municipalities poses a significant challenge. This article examines whether water and sewage coverage rates converged between 2010 and 2022, analyzing municipalities segregated by state and region. The study provides an up-to-date assessment of these indicators and identifies challenges in meeting the established targets. Empirical estimation of convergence draws on economic methodologies for growth and income convergence, incorporating beta-convergence and sigma-convergence hypotheses. This robust methodological approach enables a comprehensive analysis of the evolution of sanitation services in Brazil, offering insights to guide effective public policies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Secondhand fashion subscription boxes: A necessary condition analysis of purchase intention determinants
abstract: Research indicates that the fashion industry can be made more environmentally friendly by introducing a closed-loop economy – also known as a circular economy – and implementing sustainable business models in areas such as clothing resale, rental, repair, and remake. Secondhand clothing is the sector to which research attributes the greatest potential for success in introducing new sustainable business models. This study examines the secondhand subscription box and eleven potential determinants from the secondhand fashion consumption literature. It complements a constraint-based approach (Necessary Condition Analysis – NCA) with an effect-based approach (regression analysis) to identify the necessary-but-not-sufficient conditions and the key (regression) factors shaping purchase intention. Using a sample of 215 German participants, we found that most determinants are necessity-based bottlenecks. They must be present and reach a certain threshold. Some are also key factors that drive purchase intention. The relevance of the determinants varies across sub-groups. This has implications for both academia and practice in designing secondhand subscription boxes. However, the study reveals that the determinants are context-dependent and no general principle can be transferred to other circular economy or sustainable consumption contexts. © 2026 The Authors

title: Software-defined vehicle ecosystems in transformation
abstract: Context: The automotive industry is transitioning from hardware-centric development toward software-defined vehicles (SDVs), where software drives functionality, value creation, and competitive differentiation. This shift challenges proprietary software development, firm-centric innovation, and traditional supply chain models, giving rise to ecosystem-based collaboration. However, SDV transformation is primarily framed as a technical change, leaving its broader ecosystem implications insufficiently understood. Objective: This study explores the transformation of SDV ecosystems, their stakeholders, collaborative structures, roles and authority, and highlights associated challenges and opportunities. Methods: This systematic literature review collected 351 studies from six databases and selected 25 for detailed analysis. Results: Four interrelated shifts (from hardware-centric to software platforms, from supply chains to collaborative ecosystems, from proprietary to open and standard solutions, and from firm-level control to distributed governance) characterise the transformation, with six levels of collaboration involving twelve stakeholder groups. These collaborations are influenced by five dimensions of authority. The literature also highlights six core software development challenges and various organisational, industry and market, and regulatory, legal, and ethical challenges. It identifies five software development opportunities and various organisational, industry and market, and public value and ethical opportunities. Conclusion: The first contribution integrates previously fragmented literature on the SDV ecosystem transformation, demonstrating how SDVs are transforming the automotive industry through the four interrelated shifts driven by software advancements. Second, it proposes an SDV ecosystems model that integrates SDV architecture, stakeholder groups, collaboration structures, and governance levels to facilitate sustainable SDV ecosystems. Additionally, agendas for research and practice are outlined. © 2026 The Authors

title: The effect of rosé wine color: A conceptual replication and a generation-based extension
abstract: Recent research on crossmodal correspondences from Jaud et al. (2025) highlighted the role of rosé wine color in shaping consumer responses. Building on their work, this study aims to assess the robustness and generalizability of these findings while extending the original model in two ways. Specifically, by using a within-subjects experimental design conducted in the United States (N = 448), we replicate the model in a different cultural context by shifting from a French to a US sample. Further, we extend the underlying process by introducing perceived lightness as an additional mediating mechanism. Finally, we broaden the model by incorporating generational belonging (Generation Z vs. Generation Y) as a moderating variable. This approach enables us to assess both the robustness and the boundary conditions of previously identified effects of rosé wine color. Our findings contribute to the literature on crossmodal correspondences by demonstrating the stability of color-driven effects while highlighting generational differences in the relationship between perceived fruitiness and willingness to buy. They also offer practical insights for wine producers and distributors seeking to better align product presentation with the expectations of different generation-based consumer segments. © 2026

title: The grass is not always greener: The effects of local labor market information on search and employment
abstract: We examine how information about local labor market conditions shapes search and employment outcomes for Indian job seekers. Participants were randomly shown information about either job postings, job applicants, or both from a popular job portal for their preferred city and occupation. Treated respondents are more likely to be employed seven months later. This overall effect varies considerably by baseline employment status. Among the initially employed, treatments reduce search off the portal and increase employment, with suggestive evidence of higher persistence in baseline jobs. In contrast, among the initially unemployed, treatments increase search activity but do not raise employment. Employment gains are concentrated among job seekers with less optimistic beliefs about labor market conditions. These findings suggest that limited information about labor market fundamentals may contribute to job churn in lower-income countries. © 2026 The Authors

title: Exploring Lean-Integrated Circular Economy in the Built Environment Setting: Implications for Project Governance and Compliance
abstract: The current study establishes how lean tenets contribute to the circular economy (CE) with exploration of lean tools with circular economy core principles and framework development. While there seem to be synergies between the concepts of lean and CE, the construction management research fraternity has not fully tapped the huge research potential in this domain. To address this gap, a two-phased exploratory qualitative research design is proposed. The first phase involves mapping lean tools with 10 dimensions of CE in the context of the built environment sector through content analysis and expert validation (n=3). Continuous improvement and added value tools of lean attained maximum realization of CE dimensions. The second phase involves semistructured interviews of experts (n=9) on an understanding of the synergies between lean and CE through thematic analysis (TA). The current study identifies predominant lean tools that realize CE dimensions and develops a conceptual model of a lean-driven circular economy (LdCE) framework for construction projects. Also, the lean tenets and their allied tools enabled value optimization through effective mapping of non-value-added processes and minimizing wasteful aspects. These findings are intended to inform engineers, construction managers, and legal practitioners about actionable strategies for promoting sustainable, legally compliant project execution. This study proves to accelerate sustainable construction through a lean and CE integrated framework in developing nations. Analyzing the associativity of the lean tools in realizing the CE dimensions and the strategies of a lean-driven circular economy through models is a novel concept with this research. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: Influence of environmental stimuli on sustainable food choices: the moderating role of AI-source disclosure
abstract: Reducing meat consumption is necessary for public health and environmental sustainability. However, while the benefits of positively-valenced nature have been explored, the comparative behavioral effects and mediational patterns of positively-valenced and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli remain unclear. Across three studies, we examined how positively- and negatively-valenced environmental stimuli influence food choices. Study 1 showed that both types of environmental stimuli reduced meat-heavy meal choices compared to the control. Study 2 tested serial mediation models within a dual-system framework, and the results showed that positively-valenced stimuli were associated with stronger nature connectedness and greater consideration of future consequences (CFC), whereas negatively-valenced stimuli were associated with higher guilt and greater CFC. Study 3 manipulated AI-source disclosure for the environmental stimuli. Although AI-source disclosure did not significantly interact with environmental stimuli condition in predicting meat-heavy choices, it significantly attenuated the link between negatively-valenced stimuli and guilt, but did not attenuate the association between positively-valenced stimuli and nature connectedness. Collectively, these findings suggest that the environmental stimuli valence may be associated with food choices through two partially overlapping yet distinguishable psychological pathways, offering insights for nudging sustainable eating. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

title: Attribution of causality following service failure on online retail platforms: The roles of governance structure and recurring failures
abstract: Online retail platforms are increasingly mediating customer–vendor interactions, yet research offers limited insight into how platform governance shapes service failure attribution, especially after recurring failures. Drawing on attribution theory, this paper examines how centralized versus diffused governance structures influence consumers’ attribution of causality to the platform after service failure and their responses to recurring failures. Study 1 analyzes customer reviews using computational text analysis and shows that customers recognize governance structures and attribute causality to the platform more often under centralized than diffused governance. Employing scenario-based experiments, Study 2 demonstrates that centralized (vs. diffused) governance leads to higher failure attribution to the platform. Finally, we show that attribution following single and recurring failures serially mediates the relationship between governance structure and repurchase intention after a recurring failure. Importantly, platform attribution exerts opposite effects across failure episodes: following a single failure and successful recovery, greater platform attribution increases repurchase intention by signaling platform accountability and resolution capability. However, following a recurring failure, greater platform attribution decreases repurchase intention because recurrence signals a stable, persistent cause and reduces attributional uncertainty. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Data was collected through web scraping of customer reviews from major hotel chains on TripAdvisor. robust regressions, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), multivariate analysis.
